Book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I woke with a start because my aunt was shouting outside my door. Great way to wake up.

Book1-chapter2_Sc1.source: "He rolled onto his back and tried to remember the dream he had been having. It had been a good one. There had been a flying motorcycle in it. He had a funny feeling he’d had the same dream before."
Book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: That dream with the flying motorcycle has happened to me before. It's important to me, I can't just shrug it off.

Book1-chapter2_Sc1.source: "Well, get a move on, I want you to look after the bacon."
Book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: Aunt told me to get up and mind the bacon. So I'm in charge of breakfast whether I like it or not.

Book1-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Turning the envelope over, his hand trembling, Harry saw a purple wax seal bearing a coat of arms; a lion, an eagle, a badger, and a snake surrounding a large letter H."
Book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: It's from Hogwarts. There's a purple wax seal with the four animals and a big H. This is a Hogwarts letter.

Book1-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Hurry up, boy! What are you doing, checking for letter bombs?"
Book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: Uncle Vernon is not interested in what I might have. He rushes me, mocks me, and treats the letter like something to be laughed at or feared. I need to be careful with him.

Book1-chapter3_Sc2.source: No one, ever, in his whole life, had written to him.
Book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: No one has ever written to me. I can't believe there's actually a letter with my name on it.

Book1-chapter3_Sc2.source: Mr. H. Potter The Cupboard under the Stairs 4 Privet Drive Little Whinging Surrey
Book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: The letter is addressed to me, plain as day, to the cupboard under the stairs at 4 Privet Drive. It's meant for me and only me.

Book1-chapter3_Sc2.source: The envelope was thick and heavy, made of yellowish parchment, and the address was written in emerald-green ink.
Book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: The envelope isn't normal paper. It's thick yellow parchment and the address is written in emerald green. This isn't any ordinary letter.

Book1-chapter3_Sc2.source: Harry picked it up and stared at it, his heart twanging like a giant elastic band.
Book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: My heart's racing and I actually feel like something important is happening. This could change everything.

Book1-chapter3_Sc7.source: "I want to read it," said Harry furiously, "as it’s mine."
Book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: That's my letter. I'm not going to let them keep it from me.

Book1-chapter3_Sc7.source: "AAAAARRRGH!" Harry leapt into the air; he’d trodden on something big and squashy on the doormat — something alive!
Book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: What the hell? I just jumped because something alive was under my foot on the doormat.

Book1-chapter2_Sc4.source: [Piers was a scrawny boy with a face like a rat. He was usually the one who held people’s arms behind their backs while Dudley hit them.]
Book1-chapter2_Sc4.description: He's a scrawny kid with a rat face and he's the sort who pins people down while Dudley does the hitting. I don't trust him one bit.

Book1-chapter2_Sc4.source: [He was usually the one who held people’s arms behind their backs while Dudley hit them. Dudley stopped pretending to cry at once.]
Book1-chapter2_Sc4.description: Dudley isn't just a spoilt brat putting on an act. He's nasty when he wants to be, and Piers helps him. That's worrying.

Book1-chapter2_Sc4.source: [Harry, who couldn’t believe his luck, was sitting in the back of the Dursleys’ car with Piers and Dudley, on the way to the zoo for the first time in his life.]
Book1-chapter2_Sc4.description: I'm actually going to the zoo. I can't believe it, I'm sitting in the car with Dudley and that awful Piers and I'm finally going to see animals.

Book1-chapter3_Sc1.source: "Your new school uniform," she said. "I’m dyeing some of Dudley’s old things gray for you."
Book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: So they're making my school uniform out of Dudley’s old clothes and dyeing them gray for me.

Book1-chapter3_Sc1.source: "Get the mail, Dudley," said Uncle Vernon... "Make Harry get it." "Get the mail, Harry." "Make Dudley get it."
Book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: They boss me about and try to make me fetch things. I'm being ordered around like I'm nothing.

Book1-chapter3_Sc1.source: Three things lay on the doormat... and — a letter for Harry.
Book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: There is a letter addressed to me on the doormat.

Book1-chapter3_Sc4.source: Mr H. Potter The Cupboard under the Stairs 4 Privet Drive Little Whinging Surrey
Book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: That's my name and my cupboard. It's meant for me. I couldn't believe it when I saw my own address written so plainly.

Book1-chapter3_Sc4.source: The envelope was thick and heavy, made of yellowish parchment, and the address was written in emerald-green ink. There was no stamp.
Book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: The letter isn't ordinary. Thick yellowish parchment and green ink, and there's no stamp. This isn't the sort of post we get.

Book1-chapter3_Sc4.source: Turning the envelope over, his hand trembling, Harry saw a purple wax seal bearing a coat of arms; a lion, an eagle, a badger, and a snake surrounding a large letter H.
Book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: There's a purple wax seal with a coat of arms and a big H. That seal means something important and not Muggle.

Book1-chapter3_Sc4.source: “Hurry up, boy!” shouted Uncle Vernon from the kitchen. “What are you doing, checking for letter bombs?” He chuckled at his own joke.
Book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: Vernon is mocking me and doesn't take this seriously. He's impatient and makes crude jokes instead of caring about what the letter might mean.

Book1-chapter3_Sc8.source: [Lights clicked on upstairs and to his horror Harry realized that the big, squashy something had been his uncle’s face. Uncle Vernon had been lying at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, clearly making sure that Harry didn’t do exactly what he’d been trying to do.]
Book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: He was right there at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, his face all squashy. He was staying put to stop me getting out. What the hell, he actually sat up to block me.

Book1-chapter3_Sc8.source: [Lights clicked on upstairs and to his horror Harry realized that the big, squashy something had been his uncle’s face. Uncle Vernon had been lying at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, clearly making sure that Harry didn’t do exactly what he’d been trying to do.]
Book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: Vernon will go to ridiculous lengths to keep me under his control. Of course he would lie there like that to make sure I could not leave.

Book1-chapter2_Sc5.source: "I'm warning you now, boy, any funny business, anything at all, and you'll be in that cupboard from now until Christmas."
Book1-chapter2_Sc5.description: Vernon shoved his face right up to mine and warned me that if I do anything he calls 'funny' I'll be locked in the cupboard until Christmas. He's treating me like a menace and I won't let him bully me into hiding.

Book1-chapter5_Sc1.source: "It was a dream," he told himself firmly. "I dreamed a giant called Hagrid came to tell me I was going to a school for wizards. When I open my eyes I’ll be at home in my cupboard."
Book1-chapter5_Sc1.description: It must be a dream. Hagrid told me I'm going to a school for wizards, but I'm telling myself it's only a dream until I actually open my eyes.

Book1-chapter5_Sc1.source: There was suddenly a loud tapping noise. And there’s Aunt Petunia knocking on the door, Harry thought, his heart sinking.
Book1-chapter5_Sc1.description: There's someone at the door. Aunt Petunia's knocking and my stomach just drops when I think about her being there.

Book1-chapter5_Sc1.source: He sat up and Hagrid’s heavy coat fell off him.
Book1-chapter5_Sc1.description: Hagrid was actually here. I sat up and his huge coat fell off me, so it wasn't just a dream anymore.

Book1-chapter5_Sc1.source: Tap. Tap. Tap. "All right," Harry mumbled, "I’m getting up."
Book1-chapter5_Sc1.description: Fine, I'm getting up. No point pretending any longer.

Book1-chapter2_Sc2.source: "Mrs. Figg’s broken her leg. She can’t take him."
Book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: Mrs Figg has broken her leg and she can't take Dudley on his birthday. That means I'm not stuck with her today.

Book1-chapter2_Sc2.source: "Dudley’s mouth fell open in horror, but Harry’s heart gave a leap."
Book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I couldn't help grinning on the inside. The idea of not having to spend the day with Mrs Figg and her awful cats for a whole year actually made me feel proper relieved.

Book1-chapter2_Sc2.source: "The Dursleys often spoke about Harry like this, as though he wasn’t there — or rather, as though he was something very nasty that couldn’t understand them, like a slug."
Book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: They treat me like I'm disgusting, like I'm not even there. Petunia and Vernon talk about me as if I'm a slug and Marge hates me, so I can't expect them to be decent.

Book1-chapter2_Sc2.source: "We could phone Marge," Uncle Vernon suggested. "Don’t be silly, Vernon, she hates the boy."
Book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: They seriously considered phoning Marge to take Dudley but Petunia says Marge hates me, so I'm not an option for them.

Book1-chapter2_Sc2.source: "You could just leave me here," Harry put in hopefully
Book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I actually dared to say I could be left at home, imagining I might watch what I want on TV and maybe use Dudley's computer, which felt like a small win.

Book1-chapter3_Sc9.source: He shouted at Harry for about half an hour and then told him to go and make a cup of tea.
Book1-chapter3_Sc9.description: He can shout at me for ages and then act like I'm nothing more than a servant. I won't pretend I'm unbothered by that.

Book1-chapter3_Sc9.source: He told him to go and make a cup of tea.
Book1-chapter3_Sc9.description: I'm the one who gets sent off to make a cup of tea whenever he wants to show who's in charge. Fine, I made the tea.

Book1-chapter3_Sc9.source: By the time he got back, the mail had arrived, right into Uncle Vernon’s lap.
Book1-chapter3_Sc9.description: The post always turns up at the exact worst moment for me. I come back and there's the mail, dumped straight into Vernon's lap like it matters to him more than me.

Book1-chapter3_Sc10.source: "Uncle Vernon was tearing the letters into pieces before his eyes."
Book1-chapter3_Sc10.description: He ripped my letters up right in front of me. He actually tore them to pieces so I couldn't read them.

Book1-chapter3_Sc10.source: "He stayed at home and nailed up the mail slot."
Book1-chapter3_Sc10.description: He nailed the mail slot shut so letters can't get through. He's trying to stop any more from coming.

Book1-chapter3_Sc10.source: "See," he explained to Aunt Petunia through a mouthful of nails, "if they can’t deliver them they’ll just give up."
Book1-chapter3_Sc10.description: He thinks blocking the mail will make whoever is sending the letters give up. That's ridiculous but that's what he's doing.

Book1-chapter3_Sc10.source: "I want —" he began, but Uncle Vernon was tearing the letters into pieces before his eyes.
Book1-chapter3_Sc10.description: Uncle Vernon is actively against me getting those letters. I can't count on him to let me have them or to listen to me.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "That’s what yeh get when a powerful, evil curse touches yeh — took care of yer mum an’ dad an’ yer house, even — but it didn’t work on you, an’ that’s why yer famous, Harry."
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: So Voldemort tried to kill my parents and destroy our house and the curse failed on me. That is why people know my name.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Took yeh from the ruined house myself, on Dumbledore’s orders. Brought yeh ter this lot . . ."
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: Dumbledore sent Hagrid to rescue me from the ruined house and hand me over to the Dursleys.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Good question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you."
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: Voldemort disappeared the same night he attacked us. Nobody knows exactly what happened to him.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Not a wizard, eh? Never made things happen when you was scared or angry?"
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I thought I couldn't be a wizard, but all those weird things that happened when I was upset suddenly make sense. Maybe I am magical after all.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "I was allowed ter do a bit ter follow yeh an’ get yer letters to yeh an’ stuff — one o’ the reasons I was so keen ter take on the job —"
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: Hagrid cares about me and went out of his way to make sure I got my Hogwarts letters. He looks out for me.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "NEVER — INSULT — ALBUS — DUMBLEDORE — IN — FRONT — OF — ME!"
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: Hagrid thinks the world of Dumbledore. Hogwarts and Dumbledore are very important and respected in the wizarding world.

Book1-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Meant ter turn him into a pig, but I suppose he was so much like a pig anyway there wasn’t much left ter do."
Book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: Hagrid tried to turn Dudley into a pig and actually made a pig's tail appear. Magic can happen right in front of the Dursleys.

Book1-chapter3_Sc6.source: Dudley tried to grab the letter to read it, but Uncle Vernon held it high out of his reach.
Book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: Vernon's keeping the letter away from me. He won't let me read it and he holds things up like that on purpose.

Book1-chapter3_Sc6.source: Aunt Petunia took it curiously and read the first line.
Book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: Petunia actually read the letter. She looked shocked and I can tell whatever it said matters to them.

Book1-chapter3_Sc6.source: For a moment it looked as though she might faint. She clutched her throat and made a choking noise. "Vernon! Oh my goodness Vernon!"
Book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: Something in that letter terrifies them. If Petunia reacts like that, this is not just ordinary post. I can't ignore this.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "A Muggle," said Hagrid, "it’s what we call nonmagic folk like them."
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: A Muggle means nonmagic people. So the Dursleys are Muggles.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Knew! Of course we knew! ... she got a letter just like that and disappeared off to that — that school — and came home every vacation with her pockets full of frog spawn, turning teacups into rats."
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: My mum was a witch and she went to that school. They all knew she was different.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "CAR CRASH!" roared Hagrid ... "How could a car crash kill Lily an’ James Potter?"
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: They didn't die in a car crash. My parents were not killed by an accident.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "You-Know-Who killed ’em. An’ then — an’ this is the real myst’ry of the thing — he tried to kill you, too."
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: You-Know-Who came for my family and murdered Mum and Dad, and he tried to kill me as well.
The wizard who did it is Voldemort. People are terrified to say his name.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Never wondered how you got that mark on yer forehead? That was no ordinary cut."
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: That lightning scar isn't an ordinary cut. It came from Voldemort's attack when he tried to kill me.

Book1-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Yer mum an’ dad were as good a witch an’ wizard as I ever knew."
Book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: My parents were respected and talented witches and wizards. They were close to Dumbledore and well-regarded in the magical world.

Book1-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Pay him," Hagrid grunted into the sofa. "He wants payin' fer deliverin' the paper. Look in the pockets."
Book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: Owls expect payment for deliveries. I had to give the owl coins for dropping the newspaper.

Book1-chapter5_Sc2.source: Hagrid's coat seemed to be made of nothing but pockets — bunches of keys, slug pellets, balls of string, peppermint humbugs, teabags . . . finally, Harry pulled out a handful of strange-looking coins.
Book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: Hagrid's coat is full of pockets with all sorts of rubbish and odd coins. That's where I found the little bronze Knuts.

Book1-chapter5_Sc2.source: "The hut was full of sunlight, the storm was over... he felt as though a large balloon was swelling inside him."
Book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I'm over the moon; I'm so happy I could burst. Everything feels brilliant right now.

Book1-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Give him five Knuts," said Hagrid sleepily. "Knuts?" "The little bronze ones."
Book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: Five Knuts is the right payment for the paper. I counted out five little bronze coins and paid the owl.
Owls can be stubborn and a bit fierce when they're doing their job. This one snapped at me until I paid it.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: Rubeus Hagrid, Keeper of Keys and Grounds at Hogwarts.
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: Hagrid introduced himself as Rubeus Hagrid and said he works at Hogwarts. I know someone from that place actually came for me.
Hagrid told me I'm a wizard. Me. I couldn't believe it at first, but that means my life isn't the same as the Dursleys'.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: We are pleased to inform you that you have been accepted at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: I have a letter saying I've been accepted to Hogwarts. School starts September 1 and they expect my owl by July 31.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: Yeh look a lot like yer dad, but yeh've got yer mum's eyes.
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: Hagrid said I look like my dad and have my mum's eyes. That made me feel like my parents were real people, not just names.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: You never told him? Never told him what was in the letter Dumbledore left fer him? I was there! I saw Dumbledore leave it, Dursley!
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: Hagrid exploded at the Dursleys for hiding Dumbledore's letter from me. I now know the Dursleys kept important things from me on purpose.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: They await your owl by no later than July 31.
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: Before today I thought my life would always be locked in that hut. Now I know there's a whole different world waiting for me and I actually get to go.
Hagrid wrote a note to Dumbledore saying he gave me the letter. Someone important knows I'm coming.

Book1-chapter4_Sc1.source: I mighta sat on it at some point, but it'll taste all right.
Book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: Hagrid gave me a squashed chocolate cake for my birthday. He tried to be kind in his own rough way and I was starving, so it meant a lot.

Book1-chapter5_Sc6.source: "Which is your wand arm?" "Er — well, I’m right-handed," said Harry.
Book1-chapter5_Sc6.description: I'm right-handed. That's the arm to use when finding a wand.

Book1-chapter5_Sc6.source: "Every Ollivander wand has a core of a powerful magical substance, Mr Potter. We use unicorn hairs, phoenix tail feathers, and the heartstrings of dragons."
Book1-chapter5_Sc6.description: Wands have cores like unicorn hair, phoenix feather, or dragon heartstring and no two wands are the same.

Book1-chapter5_Sc6.source: "And of course, you will never get such good results with another wizard’s wand."
Book1-chapter5_Sc6.description: Using someone else's wand won't work properly. A wand needs to match its owner.

Book1-chapter5_Sc6.source: "He felt a sudden warmth in his fingers. He raised the wand above his head, brought it swishing down through the dusty air and a stream of red and gold sparks shot from the end like a firework"
Book1-chapter5_Sc6.description: When a wand fits me, I can feel warmth in my fingers and it will respond spectacularly, like shooting sparks.

Book1-chapter5_Sc6.source: "That will do," he said, and the tape measure crumpled into a heap on the floor.
Book1-chapter5_Sc6.description: Magic sometimes happens on its own. Things around me can act without anyone touching them.

Book1-chapter8_Sc2.source: "I don't know, sir." "Thought you wouldn't open a book before coming, eh, Potter?"
Book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I don't know, sir. Snape thinks I should have every bit of book-learning memorized and he enjoys throwing that at me. He expects me to remember stuff from One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi and uses it to needle me.

Book1-chapter8_Sc2.source: He tried not to look at Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle, who were shaking with laughter.
Book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I can't let Malfoy and his goons get under my skin. They're laughing to wind me up, so I force myself to keep my eyes on Snape and not give them the satisfaction.

Book1-chapter5_Sc3.source: I haven’t got any money and you heard Uncle Vernon last night he won’t pay for me to go and learn magic
Book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: I thought I was completely skint and Vernon would never pay, but that isn’t true anymore. I’m not ruined.

Book1-chapter5_Sc3.source: They didn’ keep their gold in the house, boy! Nah, first stop fer us is Gringotts
Book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: My parents didn’t keep their money at home. Their gold’s at Gringotts, so there’s something for me there.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "You have your mother's eyes. It seems only yesterday she was in here herself, buying her first wand. Ten and a quarter inches long, swishy, made of willow. Nice wand for charm work."
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: My mum had a ten and a quarter inch willow wand, swishy and good for charm work. And people still say I have her eyes.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Your father, on the other hand, favored a mahogany wand. Eleven inches. Pliable. A little more power and excellent for transfiguration."
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: Dad's wand was mahogany, eleven inches, pliable and better for transfiguration. It sounds like it suited him.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Well, I say your father favored it — it’s really the wand that chooses the wizard, of course."
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: Wands don't just belong to people, they choose them. It's the wand that chooses the wizard, not the other way around.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "I’m sorry to say I sold the wand that did it," "Thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Powerful wand, very powerful, and in the wrong hands ..."
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: Ollivander sold the wand that caused my scar. It was thirteen and a half inches, made of yew, and he says it was very powerful and dangerous in the wrong hands.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Oak, sixteen inches, rather bendy, wasn’t it?" "It was, sir, yes," "Good wand, that one. But I suppose they snapped it in half when you got expelled?"
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: Hagrid's wand was oak, sixteen inches and bendy. They snapped it when he was expelled, though Hagrid keeps the pieces and doesn't use them.

Book1-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Yes, yes. I thought I’d be seeing you soon. Harry Potter."
Book1-chapter5_Sc5.description: Ollivander knew who I was before I even said much. He treats me like someone important and seems to remember my parents, especially my mum.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "I just take the train from platform nine and three-quarters at eleven o'clock," he read.
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: Right, the train leaves from platform nine and three quarters at eleven. I have to find that weird platform.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "I don't know," said Harry, realizing this for the first time.
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I do not actually know where Hogwarts is on a map. I just follow the train.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Have a good term," said Uncle Vernon with an even nastier smile. He left without another word.
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: The Dursleys are sneering at me and left me at the station. They are not on my side.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "He checked his Hogwarts list yet again to make sure he had everything he needed, saw that Hedwig was shut safely in her cage,"
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: Hedwig is safe in her cage and coming with me. She's the reason I'm getting weird looks here.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Don't stop and don't be scared you’ll crash into it, that's very important. Best do it at a bit of a run if you're nervous."
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: Okay, I have to walk straight at the barrier between nine and ten and not hesitate. If I run at it, I'll get through.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "They reached King’s Cross at half past ten."
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: We're at King’s Cross with plenty of time. I will change on the train, not here in front of everyone.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: All Harry’s — it was incredible. The Dursleys couldn’t have known about this or they’d have had it from him faster than blinking. How often had they complained how much Harry cost them to keep? And all the time there had been a small fortune belonging to him, buried deep under London.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: I found out there's a fortune in my vault that the Dursleys never told me about. I couldn't believe it!

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: “The gold ones are Galleons,” he explained. “Seventeen silver Sickles to a Galleon and twenty-nine Knuts to a Sickle, it’s easy enough.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: Galleons are the gold coins. Seventeen Sickles make a Galleon and twenty-nine Knuts make a Sickle. That's how the money works.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: “Vault seven hundred and thirteen now, please, and can we go more slowly?” “One speed only,” said Griphook.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: My vault is number seven hundred and thirteen. The goblins only do one speed when they go through Gringotts.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: They bought Harry’s school books in a shop called Flourish and Blotts where the shelves were stacked to the ceiling with books as large as paving stones bound in leather; books the size of postage stamps in covers of silk; books full of peculiar symbols and a few books with nothing in them at all.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: There's a shop called Flourish and Blotts that sells all sorts of weird wizarding books. I could have spent ages there.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: “I was trying to find out how to curse Dudley.” “I’m not sayin’ that’s not a good idea, but yer not ter use magic in the Muggle world except in very special circumstances,” said Hagrid. “An’ anyway, yeh couldn’ work any of them curses yet, yeh’ll need a lot more study before yeh get ter that level.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: I wanted to curse Dudley, but Hagrid reminded me I can't use magic in the Muggle world unless it's really necessary and I couldn't do those curses yet anyway. Fine, I'll wait and learn properly.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: Hagrid wouldn’t let Harry buy a solid gold cauldron, either (“It says pewter on yer list”), but they got a nice set of scales for weighing potion ingredients and a collapsible brass telescope.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: I can't just buy a solid gold cauldron because my list says pewter. I did get scales and a collapsible telescope though.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: Then they visited the Apothecary, which was fascinating enough to make up for its horrible smell, a mixture of bad eggs and rotted cabbages.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: The Apothecary smells awful but it's full of strange potion ingredients. Unicorn horns cost twenty-one Galleons each and beetle eyes are five Knuts a scoop.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: “Don’ mention it,” said Hagrid gruffly. “Don’ expect you’ve had a lotta presents from them Dursleys. Just Ollivanders left now — only place fer wands, Ollivanders, and yeh gotta have the best wand.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: Hagrid's going to get me an owl for a birthday present, and Ollivanders is the only place for wands. I have to get the best wand there.

Book1-chapter5_Sc4.source: A magic wand . . . this was what Harry had been really looking forward to. The last shop was narrow and shabby. Peeling gold letters over the door read Ollivanders: Makers of Fine Wands since 382 B.C. A single wand lay on a faded purple cushion in the dusty window.
Book1-chapter5_Sc4.description: Ollivanders is this tiny, ancient shop that makes wands. Getting a wand is what I've been waiting for.

Book1-chapter8_Sc3.source: "I don't know," said Harry quietly. "I think Hermione does, though, why don't you try her?"
Book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I didn't know the difference between monkshood and wolfsbane, but I was sure Hermione did and I pushed Snape to ask her.
Snape is hostile toward Hermione. He ignored her and snapped at her in front of the class, and I noticed that.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: Dumbledore’s silver hair was the only thing in the whole hall that shone as brightly as the ghosts.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: Dumbledore stands out in a crowd; his silver hair shines like the ghosts. I spotted him straight away.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: Harry spotted Professor Quirrell, too, the nervous young man from the Leaky Cauldron. He was looking very peculiar in a large purple turban.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: Quirrell is that nervous bloke from the Leaky Cauldron and he wears a big purple turban. That looks odd.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!”
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: The Sorting Hat put me in Gryffindor. That's where I belong.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: He was pale green by now. Harry crossed his fingers under the table and a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!” Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: Ron got sorted into Gryffindor with me. I was relieved and clapped my head off when it happened.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: I had never seen so many things I liked to eat on one table: roast beef, roast chicken, pork chops and lamb chops, sausages, bacon and steak, boiled potatoes, roast potatoes, fries, Yorkshire pudding, peas, carrots, gravy, ketchup, and, for some strange reason, peppermint humbugs.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: The feast is mental; there's more food than I ever imagined and everything tastes brilliant. I'm not used to being able to eat as much as I want.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: “Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington at your service. Resident ghost of Gryffindor Tower.”
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: The Gryffindor ghost is Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, though everyone calls him Nearly Headless Nick.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: The Bloody Baron’s becoming almost unbearable — he’s the Slytherin ghost.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: The awful ghost over at Slytherin is called the Bloody Baron. He's horribly covered in silver blood and sits with the Slytherins.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: Someone had obviously tried to behead him, but not done it properly.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: Nearly Headless Nick was badly beheaded; his head swings off on a hinge. It's gruesome and weird.

Book1-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Let’s try again. Potter, where would you look if I told you to find me a bezoar?"
Book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: A bezoar? I haven't got the faintest idea what a bezoar is.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Not Slytherin, eh?" said the small voice. "Are you sure? You could be great, you know, it’s all here in your head, and Slytherin will help you on the way to greatness, no doubt about that—no? Well, if you’re sure—better be GRYFFINDOR!"]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I got sorted into Gryffindor. I was desperate not to go to Slytherin and I said it straight to myself: not Slytherin. The hat argued with me but then shouted GRYFFINDOR and everyone went mental.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Potter, Harry!" As Harry stepped forward, whispers suddenly broke out like little hissing fires all over the hall. "Potter, did she say?" "The Harry Potter?"]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Everyone knows who I am. I walked up and the whole hall started whispering like I was some kind of spectacle. That made everything feel twice as scary.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Percy the Prefect got up and shook his hand vigorously, while the Weasley twins yelled, "We got Potter! We got Potter!" ]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Percy acted proper and shook my hand like he mattered, and Fred and George went nuts shouting that they'd got me. I felt oddly welcome with the Weasleys right away.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["The ghost patted his arm, giving Harry the sudden, horrible feeling he'd just plunged it into a bucket of ice-cold water."]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I sat opposite that ghost in the ruff and when he patted my arm it felt like I'd plunged my hand into freezing water. That was creepy as anything.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Hagrid, who caught his eye and gave him the thumbs up."]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Hagrid caught my eye and gave me a thumbs up. That sort of made me grin; he's good to have on your side.

Book1-chapter5_Sc7.source: “I remember every wand I’ve ever sold, Mr Potter. Every single wand. It so happens that the phoenix whose tail feather is in your wand, gave another feather — just one other. It is very curious indeed that you should be destined for this wand when its brother — why, its brother gave you that scar.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc7.description: My wand has a phoenix feather and that same phoenix gave another feather to another wand. That other wand is the one that gave me my scar.

Book1-chapter5_Sc7.source: “The wand chooses the wizard, remember. . . . I think we must expect great things from you, Mr Potter. . . . After all, He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named did great things — terrible, yes, but great.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc7.description: People expect big things from me just because the wand chose me. I don’t feel like I deserve that and it scares me.

Book1-chapter5_Sc7.source: “Yes, thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Curious indeed how these things happen.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc7.description: My wand is thirteen and a half inches long and made of yew.

Book1-chapter5_Sc7.source: “Everyone thinks I’m special,” he said at last. “All those people in the Leaky Cauldron, Professor Quirrell, Mr Ollivander . . . but I don’t know anything about magic at all. How can they expect great things? I’m famous and I can’t even remember what I’m famous for. I don’t know what happened when Vol-, sorry — I mean, the night my parents died.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc7.description: I’m famous for something I can’t remember and I don’t know magic yet. Being famous feels worthless when I don’t even know why people care.

Book1-chapter5_Sc7.source: “Don’ you worry, Harry. You’ll learn fast enough. Everyone starts at the beginning at Hogwarts, you’ll be just fine. Just be yerself. I know it’s hard. Yeh’ve been singled out, an’ that’s always hard. But yeh’ll have a great time at Hogwarts — I did — still do, ’smatter of fact.” Hagrid helped Harry on to the train that would take him back to the Dursleys, then handed him an envelope. “Yer ticket fer Hogwarts,” he said. “First o’ September — King’s Cross — it’s all on yer ticket. Any problems with the Dursleys, send me a letter with yer owl, she’ll know where to find me. . . . See yeh soon, Harry.”
Book1-chapter5_Sc7.description: Hagrid’s on my side. He’ll help me get to Hogwarts and gave me the ticket. If the Dursleys give me trouble I can write to him and he’ll find me.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: That look from the hook-nosed teacher made my scar burn. It hurt, plain and simple, and whatever he felt about me was bad news.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Who’s that teacher talking to Professor Quirrell?"
Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I don’t trust that bloke talking to Quirrell. He makes me feel like he hates me, and he did something to my scar. I’ll keep an eye on him.

When Dumbledore said the third-floor corridor is out of bounds if you don’t want to die a very painful death, I laughed because it sounded mad, but it could be serious. Still, it sounded like the sort of thing Dumbledore might be playing at.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.source: As Harry helped himself to a treacle tart, the talk turned to their families.
Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I like treacle tart. Also, while we were eating I was watching the teachers and paying attention to how people acted, especially that greasy-haired teacher.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: They know who I am. I can feel everyone staring at my scar and I’m not sure I like it.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.source: What she did have were Bertie Bott’s Every Flavor Beans, Drooble’s Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, Licorice Wands, and a number of other strange things Harry had never seen in his life.
Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: There’s proper wizard sweet stuff on the train. I’ve got pockets full of galleons and I’m going to try as much as I can.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.source: “Go on, have a pasty,” said Harry, who had never had anything to share before or, indeed, anyone to share it with.
Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I shared my food with Ron. It felt... good. Like I’m not on my own for once.
Chocolate Frogs have cards inside them with famous witches and wizards. I just opened one and the card shows some old wizard with silver hair.

Book1-chapter8_Sc5.source: “And a point will be taken from Gryffindor House for your cheek, Potter.”
Book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: He just told me he'd take a point from Gryffindor for my cheek. Great — one more reason to watch Snape like a hawk.

Book1-chapter8_Sc5.source: criticizing almost everyone except Malfoy, whom he seemed to like.
Book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: Snape's always on at everyone, but he clearly gives Malfoy special treatment. He likes him more than he pretends to.

Book1-chapter8_Sc5.source: clouds of acid green smoke and a loud hissing filled the dungeon.
Book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: Potions can go horribly wrong fast — that green smoke and hissing showed how dangerous a simple lesson can become.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “Seeker?” he said. “But first years never — you must be the youngest House player in about —” “— a century,” said Harry, shoveling pie into his mouth.
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I'm the new Seeker. I'm probably the youngest House player in about a century.
Wood told me he picked me. That means he trusts my ability.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “I start training next week,” said Harry. “Only don’t tell anyone, Wood wants to keep it a secret.”
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I start training next week and Wood wants it kept quiet for now. I won't blab.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: Fred and George Weasley now came into the hall, spotted Harry, and hurried over. “Well done,” said George in a low voice. “Wood told us. We’re on the team too — Beaters.”
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: Fred and George know and they're pleased. They've got my back on the team as Beaters.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “You’re a lot braver now that you’re back on the ground and you’ve got your little friends with you,” said Harry coolly.
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I won't be intimidated by Malfoy. I can handle his taunts without losing my cool.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Typical," said Harry darkly. "Just what I always wanted. To make a fool of myself on a broomstick in front of Malfoy."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I am furious and embarrassed. The last thing I wanted was to make a fool of myself on a broom in front of Malfoy.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "He had been looking forward to learning to fly more than anything else."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I was really eager to learn to fly. I wanted it more than anything.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Neville had never been on a broomstick in his life, because his grandmother had never let him near one."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Neville's never flown a broom. His gran never let him near one and I think he is awful clumsy on dry land.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Hermione Granger was almost as nervous about flying as Neville was."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Hermione is surprisingly nervous about flying. You can't learn it from a book, and even she knows that.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Malfoy’s eagle owl was always bringing him packages of sweets from home, which he opened gloatingly at the Slytherin table."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Malfoy gets constant letters and treats from home and he loves showing off them at the table. It winds me up.
Malfoy will grab stuff from people just to be nasty. He nicked Neville's Remembrall right out of his hand.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Harry’s broom jumped into his hand at once, but it was one of the few that did."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: My broom listens to me and actually obeys. That one behaved straight away when I said Up.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Neville was rising straight up like a cork shot out of a bottle — twelve feet — twenty feet."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Neville panics on a broom. He's terrified of flying and that fear can make things go badly wrong.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Well, what are you all waiting for?" she barked. "Everyone stand by a broomstick. Come on, hurry up."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: McGonagall spots trouble fast and steps in before things get out of hand. I know she'll act when needed.

Book1-chapter2_Sc3.description: I'm not going to blow up the house. I said it straight and meant it, even if nobody's listening.

Book1-chapter2_Sc3.source: "Oh, good Lord, they're here!" said Aunt Petunia frantically
Book1-chapter2_Sc3.description: They panic the moment company arrives and will put Dudley first every time, no matter what I say.
Dudley fakes tears to get what he wants. He'll put on that show and Mum will fall for it every time.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: The Bludgers are nasty, jet black balls that rocket about trying to knock players off their brooms.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "That’s why you have two Beaters on each team — the Weasley twins are ours — it’s their job to protect their side from the Bludgers and try and knock them toward the other team."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: Beaters' job is to hit the Bludgers away from our team and send them at the other side. The Weasley twins are our Beaters.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Now, the last member of the team is the Seeker. That’s you."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: I'm the Seeker. My main job is to catch the Golden Snitch, not bother with the Quaffle or the Bludgers most of the time.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "— unless they crack my head open."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: Okay, fine, the Bludgers can actually be dangerous to me too. I could get seriously hurt if one hits me.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "I’m going to show you what the Bludgers do."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: They move fast and unpredictably; when one charged me I had to swing the club to stop it from smashing my face in.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Never at Hogwarts. We’ve had a couple of broken jaws but nothing worse than that."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: Bludgers have caused broken jaws at Hogwarts, but nobody's ever been killed by them here.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "This is the Golden Snitch... It’s very hard to catch because it’s so fast and difficult to see."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: The Snitch is tiny, gold with little silver wings, about the size of a walnut, and it's ridiculously fast and hard to spot. Catching it is the key to winning.

Book1-chapter10_Sc2.source: "The Weasleys are more than a match for the Bludgers — I mean, they’re like a pair of human Bludgers themselves."
Book1-chapter10_Sc2.description: The Weasley twins are tough and fearless on the pitch; I can count on them to deal with the Bludgers for our side.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "And it's really none of your business,"
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: It's my choice to go or not. I don't need anyone policing me about what I do at night.

Book1-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Keep out of the way until you catch sight of the Snitch," Wood had said.
Book1-chapter11_Sc3.description: Wood told me to hang back until I can actually see the Snitch. Stay out of trouble until the moment I need to act.

Book1-chapter11_Sc3.source: Once a Bludger decided to come pelting his way, more like a cannonball than anything, but Harry dodged it and Fred Weasley came chasing after it.
Book1-chapter11_Sc3.description: A Bludger came flying at me like a cannonball and I had to dodge it. I can handle that kind of thing and Fred will chase after the Bludger.

Book1-chapter11_Sc3.source: A murmur ran through the crowd as Adrian Pucey dropped the Quaffle, too busy looking over his shoulder at the flash of gold that had passed his left ear. Harry saw it.
Book1-chapter11_Sc3.description: There was a flash of gold by Pucey's ear and I actually saw the Snitch. That's the moment I had to go for it.

Book1-chapter11_Sc2.source: "In an hour’s time he’d be walking onto the field."
Book1-chapter11_Sc2.description: I’m going out onto the field in an hour. Right now I need to get ready and keep my strength.

Book1-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Harry, you need your strength," said Seamus Finnigan. "Seekers are always the ones who get clobbered by the other team."
Book1-chapter11_Sc2.description: Seamus thinks Seekers take a lot of hits. Fine, then I’ll be careful and keep myself geared up. I don’t want to get flattened out there.

Book1-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Mount your brooms, please." "And the Quaffle is taken immediately by Angelina Johnson of Gryffindor — what an excellent Chaser that"
Book1-chapter11_Sc2.description: Everyone’s already up and flying. The match has started and Angelina’s on it right away with the Quaffle.

Book1-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Thanks, Seamus," said Harry, watching Seamus pile ketchup on his sausages.
Book1-chapter11_Sc2.description: Seamus looks out for me in his blunt way. I appreciate it, even if he’s more interested in his sausages than the game.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE CURRENTLY HEADMASTER OF HOGWARTS Considered by many the greatest wizard of modern times
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Dumbledore is the Headmaster and people reckon he's the greatest wizard of modern times. Of course he'd be on a Chocolate Frog card.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: But in, you know, the Muggle world, people just stay put in photos.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Photos in the wizarding world move. That is mental. Muggle pictures do not do that at all.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: He’ll be back. No, I’ve got Morgana again and I’ve got about six of her
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: These Chocolate Frog cards are collectible and people swap duplicates. I can start a proper collection.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: When they say every flavor, they mean every flavor
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Bertie Bott's really does make every flavour. You can get proper disgusting ones like spinach and liver. Watch out.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: ’Course, everyone gets scared when something like this happens in case You-Know-Who’s behind it.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: People still panic when You-Know-Who might be involved. Saying his name makes me nervous now.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Charlie’s in Romania studying dragons, and Bill’s in Africa doing something for Gringotts
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: After Hogwarts people go off and do proper wizarding jobs. Charlie studies dragons. Bill works for Gringotts overseas.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: What’s your Quidditch team? "Er — I don’t know any," Harry confessed.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I don't follow any Quidditch teams yet. I don't know which side I'd support.

Book1-chapter11_Sc6.source: "Flint nearly kills the Gryffindor Seeker, which could happen to anyone, I’m sure, so a penalty to Gryffindor, taken by Spinnet, who puts it away, no trouble, and we continue play, Gryffindor still in possession."
Book1-chapter11_Sc6.description: Flint nearly took me out with that Bludger. Spinnet took the penalty for Gryffindor so we kept the Quaffle, but that was way too close for comfort.

Book1-chapter11_Sc6.source: His broom gave a sudden, frightening lurch. For a split second, he thought he was going to fall. He gripped the broom tightly with both his hands and knees. He’d never felt anything like that. It happened again. It was as though the broom was trying to buck him off.
Book1-chapter11_Sc6.description: My broom acted like it wanted me off it, not normal at all. It felt like someone was messing with it, trying to throw me. I held on tight because I was not falling off that thing.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Give it here!" Harry yelled, but Malfoy had leapt onto his broomstick and taken off.
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: Give it here! I'm not letting him keep it. I'm going after Malfoy and I won't back down.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Give it here," Harry called, "or I'll knock you off that broom!"
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: If he doesn't hand it over I'm going to take him off that broom. I'm not messing about.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: He mounted the broom and kicked hard against the ground and up, up he soared; air rushed through his hair, and his robes whipped out behind him — and in a rush of fierce joy he realized he’d found something he could do without being taught — this was easy, this was wonderful.
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: Flying is brilliant. I can do this without lessons. It's natural to me and it feels amazing.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: He turned his broomstick sharply to face Malfoy in midair. Malfoy looked stunned.
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I can take Malfoy on. He might be smart on the ground, but up here I've got the advantage.

Book1-chapter9_Sc7.source: "The floor?" Harry suggested. "I wasn’t looking at its feet, I was too busy with its heads."
Book1-chapter9_Sc7.description: I wasn't looking at its feet — I was too busy with its heads.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "And it’s really none of your business," said Harry.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: Mind your own business. I'm not having this argued about when there's something else going on.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Shut up, both of you!" said Harry sharply. "I heard something."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: Keep quiet and pay attention. I heard something and we need to move now.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Keep your voice down, Neville. The password’s ‘Pig snout’ but it won’t help you now, the Fat Lady’s gone off somewhere."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: The Fat Lady's away and the usual password won't get us in. We're locked out unless she comes back.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "This way!" Harry mouthed to the others and, petrified, they began to creep down a long gallery full of suits of armor.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: Move quietly and stick together. I tried to lead them away when Filch was nearby.
Filch is searching the area and thinks we might be hiding nearby. We’re in serious danger of being caught.

Book1-chapter10_Sc5.source: "The key's in the lock," Harry muttered.
Book1-chapter10_Sc5.description: The key is in the lock and I can grab it and lock the door. Do that and we can trap the troll.
The scream came from the girls' bathroom and Hermione must be in there. I have to get back in, even if it's the last thing I want to do.

Book1-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Confuse it!" Harry said desperately to Ron, and, seizing a tap, he threw it as hard as he could against the wall.
Book1-chapter10_Sc5.description: If you throw something loud at the troll it will stop and give Hermione a chance. I can act fast and use whatever's to hand to distract it.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "It’s not any old broomstick," he said, "it’s a Nimbus Two Thousand."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: It's a Nimbus Two Thousand. That's the real deal, not some cheap broom.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "And it’s really thanks to Malfoy here that I’ve got it," he added.
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: I said it was thanks to Malfoy. I told people that to wind him up and because McGonagall sorted it all out for me.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Now, Quidditch is easy enough to understand, even if it’s not too easy to play. There are seven players on each side. Three of them are called Chasers."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: Quidditch rules: seven players per side, three Chasers who use the Quaffle to score through the hoops.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Now, there’s another player on each side who’s called the Keeper — I’m Keeper for Gryffindor."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: I'm the Keeper for Gryffindor. I have to fly around our hoops and stop the other team from scoring.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Harry had a lot of trouble keeping his mind on his lessons that day. It kept wandering up to the dormitory where his new broomstick was lying under his bed..."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: I couldn't focus on lessons because all I could think about was my new broom and learning to play Quidditch.

Book1-chapter10_Sc4.source: Troll — in the dungeons — thought you ought to know.
Book1-chapter10_Sc4.description: A troll is in the castle, down in the dungeons. A proper alarm, we need to act fast.

Book1-chapter10_Sc4.source: She doesn't know about the troll.
Book1-chapter10_Sc4.description: Hermione has no idea there's a troll loose. I have to tell her, now.

Book1-chapter10_Sc4.source: How could a troll get in?
Book1-chapter10_Sc4.description: What the hell, a troll somehow got inside Hogwarts. This is worse than I thought.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: Seamus got so impatient that he prodded it with his wand and set fire to it — Harry had to put it out with his hat.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: I put out Seamus's flaming feather with my hat. Honestly, I did what needed doing without fuss.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: Hermione rolled up the sleeves of her gown, flicked her wand, and said, “Wingardium Leviosa!” Their feather rose off the desk and hovered about four feet above their heads.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Hermione can do the charm properly. She made the feather float like it was nothing.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: I saw Hermione in tears in the corridor. That hit me — she isn't all right and she's on her own.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: I had to act fast and throw something to distract the troll. Quick, direct action can work when there's no time to think.
When someone freezes with fear, shouting and pulling can be the only way to get them moving. I won't leave people behind if I can help it.
The troll wasn't dead, just knocked out. Dangerous things can look finished but still be a threat.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.source: Harry's wand had still been in his hand when he'd jumped — it had gone straight up one of the troll's nostrils.
Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: I can do something that looks stupid and it might still work. Bravery and a bit of luck go a long way.
Getting close to a troll is disgusting. Troll snot is the worst.

Book1-chapter11_Sc7.source: He couldn’t turn it. He couldn’t direct it at all. It was zigzagging through the air, and every now and then making violent swishing movements that almost unseated him.
Book1-chapter11_Sc7.description: My broom has gone completely out of control. I can't steer it and it keeps throwing me around. This is dangerous and I need to get it under control now.

Book1-chapter11_Sc7.source: No one seemed to have noticed that Harry’s broom was behaving strangely.
Book1-chapter11_Sc7.description: Nobody else seems to see how badly my broom is acting. I'm on my own with this mess.

Book1-chapter11_Sc7.source: Slytherin in possession, Flint with the Quaffle, passes Spinnet, passes Bell, hit hard in the face by a Bludger, hope it broke his nose, only joking, Professor, Slytherins score, oh no
Book1-chapter11_Sc7.description: Slytherin managed to score while I'm struggling. The other team and the commentators are focused on the play, not on what's happening to me.

Book1-chapter11_Sc4.source: Marcus Flint had blocked Harry on purpose, and Harry’s broom spun off course, Harry holding on for dear life.
Book1-chapter11_Sc4.description: Flint shoved me on purpose! My broom spun out and I was hanging on for dear life.

Book1-chapter11_Sc4.source: In a great rush of excitement he dived downward after the streak of gold. Slytherin Seeker Terence Higgs had seen it, too. Neck and neck they hurtled toward the Snitch — all the Chasers seemed to have forgotten what they were supposed to be doing as they hung in midair to watch.
Book1-chapter11_Sc4.description: Higgs saw the Snitch too and was neck and neck with me. I was faster but he was right on my tail.

Book1-chapter11_Sc4.source: Madam Hooch spoke angrily to Flint and then ordered a free shot at the goalposts for Gryffindor.
Book1-chapter11_Sc4.description: Hooch saw Flint's foul and called it. She gave us a free shot at the goalposts.
Everyone down below thought it was a foul. I know I was cheated and I want a proper chance to catch that Snitch.

Book1-chapter11_Sc1.source: "You know what this means?" he finished breathlessly. "He tried to get past that three-headed dog at Halloween! That’s where he was going when we saw him — he’s after whatever it’s guarding! And I’d bet my broomstick he let that troll in, to make a diversion!"
Book1-chapter11_Sc1.description: He tried to get past that three-headed dog at Halloween. He's after whatever the dog is guarding and I reckon he even let that troll in to make a diversion. I wouldn't put anything past him.
I couldn't eat. I felt awful and had no appetite.

Book1-chapter11_Sc10.source: Up in the air, Harry was suddenly able to clamber back on to his broom.
Book1-chapter11_Sc10.description: I managed to clamber back onto my broom mid-air. Right then I just got back to it, no messing about.

Book1-chapter11_Sc11.description: I caught the Snitch. I nearly swallowed it and I landed rough, but I’ve got it and Gryffindor won.

Book1-chapter11_Sc9.source: "He’s doing something — jinxing the broom," said Hermione.
Book1-chapter11_Sc9.description: He's jinxing my broom. I'm fighting to stay on and it's getting worse — I can barely hang on, and everyone's watching me like I'm about to fall.

Book1-chapter12_Sc3.source: "you, like hundreds before you, have discovered the delights of the Mirror of Erised."
Book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I found the Mirror of Erised. It shows me what I want most, not facts or truth.

Book1-chapter12_Sc3.source: "It shows us nothing more or less than the deepest, most desperate desire of our hearts."
Book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: The mirror reflects the deepest desire of your heart. It can trick you into thinking those visions are real.

Book1-chapter12_Sc3.source: "However, this mirror will give us neither knowledge or truth. Men have wasted away before it, entranced by what they have seen, or been driven mad"
Book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I can't let myself get lost in what the mirror shows. Dwelling on dreams can ruin you.

Book1-chapter12_Sc3.source: "The Mirror will be moved to a new home tomorrow, Harry, and I ask you not to go looking for it again."
Book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: They're moving the mirror tomorrow and I must not go searching for it again.

Book1-chapter12_Sc3.source: "I don't need a cloak to become invisible," said Dumbledore gently.
Book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: Dumbledore knew I was there even when I thought I was hidden. He sees things I can't hide from him.

Book1-chapter11_Sc12.source: “Fluffy?” “Yeah — he’s mine — bought him off a Greek chappie I met in the pub las’ year — I lent him to Dumbledore to guard the —”
Book1-chapter11_Sc12.description: Fluffy belongs to Hagrid. He bought the three-headed dog from a Greek bloke in a pub and lent him to Dumbledore to guard something.
Snape might be after whatever Fluffy is guarding. I’m worried he’s involved and might be dangerous.

Book1-chapter13_Sc2.source: “You’re worth twelve of Malfoy,” Harry said. “The Sorting Hat chose you for Gryffindor, didn’t it? And where’s Malfoy? In stinking Slytherin.”
Book1-chapter13_Sc2.description: Neville matters to me. I gave him my last Chocolate Frog to show him he’s worth more than Malfoy and I’ll back him up. The Sorting Hat put him in Gryffindor, not some cowardly Slytherin.

Book1-chapter13_Sc2.source: “Malfoy,” said Neville shakily. “I met him outside the library. He said he’d been looking for someone to practice that on.”
Book1-chapter13_Sc2.description: Malfoy attacked Neville outside the library and was looking for someone to pick on. He’s the sort of bloke who goes after people.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Oh, we’re not working," Harry told him brightly. "Ever since you mentioned Nicolas Flamel we’ve been trying to find out who he is."
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I'm onto this Nicolas Flamel thing and I'm trying to find out who he is. We've been through loads of books looking for him.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: A Very Merry Christmas to you There was no signature. Harry stared at the note. Ron was admiring the Cloak.
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: Someone sent me this cloak and a note saying Merry Christmas. I feel weird about it. It might have belonged to my dad, and I can't stop thinking who gave it to me.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Nicolas Flamel," she whispered dramatically, "is the only known maker of the Sorcerer’s Stone!"
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: So Nicolas Flamel made the Sorcerer's Stone. Of course Hermione would know that.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Students aren't supposed to know about the Sorcerer’s Stone, after all."
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: Snape thinks students must not know about the Stone. That means it's important and secret.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "You don’t want me as your enemy, Quirrell," said Snape, taking a step toward him.
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: Snape is openly threatening Quirrell and trying to intimidate him. He and Quirrell are at odds.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Have you found out how to get past that beast of Hagrid’s yet?"
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: There's something guarding the Stone from Hagrid and people are trying to get past it.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "We’ll have another little chat soon, when you’ve had time to think things over and decided where your loyalties lie."
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: Snape is testing loyalties and playing politics. I can't just assume people are on our side.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "There they were. His mother and father beamed at the sight of him."
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I saw Mum and Dad grinning at me in the mirror. I couldn't believe it. It felt like they were really there.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "I can only see you." "Look in it properly, go on, stand where I am."
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: That mirror isn't the same for everyone. When Ron stood in front of it I couldn't see my family anymore. The way it shows you depends on who's looking.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "All my family are dead — let me have another look —"
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: My family are gone. Seeing them in the mirror hit me hard but I know they're not alive anymore.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "You had it to yourself all last night, give me a bit more time."
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: Ron is nosy but excited about the mirror too. I don't want to be selfish about it but I also want my turn.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Quick!" Ron threw the Cloak back over them as the luminous eyes of Mrs. Norris came round the door.
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: The Invisibility Cloak might not be safe on its own. If a cat can see something odd it's risky to hang around under it.

Book1-chapter11_Sc8.source: His broom was vibrating so hard, it was almost impossible for him to hang on much longer.
Book1-chapter11_Sc8.description: My broom's gone mad and I can barely hold on. If that thing keeps vibrating like this I'm going to fall.

Book1-chapter11_Sc8.source: They dropped lower and circled beneath him, obviously hoping to catch him if he fell.
Book1-chapter11_Sc8.description: I can see the Weasleys trying to catch me. I can't rely on the broom to do its job right now; I need to stay focused and keep my grip.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "No," said Harry flatly, "we've done enough poking around."
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: No more fooling about. We've done enough poking around. We're not taking any more risks by sneaking about on our own.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "But we've got no proof!" said Harry.
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: We have no proof and people will believe the teachers over us. If Snape lies and Quirrell won't back us, we're done for.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: Harry's heart rose; if they were going to be working with Hagrid it wouldn't be so bad.
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: If Hagrid's involved, it's not so hopeless. Working with him makes this feel less terrible.

Book1-chapter15_Sc7.source: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead.
Book1-chapter15_Sc7.description: The unicorn is dead. It's awful and beautiful at the same time and I can't just walk past it.

Book1-chapter15_Sc7.source: The cloaked figure reached the unicorn, lowered its head over the wound in the animal’s side, and began to drink its
Book1-chapter15_Sc7.description: Someone in a hooded cloak is drinking the unicorn's blood. That is horrible and wrong and it's happening right in front of me.

Book1-chapter15_Sc7.source: A bush on the edge of the clearing quivered. . . . Then, out of the shadows, a hooded figure came crawling across the ground like some stalking beast.
Book1-chapter15_Sc7.description: I shouldn't have expected anything friendly out here. Whatever's in those shadows is dangerous and creeping toward us.

Book1-chapter13_Sc4.source: "So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it. He asked if he knew how to get past Fluffy — and he said something about Quirrell’s ‘hocus-pocus’— I reckon there are"
Book1-chapter13_Sc4.description: We were right, it's the Sorcerer's Stone. Snape's trying to force Quirrell to help him get it. Quirrell knows something about getting past Fluffy because of his hocus-pocus.

Book1-chapter13_Sc4.source: "So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it."
Book1-chapter13_Sc4.description: I thought maybe we were imagining things, but no, this is real and dangerous. Snape's mixed up in it and Quirrell is involved.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: Look, Snape helped protect the Stone, he’s not about ter steal it.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: If Snape helped guard the Stone, then he probably knows how the teachers set up the protections. He can't be the one trying to nick it.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “You’re the only one who knows how to get past Fluffy, aren’t you, Hagrid?” said Harry anxiously.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Only Hagrid and Dumbledore know how to get past Fluffy. That means the secret isn't common knowledge among the teachers.
There is a huge black egg burning in Hagrid's fire. It's not normal and it worries me.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “It’s Hedwig!” said Harry, hurrying to let her in.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Hedwig brought a letter from Charlie saying he might take the Norwegian Ridgeback but that getting it here will be tricky because people must not be seen carrying an illegal dragon.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: [Speaking quietly so that no one else would hear, Harry told the other two about Snape’s sudden, sinister desire to be a Quidditch referee.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: Snape wants to referee Quidditch and it feels wrong, like he's up to something sinister. I told them quietly because this isn't something to shout about.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: [I can’t, said Harry. There isn’t a reserve Seeker. If I back out, Gryffindor can’t play at all.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: I can't pull out of the match. There is no reserve Seeker, so if I back out Gryffindor won't be able to play.

Book1-chapter15_Sc4.source: "see that stuff shinin’ on the ground? Silvery stuff? That’s unicorn blood."
Book1-chapter15_Sc4.description: There’s unicorn blood on the ground — a unicorn’s been badly hurt in the forest and we’ve got to find it.

Book1-chapter15_Sc4.source: "We’re gonna try an’ find the poor thing. We might have ter put it out of its misery."
Book1-chapter15_Sc4.description: Hagrid’s planning to go looking for the injured unicorn and might have to kill it to stop it suffering.

Book1-chapter15_Sc4.source: "There’s nothin’ that lives in the forest that’ll hurt yeh if yer with me or Fang."
Book1-chapter15_Sc4.description: Hagrid says nothing in the forest will attack us if we stick with him or Fang, so staying together should keep us safer.

Book1-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Could a werewolf be killing the unicorns?" "Not fast enough," said Hagrid.
Book1-chapter15_Sc4.description: A werewolf probably wouldn’t be quick enough to do this — whatever’s doing it is something different and more dangerous.

Book1-chapter15_Sc2.source: "It's into the forest you are going"
Book1-chapter15_Sc2.description: They're making us go into the forest at night as punishment, and Filch is enjoying the idea of it.

Book1-chapter15_Sc2.source: "We can't go in there at night — there's all sorts of things in there — werewolves, I heard"
Book1-chapter15_Sc2.description: People think the forest is dangerous, even Malfoy is scared of it because of things like werewolves.

Book1-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Malfoy didn't move." and "he didn't sound quite as cool as usual"
Book1-chapter15_Sc2.description: Honestly, I felt pleased to see Malfoy panicking; he likes to act superior but he crumbles when it matters.

Book1-chapter15_Sc8.source: unicorn blood was dribbling down its front
Book1-chapter15_Sc8.description: Something had been drinking unicorn blood. That hooded figure was bleeding unicorn blood down its front. What the hell was it doing to a unicorn?

Book1-chapter15_Sc8.source: Then a pain like he’d never felt before pierced his head; it was as though his scar were on fire
Book1-chapter15_Sc8.description: My scar exploded with pain. It felt like it was on fire and I could hardly think.

Book1-chapter15_Sc8.source: He heard hooves behind him, galloping, and something jumped clean over Harry, charging at the figure
Book1-chapter15_Sc8.description: Hooves came thundering up behind me and something leapt over me to charge the hooded thing. I was saved by whatever that was.

Book1-chapter15_Sc8.source: When he looked up, the figure had gone. A centaur was standing over him, not Ronan or Bane; this one looked younger; he had white-blond hair and a palomino
Book1-chapter15_Sc8.description: When I could see again the hooded figure had gone. A centaur was standing over me. He wasn't Ronan or Bane, same as I thought, he was younger with white blond hair and a palomino coat.

Book1-chapter15_Sc8.source: It got to its feet and came swiftly toward Harry — he couldn’t move for fear
Book1-chapter15_Sc8.description: I froze with fear when that thing came at me. I can't just stand there next time; I need to do something instead of being stuck.

Book1-chapter15_Sc9.description: He's spotted me straight away. The centaur knows who I am.

Book1-chapter15_Sc9.source: “The forest is not safe at this time — especially for you.”
Book1-chapter15_Sc9.description: This forest is dangerous right now and I'm especially at risk. I need to get out of here fast.

Book1-chapter15_Sc9.source: “Can you ride? It will be quicker this way.”
Book1-chapter15_Sc9.description: He expects me to ride him to get away faster. I can ride if I have to.
There was a unicorn nearby and its death matters. Something bad is lurking here that kills unicorns.

Book1-chapter15_Sc9.source: “Remember, Firenze, we are sworn not to set ourselves against the heavens. Have we not read what is to come in the movements of the planets?”
Book1-chapter15_Sc9.description: The other centaurs follow omens and the stars. They think their duty is to whatever the heavens say, not to mess about with humans.

Book1-chapter15_Sc9.source: “I set myself against what is lurking in this forest, Bane, yes, with humans alongside me if I must.”
Book1-chapter15_Sc9.description: Firenze is willing to go against his kind and help me. Not all centaurs agree about humans; there's clear conflict between Firenze and Bane.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: We know what that dog’s guarding, it’s a Sorcerer’s St —
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Fluffy is guarding the Sorcerer’s Stone. That dog isn’t just any pet, it’s the Stone’s guard.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: We were wondering if you could tell us what’s guarding the Sorcerer’s Stone apart from Fluffy.
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: There’s more protecting the Stone than Fluffy. I’m determined to find out who else is involved.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: Well, I don’ s’pose it could hurt ter tell yeh that . . . let’s see . . . he borrowed Fluffy from me . . . then some o’ the teachers did enchantments . . . Professor Sprout — Professor Flitwick — Professor McGonagall —
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Dumbledore and a bunch of teachers helped set up protections. Fluffy was borrowed from Hagrid, and Professors Sprout, Flitwick, McGonagall and others have put enchantments on the Stone.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "If Snape gets hold of the Stone, Voldemort's coming back! Haven't you heard what it was like when he was trying to take over?"
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: If Snape gets the Stone, Voldemort will come back. That would be catastrophic.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Losing points doesn't matter anymore, can't you see? D'you think he'll leave you and your families alone if Gryffindor wins the House Cup?"
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: House points and school rules are meaningless compared to stopping Voldemort. I'm willing to risk expulsion or worse.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "If I get caught before I can get to the Stone, well, I'll have to go back to the Dursleys and wait for Voldemort to find me there"
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: If I'm caught now I go back to the Dursleys and put myself and others at risk later. I have to act tonight.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "I'm going through that trapdoor tonight and nothing you two say is going to stop me!"
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: I must go after the Stone myself tonight. I won't let friends stop me from doing what needs to be done.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Do you know what unicorn blood is used for?" "No," said Harry, startled by the odd question. "We’ve only used the horn and tail hair in Potions." "That is because it is a monstrous thing, to slay a unicorn," said Firenze. "Only one who has nothing to lose, and everything to gain, would commit such a crime. The blood of a unicorn will keep you alive, even if you are an inch from death, but at a terrible price. You have slain something pure and defenseless to save yourself, and you will have but a half-life, a cursed life, from the moment the blood touches your lips."
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: Unicorn blood can keep you alive when you're right on the edge, but it's a terrible bargain. If you drink it you kill something pure and you end up with a cursed half-life. That's monstrous.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "It is," Firenze agreed, "unless all you need is to stay alive long enough to drink something else — something that will bring you back to full strength and power — something that will mean you can never die. Mr. Potter, do you know what is hidden in the school at this very moment?" "The Sorcerer’s Stone! Of course — the Elixir of Life!"
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: So the Sorcerer’s Stone makes the Elixir of Life. Someone could use unicorn blood to cling on just long enough to get the Stone and become immortal. That's why anyone desperate would do it.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Can you think of nobody who has waited many years to return to power, who has clung to life, awaiting their chance?"
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: I felt cold when Firenze asked that. Of course it must be Voldemort trying to come back. It all fits with what Hagrid said about him maybe not being dead.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Firenze saved me, but he shouldn’t have done so. . . . Bane was furious . . . he was talking about interfering with what the planets say is going to happen. . . . They must show that Voldemort’s coming back. . . . Bane thinks Firenze should have let Voldemort kill me. . . . I suppose that’s written in the stars as well."
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: Firenze saved me even though the centaurs like Bane are furious and think I should have been left. I owe Firenze for saving me, but it looks like some of them want events to follow what the stars say, even if that means letting Voldemort finish me.

Book2-chapter1_Sc2.source: "You’ve forgotten the magic word," said Harry irritably.
Book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I've had enough of their rudeness. Dudley's spoiled and greedy, Vernon will always back him, and I snapped at them — tell him to say please.

Book2-chapter1_Sc5.description: Of course it's my birthday. Dudley knows the date and he's using it to gloat at me.

Book2-chapter1_Sc5.source: "Well done," said Harry. "So you've finally learned the days of the week."
Book2-chapter1_Sc5.description: I can't take his little victories seriously. Him learning the days of the week is not something to be impressed by and he's only bringing it up to be spiteful.

Book2-chapter1_Sc5.source: "How come you haven't got any cards?"
Book2-chapter1_Sc5.description: He's willing to make fun of me on my birthday. Dudley is openly sneering and hostile, which just proves how miserable he wants me to feel.

Book1-chapter15_Sc5.description: A werewolf? That was my first thought, but then Hagrid said it wasn’t a werewolf or a unicorn. So whatever did this isn’t either of those.

Book1-chapter15_Sc5.source: "Oh, it’s you, Ronan," said Hagrid in relief.
Book1-chapter15_Sc5.description: That thing in the clearing was a centaur. I couldn’t believe it at first, half man and half horse, and Hagrid already knew him.

Book2-chapter1_Sc8.source: "MUUUUUUM!" howled Dudley, tripping over his feet as he dashed back toward the house.
Book2-chapter1_Sc8.description: He panics and runs straight to his mum when he's scared. Make a bit of noise and Dudley bolts for home.

Book2-chapter1_Sc8.source: "Jiggery pokery! Hocus pocus — squiggly wiggly —" said Harry in a fierce voice.
Book2-chapter1_Sc8.description: My messing about with a few words is enough to terrify him. I can get a total reaction from Dudley when I act like I'm doing magic.

Book1-chapter15_Sc6.source: D’you think that was a centaur we heard earlier? said Harry.
Book1-chapter15_Sc6.description: Do you think that was a centaur we heard earlier? I asked. It didn't sound like hooves to me.

Book1-chapter15_Sc6.source: Did that sound like hooves to you? Nah, if yeh ask me, that was what’s bin killin’ the unicorns — never heard anythin’ like it before.
Book1-chapter15_Sc6.description: That noise wasn't hooves. Whatever made it, I reckon it's what has been killing the unicorns.

Book1-chapter15_Sc6.source: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead. Harry had never seen anything so beautiful and sad.
Book1-chapter15_Sc6.description: I stepped closer and saw the unicorn was dead. I couldn't believe how beautiful and sad it looked.
