Book2-chapter1_Sc6.source: "Haven’t you even got friends at that freak place?”
Book2-chapter1_Sc6.description: People out there call Hogwarts a 'freak place' and think my mates are weird. They'll try to wind me up with that.

Book2-chapter1_Sc6.source: "Better not let your mum hear you talking about my school," said Harry coolly.
Book2-chapter1_Sc6.description: Don't you dare talk about my school like that. I will shut that down and defend Hogwarts and the people in it.

Book2-chapter1_Sc7.source: "I’m trying to decide what would be the best spell to set it on fire," said Harry.
Book2-chapter1_Sc7.description: I was thinking about which spell would best set that hedge on fire. I'm serious about using magic if I have to.

Book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I meant 'please' — I'm trying to be careful and polite here, but it doesn't stop things from getting out of hand.

Book2-chapter1_Sc3.source: "WHAT HAVE I TOLD YOU ABOUT SAYING THE 'M' WORD IN OUR HOUSE?"
Book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I can't say the 'M' word in their house or Uncle Vernon loses it, shouting and even spraying spit across the table.
If I even try to threaten or stand up to Dudley Uncle Vernon will explode, pound the table and make a huge scene.
Uncle Vernon means business when he's angry; I need to watch what I say or he'll make a brutal fuss.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "We’ve got to go and see Hagrid, now."
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: We have to get to Hagrid right away. This is urgent and I am not wasting time.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Don’t you think it’s a bit odd that what Hagrid wants more than anything else is a dragon, and a stranger turns up who just happens to have an egg in his pocket?"
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: It all lines up too neatly: Hagrid wanting a dragon and some stranger showing up with a dragon egg. That is not a coincidence.
I missed it before and I am angry at myself for not seeing how suspicious it was sooner.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "He asked a bit about the sorta creatures I look after . . . so I told him . . . an’ I said what I’d always really wanted was a dragon . . . an’ then . . . I can’ remember too well, ’cause he kept buyin’ me drinks."
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Hagrid told that stranger about the creatures he looks after and that he always wanted a dragon. The stranger used that to get Hagrid involved.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "He said he had the dragon egg an’ we could play cards fer it if I wanted"
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: The stranger gambled a dragon egg for a card game with Hagrid. That is how Hagrid ended up with Norbert.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "I think — I know — that Sn — that someone’s going to try and steal the Stone."
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Someone is going to try to steal the Sorcerer’s Stone and I am convinced it may be tonight. I do not trust leaving it alone.
Dumbledore left for London on urgent business. He is not here to protect the school right now.
I believe Snape is the one attempting to get the Stone and that he will try to go through the trapdoor tonight now that Dumbledore is away.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Be warned, Potter — any more nighttime wanderings and I will personally make sure you are expelled."
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Snape openly threatens me. He plays the role of an enemy and will use his position to try to punish me.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "We’ve got the Invisibility Cloak," said Harry. "It shouldn’t be too difficult — I think the cloak’s big enough to cover two of us and Norbert."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: We can do this. The Invisibility Cloak will hide two of us and Norbert, so getting him up the tower is doable if we’re careful.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Nearly there!" Harry panted as they reached the corridor beneath the tallest tower.
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: We made it to the tower corridor and were close to getting Norbert where he needed to be.
Malfoy’s been caught and got detention. That’s a proper bit of luck for us.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Well, well, well," he whispered, "we are in trouble."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Filch found us at the stairs. We’re in a right mess now and need to think fast.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Charlie’s friends were a cheery lot. They showed Harry and Hermione the harness they’d rigged up, so they could suspend Norbert between them."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Charlie’s mates helped out properly. I can trust them to take Norbert away safely.

Book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I shouldn't have spoken up. I thought I could help, but as soon as I said something, it all went wrong.
Dobby reacts to my words with overwhelming gratitude and noise, and I have to beg him to calm down because it's making things worse.

Book2-chapter1_Sc4.source: I WILL NOT TOLERATE MENTION OF YOUR ABNORMALITY UNDER THIS ROOF!
Book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: He's furious about me being different and he will lash out if I push it. I can't make them accept me here so I have to keep my head down.
Fine. I'm not going to argue right now. I'll back off and try to calm things before it gets worse.

Book2-chapter1_Sc4.source: I know what day it is, sang Dudley, waddling toward him.
Book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: Dudley is gleeful and looking for trouble. He enjoys winding me up and he's not on my side.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "I'll use the Invisibility Cloak," said Harry. "It's just lucky I got it back."
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: I'll use the Invisibility Cloak. It's lucky I got it back and I can use it to keep us hidden.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Voldemort killed my parents, remember?" He glared at them.
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: Voldemort did that to my parents, and that makes this personal. I won't back down.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: No, Harry, he has not. He is still out there somewhere, perhaps looking for another body to share . . . not being truly alive, he cannot be killed.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: He's still out there. He isn't gone. He'll try other ways to come back and he can't be killed like a normal person.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: Your mother died to save you. If there is one thing Voldemort cannot understand, it is love.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: My mum's love left me a real protection in my skin. That's why Quirrell couldn't touch me. It hurts to even think about, but that's the reason.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: Ah -- your father happened to leave it in my possession, and I thought you might like it.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: The Invisibility Cloak is my dad's. Dumbledore had it and sent it to me.
Snape and my dad had history. Dad once saved Snape's life. That explains a lot about Snape's feelings and why he might be acting the way he does around me.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: only one who wanted to find the Stone -- find it, but not use it -- would be able to get it
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: The mirror only gives the Stone to someone who wants to find it but not use it. That's how I could get it.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: I think he sort of wanted to give me a chance. I think he knows more or less everything that goes on here, you know.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I don't think Dumbledore just stopped us. I think he let me have a shot at facing Voldemort if I could. He knows more than he tells and maybe he wanted me to try.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: If anything happens to me, don’t follow. Go straight to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore, right?
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: If something goes wrong, send Hedwig to Dumbledore straight away. Don't follow me.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Devil’s Snare, Devil’s Snare . . . what did Professor Sprout say? — it likes the dark and the damp —
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: That plant hates light and warmth. Light is how you get free from it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Lucky you pay attention in Herbology, Hermione
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Hermione's Herbology knowledge actually saved us. She knows what to do with dangerous plants.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: I suppose it’s here to break the fall. Come on, Hermione!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Sometimes stuff in this place is there to help us, even if it looks weird. Go on, keep moving.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Not for nothing, though, was Harry the youngest Seeker in a century. He had a knack for spotting things other people didn’t.
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: I can spot things in the air other people miss. My Seeker instincts really do help in weird situations.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: We’ve got to catch the key to the door!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: If something is enchanted to be a problem, you might have to be clever and grab the enchanted thing yourself.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: The white king took off his crown and threw it at Harry’s feet. They had won.
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Sometimes winning means doing exactly what needs doing as quickly as you can. No dawdling, no second guessing.

Book1-chapter16_Sc4.description: What did you lot do to Neville? He’s bound by a full Body-Bind and I feel awful about it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc4.source: We had to, Neville, no time to explain
Book1-chapter16_Sc4.description: We had to act, even if it meant hurting Neville for a bit. There was no time to hang about explaining.

Book1-chapter16_Sc4.source: He put Hagrid’s flute to his lips and blew.
Book1-chapter16_Sc4.description: If I play that flute like Hagrid’s, the beast drops off to sleep. I can keep it calm by playing.

Book2-chapter2_Sc6.source: "Sorry," said Harry quickly. "I know lots of people don’t like it."
Book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I said sorry. I know lots of people don't like that name.

Book2-chapter2_Sc8.source: He has braved so many dangers already! But Dobby has come to protect Harry Potter, to warn him, even if he does have to shut his ears in the oven door later.
Book2-chapter2_Sc8.description: Dobby's come all this way to look out for me and warn me. He'll even put himself through daft things to keep me safe.

Book2-chapter2_Sc8.source: He has braved so many dangers already! But Dobby has come to protect Harry Potter, to warn him, even if he does have to shut his ears in the oven door later.
Book2-chapter2_Sc8.description: I can't just write Dobby off as a nuisance. He's on my side, proper loyal, even if it gets him into trouble.

Book2-chapter2_Sc2.source: "Dobby is a house-elf — bound to serve one house and one family forever."
Book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: He's a house-elf, bound to serve one wizarding family for life. That's why he acts so scared about being here.

Book2-chapter2_Sc2.source: "Dobby will have to punish himself most grievously for coming to see you, sir. Dobby will have to shut his ears in the oven door for this."
Book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: He punishes himself for even speaking about his masters. He says he'll shut his ears in the oven door and do terrible things to himself if they find out he came to see me.
I couldn't believe he'd actually start hurting himself because he's worried about what his family would think. He's seriously terrified of them.

Book2-chapter2_Sc3.source: ["Dobby is always having to punish himself for something, sir. They lets Dobby get on with it, sir. Sometimes they reminds me to do extra punishments."]
Book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I couldn't believe it! He punishes himself and they make him do extra punishments. That's cruel.

Book2-chapter2_Sc3.source: ["A house-elf must be set free, sir. And the family will never set Dobby free. Dobby will serve the family until he dies, sir."]
Book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: So house-elves can only be freed if their family frees them. He thinks he'll serve them for life and never be free. That's mental.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: At the instant we stepped over the threshold, a fire sprang up behind us in the doorway. It wasn't ordinary fire either; it was purple. At the same instant, black flames shot up in the doorway leading onward.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: We're trapped between two kinds of magical fire, purple behind us and black ahead of us. We cannot go back or forward without the right potion.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: The smallest bottle will get us through the black fire - toward the Stone.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: The tiny bottle is the one that will get me through the black flames toward the Stone. There's only enough for one swallow.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Which one will get you back through the purple flames? Hermione pointed at a rounded bottle at the right end of the line.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: The rounded bottle at the right end will send someone back through the purple fire.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: I might be able to hold Snape off for a while, but I'm no match for him, really. - Well - I was lucky once, wasn't I? I might get lucky again.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: I'm willing to try to face whatever is ahead alone if it gives Hermione and Ron the chance to get Dumbledore. I might get lucky again, even though I know I'm not the best at everything.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Hermione dashed at Harry and threw her arms around him. - Harry - you're a great wizard, you know.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: Hermione cares about me more than she lets on. She thinks I'm a great wizard and is willing to risk things for me.

Book2-chapter2_Sc11.source: "He is too great, too good, to lose. If Harry Potter goes back to Hogwarts, he will be in mortal danger."
Book2-chapter2_Sc11.description: Someone says I'm in mortal danger if I go back to Hogwarts. That's serious and I can't ignore it.

Book2-chapter2_Sc11.source: "There is a plot, Harry Potter. A plot to make most terrible things happen at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry this year," whispered Dobby,
Book2-chapter2_Sc11.description: There's a plot to make terrible things happen at Hogwarts this year. Hogwarts isn't safe and something big is being planned.
I can't just accept this without answers. I'm surprised and I need to know why they'd target me and Hogwarts.

Book2-chapter2_Sc7.source: He stopped again. Thinking about Ron was painful, too.
Book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: Thinking about Ron hurts. It is painful to even bring him up.

Book2-chapter2_Sc7.source: “Dobby heard tell,” he said hoarsely, “that Harry Potter met the Dark Lord for a second time, just weeks ago , . . . that Harry Potter escaped yet again.”
Book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I met the Dark Lord again weeks ago and I got away again. People are talking about it.

Book2-chapter2_Sc1.source: "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you or anything"
Book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I tried to apologise and calm him down because Dobby is clearly terrified of upsetting wizards
Dobby is proud and sensitive about being insulted or treated badly

Book2-chapter2_Sc1.source: "You can't have met many decent wizards"
Book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I told him he must not have met many decent wizards because he looks at me like he already trusts and adores me

Book2-chapter2_Sc9.source: “Harry Potter must not go back to Hogwarts.”
Book2-chapter2_Sc9.description: They just told me I must not go back to Hogwarts. Me. Harry Potter. I can't believe they're saying that.

Book2-chapter2_Sc9.source: “W-what?” Harry stammered. “But I’ve got to go back - term starts on September first.”
Book2-chapter2_Sc9.description: What the hell? I have to go back. Term starts on September first. I'm supposed to be back at school, not kept away.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Let me speak to him . . . face-to-face. . . ." "He lies . . . He lies . . ."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I found out there was someone else inside Quirrell talking, not just him.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Unicorn blood has strengthened me, these past weeks . . . you saw faithful Quirrell drinking it for me in the forest . . ."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: Quirrell was drinking unicorn blood to help whoever was living inside him.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Now . . . why don't you give me that Stone in your pocket?"
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: That face knew about the Stone in my pocket and wanted it badly.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Quirrell couldn't touch his bare skin, not without suffering terrible pain"
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: Quirrell could not touch my bare skin without getting burned and in pain.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "I arrived in time to prevent that, although you were doing very well on your own, I must say."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: Dumbledore came and pulled Quirrell off me before Quirrell could take the Stone.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "As for the Stone, it has been destroyed."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: The Stone is gone. It has been destroyed and nobody can use it anymore.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "They have enough Elixir stored to set their affairs in order and then, yes, they will die."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: Flamel and his wife will die soon because the Stone is destroyed but they have enough Elixir to settle things first.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Seize him! SEIZE HIM!" "KILL HIM! KILL HIM!"
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I know for sure that whoever was with Quirrell hates me and wanted to kill me.

Book1-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Call him Voldemort, Harry. Always use the proper name for things."
Book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I was told to call him Voldemort and not to be terrified of saying his name.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Me," he said calmly. "I wondered whether I’d be meeting you here, Potter."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: So Quirrell's been here looking for me. He's the one I walked into.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Severus?" Quirrell laughed... "Yes, Severus does seem the type, doesn’t he?... Next to him, who would suspect p-p-poor, st-stuttering P-Professor Quirrell?"
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Snape isn't the mastermind; I was wrong to think he was behind everything. That idea's gone.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "No, no, no. I tried to kill you. Your friend Miss Granger accidentally knocked me over as she rushed to set fire to Snape at that Quidditch match."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Quirrell tried to make me fall off my broom and kill me at the Quidditch match. Hermione almost stopped him by accident.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Of course," said Quirrell coolly. "Why do you think he wanted to referee your next match? He was trying to make sure I didn’t do it again."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Snape actually wanted to protect me at the match. He was trying to stop Quirrell, not hurt me.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "You let the troll in?" "Certainly. I have a special gift with trolls — you must have seen what I did to the one in the chamber back there?"
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Quirrell let the troll into Hogwarts on purpose to create chaos and distract people while he searched for the Stone.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "This mirror is the key to finding the Stone," Quirrell murmured, tapping his way around the frame.
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: The Mirror of Erised is the way to find the Stone. It's how Quirrell has been trying to get it.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I met him when I traveled around the world. A foolish young man I was then, full of ridiculous ideas about good and evil. Lord Voldemort showed me how wrong I was."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Quirrell met Voldemort while traveling and he serves him now. Voldemort changed what Quirrell believes about power and right and wrong.
Something or someone told Quirrell to use me to get the Stone. He was being ordered to take advantage of me.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "He clapped his hands once, and the ropes binding Harry fell off."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: Quirrell can control magical ropes and he set me free when he wanted me to look in the mirror.

Book1-chapter17_Sc1.source: "He saw his reflection... the reflection put its hand into its pocket and pulled out a blood-red stone... Harry felt something heavy drop into his real pocket."
Book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: When I looked in the Mirror of Erised, I somehow got the Stone in my pocket. The mirror gave it to me.

Book2-chapter2_Sc13.source: With a crack like a whip, Dobby vanished.
Book2-chapter2_Sc13.description: Dobby can just vanish into thin air. I was stunned when he disappeared like that.

Book2-chapter2_Sc13.source: he shooed the shocked Masons back into the dining room, promised Harry he would flay him to within an inch of his life when the Masons had left, and handed him a mop.
Book2-chapter2_Sc13.description: Uncle Vernon will cover things up for appearances and then take it out on me. He says he will flay me and then makes me clean up. I can't count on him to protect me or be honest.

Book2-chapter2_Sc13.source: covered from head to foot in Aunt Petunia’s pudding.
Book2-chapter2_Sc13.description: I ended up soaked in Aunt Petunia's pudding and shaking, and then they made me scrub the kitchen clean. Great.

Book2-chapter2_Sc12.source: "Harry Potter must not put himself in peril. He is too important, sir!"
Book2-chapter2_Sc12.description: Someone is warning me that I'm in danger and that I'm too important to risk going back to school. I can't just ignore that.
This warning is not about You-Know-Who. Whatever's going on, it isn't Voldemort.

Book2-chapter2_Sc12.source: "Harry Potter must say he’s not going back to school —"
Book2-chapter2_Sc12.description: Someone wants me to say I will not return to school, and Dobby thinks it is for my own good. I don't like being pushed into that, but I can see they're desperate.

Book2-chapter2_Sc12.source: "Then Dobby must do it, sir, for Harry Potter’s own good."
Book2-chapter2_Sc12.description: Dobby is willing to take extreme steps on my behalf. He clearly cares about me enough to try and protect me, even if it gets messy.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Load of dung — Dad reckons he was right in You-Know-Who’s inner circle."
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: That Malfoys are dodgy and probably tied up with dark people. Malfoy would very likely have servants and plenty of money. I can't help thinking he sent someone to stop me going back to Hogwarts.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "I don’t know whether the Malfoys own a house-elf. . . ."
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: If a family has a house-elf it means they're old and rich. Makes perfect sense why Malfoy always has the best of everything.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "I’m glad we came to get you, anyway," said Ron.
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I appreciate Ron. He really worried when I didn't answer his letters and they went out of their way to fetch me. I like being here. This is the best house I've ever been in.

Book2-chapter2_Sc5.source: "Whatever you’ve heard about my greatness is a load of rubbish. I’m not even top of my year at Hogwarts; that’s Hermione, she —"
Book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: People think I'm great, but that's rubbish. I'm not even top of my year. Hermione is.

Book2-chapter2_Sc5.source: "I’m not even top of my year at Hogwarts; that’s Hermione, she —"
Book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: Hermione's ahead of me at school and thinking about her is painful.

Book2-chapter2_Sc5.source: "Harry Potter speaks not of his triumph over He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named —" "Voldemort?"
Book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: Oh — you mean Voldemort. That's who they're talking about.

Book2-chapter3_Sc4.description: Draco Malfoy hates me. He's the sort of person who would hold a grudge.

Book2-chapter3_Sc4.source: "I've heard Dad talking about him," said George. "He was a big supporter of You-Know-Who."
Book2-chapter3_Sc4.description: So the Malfoys have ties to You-Know-Who's supporters. That makes Draco even more dangerous around school.

Book2-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Well, we haven’t been expelled," Harry assured her.
Book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: We haven't been expelled. That's the important thing, okay
The road's clear and no one is watching. Let's go

Book2-chapter5_Sc2.description: Why can’t we get through? The barrier's sealed and nothing I do is getting us on that train.

Book2-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I don’t understand why the gateway’s sealed itself —"
Book2-chapter5_Sc2.description: The gateway has sealed itself for some reason and it's stopped us from getting on the train.

Book2-chapter5_Sc2.source: He wheeled his trolley forward cautiously until it was right against the barrier and pushed with all his might. The metal remained solid. "It’s gone," said Ron, sounding stunned.
Book2-chapter5_Sc2.description: I pushed as hard as I could and the barrier stayed solid, and then the train left. We're actually stuck here, we've missed it.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.source: "The Dursleys haven’t given me pocket money for about six years."
Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I haven't had any pocket money from the Dursleys for ages. Great, so I'm skint and can't help with Muggle cash.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.source: "The Dursleys haven’t given me pocket money for about six years."
Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I laughed hollowly because this is ridiculous. I'm stuck here with no money and no easy way to fix it.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Guess who I saw in Borgin and Burkes?"
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I saw Malfoy and his father in Borgin and Burkes. That means Lucius was selling, not buying.
Lucius Malfoy was selling things, not buying. Good. He's worried about something.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Oh, Harry — oh, my dear — you could have been anywhere —"
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: Molly Weasley fusses over me like I’m her own. They all care, which is comforting.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Well, gotta be off," said Hagrid, who was having his hand wrung by Mrs Weasley ("Knockturn Alley! If you hadn't found him, Hagrid!").
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: Hagrid nearly lost me in Knockturn Alley. He rescued me, then took off for Hogwarts.

Book2-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Know only that no harm can befall you whilst I am here."
Book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: He says we are safe while he's here. I don't trust him but for now he's making everyone feel safer.
They're pixies. Small, supposedly a joke, but everyone's watching them like they might do something. I leaned in to get a better look because I wanted to see what they actually were.

Book2-chapter6_Sc4.source: "I must ask you not to scream," said Lockhart in a low voice. "It might provoke them."
Book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: Lockhart is all show and drama. He tells us not to scream like he's running a play. I think he's more about the performance than the danger.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: Ron was leaning out of the back window of an old turquoise car, which was parked in midair.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: What the hell? Ron is actually in a flying car outside my window.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: Grinning at Harry from the front seats were Fred and George, Ron’s elder twin brothers.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: Fred and George are with Ron. Of course they are grinning like idiots.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: look, can you tell them at Hogwarts that the Dursleys have locked me up and won’t let me come back
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: The Dursleys have locked me in and are keeping me from going back to Hogwarts.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: obviously I can’t magic myself out, because the Ministry’ll think that’s the second spell I’ve done in three days
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I can't magic myself out without getting in even more trouble with the Ministry.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: Tie that around the bars," said Fred, throwing the end of a rope to Harry.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I have to get out by tying a rope to the bars and being pulled out by them.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: All my Hogwarts stuff — my wand — my broomstick — "Locked in the cupboard under the stairs, and I can’t get out of this room
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: My trunk, wand and broom are locked in the cupboard under the stairs and I can't reach them by myself.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: I’ve forgotten Hedwig!" Harry tore back across the room as the landing light clicked on — he snatched up Hedwig’s cage, dashed to the window, and passed it out to Ron.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: Hedwig is with me and I nearly left her behind. I wasn't going to abandon her.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Harry ran back to the window to see the bars dangling a few feet above the ground."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: The bars were off the window and dangling a few feet above the ground. I could climb out.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Panting, Ron hoisted them up into the car."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Ron got the bars into the car for me so we could get out fast.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "But all my Hogwarts stuff — my wand — my broomstick —"
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: My wand and everything are locked in the cupboard under the stairs. I can't get them right now.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "There was a small click and the door swung open."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Fred and George can pick a lock. They opened my door with a hairpin.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Watch out for the bottom stair — it creaks," Harry whispered back as the twins disappeared onto the dark landing.
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: The bottom stair creaks. We had to be careful sneaking past it.
I almost left Hedwig behind. I had to grab her cage and throw it out the window.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "For a split second, Uncle Vernon stood framed in the doorway; then he let out a bellow like an angry bull and dived at Harry, grabbing him by the ankle."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Uncle Vernon tried to stop me and grabbed my ankle. He will do anything to keep me here.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "But the Weasleys gave a gigantic tug and Harry’s leg slid out of Uncle Vernon’s grasp — Harry was in the car — he’d slammed the door shut — 'Put your foot down, Fred!' yelled Ron, and the car shot suddenly toward the moon."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: We actually got away. I thought we might be caught, but the Weasleys pulled me free and we flew off. I can't believe it, we left!
I shouted 'See you next summer' as we left. I'm going back to the Burrow, at least for now.

Book2-chapter3_Sc3.source: I don't think he could," said Harry. "I told you, every time he got close to letting something slip, he started banging his head against the wall.
Book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: Dobby tried to warn me, but he couldn't say who was behind it because every time he came close to spilling anything he started banging his head against the wall.

Book2-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Let Hedwig out," he told Ron. "She can fly behind us. She hasn’t had a chance to stretch her wings for ages."
Book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: Hedwig's coming with us; I want her free to fly alongside the car so she can stretch her wings.

Book2-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Well," said Fred, "put it this way — house-elves have got powerful magic of their own, but they can’t usually use it without their master’s permission."
Book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: Alright, house-elves can do powerful magic, but they probably can't just act on their own without their master's say-so.

Book2-chapter5_Sc1.source: [He felt perfectly confident; this wasn’t nearly as uncomfortable as using Floo powder.]
Book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: This isn't nearly as bad as Floo powder. I can do this, no problem.

Book2-chapter5_Sc1.source: [Both trolleys hit the barrier and bounced backward; Ron’s trunk fell off with a loud thump, Harry was knocked off his feet, and Hedwig’s cage bounced onto the shiny floor, and she rolled away, shrieking indignantly; people all around them stared and a guard nearby yelled, “What in blazes d’you think you’re doing?”]
Book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: I couldn't believe it! We smashed into the barrier, I got knocked flat and Hedwig went rolling. That went wrong fast.

Book2-chapter5_Sc1.source: ["Lost control of the trolley," Harry gasped, clutching his ribs as he got up.]
Book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: Lost control of the trolley. That's exactly what happened, and it hurt.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "He’s never traveled by Floo powder," said Ron suddenly.
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I’ve never used Floo powder. I’m nervous about it and I don’t know what I’m doing.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "You must speak clearly, dear," Mrs. Weasley told Harry as George dipped his hand into the flowerpot.
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I have to say the destination properly when I step into the fire or I might end up somewhere else.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "And be sure to get out at the right grate."
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: There are loads of wizard fireplaces, so I need to get out at the right grate or I’ll be lost.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "He’ll be fine, Molly, don’t fuss," said Mr. Weasley, helping himself to Floo powder, too.
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: They think I’ll manage it if I follow directions. I have to trust them and do what they say.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "But don’t panic and get out too early; wait until you see Fred and George."
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I mustn’t jump out too soon. I should wait until I see Fred and George so I know I’m at the right place.

Book2-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Oh — yes," said Harry, who was obviously supposed to agree. "I mean, nobody wishes more than I do that it had all been quick and clean, and my head had come off properly, I mean, it would have saved me a great deal of pain and ridicule."
Book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: Of course I agree that being properly beheaded would have been better for him. I feel sorry for Nick and I can see how awful that must have been.

Book2-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Well, this Halloween will be my five hundredth deathday," said Nearly Headless Nick, drawing himself up and looking dignified.
Book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: So Nick's having his five hundredth Deathday this Halloween. He's throwing a party in a roomy dungeon and inviting guests from all over the country.
I'll go to Nick's Deathday party. I don't want to leave him hanging and I said I'd come even though the school feast is on.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I have a few — ah — items at home that might embarrass me, if the Ministry were to call. . . ."
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: So Malfoy is hiding embarrassing stuff at home and is worried about Ministry raids. He's the sort who'd sell to keep himself safe.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "The name Malfoy still commands a certain respect, yet the Ministry grows ever more meddlesome."
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Malfoy thinks his name still means something and he looks down on the Ministry. He blames people like Arthur Weasley for making things difficult.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Insert a candle and it gives light only to the holder! Best friend of thieves and plunderers! Your son has fine taste, sir."
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Draco likes dangerous, flashy junk. He picked the Hand of Glory without a second thought.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I hope my son will amount to more than a thief or a plunderer, Borgin,"
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Lucius acts like he wants Draco to be better than a common thief, but he also insults him if his grades slip. He cares about status more than his son's feelings.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "It’s not my fault," retorted Draco. "The teachers all have favorites, that Hermione Granger —"
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Draco blames Hermione when he does badly. He can't handle being beaten by someone he sees as beneath him.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I would have thought you’d be ashamed that a girl of no wizard family beat you in every exam," snapped Mr Malfoy.
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Malfoy is openly contemptuous of anyone without pure wizarding pedigree, and he uses that to needle Draco. He thinks blood status matters above all.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "It’s the same all over," said Mr Borgin, in his oily voice. "Wizard blood is counting for less everywhere —"
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: Borgin feeds Malfoy's ego and agrees that wizard blood is important. He's sycophantic and willing to flatter for business.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Ha!" said Harry under his breath, pleased to see Draco looking both abashed and angry.
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I felt pleased to see Draco thrown off balance. Seeing him embarrassed by Hermione's success makes me quietly smug.

Book2-chapter4_Sc2.source: Harry watched nervously as Draco drew nearer and nearer to his hiding place, examining the objects for sale.
Book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I was hiding nearby and worried when Draco came close. He's nosy and his curiosity is dangerous when I'm trying to stay unseen.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I lied and said I didn't know who that was. I wanted away from Colin and his camera, fast.
I blurted that the photographer was a Gryffindor to calm things down. Quick, direct, keep it simple.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.source: "No one asked your opinion, you filthy little Mudblood," he spat.
Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: When Malfoy called Hermione that, I knew immediately he'd crossed a line. The whole place erupted.

Book2-chapter7_Sc4.source: Harry would have pointed out that trouble didn’t come much worse than having slugs pouring
Book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: Trouble doesn't have to be punishments from teachers to be awful. Having slugs poured all over you is right up there as proper awful. That's the kind of thing I'd call real trouble.

Book2-chapter9_Sc2.description: I felt like he was X-raying me with that twinkling look. I know he can see straight through people and he was judging the whole situation, not just me.
We're allowed to leave. Get out while we can and keep our heads down.

Book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: What's a Howler? I stared at the red envelope and at everyone looking terrified, and I had no idea what it was.

Book2-chapter7_Sc2.source: "We'd better get him to Hagrid's, it's nearest," said Harry to Hermione
Book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: We should get Ron to Hagrid's, it's the nearest place to take him.

Book2-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Givin' me advice on gettin' kelpies out of a well," growled Hagrid ... "If one word of it was true, I'll eat my kettle."
Book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe Hagrid was slagging off a teacher. If Hagrid's saying Lockhart's stories are rubbish, then Lockhart's full of it.

Book2-chapter9_Sc3.source: "D’you think I should have told them about that voice I heard?"
Book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: Should I have told them about that voice I heard? I kept asking that. I know it’s weird. The whole thing’s weird.
You do believe me, don’t you? I needed Ron to say he believed me, and he did.

Book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: Someone's been petrified. That's serious and everyone's treating it like a big deal.

Book2-chapter9_Sc1.source: “I never touched Mrs Norris!” Harry said loudly
Book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I didn't touch Mrs Norris. I'm saying it straight out because people think I did.
Filch thinks I saw his Kwikspell letter in his office and that's why he's accusing me.
Filch thinks I'm connected to him being a Squib, like he blurted out this terrible idea about me.

Book2-chapter9_Sc1.source: “And I don’t even know what a Squib is.” Harry said
Book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I don't even know what a Squib is, so I can't be that or at least I don't understand what Filch's accusation means.

Book2-chapter9_Sc1.source: “Potter and his friends may have simply been in the wrong place at the wrong time,” said Snape
Book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: People are treating me like a suspect just for being in the corridor. I'm starting to think being in the wrong place is going to get me blamed for everything.

Book2-chapter9_Sc1.source: “Why was he in the upstairs corridor at all?” Snape
Book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: Everyone's questioning why I was in the upstairs corridor. That question is being used against me, whether I like it or not.

Book2-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Remember all that water on the floor?"
Book2-chapter9_Sc7.description: Remember all that water on the floor? I'm trying to get us off the subject by bringing it up.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: Of course I'll tell Sir Patrick how frightening and impressive you find me.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.source: “Can you taste it if you walk through it?” Harry asked him.
Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I asked if ghosts can taste food when they walk straight through it.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.source: Harry watched, amazed, as a portly ghost approached the table, crouched low, and walked through it, his mouth held wide so that it passed through one of the stinking salmon.
Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe a ghost could walk right through the food like that and act like it mattered.

Book2-chapter7_Sc5.source: "I have not been giving out signed photos,"
Book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I have not been giving out signed photos. I'm furious about being blamed and I'm quick to deny it.
If Lockhart is spreading rumors about me giving out signed photos then he's the one causing trouble. I don't trust him on this.

Book2-chapter9_Sc6.source: ["Ron was standing well back and seemed to be fighting the impulse to run."]
Book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: He's terrified of spiders. He was hanging back, like he wanted to bolt.

Book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: No. Have you, Ron? Ron? I can't believe spiders are behaving like that, trying to get out like that.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: Something's up with Ron and that envelope. I asked what's wrong because it looked serious.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: Something made me pull my hand away like I'd been burned. That told me there was still something weird or unpleasant about that doorknob area.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.source: "Did you see anyone near here that night?"
Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: I asked Myrtle straight out if she saw anyone on Halloween because the cat was attacked right outside her door. I wanted a straight answer.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.source: "I wasn’t paying attention," said Myrtle dramatically. "Peeves upset me so much I came in here and tried to kill myself. Then, of course, I remembered that I’m — that I’m —" "Already dead," said Ron helpfully.
Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: Myrtle is way too wrapped up in her own drama and not a reliable witness for what happened that night. I can't count on her to have noticed anything useful.

Book2-chapter8_Sc3.source: ". . . rip . . . tear . . . kill . . ." It was the same voice, the same cold, murderous voice he had heard in Lockhart’s office.
Book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: That's the same voice I heard in Lockhart's office. It's cold and murderous, saying rip tear kill and saying it's been hungry for so long. I shut everyone up because we had to listen and work out what that meant.

Book2-chapter9_Sc9.source: Myrtle gave a tragic sob, rose up in the air, turned over, and dived headfirst into the toilet, splashing water all over them and vanishing from sight
Book2-chapter9_Sc9.description: I couldn't believe it! She actually dived headfirst into the loo and disappeared down the U-bend. That's mental.

Book2-chapter10_Sc7.source: [There was a loud crack, and Harry’s fist was suddenly clenched on thin air.]
Book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: Something hit the door or the magic nearby. I jerked my hand out of instinct. That's not normal quiet hospital stuff.

Book2-chapter10_Sc7.source: [He slumped back into bed, his eyes on the dark doorway to the hospital wing as the footsteps drew nearer.]
Book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: Someone's coming for me and I need to be ready. I won't panic but I won't let my guard down either.

Book2-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Someone's fixed it — it won't leave Harry alone. It hasn't gone for anyone else all game. The Slytherins must have done something to it."
Book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: That Bludger is after me. I swear it's following me and no one else's getting this much trouble. The Slytherins have to have done something to it.

Book2-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Listen, with you two flying around me all the time the only way I'm going to catch the Snitch is if it flies up my sleeve. Go back to the rest of the team and let me deal with the rogue one."
Book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: If Fred and George keep circling me I'm not going to have a chance to catch the Snitch. I need them off me so I can deal with the rogue Bludger myself.

Book2-chapter10_Sc4.source: "If we stop now, we'll have to forfeit the match! And we're not losing to Slytherin just because of a crazy Bludger!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: We can't just stop and hand them the match. I'm not letting Slytherin win because of some mad Bludger. We're carrying on.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Look at his family," said Harry, closing his books, too. "The whole lot of them have been in Slytherin; he’s always boasting about it. They could easily be Slytherin’s descendants. His father’s definitely evil enough."
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: He's got a Slytherin pedigree. Malfoy and his family are proper Slytherins and could be the sort to pass down something like the Chamber's key.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "They could’ve had the key to the Chamber of Secrets for centuries! Handing it down, father to son," said Ron.
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: If the Malfoys are Slytherin through and through, then yeah, it's likely the key has been kept in the family for generations.

Book2-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Professor, could you show me that blocking thing again?"
Book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I asked Lockhart to show me the blocking move again because I want to actually learn how to defend myself properly.

Book2-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Scared?" muttered Malfoy... "You wish," said Harry out of the corner of his mouth.
Book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I won't let Malfoy get under my skin. If he thinks I'm scared he can forget it.

Book2-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Hello," said Harry. "I'm looking for Justin Finch-Fletchley." ... "I wanted to tell him what really happened with that snake at the Dueling Club," said Harry.
Book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I'm going to find Justin and set the record straight about the snake. I need him to know the truth, not the rumours.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "D'you realize how much we’re going to have to steal, Hermione? Shredded skin of a boomslang, that’s definitely not in the students’ cupboard. What're we going to do, break into Snape's private stores? I don't know if this is a good idea."
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: We're going to have to steal some proper dangerous stuff. Breaking into Snape's private stores might be on the table and I don't think that's a good idea.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Here it is," said Hermione excitedly as she found the page headed The Polyjuice Potion. ... "This is the most complicated potion I’ve ever seen," said Hermione as they scanned the recipe.
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: This potion is far more complicated than I expected. If Hermione's calling it the most complicated she's seen then it's serious and not something we can just mess about with.

Book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: What on earth is a Squib. I asked it straight out because I needed to know what people meant.
People are calling me Slytherin's heir. That stings and makes me worry everyone will be afraid of me.

Book2-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Can’t hurt to have a poke around,"
Book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I decided to search the corridor myself. I got down on my hands and knees to look for clues.
There are scorch marks near the message on the wall. Something powerful or dangerous was here.
Colin called out to me and squeaked bye. He still looks up to me a bit, even with all this panic.

Book2-chapter12_Sc1.source: "you would have done well in Slytherin"
Book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: The Hat still thinks I'd fit in Slytherin. I pulled the stupid thing off and felt sick. I don't want that to be true.
Dumbledore's bird suddenly burst into flames right in front of me. For a terrifying second I thought the bird was going to die while I was alone with it.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Dobby hid and watched for Harry Potter and sealed the gateway and Dobby had to iron his hands afterward"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: You stopped the barrier from letting us through. Dobby tells me he hid and sealed the gateway so I couldn't get to platform nine and three quarters.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Dobby only wanted Harry Potter hurt enough to be sent home!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Dobby admits his Bludger was made to hurt me enough to send me home. He didn't want to kill me, just to get me out of school.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "'Tis a mark of the house-elf's enslavement, sir. Dobby can only be freed if his masters present him with clothes"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Dobby wears a pillowcase because house-elves stay enslaved until their masters give them clothes. That's why he hasn't been freed.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "the Chamber of Secrets is open once more"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Dobby says the Chamber of Secrets has been opened again at Hogwarts and that terrible things are happening or are about to happen there.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Dobby remembers how it was when He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named was at the height of his powers"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Dobby says house-elves suffered badly when Voldemort was powerful, and that people like me were a beacon of hope back then.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Harry Potter risks his own life for his friends!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I know I'll put myself in danger to protect my friends. Dobby even praises me for risking my life for them, and I accept that about myself.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Dobby can't, sir, Dobby can't, Dobby mustn't tell!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Dobby refuses to say who opened the Chamber last time or who opened it now. He's terrified to name names.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "One of my best friends is Muggle-born; she’ll be first in line if the Chamber really has been opened"
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: Someone I care about at school is Muggle-born and would be in serious danger if the Chamber targets Muggle-born students.

Book2-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Dobby is used to death threats, sir. Dobby gets them five times a day at home."
Book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: My feelings toward Dobby are conflicted. I get angry with him for what he did but I also see how miserable and abused he is, so I don't hate him.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: She said a silly little word and the gargoyle sprang to life. Say the password and the entrance opens.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.source: "the gargoyle sprang suddenly to life and hopped aside as the wall behind him split in two."
Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: A gargoyle guards the door and it actually moves when you give the right password. It's not just a statue.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.source: "Behind the wall was a spiral staircase that was moving smoothly upward, like an escalator."
Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: There's a moving spiral staircase hidden behind the wall. It goes up like an escalator to where McGonagall's office must be.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.source: "They rose upward in circles, higher and higher, until at last, slightly dizzy, Harry saw a gleaming oak door ahead, with a brass knocker in the shape of a griffin."
Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: The staircase takes you up to a gleaming oak door with a griffin-shaped knocker. That's where we're heading.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.source: "Even full of dread for what was coming, Harry couldn’t fail to be amazed."
Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: I was terrified about what would happen, but I couldn't help being amazed by the place. Hogwarts still manages to surprise me.

Book2-chapter11_Sc5.source: "As he and Professor McGonagall stepped onto it, Harry heard the wall thud closed behind them."
Book2-chapter11_Sc5.description: Once you step on that staircase the wall closes behind you. It's private and a bit claustrophobic.

Book2-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Oh, hello, Harry," he said. "Excellent flying yesterday, really excellent. Gryffindor has just taken the lead for the House Cup — you earned fifty points!"
Book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I earned fifty points for that flying. Gryffindor's in the lead now. Well, that's something.

Book2-chapter11_Sc1.source: "desperate to tell Ron and Hermione about Colin and Dobby, but they weren’t there."
Book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I was desperate to tell Ron and Hermione about Colin and Dobby, but they weren't even there. It stung that they didn't seem interested in whether I had my bones back or not.

Book2-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Rictusempra!" A jet of silver light hit Malfoy in the stomach and he doubled up, wheezing.
Book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I blasted Malfoy with Rictusempra and it actually tickled him sick. That spell hits hard enough to drop someone laughing, not just a bit of show-off magic.

Book2-chapter11_Sc2.source: "I hung back, with a vague feeling it would be unsporting to bewitch Malfoy while he was on the floor, but this was a mistake; gasping for breath, Malfoy pointed his wand at Harry’s knees, choked, "Tarantallegra!" and the next second Harry’s legs began to jerk around out of his control in a kind of quickstep."
Book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I told myself not to take advantage and hang back. That was daft. Being decent in the middle of a duel left me open and I got Tarantallegra right in the knees. Never assume mercy from Malfoy again.

Book2-chapter11_Sc2.source: "How about Malfoy and Potter?" said Snape with a twisted smile.
Book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: Snape set me up with Malfoy on purpose. He was smirking and pulling strings, so I don't trust that he has my best interests at heart when he volunteers pairings.

Book2-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Let's have a volunteer pair — Longbottom and Finch-Fletchley, how about you —" "A bad idea, Professor Lockhart," said Snape, gliding over like a large and malevolent bat. "Longbottom causes devastation with the simplest spells. We'll be sending what's left of Finch-Fletchley up to the hospital wing in a matchbox."
Book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: Lockhart tries to look confident but he's useless when it comes to real teaching. Snape will step in every time to make things worse or manipulate the situation.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: “Well, since the fluxweed has got to be picked at the full moon and the lacewings have got to be stewed for twenty-one days . . . I’d say it’d be ready in about a month, if we can get all the ingredients.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: A month to brew it. Right, that gives us time but not loads.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: “Close one, Harry!” said George, streaking past him with his club in his hand, ready to knock the Bludger back toward a Slytherin. ... the Bludger changed direction in midair and shot straight for Harry again. ... Once again, the Bludger swerved like a boomerang and shot at Harry’s head. ... He could hear the Bludger whistling along behind him. What was going on? Bludgers never concentrated on one player like this; it was their job to try and unseat as many people as possible.
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: That's mental. The Bludger is fixating on me, which is not normal. Someone or something is making it target me.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Get the Snitch or die trying," what a stupid thing to tell him —"
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I know people expect me to go for the Snitch no matter what. They shout stuff like "get the Snitch or die trying" and it puts pressure on me to do something reckless.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: He had stayed still a second too long. The Bludger had hit him at last, smashed into his elbow, and Harry felt his arm break.
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: The Bludger really was gunning for me. I let it get the better of me for one second and my arm got smashed. It's broken and it hurts like mad.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: he saw it — the Golden Snitch. It was hovering inches above Malfoy’s left ear — and Malfoy, busy laughing at Harry, hadn’t seen it.
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I saw the Snitch sitting right above Malfoy's head while he was laughing at me. If I could have managed it, I would have grabbed it off him in a heartbeat.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: "You will be able to, won’t you?" said Harry desperately. "I’ll be able to, certainly, but it will be painful," said Madam Pomfrey grimly, throwing Harry a pair of pajamas. "You’ll have to stay the night. . . ."
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: Madam Pomfrey can mend bones and she'll be able to grow mine back, but it's going to hurt and I'll have to stay in the hospital wing overnight.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: "This boy needs rest, he’s got thirty-three bones to regrow! Out! OUT!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: Pomfrey said I've got thirty-three bones to regrow. She makes it clear she wants me left alone so I can rest.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Fred, George, you heard Harry — leave him alone and let him deal with the Bludger on his own."
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: Fred and George back me up more than they tease when it matters. They argue but they step in on my side when things get serious.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Unbelievable flying, Harry," said George. "I’ve just seen Marcus Flint yelling at Malfoy. Something about having the Snitch on top of his head and not noticing. Malfoy didn’t seem too happy."
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: Even after I got hit, people noticed I was flying well. Marcus Flint was yelling at Malfoy about the Snitch on his head. Malfoy was furious, which proves I messed him up enough to scare him.

Book2-chapter10_Sc5.source: He could hear laughter from the crowd; he knew he must look very stupid, but the rogue Bludger was heavy and couldn’t change direction as quickly as Harry could; he began a kind of roller-coaster ride around the edges of the stadium
Book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: The crowd laughed at me while I dodged that rogue Bludger. I looked ridiculous but I kept going because I had to keep control and try to get the Snitch.

Book2-chapter11_Sc4.source: All I saw," said Ernie stubbornly, though he was trembling as he spoke, "was you speaking Parseltongue and chasing the snake toward Justin."
Book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: They saw me speaking Parseltongue and reckon I chased a snake toward Justin.

Book2-chapter11_Sc4.source: "I didn’t chase it at him!" Harry said, his voice shaking with anger. "It didn’t even touch him!"
Book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I didn't chase it at him! It didn't even touch him, but people are already convinced otherwise.

Book2-chapter11_Sc4.source: "This is out of my hands, Potter," said Professor McGonagall curtly.
Book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: McGonagall says it's out of her hands, so this is being taken up to the headmistress and I'm not in control of what happens next.

Book2-chapter11_Sc4.source: "And in case you’re getting ideas," he added hastily, "I might tell you that you can trace my family back through nine generations of witches and warlocks and my blood’s as pure as anyone’s, so —"
Book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: They're bringing blood status into it and using that to justify suspicion; people are assuming my abilities tie me to dark things because of blood.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Close one, Harry!" said George, streaking past him with his club in his hand, ready to knock the Bludger back toward a Slytherin.
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: That Bludger is after me. It keeps coming for my head no matter how many times others try to hit it away.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Someone's — tampered — with — this — Bludger —" Fred grunted, swinging his bat with all his might at it as it launched a new attack on Harry.
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Someone's messed with the Bludger. This isn't normal Quidditch business. It's deliberately targeting me.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: He could hear the Bludger whistling along behind him.
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I can hear it right behind me. I need to get away fast or it'll smash me out of the sky.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: He didn’t have a clue what was going on in the rest of the game until he heard Lee Jordan, who was commentating, say, "Slytherin lead, sixty points to zero —"
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Slytherin are way ahead. The rest of the game is going badly while I'm being chased by that blasted Bludger.

Book2-chapter13_Sc3.source: They were completely blank. There wasn’t the faintest trace of writing on any of them
Book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: They're totally blank. Not a single thing written in it.

Book2-chapter13_Sc3.source: Harry turned to the back cover of the book and saw the printed name of a variety store on Vauxhall Road, London.
Book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I saw a shop name from Vauxhall Road on the back. It's a Muggle shop.

Book2-chapter13_Sc3.source: “He must’ve been Muggle-born,” said Harry thoughtfully.
Book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: He must have been Muggle-born if he'd bought a diary from Vauxhall Road.
I kept the diary. I'm holding onto it.

Book2-chapter14_Sc1.source: "We always knew Hagrid had been expelled," said Harry miserably. "And the attacks must’ve stopped after Hagrid was kicked out."
Book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: Hagrid was expelled. Of course he was kicked out, and the attacks seem to have stopped once he was gone. That's what everyone thinks now.

Book2-chapter12_Sc2.source: Fawkes is a phoenix, Harry. Phoenixes burst into flame when it is time for them to die and are reborn from the ashes. Watch him
Book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: So phoenixes literally burst into flame when it's their time and then are reborn from the ashes. He really did come back from being just a pile of ash.

Book2-chapter12_Sc2.source: Your bird, I couldn't do anything, he just caught fire
Book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I thought there was nothing I could do to save Fawkes and felt useless, but seeing him reborn made me stop panicking so hard — it wasn't the end.

Book2-chapter12_Sc2.source: About time, too, He's been looking dreadful for days, I've been telling him to get a move on
Book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: Dumbledore wasn't angry or upset about Fawkes dying, he was oddly amused and calm. He treats Fawkes like family and expects this to happen, which made me feel less guilty and more confused.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "It’s ready." Harry sat up, suddenly wide awake. "Are you sure?"
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: It's ready. I woke up and wanted to know for certain, because if we're doing this tonight I need it to work.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "You do want to investigate Malfoy, don’t you?"
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: Of course I want to investigate Malfoy. I agreed to go along even though it sounds risky.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "Once we’ve drunk it, we’ll have exactly an hour before we change back into ourselves."
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: We only get an hour in someone else's body after drinking the Polyjuice. We have to be quick.

Book2-chapter13_Sc2.source: The little book lay on the floor, nondescript and soggy. Harry saw at once that it was a diary, and the faded year on the cover told him it was fifty years old.
Book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: It's a diary and it's fifty years old. The name T. M. Riddle is on the first page.

Book2-chapter13_Sc2.source: Well, we won’t find out unless we look at it," he said, and he ducked around Ron and picked it up off the floor.
Book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: Right, we're not going to just stand here. If we want answers, I have to check the thing myself.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: Leering, he showed it to Crabbe and Goyle, and Harry realized that he’d got Riddle’s diary.
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: That's Riddle's diary. I can tell it's not just any book.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: Ginny was staring from the diary to Harry, looking terrified.
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: Ginny looked terrified when she saw that diary. Whatever's going on with her is serious.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: But Harry didn’t care, he was one-up on Malfoy, and that was worth five points from Gryffindor any day.
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: Malfoy getting one over on me matters. Beating him feels like winning for all of us.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: Percy said, "As a school prefect —" but Harry had lost his temper. He pulled out his wand and shouted, "Expelliarmus!"
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: If Malfoy has something that could hurt Ginny or mess things up, I will use magic to stop him even if I'll get in trouble.

Book2-chapter15_Sc1.source: “I just want to say, Harry, that I’m sorry I ever suspected you. I know you’d never attack Hermione Granger, and I apologize for all the stuff I said. We’re all in the same boat now, and, well —”
Book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: He apologized and offered his hand. I shook it. We're not enemies anymore.

Book2-chapter15_Sc1.source: “I just want to say, Harry, that I’m sorry I ever suspected you. I know you’d never attack Hermione Granger, and I apologize for all the stuff I said. We’re all in the same boat now, and, well —”
Book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: Ernie admits he was wrong to suspect me. I can count on him not to accuse me again.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: We have to add other people's hair to the Polyjuice Potion to take their form.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: We'd better not all drink them in here.
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: We can't all change into Crabbe and Goyle in the same tiny bathroom stall or we'll not fit.
The password to that passage was 'pure-blood' and Malfoy used it to open the door.
Malfoy acted like he might know who's behind the Chamber nonsense, but I don't trust him; he sounded smug not helpful.
Someone who opened the Chamber before was expelled and they might be in Azkaban.

Book2-chapter14_Sc5.description: What does she understand? I need her to tell me straight away.

Book2-chapter15_Sc5.source: "And you . . . you didn’t come from the Chamber of Secrets?" said Harry, who could feel cold sweat on his forehead.
Book2-chapter15_Sc5.description: I thought Hagrid had opened the Chamber and released the monster, but that was wrong. Hagrid didn’t set it free.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: Don't you people realize," said Lockhart, speaking slowly, as though they were all a bit dim, "the danger has passed! The culprit has been taken away —
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: No way is this over. I don't buy that the danger has passed just because someone's saying so.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: "My dear young man, the Minister of Magic wouldn't have taken Hagrid if he hadn't been one hundred percent sure that he was guilty," said Lockhart
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: I can't trust Lockhart's smug confidence. He talks like he knows everything and he doesn't.
We're going tonight. I'm not waiting around while Hagrid gets blamed.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: "C'mon, Fang, we're going for a walk," said Harry, patting his leg, and Fang bounded happily out of the house behind them
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: Fang comes with me. He's eager and I'll use him to get into the forest.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: Harry took out his wand, murmured, "Lumos!" and a tiny light appeared at the end of it, just enough to let them watch the path for signs of spiders.
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: A little wand light is perfect for watching the path. I use Lumos to look for spiders without drawing too much attention.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: Ron started to say that he didn't think so, somehow, but stopped in midsentence when Harry kicked him hard under the desk. "We weren't there, remember?" Harry muttered.
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: Ron and I are in this together. He cares about Hagrid and I shut him up because we need to act, not argue.

Book2-chapter14_Sc4.source: I just want to give up Potions
Book2-chapter14_Sc4.description: I want to drop Potions, I'm fed up with it and would happily give it up if I could.

Book2-chapter14_Sc4.source: The voice! I just heard it again didn't you?
Book2-chapter14_Sc4.description: I heard that terrifying voice again. I'm certain something odd is happening and it might be dangerous.

Book2-chapter14_Sc2.source: "And Riddle was going to go back to some Muggle orphanage if they closed Hogwarts," said Harry.
Book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I don't blame him for wanting to stay here. If I had the choice between going back to a Muggle orphanage or staying at Hogwarts, I'd stay too.

Book2-chapter14_Sc2.source: "He was buying a Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent," said Harry quickly.
Book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I met Hagrid down Knockturn Alley and he was buying a Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent. That's what I told them, quick and simple.

Book2-chapter15_Sc2.source: "No," said Harry, so firmly that Ernie and Hannah stared.
Book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: No. I'm certain it's not Malfoy. I just won't buy that for a second.

Book2-chapter15_Sc2.source: Several large spiders were scuttling over the ground on the other side of the glass, moving in an unnaturally straight line as though taking the shortest route to a prearranged meeting.
Book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: Those spiders are moving in a straight line like they're being sent somewhere. If they keep that course, we'll know exactly where they're going.

Book2-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Hagrid?" said Harry. "Did you hear about Hermione?"
Book2-chapter14_Sc7.description: Hagrid, did you hear about Hermione?

Book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I'm one of Hagrid's friends and I'm standing up for him.
The Ministry has taken Hagrid to Azkaban.

Book2-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Hagrid has never sent men into our hollow before," he said slowly.
Book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: If Hagrid had men go into the spiders' hollow, something serious must be wrong with him.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “I was not born in the castle. I come from a distant land. A traveler gave me to Hagrid when I was an egg.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: So Aragog wasn't born in the castle. He was brought here as an egg and given to Hagrid.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “Hagrid was only a boy, but he cared for me, hidden in a cupboard in the castle, feeding me on scraps from the table.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: Hagrid looked after Aragog when he was a baby, hiding him in a cupboard and feeding him. That explains why Aragog is loyal to him.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “Hagrid is my good friend, and a good man.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: Hagrid protected Aragog and even found him a mate. Aragog sees Hagrid as a true friend and a good man.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “They believed that I was the monster that dwells in what they call the Chamber of Secrets. They thought that Hagrid had opened the Chamber and set me free.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I can't believe people blamed Aragog for the Chamber attacks. He wasn't the monster from the Chamber.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “Never,” croaked the old spider. “It would have been my instinct, but out of respect for Hagrid, I never harmed a human.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: Aragog says he never attacked anyone and avoided hurting humans out of respect for Hagrid.

Book2-chapter15_Sc6.source: “The thing that lives in the castle,” said Aragog, “is an ancient creature we spiders fear above all others.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: There is another, ancient creature living in the castle that even the spiders fear. That's the real threat.

Book2-chapter15_Sc8.source: "I bet he thought Aragog wouldn’t hurt friends of his," said Harry.
Book2-chapter15_Sc8.description: He probably thought Aragog wouldn't hurt his friends

Book2-chapter15_Sc8.source: "That Hagrid never opened the Chamber of Secrets," said Harry, throwing the
Book2-chapter15_Sc8.description: Hagrid never opened the Chamber of Secrets

Book2-chapter16_Sc2.source: The monster in the Chamber's a basilisk, a giant serpent! That's why I've been hearing that voice all over the place, and nobody else has heard it. It's because I understand Parseltongue.
Book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: It's a basilisk, a huge snake. Of course it explains the voice I keep hearing. I can talk Parseltongue so I hear it and they don't.

Book2-chapter16_Sc2.source: The basilisk kills people by looking at them. But no one's died because no one looked it straight in the eye.
Book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: The thing kills by eye contact. Nobody's been killed because nobody looked it straight in the eye. That's why people only end up petrified.

Book2-chapter16_Sc2.source: Colin saw it through his camera. The basilisk burned up all the film inside it, but Colin just got Petrified.
Book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: Colin saw it on camera but the film was ruined. He got petrified, not killed, which fits with the eye thing.
Justin's petrified too. That's another victim who didn't look straight at it but still got turned to stone.

Book2-chapter16_Sc9.description: I'm going down there. I can't not go now we've found the entrance to the Chamber. If there's even the faintest chance Ginny might be alive I have to try.

Book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: She died in this very toilet stall. The place where Myrtle haunts is where she died.

Book2-chapter16_Sc6.source: "I just remember seeing a pair of great, big, yellow eyes."
Book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: Myrtle says she saw huge yellow eyes right before she died. Whatever did it had huge yellow eyes.

Book2-chapter16_Sc6.source: "They said something funny. A different language, I think it must have been."
Book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: Someone spoke in a strange language in the bathroom when she died. It wasn't normal talk.

Book2-chapter16_Sc6.source: "Anyway, what really got me was that it was a boy speaking."
Book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: The person who came in and spoke was a boy. So a boy was involved the night she died.

Book2-chapter16_Sc6.source: "I'd hidden because Olive Hornby was teasing me about my glasses."
Book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: Myrtle was hiding in the stall because Olive Hornby was teasing her about her glasses. She was upset and crying when it happened.

Book2-chapter16_Sc5.source: "What if it’s in —" "— Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom," said Harry.
Book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: It could be in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. That's where the thing's been hiding.

Book2-chapter16_Sc5.source: "This means," said Harry, "I can’t be the only Parselmouth in the school. The Heir of Slytherin’s one, too. That’s how he’s been controlling the basilisk."
Book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I can't be the only Parselmouth here. The Heir of Slytherin can speak to the basilisk, and that's how it's been controlled.

Book2-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Let’s go to the staffroom," said Harry, jumping up. "She’ll be there in ten minutes. It’s nearly break."
Book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: We're going straight to the staffroom to find Professor McGonagall right away. She'll be there soon.

Book2-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Awfully sorry, boys, but I’ll have to put a Memory Charm on you now. Can’t have you blabbing my secrets all over the place."
Book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: Lockhart thinks he can get away with a Memory Charm to stop us telling anyone. He means to wipe our memories.

Book2-chapter16_Sc7.source: "Where exactly did you see the eyes?" said Harry. "Somewhere there," said Myrtle, pointing vaguely toward the sink in front of her toilet.
Book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: She says she saw eyes at the sink. She actually pointed at it, so I treated the sink as suspect.

Book2-chapter16_Sc7.source: Harry and Ron hurried over to it. Lockhart was standing well back, a look of utter terror on his face. It looked like an ordinary sink. They examined every inch of it, inside and out, including the pipes below.
Book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I rushed to the sink and checked it properly. It looked normal, but we went over every inch, even the pipes.

Book2-chapter15_Sc7.source: “The thing that lives in the castle,” said Aragog, “is an ancient creature we spiders fear above all others.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: There is some ancient creature living in the castle that even the spiders are terrified of.

Book2-chapter15_Sc7.source: “I never even told Hagrid the name of that dread creature, though he asked me, many times.”
Book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: Aragog never told Hagrid the name of that dread creature even though Hagrid asked him again and again.

Book2-chapter15_Sc7.source: “We do not speak of it!” said Aragog fiercely. “We do not name it!”
Book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I stopped pushing for details once Aragog snarled that they will not speak of or name it and the spiders closed in on me.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: "We must be miles under the school," said Harry, his voice echoing in the black tunnel.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: We're miles under the school. We're well below Hogwarts.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: "Under the lake, probably," said Ron, squinting around at the dark, slimy walls.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: We're probably under the lake. That's where we are.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: "Lumos!" Harry muttered to his wand and it lit again.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: My wand lights the tunnel. I can light the way when it's pitch black.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: Harry jabbed him in the back with his wand. Lockhart slid his legs into the pipe.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: I had to push Lockhart into the pipe to get things moving. He's useless without being shoved.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I went over to Myrtle because she was clearly upset. I asked what was wrong and who had been bothering her.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "It’s over there, it got washed out."
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: There was a small shabby black book under the sink that had been washed out of Myrtle's stall.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "But it can’t hurt you if someone throws something at you," said Harry.
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I thought being a ghost would mean thrown things just go through her and can't hurt her. Apparently I was wrong to be flippant about it.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Well, we won’t find out unless we look at it," he said, and he ducked around Ron and picked it up off the floor.
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I decided not to let fear stop me. If there's a mystery, I'm going to check it out myself.

Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "She’s still alive," said Riddle. "But only just."
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: She's alive but barely. I need to act fast or she'll die.

Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Are you a ghost?" "A memory," said Riddle quietly. "Preserved in a diary for fifty years."
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: That boy is not a ghost, he's a memory trapped in a diary. The diary holds him.

Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "It won’t come until it is called," said Riddle calmly.
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: The basilisk won't attack randomly. Someone has to call it first.

Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Thanks," said Harry, stretching out his hand for it. A smile curled the corners of Riddle’s mouth. He continued to stare at Harry, twirling the wand idly."
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: My wand has been taken. I don't have it and Riddle's holding it, so I'm at a real disadvantage.
