Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I’ve waited a long time for this, Harry Potter," said Riddle. "For the chance to see you. To speak to you."
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: Riddle isn't just some leftover memory; he's been waiting to meet me. This is personal and dangerous.

Book2-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Lying open there was the little black diary Harry had found in Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom."
Book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: The diary I found in Myrtle's bathroom is here in the Chamber and it's connected to what's happened to Ginny.

Book2-chapter16_Sc8.source: "Open up," he said. Except that the words weren’t what he heard; a strange hissing had escaped him, and at once the tap glowed with a brilliant white light and began to spin.
Book2-chapter16_Sc8.description: I said "Open up" and it came out as a hiss in Parseltongue, and the tap actually opened. I can force Parseltongue to work even when there is only an engraving if I really believe it.

Book2-chapter16_Sc8.source: Next second, the sink began to move; the sink, in fact, sank, right out of sight, leaving a large pipe exposed, a pipe wide enough for a man to slide into.
Book2-chapter16_Sc8.description: When the tap opened, the sink sank and revealed a big pipe I could go down. There is a passage hidden beneath the sink.

Book2-chapter16_Sc8.source: "But —" Harry thought hard. The only times he’d ever managed to speak Parseltongue were when he’d been faced with a real snake.
Book2-chapter16_Sc8.description: I used to think I could only speak Parseltongue to real snakes, but I forced it here, so I know I can trigger it by convincing myself the mark is alive.

Book2-chapter16_Sc13.source: "Wait there," he called to Ron. "Wait with Lockhart. I'll go on, If I'm not back in an hour"
Book2-chapter16_Sc13.description: I have to go on alone. I'm telling Ron to stay with Lockhart and I'm setting an hour as a cutoff. I need to get on despite being scared, so I'm pushing myself to sound confident.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: This is it. This is the answer.
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: This is it. The thing in the Chamber is a basilisk, a giant serpent, and I can hear it because I speak Parseltongue. Of course the others couldn't hear it.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: The basilisk kills people by looking at them.
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: The basilisk kills by eye contact. No one died because no one looked it straight in the eye. They got petrified instead from indirect viewing like through a camera, Nearly Headless Nick, or a mirror.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: Harry looked up at the beds around him.
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: Hermione was clutching a scrunched bit of paper in her hand. She must have worked something out and tried to warn people.

Book2-chapter16_Sc4.source: 'The Basilisk flees only from the crowing of the rooster, which is fatal to it'!
Book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: The Basilisk is terrified of roosters. If a rooster crows it drives the thing off.
Spiders run from the Basilisk. That explains why they're bolting and why Hagrid's creatures were connected to this.
It's been getting around through the plumbing. I kept hearing that voice inside the walls and now it makes sense.

Book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I can't be the only Parselmouth at Hogwarts. The Heir of Slytherin must be a Parselmouth too, and that's how he's been controlling the basilisk.
Let's go to the staffroom. McGonagall'll be there in ten minutes and we need to tell her.

Book2-chapter16_Sc12.source: "Ginny had already been in the Chamber of Secrets for hours."
Book2-chapter16_Sc12.description: Ginny's been in the Chamber for hours. There's no time to faff about.

Book2-chapter16_Sc12.source: "Wait there," he called to Ron. "Wait with Lockhart. I'll go on. If I'm not back in an hour..."
Book2-chapter16_Sc12.description: I'm going on alone. You stay with Lockhart and wait for me. If I'm not back in an hour, well, I'll have to deal with it.

Book2-chapter16_Sc11.source: Remember, any sign of movement, close your eyes right away.
Book2-chapter16_Sc11.description: If anything moves down here, shut your eyes straight away. No dawdling, it could be dangerous.

Book2-chapter16_Sc11.source: Huge cracks had appeared in it.
Book2-chapter16_Sc11.description: Those cracks in the tunnel mean it could cave in. I can't risk blasting the rocks with magic or the whole place might fall.

Book2-chapter17_Sc2.source: "My diary. Little Ginny’s been writing in it for months and months, telling me all her pitiful worries and woes — how her brothers tease her, how she had to come to school with secondhand robes and books, how ... how she didn’t think famous, good, great Harry Potter would ever like her."
Book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: She poured her heart into a diary and it was feeding whatever's in there. Ginny's been writing to it about everything, even about me. That's why she's like this.

Book2-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Dumbledore’s been driven out of this castle by the mere memory of me!"
Book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: Riddle claims Dumbledore was forced out by him. I don't believe that, but Riddle wants me to think he's powerful enough to scare Dumbledore off.

Book2-chapter17_Sc2.source: "A crimson bird the size of a swan... A second later, the bird was flying straight at Harry. It dropped the ragged thing it was carrying at his feet, then landed heavily on his shoulder."
Book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: A phoenix showed up, sat on my shoulder and dropped the Sorting Hat at my feet. It's Fawkes and he came for me.
The bird is Fawkes. He's on my side right now and he came exactly when I needed him.
The thing Fawkes dropped is the Sorting Hat. It just appeared in the Chamber and it's with me now.

Book2-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Speak to me, Slytherin, greatest of the Hogwarts Four."
Book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: The Slytherin statue is moving and something is coming out of its mouth. Whatever's in the Chamber is waking up and it's coming for me.

Book2-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Harry wanted to shout, 'Don’t leave me!' but what chance did a phoenix have against the king of serpents?"
Book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt terrified and alone for a second. Even with Fawkes here I worried we're up against something huge and dangerous.

Book2-chapter18_Sc2.source: Voldemort put a bit of himself in me?
Book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe it when Dumbledore said Voldemort put part of himself inside me. That's mental and it explains why I can do things like Parseltongue.

Book2-chapter18_Sc2.source: So I should be in Slytherin
Book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: For a second I thought I must belong in Slytherin because of what the Sorting Hat saw and because of those Slytherin traits in me, but I asked not to go there and that choice matters. Choosing Gryffindor proves something about who I am.

Book2-chapter18_Sc2.source: Only a true Gryffindor could have pulled that out of the hat, Harry
Book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: When Dumbledore handed me the sword of Godric Gryffindor and showed the name engraved on it I knew that I really am a Gryffindor. Pulling that sword out wasn't luck.

Book2-chapter18_Sc2.source: Which makes you very different from Tom Riddle. It is our choices, Harry, that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.
Book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: Dumbledore made it clear I'm not like Tom Riddle. It's my choices, not the stuff I'm capable of, that define me. I actually feel more certain about who I want to be.

Book3-chapter4_Sc3.source: He had never wanted anything as much in his whole life
Book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: I want that Firebolt more than anything. I can't stop thinking about it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc3.source: what was the point in emptying his Gringotts vault for the Firebolt, when he had a very good broom already?
Book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: I won't empty my Gringotts vault for the Firebolt. My Nimbus Two Thousand is a very good broom, and blowing all my money on a new one isn't worth it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc3.source: he returned, almost every day after that, just to look at the Firebolt
Book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: Even though I'm not buying it, I keep going back to look at the Firebolt every day. I can't help it.

Book2-chapter18_Sc3.source: [Because you gave it to her, said Harry. In Flourish and Blotts. You picked up her old Transfiguration book and slipped the diary inside it, didn’t you?]
Book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: You gave Ginny that diary by slipping it into her old Transfiguration book in Flourish and Blotts. I know you did it.

Book2-chapter18_Sc3.source: [Very fortunate the diary was discovered, and Riddle’s memories wiped from it. Who knows what the consequences might have been otherwise. . . .]
Book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: Riddle's memories were wiped from the diary, otherwise who knows how badly things would have turned out.

Book2-chapter18_Sc3.source: [Least I could do, Dobby, said Harry, grinning. Just promise never to try and save my life again.]
Book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: Dobby tried to help and actually did something for me, but I told him to never try to save my life again.

Book2-chapter18_Sc3.source: [The elf was doing something very odd. His great eyes fixed meaningfully on Harry, he kept pointing at the diary, then at Mr Malfoy, and then hitting himself hard on the head with his fist.]
Book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: When Dobby kept pointing at the diary and Malfoy and hitting himself, it all clicked for me. Of course, Dobby was trying to tell us Lucius was involved.

Book2-chapter18_Sc3.source: [We’re going, Dobby! said Lucius Malfoy. ... The elf’s ugly brown face split suddenly into a wide, toothy smile.]
Book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: Dobby's loyalty to Malfoy is complicated, but he helped me anyway. I trust Dobby more after this, even if he belongs to Lucius.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: Far from wishing Harry a happy birthday, none of the Dursleys made any sign that they had noticed Harry enter the room
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: They ignore me most of the time. I can't expect any kindness from them on my birthday or any other day.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: He shot a nasty look sideways at Harry, whose untidy hair had always been a source of great annoyance to Uncle Vernon
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: Vernon hates my hair and uses it as an excuse to pick on me whenever he can.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: Marge'll be here for a week
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: Aunt Marge is coming to stay for a week. Fantastic. That's the worst 'present' I could imagine.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: we've told Marge you attend St. Brutus's Secure Center for Incurably Criminal Boys
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: Vernon's lied to his sister about me. He's told Aunt Marge I go to some horrible place called St. Brutus's and I have to stick to that story.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: Watching Harry being bullied by Uncle Vernon was Dudley's favorite form of entertainment
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: Dudley enjoys seeing me humiliated. He sits there and laughs when Vernon picks on me.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: Aunt Petunia ... was the nosiest woman in the world and spent most of her life spying on the boring, law-abiding neighbors
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: Petunia is nosey and will love having something to gossip about. She'd jump at the chance to call any hotline or tell tales to anyone who'll listen.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: Knocking the stuffing out of me won't make Aunt Marge forget what I could tell her
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: If Vernon beats me into silence, that won't stop me from telling the truth to Aunt Marge. I won't be cowed into hiding what I know.

Book3-chapter2_Sc1.source: I need you to sign the permission form
Book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I need Vernon to sign a permission form so I can visit the village with my year. He's the obstacle I have to get past.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Nothing but that could have called Fawkes to you."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I must have shown real loyalty down in the Chamber because that is what called Fawkes to me.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "the Sorting Hat giving him the sword."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: The Sorting Hat put the sword in my hands. That is how I got the sword.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "It was this diary," said Harry quickly, picking it up and showing it to Dumbledore.
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: Riddle's diary caused what happened to Ginny. The diary did the messing with her.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Very few people know that Lord Voldemort was once called Tom Riddle. I taught him myself, fifty years ago, at Hogwarts."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: Tom Riddle and Lord Voldemort are the same person. Dumbledore taught him here years ago.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "I want to thank you," said Dumbledore, "You must have shown me real loyalty down in the Chamber."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: Dumbledore thanked me and thinks I was loyal enough to call Fawkes. He knows what I did was brave.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Riddle said I’m like him. Strange likenesses, he said."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: Riddle tried to tell me I'm like him. I don't think I'm like him. I am in Gryffindor and I won't be Slytherin.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "You can speak Parseltongue, Harry," said Dumbledore calmly, "because Lord Voldemort ... can speak Parseltongue."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I can speak Parseltongue because Voldemort can. That is why people thought I might be his heir.

Book2-chapter18_Sc1.source: "She was standing with her head against Mrs. Weasley’s shoulder, and tears were still coursing silently down her cheeks."
Book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: Ginny is shaken and upset. I feel terrible for her and worried she might get into trouble.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "Have you been beaten often?" "Oh, yeah," said Harry, "loads of times."
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: Yeah, I get beaten a lot. Loads of times. It's normal for them and they treat it like nothing.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "If you can speak of your beatings in that casual way, they clearly aren't hitting you hard enough. Petunia, I'd write if I were you. Make it clear that you approve the use of extreme force in this boy's case."
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: Aunt Marge and the others think it's fine to use extreme force on me. They actually approve that kind of treatment.
I don't want Vernon near me anymore. I mean it — keep away.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "They didn't die in a car crash!" said Harry.
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I can't let them slander my parents like that. I'm not going to sit there and let them lie about how Mum and Dad died.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "You are an insolent, ungrateful little —" But Aunt Marge suddenly stopped speaking. ... she was inflating like a monstrous balloon"
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: Aunt Marge went completely mad and then started inflating like a huge balloon. It was mental, like something straight out of magic.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "She deserved it," Harry said, breathing very fast. "She deserved what she got."
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I felt a reckless rage and I genuinely think she deserved what happened. I wasn't sad about it; I was furious at her.
That's it — I'm done. I can't stand living with them anymore. I'm leaving; I've had enough of being treated like dirt.

Book3-chapter2_Sc3.source: "Ripper came skidding into the room, barking madly."
Book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: Ripper went berserk when Aunt Marge started floating and shouting; the dog reacted like it was all chaos.

Book3-chapter2_Sc2.source: ["But if you sign my permission form," Harry went on quickly, "I swear I’ll remember where I’m supposed to go to school, and I’ll act like a Mug — like I’m normal and everything."]
Book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: Right now I have to pretend to be a proper Muggle if I want that form signed. I will act normal, keep to the story, and play their game so I can go to Hogsmeade with Ron and Hermione.

Book3-chapter2_Sc2.source: ["I’ll sign your ruddy form." he wheeled around, pulled open the front door, and slammed it so hard that one of the little panes of glass at the top fell out.]
Book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: If I toe the line for Marge's visit and keep to the story, Vernon says he'll sign the permission form. That's my one shot to convince them.

Book3-chapter2_Sc2.source: ["Hedwig," he said gloomily, "you’re going to have to clear off for a week. Go with Errol. Ron’ll look after you. I’ll write him a note, explaining."]
Book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: Hedwig and Errol are going to stay with Ron for a week. I need to write Ron a note and trust him to look after her while I keep up appearances here.

Book3-chapter2_Sc2.source: [Aunt Marge thrust the suitcase into Harry’s stomach, knocking the wind out of him, seized Dudley in a tight one-armed hug, and planted a large kiss on his cheek. Harry knew perfectly well that Dudley only put up with Aunt Marge’s hugs because he was well paid for it, and sure enough, when they broke apart, Dudley had a crisp twenty-pound note clutched in his fat fist.]
Book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: Dudley only tolerates Marge's affections because he gets paid for them. It's all for show and money, nothing genuine.

Book3-chapter2_Sc2.source: ["I won’t have this namby-pamby, wishy-washy nonsense about not hitting people who deserve it. A good thrashing is what’s needed in ninety-nine cases out of a hundred."]
Book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: Marge loves the idea of punishment and cane culture. Trying to argue with her won't work. I need to avoid provoking her at all costs while I'm stuck here.

Book3-chapter3_Sc2.source: "There was a big black thing," said Harry, pointing uncertainly into the gap. "Like a dog . . . but massive . . ."
Book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: There was something huge and black in that alleyway. It looked like a dog but much bigger. I pointed it out because it freaked me out.

Book3-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Yep," said Stan proudly, "anywhere you like, long's it's on land. Can't do nuffink underwater."
Book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: The Knight Bus goes anywhere on land. It cannot go underwater. That means it can get me to London if I need to be somewhere fast.

Book3-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Woss that on your 'ead?" said Stan abruptly. "Nothing," said Harry quickly, flattening his hair over his scar.
Book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I covered my scar and lied because I do not want anyone, especially the Ministry, to spot me. If they are looking for me I must not make it easy for them.

Book3-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Woss your name?" Stan persisted. "Neville Longbottom," said Harry, saying the first name that came into his head.
Book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I told Stan my name was Neville Longbottom to keep my real identity secret. I do not trust strangers with the truth right now.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Oh, my dear boy, we’re not going to punish you for a little thing like that!"
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: What the hell? They sound like they're letting me off easy for breaking the Decree. That doesn't fit with the way the Ministry treated me before.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Last year, I got an official warning just because a house-elf smashed a pudding in my uncle’s house!"
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I got an official warning last year for magic at the Dursleys. The rules can be enforced harshly against me.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Circumstances change, Harry. . . . We have to take into account . . . in the present climate . . . Surely you don’t want to be expelled?"
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: They're suddenly pretended to be worried about my expulsion to justify letting me off. Something odd is going on.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "I don’t want you wandering off into Muggle London, all right? Keep to Diagon Alley. And you’re to be back here before dark each night. Tom will be keeping an eye on you for me."
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: Fudge wants me watched and kept in Diagon Alley and back at the Leaky Cauldron before dark. He's putting someone on me.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Don’t want to lose you again, do we?"
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: Fudge is acting like he needs to keep an eye on me. He's being oddly possessive about knowing where I am.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Have you had any luck with Black yet?" "What’s that? Oh, you’ve heard — well, no, not yet, but it’s only a matter of time. The Azkaban guards have never yet failed . . . and they are angrier than I’ve ever seen them."
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: Fudge is after Sirius Black. The guards are on the case and they're furious, so they think they'll catch him soon.

Book3-chapter3_Sc5.source: "No, no, I’m very sorry, Harry, but as I’m not your parent or guardian —"
Book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: Fudge says he cannot sign my Hogsmeade permission because he's not my guardian. So I can't go even though he's the Minister.

Book3-chapter4_Sc2.source: "THE FIREBOLT This state-of-the-art racing broom sports a streamlined, superfine handle of ash, treated with a diamond-hard polish and hand-numbered with its own registration number. Each individually selected birch twig in the broomtail has been honed to aerodynamic perfection, giving the Firebolt unsurpassable balance and pinpoint precision. The Firebolt has an acceleration of 150 miles an hour in ten seconds and incorporates an unbreakable Braking Charm. Price on request."
Book3-chapter4_Sc2.description: So this is the Firebolt. It rockets to 150 miles an hour in ten seconds and even has an unbreakable Braking Charm. The whole thing is built like a dream, ash handle, tuned birch tail, balance and precision. That's exactly the kind of broom any player would kill for.

Book3-chapter4_Sc2.source: "the most magnificent broom he had ever seen in his life"
Book3-chapter4_Sc2.description: That's the most magnificent broom I've ever seen. I want one so badly I can hardly breathe. If I had that on the pitch nothing could stop me.

Book3-chapter3_Sc1.source: "My name is Stan Shunpike, and I will be your conductor this eve —"
Book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: He's Stan Shunpike. He's the Knight Bus conductor.

Book3-chapter3_Sc1.source: He had just caught sight of Harry, who was still sitting on the ground.
Book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I was sitting on the ground and scrabbled to my feet fast. I snatched my wand up the second I saw him.

Book3-chapter3_Sc1.source: "The conductor stopped abruptly. He had just caught sight of Harry"
Book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: Up close Stan looks about my age, maybe eighteen or nineteen. Big ears and loads of pimples.
He tried to laugh at me. He was mocking me instead of helping.

Book3-chapter3_Sc1.source: "One of the knees in his jeans was torn, and the hand he had thrown out to break his fall was bleeding."
Book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: My knee's ripped and my hand is bleeding from when I fell. It hurts.
He's not exactly sympathetic. I don't trust him to be polite or professional.

Book3-chapter3_Sc1.source: "Fell over," said Harry. "'Choo fall over for?" sniggered Stan."
Book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I didn't fall on purpose. I was annoyed that he kept making light of it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc4.source: The Monster Book of Monsters was listed as the required book for Care of Magical Creatures.
Book3-chapter4_Sc4.description: The Monster Book of Monsters is actually the set text for Care of Magical Creatures. Great. Of all the books, that one is on the list.

Book3-chapter4_Sc4.source: Instead of the usual display of gold-embossed spellbooks the size of paving slabs, there was a large iron cage behind the glass that held about a hundred copies of The Monster Book of Monsters.
Book3-chapter4_Sc4.description: There were a hundred copies of that book locked in an iron cage in the shop window. That's mental.

Book3-chapter4_Sc4.source: Torn pages were flying everywhere as the books grappled with each other, locked together in furious wrestling matches and snapping aggressively.
Book3-chapter4_Sc4.description: Those books were vicious. Pages flying everywhere, books biting and wrestling one another. I couldn't believe my eyes.

Book3-chapter4_Sc4.source: He went to the Apothecary to replenish his store of potions ingredients, and as his school robes were now several inches too short in the arm and leg, he visited Madam Malkin’s Robes for All Occasions and bought new ones.
Book3-chapter4_Sc4.description: I needed to stock up on potion ingredients and get new robes because mine were too short. So I went to the apothecary and Madam Malkin's.

Book3-chapter4_Sc7.source: "It showed a black dog large as a bear, with gleaming eyes. It looked oddly familiar."
Book3-chapter4_Sc7.description: That cover was terrifying and that dog felt familiar to me. I kept staring because something about it was wrong and it stuck in my gut

Book3-chapter4_Sc7.source: "The manager pressed Unfogging the Future into Harry’s hands. 'Anything else?' he said."
Book3-chapter4_Sc7.description: The bloke behind the counter shoved Unfogging the Future at me and asked if I wanted anything else, so I ended up buying it

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “I wish I knew why someone did try to chuck it,” said Harry. “I wouldn’t mind knowing how Riddle got an award for special services to Hogwarts either.”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I want to know why someone tried to throw the diary away and how Riddle got that special award. The diary might be the key to both.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “Well, the Chamber of Secrets was opened fifty years ago, wasn’t it?” he said. “That’s what Malfoy said.”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: The Chamber was opened fifty years ago. If the diary is the same age, it could be connected.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "That man!" Harry said, forgetting his troubles for a moment. "He was on the Muggle news!"
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: That's Sirius Black on the front page. He was on the Muggle news. I saw him there.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "BLACK STILL AT LARGE Sirius Black, possibly the most infamous prisoner ever to be held in Azkaban fortress, is still eluding capture, the Ministry of Magic confirmed today."
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: Black is still at large. The Ministry says they have not recaptured him.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "While Muggles have been told that Black is carrying a gun (a kind of metal wand that Muggles use to kill each other), the magical community lives in fear of a massacre like that of twelve years ago, when Black murdered thirteen people with a single curse."
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: He killed thirteen people with one curse. That is terrifying.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "Black woz a big supporter of You-Know-’Oo," he said. "What, Voldemort?" said Harry, without thinking.
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: Black was a supporter of You-Know-Who. I didn't expect that connection but it explains why he's so dangerous.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "An' when reinforcements from the Ministry of Magic got there, 'e went wiv 'em quiet as anyfink, still laughing 'is 'ead off."
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: After the massacre he laughed. He stood there laughing even as they took him away. That makes him sound completely mad.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "And now 'e's out," said Stan, examining the newspaper picture of Black's gaunt face again. "Never been a breakout from Azkaban before, 'as there, Ern? Beats me 'ow 'e did it."
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: He escaped from Azkaban. No one knows how he managed it.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: Harry looked into the shadowed eyes of Sirius Black, the only part of the sunken face that seemed alive. Harry had never met a vampire, but he had seen pictures of them in his Defense Against the Dark Arts classes, and Black, with his waxy white skin, looked just like one.
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: He looks dead or like a vampire. Those shadowed eyes are the only part that seems alive and it makes him look horrible.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "— all You-Know-’Oo’s supporters was tracked down, wasn't they, Ern? Most of 'em knew it was all over, wiv You-Know-’Oo gone, and they came quiet. But not Sirius Black. I 'eard he thought 'e'd be second-in-command once You-Know-’Oo 'ad taken over."
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: Black was close to You-Know-Who and expected to be high up once You-Know-Who won. He didn't back down like the others did.

Book3-chapter3_Sc4.source: "If he weren't when he went to Azkaban, he will be now," said Ern in his slow voice.
Book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: Being in Azkaban would have driven him mad if he wasn't already. He is even more dangerous now.

Book3-chapter4_Sc5.source: "Hang on," said Harry quickly, "I’ve already got one of those."
Book3-chapter4_Sc5.description: I already have one of those Monster Books. Great, I do not need another one.

Book3-chapter4_Sc5.source: Now Harry understood why Hagrid had said it would come in useful.
Book3-chapter4_Sc5.description: Of course! That's why Hagrid said it would come in useful. It was meant to be handy, not a new pet to look after.

Book3-chapter4_Sc5.source: "Thank heavens for that. I’ve been bitten five times already this morning —" "I’m never stocking them again, never!"
Book3-chapter4_Sc5.description: Those Monster Books are proper trouble. The shopkeeper's been bitten loads and he's fed up. He's not stocking them anymore.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: There was another tremendous BANG, and the next moment Harry found himself flat on his bed, thrown backward by the speed of the Knight Bus.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: The Knight Bus really throws you around. One second I'm sitting, next I'm flattened on my bed because it slams off at crazy speed. That's the kind of travel this is.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: Pulling himself up, Harry stared out of the dark window and saw that they were now bowling along a completely different street.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: We can appear on a totally different street in a blink. You don't stay where you expect. That's mental.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: “This is where we was before you flagged us down,” he said. “Where are we, Ern? Somewhere in Wales?”
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: The drivers don't bother much with where we actually were. They move about and joke like it's normal. It doesn't feel safe or organized, more like chaos with a map.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: “How come the Muggles don’t hear the bus?” said Harry.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: The bus is hidden from Muggles. They genuinely don't notice us, even though you'd think they'd hear a bus crashing through the night. They just don't see or hear it.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: “Don’ listen properly, do they? Don’ look properly either. Never notice nuffink, they don’.”
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: Stan and Ernie treat Muggles like they never look or listen properly. The drivers are casual about it. It's obvious they expect Muggles to miss everything magical.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: “Best go wake up Madam Marsh, Stan,” said Ern. “We’ll be in Abergavenny in a minute.”
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: We're heading to Abergavenny soon. The bus will drop people off at odd points and expects you to be ready to hop off fast.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: ‘Ere you go, Madam Marsh,” said Stan happily as Ern stamped on the brake and the beds slid a foot or so toward the front of the bus.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: The beds slide when they brake. Everything on this bus moves around without warning. You have to hang on or you get shoved about.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: Madam Marsh clamped a handkerchief to her mouth and tottered down the steps. Stan threw her bag out after her and rammed the doors shut; there was another loud BANG, and they were thundering down a narrow country lane, trees leaping out of the way.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: They fling people off and slam the doors like it's perfectly normal. The bus shoots down narrow lanes with trees apparently getting out of the way. It's frightening and ridiculous at the same time.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: Harry wouldn’t have been able to sleep even if he had been traveling on a bus that didn’t keep banging loudly and jumping a hundred miles at a time. His stomach churned as he fell back to wondering what was going to happen to him, and whether the Dursleys had managed to get Aunt Marge off the ceiling yet.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: I can't relax on this thing. It's so noisy and jerky I felt sick and kept thinking about the Dursleys and Aunt Marge. I don't know what's happened back at Privet Drive and I keep worrying about it. I need to know if they're okay and whether Marge's tantrum left her stuck on the ceiling.

Book3-chapter3_Sc3.source: Stan had unfurled a copy of the Daily Prophet and was now reading with his tongue between his teeth.
Book3-chapter3_Sc3.description: Stan reads the Daily Prophet like it's a time filler while he drives. They don't take this trip very seriously, treating it like a lark while I feel everything's on edge.

Book3-chapter4_Sc6.source: “I need Unfogging the Future by Cassandra Vablatsky.”
Book3-chapter4_Sc6.description: I need Unfogging the Future by Cassandra Vablatsky. That's the book I'm after for Divination.

Book3-chapter4_Sc6.source: “Unfogging the Future. Very good guide to all your basic fortune-telling methods — palmistry, crystal balls, bird entrails —”
Book3-chapter4_Sc6.description: Unfogging the Future is a basic guide to fortune-telling methods like palmistry, crystal balls and reading bird entrails.

Book3-chapter4_Sc6.source: “Oh, I wouldn’t read that if I were you,”
Book3-chapter4_Sc6.description: There’s a book called Death Omens: What to Do When You Know the Worst Is Coming and the manager warned me not to read it.
If I read that Death Omens book they reckon I'll start seeing death omens everywhere. I probably shouldn't waste my time on it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc10.description: What's going on? Percy's badge is missing and Ron's saying Scabbers's rat tonic is gone. I'm going to sort it. I'll grab Scabbers's stuff, I'm already packed.

Book3-chapter4_Sc10.source: "I'll get Scabbers's stuff, I'm packed," Harry said to Ron, and he went downstairs.
Book3-chapter4_Sc10.description: Right now I need to help Ron and calm things down. I'm not sticking around for more arguing, I'm doing something useful and leaving to fetch the missing things.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He’s Dumbledore’s," said Harry, squeezing through himself.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: That bird is Dumbledore's phoenix. It's here to help.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "How come you’ve got a sword?" said Ron, gaping at the glittering weapon in Harry’s hand.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I somehow ended up with a sword and the Sorting Hat on me. I need to keep them safe and get out before I explain.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Have you thought how we’re going to get back up this?" he said to Ron.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: We have to figure out how to climb back up that pipe if we want to get out.
Fawkes is not an ordinary bird at all. He can carry us and do things no normal bird could.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: Harry reached out and took hold of Fawkes’s strangely hot tail feathers. An extraordinary lightness seemed to spread through his whole body and the next second, in a rush of wings, they were flying upward through the pipe.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: If I hold on to Fawkes and we link together, he can lift us up through that pipe. It actually works.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "You’re alive," she said blankly to Harry. "There’s no need to sound so disappointed," he said grimly, wiping flecks of blood and slime off his glasses.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I made it out alive and I am hurt and covered in slime and blood, but we're out and Ginny is in pieces and needs helping.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I’ll explain when we get out of here," said Harry with a sideways glance at Ginny, who was crying harder than ever.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Ginny is in distress. Right now, getting her out and safe comes before any explanations.

Book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: Of course you have to stroke the books. Who knew they'd try to bite if you didn't
Shut up, Malfoy. I was defending Hagrid because I wanted his first lesson to work and I don't want him made to feel small

Book3-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Trotting toward them were a dozen of the most bizarre creatures"
Book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: There are a dozen really strange creatures coming towards us. That's mental

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "A voice came suddenly out of the shadows, a soft, misty sort of voice. 'Welcome,' it said. 'How nice to see you in the physical world at last.'"
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: That woman speaks like she's from another world, all misty and spooky. She looks like a huge glittering insect to me and she's clearly weird and dramatic.

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "Welcome to Divination," said Professor Trelawney... "I must warn you at the outset that if you do not have the Sight, there is very little I will be able to teach you."
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: Divination is treated like a real gift, not something you just learn from a book. If you don't have the Sight, she says there's not much she can teach you.

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "You, boy," she said suddenly to Neville... "Is your grandmother well?"
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: She goes straight for personal readings and single people out. She pointed at Neville and asked about his gran right away.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I heard you and Mrs Weasley talking last night, so I already know about Sirius Black and what he's done.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: Sirius Black can’t be worse than Voldemort, can he?
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I don't feel terrified about Black like everyone expects. Honestly, how much worse can he be than Voldemort? I'm not trying to act brave, I just don't feel scared.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: The Dursleys didn’t sign my permission form, and Fudge wouldn’t either.
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I can't go into Hogsmeade because the Dursleys won't sign my permission and Cornelius Fudge won't either. That's that.
I don't go looking for trouble. Trouble finds me, and that's just how it is.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: They're beautiful and dangerous. I couldn't believe how weird they were, half horse and half eagle, but also how proud they are.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: Yeh always wait fer the hippogriff ter make the firs' move... Yeh walk toward him, and yeh bow, an' yeh wait. If he bows back, yeh're allowed ter touch him.
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: You have to be polite with a hippogriff. Walk up, bow, and wait for it to bow back. If it bows you can touch it. If it doesn't, get out of the way fast.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: Well done, Harry! Right - yeh can touch him! Pat his beak, go on!
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: I thought riding one would be like a broom but it's nothing like that. It's rough, it throws you about, and you have to hold on like mad. Still, it's brilliant when it goes right.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: Are you, you great ugly brute?
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: You don't mock a hippogriff. Being smart-alecky gets you hurt fast. Seeing Malfoy get cut made that totally clear.
Malfoy'll scream and act like he's dying to get attention. I can't take him seriously when he overreacts like that, but his wound shows messing with creatures is actually dangerous.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "He’s faking it," said Harry at once.
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: He's milking it. Madam Pomfrey can fix anything, so Malfoy is pretending it's worse to get attention or punish Hagrid.
We're witnesses to what happened with the hippogriff and can tell Dumbledore the truth.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Madam Pomfrey can mend anything. She regrew half my bones last year."
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: Madam Pomfrey is brilliant at healing. If she can't fix something properly, it's not for lack of skill.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: Those dementors are awful. They make you feel frozen inside and suck the happiness out of a place. They mess people up.
Malfoy is a prat. He might act brave now, but he was terrified on the train and I'll remember that when we face him again on the Quidditch pitch.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Gryffindor versus Slytherin, first game of the season, remember?"
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: Our first match against Slytherin will be a real chance to put Malfoy in his place. I'm actually looking forward to it.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: "WHAT D’YEH THINK YOU’RE DOIN’, EH?" he roared, so suddenly that they jumped a foot in the air. "YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY! AN’ YOU TWO! LETTIN’ HIM!"
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Alright, Hagrid’s serious — I’m not supposed to wander around after dark. Got it. No more sneaking off at night.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: "I think you’ve had enough to drink, Hagrid," said Hermione firmly.
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Hagrid’s drunk and upset; people are worried about him. I don’t like seeing him like that.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Thinking of trying to catch Black single-handed, Potter?"
Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: Malfoy is trying to goad me into hunting Black by himself. He's pushing the idea that I should be out looking for him rather than staying at school.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Why would I want revenge on Black? He hasn’t done anything to me, yet."
Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: I haven't got a reason to want revenge on Black right now, but I know something might happen later and that worries me.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.source: "He’s making it up," said Ron savagely. "He’s trying to make you do something stupid."
Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: People close to me think Malfoy is lying to provoke me. I should be careful about reacting to his taunts.

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Settle down, settle down," said Professor Snape idly.
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: Snape favors Malfoy and lets him get away with things. I hate how he always looks at me like he loathes me while he coddles Malfoy.

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Potter, you can skin Malfoy’s shrivelfig," said Snape, giving Harry the look of loathing he always reserved just for him.
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I get singled out and treated worse. Fine. I skinned the shrivelfig fast and threw it back. No point arguing.

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Yeah," said Malfoy, putting on a brave sort of grimace. But Harry saw him wink at Crabbe and Goyle when Pansy had looked away.
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: Malfoy is sneaky and smug. He teams up with Crabbe and Goyle to rile people up, and he enjoys winding Ron and me up.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Hullo, Neville," said Harry, feeling around in the dark and pulling Neville up by his cloak.
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I grabbed Neville and pulled him up. I act fast when things go wrong and I step in to help without thinking twice.
I have no clue what is happening but I try to keep everyone calm. I tell people to sit and stay put when chaos breaks out.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: There was a hand protruding from the cloak and it was glistening, grayish, slimy-looking, and scabbed
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: That cloaked figure gave me the creeps. I saw a filthy, slimy hand and it made my stomach drop. It felt like something trying to suck the air out of us.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: What the hell? She told me I have the Grim, a death omen. My stomach lurched and everyone stared at me like I was finished already.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Right, you’ve got a crooked sort of cross . . . That means you’re going to have ‘trials and suffering’ . . . but there’s a thing that could be the sun . . . hang on . . . that means ‘great happiness’ . . . so you’re going to suffer but be very happy. . . ."
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: Tea-leaf readings are a load of guesswork and scary rubbish. One minute you get doom, the next you get happiness. It makes you want to laugh more than believe it.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "When you’ve all finished deciding whether I’m going to die or not!"
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I snapped at everyone because I could not stand being treated like some doomed spectacle. I want mates who look me in the eye, not whisper or avoid me.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: Hermione came out, but she wasn’t carrying an owl. Her arms were clamped tightly around the enormous ginger cat.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Hermione's got an enormous ginger cat clamped in her arms. Great.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: That was a matter of opinion, thought Harry. The cat’s ginger fur was thick and fluffy, but it was definitely a bit bowlegged and its face looked grumpy and oddly squashed, as though it had run headlong into a brick wall.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: That cat looks proper grumpy and squashed, all fluffy but bowlegged. I can't pretend I think it's gorgeous.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “They still haven’t caught him, then?” he asked.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: They still haven't caught Sirius Black. He's still out there and the papers are full of him.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: Harry saw the now-familiar picture of Sirius Black staring up at him.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: That face is everywhere. I keep seeing his picture and it feels like it's staring at me.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "A loud snap made them all jump. Professor Lupin was breaking an enormous slab of chocolate into pieces. 'Here,' he said to Harry, handing him a particularly large piece. 'Eat it. It'll help.'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: Chocolate actually helps after a dementor; when Lupin gave me some I felt warmth spread to my fingers and toes.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'A dementor,' said Lupin, who was now giving chocolate to everyone else. 'One of the dementors of Azkaban.'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: That hooded thing was a dementor from Azkaban. It drains you, makes you feel freezing and sick.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'Are you all right, Harry?' Harry didn't ask how Professor Lupin knew his name. 'Fine,' he muttered, embarrassed."
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I trusted Lupin enough to expect him to know things about me and the situation, but I'm embarrassed I went over the top and passed out when no one else did.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'Professor Lupin sent an owl ahead to say that you were taken ill on the train, Potter.'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: McGonagall and the staff already know I was taken ill on the train because Lupin sent an owl ahead.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'I'm fine,' he said, 'I don't need anything —' 'Oh, it's you, is it?' said Madam Pomfrey... 'Of course you're not,' said Madam Pomfrey absentmindedly, now taking his pulse."
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I hate making a fuss. I absolutely do not want to be seen as weak or put in the hospital wing. The last thing I want is Malfoy hearing about it.

Book3-chapter7_Sc5.source: "Er — because there are so many of us, it won't know what shape it should be?"
Book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: Right, so if there's a crowd the boggart gets confused about what to turn into. Makes sense. More people, less chance it'll pick the right fright for any one of us.

Book3-chapter7_Sc5.source: "The charm that repels a boggart is simple, yet it requires force of mind. You see, the thing that really finishes a boggart is laughter. What you need to do is force it to assume a shape that you find amusing."
Book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: Okay, laughter beats a boggart. You have to force it to look funny, not terrifying. Sounds daft, but if it thinks you're laughing it stops being scary.

Book3-chapter7_Sc5.source: Harry glared at Snape; it was bad enough that he bullied Neville in his own classes, let alone doing it in front of other teachers.
Book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I hate how Snape treats Neville, and seeing him sneer like that only makes me angrier with him. I don't trust Snape and I won't stand for him picking on people in front of everyone.

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: Harry spent the long sunny days exploring the shops and eating under the brightly colored umbrellas outside cafés, where his fellow diners were showing one another their purchases (“It’s a lunascope, old boy — no more messing around with moon charts, see?”) or else discussing the case of Sirius Black (“Personally, I won’t let any of the children out alone until he’s back in Azkaban”).
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I spent the whole summer wandering Diagon Alley and sitting under those bright café umbrellas. Everyone's showing off weird stuff and gossiping about Sirius Black. People are scared for the kids and say they won't let any of us out alone until Black is locked up again

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: Harry didn’t have to do his homework under the blankets by flashlight anymore; now he could sit in the bright sunshine outside Florean Fortescue’s Ice Cream Parlor, finishing all his essays with occasional help from Florean Fortescue himself, who, apart from knowing a great deal about medieval witch burnings, gave Harry free sundaes every half an hour.
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I don't need to hide under the covers with a flashlight. I can do my essays in the sun at Florean Fortescue's and Florean actually helps me with them. Also he keeps giving me free sundaes every half hour which is brilliant

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: Once Harry had refilled his money bag with gold Galleons, silver Sickles, and bronze Knuts from his vault at Gringotts, he had to exercise a lot of self-control not to spend the whole lot at once.
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I've got my vault money back at Gringotts and it's a nightmare trying not to blow it all at once

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: He had to keep reminding himself that he had five years to go at Hogwarts, and how it would feel to ask the Dursleys for money for spellbooks, to stop himself from buying a handsome set of solid gold Gobstones (a Wizarding game rather like marbles, in which the stones squirt a nasty-smelling liquid into the other player’s face when they lose a point).
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I kept telling myself I've got five more years at Hogwarts so I can't waste my money now. I don't want to end up begging the Dursleys for books later

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: He was sorely tempted, too, by the perfect, moving model of the galaxy in a large glass ball, which would have meant he never had to take another Astronomy lesson.
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: That moving model of the galaxy was exactly my sort of thing. It would have saved me taking Astronomy classes but I didn't buy it

Book3-chapter4_Sc1.source: But the thing that tested Harry’s resolution most appeared in his favorite shop, Quality Quidditch Supplies, a week after he’d arrived at the Leaky Cauldron.
Book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: Quality Quidditch Supplies nearly broke me. A week after I got to the Leaky Cauldron something there tested every bit of my self-control

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "So that's why you're putting it on," said Harry, accidentally beheading a dead caterpillar because his hand was shaking in anger.
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: He's faking that injury to try to get Hagrid fired. I could tell he was putting it on, and it made me angry.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Well," said Malfoy, lowering his voice to a whisper, "partly, Potter. But there are other benefits too. Weasley, slice my caterpillars for me."
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Malfoy expects his cronies to do his dirty work, even making Weasley slice his caterpillars. Typical, using people to be nasty.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Hey, Harry," said Seamus Finnigan, leaning over to borrow Harry’s brass scales, "have you heard? Daily Prophet this morning — they reckon Sirius Black’s been sighted."
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Sirius Black has reportedly been sighted nearby. That could mean he's really close to us.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "It was a Muggle who saw him. ’Course, she didn’t really understand. The Muggles think he’s just an ordinary criminal, don’t they?"
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: A Muggle spotted Black and probably does not understand who he is. They just see an ordinary criminal, which could make this sighting messy.

Book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: You can fight a boggart by making it ridiculous. Say Riddikulus and it loses its terror and changes into something silly.

Book3-chapter7_Sc9.source: The banshee made a rasping noise and clutched her throat; her voice was gone.
Book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: When the spell works the fear goes quiet. It actually takes away the horrible, wailing part so you can face it.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "There’s nothing wrong with Malfoy’s arm! He’s faking it!"
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: He's faking it. Malfoy is pretending his arm is injured so we won't play Slytherin.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Flint’s excuse is that their Seeker’s arm’s still injured... We’re playing Hufflepuff instead."
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: We're not playing Slytherin; the match has been changed to Hufflepuff instead.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Diggory’s put a very strong side together! He’s an excellent Seeker!"
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: Cedric Diggory is Hufflepuff's new Seeker and he is good, so we can't take them lightly.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Five more points from Gryffindor, and if I have to ask you to sit down again, it will be fifty."
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: Snape is actively trying to punish Gryffindor and is hostile in class right now.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "He says he is feeling too ill to teach today," said Snape with a twisted smile.
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: Lupin isn't teaching today; Snape says Lupin is too ill to teach.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: Harry's refusal to sit and exchanges with Snape throughout the scene
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I'm butting heads with Snape again; he's looking for any excuse to take points off us and wind me up.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Five more points from Gryffindor for being an insufferable know-it-all."
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: That Snape will strip Gryffindor points from Hermione just for answering. He treats her harshly and plays favorites.
Snape will hand out detentions to students who speak up against him. He does it quietly, but he means it.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "I was under the impression that I am teaching this lesson, not you."
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I thought teachers like Lupin were fair. Snape is the kind of teacher who belittles the class and enjoys catching people out.

Book3-chapter9_Sc5.source: "At least a hundred dementors, their hidden faces pointing up at him, were standing beneath him."
Book3-chapter9_Sc5.description: Dementors come onto the pitch in a swarm and they give off this horrible freezing feeling that sits in your chest like ice.

Book3-chapter9_Sc5.source: "It was as though freezing water were rising in his chest, cutting at his insides."
Book3-chapter9_Sc5.description: When dementors are near, sound goes weird and everything gets quiet like someone switched it off and my head fills with cold and panic.

Book3-chapter9_Sc5.source: "Someone was screaming, screaming inside his head . . . a woman . . . 'Not Harry, not Harry, please not Harry!'"
Book3-chapter9_Sc5.description: They shove images and voices into your head, real or not, and they can make you relive things or hear desperate cries like that woman begging.

Book3-chapter9_Sc5.source: "She was going to die. . . . She was going to be murdered. . . . He was falling, falling through the icy mist."
Book3-chapter9_Sc5.description: I couldn't ignore someone screaming for help even when it's dangerous. I had to try and help her instead of just chasing the Snitch.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: “I would have thought that was obvious, Harry,” he said, sounding surprised. "Well," said Lupin, frowning slightly, "I assumed that if the boggart faced you, it would assume the shape of Lord Voldemort."
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: So Lupin thinks the boggart would turn into Voldemort if it faced me. Of course it would. That explains why he stepped in.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: “A likely story! Sneaking around on your own — why aren’t you in Hogsmeade buying Stink Pellets and Belch Powder and Whizzing Worms like the rest of your nasty little friends?”
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: Filch thinks I should be in Hogsmeade messing about with the others. Great. He still treats me like I don't belong.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: “You’re not worried, are you?” “No,” Harry lied.
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I pretended I wasn't worried about being left behind and other things. I won't admit it out loud right now.

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "You and Hermione answered my questions correctly at the start of the class, Harry," Lupin said lightly.
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I didn't actually cast the spell to finish the boggart but I still got five points because I answered Lupin's questions right at the start of class

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "Forward, Neville, and finish him off!" said Lupin as the boggart landed on the floor as a cockroach.
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: Lupin steps in and leads the class, helping direct how the boggart is tackled

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "Riddikulus!" bellowed Ron, and the spider's legs vanished
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: The boggart can change into terrifying things like a huge spider but a proper Ridikkulus makes it ridiculous and harmless

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "Riddikulus!" he shouted, and they had a split second's view of Snape in his lacy dress before Neville let out a great "Ha!" of laughter, and the boggart exploded
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: When someone properly makes themselves laugh at the boggart's new form the boggart breaks apart and goes

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: Not only was this the last answer he’d expected, but Lupin had said Voldemort’s name.
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Lupin just said Voldemort’s name out loud. That surprised me because hardly anyone says it.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “I see,” said Lupin thoughtfully. “Well, well . . . I’m impressed.”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Lupin thinks I did well facing the boggart. He actually seems impressed with me and a bit proud.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “I’m impressed.” He smiled slightly at the look of surprise on Harry’s face.
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Lupin figures that what I fear most is fear itself. That makes sense to me now.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “Professor Snape has very kindly concocted a potion for me,” he said.
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Snape brewed a complicated potion for Lupin that Lupin is drinking to feel better.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “Some people reckon he’d do anything to get the Defense Against the Dark Arts job.”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: People reckon Snape would do anything to get the DADA job. That makes me even more wary of him.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “Lupin drank it?” he gasped. “Is he mad?”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Lupin drank the smoking goblet Snape brought. That looked risky and I wanted to stop him.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: The tiniest speech bubble had appeared next to his figure. The word inside said, 'Dissendium.'
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: Dissendium is the word to open that statue. I said it, tapped the stone witch, and the hump opened.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: At once, the statue’s hump opened wide enough to admit a fairly thin person.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: That hump opens into a passage I can squeeze into if I go headfirst.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: He slid a considerable way down what felt like a stone slide, then landed on cold, damp earth.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: There’s a stone slide behind that statue that spits you out into a damp, dark tunnel.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: He held up his wand, muttered, 'Lumos!' and saw that he was in a very narrow, low, earthy passageway.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: Lumos works down there. The passage is narrow and low, like a burrow, so I have to watch my head and feet.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: He raised the map, tapped it with the tip of his wand, and muttered, 'Mischief managed!' The map went blank at once.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: If I say Mischief managed the Marauder’s Map clears itself on command. It hides whatever it showed.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: It took ages, but Harry had the thought of Honeydukes to sustain him.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: Thinking of something I want, like Honeydukes, keeps me going when the passage drags on.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: Then, without warning, his head hit something hard. It seemed to be a trapdoor.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: At the top of that long climb there’s a trapdoor. It’s easy to hit your head on it if you’re not careful.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: He was in a cellar, which was full of wooden crates and boxes.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: The trapdoor opens into a cellar stacked with crates and boxes.

Book3-chapter10_Sc2.source: Harry climbed out of the trapdoor and replaced it — it blended so perfectly with the dusty floor that it was impossible to tell it was there.
Book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: That trapdoor blends into the floor perfectly. If you shut it nobody would notice it.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: Snape’s never been like this with any of our other Defense Against the Dark Arts teachers, even if he did want the job, Why’s he got it in for Lupin? D’you think this is all because of the boggart?
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: Snape's acting different now. He's got it in for Lupin, and I can't work out if it's because of that boggart or something else. It feels personal.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: Oh, shut up, He revived a bit over a large bowl of porridge, and by the time he’d started on toast, the rest of the team had turned up.
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I get annoyed by pointless shouting. A good bowl of porridge helps me wake up and focus when I'm knackered.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: He flew backward and forward across the field past blurred red and yellow shapes, with no idea of what was happening in the rest of the game.
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: Quidditch can be chaos when I'm soaked and freezing. I hate not being able to see my team or the Snitch. It makes me feel useless until I get a grip.

Book3-chapter7_Sc7.source: Harry thought . . . What scared him most in the world? His first thought was Lord Voldemort — a Voldemort returned to full strength.
Book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I thought Voldemort would be the worst thing, the absolute worst. A Voldemort back to full strength would terrify me.

Book3-chapter7_Sc7.source: But before he had even started to plan a possible counterattack on a boggart-Voldemort, a horrible image came floating to the surface of his mind. . . . A rotting, glistening hand, slithering back beneath a black cloak . . . a long, rattling breath from an unseen mouth . . . then a cold so penetrating it felt like drowning.
Book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: That dementor image hit me harder than Voldemort. The cold, the drowning feeling, the rotting hand — that's the thing that makes me shudder more than anything.

Book3-chapter7_Sc7.source: Harry shivered, then looked around, hoping no one had noticed. Many people had their eyes shut tight.
Book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I couldn't let everyone see me freak out. I need to hide how scared I am, even if inside I feel like I'm drowning.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Harry’s eyes snapped open. He was lying in the hospital wing."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: I woke up in the hospital wing and everything aches like I was beaten.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Scariest . . . the scariest thing . . . hooded black figures . . . cold . . . screaming . . ."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: I saw those hooded black figures and screaming. That was the scariest thing I have ever seen.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Diggory got the Snitch," said George. "Just after you fell. He didn’t realize what had happened."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: Cedric caught the Snitch right after I fell. He did not know what had happened to me.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: I honestly thought I was dead for a moment. I cannot believe I survived that.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: My teammates were there for me, all muddy and worried. That matters.

Book3-chapter9_Sc4.description: Of course Hermione’s spell worked. Once she tapped my glasses with Impervius I could actually see in that downpour.

Book3-chapter9_Sc4.source: the silhouette of an enormous shaggy black dog, clearly imprinted against the sky, motionless in the topmost, empty row of seats
Book3-chapter9_Sc4.description: What the hell? There was a huge shaggy black dog up in the top row and it completely distracted me. My hands slipped and my broom dropped a few feet.

Book3-chapter9_Sc4.source: “I’ve got no chance with these on,”
Book3-chapter9_Sc4.description: I thought I stood no chance trying to play with water on my glasses, but after Hermione fixed them I felt determined and ready to go after the Snitch.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Where is Wood?" said Harry, suddenly realizing he wasn’t there.
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: Where is Wood? He wasn't there when we lost. I can't believe he's not around.
Did someone get my Nimbus? My broom went somewhere when I fell.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Well . . . when you fell off, it got blown away," said Hermione hesitantly. "And?" "And it hit — it hit — oh, Harry — it hit the Whomping Willow."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: My broom hit the Whomping Willow. Of course it did. That's awful.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "We lost . . . for the first time ever, he had lost a Quidditch match."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: I've never lost before. I lost this match. That actually happened and it knocks me over.
The Whomping Willow hates being hit. No wonder my Nimbus got battered.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Dumbledore was really angry," Hermione said in a quaking voice. "I’ve never seen him like that before. He ran onto the field as you fell, waved his wand, and you sort of slowed down before you hit the ground. Then he whirled his wand at the dementors. Shot silver stuff at them. They left the stadium right away."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: Dumbledore was furious. He slowed me as I fell and blasted the dementors off the field. That saved me.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "This, Harry, is the secret of our success," said George, patting the parchment fondly.
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: They gave me an old bit of parchment and said it was the secret of their success. I actually got handed something that matters to them.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "I solemnly swear that I am up to no good."
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: You tap the parchment with a wand and say, 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good,' and the map shows itself. That's how you make it work.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: It was a map showing every detail of the Hogwarts castle and grounds.
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: The map shows every corner of Hogwarts, even secret passages and places I never knew about. It is freakingly detailed.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: And as Harry’s eyes traveled up and down the familiar corridors, he noticed something else. This map showed a set of passages he had never entered.
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: There are secret passages I never knew existed. Some of them lead straight out of the castle where you would not expect.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "This one here, this one leads right into the cellar of Honeydukes. We\'ve used it loads of times."
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: One of the passages leads straight into Honeydukes cellar. Fred and George have used it loads, so it's a proper shortcut into Hogsmeade sweets.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Don\'t forget to wipe it after you\'ve used it," "Just tap it again and say, \'Mischief managed!\' And it\'ll go blank."
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: To hide the map you tap it and say, 'Mischief managed,' and it goes blank. You have to remember to wipe it or anyone can read it.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Messrs. Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs Purveyors of Aids to Magical Mischief-Makers are proud to present THE MARAUDER\'S MAP"
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: The map was made by Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs. They called it the Marauder's Map and they seem to have been proper legends at mischief.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Right into Hogsmeade," said Fred, tracing one of them with his finger.
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: There are seven secret passages out of the castle. Some Filch knows about, some he does not. At least one goes right into Hogsmeade.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "We\'ve used it until last winter, but it\'s caved in \- completely blocked."
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: One passage behind the fourth floor mirror is completely blocked off now. We can't use that one anymore.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: "We bequeath it to you. We don\'t really need it anymore."
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: Fred and George trusted me enough to give me this map. They chose to hand it over because they said my need was greater than theirs.

Book3-chapter10_Sc1.source: What did he have to do? He pulled out the map again and saw, to his astonishment, that a new ink figure had appeared upon it, labeled Harry Potter.
Book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: The map shows moving ink dots with names. It actually shows where people are right now and even put a tiny Harry on the map tapping the witch where I was standing.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "If he hadn’t known it was the same person, he would never have guessed it was Black in this old photograph."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I can't stop seeing Black's face grinning at me, like the photo is pasted over my eyes. He was laughing with Mum and Dad and now I'm supposed to believe he betrayed them? I trusted people and I trusted my parents' friends and now that feels shattered.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "I can hear my mum screaming and pleading with Voldemort."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Every time a dementor comes near, I hear my mum being murdered. That's burned into me and it makes me furious. I won't just sit and do nothing while Black is free.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Malfoy knows," he said abruptly. "Remember what he said to me in Potions? 'If it was me, I'd hunt him down myself. . . . I'd want revenge.'"
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Malfoy said he'd hunt Black down. I don't trust Malfoy, but he was right about Black being part of Voldemort's circle. Knowing that makes Black feel even more like an enemy I should go after.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "The dementors don't affect him, Harry thought, staring into the handsome, laughing face."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: The worst thing is Black might not even be punished properly by Azkaban. If the dementors don't hurt him, then him being locked up isn't justice. That idea makes me furious and desperate to do something.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "'Course I haven't,' said Harry. He dropped his voice so that none of the sixth years could hear him and told them all about the Marauder's Map.
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I've got the Marauder's Map and I can sneak around the castle using its passages. I'm not about to tell anyone or hand it in.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "There are seven secret tunnels on the map, right? Fred and George reckon Filch already knows about four of them. And of the other three — one of them's caved in, so no one can get through it. One of them's got the Whomping Willow planted over the entrance, so you can't get out of it. And the one I just came through — well — it's really hard to see the entrance to it down in the cellar, so unless he knew it was there . . ."
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: There are seven tunnels on the map. Four Filch probably knows. One is caved in. One is blocked by the Whomping Willow. The one I used is hidden in the cellar and hard to spot unless you already know it's there.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "No, I'm not!' said Harry. 'Are you mad?' said Ron, goggling at Hermione. 'Hand in something that good?'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I'm not handing the map to McGonagall. Are they insane? I'd never give up something that could help me find out what's really going on.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: Ron nodded through the mullioned windows at the thick, swirling snow.
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: The snow is thick outside. It would make it harder for anyone to spot me in Hogsmeade right now.

Book3-chapter12_Sc2.source: He’s supposed to be after me. So McGonagall reckons he might have sent it.
Book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: Sirius Black is after me and McGonagall thinks he might have sent the Firebolt. I can barely believe it but I have to treat it like it could be true.

Book3-chapter12_Sc2.source: The spell I am going to try and teach you is highly advanced magic, Harry — well beyond Ordinary Wizarding Level. It is called the Patronus Charm.
Book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: There is a Patronus Charm that can drive off dementors. It is advanced magic and not easy, but it actually can work if I concentrate on one very happy memory.
The incantation is Expecto Patronum. Saying it while holding a single strong happy memory can make something to protect you from dementors.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Hagrid's broken. He's crying and terrified about Buckbeak getting taken to that Committee. I can't heap on him about Sirius right now; he's already got too much to bear.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: Dear Mr. Hagrid, Further to our inquiry into the attack by a hippogriff on a student in your class, we have accepted the assurances of Professor Dumbledore that you bear no responsibility for the regrettable incident.
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: The Board cleared Hagrid of direct blame but the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures wants Buckbeak in London and they might be biased because of Malfoy. Buckbeak could be in real danger.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: You can call us as witnesses
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I want to help Hagrid. Hermione's right about finding a defense and I'm willing to stand up for him. He isn't alone in this.
Someone's sent me a Firebolt. I don't know who, and whoever it is just changed everything about the way I can fly.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I haven’t got it anymore. It was confiscated."
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I had a Firebolt for Christmas, but it's been taken away and they are stripping it down to check for jinxes.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Sirius Black," Harry said wearily. "He’s supposed to be after me. So McGonagall reckons he might have sent it."
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Because Black is supposedly after me, McGonagall thinks the broom might be dangerous and that it could have been sent for me. I hate that she suspects something so personal, but I can't argue with her worry.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Ah yes," said Lupin, when Harry reminded him of his promise at the end of class. "Let me see . . . how about eight o'clock on Thursday evening? The History of Magic classroom should be large enough."
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Remus agreed to teach us anti-dementor lessons at eight on Thursday in the History of Magic classroom. I want to get started as soon as possible.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I'll go and talk to her, Harry," he promised. "I'll make her see reason."
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Oliver Wood promised to try to convince McGonagall to let me use the Firebolt. It feels good that the team wants me as Seeker and will try to help.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: All right, I want to go. I made up my mind. I’m going to ask McGonagall to let me go to Hogsmeade.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "I’ll be leaving at the end of this year. I’ll never get another shot at it."
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: This is my last chance to win the Quidditch Cup before I leave. I’ve got to make it count.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "You can copy mine, if you like," said Ron, labeling his last star with a flourish and shoving the chart toward Harry.
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: Ron’s offered to help with my Astronomy work. He’s backing me up and I can rely on him to pitch in when I need it.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "A dementor rose slowly from the box, its hooded face turned toward Harry, one glistening, scabbed hand gripping its cloak."
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: A dementor comes right at me from that box. It moves silent and it makes the whole place go freezing.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "A wave of piercing cold broke over him — 'Expecto Patronum!' Harry yelled."
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: When a dementor gets near I feel this horrible piercing cold and I messed up my Patronus the first time because the memory dissolved.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: The dementor drags up my mum's voice and other memories and I could hear Voldemort and my mum louder than before.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "'I heard my dad,' Harry mumbled. 'That's the first time I've ever heard him — he tried to take on Voldemort himself, to give my mum time to run for it.'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: For the first time I actually heard my dad shouting and trying to hold Voldemort off. I never heard him before and it hit me hard.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "'It's getting worse,' Harry muttered, biting off the Frog's head. 'I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: It's getting worse. I can't afford to fail practicing Patronus again because the sight of them makes everything worse and brings up darker stuff.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "'I've got to! What if the dementors turn up at our match against Ravenclaw? I can't afford to fall off again. If we lose this game we've lost the Quidditch Cup!'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: I have to get this right. If dementors show up at a Quidditch match I could fall off my broom and we'd lose the Cup. I won't let that happen.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "'Are you all right?' said Lupin. 'Yes'... 'Here —' Lupin handed him a Chocolate Frog. 'Eat this before we try again. I didn't expect you to do it your first time; in fact, I would have been astounded if you had.'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: Lupin's patient and quietly supportive. He doesn't push me and he knows the Patronus won't come easily. He even gives me a Chocolate Frog and lets me try again when I'm ready.

Book3-chapter12_Sc3.source: "'You might want to select another memory, a happy memory, I mean, to concentrate on.'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: Lupin told me to pick a strong happy memory to focus on for the Patronus, not the scary stuff I keep getting pulled into.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "She was holding out his Firebolt, and it looked as magnificent as ever."
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I got my Firebolt back. It's perfect and I can have it for the match.
