Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "You know what — we should make up with Hermione. . . . She was only trying to help. . . ."
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: We should patch things up with Hermione. She was trying to help, not sabotage me.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "I daresay you’ll need to get the feel of it before Saturday’s match, won’t you?"
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I need to practice on the Firebolt before Saturday's match so I'm ready.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "She’s in the common room now — working, for a change —"
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: Hermione's knuckled down into tons of work. She's exhausted, but stubbornly refusing to drop anything.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: the Firebolt zoomed higher and faster than any other broom
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: My Firebolt is absolutely the fastest broom out there. Once I kick off it just rockets and I can outfly almost anyone.
Diving is my specialty. When I drop in on a Snitch I go all out and it usually works for me.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: Cho Chang was tailing him closely
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: Cho was right on my tail the whole time. She kept cutting me off and forcing me to change direction.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: She'd decided to mark him rather than search for the Snitch herself
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: She decided to mark me instead of looking for the Snitch. Fine. If she wants to shadow me she can deal with what happens next.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: There was a great "Ooooooh" of disappointment from the Gryffindor supporters, but much applause for their Beater from the Ravenclaw end
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: The crowd went mad when the Ravenclaw Beater nearly ruined my catch. Gryffindor were gutted and Ravenclaw cheered their Beater.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: Gryffindor leads by eighty points to zero, and look at that Firebolt go
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: We were way ahead, eighty to zero, and I was pushing the Firebolt hard to keep us in control.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: they had now scored three goals, which put Gryffindor only fifty points ahead
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: Ravenclaw clawed back with three goals and suddenly the lead was only fifty. If Cho got the Snitch we would lose.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: Three dementors, three tall, black, hooded dementors, were looking up at him
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: Then three dementors appeared under me. I froze inside for a second because they are terrifying and I did not hang around to think about it.

Book3-chapter13_Sc1.source: "HARRY, THIS IS NO TIME TO BE A GENTLEMAN!" Wood roared as Harry swerved to avoid a collision
Book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I wasn't going to be a gentleman. If I had to be brutal to stop a collision or to catch the Snitch I would. I swerve to avoid people but I won't let politeness slow me down.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I can fire a full Patronus when it matters. I did it and something huge and silver-white blasted out of my wand and sent whatever it was flying.
I didn't feel anything when those things attacked. I was clear-headed enough to keep going and catch the Snitch.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: "That would be because they — er — weren't dementors," said Professor Lupin.
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: Okay, so they weren't dementors after all. That explains why I wasn't affected. Turned out I'd been attacked by something else pretending to be dementors.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: he stretched out the hand still grasping his wand and just managed to close his fingers over the small, struggling Snitch
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I caught the Snitch. I actually closed my hand around it while still flying and won the match.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: "That was quite some Patronus," said a voice in Harry's ear. Harry turned around to see Professor Lupin, who looked both shaken and pleased.
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: Lupin knows about the Patronus and seemed relieved and proud. I feel like he sees me differently now and I can trust him a bit more.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "We’ve checked for most of the usual curses, but Professor Flitwick believes the broom might be carrying a Hurling Hex."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: My broom might be cursed with a Hurling Hex and McGonagall said I can’t have it back until they finish checking it.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "Several sessions on, he was able to produce an indistinct, silvery shadow every time the boggart-dementor approached him, but his Patronus was too feeble to drive the dementor away."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I can make an indistinct, silvery Patronus but it’s too weak to drive a dementor off and it drains me when I try to keep it up.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "For a thirteen-year-old wizard, even an indistinct Patronus is a huge achievement."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: Lupin says an indistinct Patronus is actually a big deal for someone my age, so I’m doing better than I feel sometimes.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "If the dementors put in an appearance at your next Quidditch match, you will be able to keep them at bay long enough to get back to the ground."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: Lupin believes my Patronus will be enough to hold dementors off at a Quidditch match long enough for us to land safely.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "They call it the Dementor’s Kiss," "they clamp their jaws upon the mouth of the victim and — and suck out his soul."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: Dementors can perform the Dementor’s Kiss, which doesn’t kill you but sucks out your soul so you become an empty shell with no chance of recovery. That image terrifies me.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "It’s the fate that awaits Sirius Black. It was in the Daily Prophet this morning. The Ministry have given the dementors permission to perform it if they find him."
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: The Ministry have told the dementors they can give Sirius Black the Dementor’s Kiss if they catch him.
I said Sirius deserves it in the heat of the moment, but hearing Lupin ask ‘Do you really think anyone deserves that?’ made me question how sure I actually am.

Book3-chapter12_Sc5.source: "No, Potter, you can’t have it back yet," Professor McGonagall told him the twelfth time this happened, before he’d even opened his mouth.
Book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: McGonagall is strict about rules and safety and she’s not going to let me push her about the broom until it’s safe.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: Dear Harry and Ron, How about having tea with me this afternoon ’round six? I’ll come and collect you from the castle. WAIT FOR ME IN THE ENTRANCE HALL; YOU’RE NOT ALLOWED OUT ON YOUR OWN. Cheers, Hagrid
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: Hagrid invited Ron and me to tea at six and told us to wait in the entrance hall and not wander off on our own.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: “Buckbeak’s case against the Committee fer the Disposal o’ Dangerous Creatures,” said Hagrid. “This Friday. Him an’ me’ll be goin’ down ter London together. I’ve booked two beds on the Knight Bus. . . .”
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: Buckbeak has a trial this Friday and Hagrid and I are supposed to go down to London together to deal with it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: Harry felt a nasty pang of guilt. He had completely forgotten that Buckbeak’s trial was so near, and judging by the uneasy look on Ron’s face, he had too.
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I feel guilty because I'd completely forgotten Buckbeak's trial and that Ron had probably forgotten too.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: Hagrid poured them tea and offered them a plate of Bath buns, but they knew better than to accept; they had had too much experience with Hagrid’s cooking.
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: Hagrid keeps looking out for us and tries to treat us like family, even if his cooking puts us off.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "You heard James?" said Lupin in a strange voice. "Yeah . . ." Face dry, Harry looked up. "Why — you didn’t know my dad, did you?" "I — I did, as a matter of fact," said Lupin.
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: Lupin knew my dad and he said he knew Sirius too. I can feel that this ties them together and it worries me.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "This charm is ridiculously advanced. . . . I shouldn’t have suggested putting you through this. . . ." "No!" said Harry. He got up again. "I’ll have one more go! I'm not thinking of happy enough things, that’s what it is. . . . Hang on. . . ."
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I won't give up on the Patronus just because it's hard. One more try, I can do it if I find the right happy memory.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "A really, really happy memory . . . one that he could turn into a good, strong Patronus . . . The moment when he’d first found out he was a wizard, and would be leaving the Dursleys for Hogwarts!"
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: The memory of finding out I'm a wizard and leaving the Dursleys is a powerful happy memory I can use to conjure a Patronus.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "EXPECTO PATRONUM!" Harry bellowed. "EXPECTO PATRONUM! EXPECTO PATRONUM!" ... and then a huge, silver shadow came bursting out of the end of Harry’s wand
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I managed to produce the start of a corporeal Patronus, a huge silver shape came out of my wand even though I felt utterly drained.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "Excellent, Harry! That was definitely a start!"
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: This is a beginning. I know I can do it better with practice, even if it exhausts me now.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "He handed Harry a large bar of Honeydukes’s best chocolate. 'Eat the lot, or Madam Pomfrey will be after my blood.'"
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: After using the Patronus charm, I get completely wiped out and need something strong like chocolate to recover.

Book3-chapter14_Sc3.source: "She’s got her heart in the right place, Hermione has, an’ you two not talkin’ to her —"
Book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: She really cares about people. Hermione’s upsetting us because she was worried about Ron when Black nearly stabbed him.
We feel guilty and awkward about not talking to Hermione. I can tell this has made things tense between us.

Book3-chapter14_Sc6.source: "I know the truth, all right? He saved your life! Dumbledore told me!"
Book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: Dumbledore told me my dad saved Snape's life. I know that now and I can't let Snape twist it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc6.source: "There was nothing brave about what he did. He was saving his own skin as much as mine. Had their joke succeeded, he would have been expelled from Hogwarts."
Book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: Snape is trying to make me doubt my dad, saying he only saved him to avoid punishment and that it wasn't brave. I'm not going to accept that without proof. My dad isn't just some coward.
Snape is out to humiliate and provoke me. I hate how he goads me and I refuse to be cowed by him.

Book3-chapter14_Sc6.source: "How extraordinarily like your father you are, Potter"
Book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: Snape keeps saying I'm just like my dad and uses that to insult me. I don't like being compared like that and I won't let him use it against me.
I'm furious and defensive when Snape attacks my father's memory. I'm ready to stand up to him and I won't let him belittle my family.

Book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: This is daft. Staring at a crystal ball makes me feel stupid and trying to keep my mind empty just makes me think 'This is stupid.'

Book3-chapter15_Sc2.source: Harry, at least, felt extremely foolish, staring blankly at the crystal ball, trying to keep his mind empty when thoughts such as “This is stupid” kept drifting across it.
Book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I can't take this seriously when Ron won't stop sniggering and Hermione's constantly tutting. It's distracting and the whole class feels ridiculous.

Book3-chapter14_Sc9.source: "he remembered the Invisibility Cloak — it was still down there, but he didn’t dare go and get it."
Book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: The Invisibility Cloak is still down there but I didn’t dare go and get it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc9.source: "One look at her face convinced Harry that she had heard what had happened. His heart plummeted — had she told Professor McGonagall?"
Book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: My heart dropped when I saw Hermione's face; I was sure she knew and might have told McGonagall.

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: D’you reckon we should tell someone?
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: Should we tell someone about this? We can't just ignore it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: We know he’s not coming in through Honeydukes,
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: He's not coming through Honeydukes. If the one eyed witch is boarded up then he can't get in that way.

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: He'd've had to kill the whole House to get back through the portrait hole then he would've met the teachers.
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: If he had stayed and tried to get out the same way he came in he'd have to slaughter everyone to reach the portrait hole, and then run straight into teachers. He must have realised that and scarpered.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Mr. Prongs agrees with Mr. Moony, and would like to add that Professor Snape is an ugly git."
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: The map talks and insults people by name. It actually calls Snape an ugly git.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Mr. Wormtail bids Professor Snape good day, and advises him to wash his hair, the slimeball."
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: Those names on the map are writing about people and mocking them. It even tells Snape to wash his hair and calls him a slimeball.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "This parchment is plainly full of Dark Magic."
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I was bracing for trouble. At first it felt like a joke, but when Snape called it Dark Magic I started to fear how serious this could be.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "I don’t want to hear explanations," said Lupin shortly. "I happen to know that this map was confiscated by Mr. Filch many years ago."
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: Lupin stepped in for me and knew about the map. I felt relieved that he believed me enough to take it and deal with it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: The Invisibility Cloak came off for a moment and Malfoy saw my head. I had to get out of there fast and run back toward Hogsmeade.
Snape thinks my head was seen in Hogsmeade and is accusing me of being there. He is treating this like a serious rule-breaking issue.

Book3-chapter14_Sc5.source: I've been up in Gryffindor Tower,
Book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I pushed the Gryffindor Tower alibi because I know I'll need some defence if Snape keeps pressing me. I have to stick to it even if it makes me mad.

Book3-chapter14_Sc5.source: Maybe he'd better go to Madam Pomfrey,
Book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: Malfoy might be trying to make himself look like a victim by claiming he saw things. I tried to shrug it off by suggesting he get checked, but Snape isn't buying it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc8.source: "Why did Snape think I’d got it from the manufacturers?" "Because . . . ," Lupin hesitated, "because these mapmakers would have wanted to lure you out of school. They’d think it extremely entertaining."
Book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: So Snape thought I got the map from the makers because those mapmakers would want to lure me out of school. They'd find it a laugh to trick me into leaving.
Lupin knows those mapmakers. He's met them. That means this isn't just some random thing, someone with connections is involved.

Book3-chapter14_Sc8.source: "Don’t expect me to cover up for you again, Harry. I cannot make you take Sirius Black seriously."
Book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: Lupin won't cover for me again. He won't lie or protect me over Sirius Black if I keep hiding things.

Book3-chapter14_Sc8.source: "I would have thought that what you have heard when the dementors draw near you would have had more of an effect on you."
Book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: Lupin thinks the dementors' effect on me should've changed how I act. He expected me to take things more seriously after that.

Book3-chapter14_Sc8.source: "Your parents gave their lives to keep you alive, Harry. A poor way to repay them — gambling their sacrifice for a bag of magic tricks."
Book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: He's right. I can't just risk what my parents did for me for some fun or tricks. I feel worse than I did in Snape's office and I know I messed up.

Book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I thought it might be the Grim, right before the match, but then I saw it was a cat. I grabbed my glasses and peered straight out the window.

At first I was terrified it was the Grim, but seeing that bottlebrush tail made me breathe out in relief. Still, I pressed my nose to the glass because something about Crookshanks made me wonder if there was more going on.

Book3-chapter15_Sc3.source: He was sure he knew what was coming — “There is something here!” Professor Trelawney whispered, lowering her face to the ball, so that it was reflected twice in her huge glasses.
Book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I was certain something bad was coming, and I would have bet everything I owned on it. It's not going to be good news, is it?

Book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I feel sick thinking about the match. Every time I try not to think about it my stomach starts churning like something's trying to get out. I slept badly and had proper daft dreams about oversleeping and Malfoy arriving on dragons.

Book3-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Don’t complain, this means we’ve finished palmistry," Harry muttered back. "I was getting sick of her flinching every time she looked at my hands."
Book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: Great, palmistry's done then. I was getting fed up with her flinching at my hands all the time.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: He realized he had forgotten his Firebolt.
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I forgot my Firebolt! I was flying at breakneck speed and then I fell through the air and woke up. That's a proper nightmare.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: He fell through the air and woke with a start. It was a few seconds before Harry remembered that the match hadn’t taken place yet, that he was safe in bed
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: The match isn't on yet. I'm safe in bed. Whatever that was, it was only a dream.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: the Slytherin team definitely wouldn’t be allowed to play on dragons
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: Slytherin won't be allowed to use dragons. Thank Merlin for that.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: He was feeling very thirsty. Quietly as he could, he got out of his four-poster and went to pour himself some water from the silver jug beneath the window.
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I'm thirsty. I crept out to get a drink so I wouldn't wake anyone.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: The grounds were still and quiet. No breath of wind disturbed the treetops in the Forbidden Forest; the Whomping Willow was motionless and innocent-looking.
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: The grounds are dead calm. No wind, the Forbidden Forest is still and the Whomping Willow looks harmless. Looks like the weather will be perfect for the match.

Book3-chapter15_Sc7.source: It looked as though the conditions for the match would be perfect.
Book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: If the weather stays like this, the match should be fine. No excuses about wind or trees messing things up.

Book3-chapter15_Sc5.source: "So you must catch it only if we’re more than fifty points up," Wood told Harry constantly.
Book3-chapter15_Sc5.description: The Snitch is worth one hundred and fifty points. That means if I'm the one who catches it I can win the match but cost us the Cup unless we're more than fifty points ahead. I only go for the Snitch if we're clear by more than fifty.

Book3-chapter15_Sc5.source: This meant that the burden of winning fell largely on Harry, because capturing the Snitch was worth one hundred and fifty points.
Book3-chapter15_Sc5.description: Everyone's counting on me. The Cup basically depends on what I do up there so the pressure is on me to make the right call during the match.
I'm fed up with Oliver's constant nagging about tactics. I snapped because he keeps repeating the same thing over and over and I need to focus.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: "Okay," he said. "But I’m taking the Invisibility Cloak this time."
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Right, I’m going. But I’m taking the Invisibility Cloak this time. No chance of getting seen.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: "Leave him to me," he hissed in Ron’s ear.
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: I’m protecting Ron. If Malfoy starts, I’ll deal with him myself. I can’t just stand by.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: Harry crept silently around behind Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle, bent down, and scooped a large handful of mud out of the path.
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: If I need to, I’ll make my own distractions. A bit of muck in the right place and those prat boys are useless.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "With a little help from Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs," Fred muttered in Harry’s ear.
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Fred just muttered those names in my ear. Those are the Marauders names. Something's going on with them and people around us.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Can’t you give her a break?" Harry asked Ron quietly.
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I tried to patch things up between Hermione and Ron. I want them to stop fighting and sort it out.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I can’t, Harry. I’ve still got four hundred and twenty-two pages to read!" said Hermione, now sounding slightly hysterical.
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Hermione is frantic about this massive essay. She’s stressed out and not in the mood to celebrate.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "No idea," said Harry. "There wasn’t a card or anything with it."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Someone sent me a Firebolt and left no card. I have no idea who gave it to me.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I can’t see Lupin affording something like this."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I don't think Lupin could afford a top broom like this. It just doesn't add up for him to be the sender.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "You can’t know that, Potter," said Professor McGonagall, "not until you’ve flown it, at any rate, and I’m afraid that is out of the question until we are certain that it has not been tampered with."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: McGonagall took the Firebolt away to have it checked for jinxes. I won't be allowed to fly it until it's declared safe.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "The Pocket Sneakoscope had become dislodged... The Sneakoscope whirled and whistled in his palm."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: The Sneakoscope went off in my hand. Something about this broom and the room set that thing singing.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "He’s not looking too good, is he?" "It’s stress!" said Ron.
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Scabbers looks awful and skinny. He's definitely not the same as he used to be.

Book3-chapter15_Sc9.source: [And just then, it emerged - a gigantic, shaggy black dog, moving stealthily across the lawn, Crookshanks trotting at its side.]
Book3-chapter15_Sc9.description: I saw a huge, shaggy black dog moving across the lawn with Crookshanks right beside it.

Book3-chapter15_Sc9.source: [What did this mean? If Crookshanks could see the dog as well, how could it be an omen of Harry’s death?]
Book3-chapter15_Sc9.description: If Crookshanks can see it too, then it can't be some omen of my death. That doesn't add up.

Book3-chapter15_Sc9.source: [Crookshanks and the dog had vanished. Harry climbed onto the windowsill to look right down into the shadows of the castle, but they weren’t there.]
Book3-chapter15_Sc9.description: One moment they were there, the next they were gone. They vanished into the shadows.

Book3-chapter15_Sc9.source: ["Ron!" Harry hissed. "Ron! Wake up!" "Huh?" "I need you to tell me if you can see something!"]
Book3-chapter15_Sc9.description: I woke Ron to check if he could see the dog too because I needed someone else to confirm what I was seeing.

Book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: You killed my parents. I know you handed them to Voldemort and that is all I need to know.

Book3-chapter17_Sc7.source: You sold them to Voldemort. That’s all I need to know.
Book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: I trusted nothing about you the moment I realised you were the one who sold them. I am furious and I am not going to forgive that.

Book3-chapter17_Sc7.source: Crookshanks leapt onto Black’s chest and settled himself there, right over Black’s heart.
Book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: The cat jumped straight onto Black and sat over his heart. Crookshanks is protecting him right now, staring up at me with those yellow eyes.

Book3-chapter15_Sc10.description: Cho called out to me and I went bright red. She noticed me and it threw me a bit.

Book3-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Okay — no wind to speak of — sun's a bit bright, that could impair your vision, watch out for it — ground's fairly hard, good, that'll give us a fast kickoff —"
Book3-chapter15_Sc10.description: Right, no wind, sun's in our eyes so watch your sight, and the ground's hard so the kickoff's going to be fast.

Book3-chapter15_Sc10.source: The Slytherin table hissed loudly as they passed. Harry noticed that Malfoy looked even paler than usual.
Book3-chapter15_Sc10.description: The Slytherins hate us loud and clear. Malfoy's paler than normal, so he's rattled too.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.source: "He’s got no power ter overrule the Committee."
Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: Dumbledore tried to help but he can't overrule the Committee. They are the ones making the decision.
They're here. Fudge and the others have come down the steps.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.source: "He told ’em Buckbeak’s all right, but they’re scared."
Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I thought Dumbledore's word would carry weight, but the Committee are scared and won't listen even to him.
We have to leave now or they'll find us and we'll be in trouble.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: He killed my mum and dad. I am not holding back. I want to hurt him no matter what.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Didn’t care last time, did you? Didn’t mind slaughtering all those Muggles to get at Pettigrew."
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: He would slaughter Muggles to get at Pettigrew. He is dangerous and ruthless.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "No you don’t!" (as he kicked at Crookshanks) and his actions fighting Black
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I will fight like mad when it comes to him. I do not trust him and I will risk myself to stop him.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Whether he could see them or was following the sound of Scabbers’s squeaks, Harry couldn’t tell.
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I couldn't tell if I was seeing them or just hearing Scabbers. Either way, I had to react fast.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Harry reached for his wand, but too late — the dog had made an enormous leap and the front paws hit him on the chest; he keeled over backward in a whirl of hair; he felt its hot breath, saw inch-long teeth
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I grabbed for my wand and was too slow. The dog slammed into me, knocked me flat, and I felt its hot breath and those horrible teeth.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "I’m here on an unpleasant mission, Harry. The Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures required a witness to the execution of a mad hippogriff."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Someone from the Ministry expects Buckbeak might be executed. That means Hagrid is in real trouble and I have to worry about him.
I pictured Buckbeak flying away and safe. For a moment I actually believed he might get away from this.
Someone said it will happen tonight. That felt like a direct threat to Buckbeak and Hagrid and made me sick.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Hermione and Ron, not being on speaking terms with the Minister of Magic, hovered awkwardly in the background."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Fudge is not someone Hermione or Ron want to be friendly with right now. It’s tense.
The appeal or whatever happens at two. That’s the time everything could go wrong for Hagrid.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Are you quite sure, dear? You don’t see it writhing on the ground, perhaps, and a shadowy figure raising an axe behind it?"
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: When Trelawney suggested seeing Buckbeak beheaded I felt sick. I don’t think she was right but the idea terrified me.

Book3-chapter17_Sc10.source: [“Where is he, Sirius?” / Black raised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc10.description: What the hell? Lupin's asking about someone I don't even know he means, and then Sirius just points at Ron. I'm confused and worried and I don't trust this at all.

Book3-chapter17_Sc8.source: [Harry stared down at Black and Crookshanks, his grip tightening on the wand.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I'm ready to use my wand. I'm holding on and I'm not backing down.

Book3-chapter17_Sc8.source: [If Black wanted to save it, that only proved he cared more for Crookshanks than for Harry’s parents.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: He cares more about that damn cat than Mom and Dad. That's what it means to me.

Book3-chapter17_Sc8.source: [He was going to kill Black. He had to kill Black.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I'm going to kill Black. I have to. This is the moment to avenge them.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "She turned abruptly from Harry and Ron’s table, breathing rather heavily as she tugged her gauzy shawl more closely to her."
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: She's frantic and jolting everyone with that nonsense about prophecy. It's causing a fuss right where I'm sitting.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "She was usually last to leave the common room at night, first to arrive at the library the next morning; she had shadows like Lupin’s under her eyes, and seemed constantly close to tears."
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: Hermione's wrecked. She's working herself ragged, sleeping hardly at all and nearly in tears from the workload.

Book3-chapter17_Sc9.source: "Do it now! said a voice in his head"
Book3-chapter17_Sc9.description: I should have acted. My chance was right there and I froze. I trusted myself to do it and I blew it.
I'm left empty and shaky, like everything I thought I could do just vanished when it mattered.

Book3-chapter17_Sc9.source: "Harry wheeled around as Professor Lupin came hurtling into the room"
Book3-chapter17_Sc9.description: Lupin can move fast and take control when things go wrong. He disarmed us all and stepped in, so I know he can act when needed.

Book3-chapter17_Sc5.source: "Your father would have done the same for me. Brave of you, not to run for a teacher."
Book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: He's gloating about my father and using him to taunt me. He's trying to wound me by bringing Dad into it.

Book3-chapter17_Sc5.source: For the first time in his life, he wanted his wand back in his hand, not to defend himself, but to attack, to kill
Book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I hate him. My fear vanished and all I can think is get my wand back and finish him. I'm not defending anymore, I'm ready to strike.

Book3-chapter17_Sc4.source: "He's friends with that dog," "I've seen them together. Come on, and keep your wand out."
Book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: He's mates with that dog. I've seen them together, so stay sharp and keep your wand ready.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "We can’t," said Ron, who was paper-white. "He’ll be in worse trouble if they know we’ve been to see him. . . ."
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: We can’t go back to Hagrid or he’ll get into even more trouble. I won’t risk that.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: They set off back toward the castle, walking slowly to keep themselves hidden under the Cloak.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: We’re using the Cloak to hide while we head back to the castle. It’s meant to keep us covered as we move.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: By the time they reached open ground, darkness was settling like a spell around them.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: It’s going dark fast. That makes it harder to see and gives us less time to get inside safely.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: But Harry had just seen — slinking toward them, his body low to the ground, wide yellow eyes glinting eerily in the darkness — Crookshanks.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Crookshanks is sneaking up on us, eyes glowing in the dark. He looks dangerous and focused.

Book3-chapter17_Sc13.source: "How d’you know about the Cloak?" "No, we weren’t!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc13.description: You can show up on the Marauder's Map even under the Cloak. I was on the map going to Hagrid then coming back and someone else showed up with me. I couldn't believe it when I saw another dot labeled Sirius Black collide with us and pull two of us into the Whomping Willow.

Book3-chapter17_Sc13.source: "I saw him collide with you; I watched as he pulled two of you into the Whomping Willow"
Book3-chapter17_Sc13.description: I thought Sirius was after me, but there's something stranger going on if he ended up fighting with us near the Willow.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "AND HE WAS WRONG!" Harry yelled. "YOU'VE BEEN HELPING HIM ALL THE TIME!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: I trusted Lupin, and I can't believe he's been helping Sirius this whole time. That's a huge betrayal to me.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "If you haven't been helping him," he said, with a furious glance at Black, "how did you know he was here?" "The map," said Lupin. "The Marauder's Map. I was in my office examining it —"
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: He used the Marauder's Map and was watching it. He knew where Sirius was because of the map.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "You know how to work it?" Harry said suspiciously. "Of course I know how to work it," said Lupin, waving his hand impatiently. "I helped write it. I'm Moony — that was my friends' nickname for me at school."
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: Lupin was one of the people who made the Map. He's tightly connected to my dad's era and my friends' parents.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: My dad was one of them. James Potter actually became an Animagus.
Sirius, Peter and my dad could turn into animals at will and used that to keep Lupin company when he changed.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.source: "They sneaked out of the castle every month under James's Invisibility Cloak."
Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: They used Dad's Invisibility Cloak to get out without being seen and help Lupin during his transformations.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.source: "The Whomping Willow was planted the year I came to Hogwarts. The truth is that it was planted because I came to Hogwarts."
Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: The Whomping Willow and the tunnel weren't random. They were put there so Lupin could be safely smuggled out when he turned.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I yelled Lumos to see in the dark. I need light and I act fast when it matters.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Ron!" Harry shouted, trying to follow, but a heavy branch whipped lethally through the air and he was forced backward again.
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: Ron was being dragged into the roots and I tried to follow and shout for him. I will not stand by.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "No! That thing’s big enough to eat him; we haven’t got time —"
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: No, we can't go get help first. That dog is massive enough to finish Ron if we wait. We have to try now.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "If that dog can get in, we can," Harry panted, darting here and there, trying to find a way through the vicious, swishing branches, but he couldn’t get an inch nearer to the tree roots without being in range of the tree’s blows.
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: If that dog can get into the roots, so can we. I kept looking for a way through the branches even though the Willow kept smacking us back.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: We have to go now. He can't just sit there waiting for the executioner. I won't stand by and do nothing.
The execution is at sunset. That means there's only a few hours left and we have to hurry.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.source: If we only had the Invisibility Cloak
Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: If we had the Cloak we could get in without being seen. That's the only real way I can think of to go.
The Cloak's location matters. I left it under the one-eyed witch and if Snape sees me near there again I'm in serious trouble.

Book3-chapter20_Sc1.source: "You know what this means?" Sirius said abruptly to Harry as they made their slow progress along the tunnel. "Turning Pettigrew in?" "You're free," said Harry.
Book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: He's free if Pettigrew is turned in. That means he won't be stuck like this forever.

Book3-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Yes , , ," said Sirius. "But I'm also — I don't know if anyone ever told you — I'm your godfather." "Yeah, I knew that," said Harry. "Well . . . your parents appointed me your guardian," said Sirius stiffly. "If anything happened to them . . ." Harry waited.
Book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: Sirius is my godfather and he says my parents named him my guardian. He wants me to think about living with him once his name is cleared.

Book3-chapter20_Sc1.source: "I'll understand, of course, if you want to stay with your aunt and uncle," said Sirius. "But . . . well . . . think about it. Once my name's cleared . . . if you wanted a . . . a different home . . ."
Book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I could have a different life. I don't have to stay with the Dursleys forever. He really means it.

Book3-chapter19_Sc5.source: A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair
Book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I couldn't believe it I saw light hit Scabbers and everything change right in front of me

Book3-chapter19_Sc5.source: "Ready, Sirius?" said Lupin. "Together?" he said quietly. "I think so," said Lupin, holding Scabbers tightly in one hand and his wand in the other.
Book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: If Lupin and Black are working together to force Scabbers to show himself then this is serious and there's more going on than a silly pet rat

Book3-chapter17_Sc11.source: "I trusted you," he shouted at Lupin, his voice wavering out of control, "and all the time you’ve been his friend!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc11.description: I trusted you. I actually trusted you, and he's been Sirius's friend this whole time? That's unbelievable and it makes me furious.
I saw Lupin pull Black up and embrace him like a brother. I couldn't believe my eyes when he did that.

Book3-chapter19_Sc6.source: "There was another blinding flash of light and then — It was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing tree. ... a man was standing where Scabbers had been, cringing and wringing his hands."
Book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: That's not a rat. Scabbers turned into a man right there. He was standing where the rat had been, cringing and wringing his hands.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: You shouldn’t have done that," said Black, looking at Harry. "You should have left him to me. . . ." Harry avoided Black’s eyes. He wasn’t sure, even now, that he’d done the right thing.
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I messed up maybe. We attacked a teacher and I can’t tell if I did the right thing. I’m not sure I did the right thing, and that eats at me.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Then it’s time we offered you some proof," said Black. "You, boy — give me Peter. Now."
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Black wants me to hand over Peter as proof that I’m telling the truth. He thinks taking Peter will settle it.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: It was the photograph of Ron and his family that had appeared in the Daily Prophet the previous summer, and there, on Ron’s shoulder, was Scabbers.
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: So Sirius has a picture of Scabbers from the paper. If that’s true then someone knew exactly which rat was Scabbers.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Thank you, Harry," he said. "I’m still not saying I believe you," Harry retorted.
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Lupin thanked me but I still don’t trust him completely. I want proof not promises.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "And there was Peter, on the front page . . . on this boy’s shoulder. . . . I knew him at once . . . how many times had I seen him transform?"
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Peter Pettigrew is the rat on that boy's shoulder. I know him; I've seen him transform before.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "The biggest bit of Peter they found was his finger."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Peter faked his death by cutting off a piece of himself. That's how everyone thought he was dead.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "All this time we’ve thought Sirius betrayed your parents, and Peter tracked him down — but it was the other way around, don’t you see?"
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: I trusted Sirius and hated the idea he was a traitor. Now it makes sense that Peter framed him and Sirius was hunting Peter, not the reverse.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "Then I should’ve let Snape take you! Harry shouted."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: I'm furious and feel betrayed at how things were misread. I want answers and I feel protective of what that means for Sirius.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: He's terrified and barely human; he's tiny, squeaky, and desperate when he speaks to Sirius and Remus.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "He killed Lily and James and now he’s going to kill me too."
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Peter is accusing Sirius of murdering my parents and trying to kill him now.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "He’s come to try and kill me again!"
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Peter is panicking and pointing at Sirius like he thinks Sirius will attack him here and now.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "We’ve been having a little chat, Peter, about what happened the night Lily and James died."
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Remus is calm and trying to question Peter about the night my parents died.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "I’d like to clear up one or two little matters with you, Peter, if you’d be so —"
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Remus is serious and clearly intends to sort out exactly what happened that night.
Peter is clinging to the idea that Sirius and Remus are his friends to buy himself safety.
Peter is pleading that he was attacked by Sirius and begging Remus to believe him.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "He killed Lily and James and now he’s going to kill me too."
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: There is a direct accusation against Sirius right here in front of me from Peter.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: description of Pettigrew's hand: "he used his middle finger, because his index was missing."
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Peter is maimed; he is missing an index finger which makes him look even more ratlike and desperate.

Book3-chapter19_Sc7.source: "No one’s going to try and kill you until we’ve sorted a few things out,"
Book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: Remus is protecting the situation and holding Sirius back so they can question Peter properly.

Book3-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Professor Lupin could have killed me about a hundred times this year," Harry said.
Book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I trusted Lupin because he spent time alone with me during those dementor lessons, so if he were helping Black he would have finished me off then. I can't believe he might be on Black's side.

Book3-chapter19_Sc1.source: "YOU'RE PATHETIC!" Harry yelled. "JUST BECAUSE THEY MADE A FOOL OF YOU AT SCHOOL YOU WON'T EVEN LISTEN —"
Book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I'm furious and I won't stand being lied to or patronized. I called Snape pathetic because he's letting old slights blind him to what's happening now.
I acted fast and tried to disarm Snape the moment he threatened me. I won't wait to be pushed around.

Book3-chapter19_Sc1.source: "You shouldn't have done that," said Black, looking at Harry. "You should have left him to me. . . ."
Book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: Black thinks I should let him handle things. I avoided his eyes because I know he has his own agenda and I don't trust him either.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Peter Pettigrew is supposed to be dead, but now they're saying he's alive. What the hell? If Peter's alive and right under our noses, everything we thought makes no sense.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["There were witnesses who saw Pettigrew die," he said. "A whole street full of them . . ."]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Loads of people thought they saw Pettigrew die, but that doesn't mean they saw what they thought. Witnesses can be wrong and appearances can lie.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: [Harry looked down at Ron, and as their eyes met, they agreed, silently: Black and Lupin were both out of their minds.]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Sirius and Lupin look completely mad to me right now. I trusted Lupin, but this story sounds bonkers; I can't take their word without bloody proof.

Book3-chapter19_Sc4.source: “HE WAS THEIR SECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU TURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!”
Book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: He was their Secret-Keeper and he himself said he killed my mum and dad. I can't just accept any other version until someone proves otherwise.

Book3-chapter19_Sc4.source: “Harry I as good as killed them, I persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the last moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-Keeper instead of me.”
Book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: So Sirius says he pushed them to switch to Peter. If that's true then everything about who I trusted and who I blamed is messed up and I can't trust the stories I was told.
I burst out at him because I can't accept being told this quietly. I'm angry, confused, and I need answers before I can ever look at him the same way.

Book3-chapter20_Sc2.source: "What — live with you?" "Leave the Dursleys?" "Are you insane?" "Of course I want to leave the Dursleys! Have you got a house? When can I move in?"
Book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: You offered me a home. Of course I want to leave the Dursleys. I'm asking straight out when I can move in.

Book3-chapter20_Sc2.source: "I’ll understand, of course, if you want to stay with your aunt and uncle," said Sirius. "But think about it. Once my name's cleared, if you wanted a different home"
Book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: Sirius said that if his name gets cleared he wants me to think about living with him instead of the Dursleys.

Book3-chapter20_Sc2.source: Some sort of explosion took place in the pit of Harry’s stomach.
Book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe it! The idea of living with Sirius hit me like a shock and I knew I wanted it.

Book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: I tried to disarm him and Lupin's wand flew into the air.
Pettigrew transformed and got away while I was trying to stop him.
I won't let him get away without trying everything I can to stop him.

Book3-chapter20_Sc3.source: Lupin’s head was lengthening. So was his body. His shoulders were hunching. Hair was sprouting visibly on his face and hands, which were curling into clawed paws.
Book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: He's changing into a werewolf right in front of me. His face and hands are turning into claws and he's getting huge.
Sirius just vanished from beside me. I was suddenly on my own with that thing coming at us.

Book3-chapter20_Sc5.source: [They were locked, jaw to jaw, claws ripping at each other, Harry stood, transfixed by the sight, too intent upon the battle to notice anything else, It was Hermione’s scream that alerted him, Pettigrew had dived for Lupin’s dropped wand.]
Book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I was staring at them, completely frozen by the fight, too wrapped up in it to see anything else.

Book3-chapter20_Sc5.source: [They were locked, jaw to jaw, claws ripping at each other, Harry stood, transfixed by the sight, too intent upon the battle to notice anything else, It was Hermione’s scream that alerted him, Pettigrew had dived for Lupin’s dropped wand.]
Book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: Hermione screamed and that snapped me out of it, because Pettigrew had lunged for Lupin's dropped wand.

Book3-chapter22_Sc3.source: "We did it!" "Sirius has gone, on Buckbeak."
Book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: We did it. Sirius has escaped on Buckbeak, he's gone.

Book3-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Well done. I think —" He listened intently for any sound within the hospital wing. "Yes, I think you’ve gone too — get inside — I’ll lock you in —"
Book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: Right now it feels like everything's worked and we're safe for the moment. Hide and stay quiet, that's the plan.

Book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I need to see Dumbledore now. I woke up groggy, my glasses were taken, and I can't just lie here and say nothing.
If people say we were befuddled by a Confundus Charm, then I can't be blamed for everything that happened out there. That changes how I feel about what we did and why we did it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc1.source: He caught a glimpse of Snape’s smirk as he and Fudge passed Harry and Hermione’s hiding place.
Book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: Snape saw us. He was smirking, like he knew exactly where we were. I hate that look.

Book3-chapter22_Sc1.source: Their footsteps died away. Harry and Hermione waited a few moments to make sure they’d really gone, then started to run in the opposite direction.
Book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: We had to wait until they were really gone before moving. Patience matters when you're trying not to get caught.

Book3-chapter22_Sc1.source: “Peeves!” Harry muttered, grabbing Hermione’s wrist. “In here!”
Book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: Peeves is ahead and could give us away. Get inside, quick. No time to argue.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: Are you telling me, that we’re here in this cupboard and we’re out there too?
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: So we can exist at the same time twice. We’re in this cupboard now and we were out there moments ago. That’s mental but true.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: Dumbledore just said he could save more than one innocent life.
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: Dumbledore thinks there’s something we can change in the past to save someone else. We’ve got to act, not just stand about.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: Dumbledore said — he just told us where the window is — the window of Flitwick’s office! Where they’ve got Sirius locked up! We’ve got to fly Buckbeak up to the window and rescue Sirius!
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I suddenly get it. If we fly Buckbeak to that window we can get Sirius out. It’s risky but it could work and we have to try.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: It’s us. We’re wearing the Invisibility Cloak. Let us in and we can take it off.
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: We’re using the Invisibility Cloak to move around. If anyone sees anything weird it’s only us and Hagrid, so timing and stealth are everything.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: We’ll run for it. Straight into the forest, all right? We’ll have to hide behind a tree or something and keep a lookout
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: If anything goes wrong we bolt for the forest and hide. No heroics, just get out and regroup.

Book3-chapter22_Sc2.source: "Hermione — what’ll happen — if we don’t get back inside — before Dumbledore locks the door?"
Book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: If we don't get back inside before Dumbledore locks the door we'll be stuck out here. I am not staying out while he locks us out, not for anything.

Book3-chapter22_Sc2.source: "I don’t want to think about it!"
Book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I am panicking about the idea of being locked out. I don't want to think about what that would mean.
Dumbledore is nearby and he is actually about to lock the hospital wing. We have to move now.

Book4-chapter3_Sc3.source: he had received four superb birthday cakes, one each from Ron, Hermione, Hagrid, and Sirius. Harry still had two of them left, and so, looking forward to a real breakfast when he got back upstairs, he ate his grapefruit without complaint.
Book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I got four brilliant birthday cakes from Ron, Hermione, Hagrid and Sirius. I still have two left, so I’m saving them and ate my grapefruit without making a fuss because I’m looking forward to a proper breakfast upstairs.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "You explain," said Harry, helping himself to some more chocolate.
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: Why are we stuck here? Where's Sirius? Where's Lupin? You need to explain what's going on, because I want answers now.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "Blimey, haven’ yeh heard?" said Hagrid, his smile fading a little.
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: Buckbeak escaped and Hagrid's been celebrating that. Also Lupin says he didn't eat anything last night, which is odd and worrying.
Something's not right. If Lupin claims he didn't eat anything last night, then whatever happened isn't straightforward. I need to figure out who's telling the truth.

Book4-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Dear Mr. and Mrs. Dursley, We have never been introduced, but I am sure you have heard a great deal from Harry about my son Ron."
Book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: A letter arrived for Uncle Vernon about me. Who would write to them about me by post? I was baffled and a bit alarmed.

Book4-chapter3_Sc1.source: the diet sheet that had been sent by the Smeltings school nurse had been taped to the fridge
Book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: They've taped some Smeltings diet sheet to the fridge. Great, now they've got rules to follow and I'm stuck with them.

Book4-chapter3_Sc1.source: filled instead with fruit and vegetables and the sorts of things that Uncle Vernon called "rabbit food."
Book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: The fridge is emptied of Dudley's stuff and full of fruit and vegetables. Uncle Vernon calls it rabbit food and I get to live off it.

Book4-chapter3_Sc1.source: She now passed a grapefruit quarter to Harry. He noticed that it was a lot smaller than Dudley’s.
Book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: Aunt Petunia actually hands me a quarter of a grapefruit and gives Dudley more. She's making sure Dudley eats more than me to keep him happy.

Book4-chapter3_Sc1.source: But Aunt Petunia didn’t know what was hidden under the loose floorboard upstairs.
Book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: Petunia has no idea I've hidden supplies under the loose floorboard upstairs. That's my backup and they won't find it.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: The moment he had got wind of the fact that he was expected to survive the summer on carrot sticks, Harry had sent Hedwig to his friends with pleas for help
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: They expected me to live on carrot sticks for the whole summer. No way. I sent Hedwig out to get help.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: Hedwig had returned from Hermione’s house with a large box stuffed full of sugar-free snacks
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: Hermione sent sugar-free snacks from her house. Of course her parents are dentists so she thought ahead.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: Hagrid, the Hogwarts gamekeeper, had obliged with a sack full of his own homemade rock cakes
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: Hagrid sent a sack of his rock cakes. I didn't touch them. I've had too much of Hagrid's cooking to risk it.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: Mrs. Weasley had sent the family owl, Errol, with an enormous fruitcake and assorted meat pies
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: Mum sent Errol with a huge fruitcake and meat pies. Proper Weasley food, and brilliant.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: Poor Errol, who was elderly and feeble, had needed a full five days to recover from the journey
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: Errol was knackered by the trip. The poor old owl needed five days to recover after bringing the food.

Book4-chapter3_Sc2.source: they had risen to the occasion magnificently
Book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: My friends actually came through for me. They always do when I ask.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: They actually tried to give the Dementor's Kiss to an innocent boy. I couldn't believe it! They cannot be anywhere near the school.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Oh yes, they’ll have to go," said Fudge, running his fingers distractedly through his hair. "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy. . . . Completely out of control . . . no, I’ll have them packed off back to Azkaban tonight."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: The Minister says they're being sent back to Azkaban tonight. Good, they have to go, and fast.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Perhaps we should think about dragons at the school entrance."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: Someone suggested putting dragons at the school entrance. That's mental, but Hagrid would love it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: As he and Fudge left the dormitory, Madam Pomfrey hurried to the door and locked it again.
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: Madam Pomfrey locked the dormitory door behind them. She's protective and wants to keep us safe.

Book4-chapter3_Sc13.source: If he told Harry he couldn’t go to the Quidditch World Cup, Harry would write and tell Sirius, who would know Harry was being mistreated.
Book4-chapter3_Sc13.description: If Uncle Vernon says I can’t go to the Quidditch World Cup, I will write to Sirius and tell him I'm being mistreated.

Book4-chapter3_Sc13.source: There was only one thing for Uncle Vernon to do.
Book4-chapter3_Sc13.description: Uncle Vernon has worked it out in his head and he thinks there is only one way to deal with this. He's decided what he's going to do about me.

Book4-chapter3_Sc13.source: Harry could see the conclusion forming in his uncle’s mind as though the great mustached face were transparent.
Book4-chapter3_Sc13.description: I can practically see Vernon thinking. I know how his mind jumps to fixing things his way and that whatever he decides will be calculated to stop me from causing trouble.

Book4-chapter3_Sc4.source: Then the front door closed, and the sound of ripping paper came from the hall.
Book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: Someone came to the house and there was ripping paper in the hall. Whatever arrived was opened there and then.

Book4-chapter3_Sc4.source: He looked livid. "You," he barked at Harry. "In the living room. Now."
Book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: Uncle Vernon is furious and dragging me off on suspicion already. He'll blame me for whatever just happened.

Book4-chapter3_Sc4.source: Quick as a flash, while his mother was occupied with the kettle, Dudley stole the rest of Uncle Vernon’s grapefruit.
Book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: Dudley nicked the rest of Uncle Vernon's grapefruit, as usual.

Book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: That's Mrs Weasley. She's Ron's mum. She met him off the school train at the end of term.
Uncle Vernon wants me gone more than he wants me happy. He'd sooner get rid of me two weeks early than let me have anything that might please me.

Book4-chapter3_Sc10.source: Other people might not understand why Uncle Vernon was making a fuss about too many stamps, but Harry had lived with the Dursleys too long not to know how touchy they were about anything even slightly out of the ordinary.
Book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: They jump at anything odd. The Dursleys are ridiculously touchy about anything that is different.

Book4-chapter3_Sc10.source: Their worst fear was that someone would find out that they were connected (however distantly) with people like Mrs. Weasley.
Book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: They're terrified someone will discover they're linked to people like Mrs Weasley. That's the thing they're covering up at all costs.

Book4-chapter3_Sc10.source: Uncle Vernon was still glaring at Harry, who tried to keep his expression neutral.
Book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: Vernon is openly hostile and watching me closely. I have to stay calm and not give him an excuse to make a scene.

Book4-chapter3_Sc10.source: If he didn’t do or say anything stupid, he might just be in for the treat of a lifetime.
Book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: If I keep my mouth shut and don't do anything daft, something good might actually happen. So I'm going to stay quiet and play it cool.

Book3-chapter19_Sc10.source: It must have been the finest moment of your miserable life, telling Voldemort you could hand him the Potters.
Book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I couldn't believe it! Pettigrew betrayed my parents and handed them to Voldemort. That's why Sirius has been accused.

Book3-chapter19_Sc10.source: Me, a spy . . . must be out of your mind . . . never . . . don't know how you can say such a —
Book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: He's terrified and lying, darting his eyes to the windows and door. He's not brave, he's scared and desperate.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: He didn't Disapparate. Snape shouted that loud enough for me to hear it — they think someone tried to leave, but Snape's saying it didn't happen.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "YOU CAN'T APPARATE OR DISAPPARATE INSIDE THIS CASTLE!"
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: You can't Apparate or Disapparate inside the castle. If anyone's trying to claim otherwise, they're wrong and it's serious.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "they heard a distant roar of fury echoing from somewhere above them."
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: There's fury upstairs. Whatever's going on is getting worse and could wake everyone — this is not small.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Madam Pomfrey stood over them, making sure they ate it. But Harry could hardly swallow."
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I could hardly swallow the chocolate. I was too tense, waiting and listening, absolutely keyed up.

Book3-chapter21_Sc3.source: You conjured up a Patronus that drove away all those dementors!
Book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I conjured a Patronus and it actually drove the dementors off. I knew I could do it because I'd already done it before, so I just did it again.
I saw a stag Patronus that felt exactly like Prongs. It bowed to me and then vanished when I reached out.
I got Sirius onto Buckbeak and we had to get him out of the castle right away because the dementors were coming. I had to make sure he escaped.

Book3-chapter22_Sc8.source: Professor Lupin’s a werewolf, see. An’ he was loose on the grounds las’ night.
Book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: He’s a werewolf. He was loose on the grounds last night. I trusted him and I can’t believe this is happening.

Book3-chapter22_Sc8.source: Resigned firs’ thing this mornin’. Says he can’t risk it happenin’ again.
Book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: He’s resigned this morning because he thinks it might happen again. That doesn’t mean I’m just going to walk away. I’m going to see him.
I don’t care if he’s resigned. I still want to see him and talk to him. I’m not letting this go without trying.

Book3-chapter18_Sc3.description: What sort of animal? I wanted to know straight away, cut off though I was. I needed to understand what they could do.

Book3-chapter18_Sc3.source: So that’s why Snape doesn’t like you, said Harry slowly, because he thought you were in on the joke?
Book3-chapter18_Sc3.description: So Snape hates Lupin because he thought Lupin was in on that school prank. That explains a lot about why Snape has been so hostile.

Book4-chapter3_Sc14.source: "Well, all right then. You can go to this ruddy , this stupid , this World Cup thing. You write and tell these — these Weasleys they’re to pick you up, mind. I haven’t got time to go dropping you off all over the country. And you can spend the rest of the summer there. And you can tell your — your godfather . . . tell him . . . tell him you’re going."
Book4-chapter3_Sc14.description: Right, fine. I can go to the World Cup, but I have to write and tell the Weasleys to pick me up. I’m spending the rest of the summer there and I have to tell my godfather I’m going.

Book4-chapter3_Sc12.source: It’s been a while since he heard from me, and, you know, if he doesn’t, he might start thinking something’s wrong.
Book4-chapter3_Sc12.description: I'm writing to Sirius because it's been ages since he heard from me and I don't want him worrying.

Book4-chapter3_Sc12.source: If he tried to stop Harry writing to Sirius, Sirius would think Harry was being mistreated.
Book4-chapter3_Sc12.description: If Vernon tries to stop me writing, I can make Sirius think I'm being mistreated. Vernon hates the idea of that, so I can use it to get my way.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: Can I go to the World Cup? I'm asking straight out because I want to be there, not muck about with stupid rules.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.source: She’s my friend Ron’s mother, she was meeting him off the Hog - off the school train at the end of last term.
Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: Mrs Weasley is Ron's mum and she met him at the school train. She's the person who invited me to stay with the Weasleys.
Quidditch is a sport played on broomsticks. It's proper magic stuff and it's exactly what I want to see at the World Cup.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.source: you know, owl post. That's what's normal for wizards.
Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: Wizards use owls to send letters. That's how Mrs Weasley expected us to reply, and it's what I call normal.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.source: Only I’ve got a letter to Sirius I want to finish. You know - my godfather.
Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: Sirius is my godfather. I'm close enough to him that I write to him and I want to finish that letter before anything else.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.source: I will not be spoken to like that!
Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I'm done taking their rubbish. I won't let Uncle Vernon shout me down or stop me from going where I want.

Book4-chapter3_Sc11.source: Only after Dudley finished with them
Book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I only get to wear Dudley's hand-me-downs that are miles too big and worn out. It's ridiculous but it's how it is here.

Book4-chapter3_Sc8.source: Their worst fear was that someone would find out that they were connected (however distantly) with people like Mrs Weasley.
Book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: They hate anything odd and are terrified someone will link them to people like Mrs Weasley. That is why they make a fuss about the smallest things.

Book4-chapter3_Sc8.source: Other people might not understand why Uncle Vernon was making a fuss about too many stamps, but Harry had lived with the Dursleys too long not to know how touchy they were about anything even slightly out of the ordinary.
Book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: Uncle Vernon goes mental over tiny stuff like stamps because he is obsessed with appearing normal. I've seen this for years so I know exactly how he'll react.

Book4-chapter3_Sc8.source: If he didn’t do or say anything stupid, he might just be in for the treat of a lifetime.
Book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: If I keep my head down and say nothing daft, there is a chance Uncle Vernon will actually give me what I want. So staying calm could pay off.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: That's Dudley. He's the cousin everyone tiptoes around and he's absolutely terrified of Mr Weasley.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: "What was it?" "Ton-Tongue Toffee," said Fred brightly.
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: Someone gave me a Ton-Tongue Toffee and I ate it. The twins make mad things like that and they were testing them on people who deserve it.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: Harry and Ron exchanged glances and then quickly looked away from each other; the temptation to burst out laughing was almost overwhelming.
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: Ron and I can barely keep a straight face when Dudley acts ridiculous. We have that look that says we think he's a prat.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: Mr Weasley: "That sort of behavior seriously undermines wizard–Muggle relations!"
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: Mr Weasley cares a lot about how wizards treat Muggles. He actually campaigns against mistreatment and gets properly angry when his kids make Muggles look bad.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "They — they've tried to get here by Floo powder"
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: They're trying to come by Floo powder through the fireplace. The Dursleys have blocked the fireplace so they can't get in that way.
Mr Weasley is with the people at the fireplace and he knows my name. He's polite and friendly, and he tried to connect the Dursleys' fireplace to the Floo Network so we could get me out.
Mr Weasley seems like someone I can trust. He's cheerful and clearly on my side.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Winking at Harry, he and George left the room."
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: Fred and George know where my bedroom is and they come to help without asking. They sound like they'd make fun of Dudley if they saw him.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "It's all my fault. It just didn't occur to me that we wouldn't be able to get out at the other end."
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I don't expect the Dursleys to understand anything about magic, but the Weasleys do not blame me. They try to fix things and get me away from here.

Book4-chapter6_Sc2.source: Beyond it, Harry could just make out the ghostly shapes of hundreds and hundreds of tents, rising up the gentle slope of a large field toward a dark wood on the horizon.
Book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: Blimey, there are hundreds of tents stretching up the field toward that dark wood. That's where everyone is pitched.

Book4-chapter6_Sc2.source: When he heard their footsteps, he turned his head to look at them. “Morning!” said Mr Weasley brightly. “Morning,” said the Muggle.
Book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: That cottage bloke is the only proper Muggle for miles around. He's the one running the place.

Book4-chapter6_Sc2.source: “You’ve got a space up by the wood there.”
Book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: We're booked in for two tents and our spot is up by the wood. That's where we need to set up.

Book4-chapter6_Sc2.source: Diggory . . . second field . . . ask for Mr Payne.”
Book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: The Diggorys pointed us to the second field and said to ask for Mr Payne if we needed anything. Good to know.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Mrs Weasley likes me and is properly motherly to me, she calls me dear and fusses like family.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "He knows where he’s sleeping," said Ron, "in my room, he slept there last —"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: I’m sleeping in Ron’s room at the Burrow again, same place as before.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "So — have you heard from Sirius lately?"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Sirius has been writing to me, I heard from him twice and I wrote back yesterday, so he might reply while I’m here.
Those food parcels really meant everything when I was stuck on Privet Drive, they kept me sane and fed.

Book4-chapter6_Sc1.source: "About a quarter of a mile’s walk over there, first field you come to. Site manager’s called Mr Roberts."
Book4-chapter6_Sc1.description: The campsite is about a quarter of a mile away in the first field you come to and the site manager is called Mr Roberts.

Book4-chapter6_Sc1.source: "We’ve been here all night. . . . You’d better get out of the way, we’ve got a big party coming in from the Black Forest at five-fifteen."
Book4-chapter6_Sc1.description: They've been on site all night and there's a big group coming in from the Black Forest at five fifteen.

Book4-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Morning, Basil," said Mr Weasley, picking up the boot and handing it to the kilted wizard, who threw it into a large box of used Portkeys beside him; Harry could see an old newspaper, an empty drinks can, and a punctured football.
Book4-chapter6_Sc1.description: Basil is kilted and tossing things into a box of used Portkeys, and the box contains rubbish like an old newspaper, an empty drinks can, and a punctured football.

Book4-chapter5_Sc2.source: "So how does everyone get there without all the Muggles noticing?" he asked.
Book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: How does everyone get there without the Muggles noticing? Turns out they stagger arrivals, use a deserted moor with anti‑Muggle protections, set up safe woods as Apparition points, and use Portkeys for those who can't Apparate.

Book4-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Beyond it, Harry could just make out the ghostly shapes of hundreds and hundreds of tents, rising up the gentle slope of a large field toward a dark wood on the horizon."
Book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I could make out hundreds of tents stretching up the slope toward a dark wood. That's where the campsite is.

Book4-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Harry knew at a glance that this was the only real Muggle for several acres."
Book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: That bloke in the doorway is the only proper Muggle for miles around.

Book4-chapter6_Sc3.source: "You’ve got a space up by the wood there. Just the one night?" "That’s it," said Mr. Weasley.
Book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: Weasley booked two tents and our pitch is up by the wood, and it's only for one night.

Book4-chapter6_Sc3.source: "You’ll be paying now, then?" said Mr. Roberts. "Ah — right — certainly —" said Mr. Weasley.
Book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: They're asking for payment straight away and Weasley's fumbling with Muggle money, so I stepped in and corrected him about a twenty note.

Book4-chapter6_Sc3.source: "So this is a five?" "A twenty," Harry corrected him in an undertone, uncomfortably aware of Mr. Roberts trying to catch every word.
Book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I don't like the idea of Mr. Roberts overhearing our whispers. I made sure to correct the money quietly but I was wary of him listening in.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Harry knew that Apparating meant disappearing from one place and reappearing almost instantly in another, but had never known any Hogwarts student to do it, and understood that it was very difficult."
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: Apparating is vanishing and popping up somewhere else instantly. It's proper difficult, not something you mess about with.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "They left half of themselves behind," said Mr Weasley.
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: Splinching means you can leave parts of yourself behind when you Apparate. That's terrifying and not worth the risk.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "You have to pass a test to Apparate?"
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: You need a licence to Apparate. You can't just try it for fun at Hogwarts if you're underage.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "There are plenty of adult wizards who don't bother with it. Prefer brooms - slower, but safer."
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: If grown wizards avoid Apparition and stick to brooms because they're safer, maybe I shouldn't rush into learning it either.

Book4-chapter5_Sc4.source: “This is Hermione, friend of Ron’s — and Harry, another friend —”
Book4-chapter5_Sc4.description: Yeah, I'm one of Ron's friends. That's what everyone seems to call me here.

Book4-chapter5_Sc4.source: “Merlin’s beard,” said Amos Diggory, his eyes widening. “Harry? Harry Potter?” “Er — yeah,” said Harry.
Book4-chapter5_Sc4.description: So my name gets me noticed. Amos Diggory knows who I am and that matters to people around here.

Book4-chapter5_Sc3.source: “They’re objects that are used to transport wizards from one spot to another at a prearranged time.”
Book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: So Portkeys are things that teleport people at a set time. Simple as that.

Book4-chapter5_Sc3.source: “There have been two hundred Portkeys placed at strategic points around Britain, and the nearest one to us is up at the top of Stoatshead Hill, so that’s where we’re headed.”
Book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: There are loads of Portkeys around the country and the closest one to us is on Stoatshead Hill.

Book4-chapter5_Sc3.source: “Well, we’ve made good time — we’ve got ten minutes.”
Book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: We only have ten minutes left. No messing about, we have to find it now.

Book4-chapter5_Sc3.source: “Harry’s hands and feet were freezing. ... Each breath Harry took was sharp in his chest and his legs were starting to seize up when, at last, his feet found level ground.”
Book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: My hands and feet are numb and my legs are killing me, but I can keep going if I have to.

Book4-chapter8_Sc2.source: Harry knew exactly what was making Mr Malfoy’s lip curl like that. The Malfoys prided themselves on being purebloods; in other words, they considered anyone of Muggle descent, like Hermione, second-class.
Book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: They're snobs. The Malfoys think Hermione is beneath them because she's Muggle-born and they show it in their faces.

Book4-chapter8_Sc2.source: The veela had started to dance, and Harry’s mind had gone completely and blissfully blank.
Book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: My head went totally blank when the veela danced. I couldn't focus on anything else, they were just brilliant and distracting.

Book4-chapter8_Sc5.source: And here, all the way from Egypt, our referee, acclaimed Chairwizard of the International Association of Quidditch, Hassan Mostafa!
Book4-chapter8_Sc5.description: That's the referee. He is Hassan Mostafa, the Chairwizard from Egypt, and he looks proper official in his gold robes.

Book4-chapter8_Sc5.source: Harry spun a small dial on the side of his Omnioculars and slowed the players down enough to read the word “Firebolt” on each of their brooms
Book4-chapter8_Sc5.description: The Irish players are on Firebolts. Their brooms are top-notch and fast. No wonder they blur around like that.
The Snitch is tiny and winged and vanished in a heartbeat. You have to be sharp to spot it.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "used to people looking curiously at him when they met him, used to the way their eyes moved at once to the lightning scar on his forehead, but it always made him feel uncomfortable."
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: People always stare at my scar and it makes me skittish. I can't think of what to say when they start gassing on about it.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Ced's talked about you, of course," said Amos Diggory.
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: Cedric's been talking about me to his family. It makes everything feel even more awkward when strangers treat me like some famous thing.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "You just need to touch the Portkey, that’s all, a finger will do"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: You don't need anything fancy to use a Portkey. Just a finger on it and you're off. That's it, simple as that.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "Harry felt as though a hook just behind his navel had been suddenly jerked irresistibly forward."
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: When a Portkey goes, it feels like someone shoved a hook into my gut and yanked. It's sudden and brutal.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "he could feel Ron and Hermione on either side of him, their shoulders banging into his; they were all speeding forward in a howl of wind and swirling color; his forefinger was stuck to the boot as though it was pulling him magnetically onward"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: When we used the Portkey I was pressed between Ron and Hermione, shoved along in a wild rush, my finger almost glued to the boot. It was chaos but we were all together.

Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: The Bulgarian wizard suddenly spotted Harry’s scar and started gabbling loudly and excitedly, pointing at it.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: They all see my scar and they won't shut up about it. I hate being stared at like some sideshow.
