Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: Edging along the second row to three still-empty seats right behind Mr Weasley were none other than Dobby the house-elf’s former owners: Lucius Malfoy; his son, Draco; and a woman Harry supposed must be Draco’s mother.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: Of course the Malfoys are here. I still don't trust Lucius or Draco. They've been my enemies since the first year and that hasn't changed.

Book4-chapter6_Sc9.source: Oliver Wood dragged Harry over to his parents' tent to introduce him, and told him excitedly that he had just been signed to the Puddlemere United reserve team.
Book4-chapter6_Sc9.description: Oliver's off to play for Puddlemere's reserves. Good for him.

Book4-chapter6_Sc9.source: She waved and smiled at Harry, who slopped quite a lot of water down his front as he waved back.
Book4-chapter6_Sc9.description: Cho smiled and waved at me. I waved back and ended up soaking my front. Great.

Book4-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Who d'you reckon they are? They don't go to Hogwarts, do they?"
Book4-chapter6_Sc9.description: Those kids look like they're from somewhere else, not Hogwarts. I wanted to know who they were.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Wow, look at these!" said Harry, hurrying over to a cart piled high with what looked like brass binoculars, except that they were covered with all sorts of weird knobs and dials.
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: These Omnioculars are brilliant. You can replay action, slow things down, and get a play-by-play. I want three pairs.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "You won’t be getting anything for Christmas," Harry told him, thrusting Omnioculars into his and Hermione’s hands. "For about ten years, mind."
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: I gave Ron and Hermione the Omnioculars even though it's more than I should be spending. I'm blunt about it, but I'm doing it because I want them to have them.

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.source: All that mattered in the world was that he kept watching the veela, because if they stopped dancing, terrible things would happen
Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: I was completely mesmerized by the veela; I couldn't stop watching them because if they stopped dancing something terrible felt like it would happen

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.source: He wanted to do something very impressive, right now. Jumping from the box into the stadium seemed a good idea
Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: I wanted to do something really impressive on the spot. Jumping into the stadium seemed like a proper idea, like it would prove something

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.source: he would, of course, be supporting Bulgaria, and he wondered vaguely why he had a large green shamrock pinned to his chest
Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: I was with the crowd in wanting the veela to stay. For some reason I was backing Bulgaria, and somehow I ended up with a big green shamrock pinned to me

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Let’s go and have a look," said Harry, pointing to a large patch of tents upfield, where the Bulgarian flag — white, green, and red — was fluttering in the breeze.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Let's go and have a look. The Bulgarian tents are upfield with a white, green, and red flag and loads of the same moving posters of Krum stuck on them.

Book4-chapter6_Sc6.description: Kids are running about and making a racket. One of them trod on a giant slug and it burst. That was disgusting and a hassle to watch.
There are groups from other places here camping too. People have banners and are setting up like this is a proper gathering, not just a few tents.

Book4-chapter8_Sc4.source: Squinting up at the shamrock, Harry realized that it was actually comprised of thousands of tiny little bearded men with red vests, each carrying a minute lamp of gold or green.
Book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: They're leprechauns — tiny bearded men in red vests with little gold and green lamps. And they're the ones dropping all this gold everywhere.

Book4-chapter8_Sc4.source: Viktor Krum was thin, dark, and sallow-skinned, with a large curved nose and thick black eyebrows. He looked like an overgrown bird of prey.
Book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: Krum's here. He's thin, dark and sallow, with a big hooked nose and those heavy eyebrows — like some huge bird of prey. Hard to take your eyes off him.

Book4-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Seats a hundred thousand," said Mr Weasley, spotting the awestruck look on Harry's face.
Book4-chapter8_Sc9.description: A hundred thousand people fit in this place. I couldn't believe how huge it was.

Book4-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Prime seats!" said the Ministry witch at the entrance when she checked their tickets. "Top Box! Straight upstairs, Arthur, and as high as you can go."
Book4-chapter8_Sc9.description: We're in the Top Box. Right at the very top, dead center between the goalposts. Best view in the house.

Book4-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Muggle Repelling Charms on every inch of it. Every time Muggles have got anywhere near here all year, they’ve suddenly remembered urgent appointments and had to dash away again . . . bless them," he added fondly, leading the way toward the nearest entrance, which was already surrounded by a swarm of shouting witches and wizards.
Book4-chapter8_Sc9.description: They put Muggle Repelling Charms all over the place so Muggles keep forgetting to come near. Of course they did. Saves a right mess.

Book4-chapter8_Sc9.source: Gold writing kept dashing across it as though an invisible giant’s hand were scrawling upon the blackboard and then wiping it off again; watching it, Harry saw that it was flashing advertisements across the field.
Book4-chapter8_Sc9.description: There's a massive blackboard showing moving adverts across the field. It's loud and flashy, proper commercial.

Book4-chapter6_Sc7.source: Harry caught snatches of conversation in strange languages from the inside of tents they passed, and though he couldn’t understand a word, the tone of every single voice was excited.
Book4-chapter6_Sc7.description: People were buzzing away in loads of different languages and everyone sounded excited. It made the whole place feel alive.

Book4-chapter6_Sc7.source: They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.
Book4-chapter6_Sc7.description: Everything around the tents was covered in shamrocks so it all looked green. It really hit you right away.
Seamus called over to us, sitting with his mum and Dean. Seamus and Dean are still mates, and their families are here and friendly.

Book4-chapter8_Sc7.source: Harry screwed up his eyes too; he wanted to keep his mind on the game.
Book4-chapter8_Sc7.description: I shut everything out. If I let the veela or the crowd in, I lose focus. I have to keep my eyes on the match and nothing else.

Book4-chapter8_Sc7.source: He watched as Krum and Lynch dived again in slow motion. Wronski Defensive Feint — dangerous Seeker diversion read the shining purple lettering across his lenses. He saw Krum’s face contorted with concentration as he pulled out of the dive just in time, while Lynch was flattened, and he understood — Krum hadn’t seen the Snitch at all, he was just making Lynch copy him.
Book4-chapter8_Sc7.description: Of course he was faking it. Krum's dive was a feint to make Lynch copy him so Lynch would get knocked flat. Krum was playing the opponent, not chasing the Snitch.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Hedwig hasn’t arrived with a letter for me, has she?" "Hedwig, dear?" "No . . . no, there hasn’t been any post at all."
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Hedwig hasn't brought me any post. There's no letter waiting. That's it, nothing's come through.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "There’s something I haven’t told you," "On Saturday morning, I woke up with my scar hurting again."
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: My scar started hurting again on Saturday morning. It's happened and I can't keep it from you lot.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "All right if I go and dump my stuff in your room, Ron?" "Yeah . . . think I will too," "Hermione?" "Yes,"
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Ron and Hermione are right with me — they let me crash in Ron's room and moved quickly, like proper mates. I can count on them to react and act without making a fuss.

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: What the hell? I couldn't believe it when I looked up and Levski had the Quaffle while Bagman was shouting that Troy scored

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "He was pressing his Omnioculars so hard to his glasses..."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: I was glued to my Omnioculars and kept slowing the replay so I could see every move, even if that almost made me miss stuff

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Harry spun the slow dial on the right of his Omnioculars again, pressed the play-by-play button..."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: Watching in slow motion showed formations and ploys you don't spot in real time

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "the leprechauns watching from the sidelines had all risen into the air again and formed the great, glittering shamrock."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: The leprechauns put on that huge shamrock display again, right above the pitch

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Across the field, the veela were watching them sulkily."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: The veela were sulking on the sidelines, they were clearly put out by the leprechauns' stunt

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Harry knew enough about Quidditch to see that the Irish Chasers were superb."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: They're mental on the pitch. The Irish Chasers move like they can read each other's minds
My rosette kept squeaking their names every time they moved together: Troy, Mullet, Moran

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "And within ten minutes, Ireland had scored twice more, bringing their lead to thirty–zero..."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: Ireland got to thirty zero in no time, the crowd went totally mad

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "The match became still faster, but more brutal."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: After that the game just sped up and got rougher, it was proper brutal

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: Krum hardly looked as though he was using a broomstick at all; he moved so easily through the air that he looked unsupported and weightless.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: Krum flies like nothing I've ever seen. He looks weightless up there. It's almost like he does not need a broom.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: He was now circling high above Lynch, who was being revived by mediwizards with cups of potion.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: While Lynch was being revived, Krum was using the time to scan the pitch for the Snitch. He's patient and focused when it counts.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: Ireland had pulled ahead by ten more goals. They were now leading by one hundred and thirty points to ten, and the game was starting to get dirtier.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: Ireland smashed ahead. The score is 130 to 10 and things are getting nasty out there.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: As Mullet shot toward the goalposts yet again, clutching the Quaffle tightly under her arm, the Bulgarian Keeper, Zograf, flew out to meet her.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: Mullet is a real threat on the pitch and Zograf will come out hard to stop her. That clash just sparked the crowd into a frenzy.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: Clutching their purchases, Mr Weasley in the lead, they all hurried into the wood, following the lantern-lit trail.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: Mr Weasley is leading the way through the woods with everyone's stuff. He's bossing us along in his own way.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: They could hear the sounds of thousands of people moving around them, shouts and laughter, snatches of singing. The atmosphere of feverish excitement was highly infectious; Harry couldn’t stop grinning.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: The place is alive. The crowd noise, the singing, it's impossible not to grin. The excitement is contagious.

Book4-chapter8_Sc8.source: until at last they emerged on the other side and found themselves in the shadow of a gigantic stadium.
Book4-chapter8_Sc8.description: We end up in front of a giant stadium. It's massive and a bit awe inspiring when you see it looming out of the trees.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "But I was dreaming about him . . . him and Peter - you know, Wormtail. I can't remember all of it now, but they were plotting to kill . . . someone."
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I dreamed about Voldemort and Wormtail plotting to kill someone, and it felt real enough that I can't shrug it off.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "I'm sure he wasn't on Privet Drive," said Harry.
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: Voldemort wasn't physically on Privet Drive when my scar hurt.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "It's weird, isn't it? . . . My scar hurts, and three days later the Death Eaters are on the march, and Voldemort's sign's up in the sky again."
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: When my scar hurts, bad things follow. My pain seems to happen right before the Death Eaters act and Voldemort shows himself.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "You weren't there," said Harry. "You didn't hear her. This time was different."
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I feel like what I experienced was different from what others saw or thought, and I need them to take it seriously.

Book4-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Yeah, I want to play Quidditch," "Hang on, I’ll get my Firebolt."
Book4-chapter9_Sc6.description: I want to play Quidditch. I'm off to fetch my Firebolt right now.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Harry liked this clock. It was completely useless if you wanted to know the time, but otherwise very informative."
Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: I like that stupid clock. It does me no good for time but it tells you what matters. I can see where everyone is at a glance.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.source: "There were no numerals around the face, but descriptions of where each family member might be. 'Home,' 'school,' and 'work' were there, but there was also 'traveling,' 'lost,' 'hospital,' 'prison,' and, in the position where the number twelve would be on a normal clock, 'mortal peril.'"
Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: The clock shows all sorts of mad places, even 'mortal peril' at the top. That bit makes you sit up.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Eight of the hands were currently pointing to the 'home' position, but Mr Weasley’s, which was the longest, was still pointing to 'work.'"
Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: Dad's hand is still on 'work'. He's working ridiculous hours today and hasn't come home yet.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Mrs Weasley sighed. 'Your father hasn't had to go into the office on weekends since the days of You-Know-Who,' she said. 'They're working him far too hard. His dinner's going to be ruined if he doesn't come home soon.'"
Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: Mrs Weasley thinks Dad is being overworked and his dinner will get ruined if he doesn't hurry. I agree, and I'm annoyed that he's stuck at the Ministry.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "I told Sirius about my scar," said Harry, shrugging. "I'm waiting for his answer."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I told Sirius about my scar and I'm waiting for him to write back. I want to know what he thinks and if he can help.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "I told Sirius about my scar," said Harry, shrugging. "I'm waiting for his answer."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Sirius might be the one who knows what to do. I reckon he'll know how to help with this.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Yeah, I know," said Harry, but there was a leaden feeling in his stomach as he looked out of the window at the Hedwig-free sky.
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Hedwig hasn't come and I can't rely on her to bring news quickly. That makes me nervous.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "I told Sirius about my scar," said Harry, shrugging. "I'm waiting for his answer."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I trust Sirius enough to tell him about the scar. I want him on my side.

Book4-chapter9_Sc11.source: [Harry looked away. He would willingly have split all the money in his Gringotts vault with the Weasleys, but he knew they would never take it.]
Book4-chapter9_Sc11.description: I'd give them everything in my vault if they'd take it. I care about them that much and I won't force it on them.

Book4-chapter9_Sc8.source: Harry was polishing his Firebolt, the broomstick servicing kit Hermione had given him for his thirteenth birthday open at his feet.
Book4-chapter9_Sc8.description: I'm polishing my Firebolt. Hermione gave me a servicing kit for my thirteenth birthday and I'm using it now.

Book4-chapter9_Sc8.source: A few moments later, Mr Weasley came into the warm living room carrying his dinner on a tray.
Book4-chapter9_Sc8.description: Mr Weasley is home and he just came in carrying his dinner on a tray.

Book4-chapter10_Sc4.source: [The lunch trolley came rattling along the corridor, and Harry bought a large stack of Cauldron Cakes for them to share.]
Book4-chapter10_Sc4.description: I grabbed a huge stack of Cauldron Cakes to share. Quick, practical, everyone eats and we keep talking.

Book4-chapter10_Sc4.source: [Several of their friends looked in on them as the afternoon progressed, including Seamus Finnigan, Dean Thomas, and Neville Longbottom]
Book4-chapter10_Sc4.description: My mates keep dropping in on the compartment. It's tight but good — people popping by, having a laugh.

Book4-chapter10_Sc4.source: [After half an hour or so, Hermione, growing tired of the endless Quidditch talk, buried herself once more in The]
Book4-chapter10_Sc4.description: Quidditch talk can go on and on. I get why people get bored of it, even if I'm into it — it dominates everything.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "It’s got to be a pretty boring life, hasn’t it, being a hat? I suppose it spends all year making up the next one."
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: A hat sings different songs every year. That's actually what the Sorting Hat does, so yeah, it must spend the year thinking up tunes.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Harry looked away, staring very hard at the Sorting Hat, now Sorting Emma Dobbs."
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: I kept my eyes on the Sorting Hat when it was doing its job. I wanted to know where people were going like everyone else.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "He winked at them as he sat down at the end of the staff table and watched Dennis Creevey putting on the Sorting Hat."
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: Hagrid might look scary, but he's proper kind. I don't trust looks alone anymore.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: Hi, Hagrid! I called out when I saw his huge shape on the platform.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: He didn’t talk much as they changed into their school robes, and was still glowering when the Hogwarts Express slowed down at last and finally stopped in the pitch-darkness of Hogsmeade station.
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: I was still glowering and not talking much while we changed into robes. I felt fed up and tense as the train pulled in.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: "See yeh at the feast if we don’ drown!"
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: Hagrid was already joking about the weather. I shouted back and expected we'll have to keep our heads down to make it to the feast.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: A hundred horseless carriages stood waiting for them outside the station.
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: There were loads of horseless carriages waiting, so we piled into one as soon as we could and shut the door against the rain.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Hedwig’s cage stood next to it, still empty. 'It’s been over a week,' Harry said, looking at Hedwig’s deserted perch."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Hedwig's cage is still empty and it's been over a week. I keep staring at her perch and it makes me worry.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Ron, you don’t reckon Sirius has been caught, do you?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: I'm genuinely worried Sirius might have been caught. I can't stop thinking about that as a real possibility.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Look, here’s the stuff Mum got for you in Diagon Alley. And she’s got some gold out of your vault for you . . . and she’s washed all your socks."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Mum sent me shopping from Diagon Alley, she took gold from my vault and she even washed my socks. I've got new school supplies and money.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Apart from The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4, by Miranda Goshawk, he had a handful of new quills, a dozen rolls of parchment, and refills for his potion-making kit — he had been running low on spine of lionfish and essence of belladonna."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: I got The Standard Book of Spells Grade 4, new quills, parchment and potion refills. My potion supplies are topped up.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "I got some for Harry too . . . show him, Harry. . . ." In some trepidation, Harry opened the last parcel on his camp bed. It wasn’t as bad as he had expected, however; his dress robes didn’t have any lace on them at all — in fact, they were"
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Mum got me dress robes as well. I was nervous about them but they're not as awful as I feared. No lace, so that's a relief.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: I'm not having Malfoy insult Ron's family. If someone attacks my mate, I step in. Keep your fat mouth shut, then.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Oh yeah, you were staying with them this summer, weren’t you, Potter?" sneered Malfoy.
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: So I stayed with the Weasleys this summer. I know their house and I know their family. I'm ready to defend them.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: Harry plunged his hand into his robes for his wand, but before he’d even touched it, he heard a second loud BANG.
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: If things go ugly I will reach for my wand. I'm on edge and I react fast when someone attacks or when there's danger.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: No, I'm not a midwinter baby. I was born in July.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.source: Professor Trelawney said, "I fear the thing you dread will indeed come to pass"
Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: I can't help worrying about what she said about whatever I dread. I keep thinking about Sirius possibly being caught, even though I reckon Trelawney's often a fraud.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.source: “I’ve got two Neptunes here,” said Harry
Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: My chart looks wrong to me right now because I've put two Neptunes on my parchment and that doesn't make sense.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.source: Harry thinking about Trelawney's prediction of Voldemort rising again
Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: Okay, that one time she predicted Voldemort rising again actually seemed genuine — Dumbledore thought her trance was real when I told him — so maybe she isn't always talking rubbish.

Book4-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Shh!" Hermione whispered suddenly, pressing her finger to her lips and pointing toward the compartment next to theirs. Harry and Ron listened, and heard a familiar drawling voice drifting in through the open door.
Book4-chapter10_Sc2.description: Alright, quiet then. I'm listening because something's being said next door. There's a drawling voice I recognize and it's worth hearing.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "How are you supposed to defend yourself against something you’ve never seen?"
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: You can't defend against what you haven't seen. You need to be prepared and watchful, otherwise you're toast.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "The Imperius Curse can be fought, and I’ll be teaching you how, but it takes real strength of character, and not everyone’s got it."
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: The Imperius Curse can be resisted, but it takes serious inner strength. Not everyone can do it.
Right, so Moody's not messing about. We have to keep our guard up all the time.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Hope they hurry up with the Sorting. I’m starving.
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: I'm starving and actually looking forward to the Sorting. I haven't been at one since my own so I'm proper keen to see it.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Brothers and sisters usually go in the same Houses, don’t they?
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: Brothers and sisters often go in the same Houses, or at least I reckon they tend to, because all the Weasleys ended up in Gryffindor.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Where’s the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher?
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: There isn't a new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher at the table. So either they couldn't get anyone or the post is still empty. That's worrying.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: On Snape’s other side was the sallow-faced, hook-nosed, greasy-haired Potions master, Snape — Harry’s least favorite person at Hogwarts.
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: I still can't stand Snape. It's obvious he hates me too and things only got worse after last year when Sirius escaped.
That first year fell in the lake and Hagrid's coat is massive on him. He looked thrilled about it which was kind of brilliant.

Book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: Who is Mad-Eye? Right, he used to be an Auror. He was one of the best, a Dark wizard catcher. Half the cells in Azkaban are full because of him and he’s got loads of enemies. He’s gotten really paranoid and trusts no one now.

Book4-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Yeah, thanks for everything, Mrs. Weasley," said Harry.
Book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: Thanks, Mrs Weasley. I appreciate it. She’s proper kind to us and I’m grateful for being looked after.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.source: "But you’re behind — very behind — on dealing with curses," said Moody. "So I’m here to bring you up to scratch on what wizards can do to each other."
Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: We're behind on dealing with curses and Moody's going to teach us what wizards can do to each other so we can catch up.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.source: "I’m not supposed to show you what illegal Dark curses look like until you’re in the sixth year."
Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: Normally we wouldn't see illegal Dark curses until sixth year but Moody's going to show us earlier because Dumbledore thinks we can cope.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Yeah, I’m staying just the one year. Special favor to Dumbledore. . . . One year, and then back to my quiet retirement."
Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: Moody is only staying for one year as a favor to Dumbledore.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: So Durmstrang is a proper wizarding school, not just a rumor. I think I've heard of it but I don't know where it is.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Er . . . if you say so," said Harry.
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: I'm not totally convinced by all the fancy explanations about hiding schools, but I'm willing to go along until someone gives me proof.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "It seemed that Moody’s rolling eye was magical and could see out of the back of his head."
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Moody really can see out of the back of his head with that rolling eye. That's mental.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I don’t like people who attack when their opponent’s back’s turned," growled Moody as the ferret bounced higher and higher.
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Moody punishes cowardly attacks. He reacts viciously to someone attacking from behind.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Moody, we never use Transfiguration as a punishment!" said Professor McGonagall.
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Teachers like McGonagall think turning someone into an animal as punishment is wrong. Even so, Moody does it anyway sometimes.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I know your father of old, boy. . . . You tell him Moody’s keeping a close eye on his son . . . you tell him that from me. . . . Now, your Head of House’ll be Snape, will it?"
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Moody and Malfoy have history with Malfoy's family. Moody's watching Draco and plans to have words with Snape about him.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "He knows what it’s like to be out there doing it," said George. "Doing what?" said Harry. "Fighting the Dark Arts," said Fred.
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: People reckon Moody's been out fighting the Dark Arts. After seeing him, I agree he actually knows what he's talking about.

Book4-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Potter fought! He fought it, and he damn near beat it! We’ll try that again, Potter, and the rest of you, pay attention — watch his eyes, that’s where you see it — very good, Potter, very good indeed! They’ll have trouble controlling you!"
Book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I fought the curse and almost beat it. Moody made me go at it again and again until I could throw it off completely.

Book4-chapter15_Sc2.source: "The way he talks," Harry muttered as he hobbled out of the Defense Against the Dark Arts class an hour later (Moody had insisted on putting Harry through his paces four times in a row, until Harry could throw off the curse entirely), "you'd think we were all going to be attacked any second."
Book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: Moody talks like we should expect danger any minute. He makes everything feel urgent and threatening.

Book4-chapter15_Sc2.source: "He remembered exactly what was happening, and the pain in his knees seemed to double."
Book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: My knees hurt like mad after Moody forced me to keep fighting the curse over and over.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Don’t remember asking you to join us, Malfoy," said Harry coolly.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: I told Malfoy to butt out. He annoys me and I won't let him crash our conversation.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Either explain what you’re on about or go away, Malfoy," said Hermione testily, over the top of The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: I backed Hermione up and demanded Malfoy stop sniping and either explain himself or leave.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: I reckon Snape’s a bit scared of him, you know,” Harry said thoughtfully.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Snape isn't just annoyed about losing the job, he's actually scared of Moody. Weird, but true. Snape avoids Moody's eye whenever he can.
We won't need our books in Moody's class. He's going to show us things in person, not from a book.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: Professor Dumbledore’s got a higher opinion of your nerves, he reckons you can cope, and I say, the sooner you know what you’re up against, the better.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Dumbledore thinks we can handle being shown illegal curses now, so Moody's going to teach us more dangerous stuff this year because we need to know it.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: You’ll be Arthur Weasley’s son, eh? Your father got me out of a very tight corner a few days ago. . . . Yeah, I’m staying just the one year.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Moody is only staying one year at Hogwarts. He owes my dad a favor or at least someone did him a favor connected to Arthur Weasley.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "You’ve got to know. It seems harsh, maybe, but you’ve got to know. No point pretending . . . well . . . come on, Longbottom, I’ve got some books that might interest you."
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Yeah, Moody’s right about some things. We have to see what we’re up against. Hiding from it won’t help.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "I’m flying north immediately. This news about your scar is the latest in a series of strange rumors that have reached me here. If it hurts again, go straight to Dumbledore — they’re saying he’s got Mad-Eye out of retirement, which means he’s reading the signs, even if no one else is. I’ll be in touch soon. My best to Ron and Hermione. Keep your eyes open, Harry."
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Oh no. If people think my scar means something serious then Dumbledore might come back because he thinks I’m in danger. That’s not good. I shouldn’t have told him anything.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Okay . . . on Monday, I will be in danger of — er — burns."
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: We’re joking around making terrible predictions, but it feels like we’re just tempting fate. I’m not convinced these fortunes mean anything, but it’s unnerving.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "She’s got an answer!" "What does it say?"
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Hedwig is brilliant. She brings news straight away and I rely on her. If she’s upset when I ignore her, I get it right in the face.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.source: Only one known person has ever survived it, and he’s sitting right in front of me.
Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: That's me. Someone just said I'm the only person known to have survived the Killing Curse, so people are looking at me like I'm some freak. I feel sick thinking my parents died the same way as that spider, just a flash of green and then gone. I can't stand the idea of them being wiped out like that.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.source: Avada Kedavra! Moody roared. There was a flash of blinding green light and a rushing sound...the spider rolled over onto its back, unmarked, but unmistakably dead.
Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: So that's what Avada Kedavra looks like. A rush, a green flash, and the victim is just...dead. It's brutal and instant. Knowing that makes me even more certain I have to be ready for anything.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.source: Avada Kedavra’s a curse that needs a powerful bit of magic behind it — you could all get your wands out now and point them at me and say the words, and I doubt I’d get so much as a nosebleed.
Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I can't rely on words alone to protect me. That curse needs real power behind it, so I have to be realistic about who can use it and when. I won't be complacent.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: "The champions will be chosen by an impartial selector: the Goblet of Fire."
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: So the champions are picked by the Goblet of Fire. Three schools, three champions, and whoever scores highest after three dangerous tasks wins the Cup.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: "There will be three tasks, spaced throughout the school year, and they will test the champions in many different ways . . . their magical prowess — their daring — their powers of deduction — and, of course, their ability to cope with danger."
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: There are three separate tasks over the year designed to test magic, daring, thinking and how well you handle danger. This is not a joke, it's serious.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: Narration: "Bartemius Crouch did not smile or wave... His toothbrush mustache and severe parting looked very odd next to Dumbledore's long white hair and beard."
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: Crouch looks off to me. He does not seem like Bagman at all. That neat suit and tiny moustache make him feel weird and not the kind of bloke who cracks jokes.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: "The casket, then, if you please, Mr. Filch." Filch... now approached... carrying a great wooden chest encrusted with jewels.
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: They're bringing out some old jewel-encrusted casket to put the Goblet of Fire in. It's massive and everyone is buzzing about it.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Mr. Bagman and Mr. Crouch have worked tirelessly over the last few months on the arrangements for the Triwizard Tournament"
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: Bagman and Crouch have been organising this thing at length, and they'll be judging alongside Karkaroff and Madame Maxime.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: He raised his wand, pointed it at Harry, and said, "Imperio!" It was the most wonderful feeling. Harry felt a floating sensation as every thought and worry in his head was wiped gently away, leaving nothing but a vague, untraceable happiness.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: The Imperius Curse feels amazing at first. Everything goes light and empty and you feel this stupid, stupid happiness like nothing matters.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: And then he heard Mad-Eye Moody’s voice, echoing in some distant chamber of his empty brain: Jump onto the desk . . . jump onto the desk.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: While it's on you, someone can tell you to do things and you want to obey, even if they are daft orders like jumping onto a desk.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: No, I don’t think I will, thanks, said the other voice, a little more firmly . . . no, I don’t really want to. . . . Jump! NOW! The next thing Harry felt was considerable pain. He had both jumped and tried to prevent himself from jumping
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I can fight it. I actually pushed back against the curse, even if not fully, and it hurt. I tried to stop myself and ended up smashing into the desk. That counts as resisting.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Now, that’s more like it!" growled Moody’s voice, and suddenly, Harry felt the empty, echoing feeling in his head disappear.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: Moody can take the curse off whenever he wants. He was testing us, making sure we know what it does and how to deal with it.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: He stood there feeling immensely relaxed, only dimly aware of everyone watching him.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: When the curse hits you properly, you barely register anything else. You go blank and relaxed and people watching are only faint shapes.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [It is also my painful duty to inform you that the Inter-House Quidditch Cup will not take place this year.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: What the hell? They've just cancelled the Quidditch Cup.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [May I introduce our new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher? Professor Moody.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Mad-Eye Moody is our new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher. He's proper odd looking and everyone is staring at him.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [This year at Hogwarts — The Triwizard Tournament will be taking place at Hogwarts this year.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: The Triwizard Tournament is happening at Hogwarts this year.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [An impartial judge will decide which students are most worthy to compete for the Triwizard Cup, the glory of their school, and a thousand Galleons personal prize money.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: There'll be an impartial judge picking champions at Halloween and the winner gets a thousand Galleons.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [Only students who are of age — that is to say, seventeen years or older — will be allowed to put forward their names for consideration.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Only students who are seventeen or older can put their names forward. That rules a lot of people out.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [The Heads of Beauxbatons and Durmstrang will be arriving with their shortlisted contenders in October, and the selection of the three champions will take place at Halloween.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Beauxbatons and Durmstrang will be visiting in October with their contenders.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [We have worked hard over the summer to ensure that this time, no champion will find himself or herself in mortal danger.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: I want to believe they're making it safe, but given the history I don't trust that no one will be in real danger.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [As he lifted his arm to drink, his cloak was pulled a few inches from the ground, and Harry saw, below the table, several inches of carved wooden leg, ending in a clawed foot.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Moody's leg is wooden and clawed. He drinks from a hip flask and looks like he has every scar and oddity you can imagine.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: "I was telling the truth." "Ah . . . okay," said Cedric. Harry could tell Cedric didn’t believe him. "Well . . . see you, then."
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: They don't believe me. Cedric heard me say I was telling the truth and still walked off like I was lying. I can't force anyone to accept it.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: "You should've told us you'd entered!" bellowed Fred; he looked half annoyed, half deeply impressed. "How did you do it without getting a beard? Brilliant!" roared George.
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: Fred and George think I sneaked into the contest or tricked something. They're impressed and loud about it, not listening to me.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: "Oh if it couldn't be me, at least it's a Gryffindor —" (Angelina) "You'll be able to pay back Diggory for that last Quidditch match, Harry!" (Katie Bell)
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: Angelina and Katie are treating this like a Gryffindor victory. Angelina's all over me like I'm a prize and Katie's already talking quidditch payback.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: Lee Jordan had unearthed a Gryffindor banner from somewhere, and he insisted on draping it around Harry like a cloak.
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: Lee's dragged out a banner and wrapped me up in it. They're forcing a celebration whether I want one or not.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: "I didn't," he said, over and over again, "I don't know how it happened."
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: I keep saying I didn't put my name in and I don't know how it happened, but nobody's listening. Saying it again doesn't change that they're convinced something clever or sneaky happened.

Book4-chapter17_Sc5.source: "I'm tired!" he bellowed finally, after nearly half an hour. "No, seriously, George — I'm going to bed —"
Book4-chapter17_Sc5.description: I'm exhausted and fed up. Shouting that I'm going to bed is the only way I can try to get away from all of them.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "And what's with the hair and the suit?"
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: What's with the hair and the suit? Hagrid's gone and dressed up and he's all shy about it. He's proper smitten with Madame Maxime.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "He’s going up to the castle with her!"
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: He’s gone off with Madame Maxime instead of waiting for us. Typical Hagrid, following his heart, not thinking about the rest of us.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "The Goblet of Fire now shone more brightly than anything in the whole Hall"
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: The goblet's show is mental; when it gets going everyone stops eating and stares. I just wanted them to clear the plates so we could hear who the champions are.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "The champion for Beauxbatons, is Fleur Delacour!" "It's her, Ron!"
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: Of course Fleur got picked for Beauxbatons. She's like that veela-type girl everyone notices the second she moves.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: I didn't enter the Tournament. I keep saying it, because I didn't put my name in.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "I haven’t really thought . . . yeah, nervous, I suppose,"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: I'm nervous about the tasks ahead. It wasn't something I'd thought about properly before, but I feel it now.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Champions have died in the past, haven’t they?"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: People remind me that champions have died in previous Tournaments, so danger is real.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Well . . . they say it’s going to be a lot safer this year,"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: They're saying this year will be safer, though I'm not sure how much I can trust that.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Of course, you’ve looked death in the face before, haven’t you?"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: Others point out that I've faced death before, like it's something I should be used to.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Can you remember your parents at all?"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: I can't remember my parents. I can't tell people how they'd feel about me doing this because I don't know them.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Tears fill those startlingly green eyes as our conversation turns to the parents he can barely remember."
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: I'm fed up with people prying about my parents and I don't like how the press twists things about me. I'm angry and defensive when they try to make me look weak.

Book4-chapter18_Sc5.source: "I have NOT got tears in my eyes!"
Book4-chapter18_Sc5.description: I won't let them say I'm crying about my parents. I'm not giving them that moment.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: Thanks, Hedwig. Having Hedwig back makes me feel a bit safer. If Sirius can get back without being caught, he might be closer than I thought and I won't have to wait ages for an answer when I write.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “How, then? Broomsticks?” Harry suggested, looking up at the starry sky.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: Broomsticks probably won't be used from that far away. If something's coming, it's not going to be a lone broomstick show from miles off.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: They scanned the darkening grounds excitedly, but nothing was moving; everything was still, silent, and quite as usual.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I'm not getting dramatic entrances yet. The grounds are dead quiet and I'm starting to freeze, so whatever the delegations are planning, it's taking its time.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Don’t touch my hand, now. I’ve just washed it, you see; don’t want a Mudblood sliming it up."
Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I lost it when Malfoy insulted Hermione. I will defend her and I’ll draw my wand without thinking if someone sneers like that.
I cast a spell in anger at Malfoy. I act first and worry later when I’m pushed.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.source: "It’s amazing, isn’t it, Harry?" said Colin, ... "What do they want photos for, Colin?" "The Daily Prophet, I think!"
Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I don’t want the extra publicity. More attention is the last thing I need right now.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Fifty points from Gryffindor and a detention each for Potter and Weasley."
Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: Snape will punish me and Ron even when we were both attacking at the same time. He takes points without a fair hearing.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Nice try, Harry. I’m back in the country and well hidden. I want you to keep me posted on everything that’s going on at Hogwarts."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Sirius is back in the country and hiding out. He wants me to keep him posted on everything happening at Hogwarts.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Nice try, Harry. I’m back in the country and well hidden. I want you to keep me posted on everything that’s going on at Hogwarts."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Sirius trusts me enough to be in contact and to ask me to update him. I need to keep him informed.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "She folded her wings, and held out her leg wearily."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Hedwig is loyal and tired sometimes, but she still comes straight to me and expects to be looked after.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "True, both of them had paid two Sickles for a S.P.E.W. badge, but they had only done it to keep her quiet."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I only paid for that S.P.E.W. badge with Ron to shut Hermione up. I’m not exactly sold on the whole thing, but I put my money where it would stop the nagging.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Harry looked up at once, and saw Hedwig soaring toward him."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Whenever an owl arrives for me I tend to look up straight away. Hedwig always finds me.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "To his immense relief, Hermione accepted his story without question."
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: You're not the first person to suspect me, and I nearly had a heart attack until Hermione believed me. I'm relieved she did.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Have you seen Ron?" "Erm . . . yes . . . he was at breakfast,"
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Ron was at breakfast. He's around but I haven't spoken to him about this yet.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "He’s jealous!" "Jealous?" "Jealous of what? He wants to make a prat of himself in front of the whole school, does he?"
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Maybe Ron isn't accusing me because he hates me but because he's jealous. That stings, but I don't want his attention if it's that.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Great," said Harry bitterly. "Really great. Tell him from me I’ll swap any time he wants."
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I feel bitter about being famous and noticed all the time. If Ron wants my fame, fine, I don't want it either.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: May I introduce — incredible though it may seem — the fourth Triwizard champion?
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I'm the fourth Triwizard champion. I can't believe it, but that's what they just said.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: Harry's name just came out of the Goblet of Fire!
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: My name actually came out of the Goblet of Fire. That is why everyone's looking at me like this.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: But, as you know, the age restriction was only imposed this year as an extra safety measure.
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: The age rule was only added this year to make things safer, so apparently the rules mean I can't just back out.
Fleur thinks it's a mistake and that I'm too young to compete. People don't all agree I'm fit for this.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: Viktor Krum straightened up. His surly face darkened as he surveyed Harry.
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: Krum's looking at me like he's not pleased. He's not warm about this.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: Cedric looked nonplussed. He looked from Bagman to Harry and back again as though sure he must have misheard what Bagman had said.
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: Cedric seems baffled and polite. He doesn't seem hostile, just surprised.

Book4-chapter17_Sc1.source: He took Harry by the arm and led him forward. 'Extraordinary!' he muttered, squeezing Harry's arm.
Book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: Bagman is thrilled and making a fuss over me. He's treating this as a big spectacle.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "How this situation arose, we do not know," said Dumbledore, speaking to everyone gathered in the room. "It seems to me, however, that we have no choice but to accept it. Both Cedric and Harry have been chosen to compete in the tournament. This, therefore, they will do."
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: So I'm competing in the tournament, and Cedric is too. That's it, we're both champions whether we like it or not.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "I’m guessing they submitted Potter’s name under a fourth school, to make sure he was the only one in his category."
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: Someone might have put my name in under a fourth school to make sure I'd be the only one in my category. That's mental.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "It’s my job to think the way Dark wizards do, Karkaroff — as you ought to remember."
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: Moody says he has to think like Dark wizards. Fine, he can be paranoid, but if he says someone played tricks with my name then I can't just shrug it off.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "So," said Cedric, with a slight smile. "We’re playing against each other again!"
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: Cedric's being polite about it, acting like we're mates who'll compete fairly. Doesn't change that we're up against each other now.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "She wasn’t the only one either. Snape looked furious; Karkaroff livid; Bagman, however, looked rather excited."
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: Not everyone is pleased. Snape's raging, Karkaroff's furious, Madame Maxime's glaring, and Bagman's actually buzzing about it.
Dumbledore called Moody by name like he expects him to behave. So Moody's out there stirring things up, and Dumbledore has to keep him in check.

Book4-chapter17_Sc4.source: "Well, shall we crack on, then?" he said, rubbing his hands together and smiling around the room. "Got to give our champions their instructions, haven't we? Barty, want to do the honors?"
Book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: They're about to give us instructions. No time for arguing, they just want to get on with it.

Book4-chapter19_Sc3.source: "Nice Cloak, Potter." "Yeah, it can see through Invisibility Cloaks," Moody said quietly.
Book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: What the hell, Moody can see right through my Invisibility Cloak. He knows I'm here even when I think I'm hidden.

Book4-chapter19_Sc3.source: Hagrid was beaming down at Harry too. Harry knew Hagrid couldn’t see him, but Moody had obviously told Hagrid he was there.
Book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: Hagrid's chuffed with me even though he can't actually see me. Moody must have let him know I'm here.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "I would’ve if it had been me . . . wouldn’t have wanted everyone watching. What if the goblet just gobbed you right back out again?"
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: If I wanted to enter the Goblet privately I would have done it when no one was watching. I reckon the Goblet might just spit you back out if it didn't like you.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Done it," Fred said in a triumphant whisper to Harry, Ron, and Hermione. "Just taken it." "What?" said Ron. "The Aging Potion, dung brains," said Fred. "One drop each," said George, rubbing his hands together with glee. "We only need to be a few months older."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Fred and George tried to fool the Goblet by using an Aging Potion to make themselves older. They were idiots enough to try it right in front of everyone.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "There’s a rumor going around that Warrington got up early and put his name in," Dean told Harry. "That big bloke from Slytherin who looks like a sloth."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: People are saying Warrington from Slytherin might have put his name in. I do not want a Slytherin champion.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Hey, Ron," said Harry suddenly. "It’s your friend . . ."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I noticed Ron's mate showed up and everyone was buzzing. The whole place is wound up about who entered.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "You wait," he said, grinning. "You jus’ wait. Yer going ter see some stuff yeh’ve never seen before. Firs’ task . . . ah, but I’m not supposed ter say."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Hagrid reckons the tasks are going to be spectacular. He thinks the champions will have their work cut out.

Book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: No, I did not put my name into the Goblet of Fire.
Absolutely not, I did not get an older student to put my name in either.

Book4-chapter17_Sc2.source: He was very aware of everybody watching him closely.
Book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: Everyone's watching me like I'm guilty, and I can feel their suspicion weighing on me.

Book4-chapter18_Sc4.source: "I didn't. I don't know how my name got into the Goblet of Fire. I didn't put it in there."
Book4-chapter18_Sc4.description: My name ended up in the Goblet of Fire and I did not put it there. I did not enter the tournament.

Book4-chapter18_Sc4.source: "You won't mind, Harry, if I use a Quick-Quotes Quill? It leaves me free to talk to you normally."
Book4-chapter18_Sc4.description: That reporter uses a Quick-Quotes Quill that writes sensational rubbish on its own. I can see it scribbling stuff about my scar and my past while I'm not even speaking.
Rita is pushy and sneaky. She grabbed my arm, steered me into a broom cupboard and shut the door so she could trap me for an interview. I don't trust her for a second.
Bagman was eager to be helpful and keen to make a fuss about me. He seemed more than happy to let reporters close in.

Book4-chapter19_Sc6.source: judging by the fact that it smelled quite normal, Hermione had not needed to set off any Dungbombs to ensure that he and Sirius got privacy
Book4-chapter19_Sc6.description: Of course Hermione didn't have to blitz the place with Dungbombs. It smelled normal, so we had privacy without a fuss.

Book4-chapter19_Sc6.source: Support Cedric Diggory! badges the Creeveys had been trying to improve were glinting in the firelight. They now read POTTER REALLY STINKS
Book4-chapter19_Sc6.description: The Creeveys' badges had been messed with. Instead of 'Support Cedric Diggory' they said 'POTTER REALLY STINKS'. Great.

Book4-chapter19_Sc6.source: Harry pulled off the Invisibility Cloak and threw himself into an armchair in front of the fire... Harry looked back into the flames, and jumped
Book4-chapter19_Sc6.description: I took the cloak off and flopped into a chair by the fire, and something in the flames made me jump. That startled me.

Book4-chapter19_Sc5.source: Then Hermione opened the Fat Lady for him from outside as they had planned.
Book4-chapter19_Sc5.description: Hermione's got my back. She did exactly what we planned, so I can rely on her to help me out when I need to sneak off.

Book4-chapter19_Sc5.source: The grounds were very dark. Harry walked down the lawn toward the lights shining in Hagrid’s cabin. The inside of the enormous Beauxbatons carriage was also lit up; Harry could hear Madame Maxime talking inside it as he knocked on Hagrid’s front door.
Book4-chapter19_Sc5.description: The grounds are dark but Hagrid's cabin is lit. The Beauxbatons carriage is lit too and I can hear Madame Maxime inside.

Book4-chapter19_Sc5.source: He slipped past her with a whispered “Thanks!”
Book4-chapter19_Sc5.description: I slipped past the Fat Lady and whispered thanks to Hermione. Quick, quiet and straight to the point.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "He came back to the country just because my scar twinged. He’ll probably come bursting right into the castle if I tell him someone’s entered me in the Triwizard Tournament —"
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: If I tell Sirius about the tournament he'll come rushing back here because of my scar. He cares enough that he'll turn up if he thinks I'm in danger.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Okay, okay, I’ll write to him," said Harry, throwing his last piece of toast into the lake.
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: Fine, I'll write to Sirius. I mean it, I'll send him word about what's been happening.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I’m not asking Ron for anything," Harry said flatly.
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I'm not going to ask Ron for help or favours right now. I'm keeping my distance on this.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Maybe he’ll believe I’m not enjoying myself once I’ve got my neck broken or —"
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: If I get hurt badly maybe people will finally believe me that this isn't some laugh. I'm serious and I could get badly hurt.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: They both stood and watched it floating there for a moment, before a large tentacle rose out of the water and scooped it beneath the surface.
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: The lake isn't harmless. I threw my toast and something in the water grabbed it. There's weird stuff out there.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "He told me not to use Hedwig again."
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: Sirius told me not to use Hedwig to send this kind of message. I need to find another owl or use a school one.

Book4-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Moody had told them all during their last Defense Against the Dark Arts lesson that he preferred to prepare his own food and drink at all times, as it was so easy for Dark wizards to poison an unattended cup."
Book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: Of course Moody makes his own food and drink. He says it's too easy for Dark wizards to poison an unattended cup.

Book4-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Hagrid was leaning low, talking to Professor Moody. Hagrid had his usual enormous tankard in front of him, but Moody was drinking from his hip flask."
Book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: Hagrid was down at Moody's ear, with his enormous tankard in front of him, while Moody was drinking from his hip flask.

Book4-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Madam Rosmerta, the pretty landlady, didn’t seem to think much of this; she was looking askance at Moody as she collected glasses from tables around them."
Book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: Rosmerta gave Moody that look like she thought he'd insulted her mulled mead.

Book4-chapter19_Sc2.source: "He waved, then remembered that Hagrid couldn’t see him."
Book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I waved, then remembered Hagrid couldn't see me.

Book4-chapter19_Sc10.source: Moody was attacked the night before he started at Hogwarts
Book4-chapter19_Sc10.description: Moody was attacked the night before he started at Hogwarts. If someone tried to stop him getting here then this is serious. Mad-Eye might shrug it off as another false alarm but I don't buy that.

Karkaroff might actually be trying to kill me. That thought just hit me and I can't ignore it. If someone wanted Moody out of the way because he'd make things harder, they'd go after anyone who threatens them next.

Book4-chapter19_Sc9.description: Karkaroff's out of Azkaban now. I can't believe they'd let him go.

Book4-chapter19_Sc9.source: "He did a deal with the Ministry of Magic," said Sirius bitterly. "He said he'd seen the error of his ways, and then he named names . . . he put a load of other people into Azkaban in his place."
Book4-chapter19_Sc9.description: He made a deal with the Ministry, fessed up and sold other people out so he could walk free. That's rotten and explains why he's not popular in there.

Book4-chapter19_Sc9.source: "But . . . are you saying Karkaroff put my name in the goblet? Because if he did, he's a really good actor. He seemed furious about it. He wanted to stop me from competing."
Book4-chapter19_Sc9.description: If Karkaroff really put my name in the Goblet, then he fooled everyone. He can act like he's furious but be playing a part to cover something else.

Book4-chapter19_Sc9.source: "And since he got out, from what I can tell, he's been teaching the Dark Arts to every student who passes through that school of his. So watch out for the Durmstrang champion as well."
Book4-chapter19_Sc9.description: Since his release he's been teaching Dark Arts at Durmstrang. I need to be careful around their champion.

Book4-chapter19_Sc12.source: "So . . . so Voldemort could have found out about the tournament?" said Harry.
Book4-chapter19_Sc12.description: Voldemort might know about the tournament. I can't just assume this is normal school stuff anymore.

Book4-chapter19_Sc12.source: "You think Karkaroff might be here on his orders?"
Book4-chapter19_Sc12.description: Karkaroff could be acting for Voldemort or at least working with people who want me hurt. That's a proper threat.

Book4-chapter19_Sc12.source: "whoever put your name in that goblet did it for a reason, and I can't help thinking the tournament would be a very good way to attack you and make it look like an accident."
Book4-chapter19_Sc12.description: Someone put my name in the Goblet on purpose to get me into the tournament so they could attack me under the cover of a competition. It's meant to look accidental.

Book4-chapter19_Sc12.source: "dragons are strong and too powerfully magical to be knocked out by a single Stunner, you need about half a dozen wizards at a time to overcome a dragon"
Book4-chapter19_Sc12.description: Dragons are far too tough to be stunned by one spell. You'd need several wizards working together to take one down.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.source: Harry, meet me tonight at midnight at me cabin. Wear that Cloak.
Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: Hagrid told me to meet him at midnight at his cabin and to wear the Invisibility Cloak. A secret midnight meeting with Hagrid.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.source: Why does Hagrid want me to meet him at midnight?
Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: That sounded odd and important. I can't just ignore it even if it feels risky. If Hagrid's asking me, it's worth checking out.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.source: The Creevey brothers had managed to get hold of a stack of Support Cedric Diggory! badges and were trying to bewitch them to make them say Support Harry Potter! instead.
Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: The Creeveys are messing about with badges trying to make them support me, but all they've done is make them say POTTER STINKS. People are either trying to help in ridiculous ways or making things worse.

Book4-chapter19_Sc8.source: "Karkaroff," said Sirius. "Harry, he was a Death Eater. You know what Death Eaters are, don't you?"
Book4-chapter19_Sc8.description: What the hell? Karkaroff was a Death Eater and he's involved with Voldemort's crew. That's dangerous.

Book4-chapter19_Sc8.source: "He was caught, he was in Azkaban with me, but he got released."
Book4-chapter19_Sc8.description: So he got caught and sent to Azkaban, and then he was let out. Of course that's worrying now he's back.

Book4-chapter19_Sc8.source: "I’d bet everything that’s why Dumbledore wanted an Auror at Hogwarts this year — to keep an eye on him."
Book4-chapter19_Sc8.description: Of course Dumbledore asked for an Auror. He's trying to keep an eye on Karkaroff because he's a threat.
Moody was the one who caught him. If Moody was on it, it must have been serious.

Book4-chapter19_Sc8.source: "What?" said Harry, feeling his spirits slip a further few notches.
Book4-chapter19_Sc8.description: I felt my spirits fall. This is worse than dragons. If a Death Eater is at Hogwarts, things are a lot darker than I thought.

Book4-chapter19_Sc11.source: She disappeared in Albania, and that’s definitely where Voldemort was rumored to be last and she would have known the Triwizard Tournament was coming up, wouldn’t she?
Book4-chapter19_Sc11.description: Bertha Jorkins vanished in Albania, and that’s where people say Voldemort was hiding. She would have known about the Triwizard Tournament.

Book4-chapter19_Sc11.source: Yeah, but it's not very likely she'd have walked straight into Voldemort, is it?
Book4-chapter19_Sc11.description: I don't buy that she'd have just walked straight into Voldemort. That sounds unlikely to me.

Book4-chapter19_Sc13.source: "Just thought you’d come nosing around, did you?" Harry shouted.
Book4-chapter19_Sc13.description: You're nosing where you shouldn't be. I think you were snooping on me and I don't care if you didn't mean to.

Book4-chapter19_Sc13.source: "He knew that Ron had no idea what he’d walked in on, knew he hadn’t done it on purpose, but he didn’t care — at this moment he hated everything about Ron, right down to the several inches of bare ankle showing beneath his pajama trousers."
Book4-chapter19_Sc13.description: I hate you right now. I can see every stupid little thing about you and it pisses me off.

Book4-chapter19_Sc13.source: "There you go," Harry said. "Something for you to wear on Tuesday. You might even have a scar now, if you’re lucky."
Book4-chapter19_Sc13.description: I'm going to make sure you get some of this back. If it comes to it, I wouldn't mind seeing you get a bit of trouble out of this.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: What about Ron, though? Don’t you want to go with him?
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I don't want to meet Ron there. I'll go, but I'm not meeting Ron and I'm wearing my Invisibility Cloak.
I'm flat about Ron coming along; I'm done playing around with that idea.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: Hermione, when are you going to give up on this spew stuff?
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I think Hermione is being stubborn about S.P.E.W. and I'm starting to get frustrated with how serious she is about it.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: No idea, ask Fred and George
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I don't know how to get into the kitchens, so I'm sending Hermione off to ask Fred and George.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: He took a swig of butterbeer under the Cloak.
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I'm sitting under the Invisibility Cloak, drinking butterbeer while Hermione keeps busy with her notes.

Book4-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Fleur and Krum will know by now — Maxime and Karkaroff both saw the dragons too."
Book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: Of course others know about the dragons now. Fleur and Krum know it, and Maxime and Karkaroff saw them as well.
It's only fair we all know the same things. We should be on an even footing, not keeping secrets that would give someone an advantage.

Book4-chapter20_Sc2.source: "He was best at flying. He needed to pass the dragon in the air. For that, he needed his Firebolt."
Book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I'm best at flying, so I have to get past the dragon in the air. That means I need my Firebolt to compete properly.
Cedric looked puzzled and a bit suspicious when I told him. He doesn't seem to have seen the dragons himself, so I can't assume he trusts me yet.

Book4-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Hermione," Harry whispered, when he had sped into the greenhouse three minutes
Book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I need Hermione's help to get the Firebolt or to make sure I can use it. She's someone I turn to when I need things sorted.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: You’re tied in first place, Harry! You and Krum!
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: I’m tied for first with Krum. Okay. That changes things a bit.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: If you look down at those golden eggs you’re all holding, you will see that they open . . . see the hinges there? You need to solve the clue inside the egg — because it will tell you what the second task is
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: Those golden eggs open and hold a clue about the second task. I need to figure out what the clue means so I can get ready.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: He didn’t care about the Slytherins, he could stand whatever they threw at him now.
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: I don’t care what the Slytherins think anymore. I can take whatever they throw at me now. Let them mouth off.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: "Yeah, you can have a word," said Harry savagely. "Good-bye."
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: I don’t want to sit for Rita Skeeter. She can have a quick word and then sod off. I’m not playing her game.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I can pull things to me with the Summoning Charm if I really focus. When I say the word and concentrate, the object will fly across the room.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.source: "A great big dragon keeps popping up in my head for some reason."
Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: My mind can sabotage my magic. If I let panicky images take over, I lose control, so I have to fight that stuff or the spell fails.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.source: "The Firebolt's going to be much farther away than the stuff in here, it's going to be in the castle, and I'm going to be out there on the grounds."
Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: Summoning something across long distances is harder than doing it in a classroom. I need stronger focus for the Firebolt because it'll be farther away and not right in front of me.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Hermione, I need you to help me."
Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: Hermione will help me and push me to practice. I can rely on her to make me work at it and stop me from slacking off.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I called my broom straight to me with Accio and the Firebolt came flying in on cue, so summoning works under pressure.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: "This was just another Quidditch match, that was all"
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: When I was on the broom everything clicked, like it was just a Quidditch match, and my fear vanished. Flying clears my head and makes me sharp.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: "You’ll need to see Madam Pomfrey before the judges give out your score."
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Madam Pomfrey will fix me up right away. A dragon nick stings but she can clean and heal it instantly.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: "Our youngest champion is quickest to get his egg!"
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Getting the egg fast matters. If you distract the dragon slowly and then dive in, you can grab the prize before it leaves its clutch.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: how Rita Skeeter had lied about him in the Daily Prophet
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: I can't believe reporters like Rita can just make stuff up about me and everyone swallows it.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: how no one believed he hadn’t entered the tournament of his own free will
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: People think I entered the tournament on purpose. That's wrong and it's ruining everything for me.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: how he couldn’t walk down a corridor without being sneered at
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: I can't walk down a corridor without people sneering at me. It's unbearable.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: and about Ron, Ron not believing him, Ron’s jealousy
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: Ron doesn't believe me and I suspect he's jealous. That hurts more than anything.
Seeing the first task is dragons and I feel like I'm finished. I'm terrified of it.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: Sirius looked different from Harry’s memory of him
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: Sirius looks younger and healthier than I remembered, more like the photograph I have of him.

Book4-chapter19_Sc7.source: Sirius looked at him, eyes full of concern
Book4-chapter19_Sc7.description: Sirius actually cares about me. He looks worried and he's trying to help.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: It was hollow and completely empty — but the moment Harry opened it, the most horrible noise, a loud and screechy wailing, filled the room.
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I opened the egg and it was empty, but it made this awful, screeching wail that filled the room. That sound was proper horrible.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: I was supposed to work out how to get past the dragon on my own too,
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I kept telling myself I had to work things out on my own, like with the dragon. I can't rely on others to solve the tournament clues for me.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: Fred passed Harry the egg, and Harry dug his fingernails into the groove that ran all the way around it and prised it open.
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I prised the groove on the egg and opened it myself. If it wants me to, I will be the one to figure it out.
I had a bad feeling when Hagrid agreed to be interviewed by Rita Skeeter. I didn't want Hagrid making deals with that woman, but I couldn't stop it without making it worse.

Book4-chapter21_Sc2.source: "She'll twist everything he says," Harry said under his breath.
Book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: She'll twist everything he says. I know Rita'll make Hagrid sound worse than he is and I can't stand that.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "They've got four, one for each of us, and we've got to get past them."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Right, there are four dragons and each of us has to get past one. That's the first task.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "'Dragons are extremely difficult to slay, owing to the ancient magic that imbues their thick hides, which none but the most powerful spells can penetrate . . .' But Sirius said a simple one would do it. . . ."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Everyone says dragons are nearly impossible to get through, but Sirius reckoned a simple spell might work. I can't just assume the big spells are the only way.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Let's try some simple spellbooks, then," said Harry, throwing aside Men Who Love Dragons Too Much.
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Simple spells are worth checking. Fancy books about loving dragons are useless for getting past them.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Somehow, the knowledge that he would rather be here and facing a dragon than back on Privet Drive with Dudley was good to know; it made him feel slightly calmer."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I actually prefer being here facing a dragon to being stuck on Privet Drive with Dudley. That thought steadies me.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Cedric still didn't know about the dragons . . . the only champion who didn't, if Harry was right in thinking that Maxime and Karkaroff would have told Fleur and Krum."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Cedric does not know the task yet. He's the only champion who might be in the dark about the dragons.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "'Will you shut up for a bit, please? I'm trying to concentrate.'"
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I get easily distracted and need silence to focus. When Hermione talks nonstop it actually makes my head go blank.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.source: They only like him because he’s famous!
Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: They might only be asking people to the ball because of fame. If Cho asked me, I would worry she only wanted to go with me because I'm a champion.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.source: She can’t keep writing about what a tragic little hero I am, it’ll get boring.
Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: Rita Skeeter is looking for a new angle on me. I don't want more publicity making me into some tragic hero.
If someone really wanted dirt on me they'd get it from Snape. I reckon he'd be happy to throw me under the bus.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: Hagrid's not answering. I shouted and pounded on the door, Fang was barking and scratching, and still nothing. He's gone or he's not coming back.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.source: [They hammered on it for ten more minutes; Ron even went and banged on one of the windows, but there was no response.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I couldn't believe he'd just ignore us like that. It's not like Hagrid to shut us out, so something's wrong.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "your task is to collect the golden egg!"
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: I have to get the golden egg. That's my task, plain and simple.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "and out came the blueish-gray Swedish Short-Snout, the number one tied around its neck."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: Cedric pulled the Swedish Short-Snout and got number one.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "He pulled out the scarlet Chinese Fireball. It had a number three around its neck."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: Krum has the scarlet Chinese Fireball with number three.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "She put a shaking hand inside the bag and drew out a tiny, perfect model of a dragon — a Welsh Green. It had the number two around its neck."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: Fleur drew the Welsh Green and it has number two.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "Harry put his hand into the silk bag and pulled out the Hungarian Horntail, and the number four."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: I pulled the Hungarian Horntail and got number four. Great.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "But they, at least, had volunteered for this."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: They volunteered for this dangerous task. I'm the only one who didn't choose it, but I'm stuck with number four.
Cedric tried to be decent about it. He gave me a small smile. At least he's civil.

Book4-chapter20_Sc5.source: "Harry felt as separate from the crowd as though they were a different species."
Book4-chapter20_Sc5.description: I felt cut off from everyone else, like I was on my own and nobody really understood what this felt like.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "I haven’t got a problem with Hermione coming with Krum"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I don't mind Hermione going with Krum. I'm tired of their arguing about it.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "I jus’ knew . . . knew you were like me." / "Another half-giant, o’ course!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Hagrid is half-giant. That explains things about him but it doesn't change how I feel about him.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "We’re walking," Ron told Snape shortly. "Not against the law, is it?"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Snape is nasty and quick to pick on people. He'll make scenes and take points in front of others.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Fleur and Roger Davies standing half-concealed in a rosebush nearby."
