Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Fleur and Roger were nearby when Hagrid and Madame Maxime were talking, so they saw some of it.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: [As if this were not enough, the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard. He is not, in fact, even pure human. His mother, we can exclusively reveal, is none other than the giantess Fridwulfa, whose whereabouts are currently unknown.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: What? Hagrid's mother is a giant? The Prophet says he's part-giant and that his mum is Fridwulfa. I can't believe they'd print that about him.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: [Perhaps Harry Potter is unaware of the unpleasant truth about his large friend — but Albus Dumbledore surely has a duty to ensure that Harry Potter, along with his fellow students, is warned about the dangers of associating with part-giants.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: So they reckon everyone should be warned off me being friends with Hagrid. That's rubbish. I'm not listening to that sort of scaremongering.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: ["What d’you mean, ‘we all hate Hagrid’?" Harry spat at Malfoy. "What’s this rubbish about him getting a bad bite off a flobberworm? They haven’t even got teeth!"]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: I defended Hagrid straight away. Nobody's going to slag him off in front of me. He's a good bloke and I won't stand for this.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: ["How did she find out?" he whispered.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: How did the Prophet dig up this stuff? Seriously, who told them? That question's running round my head.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: [Yet if he didn’t do it soon, she was bound to have been asked by somebody else.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: If I do not ask Cho soon someone else will. I have to get on with it before she is taken.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: [But every time he glimpsed Cho that day — during break, and then lunchtime, and once on the way to History of Magic — she was surrounded by friends.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: She always seems to be with a crowd. I can't find a moment alone with her to ask her properly.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: [He didn’t care, though; he was too busy screwing up his courage for what he was about to do.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I messed up my Potions test because I was too preoccupied working up the nerve to ask Cho. Courage was all I could think about.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: [He and Ron were getting very nervous now, though as Harry pointed out, Ron would look much less stupid than he would without a partner; Harry was supposed to be starting the dancing with the other champions.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm meant to start the dancing with the other champions. I feel like everything falls on me and I look a right idiot if I go without a partner.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: ["I suppose there’s always Moaning Myrtle," he said gloomily, referring to the ghost who haunted the girls’ toilets on the second floor.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm desperate enough to joke that Moaning Myrtle could be my fallback. I am not confident about asking Cho.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Congratulations on getting past the Horntail. Whoever put your name in that goblet shouldn’t be feeling too happy right now!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Someone put my name in the Goblet and they are not happy about it. I survived the Horntail but whoever did this still wants to hurt me so I need to stay sharp.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Keep your eyes open — particularly when the person we discussed is around — and concentrate on keeping yourself out of trouble."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I need to keep my eyes open, especially around that person we talked about. I can't take anything for granted and I have to watch my back.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Dobby is only wanting to wish Harry Potter ‘Merry Christmas’ and bring him a present, sir!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dobby cares about me and goes out of his way to bring me presents. He gets really happy over the smallest things and he means well.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Socks are Dobby’s favorite, favorite clothes, sir!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dobby loves socks. Giving him socks makes him absurdly grateful. If I want to make him over the moon, just give him some clothes.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "You really ought to have a look at that egg, you know, and start working out what it means."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Hermione thinks I should examine the egg from the first task. Fine. I should at least try to work out what it means before the next task.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "‘Constant vigilance!’ You’d think I walk around with my eyes shut, banging off the walls."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: People like Moody talk like I'm fragile but that warning matters. I feel a bit boxed in by their worry but I know they want me safe.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Percy drew out the empty chair beside him, staring pointedly at Harry."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Percy saved the empty seat for me. Someone at the top table is paying attention to where I sit.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: Harry glanced back as they reached the door. Rita Skeeter’s Quick-Quotes Quill was out; it was zooming backward and forward over a piece of parchment on the table.
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I looked back and saw Rita's Quill already scribbling away. She's going to write something about us if we give her the chance.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: They left; many people were staring at them as they went.
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: People noticed us. If Rita spins this, it won't just be private anymore. That makes things worse for Hagrid and Hermione.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “Of course we still want to know you!” Harry said, staring at Hagrid.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: I still want Hagrid around. Of course I do. Nobody gets to push him out and think I'll just stand by.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “You don’t think anything that Skeeter cow — sorry, Professor,” he added quickly, looking at Dumbledore.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: I won't believe that woman's rubbish about Hagrid. She's full of it and she doesn't matter to me.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: Two fat tears leaked out of Hagrid’s beetle-black eyes and fell slowly into his tangled beard.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Seeing Hagrid upset hit me. I couldn't just shrug it off; I feel furious and protective instead.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “Look at the Dursleys!” said Harry furiously.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: If anyone's treated like dirt, it's the Dursleys. That makes me mad, and I use that anger to stand up for Hagrid now.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: He was very skinny indeed, but apparently a lot tougher than he looked, because he climbed up onto the side of the ship, stretched out his arms, and dived, right into the lake.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Krum is mad but tough. He dives into the freezing lake and seems tougher than he looks.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: They . . . er . . . they’re looking for Barty Crouch.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Goblins showed up asking about Barty Crouch. Something odd is going on with Crouch not being at work.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: Listen, Harry, I feel very bad about all this . . . you were thrown into this tournament, you didn’t volunteer for it . . . and if . . . if I can help at all . . . a prod in the right direction . . . I’ve taken a liking to you . . . the way you got past that dragon! . . . well, just say the word.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Bagman fancies me and is trying to buddy up. He offered to help with the egg and I do not trust getting help from him.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: Dobby beamed very brightly, and happy tears welled in his eyes again. “And Professor Dumbledore says he will pay Dobby, sir, if Dobby wants paying! And so Dobby is a free elf, sir, and Dobby gets a Galleon a week and one day off a month!”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Dobby is free now and Dumbledore is paying him a Galleon a week and a day off a month. Dobby's actually delighted about being free.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Harry Potter . . . can Dobby come and see you sometimes, sir?” Dobby asked tentatively.
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Dobby wants to come and see me sometimes. I can have a kid-like little house-elf friend popping in.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Winky is a disgraced elf, but Winky is not yet getting paid!” she squeaked.
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Winky is ashamed about being freed and she isn't getting paid. She's struggling badly with the change.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Let’s hope they don’t look too closely at Winky,” said Harry.
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Winky's state worries me. She seems devoted to Crouch even though she's better off free, and that could make things awkward.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Mr Bagman comes too?” squeaked Winky, and to Harry’s great surprise (and Ron’s and Hermione’s too, by the looks on their faces), she looked angry again. “Mr Bagman is a bad wizard! A very bad wizard!”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Winky thinks Bagman is bad and Crouch doesn't like him. There are secrets these elves are protecting about their masters.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "I\'ve already said I\'ll go with someone else."
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: She told me she\'s already going with someone else. Fine. Cho\'s going with Cedric Diggory. That stings but I can deal with it.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Who\'re you going with?" "Oh \- Cedric," she said. "Cedric Diggory."
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Cho is going with Cedric Diggory. End of story.
Fleur is part veela through her grandmother. That explains why she looks like she\'s casting charms at people.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Yes, all right then," she said finally, blushing furiously.
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Parvati said yes when I asked her to the ball. Good, now at least someone has agreed to come with me.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "I suppose my sister might . . . Padma, you know . . . in Ravenclaw. I\'ll ask her if you like."
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Parvati thinks her sister Padma might go with Ron. That could sort Ron out if she actually asks her.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Cedric did this weird thing where he Transfigured a rock on the ground turned it into a dog he was trying to make the dragon go for the dog instead of him.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Cedric turned a rock into a dog to distract the dragon and it actually worked for a bit.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [he did get the egg but he got burned as well the dragon changed its mind halfway through and decided it would rather have him than the Labrador he only just got away.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Cedric did get the egg but got burned because the dragon changed its mind and went after him.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [And that Fleur girl tried this sort of charm I think she was trying to put it into a trance well that kind of worked too it went all sleepy but then it snored and this great jet of flame shot out and her skirt caught fire she put it out with a bit of water out of her wand.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Fleur tried a charm to put the dragon to sleep; it dozed but then sneezed out fire and set her skirt alight and she doused it with wand water.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Krum you won t believe this but he didn t even think of flying he was probably the best after you though Hit it with some sort of spell right in the eye Only thing is it went trampling around in agony and squashed half the real eggs they took marks off for that he wasn t supposed to do any damage to them.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Krum hit the dragon in the eye with a spell instead of flying and was probably the best after me but he caused the dragon to rampage and crush eggs so they docked his marks.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [It s marks out of ten from each one Madame Maxime ... Mr. Crouch ... Dumbledore ... Ludo Bagman ten ... Karkaroff ... four.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: The judges mark out of ten each. Maxime, Crouch, Dumbledore, Bagman and Karkaroff all gave their scores and Bagman even gave me a ten while Karkaroff gave me a four.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [But Harry didn t care he wouldn t have cared if Karkaroff had given him zero Ron s indignation on his behalf was worth about a hundred points to him.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: I didn't care about Karkaroff's low score. Ron standing up for me felt way more important than the points.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Ron s indignation on his behalf was worth about a hundred points to him he didn t tell Ron this of course but his heart felt lighter than air as he turned to leave the enclosure.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Romantic or not I noticed Ron's support makes everything lighter. I appreciate him loads even if I did not say it out loud.

Book4-chapter25_Sc3.source: Moody’s magical eye travel over Snape, and then, unmistakably, onto himself.
Book4-chapter25_Sc3.description: Moody can see through my Invisibility Cloak. He saw me there on the stairs.

Book4-chapter25_Sc3.source: That egg is Potter’s egg. That piece of parchment belongs to Potter.
Book4-chapter25_Sc3.description: Snape recognizes my things and suspected I was the intruder. He put two and two together and thought the map and egg were mine.
I saw who broke into Snape’s office and it was Barty Crouch.

Book4-chapter25_Sc3.source: Put it this way, Potter, they say old Mad-Eye's obsessed with catching Dark wizards but I'm nothing compared to Barty Crouch.
Book4-chapter25_Sc3.description: Moody clearly respects Crouch and thinks Crouch is a big deal in catching Dark wizards. Crouch being involved makes this more serious than I thought.
Moody took the Marauder’s Map from me and wants to keep it to use. I owe him a favor now.

Book4-chapter25_Sc3.source: It’s the property of the champion he stole it from.
Book4-chapter25_Sc3.description: Filch thinks the egg is a Triwizard clue and that Peeves stole it from a champion.

Book4-chapter24_Sc8.source: Tha’s my boy, you show ’em, Harry, you show ’em. Beat ’em all.
Book4-chapter24_Sc8.description: Hagrid's proud of me. He's shouting encouragement, telling me to show them and to beat them all.
I told Hagrid I'm doing great with the egg. I'm trying to sound confident and keep him happy.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.source: "Yeh know wha', Harry? ... Yeh know what I'd love, Harry? I'd love yeh ter win, I really would. It'd show 'em all ... Yeh don' have ter be pureblood ter do it."
Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: I felt Hagrid rooting for me. He thinks if I win it'll prove you don't have to be pureblood to be great at magic. That made me want to try even harder.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.source: "Yeh know wha', Harry? ... when I firs' met you, you reminded me o' me a bit. Mum an' Dad gone, an' you was feelin' like yeh wouldn' fit in at Hogwarts ... an' now look at yeh, Harry! School champion!"
Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: I know Hagrid sees a bit of himself in me and he cares. I'm closer to him now and I don't want to let him down.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.source: "Dumbledore was the one who stuck up for me after Dad went. Got me the gamekeeper job ... Gives 'em second chances ... tha's what sets him apar' from other Heads"
Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: Dumbledore really believes in giving people second chances. If he trusts someone it matters. That's why I trust him more.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Okay," said Harry, standing up, his fork falling onto his plate with a clatter.
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: Okay. I'm standing up even though I feel like my stomach's dropped and everyone is watching.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Yeah," said Harry in a voice that was most unlike his own.
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I sound flat and distant. I can tell I'm not the same calm me right now, I'm on edge.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Now, don't panic," she said, "just keep a cool head. . . . We've got wizards standing by to control the situation if it gets out of hand. . . . The main thing is just to do your best, and nobody will think any the worse of you. . . . Are you all right?"
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: Don't panic. Keep a cool head. There are wizards ready to step in. Just do my best and people won't think less of me.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "You’re to go in here with the other champions," said Professor McGonagall, in a rather shaky sort of voice, "and wait for your turn, Potter. Mr. Bagman is in there . . . he’ll be telling you the — the procedure. . . . Good luck."
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I have to go into the tent with the other champions and wait. Bagman will tell us the procedure. Good luck to me.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Yes," Harry heard himself say. "Yes, I'm fine."
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I tell people I'm fine even when I'm terrified. I don't trust that I actually feel fine.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: It was a state of nervousness so advanced that he wondered whether he mightn’t just lose his head when they tried to lead him out to his dragon, and start trying to curse everyone in sight.
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I'm so nervous I can imagine losing control and lashing out. That's how bad it feels.

Book4-chapter26_Sc7.source: "Got lost!" he mouthed, "Fleur and Krum’re coming now!"
Book4-chapter26_Sc7.description: Cedric found us. He mouthed that he got lost but said Fleur and Krum are on their way.

Book4-chapter26_Sc7.source: "He pulled a knife out of his pocket and cut Cho free."
Book4-chapter26_Sc7.description: Cedric cut Cho free and pulled her up to the surface.
I felt massive relief seeing Cedric and knowing help was coming. For once I wasn't panicking alone.
Krum is coming too, though he looks terrifying down here, like a shark-headed swimmer.

Book4-chapter26_Sc7.source: "Time was getting short, and according to the song, the hostages would be lost after an hour."
Book4-chapter26_Sc7.description: We have very little time left. If we don't get out soon the hostages could be lost.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: The ropes of weed tying the hostages to the statue were thick, slimy, and very strong.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: Those weeds are brutal and proper strong. I can't just yank them off, they're clinging like mad and will not come loose with a bit of pulling.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: A choir of merpeople was singing in the middle, calling the champions toward them, and behind them rose a crude sort of statue; a gigantic merperson hewn from a boulder.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: There's a whole crowd here, singing and dragging attention to that statue. They're organized and not about to let me rush in without them noticing.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: For a fleeting second he thought of the knife Sirius had bought him for Christmas — locked in his trunk in the castle a quarter of a mile away, no use to him whatsoever.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: I should've had something on me. That knife would have helped but it's miles away and I'm stuck here without it. Great timing, right?

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: He sped toward the hostages, half expecting the merpeople to lower their spears and charge at him, but they did nothing.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: I thought they'd attack the moment I came near but they're holding back. That means they're watching, waiting for something else to happen. I need a different plan than brute force.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: Ron's right there, caught in the middle between Hermione and Cho. I have to get to him first.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “Come seek us where our voices sound, We cannot sing above the ground, And while you’re searching, ponder this: We’ve taken what you’ll sorely miss, An hour long you’ll have to look, And to recover what we took, But past an hour — the prospect’s black, Too late, it’s gone, it won’t come back.”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Right, the egg actually sang that riddle. It’s pointing me to voices that can only be heard underwater and warning I have an hour to get back whatever they take.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “I’d try putting it in the water, if I were you.”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Myrtle told me to open the egg under water. I did and that’s how I heard the song, so the clue only works underwater.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “Myrtle, there aren’t merpeople in there, are there?” “Oooh, very good,”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Of course! The voices belong to the merpeople in the lake. The second task is about the lake and the merpeople.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “You need to put your head under too,”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I had to put my head under the water to hear the egg properly. Whatever I need to do for the task will probably mean being underwater for a while.
I’m not a good swimmer and I don’t know how I’ll breathe underwater. This is a real problem for the task.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “Egg? My sweet! This is a Triwizard clue! This belongs to a school champion!”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Filch found the egg and called it a Triwizard clue. If anyone thinks Peeves stole it or it was in someone’s office, this is going to cause trouble and draw attention to whoever has the egg.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: “I seal my office with a spell none but a wizard could break!”
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Snape is sure his office was tampered with and is taking this seriously. If Filch and Snape are searching the corridors, I could be caught even under the Invisibility Cloak if the map shows me.
Moody turned up in the corridor just as Filch and Snape were arguing. His arrival makes things even more dangerous and unpredictable.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.source: Harry thinking about Myrtle and her spying
Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: Myrtle spies from the pipes and likes to boss people around. She’s touchy about being dead and will blubber if you mention breathing near her.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "I haven't been anywhere near your office!" "Do you know what this is, Potter?" "It is Veritaserum"
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: Right, Snape thinks I broke into his office and he is threatening to force me to tell the truth with Veritaserum. He will try to bully me into confessing even though I did not do it.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Fulfilling my duty as godfather," "You three and Dumbledore are the only ones around here who know I'm an Animagus"
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: Sirius is here for me. He is acting like my godfather, sneaking around, stealing papers and even risking being seen because he wants to help. He is an Animagus and only a few people know that.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Ten minutes?" Harry croaked. "Ten — ten minutes?" He looked down at his watch. Dobby was right. It was twenty past nine.
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I've only got ten minutes. This is mad but I have to move, now.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Dobby will do the task for him!" and "Dobby knew Harry had not found the right book, so Dobby did it for him!"
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: Dobby has gone and sorted this out for me because I hadn't found the right book. He's trying to help, even if it's at the last minute.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Harry Potter has to go into the lake and find his Wheezy" and "They've got . . . they've got Ron?"
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: They've taken Ron. I have to go into the lake and get him back. That's what's been taken from me.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "You has to eat this, sir!" and Dobby drew out a ball of what looked like slimy, grayish-green rat tails. "Right before you go into the lake, sir — gillyweed!" "It will make Harry Potter breathe underwater, sir!"
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: Gillyweed will let me breathe underwater. I need to eat it before I go in if I'm going to reach Ron.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Dobby hears things, sir, he is a house-elf, he goes all over the castle as he lights the fires and mops the floors. Dobby heard Professor McGonagall and Professor Moody in the staffroom, talking about the next task."
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: If Dobby overheard McGonagall and Moody, then this gillyweed plan actually comes from what staff were saying. I trust it enough to use it now.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "All our champions are ready for the second task... They have precisely an hour to recover what has been taken from them."
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: We have exactly one hour to get back whatever they took. No messing about, that's the limit.

Book4-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Relashio!" Harry shouted, except that no sound came out.
Book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I tried to shout a spell and nothing came out. My voice can fail me under pressure so I can't rely on shouting.

Book4-chapter26_Sc6.source: "We do not help," he said in a harsh, croaky voice.
Book4-chapter26_Sc6.description: They won't help us. They don't care about anyone but their own. I tried to get that spear and they just laughed and shook their heads.

Book4-chapter26_Sc6.source: "Your task is to retrieve your own friend,"
Book4-chapter26_Sc6.description: No way I'm leaving anyone. Even if they expect me to save only Ron, I won't just stand by and let Hermione or anyone else be left to die.
Hermione is my friend as much as Ron is. I care about both of them and I'm going to try and get them free.

Book4-chapter26_Sc8.source: Their yellowish eyes were fixed upon Harry's wand, and they looked scared. There might be a lot more of them than there were of him, but Harry could tell, by the looks on their faces, that they knew no more magic than the giant squid did.
Book4-chapter26_Sc8.description: Right, they can see my wand and they're scared. They don't know much magic, just like the giant squid, so if I act fast I might bluff them.
Get out of the way! I shouted it and they stopped. Okay, shouting worked. If I sound certain they'll listen, at least for a bit.
You've got until three. Counting them down actually makes them back off for now. I can buy a little time if I make a stand.

Book4-chapter26_Sc8.source: He snatched up the stone, which Krum had dropped, but the mermen now closed in around Ron and the little girl, shaking their heads at him.
Book4-chapter26_Sc8.description: Right now I have to hold them off and hope Fleur turns up. I can't leave Ron and the little girl, but I can't help Hermione if I'm pulled under. I have to be ready to fight to the surface.

Book4-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Sending a letter," said Harry and George in unison.
Book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I'm sending a letter. Plain and simple, that's what I'm doing.

Book4-chapter29_Sc1.source: Harry glanced at it, but Fred, whether accidentally or on purpose, shifted his hand so that the name on it was covered.
Book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I had a sealed envelope with a name on it, and Fred made sure I couldn't show it. Something's up with who that letter is for.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: “Fleur didn’t turn up, I couldn’t leave her,” Harry panted.
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: I dragged her up because Fleur wasn't there. I couldn't just leave her down there.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: He could feel pain on the sides of his neck again  he was becoming very aware of how wet the water was in his mouth  yet the darkness was definitely thinning now  he could see daylight above him
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: I was dying for air, fighting like mad for the surface, and I nearly didn't make it. Getting to the light was everything.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: Harry had the impression they thought that Ron and the little girl might be dead, but they were wrong  both of them had opened their eyes
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: I thought everyone might assume the worst, but Ron and Gabrielle came round. We're not dead, and we made it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: surrounded by spear-carrying merpeople who’d looked more than capable of murder
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Those merpeople looked dangerous as anything. Down there I didn't feel safe for a second.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: Dumbledore and Bagman were pulling Harry upright
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Dumbledore pulled me up. I don't know what I'd have done without someone getting me out of that mess.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Snape said Moody's searched his office as well?"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Moody has been searching Snape's office. That makes me think someone is really watching Snape.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Moody said Dumbledore only lets Snape stay here because he’s giving him a second chance or something."
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Even though Snape hates me and gives me grief, Dumbledore might have given him a second chance. I can't just assume he is all bad.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "it was true that Snape had saved his life once, but the odd thing was, Snape definitely loathed him"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Snape saved my life before, but he still loathes me. He treats me like he did James. I distrust him but I remember he has helped me.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I just need to — sort of fine-tune it, all right?"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I'm trying to fine tune my plan about the egg clue. I need time and space to work it out.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "they found nothing whatsoever that would enable Harry to spend an hour underwater and live to tell the tale."
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I've searched everywhere and there is no spell that will let me live underwater for an hour. I am running out of options and time.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "There was a week to go before February the twenty-fourth"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: The deadline is getting closer. Time is slipping and I have to find a way to get to the lake soon.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: "Yeah, that’s right," said Harry, raising his voice slightly so that Karkaroff could hear him.
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Karkaroff's watching me. I made a point of shouting so he knows I noticed him. He's not pleased.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Dumbledore was crouching at the water’s edge, deep in conversation with what seemed to be the chief merperson
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Dumbledore can speak Mermish and he was talking with the merpeople. He had things under control down there.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Now he was out of the water, it seemed perfectly clear that Dumbledore’s safety precautions wouldn’t have permitted the death of a hostage just because their champion hadn’t turned up.
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Of course Dumbledore set strict safety measures. I don't need to beat myself up about not grabbing Ron immediately.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Fleur bent down, kissed Harry twice on each cheek
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Fleur's grateful and over the moon with me. That was awkward and flattering at the same time.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Harry’s feeling of stupidity was growing. Now he was out of the water, it seemed perfectly clear that Dumbledore’s safety precautions wouldn’t have permitted the death of a hostage.
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: I feel stupid for a second, but it makes sense now that Dumbledore wouldn't let someone die. I shouldn't be beating myself up.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "I . . . escaped . . . must warn . . . must tell . . . see Dumbledore . . . my fault . . . all my fault . . ."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: He escaped and is desperate to warn Dumbledore. He's clearly frantic and thinks everything is his fault.
Krum was attacked from behind. Someone from the Triwizard entourage was hurt and blamed Crouch.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "I don’t know where Barty Crouch is," Dumbledore told Moody, "but it is essential that we find him."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Dumbledore needs Crouch found right away. This is urgent and everyone is looking for him.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "You stay here with him!" "I’ll get Dumbledore if you let me go, Mr. Crouch!"
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: I thought I could run off and sort things out, but this is bigger than me. I have to follow orders and stay put when told.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "You will take Harry back to school, Hagrid," Dumbledore repeated firmly. "Take him right up to Gryffindor Tower. And Harry — I want you to stay there."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Dumbledore is being protective and strict with me. He wants me kept safe and under watch.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "How dare he accuse Dumbledore. Like Dumbledore’d do anythin’ like that."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Hagrid defends Dumbledore fiercely. People who accuse Dumbledore get a straight answer from Hagrid.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "The less you lot ’ave ter do with these foreigners, the happier yeh’ll be. Yeh can’ trust any of ’em."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Hagrid thinks we should be wary of the foreign students. It's made me more aware that not everyone from other schools is automatically to be trusted.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "Treachery!" he bellowed, pointing at Dumbledore. "It is a plot! You and your Ministry of Magic have lured me here under false pretenses, Dumbledore!"
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Karkaroff accuses Dumbledore of plotting and cheating. He is furious and paranoid right now.

Book4-chapter28_Sc3.source: "No need, Dumbledore," said a wheezy growl. "I’m here."
Book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: Moody is on the scene and ready to help. He arrives fast even with his leg and takes things seriously.

Book4-chapter26_Sc2.source: Send date of next Hogsmeade weekend by return owl.
Book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I got that tiny letter from Sirius telling me to send the Hogsmeade date back, so I scribbled the weekend after next on the parchment and sent the owl straight away.

Book4-chapter26_Sc2.source: He carried them over to a table, then set to work, searching them by the narrow beam of his wand, occasionally checking his watch.
Book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I was going through every book I could find by the light of my wand, refusing to stop until I found something about surviving underwater. I kept telling myself next book, next book, because I had to find it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc2.source: The mermaid in the painting in the prefects’ bathroom was laughing.
Book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I kept dreaming about being stuck underwater, the mermaid laughing and teasing me while I tried to get my broom back. It feels like I can't catch a break, even in my sleep.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “They’re making it sound like he’s dying,” said Harry slowly.
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: They’re making it sound like he’s dying, but he can’t be that ill if he managed to get up here.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “I didn’t need to use it before we got in the forest. And then I put my hand in my pocket, and all that was in there were my Omnioculars.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: My wand wasn’t in my pocket after the Top Box and before the forest. If the Dark Mark was conjured from the Top Box then someone could have taken my wand there.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “Yeah, at the Quidditch World Cup,” said Harry, and he launched into the story of the Dark Mark’s appearance, and Winky being found with Harry’s wand clutched in her hand, and Mr. Crouch’s fury.
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Winky being found holding my wand makes me suspect something odd happened in the Top Box and that Crouch reacted by blaming his elf instead of looking properly.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “Once the boy had died, people started feeling a bit more sympathetic toward the son and started asking how a nice young lad from a good family had gone so badly astray.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Crouch's family fell apart after his son died and people turned against the father. That's why his reputation crashed.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “If you ask me, he still thinks he can bring back the old popularity by catching one more Death Eater.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Crouch isn't just obsessed with justice. He might be chasing Death Eaters to win his reputation back, not only for duty.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “Karkaroff wanted to talk to Snape, he says Snape’s been avoiding him. Karkaroff looked really worried. He showed Snape something on his arm, but I couldn’t see what it was.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Karkaroff went to Snape and showed him something on his arm, and Snape looked worried and evasive. That smells dodgy.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “And don’t forget, if you’re talking about me among yourselves, call me Snuffles, okay?”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Sirius wants us to call him Snuffles when we talk about him to each other.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “I don’t want you lot sneaking out of school to see me, all right? Just send notes to me here.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Sirius is serious about keeping me at Hogwarts. He wants notes, not midnight visits.

Book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: Moody said my name and told me to come in. He was the one doing the inviting.

Book4-chapter30_Sc1.source: Harry walked inside. He had been inside Dumbledore’s office once before; it was a very beautiful, circular room, lined with pictures of previous headmasters and headmistresses of Hogwarts, all of whom were fast asleep, their chests rising and falling gently.
Book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I walked into Dumbledore's office again. It's a beautiful, round room full of sleeping portraits of former headteachers, their chests going up and down.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Maybe she had you bugged," said Harry.
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Maybe Rita's not using Muggle gadgets, but she's eavesdropping on people by magic. That explains how she's getting dirt on us.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "I want to know how she heard me talking to Viktor!"
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I don't think Rita's just gossiping. I believe she's actively spying on people and inventing stories from what she hears.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "We’re friends. She’s not my girlfriend and she never has been."
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Hermione and I are mates. People can stop reading into it. She's not my girlfriend.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "The Triwizard Cup will be placed in the center of the maze. The first champion to touch it will receive full marks."
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: The third task is a maze and touching the Cup gives full marks. It's straightforward but dangerous because of the obstacles Hagrid will supply.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "He looked as though he had been traveling for days."
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Crouch is not all right. Seeing him muttering and falling apart made me think something really bad has happened to him.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “You saved my life with that gillyweed, Dobby, you really did,” said Harry.
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Dobby saved me with that gillyweed. I owe him big time. He helped keep me alive, plain and simple.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “Winky still thinks Mr. Crouch is her master, sir, and nothing Dobby says will persuade her that Professor Dumbledore is her master now.”
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Winky thinks Mr Crouch is still her master and she won’t accept Dumbledore as her master. She’s miserable and it’s making her drink herself into a stupor.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “’Tis strong for a house-elf, sir,” he said.
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Butterbeer hits house-elves a lot harder than it does us. What seems weak to us can knock them sideways.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “Oh . . .” he said, the memory coming back to him at last. “I dunno . . . I never noticed it had gone. I was more worried about my wand, wasn’t I?”
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I didn’t even clock that Ron’s leprechaun gold had vanished at the time. I was so wrapped up in my wand and everything else that I missed it.

Book4-chapter29_Sc3.source: "Who’s he, to lecture me about being out-of-bounds?" said Harry in mild indignation as he folded up Sirius’s letter and put it inside his robes.
Book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: Who is he to lecture me about being out of bounds? After everything he did at school, I can't exactly take lectures from him.

Book4-chapter29_Sc3.source: "No one’s tried to attack me all year," said Harry. "No one’s done anything to me at all —"
Book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: No one has attacked me this year. Honestly, nothing's happened to me at all, so I'm not convinced there's an immediate threat.

Book4-chapter29_Sc6.source: "Harry saw George half glance at Fred, before smiling at Ron."
Book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I saw George give Fred a quick look before he smiled at Ron and Fred's grin disappeared. Something was up between them.

Book4-chapter29_Sc6.source: "George walked over to Fred, pulled the letter out of his hands, and began attaching it to the leg of the nearest barn owl."
Book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: George just nicked the letter off Fred and sent it away on an owl. They were treating it like a joke, not something serious.

Book4-chapter30_Sc2.source: "It was you who found him, was it not?" "Yes," said Harry.
Book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I found Mr Crouch. I was the one who turned him up on the grounds.

Book4-chapter30_Sc2.source: "I didn't see Madame Maxime anywhere, though, and she'd have a job hiding, wouldn't she?"
Book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I didn't see Madame Maxime anywhere. If she was here she'd have a job hiding, so she must not be around.

Book4-chapter30_Sc2.source: "Wait here for me, Harry," he said. "Our examination of the grounds will not take long."
Book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: Dumbledore told me to wait while they checked the grounds and said it would not take long.

Book4-chapter30_Sc3.source: "the clunks of Moody’s wooden leg growing fainter in the corridor below."
Book4-chapter30_Sc3.description: Moody's left. I can hear his wooden leg getting fainter down the corridor so I'm on my own here.
Hello, Fawkes. I'm talking to Fawkes now, we're alone together.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "No," said Harry. "If it was something that serious, they'd tell someone. They'd tell Dumbledore."
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: If it were really serious, they'd tell Dumbledore. I'm sure of it. They wouldn't keep something that big to themselves.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Yes," said Harry. "He'd probably blast us through the door if we wake him at the crack of dawn; he’ll think we’re trying to attack him while he’s asleep."
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: Moody is the sort of man who'd react like a cannon if we woke him up early. I don't want to risk him thinking we're attacking him.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Where's Hagrid? He's not at his door and the curtains are closed. Something's wrong and I want to know what.
Hagrid's indisposed. Someone's said he's too ill or otherwise unable to be out here.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: "There you go," he said. "Hate to break it to you, Potter. . . ."
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Someone shoved a Daily Prophet at me and I read that they are saying awful things about Hagrid.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: Article heading: "DUMBLEDORE'S GIANT MISTAKE" and text naming Hagrid as part-giant and dangerous
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: The Prophet says Hagrid is part-giant, breeds dangerous creatures like Blast-Ended Skrewts, has maimed pupils, and that Dumbledore made a mistake hiring him.
I can't believe the paper's dug up stuff about Hagrid's mother and his blood. How did they find out about Fridwulfa and all this? It's shocking.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "let's say Sirius is right, and someone Stunned Krum to kidnap Crouch. Well, they would’ve been in the trees near us, wouldn’t they? But they waited till I was out of the way until they acted, didn’t they? So it doesn’t look like I’m their target, does it?"
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I'm not their target. If they could wait until I was away to act, they were aiming at someone else, not me.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "I don't think so," said Harry, shaking his head. "He seemed really weak — I don't reckon he was up to Disapparating or anything."
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Crouch looked too weak to have Disapparated. He couldn't have just vanished on his own because he was too ill.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "I’ve told you, he wasn’t making much sense," said Harry. "He said he wanted to warn Dumbledore about something. He definitely mentioned Bertha Jorkins, and he seemed to think she was dead. He kept saying stuff was his fault. . . . He mentioned his son."
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: He was rambling and all over the place. He kept talking about warning Dumbledore, Bertha Jorkins, his guilt, and his son.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "I’ve told you," Harry repeated dully. "He said he’s getting stronger."
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: He said You-Know-Who is getting stronger. That stuck with me and it worries me.

Book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: Someone's ordering them to hurry. That voice is cold and urgent and they need this potion done fast.

Book4-chapter32_Sc6.source: The liquid in the cauldron seemed to heat very fast. The surface began not only to bubble, but to send out fiery sparks, as though it were on fire.
Book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: The potion is heating up crazy quickly and looks dangerous. It's bubbling and throwing sparks like it's on fire.

Book4-chapter32_Sc6.source: Wormtail was busying himself at the bottom of the cauldron with a wand. Steam was thickening, blurring the outline of Wormtail tending the fire. The movements beneath the robes became more agitated.
Book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: Wormtail's working the fire under the cauldron, and he's getting anxious. He's moving about like he's rushed and worried.

Book4-chapter32_Sc6.source: The large snake slithered away into the darkness.
Book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: The snake bolted off into the dark. It's gone, leaving the potion to heat up without it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: A large bubble issued from his mouth, and his wand, instead of sending sparks at the grindylows, pelted them with what seemed to be a jet of boiling water, for where it struck them, angry red patches appeared on their green skin.
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: My wand blasted them with what looked like boiling water and it actually burned the grindylows where it hit them. I had to spray shots behind me to keep them off.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: Harry pulled his ankle out of the grindylow’s grip and swam, as fast as he could, occasionally sending more jets of hot water over his shoulder at random; every now and then he felt one of the grindylows snatch at his foot again, and he kicked out, hard; finally, he felt his foot connect with a horned skull, and looking back, saw the dazed grindylow floating away, cross-eyed, while its fellows shook their fists at Harry and sank back into the weed.
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: Those grindylows latch onto ankles and keep coming back. I had to kick like mad and even rammed one with my foot to shake them off.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: He whipped around and saw Moaning Myrtle floating hazily in front of him, gazing at him through her thick, pearly glasses. "Myrtle!" Harry tried to shout — but once again, nothing came out of his mouth but a very large bubble. Moaning Myrtle actually giggled. "You want to try over there!" she said, pointing. "I won’t come with you. . . . I don’t like them much, they always chase me when I get too close. . . ."
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: Myrtle turned up and told me where to go but she won't come with me. She thinks the grindylows chase her and she's not coming anywhere near them.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: Then, at long last, he heard a snatch of haunting mersong. "An hour long you’ll have to look, And to recover what we took . . ." Harry swam faster and soon saw a large rock emerge out of the muddy water ahead.
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: The merpeople sing about the time limit. Their song made it clear I have an hour to find what they took, so I had to hurry toward that rock.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: ". . . your time’s half gone, so tarry not Lest what you seek stays here to rot. . . ." A cluster of crude stone dwellings stained with algae loomed suddenly out of the gloom on all sides. Here and there at the dark windows, Harry saw faces . . . faces that bore no resemblance at all to the painting of the mermaid in the prefects’ bathroom. . . . The merpeople had grayish skin and long, wild, dark green hair. Their eyes were yellow, as were their broken teeth, and they wore thick ropes of pebbles around their necks.
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: The merpeople are nothing like the pretty mermaid in the bathroom. They look nasty and dangerous, with grayish skin, yellow eyes and teeth, and weird ropes of pebbles. This place is serious.

Book4-chapter26_Sc4.source: He turned full circle in the water, the silence pressing harder than ever against his eardrums. He knew he must be even deeper in the lake now, but nothing was moving but the rippling weed. "How are you getting on?" Harry thought he was having a heart attack.
Book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I felt like I was alone down there, deeper than I expected, with the silence closing in on me. It made me panic for a second, like I was having a heart attack, but I forced myself to keep going.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I've been promoted," Percy said before Harry could even ask
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Percy's gone all puffed up about being promoted. He brags like he's the supreme ruler of the universe.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I'm now Mr. Crouch's personal assistant, and I'm here representing him."
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Percy is standing in for Crouch because Crouch is not well. He's been knocked about since the World Cup and they think he's overworked.
Dumbledore speaks to his plate and orders pork chops. Of course he does.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Her-my-oh-nee," she said slowly and clearly. "Herm-own-ninny." "Close enough," she said, catching Harry's eye and grinning.
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Hermione's teaching Krum to say her name and she caught my eye with a grin. She's messing about and enjoying it.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Nice socks, Potter," Moody growled as he passed, his magical eye staring through Harry's robes.
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Moody noticed my socks and called them out. Dobby knitted them for me, and I told him so, because I thought it was funny.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Come on!" Parvati hissed. "We're supposed to dance!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Parvati grabbed me to dance. I kept my head down, did the dancing, and she steered the whole time. Then she left mid-evening to dance with someone else.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "He's from Durmstrang!" spat Ron. "He's competing against Harry! Against Hogwarts!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Ron blew up about Krum being from Durmstrang and acting like Hermione is betraying Hogwarts by talking to him. Ron's made himself really obvious about being jealous and cross.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "The use of an Unforgivable Curse on a fellow human being meant a life term in Azkaban, that was what Moody had told them. Krum surely couldn’t have wanted the Triwizard Cup that badly. . . ."
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I can't believe Krum did that. I thought he was all right, but seeing him use an Unforgivable Curse makes me question him. He must have been desperate or messed up in some way.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Answer on your first guess — I let you pass. Answer wrongly — I attack. Remain silent — I will let you walk away from me unscathed."
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: Right, with that sphinx you only get one shot. I asked for the riddle and worked it out under pressure. Thinking fast actually mattered there.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Spy . . . er . . . spy . . . er . . ." said Harry, pacing up and down. "A creature I wouldn’t want to kiss . . . a spider!" The sphinx smiled more broadly. She got up, stretched her front legs, and then moved aside for him to pass.
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I figured the sphinx's riddle out. Spy, er, spy, er, spider. That felt good. I got lucky but I did it.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Cedric was sprinting as fast as he could toward the cup, and Harry knew he would never catch up, Cedric was much taller, had much longer legs —"
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: Cedric's faster than me. I knew I probably couldn't beat him in a straight race to the cup.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Cedric looked around at Harry again, who was now holding onto the hedge to support himself. Cedric took a deep breath. 'You take it. You should win. That’s twice you’ve saved my neck in here.'"
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: Cedric's decent. He wants me to have it after I helped him. He even tells me to take the cup. That shows he's honorable, which I did not expect in a competition like this.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "We’ll take it at the same time. It’s still a Hogwarts victory. We’ll tie for it."
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: We decide to share the win. Cedric and I go for the cup together. We're partners in that moment, not opponents.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "He was lifted into the air in its front legs; struggling madly, he tried to kick it; his leg connected with the pincers and next moment he was in excruciating pain."
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: That spider hit me hard. My leg's busted and bleeding. Spells like Stupefy barely work on those things alone. Getting disarmed and dropped hurt like mad.

Book4-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Harry raised his wand as the spider opened its pincers once more and shouted 'Expelliarmus!' It worked — the Disarming Spell made the spider drop him, but that meant that Harry fell twelve feet onto his already injured leg, which crumpled beneath him."
Book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: Expelliarmus actually saved me from worse, but I still came down badly. My ankle’s messed up and I can barely stand.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "He was sanest when he was trying to talk about Voldemort," said Harry, and Ron winced at the sound of the name.
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: When he talked about Voldemort he was the clearest. He kept trying to say he had to see Dumbledore. That part sounded real.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "If Snape hadn't held me up," Harry said bitterly, "we might've got there in time. 'The headmaster is busy, Potter, what's this rubbish, Potter?' Why couldn't he have just got out of the way?"
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: If Snape hadn't delayed me we might have made it. I keep thinking he blocked us for a reason and I hate that.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "If he had the Marauder's Map on him, it would've been easy," said Harry.
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: If Crouch had the Marauder's Map it would have been simple to find him inside the grounds.

Book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: TOM RIDDLE is carved on the headstone. I saw his name in the wandlight.
What the hell? It's Wormtail under the hood. I can tell by the missing finger and his breathing.

Book4-chapter32_Sc4.source: the cloaked man was now conjuring tight cords around Harry, tying him from neck to ankles to the headstone
Book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I'm tied to the headstone so tight I can't move an inch. He bound me from neck to ankles.

Book4-chapter32_Sc4.source: he hit him — hit him with a hand that had a finger missing
Book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: Wormtail's not just creepy, he's actively attacking me. He's an enemy who just grabbed me and tied me up.

Book4-chapter32_Sc1.source: "Did anyone tell you the Cup was a Portkey?"
Book4-chapter32_Sc1.description: The Cup was a Portkey. Nobody told me it would send us somewhere.
We're not at Hogwarts anymore; we're miles away in a dark, overgrown graveyard. That's bad news.
This feels dangerous, so I grabbed my wand straight away and got ready for trouble.

Book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: Blast-Ended Skrewts are huge and dangerous. I had to get away fast when Cedric warned me about them.
A Patronus actually works on dementors. I summoned a silver stag and it drove the thing back and made it stumble.
Sometimes things in the maze can be illusions or shape-shifters. Calling it out and using a trick can make them explode into smoke.
Reducto only works on solid stuff. It went straight through that golden mist and did nothing.
Fleur screamed and then went silent. That scream told me she might be out of the task or in trouble.
Stupefy can stop another champion in their tracks. I used it on Krum and it brought him down.
Impedimenta can freeze a creature if you hit the right spot. I managed to stop the skrewt by hitting its soft underside.

Book4-chapter31_Sc2.source: “What are you doing?” yelled Cedric’s voice. “What the hell d’you think you’re doing?”
Book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: Krum will attack another champion without warning. I barged through the hedge and found Cedric under an Unforgivable Curse.
Someone actually used the Cruciatus Curse in the maze. Cedric was writhing and twitching from it and I had to act fast.
I went straight to Cedric after stopping Krum. I grabbed him and checked he was breathing and okay.

Book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: Someone's coming. I can feel we're being watched and there's a short hooded figure walking toward us between the graves. It's carrying something that looks like a baby or a bundle of robes and it stopped about six feet away.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Cedric’s body was lying some twenty feet away.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: Cedric is dead. His body is about twenty feet away and I can see him lying there.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Some way beyond him, glinting in the starlight, lay the Triwizard Cup.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: The Triwizard Cup is nearby, glinting in the starlight not far past Cedric.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Harry’s wand was on the ground at Cedric’s feet.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: My wand is on the ground by Cedric’s feet. I do not have my wand.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: The bundle of robes that Harry had thought was a baby was close by, at the foot of the grave.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: That bundle of robes I thought was a baby is at the foot of the grave and it is moving.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: It seemed to be stirring fretfully.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: The thing in the robes is trying to get out. It is moving and struggling.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Harry watched it, and his scar seared with pain again
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: My scar is burning with pain again. I feel it, and it tells me something awful is happening.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: He couldn’t make a sound, nor could he see where Wormtail had gone; he couldn’t turn his head to see beyond the headstone; he could see only what was right in front of him.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I am tied up and I cannot move my head or make a sound. I can only see what is right in front of me.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: He looked down and saw a gigantic snake slithering through the grass, circling the headstone where he was tied.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: There is a huge snake slithering around the headstone where I am tied. It is circling me.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Wormtail’s fast, wheezy breathing was growing louder again. It sounded as though he was forcing something heavy across the ground.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: Wormtail is nearby, breathing wheezily, like he is dragging something heavy.

Book4-chapter32_Sc5.source: Then he came back within Harry’s range of vision, and Harry saw him pushing a stone cauldron to the foot of the grave. It was full of what seemed to be water — Harry could hear it slopping around — and it was larger than any cauldron Harry had ever used; a great stone belly large enough for a full-grown man to sit in.
Book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: Wormtail has pushed a huge stone cauldron to the grave. It is full of water and it is big enough for a grown man to sit in.

Book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: It didn't work. The revival failed. Nothing came back.

Book4-chapter32_Sc9.source: Let it have drowned, Harry thought, let it have gone wrong.
Book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I wanted it to have gone wrong. I actually hoped the whole thing had failed rather than what was happening now.

Book4-chapter32_Sc9.source: A surge of white steam billowed thickly from the cauldron instead, obliterating everything in front of Harry, so that he couldn’t see Wormtail or Cedric or anything but vapor hanging in the air.
Book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: A blast of thick white steam filled my view. I couldn't see Wormtail or Cedric anymore, just vapor everywhere.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore reckons You-Know-Who's getting stronger again as well?"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Dumbledore thinks You-Know-Who is getting stronger again. Great. Just what we needed.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He really trusts Snape, even though he knows he was a Death Eater?"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Dumbledore trusts Snape even though Snape used to be a Death Eater. I can't just dismiss that. If Dumbledore trusts him, there's got to be more going on.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "HARRY POTTER 'DISTURBED AND DANGEROUS'" headline and article
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Rita Skeeter has run a story calling me disturbed and dangerous, saying I collapse from my scar and even implying I might be like You-Know-Who. That's rubbish and it's meant to turn people against me.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Potter can speak Parseltongue," reveals Draco Malfoy
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: They're making a big deal out of the fact I can speak Parseltongue. Malfoy and others are using it to link me to Dark stuff. It's nasty and it scares people.
If Rita got details like my scar hurting from outside my dorm, then someone must have been listening or spying. I can't assume everything is private anymore.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "We are going to be patrolling the outside of the maze," said Professor McGonagall
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: McGonagall and the professors are guarding the maze. If I get into trouble I can send red sparks and they'll come for me. That makes the whole thing slightly less terrifying.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Tied in first place, with eighty-five points each — Mr. Cedric Diggory and Mr. Harry Potter"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: I'm tied with Cedric going into the final task. It's down to me to keep my head and do the hexes I practiced.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Surprise!" Mrs. Weasley said excitedly... "Thought we'd come and watch you, Harry!"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: The Weasleys turned up to watch me. That means more than I can say. It's good to have them here.

Book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: What the hell is that? They had some creature, shaped like a crouched child but not a child at all, hairless and scaly with a flat, snakelike face and gleaming red eyes. They lowered it into the cauldron, it hissed and vanished below the surface.
Wormtail looked sick and weak, not proud. He carried that thing with revulsion on his face, which makes him seem even more cowardly and miserable to me.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "he was not going to die crouching here like a child playing hide-and-seek; he was not going to die kneeling at Voldemort’s feet . . . he was going to die upright like his father, and he was going to die trying to defend himself, even if no defense was possible."
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: I am not going to curl up and hide. If I die, I will stand up and fight like my father. I'm doing this on purpose and I refuse to go down on my knees.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "As Harry shouted, 'Expelliarmus!' Voldemort cried, 'Avada Kedavra!' A jet of green light issued from Voldemort’s wand just as a jet of red light blasted from Harry’s — they met in midair"
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: My spell can meet his spell head on. When I shout Expelliarmus against Avada Kedavra they collide and something strange happens to both wands.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "a narrow beam of light connected the two wands, neither red nor green, but bright, deep gold."
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: When our spells connected a golden thread joined my wand to his. The wands can link in a way I have never seen before.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "It was a sound Harry recognized, though he had heard it only once before in his life: phoenix song."
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: That music is phoenix song. It fills me with hope and it feels like Dumbledore is right there with me. I can feel it inside me.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "His wand began to vibrate more powerfully than ever . . . and now the beam between him and Voldemort changed too . . . it was as though large beads of light were sliding up and down the thread connecting the wands"
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: The connection can push toward me. The light beads move along the thread and my wand gets unbearably hot when they come near. I can fight to shove them back though.

Book4-chapter34_Sc2.source: "He concentrated every last particle of his mind upon forcing the bead back toward Voldemort, his ears full of phoenix song, his eyes furious, fixed . . . and slowly, very slowly, the beads quivered to a halt, and then, just as slowly, they began to move the other way"
Book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: If I hold on and focus hard enough I can force the magic back toward him. I can resist and even reverse whatever is coming at me.

Book4-chapter32_Sc8.source: Bone of the father, unknowingly given, you will renew your son!
Book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: They're using a piece of someone's bones to bring someone back. That's what that line meant. They're actually trying to renew him with a father's bone.

Book4-chapter32_Sc8.source: Flesh of the servant willingly given you will revive your master
Book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: Wormtail is cutting himself and giving his own flesh to make this thing work. He is willing to hurt himself to bring his master back.

Book4-chapter32_Sc8.source: B-blood of the enemy forcibly taken you will resurrect your foe
Book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: They took my blood and poured it into that cauldron to revive him. My blood is part of the ritual and that's why they needed me tied up.

Book4-chapter32_Sc8.source: He felt its point penetrate the crook of his right arm and blood seeping down the sleeve of his torn robes
Book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: I couldn't believe Wormtail would stab me to get my blood. I know now that I'm helpless in his hands and he'll hurt me to bring his master back.

Book4-chapter32_Sc8.source: He was whimpering... He pulled a long, thin, shining silver dagger from inside his cloak
Book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: Wormtail isn't just loyal, he's desperate and terrified. He's willing to do filthy things for his master even if it means hurting me. He's a coward who'll betray any decency to save his boss.

Book4-chapter34_Sc1.source: "I said, bow," Voldemort said, raising his wand — and Harry felt his spine curve as though a huge, invisible hand were bending him ruthlessly forward, and the Death Eaters laughed harder than ever.
Book4-chapter34_Sc1.description: He can force people to obey with his wand and scares everyone into laughing at me when I'm on the receiving end.
I can shout no and drag myself out of whatever his spells try to do to my mind. I refused the command and it snapped me back.

Book4-chapter34_Sc1.source: "You won't say no? Harry, obedience is a virtue I need to teach you before you die."
Book4-chapter34_Sc1.description: Voldemort wants me to be obedient before he kills me. He's trying to break me and teach me to obey him.

Book4-chapter34_Sc1.source: "with the reflexes born of his Quidditch training, he flung himself sideways onto the ground; he rolled behind the marble headstone of Voldemort’s father, and he heard it crack as the curse missed him."
Book4-chapter34_Sc1.description: My Quidditch reflexes actually save me in a fight. I can dodge when it counts.

Book4-chapter34_Sc1.source: "he was not going to give him that satisfaction.\u0020.\u0020.\u0020he wasn't going to obey Voldemort\u0020.\u0020.\u0020he wasn't going to beg."
Book4-chapter34_Sc1.description: I won't play along or beg for my life just to make him happy. I'll stay proud even if it costs me.

Book4-chapter32_Sc3.description: My scar exploded with pain the moment that high cold voice said "Kill the spare" and I heard "Avada Kedavra". That voice and that curse hit me like nothing before and made my scar scream.

Book4-chapter32_Sc3.source: Cedric was lying spread-eagled on the ground beside him. He was dead.
Book4-chapter32_Sc3.description: Cedric is dead. He's lying next to me with open gray eyes and his mouth half-open. I couldn't believe it!

Book4-chapter32_Sc3.source: The short man in the cloak had put down his bundle, lit his wand, and was dragging Harry toward the marble headstone.
Book4-chapter32_Sc3.description: That short man in the cloak grabbed me, put me on my feet and dragged me toward the marble headstone. He's the one who shoved me into this, he's in control of what happens to me now.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: He is back. Voldemort is back. I couldn't believe it when I saw him.
Cedric is dead. They killed Cedric and I held him and I tried to bring him back for his parents.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.source: "He took stuff from his father’s grave, and from Wormtail, and me," said Harry.
Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: Voldemort used stuff from his father's grave, stuff from Wormtail, and my blood to get himself back. He used me against him.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.source: "And the Death Eaters? They returned?" "Yes," said Harry. "Loads of them"
Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: Loads of Death Eaters came back with him. He has allies again.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.source: "I saw my mum and dad . . . they came out of his wand."
Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I saw Mum and Dad come out of his wand. That was the weirdest thing, like they were real and then gone again.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.source: "There’s a Death Eater at Hogwarts! There’s a Death Eater here — they put my name in the Goblet of Fire, they made sure I got through to the end —"
Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: There is a Death Eater at Hogwarts who rigged the Triwizard stuff to make me compete. Someone here betrayed me.

Book4-chapter35_Sc1.source: "The Dark Lord got his body back? He’s returned?"
Book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I used to hope he was gone for good. Not anymore. He's back in a body and that changes everything.

Book4-chapter36_Sc1.source: "Minerva, could I ask you to stand guard here while I take Harry upstairs?" "Of course," said Professor McGonagall.
Book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: Professor McGonagall is staying here to keep watch while Dumbledore takes me upstairs. She's solid about it even if she looks a bit sick.

Book4-chapter36_Sc1.source: "Severus" — Dumbledore turned to Snape — "please tell Madam Pomfrey to come down here; we need to get Alastor Moody into the hospital wing."
Book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: Dumbledore wants Snape to fetch Madam Pomfrey so Moody can go to the hospital wing. Moody needs medical attention and Dumbledore's heading there.

Book4-chapter36_Sc1.source: "Then go down into the grounds, find Cornelius Fudge, and bring him up to this office. He will undoubtedly want to question Crouch himself."
Book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: Dumbledore is sending Snape to bring Fudge up here because Fudge will want to question Crouch in person.

Book4-chapter36_Sc1.source: "Tell him I will be in the hospital wing in half an hour’s time if he needs me."
Book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: Dumbledore says he'll be in the hospital wing in half an hour if Fudge needs him. He's prioritizing the hospital wing right now.

Book4-chapter36_Sc1.source: "Snape nodded silently and swept out of the room."
Book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: Snape nodded and left without a word. He's following Dumbledore's orders straight away and doesn't hang about.
Dumbledore is still looking out for me. He speaks to me gently and is taking responsibility for what happens next.

Book4-chapter36_Sc3.source: "They are with Professor Sprout," said Dumbledore.
Book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: Cedric's parents are with Professor Sprout. She's looking after them because she was Head of his House.

Book4-chapter36_Sc3.source: "Mad-Eye Moody, inside the trunk. Wormtail, slumped on the ground, cradling his stump of an arm. Voldemort, rising from the steaming cauldron. Cedric . . . dead . . . Cedric, asking to be returned to his parents."
Book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I saw Moody in a trunk, Wormtail wounded, Voldemort rising from a cauldron, and Cedric dead asking to be returned to his parents.

Book4-chapter36_Sc3.source: "I need to know what happened after you touched the Portkey in the maze, Harry," said Dumbledore.
Book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I touched the Portkey in the maze and whatever happened after that matters. I can't just avoid it forever even though I want to.

Book4-chapter36_Sc3.source: "Let him have a sleep. Let him rest."
Book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: Sirius cares about me and wants me to rest. I felt grateful when he put a hand on my shoulder.

Book4-chapter36_Sc3.source: There was a soft rush of wings. Fawkes the phoenix had left his perch, flown across the office, and landed on Harry's knee.
Book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: Fawkes is comforting. His weight and presence calmed me when everything else was raw.

Book4-chapter34_Sc3.source: "The ghost of the hand he had made Wormtail"
Book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: Something can be forced out of Voldemort's wand, like a smoky hand or even people. I actually pushed a bead of light back into his wand and things started coming out of it.
Cedric came out of Voldemort's wand as a solid looking shade and spoke to me. He trusted me enough to ask me to take his body back to his parents. I promised I would.

Book4-chapter34_Sc3.source: "Your father's coming. Hold on for your father. It will be all right. Hold on."
Book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: My mum and dad showed up from the wand too. My mum told me to hold on for my dad and my dad told me to be ready to run and get to the Portkey that will return me to Hogwarts. I have to get to that Portkey when I can.

Book4-chapter34_Sc3.source: "Voldemort's wand began to emit echoing screams of pain"
Book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: Voldemort's wand can suffer and be disrupted when something is forced back into it. That shook me. It made me realise he is not untouchable.

Book4-chapter34_Sc3.source: "Don't let him get you, Harry don't let go!"
Book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: The dead people that came out of the wand were trying to keep me alive by shielding me from Voldemort's gaze and shouting encouragement. They bought me the chance to run.
When I yelled Accio at the Triwizard Cup I was trying to pull it toward me. I can summon the Cup under pressure even with curses flying everywhere.
When the golden thread broke, the cage of light vanished but the shades stayed long enough to help. I had to run as fast as I could right then or lose the chance.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “Karkaroff fled tonight, when he felt the Dark Mark burn upon his arm. He betrayed too many faithful supporters of the Dark Lord to wish to meet them . . . but I doubt he will get far. The Dark Lord has ways of tracking his enemies.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: Karkaroff ran away the night his Dark Mark burned. He betrayed people and now he is on the run because Voldemort can track his enemies.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “No,” said Moody slowly. “No, he didn't. It was I who did that.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: Moody just told me he was the one who put my name into the Goblet of Fire.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “No, you didn’t,” he said. “You didn’t do that . . . you can’t have done . . .”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe Moody at first. I kept thinking he couldn't have done it.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “Who put your name in the Goblet of Fire, under the name of a different school? I did. Who frightened off every person I thought might try to hurt you or prevent you from winning the tournament? I did. Who nudged Hagrid into showing you the dragons? I did. Who helped you see the only way you could beat the dragon? I did.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: He admits he rigged the whole thing for me. He put my name in, scared off anyone who might stop me, pushed Hagrid to show me the dragons, and helped me figure out how to beat the dragon.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “I was keeping watch on you, Potter. I knew you hadn’t worked out the egg’s clue, so I had to give you another hint —”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: Moody was spying on me the whole time. He says he saw I didn't get the egg clue and that he gave me another hint.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “Who told Cedric to open it underwater? I did. I trusted that he would pass the information on to you. Decent people are so easy to manipulate, Potter. I was sure Cedric would want to repay you for telling him about the dragons, and so he did.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: He claims he told Cedric how to open the egg underwater, relying on Cedric to pass it to me. He thinks people like Cedric are easy to manipulate.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “I planted it there early on, I gave it to the Longbottom boy, don’t you remember?”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: Moody says he planted the book I needed in my dormitory by giving it to Neville.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: At the same time, Moody drew out his wand and pointed it at Harry.
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: Moody just pointed his wand at me while telling me this. I feel betrayed and threatened by him now.

Book4-chapter35_Sc2.source: “I have had to use every ounce of cunning I possess, so that my hand would not be detectable in your success. Dumbledore would have been very suspicious if you had managed everything too easily. As long as you got into that maze, preferably with a decent head start — then, I knew, I would have a chance of getting rid of the other champions and leaving your way clear.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: He admits he planned everything so Dumbledore would not suspect him, and that he arranged for me to have the best chance in the maze by getting rid of the other champions.

Book4-chapter36_Sc2.source: the pain in his leg, which he had not noticed all the time he had been listening to Crouch, now returned in full measure
Book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: My leg started hurting again, proper pain this time, after all that listening. I was aching and weak.

Book4-chapter36_Sc2.source: He also realized that he was shaking
Book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I was shaking. My hands felt useless and everything was a bit wobbly.

Book4-chapter36_Sc2.source: Dumbledore gripped his arm and helped him out into the dark corridor
Book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: Dumbledore grabbed my arm and helped me along. He's watching out for me right now.
