Book4-chapter36_Sc2.source: “I want you to come up to my office first, Harry,” he said quietly as they headed up the passageway. “Sirius is waiting for us there.”
Book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: Dumbledore told me to go up to his office first and said Sirius is waiting there. Sirius is here.

Book4-chapter36_Sc2.source: A kind of numbness and a sense of complete unreality were upon him, but he did not care; he was even glad of it
Book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I felt numb and unreal, and strangely I didn't mind. I was almost glad to be detached from it all.

Book5-chapter3_Sc1.source: “Lower your wand, boy, before you take someone’s eye out,” said a low, growling voice.
Book5-chapter3_Sc1.description: I know that voice. I recognised it straight away, even if I wasn't sure what to do next.

Book5-chapter3_Sc1.source: “Professor Moody?” he said uncertainly. “I don’t know so much about ‘Professor,’” growled the voice, “never got round to much teaching, did I? Get down here, we want to see you properly.”
Book5-chapter3_Sc1.description: I'm suspicious of him. I didn't lower my wand all the way and I kept my grip tight because I don't trust whatever Moody really is.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: I'm not messing about. If someone's trying to wind me up or threaten me I tell them to get out. I won't put up with it.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.source: "You going to tell us, then?" he said to George. "Who you were blackmailing?"
Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: Right, so there was blackmail involved and George was mixed up in it. I need to know who's behind things if it's going to affect any of us.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.source: "Bagman?" said Harry sharply. "Are you saying he was involved in —"
Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: Bagman was involved in the mess with the leprechaun gold and bets. That explains why he was hanging around helping me so much.

Book5-chapter2_Sc4.source: "I did the Patronus Charm to get rid of the dementors,"
Book5-chapter2_Sc4.description: I cast the Patronus Charm to drive the dementors away. It is the only thing that works against them.

Book5-chapter2_Sc4.source: "He must have sent them," said Harry quietly, more to himself than to Uncle Vernon.
Book5-chapter2_Sc4.description: I think Voldemort must have sent the dementors. It feels like they were there for me on purpose.
Voldemort is back. I saw him a month ago and he's returned.

Book5-chapter2_Sc4.source: "Back?" whispered Aunt Petunia. She was looking at Harry as she had never looked at him before.
Book5-chapter2_Sc4.description: Aunt Petunia looked at me with real fear for the first time. Her whole attitude toward magic cracked open.

Book5-chapter2_Sc4.source: "If it was demenders who hurt Dudley, how come you've been expelled? You did you-know-what, you've admitted it!"
Book5-chapter2_Sc4.description: Dudley got hurt and the Ministry thinks I did magic there. I'm facing an expulsion case whether or not the dementors were involved.

Book4-chapter36_Sc6.source: "I don't want that gold," said Harry in an expressionless voice. "You have it. Anyone can have it. I shouldn't have won it. It should've been Cedric's."
Book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I feel awful about winning. I shouldn't have had the Cup. Cedric should have won, not me.

Book4-chapter36_Sc6.source: "I told him to take the Cup with me," said Harry.
Book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I told Cedric to take the Cup with me. I said it out loud and I can't get rid of the thought that what I said mattered.

Book4-chapter36_Sc6.source: "You’ll see me very soon, Harry," said Sirius, turning to him. "I promise you." "Yeah," said Harry. "Yeah . . . of course I do."
Book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: Sirius promised he'll be back and I said I understood. I want to believe him and I'm clinging to that promise.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: There’s nothing in there. You can look for yourself, but there’s nothing at all. I’ve been checking every day. Just a small piece the day after the third task saying you won the tournament. They didn’t even mention Cedric. Nothing about any of it. If you ask me, Fudge is forcing them to keep quiet.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: They're trying to bury Cedric and the real story. The Prophet has barely mentioned any of it and I think Fudge is making them keep quiet. That's dodgy and wrong.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: Oh, Rita hasn’t written anything at all since the third task
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Rita Skeeter has gone quiet on paper since the third task. She might still be a problem, but she hasn't printed anything new.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: That’s never — you’re kidding — No, I’m not ... I caught her on the windowsill in the hospital wing. Look very closely, and you’ll notice the markings around her antennae are exactly like those foul glasses she wears.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Rita Skeeter is an Animagus who turns into a beetle. She's been spying on people in bug form. I can't believe she was that brazen, but Hermione's right.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: I liked Diggory ... He vos alvays polite to me. Alvays. Even though I vos from Durmstrang — with Karkaroff
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Krum liked Cedric and thought he was polite. That tells me Cedric was respected even by other schools. It matters that people across schools thought well of him.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "You take this," he muttered to her. "It should’ve been Cedric’s, he got there first, you take it —"
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: I grabbed Cedric's gold and tried to give it away. I wanted to give it to his family because he deserved it, but they wouldn't take it. I felt like I should do something for him.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "You all righ’?" he said gruffly. "Yeah," said Harry. "No, yeh’re not," said Hagrid.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Hagrid hugged me and made it clear I'm not all right. I'm shaken and he sees it, but he keeps saying we'll have to get on with it and fight.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Knew he was goin’ ter come back," said Hagrid, and Harry, Ron, and Hermione looked up at him, shocked.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: I can't pretend anymore. Voldemort is back and people like Hagrid have been expecting this. It's not just some horrible dream. We have to face it.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Yeh did as much as yer father would’ve done, an’ I can’ give yeh no higher praise than that."
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Hagrid told me I did as much as my dad would have. That mattered to me. It made me feel a bit like my parents were still with me.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Remember Cedric. Remember, if the time should come when you have to make a choice between what is right and what is easy, remember what happened to a boy who was good, and kind, and brave, because he strayed across the path of Lord Voldemort. Remember Cedric Diggory."
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Dumbledore told everyone to remember Cedric and to choose the right thing when it counts. That speech made it clear how serious this is and that people expect better of me.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: Harry’s trunk was packed; Hedwig was back in her cage on top of it.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: My trunk is packed and Hedwig is with me. I'm leaving Hogwarts feeling empty and I'm dreading going back to Privet Drive.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: We're going by broomstick. That's how we're getting there.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.source: "Only way. You're too young to Apparate, they'll be watching the Floo Network, and it's more than our life's worth to set up an unauthorized Portkey."
Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: I can't Apparate, the Floo network is being watched, and a Portkey is off the table. Flying is the only safe option.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.source: "I want three-hundred-and-sixty degrees visibility on the return journey."
Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: Moody's making sure we can see everything on the way back. He's serious about keeping watch.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.source: "Remus says you're a good flier," said Kingsley Shacklebolt ... "He's excellent," said Lupin.
Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: Remus and Kingsley think I can handle a broom. Lupin says I'm excellent, so they expect me to fly well.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.source: "Anyway, you'd better go and get packed, Harry, we want to be ready to go when the signal comes."
Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: I need to pack now and be ready to leave the moment they give the signal.

Book5-chapter3_Sc4.source: "I'll come and help you," said Tonks brightly.
Book5-chapter3_Sc4.description: Tonks is coming to help me pack. She's cheerful about it.

Book5-chapter2_Sc2.source: Of course he has," said Mrs Figg impatiently.
Book5-chapter2_Sc2.description: Dumbledore had me followed. I can't believe they'd shadow me, but Mrs Figg says they did so I need to expect more of that.
I did not cast the thing that made Dudley hear those horrors. I am not the one responsible for that.

Book5-chapter2_Sc2.source: I’ll take you to the door," said Mrs Figg
Book5-chapter2_Sc2.description: Mrs Figg is watching out for me. She is on my side and will try to keep me safe and give instructions when needed.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: he saw the sparkling surface of the potion that had revived Voldemort;
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I saw the potion that brought Voldemort back. The surface was sparkling and I know that's what woke him up.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: he saw the Death Eaters Apparating between the graves around them;
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: The Death Eaters apparated all around the graves. They turned up out of nowhere, right where we were.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: he saw Cedric’s body, lying on the ground beside the cup.
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: Cedric was lying dead by the cup. He was right there on the ground.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: When Harry told of Wormtail piercing his arm with the dagger, however, Sirius let out a vehement exclamation
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: Wormtail stabbed me in the arm with a dagger. It hurt like mad and it was Voldemort's sidekick who did it.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: It was even a relief; he felt almost as though something poisonous were being extracted from him.
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: Telling it all made me feel better. Saying it out loud pulled something poisonous out of me, like I could breathe again.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: Once or twice, Sirius made a noise as though about to say something, his hand still tight on Harry’s shoulder, but Dumbledore raised his hand to stop him
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: Sirius is desperate and protective, grabbing my shoulder like he wants to jump in. Dumbledore stopped him, which showed me Dumbledore wants control of how this is handled.

Book4-chapter36_Sc4.source: Dumbledore stood up so quickly that Harry started.
Book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: Dumbledore's reaction when I said Wormtail stabbed me was instant. He sprang up so fast it made me start, so I know he takes this seriously and he's ready to act.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "Of course I know Dumbledore, who doesn’t know Dumbledore?"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Mrs Figg knows Dumbledore and was acting on his orders to watch me. I can't believe she was spying on the Dursleys for Dumbledore all that time.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "I’m a Squib, as Mundungus knows full well, so how on earth was I supposed to help you fight off dementors?"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Mrs Figg is a Squib. She can't perform magic to help against dementors, which is why she couldn't defend me.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "MUNDUNGUS FLETCHER, I AM GOING TO KILL YOU!"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Mundungus was supposed to be on watch and he left. He abandoned his duty while I was attacked by dementors.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "There was a loud crack and a strong smell of mingled drink and stale tobacco filled the air as a squat, unshaven man in a tattered overcoat materialized right in front of them."
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Mundungus can Apparate and he has an Invisibility Cloak. He's dodgy and not exactly reliable.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "The Ministry have their own ways of detecting underage magic, they’ll know already, you mark my words"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: The Ministry will probably detect that I used magic, and that could get me into real trouble even though I used it to save us from dementors.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "I’ve got an owl, you can borrow her,"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: I can use my owl to send word to Dumbledore or get help, so I have a way to contact people quickly.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "Dementors attacking the boy on your watch!"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Dementors were actually in Wisteria Walk and they attacked me. That's why I had to use magic in front of Dudley.

Book5-chapter2_Sc1.source: "Get your fat bottom off the ground, quick!"
Book5-chapter2_Sc1.description: Dudley was knocked out or in shock after the dementor attack and I had to drag him. He's helpless right now and I had to haul him along.

Book5-chapter4_Sc2.source: "What on earth were they doing in a house that looked as though it belonged to the Darkest of wizards?"
Book5-chapter4_Sc2.description: This place looks like it belongs to a Dark wizard. What the hell is going on here?

Book5-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Ron and Hermione will explain everything, dear, I’ve really got to dash,"
Book5-chapter4_Sc2.description: Mrs Weasley's rushing off and says Ron and Hermione will explain things. Fine, I'll get the explanation from them.

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “I’m a Metamorphmagus,” she said, looking back at her reflection and turning her head so that she could see her hair from all directions.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: So Tonks can change her appearance whenever she wants. She was born like that. That is mental
Tonks is an Auror. Kingsley is higher up than her and she only qualified a year ago

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “Metamorphmagi are really rare, they’re born, not made.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: You can’t learn to be a Metamorphmagus. You’re born one or you use wandwork and potions instead

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “Scourgify —” She pointed her wand at Hedwig’s cage; a few feathers and droppings vanished.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: Tonks can do some cleaning spells but she’s not brilliant at household magic. Hedwig’s cage was getting smelly

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “Wow! A Firebolt?” Her eyes widened as they fell on the broomstick in Harry’s right hand.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: My Firebolt is special. It’s my pride and joy and it actually matters to others. I still ride a proper broom and I care about that

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “Bet you wouldn’t mind hiding that scar sometimes, eh?” Her eyes found the lightning-shaped scar on Harry’s forehead.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: I don’t like people staring at my scar. I wish I could hide it sometimes

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “I’ve left a letter telling your aunt and uncle not to worry —”
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: Lupin left a letter for the Dursleys so they’ll think I’m safe and will see me next summer

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: “Come here, boy,” said Moody gruffly, beckoning Harry toward him with his wand. “I need to Disillusion you.”
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: Moody gave me a Disillusionment Charm because the Invisibility Cloak won’t stay on while we’re flying. It feels odd like something cold running down me

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: He clicked the unlighter again; the next lamp went out. He kept clicking until every lamp in the square was extinguished
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: Moody has a Put-Outer that can snuff streetlamps. He borrowed it from Dumbledore

Book5-chapter3_Sc5.source: Harry started picking up books and throwing them hastily into his trunk.
Book5-chapter3_Sc5.description: I was a complete mess packing because I’d been stuck in my room and in a bad mood. My stuff was everywhere and I packed in a rush

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “This is not Alastor Moody,” said Dumbledore quietly.
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Moody was not the real Alastor Moody. I trusted him and he was an imposter posing as Moody.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “I called the elf to the staffroom to collect some robes for cleaning. I staged a loud conversation with Professor McGonagall about the hostages who had been taken, and whether Potter would think to use gillyweed. And your little elf friend ran straight to Snape’s office and then hurried to find you. . . .”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Someone staged things to trick Dobby and get me the gillyweed. I was being manipulated into thinking Dobby helped me when it was arranged to make me prepare for the task.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “You were so long in that lake, Potter, I thought you had drowned.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: They knew I was in the lake for ages and thought I might have died. I was closer to real danger than I knew.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “I was patrolling around it, able to see through the outer hedges, able to curse many obstacles out of your way. I Stunned Fleur Delacour as she passed. I put the Imperius Curse on Krum, so that he would finish Diggory and leave your path to the Cup clear.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: The imposter controlled the maze. He stunned Fleur and used the Imperius Curse on Krum to clear a path for me. My 'win' was rigged by him.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “The Dark Lord didn’t manage to kill you, Potter, and he so wanted to,” whispered Moody. “Imagine how he will reward me when he finds I have done it for him. I gave you to him — the thing he needed above all to regenerate — and then I killed you for him.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I thought Voldemort's return and the maze were separate, but the imposter says he handed me to Voldemort and tried to help him. That means I was used as bait and almost killed to help Voldemort come back properly.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “We’ll see who’s mad, now that the Dark Lord has returned, with me at his side! He is back, Harry Potter, you did not conquer him — and now — I conquer you!”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: The imposter wanted to join Voldemort and believed he would be rewarded. He betrayed everything and wanted to be on Voldemort's side.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “Stupefy!” There was a blinding flash of red light, and with a great splintering and crashing, the door of Moody’s office was blasted apart — Moody was thrown backward onto the office floor. Harry, still staring at the place where Moody’s face had been, saw Albus Dumbledore, Professor Snape, and Professor McGonagall looking back at him out of the Foe-Glass.
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Dumbledore, Snape and McGonagall arrived to stop the imposter. I was found and pulled out of the situation by them.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: The look upon Dumbledore’s face as he stared down at the unconscious form of Mad-Eye Moody was more terrible than Harry could have ever imagined. There was no benign smile upon Dumbledore’s face, no twinkle in the eyes behind the spectacles. There was cold fury in every line of the ancient face.
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Dumbledore was furious and deadly serious about the imposter and what had been done. This was not a small matter to him.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “Severus, please fetch me the strongest Truth Potion you possess, and then go down to the kitchens and bring up the house-elf called Winky. Minerva, kindly go down to Hagrid’s house, where you will find a large black dog sitting in the pumpkin patch. Take the dog up to my office, tell him I will be with him shortly, then come back here.”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wanted a Truth Potion and Winky brought up. He was going to get the truth out of the imposter and sort this properly.

Book4-chapter35_Sc3.source: “Come along, Potter,” she whispered. The thin line of her mouth was twitching as though she was about to cry. “Come along . . . hospital wing . . .”
Book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: Professor McGonagall was worried about me. Even though I needed to face what happened, she's clearly frightened and cares about my wellbeing.

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "He could still’ve kept me informed if he’d wanted to," "Maybe he thinks I can’t be trusted"
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: Dumbledore has been keeping me out of the loop on purpose and I reckon he might not trust me as much as I thought

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "WHO SAVED THE SORCERER’S STONE? WHO GOT RID OF RIDDLE? WHO SAVED BOTH YOUR SKINS FROM THE DEMENTORS?"
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: I did the dangerous stuff before and I saved people that mattered. I know I handled things no one expected me to

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "How come I have to stay at the Dursleys’ while you two get to join in everything that’s going on here?"
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: I feel shut out from my friends and angry that they get to be together at Hogwarts while I’m stuck with the Dursleys

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "It was me that lured them out of the way. Sent a letter by Muggle post telling them they'd been short-listed for the All-England Best-Kept Suburban Lawn Competition."
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: Tonks tricked the Dursleys and got them out of the house by sending a fake Muggle letter. Lucky for me, they are gone because of her trick.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Almost at once," said Lupin, "we're just waiting for the all-clear."
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: We are leaving very soon. They are just waiting for a signal before we go.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Not the Burrow, no," said Lupin, motioning Harry toward the kitchen; the little knot of wizards followed, all still eyeing Harry curiously. "Too risky. We've set up headquarters somewhere undetectable."
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: We're not going to the Burrow because it's too risky. They have set up some hidden headquarters instead.
There are a whole lot of people here to watch over me. They are acting as my guard.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Don't call me Nymphadora, Remus," said the young witch with a shudder. "It's Tonks."
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: She wants to be called Tonks, not Nymphadora. She hates that name.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "This is Alastor Moody, Harry," Lupin continued, pointing toward Moody.
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: Moody is Alastor Moody. I already knew his face, but now I know who he really is.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Get me a glass of water, would you, Harry?" asked Moody.
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: Moody told me to fetch him a glass of water. He can be blunt and bossy even here.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "Damn it," he added angrily, putting a hand up to the magical eye, "it keeps sticking"
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: Moody's magical eye is unreliable and it irritates him. He actually pops it out when it sticks.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "A surprising number of people volunteered to come and get you," said Lupin
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: More people than I expected turned up to collect me. I feel like I'm suddenly very important and everyone is watching me.
We only have about fifteen minutes before the all-clear or we have to move. There is no time to hang about.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "My dad's Muggle-born and he's a right old slob. I suppose it varies, just like with wizards?"
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: Tonks was comparing Muggles to wizards and mentioning her Muggle-born dad. She notices things about Muggle houses and finds them interesting.

Book5-chapter3_Sc3.source: "We are just waiting for the signal to tell us it's safe to set off," said Lupin
Book5-chapter3_Sc3.description: They are not telling me much because it's too risky to talk. Everything is being kept quiet until it's safe.
Moody can shut people down when it's risky to talk. He takes his job as guard seriously and is quick to silence anyone who might blabber.

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "He said my blood would make him stronger than if he’d used someone else’s"
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: My blood protects me because of Mum. Voldemort used my blood so he could touch me without hurting himself and try to steal that protection
When wands that share the same core are forced to duel they can cause Priori Incantatem and force echoes of the spells the other wand has done to reappear

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "The last murders the wand performed," said Dumbledore, nodding.
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: Those echoes can show the most recent victims first so Cedric and even my parents could appear as echoes coming out of Voldemort's wand

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "You’ve been reading Rita Skeeter, Mr. Fudge," he said quietly.
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: People like Fudge are listening to gossip and lying journalists instead of what actually happened to me and that stinks

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "You’ll see me very soon, Harry," said Sirius, turning to him. "I promise you."
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: Sirius promised he’ll come back to me soon even though he has to go off and warn the others

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "I don't want that gold," said Harry in an expressionless voice. "You have it."
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: I don't care about the thousand Galleons. Winning means nothing when people I care about are dead and Voldemort is back

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: CAN’T’VE WANTED TO THAT MUCH, CAN YOU, OR YOU’D HAVE SENT ME AN OWL, BUT DUMBLEDORE MADE YOU SWEAR —
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: So you lot knew enough to get Dumbledore to make them swear secrecy and still didn't send me an owl. I trusted you to tell me. That's messed up.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix,” said Ron at once.
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: This is the Order of the Phoenix's headquarters. Right here. So we're actually with the people fighting him.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “It’s a secret society,” said Hermione quickly. “Dumbledore’s in charge, he founded it. It’s the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time.”
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: The Order is a secret society. Dumbledore founded it. They're the ones who fought You-Know-Who before.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Fred and George have invented Extendable Ears, see,” said Ron.
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: Fred and George made something called Extendable Ears. Sounds useful if we want to know what people are saying.

Book5-chapter3_Sc2.source: [“It’s all right, Harry. We’ve come to take you away.”]
Book5-chapter3_Sc2.description: You're here to take me away. Thank you. I can't believe they're here after four weeks of nothing.
That's Lupin's voice. I know him. He's real and he came back for me.

Book5-chapter3_Sc2.source: [“Harry, what form does your Patronus take?” “A stag,” said Harry nervously.]
Book5-chapter3_Sc2.description: My Patronus is a stag. They already know that and that proves I'm me.

Book5-chapter3_Sc2.source: [Lupin held out his hand and shook Harry’s.]
Book5-chapter3_Sc2.description: Lupin is on my side. He shook my hand and looked at me like he meant it.

Book5-chapter3_Sc2.source: [He had recently spent nine months in what he had thought was Mad-Eye Moody’s company only to find out that it wasn’t Moody at all, but an impostor; an impostor, moreover, who had tried to kill Harry before being unmasked.]
Book5-chapter3_Sc2.description: I can't trust appearances. People I thought I knew can be impostors. I need real proof before I trust anyone.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Think about what you’ve just memorized," said Lupin quietly.
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: I remembered the name Twelve Grimmauld Place and as soon as I did a battered door appeared between numbers eleven and thirteen. That place was hiding in plain sight.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Not here, boy!" snarled Moody. "Wait till we’re inside!" He pulled the piece of parchment out of Harry’s hand and set fire to it with his wand-tip.
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: Moody burned the message right out of my hand. No way to keep that note now. He means business and is not messing about.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "No, Harry, the meeting’s only for members of the Order. Ron and Hermione are upstairs, you can wait with them until the meeting’s over and then we’ll have dinner. And keep your voice down in the hall," she added in an urgent whisper.
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: I’m not allowed in the Order meeting. Ron and Hermione are waiting upstairs and I have to keep quiet in the hallway or Mrs Weasley warns it could wake something up.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: A closer look showed Harry that the heads belonged to house-elves.
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: There are shrunken house-elf heads mounted on the wall. That’s grim and weird even for a wizarding house.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Oh, Harry, it’s lovely to see you!" she whispered, pulling him into a rib-cracking hug before holding him at arm’s length and examining him critically. "You’re looking peaky; you need feeding up, but you’ll have to wait a bit for dinner, I’m afraid . . ."
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: Mrs Weasley fusses over me like always. I might be treated like a kid but I know she’s on my side and I can count on her to look out for me.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: Could it have been me? I said that sarcastically because I felt accused, but I know I wasn't involved in whatever they were on about.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "We knew you’d be angry, Harry, we really don’t blame you, but you’ve got to understand, we did try and persuade Dumbledore —"
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: They tried to get Dumbledore on their side. I’m not surprised they did, and I can grudgingly admit they at least tried.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Both of them were watching him apprehensively, as though they feared that he would start shouting again now that everyone else had gone."
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: Seeing them so nervous made me feel guilty. I can’t just keep snapping at them; I feel bad when they’re scared of me.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: “De — men — tors,” said Harry slowly and clearly. “Two of them.”
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: There were two dementors there. I saw them. I won't pretend otherwise.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: “They guard the wizard prison, Azkaban,” said Aunt Petunia.
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: Dementors are the guards from Azkaban. They aren't random animals, they're tied to the wizarding world.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: “I told you — they suck all the happiness out of you,” said Harry, “and if they get the chance, they kiss you —”
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: Dementors drain all your happiness and can 'kiss' you, which is basically having your soul taken. That's not a metaphor. It's terrifying.
The Patronus Charm is the only thing that works against dementors. I used it to save Dudley.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: Harry read Sirius’s message. "Arthur’s just told us what happened. Don’t leave the house again, whatever you do."
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: Sirius knows something happened because Arthur told him. He's worried and blunt about it. He didn't send the long explanation I wanted.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: “If it was demenders who hurt Dudley, how come you’ve been expelled? You did you-know-what, you’ve admitted it!”
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: The Ministry thinks I did something wrong and I've been expelled from school for it, even though I used the Patronus to fight dementors off.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: “It’s you,” said Uncle Vernon forcefully. “It’s got something to do with you, boy, I know it. Why else would they turn up here? Why else would they be down that alleyway? You’ve got to be the only — the only —”
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: The Dursleys blame me for attracting trouble. They already see me as the reason dementors showed up, and they won't hesitate to say I caused it.

Book5-chapter2_Sc3.source: He was desperate to be alone, to think, perhaps to send a letter to Ron, Hermione, or Sirius.
Book5-chapter2_Sc3.description: After everything, I just want to get away and tell someone I trust what happened. I need help and answers, not lectures.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "— swear not to tell me," said Harry.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: They were made to swear not to tell me what was going on. Dumbledore got them to keep things from me.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "that’s why he’s had people from the Order of the Phoenix tailing you all the time,"
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Everyone knew I'd been followed by the Order of the Phoenix this summer, except me. So people were watching my every move and I had no idea.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "So everyone had known he was being followed except him."
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: I feel betrayed and furious that they all knew about the tailing and kept me in the dark. I looked after myself anyway, and they still treated me like I couldn't cope.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "The warm glow that had flared inside him at the sight of his two best friends was extinguished as something icy flooded the pit of his stomach."
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: I wanted to be happy seeing Ron and Hermione, but finding out they hid this from me put distance between us. I don't feel like celebrating right now.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Hedwig!" The snowy owl clicked her beak and nibbled his ear affectionately as Harry stroked her feathers.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Hedwig came straight to me and is glad to see me. She's been in a state because of everything, but she's mine and she trusts me.

Book5-chapter7_Sc5.source: “Eleven inches, phoenix-feather core, been in use four years. That correct?”
Book5-chapter7_Sc5.description: My wand is eleven inches with a phoenix-feather core and I've used it for four years.

Book5-chapter7_Sc5.source: “I keep this,” said the wizard, impaling the slip of parchment on a small brass spike. “You get this back,” he added, thrusting the wand at Harry.
Book5-chapter7_Sc5.description: The wand-checking wizard keeps a record of my wand on a little slip of parchment but gives me the actual wand back.

Book5-chapter7_Sc5.source: “Thank you, Eric,” said Mr Weasley firmly, and grasping Harry by the shoulder, he steered him away from the desk
Book5-chapter7_Sc5.description: Mr Weasley is looking out for me. He grabs my shoulder and steers me away from the desk like he's in charge and won't let anyone bother me.

Book5-chapter7_Sc5.source: Jostled slightly by the crowd, Harry followed Mr Weasley through the gates into the smaller hall beyond, where at least twenty lifts stood behind wrought golden grilles.
Book5-chapter7_Sc5.description: After the check we went through the golden gates into a smaller hall full of lifts behind golden grilles.

Book5-chapter6_Sc3.source: Harry took as much time as he dared to close the drawing room door; he wanted to listen to what was going on downstairs.
Book5-chapter6_Sc3.description: I hung back a bit before shutting the door because I wanted to hear the commotion downstairs. I can’t stand being shut out of what’s happening.

Book5-chapter7_Sc3.source: Mrs Weasley hugged him. "We’ve all got our fingers crossed," she said.
Book5-chapter7_Sc3.description: Mum's worried for me and she cares a lot. She hugged me and said they're all keeping their fingers crossed for me.

Book5-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Arthur Weasley, Misuse of Muggle Artifacts Office, here to escort Harry Potter, who has been asked to attend a disciplinary hearing . . ."
Book5-chapter7_Sc3.description: Mr Weasley is Arthur Weasley from the Misuse of Muggle Artifacts Office and he's escorting me to some disciplinary hearing.

Book5-chapter7_Sc3.source: "As a matter of fact I’ve never even used the visitor’s entrance before."
Book5-chapter7_Sc3.description: Mr Weasley doesn't use the visitor's entrance and gets confused by Muggle travel. He does not know all the Muggle ways.

Book5-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Welcome to the Ministry of Magic. Please state your name and business."
Book5-chapter7_Sc3.description: The Ministry entrance is hidden in a scruffy Muggle telephone box and it has that cold automated welcome that asks for your name and business.

Book5-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Visitor, please take the badge and attach it to the front of your robes."
Book5-chapter7_Sc3.description: You get a visitor badge from a chute in the phone box that comes out where coins normally appear. That is how you check in at the Ministry.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: I'm not on the Black family tree anymore. My name has been ripped off that tapestry, like I never belonged there.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: I used to be there, My sweet old mother blasted me off after I ran away from home
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: Sirius is bitter about his family. He hates them and left because he couldn't stand their snobbish pure-blood rubbish.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: He was younger than me, and a much better son, as I was constantly reminded.
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: Regulus was Sirius's brother and he ended up dead, and the family used Regulus as the 'good son' to shame Sirius.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: Oh no, No, he was murdered by Voldemort. Or on Voldemort’s orders, more likely
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: Regulus didn’t just die by accident. He was killed because of his involvement with Voldemort, probably on Voldemort's orders.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: Kreacher can see the scar, it must be true, that’s that boy who stopped the Dark Lord
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: Kreacher recognizes me by my scar. Even that filthy old elf knows who I am and what I did.

Book5-chapter7_Sc1.source: "M-m-morning, Harry," yawned Tonks. Her hair was blonde and curly this morning.
Book5-chapter7_Sc1.description: Tonks looks different this morning, all blonde and curly and sleepy. She's been up and out of sorts, so I shouldn't expect her to be sharp right now.

Book5-chapter7_Sc1.source: "I’ve b-b-been up all night," she said, with another shuddering yawn.
Book5-chapter7_Sc1.description: Tonks has been up all night. She's tired and jittery, so whatever she's said might be half of what she means.

Book5-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Oh . . . yeah . . . well, we need to be a bit more careful, he’s been asking Kingsley and me funny questions . . ."
Book5-chapter7_Sc1.description: Scrimgeour has been asking Kingsley and Tonks odd questions. They think we need to be more careful around him.
I just want something simple and quiet right now. I don't want to get pulled into a fuss.
I'm uneasy and squirming inside, glad I don't have to join the grown-ups talking about Scrimgeour.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: "The hearing's on my floor, in Amelia Bones's office. She's Head of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement and she's the one who'll be questioning you."
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: The hearing will be in Amelia Bones's office on Mr Weasley's floor. She's the one who is going to question me.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: "The law's on your side," said Lupin quietly. "Even underage wizards are allowed to use magic in life-threatening situations."
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: Lupin says the law lets underage wizards use magic if lives are at risk. That's my defence.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Amelia Bones is okay, Harry," said Tonks earnestly. "She's fair, she'll hear you out."
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: Tonks thinks Amelia Bones will be fair. I can at least hope she'll listen to what happened.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: "And if it's not," said Sirius grimly, "I'll see to Amelia Bones for you . . ."
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: Sirius will stand up for me if it goes badly. He is ready to act on my behalf.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Don't lose your temper," said Sirius abruptly. "Be polite and stick to the facts."
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: Sirius and the others think I need to keep calm, be polite and stick to the facts at the hearing.

Book5-chapter7_Sc2.source: Mrs Weasley pressed hard on the top of his head. "Doesn't it ever lie flat?" she said desperately.
Book5-chapter7_Sc2.description: Mrs Weasley fusses over me and tries to fix my hair even when I don't want her to. She cares and gets nervous.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "You know, I’m surprised at you. I thought the first thing you’d do when you got here would be to start asking questions about Voldemort."
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: I want answers about Voldemort. I asked Ron and Hermione but they said I’m not allowed in the Order, so I’ve been shut out. I saw Voldemort come back and that gives me every right to ask questions.
Molly hates Mundungus. Sirius says he’s useful and loyal to Dumbledore, but Mum thinks inviting him for dinner is too much. That’s awkward for me.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "He’s useful," Sirius muttered. "Knows all the crooks — well, he would, seeing as he’s one himself. But he’s also very loyal to Dumbledore, who helped him out of a tight spot once."
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: Sirius thinks Mundungus is shady but valuable. He hears things we wouldn’t otherwise. That explains why Dung is around despite Mum’s disapproval.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "He’s not a member of the Order of the Phoenix!" said Mrs Weasley. "He’s only fifteen and —" "— and he’s dealt with as much as most in the Order," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: People argue about whether I should be told things. I feel I’m not just a kid to be sheltered. I’m older than they treat me and I deserve a say.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Dumbledore must have had his reasons for not wanting Harry to know too much," said Mrs Weasley.
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: Dumbledore deliberately kept stuff from me for reasons I may not like but that were supposed to protect me. Now I’m at headquarters and that position is shifting.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Hestia’s just relieved me, so she’s got Moody’s cloak now, thought I’d leave a report for Dumbledore . . ."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Kingsley just arrived and left a report for Dumbledore. Hestia has Moody's cloak now.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Right, you lot, you need to be careful, because doxies bite and their teeth are poisonous. I’ve got a bottle of antidote here, but I’d rather nobody needed it."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Mrs Weasley warned that doxies bite and their teeth are poisonous and she has an antidote. We had to spray them and drop them in a bucket.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "When I say the word, start spraying immediately," she said. "They’ll come flying out at us, I expect, but it says on the sprays one good squirt will paralyze them."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Doxycide works fast. One good squirt will paralyze a doxy and you can pick it up.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "We want to experiment with doxy venom for our Skiving Snackboxes," George told Harry under his breath.
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Fred and George are using doxy venom to test effects for their Skiving Snackboxes.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Range of sweets to make you ill," George whispered, "Not seriously ill, mind, just ill enough to get you out of a class when you feel like it."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Skiving Snackboxes are sweets designed to make you briefly ill so you can skip class, then recover with the other half of the sweet.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Well, we haven’t had a chance to get premises yet," said Fred, "so we’re running it as a mail-order service at the moment. We put advertisements in the Daily Prophet last week."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Their joke shop isn't open yet. They're running it by mail order and they put ads in the Daily Prophet.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "But don’t worry . . . Mum hasn’t got a clue. She won’t read the Daily Prophet anymore, ’cause of it telling lies about you and Dumbledore."
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: Mrs Weasley doesn't read the Daily Prophet now, so she won't know about the twins' ads or my part in funding them.

Book5-chapter6_Sc4.source: "He had forced the Weasley twins to take the thousand-Galleon prize money he had won in the Triwizard Tournament to help them realize their ambition to open a joke shop"
Book5-chapter6_Sc4.description: I gave the twins my thousand Galleons to help them start their joke shop. They think it's brilliant and Mum does not know I helped.

Book5-chapter7_Sc4.source: "Visitor to the Ministry, you are required to submit to a search and present your wand for registration at the security desk, which is located at the far end of the Atrium."
Book5-chapter7_Sc4.description: Visitors have to be searched and hand over their wand at the security desk at the far end of the Atrium.

Book5-chapter7_Sc4.source: "Step over here," said the wizard in a bored voice. Harry walked closer to him and the wizard held up a long golden rod, thin and flexible as a car aerial, and passed it up and down Harry's front and back. "Wand," grunted the security wizard at Harry, putting down the golden instrument and holding out his hand.
Book5-chapter7_Sc4.description: The security wizards physically scan you with a long golden rod and then demand your wand.

Book5-chapter7_Sc4.source: "I'm escorting a visitor," said Mr Weasley, gesturing toward Harry.
Book5-chapter7_Sc4.description: Mr Weasley is escorting me through the Ministry. He is looking out for me right now.

Book5-chapter7_Sc4.source: If I'm not expelled from Hogwarts, I'll put in ten Galleons, Harry found himself thinking desperately.
Book5-chapter7_Sc4.description: If I manage to stay at Hogwarts, I want to put ten Galleons in the fountain for St. Mungo's.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “I mean, all they’ve really said is that the Order’s trying to stop people joining Vol —”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: The Order is trying to stop people joining Voldemort. I’m not surprised, that’s basically what they kept going on about.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “When are you going to start using his name? Sirius and Lupin do.”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: People should use his name. I want us to say Voldemort properly like Sirius and Lupin do, not skirt around it.
Sirius hinted at some kind of weapon. I’ve got to find out what he really meant.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “He’s got the Cruciatus Curse for causing pain,”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: Voldemort already has the Cruciatus for torture, so whatever this weapon is, it might be something different from just causing pain.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "I mean, all they’ve really said is that the Order’s trying to stop people joining Vol —" "— demort ,"said Harry firmly.
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: They're trying to stop people joining Voldemort. Say his name. Sirius and Lupin do.
There’s some weapon out there that worries me. It could be something that kills loads of people at once or tortures them. I want to know what it is and who’s got it.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "He’s got the Cruciatus Curse for causing pain," said Harry.
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: I’m thinking Voldemort already has ways to cause terrible pain. He doesn’t need anything more efficient than that, but whatever this weapon is, it’s bad news.

Book5-chapter7_Sc9.source: "they've changed the time and venue — it starts at eight o'clock now and it's down in old Courtroom Ten"
Book5-chapter7_Sc9.description: They've moved my hearing. It starts at eight o'clock now and it's down in old Courtroom Ten. If we'd been five minutes later we'd have missed it.

Book5-chapter7_Sc9.source: "Quick, Harry, we should have been there five minutes ago!"
Book5-chapter7_Sc9.description: We're already late. I felt sick and stupid, like I'd left all my insides back at Perkins's desk, and we had to race through the Ministry to get there.

Book5-chapter7_Sc9.source: "Those courtrooms haven't been used in years," said Mr Weasley angrily. "I can't think why they're doing it down there"
Book5-chapter7_Sc9.description: Using the old courtrooms is odd. It makes me uneasy, like something about the hearing is off or being hidden.
The Department of Mysteries was named as where we were headed or involved. That name put me on edge and made the whole thing feel more serious.

Book5-chapter7_Sc8.source: "Sirius’s face was blinking down at him from every direction."
Book5-chapter7_Sc8.description: Sirius is everywhere in this office. His face is on every scrap of paper and it gave me a proper shock when I walked in.

Book5-chapter7_Sc8.source: "Give him the magazine, he might find it interesting."
Book5-chapter7_Sc8.description: Kingsley still looks out for me. He’d wink and shove something my way because he thinks I’d want to see it.

Book5-chapter7_Sc8.source: "They were talking to each other as though they hardly knew each other, and when Harry opened his mouth to say hello to Kingsley, Mr Weasley stood on his foot."
Book5-chapter7_Sc8.description: Mr Weasley is rushed and a bit distracted here. He barely notices what’s going on and even ends up standing on my foot when I try to say hello.

Book5-chapter7_Sc7.source: “aren’t we underground?” “Yes, we are,” said Mr Weasley, “those are enchanted windows; Magical Maintenance decide what weather we’re getting every day.”
Book5-chapter7_Sc7.description: So these windows are enchanted and Magical Maintenance chooses the weather for the Ministry. Weird, but it explains the sunlight even though we are underground.

Book5-chapter7_Sc7.source: “Just Interdepartmental memos,” Mr Weasley muttered to him. “We used to use owls, but the mess was unbelievable . . . droppings all over the desks . . .”
Book5-chapter7_Sc7.description: The memos flying around are actually Ministry interdepartmental memos. They replaced owls because of the mess. That explains all the fluttering bits.

Book5-chapter7_Sc7.source:
“Level two, Department of Magical Law Enforcement, including the Improper Use of Magic Office, Auror Headquarters, and Wizengamot Administration Services.”

“This is us, Harry,” said Mr Weasley, and they followed the witch out of the lift into a corridor lined with doors. “My office is on the other side of the floor.”
Book5-chapter7_Sc7.description: We're heading to the Department of Magical Law Enforcement and Mr Weasley works somewhere on that floor near Auror Headquarters. This is where he works.

Book5-chapter7_Sc7.source: Harry looked surreptitiously through the doorways as they passed.
Book5-chapter7_Sc7.description: The place is full of cubicles and people; memos zoom everywhere and Auror Headquarters looks busy. It's loud and chaotic in a proper Ministry sort of way.

Book5-chapter8_Sc1.source: "An owl was sent to you this morning."
Book5-chapter8_Sc1.description: They sent an owl this morning. I missed it and that's why I'm being told I'm late.
They ordered me to sit down right away. There's no messing about.

Book5-chapter8_Sc1.source: Harry dropped his gaze to the chair in the center of the room, the arms of which were covered in chains
Book5-chapter8_Sc1.description: That chair in the middle has chains on the arms. They're clearly planning to chain someone in it.
They're blaming me for being late. I can feel the whole place watching me like I'm in trouble already.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: "We thought it was a bog-standard chicken until it started breathing fire."
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: That box might not hold a normal animal. It actually breathed fire. That's mental and could be dangerous.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: "All right, Arthur?" said the wizard, nodding at Mr Weasley.
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: I stuck close to Mr Weasley, trying not to draw attention. I was jammed against the back wall of the lift and trying to keep my head down.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: "Level seven, Department of Magical Games and Sports, incorporating the British and Irish Quidditch League Headquarters, Official Gobstones Club, and Ludicrous Patents Office."
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: The Ministry has a floor for Quidditch and other odd departments. The lift announces every level so you know exactly where you're going.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: Harry glimpsed an untidy-looking corridor, with various posters of Quidditch teams tacked lopsidedly on the walls; one of the wizards in the lift, who was carrying an armful of broomsticks, extricated himself with difficulty and disappeared down the corridor.
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: There are Quidditch posters everywhere and people carrying broomsticks. The place smells like it's full of sports and chaos.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: The doors closed, the lift juddered upward again, and the woman’s voice said, "Level six, Department of Magical Transport, incorporating the Floo Network Authority, Broom Regulatory Control, Portkey Office, and Apparation Test Center."
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: Another floor handles transport stuff like the Floo and Portkeys. The Ministry splits everything up into very specific departments.

Book5-chapter7_Sc6.source: Once again the lift doors opened and four or five witches and wizards got out; at the same time, several paper airplanes swooped into the lift.
Book5-chapter7_Sc6.description: People here act a bit chaotic. Paper airplanes flying into a lift? That's exactly the sort of thing that happens around the Ministry.

Book5-chapter8_Sc5.source: "If it is true that the dementors are taking orders only from the Ministry of Magic, and it is also true that two dementors attacked Harry and his cousin a week ago, then it follows logically that somebody at the Ministry might have ordered the attacks," said Dumbledore politely.
Book5-chapter8_Sc5.description: Two dementors attacked me and Dudley a week ago. If dementors only take orders from the Ministry, someone at the Ministry might have sent them. That possibility terrifies me.

Book5-chapter8_Sc5.source: "I can summon him here in an instant to give evidence if you wish."
Book5-chapter8_Sc5.description: Dumbledore is willing to stand up for me and bring evidence on my behalf. He actually offered to summon the house-elf to back me up, so I can trust he cares about proving the truth.

Book5-chapter8_Sc5.source: "Have you ever bothered to tot up the number of cock-and-bull stories this boy has come out with, Dumbledore, while trying to cover up his flagrant misuse of magic out of school?" roared Fudge.
Book5-chapter8_Sc5.description: Cornelius Fudge is openly hostile and convinced I'm lying or dangerous. The Ministry, or at least Fudge, is out to punish me no matter what I say.

Book5-chapter8_Sc2.source: When he sat gingerly on the edge of the chair the chains clinked rather threateningly but did not bind him.
Book5-chapter8_Sc2.description: Those chains moved and clinked at me, like they could have latched on, but they didn't. I sat there feeling sick because they looked ready to snap shut and then nothing happened.

Book5-chapter8_Sc2.source: There were about fifty of them, all, as far as he could see, wearing plum-colored robes with an elaborately worked silver W on the left-hand side of the chest and all staring down their noses at him, some with very austere expressions, others looks of frank curiosity.
Book5-chapter8_Sc2.description: There were dozens of them up on the bench in plum robes with that silver W. They were all looking at me like I was a curiosity or something to be judged.

Book5-chapter8_Sc2.source: A broad, square-jawed witch with very short gray hair sat on Fudge’s left; she wore a monocle and looked forbidding.
Book5-chapter8_Sc2.description: That woman next to Fudge looks proper intimidating. I reckon whatever she thinks matters in here and she isn't someone to mess with.

Book5-chapter8_Sc2.source: Harry looked at Percy, expecting some sign of recognition from him, but none came. Percy’s eyes, behind his horn-rimmed glasses, were fixed on his parchment, a quill poised in his hand.
Book5-chapter8_Sc2.description: Percy didn't even look at me. He just stared at his parchment and took notes like I was nothing. That stung. I expected he might at least look my way.

Book5-chapter8_Sc2.source: — Witness for the defense, Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore,” said a quiet voice from behind Harry, who turned his head so fast he cricked his neck. Dumbledore was striding serenely across the room wearing long midnight-blue robes and a perfectly calm expression.
Book5-chapter8_Sc2.description: Dumbledore turned up and said he was the witness for my defense. He walked in calm as anything, and seeing him there felt like someone actually had my back.

Book5-chapter8_Sc3.source: "A corporeal Patronus?" "Yes," said Harry, "because —" "A — what?" said Harry. "Your Patronus had a clearly defined form? I mean to say, it was more than vapor or smoke?" "Yes," said Harry, feeling both impatient and slightly desperate, "it's a stag, it's always a stag."
Book5-chapter8_Sc3.description: My Patronus is a fully formed stag. It's not some faint wisp, it's a proper, corporeal Patronus and it's always taken that shape.

Book5-chapter8_Sc3.source: "I learned this at school?" "Yes, Professor Lupin taught me in my third year, because of the —"
Book5-chapter8_Sc3.description: I was taught to produce a Patronus at school by Professor Lupin during my third year. That is where I learned how to do it.

Book5-chapter8_Sc3.source: "You received an official warning from the Ministry for using illegal magic three years ago, did you not?" "Yes, but —"
Book5-chapter8_Sc3.description: I already have an official Ministry warning for using magic when I was younger. They can bring that up against me now.

Book5-chapter8_Sc3.source: "I did it because of the dementors!" "Dementors?" "I mean there were two dementors down that alleyway and they went for me and my cousin!"
Book5-chapter8_Sc3.description: I used the Patronus because there were dementors attacking me and Dudley in that alley. I did it to protect us, that's why I cast it there.

Book5-chapter8_Sc3.source: "We do, in fact, have a witness to the presence of dementors in that alleyway," he said, "other than Dudley Dursley, I mean." "I brought her with me," said Dumbledore. "She’s just outside the door."
Book5-chapter8_Sc3.description: Dumbledore says there's a witness to the dementors and that she's just outside. That gives me hope that someone else saw what happened and I'm not just making it up.

Book5-chapter11_Sc2.source: "To our newcomers," said Dumbledore in a ringing voice, his arms stretched wide and a beaming smile on his lips, "welcome! To our old hands — welcome back! There is a time for speech making, but this is not it. Tuck in!"
Book5-chapter11_Sc2.description: Seeing Dumbledore standing there actually calmed me. Even after being angry with him, when he greets everyone like that I feel like this is where I belong again.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "That’s because there haven’t been any suspicious deaths yet," said Sirius, "not as far as we know, anyway. . . . And we know quite a lot."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: So there haven’t been suspicious deaths yet. He’s being careful and keeping low for now.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Because he doesn’t want to draw attention to himself at the moment," said Sirius. "It would be dangerous for him. His comeback didn’t come off quite the way he wanted it to, you see. He messed it up."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Voldemort’s holding back because his return went wrong. He doesn’t want to risk acting openly yet.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "You weren’t supposed to survive!" said Sirius. "Nobody apart from his Death Eaters was supposed to know he’d come back. But you survived to bear witness."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Because I survived, people know he’s back. That made Dumbledore act straight away and dragged others into it.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore was the only one You-Know-Who was ever scared of!" said Bill.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Dumbledore is Voldemort’s real threat. That’s why the Ministry and Voldemort both fear him.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore’s got a shrewd idea," said Lupin, "and Dumbledore’s shrewd ideas normally turn out to be accurate."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Dumbledore has plans about what Voldemort wants and his guesses are usually right.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Well, firstly, he wants to build up his army again," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Voldemort is trying to rebuild his followers and dark forces. He won’t try to fight the Ministry with only a few people.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "It’s proving tricky, though." "Why?" "Because of the Ministry’s attitude," said Tonks.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: The Ministry refuses to believe Voldemort’s back, and that makes warning people way harder.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Fudge is frightened of him, you see," said Tonks sadly.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Fudge is more scared of Dumbledore than he is willing to admit. He thinks Dumbledore might try to take his job.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "While the Ministry insists there is nothing to fear from Voldemort, it’s hard to convince people he’s back," said Lupin.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Because the Ministry denies it, lots of wizards won’t believe Voldemort’s return, which makes people vulnerable.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "They’ve demoted him from Chief Warlock on the Wizengamot ... and they’re talking about taking away his Order of Merlin, First Class, too."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: The Ministry is openly attacking Dumbledore and trying to discredit him to silence warnings about Voldemort.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Voldemort doesn’t march up to people’s houses and bang on their front doors, Harry," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Voldemort recruits in secret, using tricks, jinxes, and blackmail. He works quietly and cleverly.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Like a weapon. Something he didn’t have last time." "When he was powerful before?" "Yes."
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: He might be hunting for some secret weapon or tool this time, something worse or different than before.
I wasn’t going to keep Ron in the dark. I’ll tell him and Hermione everything they need to know.

Book5-chapter5_Sc1.source: "But what’s a portrait of your mother doing here?" "Hasn’t anyone told you? This was my parents’ house," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter5_Sc1.description: This used to be my parents' house and Sirius owns it now. Of course it's his place, he offered it to Dumbledore for headquarters.

Book5-chapter5_Sc1.source: "There was something about the slightly flattened tone of voice in which Sirius uttered Dumbledore’s name that told Harry that Sirius was not very happy with the headmaster either."
Book5-chapter5_Sc1.description: Sirius is cross with Dumbledore right now. I can tell he's not happy with him, and I feel protective and close to Sirius because of it.

Book5-chapter5_Sc1.source: "The Ministry of Magic’s still after me, and Voldemort will know all about me being an Animagus by now, Wormtail will have told him"
Book5-chapter5_Sc1.description: Sirius can't move freely because the Ministry is after him and Wormtail probably exposed his Animagus status.

Book5-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Personally, I’d have welcomed a dementor attack. A deadly struggle for my soul would have broken the monotony nicely. You think you’ve had it bad, at least you’ve been able to get out and about, stretch your legs, get into a few fights"
Book5-chapter5_Sc1.description: Sirius hates being stuck inside. I get why he's fed up with the waiting around and reports. He wants to be doing something, not just sitting on his hands.

Book5-chapter8_Sc6.source: "he was not at all sure that Dumbledore was right in telling the Wizengamot, in effect, that it was about time they made a decision. Again, however, Dumbledore seemed oblivious to Harry’s attempt to catch his eye."
Book5-chapter8_Sc6.description: I tried to catch Dumbledore's eye for reassurance and he looked like he couldn't care less. I started to doubt that he was backing me at all.

Book5-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Those in favor of clearing the accused of all charges?" ... "There were hands in the air, many of them ... more than half!"
Book5-chapter8_Sc6.description: More than half the Wizengamot put up their hands to clear me. There were enough votes to wipe the whole thing.

Book5-chapter8_Sc6.source: "He had expected the hearing to last longer than this. He was not at all sure that he had made a good impression. He had not really said very much. He ought to have explained more fully about the dementors, about how he had fallen over, about how both he and Dudley had nearly been kissed."
Book5-chapter8_Sc6.description: I kept thinking I messed it up. I barely spoke and kept wanting to explain the dementors properly and what happened with Dudley.

Book5-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Very well, very well ... cleared of all charges."
Book5-chapter8_Sc6.description: Fudge gave in and the verdict was 'cleared of all charges.' I was officially free.

Book5-chapter9_Sc3.source: ["Sprawled on the dusty old carpet in a patch of moonlight, clearly dead, was Ron."]
Book5-chapter9_Sc3.description: I saw Ron lying there as if he were dead and it hit me like a punch to the stomach. I couldn't believe it and I felt sick.
The boggart even turned into my own dead body. Seeing myself 'dead' on the floor was terrifying and wrong.

Book5-chapter9_Sc3.source: ["Pulling out his own wand he said, very firmly and clearly, 'Riddikulus!' Harry's body vanished."]
Book5-chapter9_Sc3.description: Lupin can banish the boggart's form quickly. He handled it calmly and made the apparition disappear.

Book5-chapter9_Sc3.source: ["Molly, don't . . ." Next second she was sobbing her heart out on Lupin's shoulder. "Molly, it was just a boggart," he said soothingly, patting her on the head. "Just a stupid boggart . . ."]
Book5-chapter9_Sc3.description: Mum is terrified of losing us and it drives her to hysteria. Lupin tried to calm her down and called it 'just a boggart' to make her see sense.

Book5-chapter9_Sc3.source: ["D-d-don't tell Arthur," Mrs. Weasley was gulping now, mopping her eyes frantically with her cuffs. "I d-d-don't want him to know."]
Book5-chapter9_Sc3.description: Mum begged not to tell Dad. She doesn't want Arthur finding out about these nightmares.

Book5-chapter9_Sc3.source: ["Moody was looking at Harry, who avoided his gaze. He had a funny feeling Moody's magical eye had followed him all the way out of the kitchen."]
Book5-chapter9_Sc3.description: Moody's magical eye keeps an unsettling watch on me. I could feel it on me the whole time.

Book5-chapter8_Sc4.source: "She looked scared and more batty than ever. Harry wished she had thought to change out of her carpet slippers."
Book5-chapter8_Sc4.description: She seems doddery and terrified. I wish she had acted a bit more sensible. Still, she saw something important.

Book5-chapter8_Sc4.source: "They were big. Big and wearing cloaks."
Book5-chapter8_Sc4.description: There were dementors. Big, cloaked things heading toward two boys. That sinking feeling in my stomach tells me it was real.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: the very thought of him made Harry’s insides burn with anger again.
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: I get furious just thinking about Dumbledore. It makes me want to change the subject quick.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: In the very center of the group Harry saw the dark, greasy-haired head and prominent nose of his least favorite teacher at Hogwarts, Professor Snape.
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: Snape is right there in the hall with the others. Of course he's snooping around whatever the Order is doing.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: A thin piece of flesh-colored string descended in front of Harry’s eyes. Looking up he saw Fred and George on the landing above, cautiously lowering the Extendable Ear toward the dark knot of people below.
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: Fred and George are using an Extendable Ear to eavesdrop. If they fail, we'll miss what they're trying to hear.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: They heard the front door open and then close.
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: Someone left through the front door. That could change whatever's happening in the hall below.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Cleared," Harry said, pulling the door closed behind him, "of all charges!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: I was cleared of all charges. I got off at the Wizengamot and I am going back to Hogwarts. That relief hit me like a punch.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Well, well, well . . . Patronus Potter," said Lucius Malfoy coolly.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Malfoy is right here in the Ministry talking to Fudge. He sneers at me like he always does and I hate that he can just stare me down after what he did.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Why wasn't he waiting outside Fudge's office if they've got business to do together?" Harry burst out furiously.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: If Fudge is meeting Malfoy privately then something is really wrong at the Ministry. I think Fudge might be being influenced or at least making dangerous choices.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "The Minister was just telling me about your lucky escape, Potter," drawled Mr Malfoy.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Fudge has been talking about me with Malfoy. If the Minister is chatting with people like Lucius then the Ministry is full of people I cannot trust.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Scar," Harry mumbled. "But it's nothing. . . . It happens all the time now . . ."
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: My scar is burning more often now. It flares up and I can feel it sharply. It is a bad sign and it worries me.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Yeah, he swung it for me," said Harry.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Dumbledore's influence helped clear me. He backed me and that made the difference at the trial.

Book5-chapter10_Sc2.description: People keep staring at me because of who I am. I wish they wouldn’t make such a fuss.
I got a face full of Stinksap and it made me spit it out, but at least it won’t kill me.

Book5-chapter10_Sc2.source: Harry stared at the thing. It was pulsating slightly
Book5-chapter10_Sc2.description: Neville’s into Herbology in a big way, even if his plants look disgusting. He really cares about them.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: He's not at the staff table. Hagrid is missing and I can see it straight away.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Maybe he’s not back yet. You know — from his mission — the thing he was doing over the summer for Dumbledore."
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: Maybe Hagrid's still away on that job for Dumbledore. That would explain him not being here.
That woman sitting by Dumbledore is Umbridge. She's actually here at the staff table.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Again Harry noticed people putting their heads together to whisper as he passed; he gritted his teeth and tried to act as though he neither noticed nor cared."
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: People keep whispering about me and I'm fed up with it. I try to ignore it and act like I don't care.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Anything good in there?" asked Ron as Harry closed the magazine.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: That magazine is rubbish, full of daft claims. I can't take most of it seriously, it's just nonsense aimed to wind people up.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Of course not," said Hermione scathingly, before Harry could answer, "The Quibbler's rubbish, everyone knows that."
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Even Hermione thinks the Quibbler is rubbish, which backs me up, but some of it still makes me uneasy.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Anything good in there?" asked Ron as Harry closed the magazine.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Seeing that stuff about Sirius in print made me uneasy. It might be a joke, but I can't shrug off the idea that people could be pointing fingers in the wrong direction.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Yeah," said Harry, "but you, unlike me, are a git, so get out and leave us alone."
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: I'm jumpy and I don't want prying eyes or mouths around right now. I pushed people away because I need to think and I don't trust how obvious I'm acting.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "I seem to have touched a nerve," said Malfoy, smirking. "Well, just watch yourself, Potter, because I’ll be dogging your footsteps in case you step out of line."
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Malfoy saying he'll be dogging my footsteps put me on edge. If he spots anything odd, like the black dog, it could blow everything for Sirius and the people helping him.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: Harry could not talk freely in front of Neville and Luna. He exchanged another nervous look with Hermione and then stared out of the window.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: I can't talk openly with everyone here. I have to keep quiet and I trusted Hermione to know why I'm tense, but I won't risk saying anything in front of others.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: He had thought Sirius coming with him to the station was a bit of a laugh, but suddenly it seemed reckless, if not downright dangerous.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: I thought it was funny for Sirius to come, but now I see that was stupid. He shouldn't have come; it could put him and everyone who knows at risk.

Book5-chapter11_Sc3.source: "And it wants all the Houses to be friends?" "Fat chance."
Book5-chapter11_Sc3.description: Yeah right. Like Gryffindor and Slytherin are suddenly going to be pals. Fat chance.

Book5-chapter11_Sc6.source: Of course everyone was staring at him: He had emerged from the Triwizard maze two months ago clutching the dead body of a fellow student and claiming to have seen Lord Voldemort return to power.
Book5-chapter11_Sc6.description: Everyone's staring at me because I came out of the maze holding Cedric and said Voldemort's back. Great. That's why no one wants to talk to me.

Book5-chapter11_Sc6.source: There had not been time last term to explain himself before everyone went home, even if he had felt up to giving the whole school a detailed account of the terrible events in that graveyard.
Book5-chapter11_Sc6.description: I didn't get a chance to explain any of it before the holidays, and I still feel wrecked at the idea of having to tell the whole school what happened.

Book5-chapter11_Sc6.source: No password, no entrance," she said loftily.
Book5-chapter11_Sc6.description: I couldn't get in until someone remembered the new password. I wasn't in the mood for faffing about with that.

Book5-chapter11_Sc6.source: "Guess what it is? I’m actually going to be able to remember it for once —" He waved the stunted little cactus he had shown them on the train. "Mimbulus mimbletonia!"
Book5-chapter11_Sc6.description: Neville's around and trying to help, remembering the password and all that. At least someone was cheery enough to make it easier for me.

Book5-chapter11_Sc6.source: Harry waved good night to them and headed straight for the door to the boys’ dormitories; he was not in much of a mood for talking at the moment.
Book5-chapter11_Sc6.description: I didn't want to talk. I just wanted to get away and be alone in the dormitory.

Book5-chapter11_Sc5.source: "A blond boy next to Euan Abercrombie looked petrified, nudged Euan, and whispered something in his ear. Euan Abercrombie looked equally frightened and stole a horrified look at Harry, who felt the grin slide off his face like Stinksap."
Book5-chapter11_Sc5.description: People are staring at me and it's horrible. I tried to grin but it vanished the second they looked terrified. I don't want that attention.

Book5-chapter11_Sc5.source: "See you later," he said to Ron and Hermione and he made his way out of the Great Hall alone, doing everything he could to ignore more whispering, staring, and pointing as he passed."
Book5-chapter11_Sc5.description: I left the hall on my own to get away from the whispering and pointing. Being alone was better than listening to that.

Book5-chapter11_Sc5.source: "He kept his eyes fixed ahead as he wove his way through the crowd in the entrance hall, then he hurried up the marble staircase, took a couple of concealed shortcuts, and had soon left most of the crowds behind."
Book5-chapter11_Sc5.description: I know a few ways around the castle to dodge crowds and eyes. Quick shortcuts do the trick when you want to disappear.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Mum and Dad just sent Hedwig back"
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Hedwig has been sent back by my family so I need to take her cage with me and keep her safe.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "We have to go to King’s Cross with a guard?"
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: There will be a guard escorting us to King cross. That makes this trip more serious than usual.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "He shouldn't have come with us," said Hermione in a worried voice.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Sirius coming with us worried Hermione but I think he needed the fresh air. Still, I get why she was tense about it.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Thanks, Lee," said Harry, grinning, as Sirius wagged his tail frantically.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: I appreciate people like Lee giving a hand. I'm still glad to have friends around even when things get noisy and awkward.
Ron and Hermione are off to the prefect carriage so this trip starts without Ron as my constant companion. That feels weird.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "After he had met this behavior in five consecutive carriages he remembered that the Daily Prophet had been telling its readers all summer what a lying show-off he was."
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: People are staring because of what the Prophet printed about me. I can't pretend I don't care. It's annoying and unfair.

Book5-chapter11_Sc4.source: "Sounded like a load of waffle to me."
Book5-chapter11_Sc4.description: It sounded like a load of waffle. I couldn't believe everyone made such a fuss about it.
So there were actually bits worth paying attention to. Fine, I admit it might've had some meaning hidden in the waffle.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: Does he think he’ll turn into a nutter if he stays in a room with me too long?
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: I reckon Seamus is avoiding me and it stinks. I don't like being pushed out like I'm the problem.
Talking to Cho is going to be awkward. Between Neville and Ron I can never get a moment with her that doesn’t go wrong.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: Well, it’d be cool to be an Auror
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Being an Auror would be brilliant and proper important. I want that kind of job too.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: You don’t support them, do you?
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: People jump on bandwagons. If someone suddenly starts supporting a team they might not be a real fan and that can make things messy in conversations.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: Potter, what is this supposed to be?
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: I messed up in Potions because I missed an instruction. Snape will gloat and of course I’ll get shouted at. I can't afford mistakes this year.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: She didn't want me to come back to Hogwarts.
Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: She didn't want me to come back to Hogwarts. My presence is the reason Seamus's mum tried to stop him coming.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: Well, she er well, it's not just you, it's Dumbledore too
Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: She not only thinks I'm a liar, she blames Dumbledore as well. They're buying what the Daily Prophet prints.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: She believes the Daily Prophet? She thinks I’m a liar and Dumbledore’s an old fool?
