Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: I can't pretend anymore. Some people genuinely believe I'm making everything up and Dumbledore's mad. That's how they see me now.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: I'll have a go at anyone who calls me a liar
Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: I'm not going to let people call me a liar without fighting back. I'm done taking it lying down.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: Look what did happen that night when you know when with Cedric Diggory and all?
Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: People around me are itching for the story about Cedric. They're asking in front of others and it's making everything worse.

Book5-chapter11_Sc7.source: Don't talk to me like that!
Book5-chapter11_Sc7.description: I'm fed up with being treated like some circus act. I feel angry and cornered and I won't be spoken to with that kind of disbelief.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "We'd better change," said Hermione at last.
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: I was staring at the window trying to see Hogwarts and feeling fed up, then Hermione said we should get changed, so I knew it was time to move.
I was worried about Hagrid not being there and I said it out loud because it felt wrong he wasn't around.
Those creatures pulling the coaches were horrific, half-dragon, bone-showing, bat-winged things and I could see them clearly.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Can’t you see what’s pulling the carriages?"
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: At first I thought everyone could see the beasts but when Ron couldn't, I started to suspect others might not be seeing what I see.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Oh yes," said Luna, "I’ve been able to see them ever since my first day here."
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Luna sees weird things like I do, so I felt less alone and that I could trust her a bit more about strange stuff.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: Oh hello, Harry, Um bad time?
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: She said hello all nervous and then ran off. I liked her, and that was embarrassing. I wanted to look cool and she caught me with Neville and Luna. Typical.
Sirius Black is being smeared in The Quibbler, like they are calling him a mass murderer. This is the article Kingsley gave to my godfather.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: SIRIUS — Black As He’s Painted? Notorious Mass Murderer OR Innocent Singing Sensation?
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: They've got that stupid cartoon of Sirius standing on bones and are asking if he's guilty or some singing sensation. That's mental. People are deciding his entire life for him in a joke of a magazine.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: Can I have a look at this?
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: The Quibbler Kingsley gave Mr Weasley must be the same one Luna's reading. I grabbed it because I needed to see what they were saying about Black.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Cool," Harry said, and he was relieved to hear that his voice had stopped sounding hearty.
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I told Ron he did well, even though I hated that I felt jealous. I can still be pleased for him and keep my mouth shut about the badge.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Nah, I’ve caused too much trouble," Harry said, echoing Fred.
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Maybe Dumbledore didn't make me a prefect because of the trouble I get into, not because I'm not trusted. That actually makes sense and I can live with that.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: He had forgotten completely about prefects being chosen in the fifth year.
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I forgot prefects were chosen this year, so I wasn't expecting a badge. That explains why Ron got one and I didn't.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "I’ve definitely done more, Harry thought indignantly. I’ve done more than either of them!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I keep telling myself I've done more dangerous things than Ron and Hermione, but that doesn't mean I'm the one who should be a prefect.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "We’d better get these upstairs . . ." Harry watched them go, feeling slightly uneasy.
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I gave the twins my Triwizard winnings to help them out and now I worry it might cause trouble with Mum. I don't want Mrs Weasley to think less of me for helping them.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "There is nothing waiting out there, Mr. Potter."
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: They're pretending there is no danger. The Ministry and Umbridge are denying that Voldemort's back and trying to make us act like nothing's happened.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "It is NOT a lie! I saw him, I fought him!"
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: I know what I saw. Voldemort came back and I fought him. I'm not going to shut up about it.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "Cedric Diggory's death was a tragic accident," she said coldly.
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Cedric was murdered by Voldemort. I can't let them dress it up as an accident.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "Detention, Mr. Potter! Tomorrow evening. Five o'clock. My office."
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Umbridge hates me and will use every bit of power she has to punish me. She means trouble for me personally.
McGonagall sees how dangerous this is. I can't just storm about without thinking. I have to be careful because other people could get hurt or worse.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Well, we’ve never had great Defense Against the Dark Arts teachers, have we?" said Harry. "You know what it’s like, Hagrid told us, nobody wants the job, they say it’s jinxed."
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: We never get great DADA teachers. Hagrid said no one wants the job because it's jinxed. That's just how it is.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Can’t we just . . . Let’s just do that homework, get it out of the way . . ."
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: Let's get the homework done and stop arguing. I just want to get on with it and not make things worse.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Fainting Fancies?" Harry suggested quietly. One by one, as though hit over the heads with invisible mallets, the first years were slumping unconscious in their seats
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: Fred and George are handing out sweets that make first years faint. That is dangerous messing about.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: People were coming back from dinner now. Harry kept his face averted from the portrait hole, but could still sense the stares he was attracting.
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: I can feel everyone staring at me. I don't want more attention so I avoid the portrait hole.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "I was supposed to be at the tryouts for the new Keeper at five o'clock on Friday and I was — was wondering whether I could skip detention that night"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: I asked if I could miss detention to attend the Quidditch keeper tryouts because it's important to me and my team.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "Oh no, no, no. This is your punishment for spreading evil, nasty, attention-seeking stories, Mr Potter"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: Umbridge sees my attempt to avoid detention as unacceptable and thinks I'm been spreading 'evil, nasty, attention-seeking stories'.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "No, you will come here at five o'clock tomorrow, and the next day, and on Friday too"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: She insists I must attend detention at five every day she schedules, no exceptions for things I actually need to do.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "I want you to write 'I must not tell lies'"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: She ordered me to write a phrase over and over as punishment: 'I must not tell lies.'
She gave me a special black quill that doesn't need ink and I had to use it instead of my own.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "He let out a gasp of pain. The words had appeared on the parchment in what appeared to be shining red ink. At the same time, the words had appeared on the back of Harry's right hand, cut into his skin"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: When I wrote with that quill the words showed up on the paper in red and the same words were cut into the back of my hand, then the skin healed leaving redness.

Book5-chapter13_Sc5.source: "She was watching him with her head slightly to one side, still smiling widely, as though she knew exactly what he was thinking"
Book5-chapter13_Sc5.description: She's not just petty, she's enjoying having power over me and watching my reactions. She's deliberately cruel.

Book5-chapter13_Sc6.source: He looked back at the parchment, placed the quill upon it once more, wrote I must not tell lies, and felt the searing pain on the back of his hand for a second time; once again the words had been cut into his skin, once again they healed over seconds later.
Book5-chapter13_Sc6.description: She made me write 'I must not tell lies' in my own blood and the quill cuts my hand every time. It's meant to hurt and humiliate me, but I won't give her the satisfaction of seeing me break.

Book5-chapter13_Sc6.source: He knew she was watching him for signs of weakness and he was not going to show any, not even if he had to sit here all night, cutting open his own hand with this quill.
Book5-chapter13_Sc6.description: She's watching for weakness. I won't show it. If I have to sit here all night and bleed, I will.

Book5-chapter13_Sc6.source: “Hand,” she said. He extended it. She took it in her own. Harry repressed a shudder as she touched him with her thick, stubby fingers on which she wore a number of ugly old rings.
Book5-chapter13_Sc6.description: She inspects me like I'm some troublesome child and touches me in a way that makes me want to shudder. She's got this smug, poking kind of cruelty.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "There’s no point trying to finish this now, I can’t do it without Hermione, I haven’t got a clue what you’re supposed to do with moonstones, have you?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: I can't finish Snape's essay without Hermione. Plain and simple, I need her help.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "He hurried back around the table to Ron and Hermione, who were squatting on the grass some distance away and attempting to persuade a bowtruckle to remain still long enough to draw it."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: We're supposed to be sketching bowtruckles, and Hermione knows loads about them so I should stick with them.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Maybe he’s been messing with stuff that’s too big for him, if you get my drift."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: If Malfoy is hinting Hagrid got hurt, I suddenly think Hagrid might be in real trouble and I’m worried about what Malfoy knows.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Harry shook his head, noticing as he did so that the ache in his right temple was getting worse."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: My head's aching worse again. I feel sharp pain when I think about the essay on giant wars.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "Er — thanks very much, Ernie," said Harry, taken aback but pleased.
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: I was really pleased and surprised to get Ernie's support. It matters to me when people who aren't daft about this back me up.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "I think we'd better check with Puddlemere United whether Oliver Wood's been killed during a training session, because she seems to be channeling his spirit."
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: I honestly think Umbridge is acting like a mad Quidditch coach right now. She's over the top and bossy and it's ridiculous.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "I hope she doesn't keep me too long this evening. You realize we've got to write three essays, practice Vanishing Spells for McGonagall, work out a countercharm for Flitwick, finish the bowtruckle drawing, and start that stupid dream diary for Trelawney?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: I've got loads to do tonight. If Umbridge keeps me ages in detention I'm screwed for all my homework and practice.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "Come in," in a sugary voice. He entered cautiously, looking around.
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: Umbridge's office is all sickly cosy and horrible. It's nothing like it used to be with Lockhart or Lupin or Moody. It's full of lace and kittens and dried flowers and it makes me feel on edge.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: Right, Percy sent Ron a letter. It’s from him and it’s about Ron being made a prefect.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.source: Ron thrust the letter at Harry and Hermione, who leaned toward each other to read it together
Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: This feels like Percy showing off and lecturing Ron. I don’t like the smug tone he’s taking.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Hey, Potter, how’s your scar feeling?" called Malfoy.
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Malfoy’s still having a go at my scar. He’ll shout things to rile me up and try to make me look weak.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "All right," called Angelina, "Fred, George, go and get your bats and a Bludger; Ron, get up to the goalposts, Harry, release the Snitch when I say so."
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Angelina runs the plays and she tells me when to release the Snitch. I do what she says and I wait for her signal.
Ron’s messing up because he’s nervous, not because he can’t play. He was fine in practice this morning.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Here, take this," Fred told her, handing her something small and purple from out of his pocket.
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Fred and George carry stuff to patch people up quick. They’ll sort out Katie if something happens.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Fred passed to Angelina; she reverse passed to Harry, who had not been expecting it, but caught it in the very tips of his fingers and passed it quickly to Ron, who lunged for it and missed by inches."
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Fred and George back us up in games and their passing can catch me off guard, but I can still react under pressure.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "I was just up in Umbridge's office and she touched my arm"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: My scar hurt when Umbridge touched me. It felt wrong and I know it means something is up.
She is twisted and dangerous. I don't trust her for a second.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "I think I'll write and tell Sirius about it, see what he thinks"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: I thought about writing to Sirius, but then I backed off because of how risky letters could be.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "I think I'll write and tell Sirius about it, see what he thinks" and "All right, all right, I won't tell him, then!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: I want to tell Sirius what's happening, but I won't if it's too dangerous. I won't put him or me at risk with an owl right now.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "I'm not bothering him with this. Like you just said, it's not a big deal. It's been hurting on and off all summer"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: I don't want to bother Dumbledore about this. My scar has been a pain on and off all summer and I don't want to make a fuss.
I asked Hermione to tell Ron for me because I didn't want to hang around arguing.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Peeves is planning an amusing joke on the next person to pass the bust of Paracelsus halfway down the corridor."
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: Peeves is up to no good near the Paracelsus bust. I wouldn’t go past there if I can help it.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Does it involve Paracelsus falling on top of the person’s head?"
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: If Peeves’s joke is what Nick thinks, someone’s going to get Paracelsus dropped on their head. Lovely.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Exactly the attitude I want, Harry," said Angelina approvingly
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: Angelina’s backing me and she likes the way I’m playing. That’s good to have from the captain.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "What’s that Weasley’s riding?" Malfoy called in his sneering drawl.
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: Those Slytherin lot are going to try and wind Ron and me up. Fine. Ignore them and let our play do the talking.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: since when has Snape ever been fair to me?
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Snape will never be fair to me. I know it. Ever since I got here it's been like that and I can't pretend otherwise.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: Evanesco. The contents of Harry’s potion vanished; he was left standing foolishly beside an empty cauldron.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: My potion disappeared right in front of me. Great. I ended up standing there looking stupid next to an empty cauldron.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: I did think he might be a bit better this year ... Now he's in the Order and everything.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Hermione thought Snape might be different because he's in the Order. I don't buy it. Being in the Order doesn't mean he stops being horrible to me.
I don't want to share my dreams. My graveyard nightmare is mine and I don't need anyone telling me what it means.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: The constant changing of teachers ... has unfortunately resulted in your being far below the standard we would expect to see in your O.W.L. year.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: The Defense class is being treated like theory-only because of all the awful turnover. That worries me for O.W.L.s.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: Wands away and quills out, please.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Umbridge's rule is no wands in class. She's all about writing and talking and nothing about actually using defensive spells.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: There will be no need to talk.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Umbridge's lessons are going to be dull and strict. She's going to make lessons pointless and boring, and that means trouble when you actually need to learn to defend yourself.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: it was his job to recapture the tiny fluttering golden ball that was worth a hundred and fifty points to the Seeker’s team and doing so required enormous speed and skill.
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: It's my job to catch the Snitch. That little golden thing is worth a hundred and fifty points and I have to be insanely fast and focused to get it.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: When Angelina blew her whistle, Harry released the Snitch and Fred and George let fly the Bludger; from that moment on, Harry was barely aware of what the others were doing.
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: When the whistle goes, everything else blurs out. Once the Snitch is released I'm focused on it and nothing else matters.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: “Stop — stop — STOP!” screamed Angelina. “Ron — you’re not covering your middle post!”
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: Angelina will shout at us if our positions slip. I get that if someone doesn't hold their post properly we suffer, and I can't afford to ignore it while I'm chasing the Snitch.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: Harry, who had just sighted the Snitch circling the opposite goalpost, pulled up feeling distinctly aggrieved.
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: I saw the Snitch and had to pull up because of the stoppage. It's maddening when I spot it and then we're told to stop.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: I kept my mouth shut the whole time. I only said "Good evening" when I arrived and "Good night" when I left.
Umbridge made me write "I must not tell lies" on my hand and it got cut into my skin, oozing blood. It's not fading anymore.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: He was not really sure why he was not telling Ron and Hermione exactly what was happening in Umbridge’s room
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: This is my fight with Umbridge. I do not want to give her the satisfaction of seeing them horrified, so I am keeping it to myself.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: It was half-past two by the time he had finished it.
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: After detention I had to work all night on Snape's essay and other homework. I finished at half past two and I know it is a poor job but I had no choice.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: he fell fully clothed on top of the bed covers and fell asleep immediately.
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: I was so exhausted that I collapsed fully clothed and slept straight away.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "She’s evil, he thought, as he climbed a staircase to the seventh floor, she’s an evil, twisted, mad, old —"
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: She's wicked. I hate her more than Snape now. She's just plain evil, twisted and mad.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "Oh yes," said Professor Umbridge, smiling widely as before. "Yes, I think we can etch the message a little deeper with another evening’s work."
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: She's going to make me come back and go even further with those lines. She's not stopping after one night.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "It’s just a cut — it’s nothing — it’s —"
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: My hand's been carved. It's more than a cut. It hurts and it shows what she does to people.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "He’s got enough on his mind," said Harry, but that was not the true reason. He was not going to go to Dumbledore for help when Dumbledore had not spoken to him once since last June.
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: I won't go running to Dumbledore. He hasn't even spoken to me since June, so I'm not asking him for this.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "No," said Harry at once. "I’m not giving her the satisfaction of knowing she’s got to me."
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: I'm not going to let her see she's got to me. I refuse to give her that satisfaction.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "OUCH!" Harry had gripped the bowtruckle so hard that it had almost snapped; it had just taken a great retaliatory swipe at his hand with its sharp fingers, leaving two long deep cuts there.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: That little bugger can swipe back. I held the bowtruckle and it sliced my hand with those sharp fingers. Careful handling matters, or you get cut.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "If he calls Hagrid a moron one more time . . ." snarled Harry.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: I am dead set on Hagrid. Hearing people call him a moron winds me up so much I want to do something about it. I won't stand by while they rubbish him.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I just wish Hagrid would hurry up and get back, that’s all," said Harry in a low voice, as they reached the greenhouses.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: I want Hagrid back teaching Care of Magical Creatures. Nothing about Grubbly-Plank will be as good as him, and I want him back in charge.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "D’you mind not offending the only people who believe me?" Harry asked Hermione as they made their way into class.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: I stick up for people who get laughed at, even if I don't get everything they say. I won't let Hermione mock someone out loud when it's obvious they're already getting enough grief.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: It was plain that Angelina had stopped training just in time; Katie was now chalk-white and covered in blood.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Katie is hurt bad. Angelina stopped training and she needs the hospital wing. We can't carry on without Beaters and a Chaser.
I won't slag Ron off. He's not rubbish just because practice went badly. I'll stick up for him.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Well, I suppose he could’ve played better,” Harry muttered, “but it was only the first training session, like you said . . .”
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Okay, he could've done better, but it's the first session. We need to give it time and not panic.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: MINISTRY SEEKS EDUCATIONAL REFORM DOLORES UMBRIDGE APPOINTED FIRST-EVER “HIGH INQUISITOR”
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: So Umbridge is the new High Inquisitor. Great. She means trouble for us and the school rules are about to get nastier.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: The Inner Eye does not See upon command!
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Trelawney might be a bit of a fraud, but I hate Umbridge enough that I was on Trelawney's side when Umbridge bullied her.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: I think another week’s detentions would do you some good, Mr. Potter
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Umbridge singled me out for punishment. She gave me detentions that made my cut bleed again and forced me to write lines. I will not give her the satisfaction of whining about it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: I saw You-Know-Who. I'm not wasting time trying to convince anyone who won't believe Dumbledore or me.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: The barman's eyes traveled over Harry, resting for a fraction of a second on his scar.
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: People notice my scar. Even rough pub types clock it, so my presence changes how folks act around me.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: There was a man at the bar whose whole head was wrapped in dirty gray bandages
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: The Hog's Head is full of weird, shady types who hide their faces. It's the kind of place where people keep secrets and don't mind if you do the same.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: What have you been telling people? ... What are they expecting?
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: Hermione's gone and organized this whole thing. Loads of people turned up expecting me to talk. She's the one who pulled everyone together, whether I wanted that or not.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: If you didn't believe him, you don't believe me
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: If folks won't believe Dumbledore, they won't believe me either. I won't waste my time arguing with them.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I’m already being punished by her, why do you have to take points as well?"
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: This is unfair. I'm getting punished by Umbridge already and then McGonagall takes points off Gryffindor on top of that. How is that supposed to help?

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Because detentions do not appear to have any effect on you whatsoever!" said Professor McGonagall
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: People think detentions don't work on me. They reckon I'm not learning my lesson from Umbridge's punishments.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I wish she hadn't taken points from you, but I think she's right to warn you not to lose your temper with Umbridge," said Hermione's voice
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Fine, I don't want to lose my temper with Umbridge. But I'm still mad about the points. I can see Hermione's point though.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Harry could not help giving her a faint smile and could have sworn he received one in return."
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: McGonagall and I can be on the same side sometimes. I think she understands me more than she lets on.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I wonder — the headmaster seems strangely reluctant to give me any information on the matter — can you tell me what is causing Professor Hagrid’s very extended leave of absence?"
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Umbridge is trying to get info on Hagrid's leave. People are watching Hagrid closely and I should be careful because others might tattle.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "She’s taken points off Gryffindor because I’m having my hand sliced open every night! How is that fair, how?"
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: I can't believe they treat me like I'm the troublemaker when I'm the one getting hurt. That's just not right.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: I thought it was a good idea from the start
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Okay, I kept thinking about it. Teaching Defense makes sense to me. I find myself planning lessons and thinking about the spells that actually worked for me.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: You know the first weekend in October's a Hogsmeade weekend?
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: The first weekend in October is a Hogsmeade weekend. Hermione wants to use that to meet anyone who wants lessons.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: Yeah, but I doubt anyone except you two would want to be taught by me. I'm a nutter, remember?
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: I still feel like a bit of a freak and worry people won't want me to teach, but I'm at least willing to try if Hermione and Ron want me to.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: He said he was tipped off you were ordering Dungbombs? But who had tipped him off?
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Filch came barging in after I sent a letter to Sirius. Someone must have tipped him off about the letter or the dungbombs and he sniffed around my stuff.
I'm worrying about Sirius turning up in Hogsmeade when we meet. I keep picturing the big black dog bounding up the street and what might happen if Malfoy spots him.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [Because I’ve just seen Sirius’s head in the fire]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: I just saw Sirius's head in the fire. I know I saw him before in those flames so I can't just brush this off. That's why I went down to stare into it like an idiot.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [At the mention of Harry’s letter, Hermione and Ron had both turned to stare at him]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: I wrote to Sirius and he answered. I keep thinking about him and apparently he keeps checking in on me. That matters to me more than I expected.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [Well, I know it can’t be fun when it hurts, but we don’t think it’s anything to really worry about]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: My scar is bothering people. They don't think it's really dangerous right now but everyone is watching it and worried. I can feel that.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “Oh yeah — ‘sever ties’ with me, I swear I won’t get violent.”
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Percy actually told Ron to sever ties with me and to rat me out to Umbridge. I can't believe my own brother thinks I'm dangerous.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: He knew that half the people inside Hogwarts thought him strange, even mad; he knew that the Daily Prophet had been making snide allusions to him for months
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: People at Hogwarts and in the Prophet are convinced I'm odd and a menace. That's real now, not just rumours.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: He had known Percy for four years, had stayed in his house during the summers, shared a tent with him during the Quidditch World Cup, had even been awarded full marks by him in the second task of the Triwizard Tournament last year
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Percy and I have a history — I lived with him, shared a tent, even got top marks from him once. That makes his betrayal sting even more.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: And with a surge of sympathy for his godfather, Harry thought that Sirius was probably the only person he knew who could really understand how he felt at the moment
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Sirius would get how rotten this feels. He's been blamed and hated for years, so he knows what it's like to be on the wrong end of everyone.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: It was now past midnight and the common room was deserted but for the three of them and Crookshanks.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: It's past midnight and we're the only ones up with Crookshanks. I'm exhausted and tense.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "She obviously reckons Trelawney’s an old fraud too. . . . Looks like she’s put her on probation."
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Umbridge has put Trelawney on probation. That's why Trelawney's making a fuss and crying in class.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Please turn to page thirty-four of Defensive Magical Theory and read the third chapter, entitled ‘The Case for Non-Offensive Responses to Magical Attack.'"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Umbridge's lessons are all about non-offensive responses. She wants us to learn theory, not actually defend ourselves properly.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "No Quidditch practice," said Angelina in hollow tones
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: The Ministry decree means no Quidditch practice for us. Umbridge is using rules to punish and control us.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He was the witch under the veil." "That was Mundungus?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Mundungus was spying on our meeting at the Hog's Head. People in the Order or shady followers are watching us.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "This year we know that there’s someone outside Hogwarts who’d like to kill us all, so I think learning to defend yourselves properly is a very good idea!"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Sirius makes me feel that learning real defense is urgent. I'm convinced we need to practice even if it's risky.
We suggested meeting places. The Shrieking Shack was proposed but might not work for twenty-eight people who are not Animagi.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "But it was still sealed and everything," said Harry, trying to convince himself as much as her.
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: The Floo message was sealed when we got it. It looked genuine, so I keep telling myself nobody must have tampered with it.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "And nobody would understand what it meant if they didn’t know where we’d spoken to him before, would they?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: If you don't know where we last spoke to him, that message wouldn't make sense to you. I can't see how someone could use it unless they already knew our meeting place.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "I had to stop you," Harry gasped, picking up his bag. "Crabbe and Goyle would’ve torn you apart."
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Neville matters to me. I stepped in because I won't watch him get bullied into a fight he can't win.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "You will write me an essay on the correct composition of this potion, indicating how and why you went wrong, to be handed in next lesson, do you understand?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Snape's given me homework and it's going to eat into my night. Great, another sleepless one because of him.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "She strode between two lines of desks toward Snape, who was bending over Dean Thomas’s cauldron."
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Umbridge is out to interfere with teaching. If she can get the Ministry to remove lessons she doesn't like, she'll try.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "You think Umbridge attacked Hedwig?" he said, outraged.
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: You did that? I can't believe Umbridge would attack Hedwig. I reckon she might be the one who did it and I'm furious about it.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Umbridge has been reading your mail, Harry. There’s no other explanation."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Someone's been reading my letters. If Umbridge's involved, she could have seen anything sent to me.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Charms was always one of the best lessons in which to enjoy a private chat: There was generally so much movement and activity that the danger of being overheard was very slight."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Charms lessons are brilliant for talking privately because everyone and everything is noisy and moving about.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "It was a very, very close call last night," said Hermione. "I just wonder if Umbridge knows how close it was."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Hermione thinks it was a near miss and that Umbridge might know how close she came to catching Sirius. Hermione's really worried about how dangerous this is.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "Dumbledore said it happened whenever Voldemort was feeling a powerful emotion,"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Dumbledore said my scar hurts when Voldemort feels powerful emotions, so if it ached during that detention it was probably because he was really angry.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "So now he's back it's bound to hurt more often," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Now that Voldemort's back I think the pain will happen more often and that means I'm going to be feeling it a lot.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "You're less like your father than I thought," he said finally, a definite coolness in his voice.
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Sirius seems colder with me now, like he's judging me against my dad and disappointed when I won't take risks.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "She's not letting us use magic at all!"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Umbridge won't let us practice magic in Defense class, we only read from the textbook.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "That's exactly what he thinks you are doing," said Sirius, "or rather, that's exactly what he's afraid Dumbledore's doing - forming his own private army"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: The Ministry, especially Fudge, actually thinks Dumbledore is building an army of us, which is why they're keeping us from learning proper defense.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "When's your next Hogsmeade weekend anyway? I was thinking, we got away with the dog disguise at the station, didn't we? I thought I could —"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Sirius wants to visit at Hogsmeade and thinks he could come up in his dog form, but that would be risky because people might recognise him.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Only because he was too stupid to listen to what Hagrid told him to do," said Harry angrily.
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: I hate people who blame Hagrid for things. If someone gets hurt because they ignored instructions, that pisses me off.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Another night's detention, I think," she said softly.
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: Umbridge dishes out detentions for everything and she'll use them to shut people up. She is dangerous for students who speak up.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "You don't know what it's like! You neither of you you’ve never had to face him, have you?"
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: Nobody who hasn't faced Voldemort can understand how terrifying it is. You don't just cast spells like a lesson when your life is on the line.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "We need to know what it’s r-really like . . . facing him . . . facing V-Voldemort."
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: Hermione and Ron want me to teach them Defense because they trust me about facing Voldemort. I feel guilty but I agreed to try and help.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Reparo," Harry muttered, pointing his wand at the broken pieces of china.
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: I can fix things with magic even when I'm shaken. That might help when things go wrong.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "But he’s all for it!" said Harry.
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: Sirius backs what we're doing with this group. I trust him, plain and simple.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Hermione did it," said Harry. He pulled out his wand, tapped his glasses and said, "Impervius!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: I can cast Impervius on my glasses to stop them fogging in the rain. It works and it's handy in storms.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Do you honestly trust his judgment?" "Yes, I do!" said Harry at once. "He’s always given us great advice!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: I won't suddenly doubt Sirius. He gives good advice and I still listen to him.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: the presence of hundreds of books had finally convinced Hermione that what they were doing was right.
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Right, Hermione's completely on board now. Hundreds of books and she thinks this is the proper way to go.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: By the time eight o'clock arrived, every cushion was occupied.
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Everyone showed up and we filled the place. It's going to be crowded but at least we'll all be here together.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "This isn\'t a coincidence," he said, his hands forming fists. "She knows."
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: She knows about the meetings. This is not a coincidence. I am furious and I am sure Umbridge has been told.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Bear in mind," she said quickly and quietly, her eyes on the scroll in his hand, "that channels of communication in and out of Hogwarts may be being watched, won\'t you?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: Right, channels in and out of Hogwarts might be watched. We can no longer assume our messages are safe.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "She\'s hurt!" Harry whispered, bending his head low over her.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: Hedwig is injured. She arrived later than the other post and her wing is damaged. I need to get her to someone who can fix her.
Sirius sent a message. He wants to meet today at the same time and the same place. I am going anyway.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I don\'t think we\'re going to be as lucky, though, do you?" he asked Harry as the second years hurried away.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: Not everyone at that pub can be trusted. Someone from that gathering might have blabbed to Umbridge.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "That wasn't bad," said Harry, "but there's definite room for improvement."
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: That went alright but we can do better. We need to keep practising and tighten things up.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "'Well, no, it was lousy, but I know you can do it properly, I was watching from over there . . .' She laughed."
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: I tried to spare Cho's feelings and back her up even when I thought she messed up. I'm not going to be cruel about it.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "Let's say next Wednesday night, then," said Harry, "and we can decide on additional meetings then."
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: We're meeting next Wednesday night. We'll sort out extra sessions when we meet.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "He blew his whistle; everybody stopped shouting, 'Expelliarmus!' and the last couple of wands clattered to the floor."
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: I can control the meeting. A quick signal gets everyone to stop and listen.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "He pulled out the Marauder's Map again and checked it carefully for signs of teachers on the seventh floor."
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: I used the Marauder's Map to keep watch for teachers. I'm making sure everyone gets back safely and avoids Filch.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Dobby has used it, sir," said the elf, dropping his voice and looking guilty, "when Winky has been very drunk. He has hidden her in the Room of Requirement and he has found antidotes to butterbeer there, and a nice elf-sized bed to settle her on while she sleeps it off, sir."
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: So the Room of Requirement can hide someone and even has things like antidotes and a tiny bed. That could be brilliant for keeping people safe or hidden when we need to.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "And Dobby knows Mr. Filch has found extra cleaning materials there when he has run short, sir, and —"
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: The room can produce supplies, like extra cleaning materials. It gives you what you need.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "and if you really needed a bathroom," said Harry, suddenly remembering something Dumbledore had said at the Yule Ball the previous Christmas, "would it fill itself with chamber pots?" "Dobby expects so, sir," said Dobby, nodding earnestly. "It is a most amazing room, sir."
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: It can probably create practical things on demand, even chamber pots. It truly adapts to what you need it to be.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Very few, sir. Mostly people stumbles across it when they needs it, sir, but often they never finds it again, for they do not know that it is always there waiting to be called into service, sir."
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: Very few people know about the Room. Most find it by chance and then can never find it again because you have to know how to call it.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "It sounds brilliant," said Harry, his heart racing. "It sounds perfect, Dobby. When can you show me where it is?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: This is perfect for our meetings. I used to be worried about security and space but now I know there is a place that appears exactly when needed and stays hidden otherwise.

Book5-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Good," said Harry quietly, when she told him, "because we’ve found somewhere to have our first Defense meeting. Tonight, eight o’clock, seventh floor opposite that tapestry of Barnabas the Barmy being clubbed by those trolls."
Book5-chapter18_Sc5.description: The first D.A. meeting is set. Tonight at eight o'clock in the Room of Requirement on the seventh floor opposite the Barnabas the Barmy tapestry. We have a time and a place.

Book5-chapter18_Sc4.source: Dobby volunteered to return Harry Potter’s owl! Professor Grubbly-Plank says she is all well now, sir!
Book5-chapter18_Sc4.description: Hedwig's back with me and she's been fixed by Professor Grubbly-Plank. She's all right now.

Book5-chapter18_Sc4.source: Not really bad, said Harry, yawning and rubbing his eyes. I’ve had worse.
Book5-chapter18_Sc4.description: That dream with the door was really vivid and it's stuck in my head, even if it wasn't the worst thing I've had.

Book5-chapter18_Sc4.source: Dobby wishes he could help Harry Potter, for Harry Potter set Dobby free and Dobby is much, much happier now
Book5-chapter18_Sc4.description: Dobby is loyal to me and grateful because I set him free. He's happier now and wants to do things for me.

Book5-chapter18_Sc4.source: You can’t help me, Dobby, but thanks for the offer
Book5-chapter18_Sc4.description: I don't think Dobby can help with what I'm dealing with, but I appreciate him trying.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "Dark Detectors," said Harry, stepping between the cushions to reach them. "Basically they all show when Dark wizards or enemies are around, but you don't want to rely on them too much, they can be fooled ."
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: Dark detectors show when Dark wizards or enemies are nearby but they can be fooled, so I won't trust them completely.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "Everyone put up their hands, even Zacharias Smith, though he did it very halfheartedly."
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: People are willing to back me as leader, even some who don't seem keen, so I know they've put their trust in me even if I'm nervous about it.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "I was thinking, the first thing we should do is Expelliarmus, you know, the Disarming Charm."
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: We should start training with Expelliarmus, the Disarming Charm, because it's practical and something everyone can learn first.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "I've used it against him," said Harry quietly. "It saved my life last June."
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: I've used Expelliarmus on You-Know-Who and it saved my life last June. It's not just a showy trick, it actually works when it matters.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "But if you think it’s beneath you, you can leave," Harry said.
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: If someone thinks a simple defensive spell is beneath them, they can sod off. We all need to learn the basics, no matter how clever we think we are.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Listen, Neville, can you take it in turns to practice with Ron and Hermione for a couple of minutes so I can walk around and see how the rest are doing?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: I should get everyone practicing the basics in pairs so I can walk around and spot who's doing the spell wrong. It's the only way they'll actually learn.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "I DID IT!" said Neville gleefully. "I’ve never done it before — I DID IT!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Neville can do it if he gets the chance. He just needed someone to practice with and a bit of encouragement.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Sorry, Harry," said George hastily, when Harry caught his eye. "Couldn’t resist . . ."
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Fred and George can't resist mucking about in the middle of practice. I can expect distractions from them and need to keep an eye out.
When things get out of hand I just need to shout and take control. A whistle would be handy to get everyone's attention quickly.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Very good, Miss Granger!" said Professor Flitwick's squeaky little voice and Harry, Ron, and Hermione all jumped.
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: I jumped at Flitwick's voice. Loud surprises throw me off, plain and simple.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I’ve got permission! To re-form the Quidditch team!" "Excellent!" said Ron and Harry together.
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Quidditch is back on. I'm glad. We need every edge we can get, so I'm in.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Hope this clears up . . . What’s up with you, Hermione?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Hermione's distracted. I can't ignore it. Something's bothering her even now, and that matters.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Hagrid’s been out looking for giants and he really found them. He said flat out he has.
The giants are up in the mountains. That’s where they live.
They’re huge. About twenty feet tall, some even bigger. That’s not something you mess with.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "I’m tellin’ yeh, I’m fine," said Hagrid.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Hagrid’s badly hurt but he’s trying to play it down. He’s damaged and stubborn about getting help.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore knew, an’ he told us," said Hagrid.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Dumbledore sent Hagrid to find the giants. Hagrid trusts Dumbledore and went because Dumbledore told him to.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "The Ministry’s keepin’ an eye on Dumbledore an’ anyone they reckon’s in league with him,"
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: The Ministry is watching Dumbledore and anyone thought to be with him. We can’t assume people aren’t being watched.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: Dumbledore mentioned the Room to me in passing at the Yule Ball. If Dumbledore knows about it then it can't be some daft prank.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: "I solemnly swear that I am up to no good."
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: This bit of parchment is the Marauder's Map. Tap it with the words and the whole castle shows up on it.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: At half-past seven Harry, Ron, and Hermione left the Gryffindor common room, Harry clutching a certain piece of aged parchment in his hand.
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: Hermione and Ron are with me on this. We spent the day rounding people up and we're all heading out together to use the Map and set things in motion.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: by the end of dinner he was confident that the news had been passed to every one of the twenty-five people who had turned up in the Hog's Head.
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: We actually got the word out — all twenty-five people who signed turned up. That's more than I expected.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "What’s he keeping in there? Did he say?" asked Harry.
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: I wanted to know what Hagrid had hidden in the Forest. I saw the black winged horses with my own eyes so they are real and Hagrid wasn't making them up.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "A great wave of relief broke over Harry. Here at last was proof that he had not imagined these creatures, that they were real"
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: I couldn't believe it at first but seeing the horses eat made me relieved. I know now the creatures are real and Hagrid knows about them too.

Book5-chapter18_Sc7.source: A highly polished door had appeared in the wall.
Book5-chapter18_Sc7.description: A door can just appear when you need a place to practise. I went straight for the handle and led us in.

Book5-chapter18_Sc7.source: Harry reached out, seized the brass handle, pulled open the door, and led the way into a spacious room lit with flickering torches like those that illuminated the dungeons eight floors below.
Book5-chapter18_Sc7.description: The room inside is huge and dungeon-like with flickering torches, walls lined with bookcases, and big silk cushions instead of chairs. Perfect for training.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "I have never seen such a disgraceful exhibition. Two onto one! Explain yourselves!"
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: That looked like a set-up to me, but I know I got in trouble for it. I did what I had to. Still, Minerva gave us detention and Umbridge is making things worse.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "The High Inquisitor will henceforth have supreme authority over all punishments, sanctions, and removal of privileges pertaining to the students of Hogwarts"
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Umbridge has official power now. She can override other teachers and take away our privileges whenever she wants.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "I think a lifelong ban ought to do the trick"
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Umbridge wants to ban me from playing Quidditch for life. That is ridiculous and cruel, and it feels like she is trying to humiliate me.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "I'm going to resign first thing tomorrow."
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Ron is devastated and thinking about quitting the team. If he does, we will be in a real mess because we're already short of players.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: It was over in two breathless, desperate, windswept seconds — Harry’s fingers closed around the tiny, struggling ball — Malfoy’s fingernails scrabbled the back of Harry’s hand hopelessly — Harry pulled his broom upward, holding the struggling ball in his hand and the Gryffindor spectators screamed their approval.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: I caught the Snitch. I grabbed it with everything I had and the whole stand went mental.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: WHAM! A Bludger hit Harry squarely in the small of the back and he flew forward off his broom; luckily he was only five or six feet above the ground, having dived so low to catch the Snitch, but he was winded all the same as he landed flat on his back on the frozen pitch.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: I got clocked by a Bludger right after I caught it and landed flat on my back. I was winded and sore.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: “Saved Weasley’s neck, haven’t you?” he said to Harry. “I’ve never seen a worse Keeper . . . but then he was born in a bin. . . .”
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: Malfoy slagged off Ron and my ties to the Weasleys. I don't like him one bit. If he insults Ron I will do something about it.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: Harry grabbed hold of George; meanwhile it was taking the combined efforts of Angelina, Alicia, and Katie to stop Fred leaping on Malfoy, who was laughing openly.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: I lost it and went for Malfoy. I punched him in the gut out of pure anger because of what he said about Mum and the Weasleys.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: He could hear girls’ voices screaming, Malfoy yelling, George swearing, a whistle blowing, and the bellowing of the crowd around him, but he did not care, not until somebody in the vicinity yelled “IMPEDIMENTA!” and only when he was knocked over backward by the force of the spell did he abandon the attempt to punch every inch of Malfoy he could reach.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: I got hit with an Impedimentia curse and was knocked over. That was the only thing that stopped me from decking Malfoy properly.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: “I’ve never seen behavior like it — back up to the castle, both of you, and straight to your Head of House’s office! Go! Now!”
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: Madam Hooch sent me and George straight to McGonagall's office. We're in proper trouble and there's no point pretending otherwise.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.source: "it was he who had attacked Mr. Weasley in the first place."
Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: I keep seeing things I can't explain and the worst part is thinking I was the one who attacked Mr Weasley. I feel sick about it and guilty as anything.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.source: "I felt like I wanted to attack Dumbledore too."
Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: I can get these urges — I don't just see things, I feel like I could act on them. That scares me more than the visions themselves.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.source: "Dad is still alive. I am setting out for St. Mungo's now. Stay where you are. I will send news as soon as I can. Mum."
Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: Mrs Weasley is on her way to St Mungo's and Dad is still alive. They're going to keep us waiting here until they send news.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.source: "We would not be here if it were not for him; they would all still be asleep in bed."
Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: Everyone's here because I raised the alarm. I keep thinking it's my fault they're in this mess and I can't shake that.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: I saw it happen. I had a vision of Mr Weasley being attacked by a giant snake and it felt real.
I was inside the snake. I watched the whole attack from the snake's point of view.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: It wasn’t an ordinary dream it was real
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: This wasn't just some ordinary dream. It was real enough that I know Arthur Weasley has been badly hurt.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: Ron looked from Harry to Dumbledore white-faced and shocked
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: Ron is terrified for his dad. He's pale and stunned and I can tell he's scared out of his mind.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: Fred George and Ginny continued to stare at him for a moment
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: Fred, George and Ginny are looking at me like they might blame me for what I saw. I toned my story down and said I watched from the sidelines because I didn't want them accusing me of anything worse.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: Please sit down all three of you Everard and Dilys may not be back for several minutes
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: Dumbledore is getting other portraits involved and trying to find out more. He thinks Everard and Dilys might help locate Mr Weasley.
Dumbledore wants to send a warning out. He's already waking people and getting Fawkes involved to help.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: why were they all so slow on the uptake did they not realize how much a person bled when fangs that long pierced their side
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: I get frustrated when people don't react as quickly as I think they should. I keep thinking about how badly someone could be hurt and want action now.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "So," said Harry, "you saw them and then what?"
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: You saw giants up close and watched what happened next. I wanted Hagrid to tell me exactly how they met them and what went wrong.
They gave the giant a piece of everlasting fire as a gift. That was supposed to make the giants trust them.
Karkus didn't speak English, so they had to get other giants to translate. Not everything went smoothly at first.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "How did you get out of that?"
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: Hagrid nearly got killed by Golgomath but Olympe used fast spellwork to save him. They escaped because of quick magic, not brute force.

Book5-chapter21_Sc2.source: "The only people who can see thestrals," she said, "are people who have seen death."
Book5-chapter21_Sc2.description: I can see thestrals because I have seen death. That explains why some people can't see them.
Thestrals aren't evil omens. They're animals, not harbingers of doom, and they only bite if you really annoy them.

Book5-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Please continue teaching as usual. I am going to walk"
Book5-chapter21_Sc2.description: Umbridge is just there to interfere and boss people around. She treats Hagrid like he's stupid and is trying to control the lesson.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: I have a message for you from Albus Dumbledore." "Stay where you are."
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dumbledore told me to stay put. I don't like being kept out of the loop but apparently I'm meant to wait and do nothing for now.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: You lot disappeared right under her nose, even though Dumbledore told her Mr. Weasley was in St. Mungo's, and he'd given you all permission to visit.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Okay, so Dumbledore cleared things up with Umbridge enough for other people. That makes me think he's handling the grown-up stuff, even if he won't explain it to me.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: It was like I was the snake.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: That dream about being inside the snake felt different and awful. It wasn't just a vision. It felt like I was the snake itself.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: When he did it to me, I couldn't remember what I'd been doing for hours at a time.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Ginny says possession leaves you with big gaps. I can remember everything, so maybe I wasn't possessed like she was. That actually takes a weight off me.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: I forgot," he said. "Lucky you," said Ginny coolly. "I'm sorry," Harry said, and he meant it.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: I needed to apologise to Ginny properly. She called me out and I meant it when I said sorry.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: Stay where you are.' 'I haven't moved!' said Harry, his hand still upon the doorknob.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: I'm fed up with adults telling me to wait without explaining. I feel angry and boxed in, and I don't trust being left out of decisions about things that involve me.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: Couple of 'em were visitin' him every day, bringin' gifts to the Gurg
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: They're not just random troublemakers. Death Eaters were visiting the giants, bringing them gifts. This is organized. Voldemort's lot are working with some of the giants.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: She'll be informing the Minister of your late return
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: Umbridge is actively spying and reporting. We have to expect the Ministry to be watching us and act like everything we do could be used against Dumbledore and his allies.
Hermione and Ron are my people to rely on in a crisis. We stick together, hide together and trust each other when things get ugly.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: I don’t know what would have happened if it hadn’t been for you, Harry
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: I saw a vision of Mr Weasley being attacked and if I hadn't acted he might have died. I was there and I helped, and that is why Arthur is alive.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: When he paused for breath, Sirius said, "Did you tell Dumbledore this?"
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: I told Dumbledore about the vision but he didn't explain what it meant. He didn't give me answers.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: It must have been the aftermath of the vision, that’s all
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: I don't think it was just aftereffects. For a moment I actually felt like a snake and wanted to attack Dumbledore. Something inside me felt like a snake and that scares me.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: You’re in shock, Harry; you’re blaming yourself for something you only witnessed, and it’s lucky you did witness it or Arthur might have died. Just stop worrying
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: Sirius stuck up for me and calmed me down. I can rely on him to be steady and protective when I'm rattled.

Book5-chapter25_Sc3.source: “Oh, you’ll talk to Hermione Granger!” she said shrilly, her face now shining with tears
Book5-chapter25_Sc3.description: She thinks I prefer talking to Hermione over her. She’s hurt and thinks I’m excluding her, and that made her lash out at me. I didn’t mean it that way.

Book5-chapter25_Sc3.source: “There — there wasn’t time for him to say anything.”
Book5-chapter25_Sc3.description: There was no time for Cedric to say anything before he died. He didn’t get to tell anyone anything, not even Cho.

Book5-chapter25_Sc3.source: “In the same boat, you an’ me, aren’ we, Harry? ... An’ both orphans. Yeah ... both orphans.”
Book5-chapter25_Sc3.description: Hagrid and I are both outsiders and both orphans. He’s feeling battered and alone and I can see how much that family stuff still hurts him, so I can’t just write him off.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: She held up ten stubby little fingers, then, her smile wider and more toadlike than ever before beneath her green hat, she bustled from their midst
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: That Umbridge is completely unbearable. She plays nice but she sneers at you the whole time and I can't stand her face.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: I thought this evening we should just go over the things we've done so far, because it's the last meeting before the holidays and there's no point starting anything new right before a three-week break
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: The D A is real and it's working. We can actually teach people practical spells and they're getting better. I feel proud and responsible for it.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: When he passed Cho she beamed at him; he resisted the temptation to walk past her several more times
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Cho still makes me feel sick in the stomach and I keep noticing her. I'm trying not to make a fool of myself but it bothers me more than I want to admit.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: Half of him wanted to tell Ron and Hermione what had just happened, but the other half wanted to take the secret with him to the grave
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: I am rattled and not sure who to tell. Part of me wants to keep whatever happened to myself because it feels too heavy to say out loud.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: D'you reckon if you saw someone snuff it you'd be able to see the Quaffle better? He, Crabbe, and Goyle roared with laughter as they pushed past
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Malfoy and his lot are vile and petty. They'll mock anything to get under your skin, even the nastiest stuff, so I should expect them to try to wind people up.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "She — er —" "Did you kiss?" asked Hermione briskly.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Yeah. I kissed Cho. It happened and I felt sick about how it went.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "How was it?" Harry considered for a moment. "Wet," he said truthfully.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: The kiss was awful. She was crying into my shoulder so it was just... wet. Not like anything I'd imagined.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "I'll have to, won't I?" said Harry. "We've got D.A. meetings, haven't we?"
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I can't avoid seeing her. We're going to have to meet at D.A., so I'll have to face this again whether I want to or not.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "I sort of — patted her on the back a bit."
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I tried to be nice. I patted her on the back because I didn't know what else to do when she started sobbing.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Harry's liked her for ages, haven't you, Harry?"
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I've liked Cho for ages, but I always imagined a happier version of her. Seeing her like that makes me question whether I even want to ask her out now.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "wishing more than anything that Sirius's head would appear there and give him some advice about girls."
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I want help. I wish Sirius were here to tell me what to do about girls because I have no idea.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "This is our long-term resident ward," she informed Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Ginny in a low voice. "For permanent spell damage, you know."
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Okay, so this is the long-term ward for permanent spell damage. People here are seriously hurt and some of them might not get better.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "He does seem to be getting back some sense of himself," and the description of Gilderoy signing photographs feverishly.
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Lockhart's wandering about and signing photos like a loon because his memory's shot. He's not dangerous to others but he's a danger to himself.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "My son and his wife were tortured into insanity by You-Know-Who's followers."
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Neville's parents were Aurors and were tortured into this state by Voldemort's people. That's why they're here.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Yes, I know who you are, of course. Neville speaks most highly of you."
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Neville looks terrified and ashamed, but Mrs Longbottom says he talks about me. That means he does trust me even if he won't meet my eye.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "She no longer had the plump, happy-looking face Harry had seen in Moody's old photograph of the original Order of the Phoenix."
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Neville's mum is here and she's a shadow of the woman in that old Order photo. It's awful to see what they've done to her.

Book5-chapter27_Sc4.description: Someone got me with a Trip Jinx. I went flying and skidded along the floor. Brilliant.

Book5-chapter27_Sc4.source: "It’s him!" she said jubilantly at the sight of Harry on the floor.
Book5-chapter27_Sc4.description: Umbridge is gleeful about catching me. She actually looks pleased to have hauled me in. That makes everything worse.

Book5-chapter27_Sc4.source: "You can come with me to the headmaster’s office, Potter."
Book5-chapter27_Sc4.description: Umbridge is taking me straight to Dumbledore. She grabbed my arm like I was a criminal and expects me to come along. Malfoy helped her and got rewarded with points.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "It was a complete fiasco, now you mention it."
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: That date was a complete fiasco. I told Cho the truth and it blew up in my face.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "people have got to know what Voldemort's capable of, haven't they?"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: People need to know how dangerous Voldemort is. I have to tell them, even if they think I'm mad.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I mean, what was all that about? What was going on?"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Cho and I are messed up right now. I do like her but whatever happened at that tea shop has put a wall between us.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "HARRY POTTER SPEAKS OUT AT LAST: THE TRUTH ABOUT HE-WHO-MUST-NOT-BE-NAMED AND THE NIGHT I SAW HIM RETURN"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: My interview is out in The Quibbler and people are writing to me about it. It's public now and I can't take it back.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "There will be no more Hogsmeade trips for you, Mr. Potter,"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Umbridge is furious about the interview. She will use it as an excuse to punish me and restrict me at school.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: Your dad has been attacked. I saw him get bitten and there was blood everywhere.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.source: [No! It wasn’t a dream . . . not an ordinary dream. . . . I was there, I saw it. . . . I did it . . .]
Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: It wasn't just a dream. I was there and I did it. I actually saw it happen.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.source: [He’s been bitten, it’s serious, there was blood everywhere . . .]
Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: This is serious. He was bitten and bleeding badly.
There was a huge snake involved. That’s what attacked him.
I kept insisting I'm fine even though I’m sweating, shaking and my head hurts like mad.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.source: [There’s nothing wrong with me, it’s your dad you’ve got to worry about — we need to find out where he is — he’s bleeding like mad — I was — it was a huge snake . . .]
Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: I had to tell Ron right away that his dad was the one in danger and we had to find him now.

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore wants to stop you having those dreams about Voldemort," said Hermione at once.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Dumbledore's made me take Occlumency lessons with Snape to stop those dreams about You-Know-Who

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "You will find yourself easy prey for the Dark Lord!" said Snape savagely.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Snape thinks if I can't control my emotions I'll be easy meat for Voldemort and he keeps pushing me to 'master myself'

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I saw that door when your dad took me down to the courtrooms for my hearing and it's definitely the same one he was guarding when the snake bit him."
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: That door I saw is the same one Arthur was guarding at the Ministry so whatever Voldemort wants is probably behind it

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "In the Department of Mysteries, it's got to be," Harry whispered.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Of course the thing Voldemort's after is in the Department of Mysteries

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I want you to take this," he said quietly, thrusting a badly wrapped package roughly the size of a paperback book into Harry's hands.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Sirius trusts me enough to give me something to contact him if I need him but I will not be the one to lure him out of Grimmauld Place

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "You must remain focused. Repel me with your brain and you will not need to resort to your wand."
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Snape expects me to block him with my mind not my wand and thinks I keep handing him the memories I fear

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I told you to empty yourself of emotion!"
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: I can't just switch off my feelings on command and Snape's methods are making me furious and shaky

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "You know what these remind me of?" "No, what’s that?" "The Death Eaters’ scars. Voldemort touches one of them, and all their scars burn, and they know they’ve got to join him."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Right away I made the connection to those Death Eater scar things. It sounded horrible but Hermione's idea to use metal coins instead of people makes sense. I liked that better.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "I suppose the only danger with these is that we might accidentally spend them." "Fat chance," said Ron, who was examining his own fake Galleon with a slightly mournful air. "I haven’t got any real Galleons to confuse it with."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Those fake Galleons are clever and quiet. I slipped mine in my pocket and felt safer knowing they change by charm when Hermione sets the date.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Weasley cannot save a thing, He cannot block a single ring, That’s why Slytherins all sing: Weasley is our King."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Hearing them sing that at Ron actually made me angry. I wanted to ignore it but I ended up diving straight for Ron to try and help. I will not stand by while they hound him.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "But Harry had seen it at last: The tiny fluttering Golden Snitch was hovering feet from the ground at the Slytherin end of the pitch."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: There it was. I spotted the Snitch. Game on. Find it and end this.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Warrington’s aim’s so pathetic I’d be more worried if he was aiming for the person next to me," he retorted, which made Ron and Hermione laugh and wiped the smirk off Pansy Parkinson’s face.
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: When I stick up for Ron with a jab like that it actually cracks the Slytherins up and makes Pansy shut up for a moment. I know I can get under their skin as well as they get under ours.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: I don’t want to talk about Cedric Diggory, all right? So if that’s what you’re here for, you might as well clear out.
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: I don’t want to go over how Cedric died. Don’t expect me to describe it. I’m done being paraded and poked about it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: Is it true that you can produce a Patronus? ... Yeah, ... A corporeal Patronus? ... She’s my auntie ... I’m Susan Bones. ... So — is it really true? You make a stag Patronus? ... Yes ...
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Yes, I can conjure a Patronus, a stag. It’s real and it’s mine.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: And did you kill a basilisk with that sword in Dumbledore’s office? ... Er — yeah, I did, yeah
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: I did kill the basilisk with that sword in Dumbledore’s office. That happened, and it’s not something I brag about.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: I . . . I don’t want to sound like I’m trying to be modest or anything, but . . . I had a lot of help with all that stuff . . .
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Look, I had help with a lot of the dangerous stuff last year. Some of it I did on my own, but most of it involved others. I don’t want people thinking I did it all alone.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: She had decided to display him like some sort of freak and of course they had all turned up to see just how wild his story was.
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Hermione’s gone and shown me off, and now everyone’s treating me like a curiosity. I’m angry about that.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: I turned into You-Know-Who in that vision. I actually was him for a bit and then snapped back with my scar burning.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: “Bode could never have taken it, Master. . . . Bode would have known he could not.”
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: Bode couldn’t have removed the thing because of something on the weapon or around it that stops people meddling with it.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: “He was with Rookwood, he’s one of the Death Eaters who escaped from Azkaban, remember?”
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: Rookwood is one of the Death Eaters and he’s involved in whatever went wrong with Bode and the weapon.
I’m not going to blurt this out. They want me to learn Occlumency to stop this, and if I tell everyone I’ll just prove their point.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: “I wouldn’t have seen it at all if I could do Occlumency.”
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: If I could do Occlumency properly I wouldn’t be getting these visions shoved into my head.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: Harry's anger and cold voice toward Rookwood scene
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: When I’m confronting someone tied to Voldemort I get cold and dangerous; I can be cruel and commanding when I need answers.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Harry Potter," he said, holding out a hand when Harry entered.
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: I shook Firenze's hand. He's not smiling, but he spoke to me like he expected we'd meet again.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "It was foretold that we would meet again."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: So he thinks our meeting was meant to happen. That's a bit creepy but I can't deny it's awkwardly true.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Harry noticed that there was the shadow of a hoof-shaped bruise on Firenze's chest."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: Firenze's got a hoof-shaped bruise on his chest. Someone's been rough with him.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "He wondered whether it had been Bane who had kicked Firenze in the chest."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: I reckon Bane or one of the herd might've done it. It makes sense given how they treated Firenze before.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "A twinkling red star winked at him from overhead."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: I lay back and a red star winked at me on the ceiling. Weird, but I'm watching what the stars say.
I asked how Trelawney was because I care if she's all right after being sacked.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Occlumency, Potter. The magical defense of the mind against external penetration."
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: So I'm being told to learn Occlumency. Fine. I need to protect my mind so people cannot get into it.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "I am in rather a hurry, Black . . . unlike you, I do not have unlimited leisure time . . ."
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Snape is the one who will be teaching me. Great, extra lessons with him. Lovely.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "You will receive private lessons once a week, but you will not tell anybody what you are doing, least of all Dolores Umbridge."
