Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Dumbledore wants this kept secret from Umbridge. I am not to tell anyone about the lessons.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "And listen . . . Harry, I know you don’t like Snape, but he is a superb Occlumens and we all — Sirius included — want you to learn to protect yourself, so work hard, all right?"
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Sirius and Lupin actually want me to learn this. They still back me, even if I hate that Snape will teach it.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "I’ll get to the point, then," said Sirius, standing up.
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: I thought Sirius would always just defend me without thinking. He does care, but he can be fierce about Snape too. I need to stay out of their fights.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "You’ll be safe once you’re in the grounds," said Tonks, casting a careful eye around at the deserted road.
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Once I'm inside Hogwarts grounds I should be safer. For now, I still feel exposed and nervous about the lessons to come.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: MASS BREAKOUT FROM AZKABAN MINISTRY FEARS BLACK IS RALLYING POINT FOR OLD DEATH EATERS
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Ten high-security prisoners have escaped from Azkaban and the Ministry is saying Sirius Black is the rallying point. That's why Fudge is making such a fuss.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: Bellatrix Lestrange, convicted of the torture and permanent incapacitation of Frank and Alice Longbottom.
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Bellatrix Lestrange is one of the escapees and she was involved in torturing the Longbottoms. She's dangerous and tied to Black.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: TRAGIC DEMISE OF MINISTRY OF MAGIC WORKER ... strangled by a potted-plant.
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Someone at the Ministry, Broderick Bode, was killed by a plant sent to St. Mungo's. That means Death Eaters or whoever's behind this are willing to use clever, hidden attacks.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “I met Bode,” he said slowly. “I saw him at the Ministry with your dad . . .”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: I met Bode in the Department of Mysteries with Mr Weasley. This connects people I know to the attack and makes it real for me.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: They sounded curious rather than hostile now, and once or twice he was sure he overheard snatches of conversation that suggested that the speakers were not satisfied with the Prophet’s version
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: People at Hogwarts are starting to doubt the Prophet and some are thinking Dumbledore and I might have been right all along. The mood has shifted from pure hostility to curiosity.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “He heard every word Potter said and hastened straight to the school to report to me —”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Heard every word I said in the Hog's Head and ran straight to Umbridge. So Willy Widdershins really did hear me and told on me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “If you remember, the Ministry decree banning all student societies was not put into effect until two days after Harry’s Hogsmeade meeting, so he was not breaking any rules in the Hog’s Head at all.”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Dumbledore says I wasn't breaking any rules at that first meeting. The ban came in two days later. That means the Hogsmeade meeting itself wasn't illegal.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “Just nod or shake your head, dear,” Umbridge said coaxingly to Marietta.
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Umbridge tried to force Marietta to confirm the meetings by making her nod or shake her head. She was trying to make Marietta give evidence.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “And to Harry’s horror, she withdrew from her pocket the list of names that had been pinned upon the Room of Requirement’s wall and handed it to Fudge.”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Marietta handed Umbridge the list from the Room of Requirement. She betrayed us and gave them the names.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “See what they’ve named themselves?” said Fudge quietly. “Dumbledore’s Army.”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: They found the heading on the parchment. We've been named 'Dumbledore's Army' and they know it now. That's a proper disaster.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “Miss Edgecombe tipped me off and I proceeded at once to the seventh floor, accompanied by certain trustworthy students, so as to catch those in the meeting red-handed.”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Marietta, who I thought was a friend or at least just a classmate, tipped off Umbridge. I feel betrayed and furious with her.

Book5-chapter27_Sc6.source: “I could have sworn too that he felt something brush against his side, a gentle something like a draft or bird wings, but looking down he saw nothing there.”
Book5-chapter27_Sc6.description: Something unseen passed by Kingsley and I felt a brush like wings. I think there was some quiet magic or a protective thing going on that we couldn't see.

Book5-chapter27_Sc8.source: "Listen to me, Harry, you must study Occlumency as hard as you can, do you understand me? Do everything Professor Snape tells you and practice it particularly every night before sleeping so that you can close your mind to bad dreams"
Book5-chapter27_Sc8.description: I have to study Occlumency properly. I need to do exactly what Snape says and practise every night so I can close my mind against bad dreams and whatever else tries to get in.
Close my mind. That's the bit that matters in the moment. Shut it right up when I sleep and when people probe me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc8.source: "I am not leaving to go into hiding. Fudge will soon wish he�d never dislodged me from Hogwarts, I promise you"
Book5-chapter27_Sc8.description: Dumbledore isn't running away to hide me. He means to fight this in plain sight, and I can't expect to be quietly saved by him forever.

Book5-chapter27_Sc8.source: "As Dumbledore's fingers closed over Harry's skin, a pain shot through the scar on his forehead, and he felt again that terrible, snakelike longing to strike Dumbledore, to bite him, to hurt him"
Book5-chapter27_Sc8.description: When Dumbledore touched me my scar screamed and I wanted to lash out at him. I hate that the scar can do that to me. It makes me dangerous and terrified at the same time.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "If somebody had tipped off Umbridge about the D.A. then he, the leader, might as well be packing his trunk right now."
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: If someone ratted us out I could be finished at Hogwarts. Brilliant. That's exactly what I was terrified might happen.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "Marietta raised her head... her face was horribly disfigured by a series of close-set purple pustules that had spread across her nose and cheeks to form the word 'SNEAK.'"
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: Marietta betrayed us and got her face hexed to spell SNEAK. She told Umbridge and that's how they found out.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "I have testimony from Willy Widdershins, Minerva, who happened to be in the bar at the time. He... heard every word Potter said and hastened straight to the school to report to me —"
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: Willy Widdershins claims he heard me recruiting in the Hog's Head and reported it. That's the evidence they're using against me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "There’s nothing like a good witness, is there, Dumbledore?" "Nothing at all, Cornelius," said Dumbledore gravely, inclining his head.
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: Dumbledore's backing me. He keeps signalling I'm not to panic. He's quietly protecting me here, and that's a huge relief.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "I do not deny — and nor, I am sure, does Harry — that he was in the Hog’s Head that day... the Ministry decree banning all student societies was not put into effect until two days after Harry’s Hogsmeade meeting, so he was not breaking any rules in the Hog’s Head at all."
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: Okay, so the first meeting wasn't illegal because the decree came later. That means I'm not automatically guilty for that Hogsmeade meeting.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "Well, now," said Fudge... "It is very brave of you, my dear, coming to tell Professor Umbridge, you did exactly the right thing."
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: Fudge is treating Marietta like a hero for snitching. The Minister's decided to use any witness to crush us, and he's delighted someone tattled.

Book5-chapter27_Sc5.source: "You are not aware that you have broken any school rules?" "School rules?" said Harry. "No."
Book5-chapter27_Sc5.description: They tried to trap me into admitting I knew I broke rules. I kept my head and denied knowing anything so they couldn't pin it on me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc9.source: "I’m afraid this is the end of your friend Dumbledore."
Book5-chapter27_Sc9.description: Dumbledore is gone. He's dead. I can't believe it

Book5-chapter27_Sc9.source: "You'd better get those two off to bed," said Fudge, looking back at Professor McGonagall with a dismissive nod toward Harry and Marietta.
Book5-chapter27_Sc9.description: Fudge doesn't care about us. He's dismissive and bossy, more worried about appearances than what's happened here

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "I'll let you know when the next one is,"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: I keep having to tell people I will let them know about D.A. meetings because I can't do one tonight since I've got Remedial Potions.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "Er d'you want to come into Hogsmeade with me on Valentine's Day?"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Cho asked me to go into Hogsmeade on Valentine's Day and I said yes, so that's actually a date now.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "And why does Professor Dumbledore think I need it, sir?"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Dumbledore thinks I need to learn Occlumency so I can stop sharing thoughts and feelings with the Dark Lord.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "It is the ability to extract feelings and memories from another person’s mind"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Legilimency is basically getting into someone else's head and pulling out their memories and feelings, like mind reading but worse.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "The curse that failed to kill you seems to have forged some kind of connection between you and the Dark Lord."
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: That curse made some sort of link between me and Voldemort, which is why I can sometimes feel or see what he's feeling or seeing.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "And he might try and make me do things?"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: If the Dark Lord can get into my head then he could try to make me do things, and that actually scares me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "Harry Potter, you are a friend of Hagrid’s, are you not?"
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: I'm Hagrid's friend. If Firenze says Hagrid's attempt isn't working, I have to warn him.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "His attempt is not working. He would do better to abandon it."
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: Firenze thinks whatever Hagrid's trying won't work and that Hagrid should give it up.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "Mars, bringer of battle, shines brightly above us, suggesting that the fight must break out again soon."
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: Centaurs read the sky very differently; they reckon war might be coming again and take ages to be sure.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "Centaurs have unraveled the mysteries of these movements over centuries."
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: Centaurs study the heavens for generations and think they can glimpse big changes from the stars.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "Sybill Trelawney may have Seen, I do not know,"
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: Firenze thinks Trelawney is mostly blind to real patterns and wastes time on human fortune-telling, though he won't rule out a true Seeing.

Book5-chapter27_Sc7.source: "Dumbledore's Army, Cornelius," said Dumbledore, still smiling as he waved the list of names before Fudge's face.
Book5-chapter27_Sc7.description: So it was never my 'army' at all. Dumbledore set this up and he even has a list of names. That's why they're calling it Dumbledore's Army.
McGonagall and Kingsley are clearly scared. If they've got fear on their faces in front of Dumbledore, things are serious and I'm not the only one worried.

Book5-chapter27_Sc7.source: "You have been plotting against me!" he yelled. "That's right," said Dumbledore cheerfully.
Book5-chapter27_Sc7.description: Dumbledore is openly admitting he organized opposition to Fudge. He's not hiding it and he isn't ashamed of it either.

Book5-chapter27_Sc7.source: "NO!" shouted Harry. Kingsley flashed a look of warning at him, McGonagall widened her eyes threateningly, but it had suddenly dawned upon Harry what Dumbledore was about to do, and he could not let it happen.
Book5-chapter27_Sc7.description: I tried to stop Dumbledore because I could see what he was about to do. I wasn't going to just let him hand this to Fudge without a fight.

Book5-chapter27_Sc7.source: "Weasley, have you written it all down, everything he's said, his confession, have you got it?" "Yes, sir, I think so, sir!" said Percy eagerly, whose nose was splattered with ink from the speed of his note-taking.
Book5-chapter27_Sc7.description: Percy is all over this. He's taken down Dumbledore's 'confession' and he's thrilled to be part of it. He'll run with it to the Ministry and the papers.

Book5-chapter27_Sc7.source: "Duplicate your notes, Weasley, and send a copy to the Daily Prophet at once. If we send a fast owl we should make the morning edition!"
Book5-chapter27_Sc7.description: Fudge is already planning to make a public show of this. He's going to feed it straight to the Prophet and celebrate having 'proof' against Dumbledore.

Book5-chapter27_Sc3.source: Harry Potter, sir . . . Dobby has come to warn you . . .
Book5-chapter27_Sc3.description: Dobby warned me. Dobby risked everything to tell me Umbridge is involved and that she knows enough to be dangerous. I have to act now.

Book5-chapter27_Sc3.source: WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR? RUN!
Book5-chapter27_Sc3.description: We cannot hang about. If Dobby is terrified then whatever's coming is serious. I shouted for everyone to get out and stop arguing.

Book5-chapter27_Sc3.source: get back down to the kitchen with the other elves, and if she asks you whether you warned me, lie and say no!
Book5-chapter27_Sc3.description: I ordered Dobby to go back to the kitchen and to lie if Umbridge questions him. I will not let him hurt himself and I will protect the others by getting them away.
Dobby trusts me. He risked everything to warn me and he is grateful. That means I have to look out for him.

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "He was in the Department of Mysteries corridor that day! Your dad said he was probably trying to sneak down and find out what happened in my hearing"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: I saw Sturgis that day in the Department of Mysteries corridor. Your dad thought he was sneaking about my hearing

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "So when Sturgis next had an opportunity ... he tried to get into the department to steal the weapon for Voldemort"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: It makes sense that Sturgis might have been used to try to steal that weapon. If someone put the Imperius on him he could have been made to go after it

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Rookwood used to work there. . . . Maybe Voldemort'll send Rookwood to do it?"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Rookwood knows the Department of Mysteries and could be used to get at the weapon

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "You do know why we are here, don't you, Potter?" "So I can learn Occlumency"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: I'm supposed to be learning Occlumency so I can close my mind to these visions

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Protego!" and the following scene where Snape staggered and memories flooded my head
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: I managed to use a Shield Charm against Snape's attack and it actually worked. The shield bought me a moment but I still broke into memories that weren't mine
I snapped at Snape and he admitted it's his job to go into the Dark Lord's thoughts. That made things worse between us

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Why do you call Voldemort the Dark Lord, I've only ever heard Death Eaters call him that"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: I asked Snape why he calls him the Dark Lord because I only heard Death Eaters use that name

Book5-chapter29_Sc3.source: "I just wanted to talk . . . about my dad . . ."
Book5-chapter29_Sc3.description: I watched my dad as a teenager in the Pensieve and he wasn't the hero I imagined at fifteen. He bullied Snape and showed off a lot.

Book5-chapter29_Sc3.source: "I wouldn't like you to judge your father on what you saw there, Harry. He was only fifteen —"
Book5-chapter29_Sc3.description: Okay, fine, he was young and stupid. I can't judge James only by that memory. People can grow out of being idiots.

Book5-chapter29_Sc3.source: "I think James was everything Snape wanted to be — he was popular, he was good at Quidditch, good at pretty much everything."
Book5-chapter29_Sc3.description: I feel a bit sorry for Snape now. Seeing how James and the others treated him changed how I see Snape and my dad.

Book5-chapter29_Sc3.source: "He told me he'd never teach me Occlumency again"
Book5-chapter29_Sc3.description: Snape has stopped my Occlumency lessons. That matters because I need to learn it and Dumbledore thinks it's vital.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: So there is an Inquisitorial Squad now and they have the power to dock points. Fine, more official nastiness to watch out for.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Malfoy just docked us all about fifty points," said Harry furiously
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Malfoy will use that I badge to bully us and actually take points off Gryffindor. I can't just stand there and let him get away with it.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Phase one is about to begin. Id get in the Great Hall for lunch if I were you," said George.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Fred and George are planning something in the Great Hall at lunch. They're not scared of getting in trouble anymore, and they want us around as cover.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "The headmistress would like to see you, Potter," he leered.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Umbridge is already watching me. Filch is being used to send me to her, which means I need to be ready for interrogation or worse.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "I’ve been telling Dumbledore for years and years he’s too soft with you all," said Filch, chuckling nastily.
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Filch has long been on Dumbledore for being soft and he hates us. He’s been primed to be vicious if given power.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "But when Educational Decree Twenty-nine comes in, Potter, I’ll be allowed to do them things."
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Umbridge is pushing rules that let people like Filch brutalize students. Things at school are about to get a lot harsher.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "And she’s asked the Minister to sign an order for the expulsion of Peeves."
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Umbridge has already asked the Minister to get rid of Peeves. She’s working the system and making Hogwarts quieter for her own sake.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Here we are," he said, leering down at Harry as he rapped three times upon Professor Umbridge’s door and pushed it open. "The Potter boy to see you, ma’am."
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Filch is clearly in Umbridge’s pocket and is being used to report on students. He’ll help her because he’s eager to prove himself.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "What would you like to drink?" "To drink, Mr. Potter," she said, smiling still more widely. "Tea? Coffee? Pumpkin juice?"
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Umbridge pretends to be sweet but everything she does is a performance to unsettle me. She used a drink to try and make me relax and talk.
Umbridge is directly accusing me of knowing where Dumbledore is and trying to force me to tell her. She’s not above threatening tactics.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "In that case, you will kindly tell me the whereabouts of Sirius Black."
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: She thinks I’m meeting Sirius and is trying to bully me into giving him up. She’ll use whatever she can to find out.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "All channels of communication in and out of this school are being monitored. A Floo Network Regulator is keeping watch over every fire in Hogwarts — except my own, of course."
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Umbridge has the Floo Network monitored and is watching all communication into and out of Hogwarts. There are almost no private ways to contact people anymore.

Book5-chapter28_Sc2.source: "One of the horrible painted kittens behind Umbridge had great round blue eyes just like Mad-Eye Moody’s magical one,"
Book5-chapter28_Sc2.description: Seeing that painted kitten with a magical eye made me think straight away that drinking anything offered by an enemy is dangerous. I won’t be gullible about traps like that.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I’m not the weapon after all, thought Harry."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: I'm not the weapon after all. I'm actually human and not just some tool for Voldemort.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Even Voldemort couldn’t just make you fly out of your dormitory, Harry."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: You can’t Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts. Even Voldemort couldn't just teleport me out of my dormitory.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Dobby did, he left the Malfoys’ to give me warnings three years ago."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: House-elves can leave if given clothes or in extreme situations. Dobby left the Malfoys to warn me once.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "They can leave the house if they really want to," Harry contradicted him. "Dobby did, he left the Malfoys’ to give me warnings three years ago. He had to punish himself afterward, but he still managed it."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: House-elves are supposed to be bound to a house, but they can defy that if they choose, as Dobby did.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Sirius and Lupin had given Harry a set of excellent books entitled Practical Defensive Magic and Its Use Against the Dark Arts"
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Practical Defensive Magic is exactly the sort of book I need for the D.A. It's got useful counterjinxes and proper illustrations.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "He felt like joining in as they heard Sirius tramping past their door toward Buckbeak’s room, singing 'God Rest Ye Merry, Hippogriffs' at the top of his voice."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: I felt close to Sirius and the others. When they comfort me, I actually want to join in and be part of it.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "By the looks of it, hers was Kreacher’s favorite photograph; he had placed it to the fore of all the others and had mended the glass clumsily with Spellotape."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Kreacher really favors Bellatrix Lestrange. He keeps her photograph front and center among the family pictures.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "He had also managed to retrieve the silver-framed family photographs that Sirius had thrown away over the summer."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Kreacher saved bits and pieces from the house when Sirius tried to purge it. He’s magpie-like about things he can salvage.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Fred and George Apparated at the foot of his bed."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Fred and George can Apparate into the house. They popped into my room with a crack and a grin.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "You were ordering him out of the kitchen." "Yeah . . . You know, I think that’s the last time I saw him, too. . . . He must be hiding upstairs somewhere . . ."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Kreacher went into hiding after being shouted at. He might be somewhere upstairs, avoiding people.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Mrs. Weasley shriek, 'WHAT DO YOU MEAN, THAT’S THE GENERAL IDEA?'"
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Mrs. Weasley absolutely loses it when she thinks someone has been sewing their own wounds. Dad trying Muggle remedies is a bad idea in her book.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Because he had just opened Harry’s gift of fuse-wire and screwdrivers."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Mr. Weasley loved practical Muggle things like fuse-wire and screwdrivers. Give him tools and he's thrilled.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Professor Lockhart!" ... "Haven't we met?" "Er . . . yeah, we have," said Harry. "You used to teach us at Hogwarts, remember?" "Teach?" repeated Lockhart, looking faintly unsettled."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Lockhart's memory is a mess. He doesn't seem to remember teaching us properly anymore.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "I’ve told you, Snape reckons I can carry on by myself now I’ve got the basics . . ."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Snape says I can keep doing Occlumency on my own now that I've got the basics, so I stopped the lessons.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "He had been so sure that his parents had been wonderful people that he never had the slightest difficulty in disbelieving Snape’s aspersions on his father’s character."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: I used to be sure my parents were wonderful, but the Pensieve memories have made me doubt James. I can see things Snape said might have been true, and that messes me up.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "I wish I could talk to Sirius," he muttered. "But I know I can’t."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: I want to talk to Sirius desperately, but with Umbridge watching the fires and reading mail I think I can't reach him.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "It’s Easter eggs from Mum," said Ginny. "There’s one for you. . . ."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: I got an Easter egg from Mum in a package that had been inspected by Umbridge's lot, which made me feel strangely upset for some reason.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Well, I thought of, maybe, being an Auror," Harry mumbled.
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: I'm thinking about becoming an Auror, but McGonagall made it clear they want top grades and I’m only averaging Acceptable right now.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "I would also advise Transfiguration ... then you ought to do Charms, always useful, and Potions."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: If I want to be an Auror I should take Defense Against the Dark Arts, Transfiguration, Charms and Potions for N.E.W.T.s and work hard to raise my marks.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Potter has a criminal record," said Umbridge loudly.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: What the hell. Umbridge is telling everyone I have a criminal record. That is not going to help my chances with the Ministry.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Potter has been cleared of all charges," said Professor McGonagall, even more loudly.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Minerva stands up for me. She actually promises to help me become an Auror if she has to coach me every night. I can count on her to fight for me.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "The Minister of Magic will never employ Harry Potter!" said Umbridge, her voice rising furiously.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: If the Ministry is set against me then I have to decide for myself what I want. I cannot rely on them to make it easy.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "I will assist you to become an Auror if it is the last thing I do! If I have to coach you nightly I will make sure you achieve the required results!"
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Minerva will train me hard. I need to get my grades up and be ready for more exams after Hogwarts.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "He has achieved high marks in all Defense Against the Dark Arts tests set by a competent teacher."
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: My Defense scores are good when someone competent teaches me. That matters.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: He pulled off his Cloak and, striding over to the fireplace, found what he was looking for within seconds: a small box containing glittering Floo powder.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: I took Sirius's knife, put the Invisibility Cloak on and nicked Umbridge's Floo powder. I will go where I need to go to find out what is happening.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Harry, don’t do it, please don’t do it!" Hermione said in anguished tones as the bell rang at the end of the class.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Hermione is terrified I'm doing something reckless. I feel guilty about worrying her but I'm going anyway. I have to see what's going on.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "He was, as Hagrid had said, at least sixteen feet tall."
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Grawp is massive. He is huge, clumsy and unpredictable, and getting close to him makes the ground shake.
Grawp can lash out suddenly. He nearly grabbed Hermione and Hagrid got hurt when he swung at him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "I thought that we told you, Hagrid," said a deep male voice, "that you are no longer welcome here?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: The centaurs don’t want humans in the forest. They’re hostile and quick to assert control over who comes in.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "Firenze has entered into servitude to humans," said a gray centaur with a hard, deeply lined face.
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: I’m clearer now that things have gone wrong between Firenze and the centaurs. They see him as a traitor and that changes how the centaurs treat anyone associated with him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "We agreed, I think, what we would do if this human showed his face in the forest again?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: My presence in the forest isn’t safe. The centaurs don’t recognize me and make it plain they don’t welcome humans here.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: Voldemort has Sirius and I saw it. He's torturing him and says he'll kill him.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "They've taken McGonagall to St. Mungo's this morning."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: McGonagall is out of Hogwarts and in St. Mungo's, so there is no one left here from the Order to tell.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "There's a room in the Department of Mysteries full of shelves covered in these little glass balls, and they're at the end of row ninety-seven."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: The Department of Mysteries has that room with glass spheres and I know exactly where Voldemort is trying to get to.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "If you don't want to do it, fine, but I'm going, understand?"
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: I expect Ron and Hermione to come with me or I'm going regardless. I'm desperate and I'm going to try to save Sirius.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “Hagrid’s nose was gently dripping blood. His eyes were both blackened.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Hagrid is hurt and looking terrible. I can tell he has been attacked and he needs help right now.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “Umbridge reckons it was me that put tha’ niffler in her office.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Umbridge is out to get Hagrid and she is looking for any excuse to get him fired.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “Well, there’s a good chance I’m goin’ ter be gettin’ the sack any day now.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Hagrid thinks he is going to be sacked soon and he is worried about what will happen to Grawp if he is forced to leave.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “He’s been hurting you all this time, hasn’t he?” and “He don’ know his own strength!”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Grawp has been injuring Hagrid because he does not know his own strength. He is dangerous sometimes but not malicious.
Grawp is Hagrid’s half brother. That explains why Hagrid is determined to bring him back and keep him safe.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “If yeh could jus’ nip down here in yer Invisibility Cloak maybe once a week an’ have a little chat with him.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: I promised Hagrid we would try to help Grawp. I had no idea exactly what that would mean, but I promised and I mean to keep it.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “There’s ropes thick as saplings stretching from around the trunks of the largest nearby trees toward the place where Grawp lay curled on the ground.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Grawp is kept tied up with huge ropes. He is not free to wander because he could be a danger if he gets angry.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "It's lessons with Snape that are making it worse," said Harry flatly.
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: Snape's lessons are making my scar worse and I'm getting more sensitive to Voldemort because of them. It's making me feel sick and wired all the time.
I'm putting in the hours at Occlumency but it's not getting better. I can't just switch it off even when I'm trying.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "If she catches yeh, it’ll be all of our necks on the line," he told them flatly.
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: Hagrid thinks Umbridge catching us with him would ruin everything for him and for us. So visiting him after dark is too dangerous.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "I'm getting sick of my scar hurting, and I'm getting bored walking down that corridor every night."
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: I'm fed up with the dreams about the Department of Mysteries and the constant pain in my scar. It's like being tuned to Voldemort and I hate it.
I really miss Quidditch. Watching Ron and Ginny on the stands reminded me how much being kept out of it hurts.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "The Ministry places a rather higher value on my life than yours, I'm afraid."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: She thinks she's untouchable because of her Ministry job. I know she will act like she's important and dangerous, and I don't trust her for a second.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "His scar was throbbing in the soft evening air but it had not yet burned white-hot, as he knew it would if Voldemort had moved in for the kill."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: My scar throbs when Voldemort is near. If it went white-hot I'd know he's about to strike. Right now it's warning me and making me tense.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "Can we have your wand, then, if we're going first?" "No, I don't think so, Mr. Potter," said Umbridge sweetly, poking him in the back with it.
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: Going into the forest without wands is stupid and risky. Umbridge refuses to give hers, which makes being unarmed even worse.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "Her wand fell from her hand to the ground and Harry's heart leapt, if he could just reach it — But as he stretched out a hand toward it, a centaur's hoof descended upon the wand and it broke cleanly in half."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: When Umbridge loses her wand and it gets broken I wanted to grab it and stop her causing more trouble. I felt helpless and furious watching the centaurs handle her.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "'Now!' roared a voice in Harry's ear and a thick hairy arm descended from thin air and dragged him upright; Hermione too had been pulled to her feet."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: The centaurs don't just attack randomly. They can seize us and drag us around. I need to be ready for them to act fast and violently.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: [Harry could see Hagrid watching anxiously out of his cabin window.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: I saw Hagrid watching from his window and gave him a quick thumbs-up. I care about him and I wanted him to know I'm behind him.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: [Even by Harry’s low standards in Divination, the exam went very badly.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Divination is hopeless for me. I messed up the crystal ball, I got tea leaves wrong, and I even mixed up palm lines. I'm done pretending I care about it.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: ["I just hope Professor McGonagall’s all right," said Lavender tearfully. "They carried her back up to the castle, we watched through the dormitory window," said Colin Creevey. "She didn’t look very well..." "Madam Pomfrey will sort her out," said Alicia Spinnet firmly.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Professor McGonagall was carried back to the castle and looked badly hurt. People expect Madam Pomfrey to patch her up.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: ["Umbridge hates part-humans," said Hermione bitterly, flopping down into an armchair.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Umbridge hates part-humans, and that's probably why she's trying to get Hagrid sacked.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: [A voice issued from his own mouth, a high, cold voice empty of any human kindness, "Take it for me. Lift it down, now. I cannot touch it but you can." ... heard the high, cold voice say, "Crucio!" The man on the floor let out a scream of pain...]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Something forced my body to say things and to cast a curse. I suddenly spoke with this cold voice and the Cruciatus hit the man on the floor. That was terrifying and not under my control.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: [Very slowly, his arms trembling, the man on the ground raised his shoulders a few inches and lifted his head. His face was bloodstained and gaunt, twisted in pain yet rigid with defiance. "You’ll have to kill me," whispered Sirius.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Sirius is here, he's hurt and defiant, and he begged me that he'd have to be killed rather than give in. I trusted him and this hurts like mad.
There was a voice saying Voldemort is waiting. Whatever's happening involves Voldemort being close by or involved in what's going on.

Book5-chapter32_Sc4.source: “Master will not come back from the Department of Mysteries!”
Book5-chapter32_Sc4.description: No way is Sirius safe at the Department of Mysteries. If Kreacher is right then Padfoot will not come back from there
I know someone has got Padfoot and it is urgent. I shouted that because I had one last chance to tell someone at Hogwarts

Book5-chapter32_Sc4.source: “They were all bleating about silencing you somehow — discrediting you — but I was the one who actually did something about it”
Book5-chapter32_Sc4.description: It was Umbridge who sent the dementors after me. She lied to cover it up and is willing to do dirty things to silence me
Snape is still cold and unreadable. I pinned my hopes on him and he walked away without helping, so I can no longer rely on him to save Sirius

Book5-chapter34_Sc3.source: I don’t think Sirius is here.
Book5-chapter34_Sc3.description: Sirius should be here where I saw him. If he is not, something is very wrong. I feel sick about it and I have to find him.

Book5-chapter34_Sc3.source: It’s — it’s got your name on
Book5-chapter34_Sc3.description: There's a dusty glass sphere with my name on the label. My name is literally on one of these things. That has to mean something.
When I pick up the orb it is warm like it has been in the sun. Touching it feels like it matters somehow, even though at first nothing happened.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "Because they got the gold from me. I gave them my Triwizard winnings last June."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I gave Fred and George my Triwizard winnings last June. They used that money to set up whatever they have now.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "And I don't regret it either — I didn't need the gold, and they'll be great at a joke shop . . ."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I don't regret giving them the money. It was the right thing to do and I back them setting up their joke shop.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "After putting four successive classes in detention and failing to discover their secret she was forced to give up and allow the bleeding, swooning, sweating, and vomiting students to leave her classes in droves."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Umbridge's lessons are a nightmare for students. Her own measures are getting laughed at and students are deliberately making her look ridiculous.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "Peeves...spent hours at a time floating along after Umbridge and blowing loud raspberries every time she spoke."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Peeves is making Umbridge's life hell and nobody else is doing much to stop him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "You are trying to block your mind, aren't you?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I'm trying to let those dreams lead me on. I actually want to get back to that corridor in the Department of Mysteries even if it's dangerous.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "If Montague doesn't recover before Slytherin play Hufflepuff, we might be in with a chance of winning the Cup."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: If Montague stays out of it, Slytherin will be weaker and Gryffindor might have a shot at the Cup.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "He'd been regretting this ever since; Hermione would not let the subject drop and kept reverting to it when Harry least expected it."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Hermione won't let me drop the Occlumency subject. She's pushy about it and keeps bringing it up.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "He was not sure what he wanted to happen anymore, except that he could not stand any more rows."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Watching Cho play just makes everything confusing for me. I can't handle more arguments or petty rubbish right now.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Yes," said Harry, as his scar gave another painful prickle, "and I'm sure Sirius is still alive, but I can't see how we're going to get there to help him."
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: Sirius is alive and being held by You-Know-Who, but I have no idea how we're supposed to reach him to help.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "I`m not that fussed, to be honest," said Harry bitterly.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: Grawp caused the centaurs to scatter and I feel furious and helpless about what just happened.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Not only had Harry managed to lose his wand but they were stuck in the middle of the Forbidden Forest with no means of transport whatsoever."
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: I've lost my wand and we're stranded in the Forbidden Forest with no way to get to London or to rescue Sirius quickly.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "How could he ever have thought them ugly?" (Harry pats the thestral)
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: Thestrals are not ugly to me anymore. They can help us and I want to use them to fly where we need to go.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Okay, fine, it's your choice," he said curtly. "But unless we can find more thestrals you're not going to be able —"
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: We need more thestrals to carry everyone. Time is slipping and every delay could cost Sirius his life.

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: There was still a member of the Order of the Phoenix at Hogwarts — Snape.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: I can't believe I forgot Snape's still at Hogwarts. Of course there's someone from the Order here

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: Voldemort's got Sirius in the Department of Mysteries, he thought desperately. Voldemort's got Sirius —
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Voldemort has Padfoot and he's in the Department of Mysteries. I saw him there in the vision and I know it's real
Umbridge is onto me and she'll try to stop anything I do. She's a problem I have to work around

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: I wish to interrogate him! ... I have no idea, said Snape coldly. "Potter, when I want nonsense shouted at me I shall give you a Babbling Beverage.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Snape isn't going to play along with Umbridge's craziness, and I can't count on him to help me out in front of her

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: He knelt down quickly, thrust his head into the dancing fire, and cried, 'Number twelve, Grimmauld Place!' ... There was nobody there.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Grimmauld Place is empty right now. Sirius isn't at home where he should be

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Voldemort knows you, Harry! He took Ginny down into the Chamber of Secrets to lure you there, it’s the kind of thing he does, he knows you’re the — the sort of person who’d go to Sirius’s aid!”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Voldemort goes after people he knows I care about. He set Ginny up to draw me in because he expects me to try to save Sirius.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Sirius is trapped — I’ve seen him — Voldemort’s got him, and no one else knows, and that means we’re the only ones who can save him,”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: I've seen Sirius. He is trapped and no one else knows, so it falls to us to act.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “I’m not having nightmares, I’m not just dreaming! What d’you think all the Occlumency was for, why d’you think Dumbledore wanted me prevented from seeing these things? Because they’re REAL,”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Those visions aren't just dreams. Occlumency was to stop me seeing real things. I know the visions are real.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Master will not come back from the Department of Mysteries!”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Kreacher said Sirius will not come back from the Department of Mysteries.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “If I remember rightly, you didn’t have a problem with my saving-people-thing when it was you I was saving from the dementors, or” — he rounded on Ron — “when it was your sister I was saving from the basilisk —”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: My friends have supported me when I acted to save them before. I expect loyalty from them now when I say Sirius needs saving.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Take his wand,” she barked at someone he could not see, and he felt a hand grope inside the chest pocket of his robes and remove the wand.
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Umbridge set traps and Stealth Sensoring Spells. She was waiting and she seized our wands when she found us.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “You think that after two nifflers I was going to let one more foul, scavenging little creature enter my office without my knowledge? I had Stealth Sensoring Spells placed all around my doorway after the last one got in, you foolish boy.”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Umbridge is cunning and paranoid about security. I can't assume her office is easy to sneak into again.

Book5-chapter33_Sc2.source: "We\'re not going to say anything like that!"
Book5-chapter33_Sc2.description: We are not going to let them pretend we made them do it. I shouted that because I know we didn\'t ask them to help and we won\'t let them claim otherwise.

Book5-chapter33_Sc2.source: "Please," said Hermione breathlessly, "please, don\'t attack us, we don\'t think like her, we aren\'t Ministry of Magic employees! We only came in here because we hoped you\'d drive her off for us —"
Book5-chapter33_Sc2.description: I saw Hermione try to explain and mess it up. I feared her words would make things worse and they did. I expected talking might help but it didn\'t.
Grawp thinks Hagrid is his and he wants him. I watched Grawp reach for us and knew he meant Hagrid, not trouble for us at first, though it turned violent when the centaurs shot at him.
Hermione clings to me when things get dangerous. I felt responsible and ready to fight or do whatever it takes to keep her safe.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "Like you won't kill us all the moment I hand it over anyway!"
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: I know they're not bluffing. If I give Dolohov the prophecy he'll just kill us straight away. I won't make that choice.
I can stop someone fast when I need to. When it mattered I froze Dolohov and the other Death Eater solid and bought us time.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "Hermione," Harry said at once, shaking her as the baby-headed Death Eater blundered out of sight again.
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: Hermione's life matters above everything right now. I panicked at the thought she might be dead and everything else narrowed down to getting her safe.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "RON?" Harry yelled, turning quickly from the monstrous transformation taking place before them.
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: I feel protective of Ron and Ginny and the others. When I heard them I dropped everything to get to them. They're my responsibility in the moment.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: Glimmering eerily they drifted in and out of sight in the depths of the green water, looking something like slimy cauliflowers.
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: Those things in the tanks are real and disgusting. I could see them clearly now and they were like slimy cauliflowers floating in green water.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: I think we should go back and try from there.
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: If we went the way I dreamed, we might get somewhere. We have to try the route from the dark room again.
This place is enormous and full of doors. We can’t assume one entrance leads everywhere.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: There was no answering voice, but the veil continued to flutter and sway.
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: That veil is active. It’s moving like someone just went through it so something’s on the other side.
When I saw that archway and the veil, I couldn’t shake the idea that Sirius might be trapped on the other side. I kept thinking he could be there.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: Harry, we are supposed to be here for Sirius!
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: Everything we’re doing is about saving Sirius. I’m convinced that’s what this is for and I won’t let that go.
Hermione and I worked out the row numbers. Row ninety-seven is where we think he should be so we have to check it thoroughly.

Book5-chapter36_Sc1.source: The door right behind him flew open, and the corridor toward the lifts stretched ahead of him, torch-lit and empty.
Book5-chapter36_Sc1.description: The exit opened right behind me and led straight to the lifts. If I can get to the Atrium I can take a lift out.

Book5-chapter36_Sc1.source: “Come out, come out, little Harry!” she called in her mock-baby voice, which echoed off the polished wooden floors. “What did you come after me for, then? I thought you were here to avenge my dear cousin!”
Book5-chapter36_Sc1.description: Bellatrix is gloating and taunting me. She mocks me and provokes me, so this is personal and dangerous.

Book5-chapter36_Sc1.source: Hatred rose in Harry such as he had never known before. He flung himself out from behind the fountain and bellowed “Crucio!”
Book5-chapter36_Sc1.description: I felt a new kind of hatred, so strong I actually used Crucio on her. I never thought I'd do something like that, but I did it because I couldn't stand her.

Book5-chapter28_Sc3.source: "My Inquisitorial Squad is opening and reading all owl post entering and leaving the castle. And Mr. Filch is observing all secret passages in and out of the castle."
Book5-chapter28_Sc3.description: So Umbridge is spying on everyone's mail and Filch is watching the secret passages. They're watching us from all sides.
Umbridge tries to boss me around and kick me out whenever she can. I won't do what she wants easily.

Book5-chapter28_Sc3.source: "She sold us all out, including you!"
Book5-chapter28_Sc3.description: I can't trust everyone in the D.A. anymore. People I thought were friends can betray us and that's dangerous.

Book5-chapter28_Sc3.source: "Are you okay? Umbridge hasn't been asking you about the D.A., has she?"
Book5-chapter28_Sc3.description: I feel let down by Cho. She defended Marietta and it made me angrier at her. We're not on the same page right now.

Book5-chapter28_Sc3.source: "You will not tell anybody what you saw!"
Book5-chapter28_Sc3.description: Snape is volatile about what he doesn't want known. He panics and lashes out when something touches a private memory.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "I’m just glad we won, that’s all."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: We won. I’m glad about that, plain and simple.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "And then, when Chambers came at me about five minutes later — what?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: I made a couple of good saves in the match, and yeah, I remembered the moves in the moment.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He decided to tell us why he’s been covered in injuries ever since he got back from the giants."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Hagrid has been dealing with giants stuff and he wanted us involved, which ties me closer into whatever trouble he drags in.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He brought one back and hid it in the forest?" "Yep."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Hagrid brought a giant back and hid him in the forest. That thing, Grawp, is real and huge.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Teach him English, yeah."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Hagrid made us promise to help teach Grawp English. We actually promised and that matters.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "As you can see, your O.W.L.s are spread over two successive weeks."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Our O.W.L.s are coming up, theory in the mornings, practicals in the afternoons, and Astronomy at night. Exams are stacked and serious.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "I must warn you that the most stringent Anti-Cheating Charms have been applied to your examination papers."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Professor McGonagall warned that the exams are heavily protected against cheating. No easy shortcuts.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “Oh it’s easy,” said Luna, sliding obligingly from her thestral and marching over to him, Hermione, and Ginny. “Come here . . .” She pulled them over to the other thestrals standing around and one by one managed to help them onto the backs of their mounts.
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: I can ride thestrals to get places even if others cannot see them. I have to hold on tight because they launch and fly dead fast.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: Then, with a sweeping movement that nearly unseated him, the wings on either side extended, the horse crouched slowly and then rocketed upward so fast and so steeply that Harry had to clench his arms and legs tightly around the horse to avoid sliding backward over its bony rump.
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: That flight was terrifyingly fast. Once they take off you better grip on or you'll go flying off.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: Harry felt sure that there ought to be a security person there, sure that their absence was an ominous sign, and his feeling of foreboding increased as they passed through the golden gates to the lifts.
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: Something's wrong at the Ministry. No security people where they should be means we are walking into trouble.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “Visitors, please take the badges and attach them to the front of your robes.” Half a dozen badges slid out of the metal chute where returned coins usually appeared. Hermione scooped them up and handed them mutely to Harry over Ginny’s head; he glanced at the topmost one. HARRY POTTER RESCUE MISSION
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: We're being treated as a rescue party at the Ministry. My name is literally stamped on a badge for a rescue mission.

Book5-chapter36_Sc3.source: "So you smashed my prophecy?" said Voldemort softly, staring at Harry with those pitiless red eyes.
Book5-chapter36_Sc3.description: He turned up in the middle of the hall, pale and snake-faced, and he was looking straight at me like I was the problem. He thinks the prophecy matters and that I ruined it.
He tried to kill me outright with Avada Kedavra and I could not move. That Killing Curse came for me and I was helpless.

Book5-chapter36_Sc3.source: "Master, I am sorry, I knew not, I was fighting the Animagus Black!" sobbed Bellatrix, flinging herself down at Voldemort's feet
Book5-chapter36_Sc3.description: Bella was on her knees, all desperate and sniveling, blaming the Animagus for screwing things up. She was terrified of him.
Dumbledore showed up and everything changed. He arrived like he always does, calm and dangerous, and got stuck into Voldemort straight away.

Book5-chapter36_Sc3.source: The headless golden statue of the wizard in the fountain had sprung alive, leaping from its plinth, and landed on the floor with a crash between Harry and Voldemort.
Book5-chapter36_Sc3.description: The statues actually came to life to protect me. The headless golden statue threw itself between Voldemort and me and took a hit for me. I was shoved out of the way and kept safe by stone.

Book5-chapter36_Sc3.source: the other statues sprang to life too. The statue of the witch ran at Bellatrix, who screamed and sent spells streaming uselessly off its chest
Book5-chapter36_Sc3.description: More statues jumped in. One pinned Bella to the floor and her spells bounced off it. The place turned into a proper fight with stone on our side.

Book5-chapter36_Sc3.source: "It was foolish to come here tonight, Tom," said Dumbledore calmly. "The Aurors are on their way -"
Book5-chapter36_Sc3.description: Dumbledore taunted him and said the Aurors were coming. Voldemort claimed he would be gone before then, but Dumbledore was holding him off and stalling for help.

Book6-chapter3_Sc3.source: [The Wizarding community is currently under threat from an organization calling itself the Death Eaters.]
Book6-chapter3_Sc3.description: The Death Eaters are back and the whole wizarding world is on alert. That leaflet spells it out plain.

Book6-chapter3_Sc3.source: [You are advised not to leave the house alone.]
Book6-chapter3_Sc3.description: Don't go out on your own. Seriously, travelling alone is a bad idea right now.

Book6-chapter3_Sc3.source: [Unconfirmed sightings suggest that the Death Eaters may now be using Inferi (see page 10). Any sighting of an Inferius, or encounter with same, should be reported to the Ministry IMMEDIATELY.]
Book6-chapter3_Sc3.description: They're even using Inferi. That is creepy and dangerous. If you see one you report it straight away.

Book6-chapter3_Sc3.source: [Agree on security questions with close friends and family so as to detect Death Eaters masquerading as others by use of the Polyjuice Potion (see page 2).]
Book6-chapter3_Sc3.description: People can be disguised with Polyjuice. We need security questions so mates can tell if someone is an imposter.

Book6-chapter3_Sc3.source: [Should the Dark Mark appear over any dwelling place or other building, DO NOT ENTER, but contact the Auror office immediately.]
Book6-chapter3_Sc3.description: If the Dark Mark shows up over a place, do not go in. Call the Aurors. That is not the time to be brave.

Book5-chapter36_Sc2.source: "The prophecy smashed when I was trying to get Neville up the steps!"
Book5-chapter36_Sc2.description: The prophecy is gone. It smashed when I tried to get Neville up those steps so there is nothing left to fetch.

Book5-chapter36_Sc2.source: "And he knows!" said Harry with a mad laugh to match Bellatrix’s own. "Your dear old mate Voldemort knows it’s gone!"
Book5-chapter36_Sc2.description: My scar burns when Voldemort finds out something. The pain hit me hard and I knew Voldemort would know the prophecy was destroyed.

Book5-chapter36_Sc2.source: "I was and am the Dark Lord’s most loyal servant, I learned the Dark Arts from him, and I know spells of such power that you, pathetic little boy, can never hope to compete —"
Book5-chapter36_Sc2.description: Bellatrix is fanatically loyal to Voldemort and believes she has power I can't match. Hearing her made me even more sure she will do anything for him.
She tried to summon the prophecy right there in the room. She shouted a direct summoning and expected it to appear.

Book5-chapter36_Sc2.source: "What? What do you mean?" she cried, and for the first time there was fear in her voice.
Book5-chapter36_Sc2.description: Bellatrix sounded scared for the first time when I said the prophecy was smashed. That fear showed me she is terrified of Voldemort's reaction.

Book5-chapter36_Sc2.source: "Well, you’re going to have to kill me, because it’s gone!" Harry roared — and as he shouted it, pain seared across his forehead.
Book5-chapter36_Sc2.description: I was ready to die rather than give the prophecy up because it no longer existed to hand over anyway. The scar pain hit me as I said it, proving how connected I am to what Voldemort feels.

Book6-chapter3_Sc7.source: "Er — Kreacher — I want you to go to Hogwarts and work in the kitchens there with the other house-elves."
Book6-chapter3_Sc7.description: I'll put Kreacher in the Hogwarts kitchens with the other house-elves so they can keep an eye on him.

Book6-chapter3_Sc7.source: "No," said Harry at once, "he can stay with Hagrid. I think Buckbeak would prefer that."
Book6-chapter3_Sc7.description: Buckbeak is mine but I'm leaving him with Hagrid because that's where he'd be happiest.

Book6-chapter3_Sc7.source: "Incidentally, we have decided, in the interests of Buckbeak's safety, to rechristen him 'Witherwings' for the time being,"
Book6-chapter3_Sc7.description: They've renamed Buckbeak 'Witherwings' for his safety, at least for now.

Book6-chapter3_Sc7.source: "Doubtful that I would turn up?" Dumbledore suggested shrewdly.
Book6-chapter3_Sc7.description: Dumbledore thinks I might not show up somewhere important, like my trunk might not even be packed.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: If it is convenient to you, I shall call at number four, Privet Drive this coming Friday at eleven P.M. to escort you to the Burrow, where you have been invited to spend the remainder of your school holidays.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: Dumbledore's coming on Friday at eleven P.M. to take me to the Burrow. It's that simple. He invited me to spend the rest of the holidays there.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: If you are agreeable, I should also be glad of your assistance in a matter to which I hope to attend on the way to the Burrow.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: He wants my help with something on the way to the Burrow. No idea what yet, but he expects me to come along and help.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: Kindly send your answer by return of this owl.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: Dumbledore told me to send my answer back by owl. I already sent a 'yes' as he asked.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: Harry had read this letter so often since its arrival three days ago that although it had been delivered in a tightly furled scroll, it now lay quite flat.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: I've been staring at this letter non-stop for three days. I know every word by heart and I keep checking the window to see if he turns up.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: Either Dumbledore was going to come, or he was not.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: I can't do anything about it now; either he shows up or he doesn't. Waiting is pointless, but I can't stop watching for him.

Book6-chapter3_Sc4.source: An alarm clock, repaired by Harry several years ago, ticked loudly on the sill, showing one minute to eleven.
Book6-chapter3_Sc4.description: I've still got that alarm clock I fixed years ago. It's ticking away and it's nearly eleven, which makes me even more on edge.
I haven't packed a thing. I kept thinking I'd panic and get ready, but I just sat by the window instead.

Book6-chapter3_Sc6.source: "Sirius’s will was discovered a week ago and that he left you everything he owned."
Book6-chapter3_Sc6.description: Sirius left me everything he owned. I have his money at Gringotts and whatever personal things he had.

Book6-chapter3_Sc6.source: "Sirius also left you number twelve, Grimmauld Place."
Book6-chapter3_Sc6.description: Sirius left me number twelve, Grimmauld Place. I own the house now whether I like it or not.

Book6-chapter3_Sc6.source: "Kreacher belongs to Miss Bellatrix, oh yes, Kreacher belongs to the Blacks, Kreacher wants his new mistress, Kreacher won’t go to the Potter brat, Kreacher won’t, won’t, won’t -"
Book6-chapter3_Sc6.description: Kreacher is tied up in the Black family and Bellatrix thinks he should belong to her. He is hostile and refuses to come to me.

Book6-chapter3_Sc6.source: "Well, that simplifies matters," said Dumbledore cheerfully. "It seems that Sirius knew what he was doing. You are the rightful owner of number twelve, Grimmauld Place and of Kreacher."
Book6-chapter3_Sc6.description: I am the rightful owner of Grimmauld Place and of Kreacher. I hate the idea of owning Kreacher. I don't want him after what he did, but legally he belongs to me.

Book6-chapter3_Sc6.source: "It might be that Bellatrix will arrive on the doorstep at any moment."
Book6-chapter3_Sc6.description: If the house is enchanted to stay in the Black line then Bellatrix could try to claim it. That's dangerous and I do not want her getting hold of Grimmauld Place.

Book6-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Hello, Professor," she said. "Wotcher, Harry." "Hi, Tonks." Harry thought she looked drawn, even ill, and there was something forced in her smile.
Book6-chapter5_Sc1.description: Tonks looks drawn and ill. She tried to act normal but I can tell something's off with her.

Book6-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Yes, Rufus Scrimgeour has set up several new offices in response to the present situation, and Arthur’s heading the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects."
Book6-chapter5_Sc1.description: Arthur is running a new office that busts dodgy so-called protective products. He's dealing with fake protections and cursed junk.

Book6-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Some idiot’s started selling Metamorph-Medals. Just sling them around your neck and you’ll be able to change your appearance at will. A hundred thousand disguises, all for ten Galleons!" "Mostly you just turn a fairly unpleasant orange color, but a couple of people have also sprouted tentaclelike warts all over their bodies."
Book6-chapter5_Sc1.description: People are selling dangerous fake items like Metamorph-Medals that don't work and can make you orange or give you horrible warts.

Book6-chapter5_Sc1.source: She pointed at the clock’s face. Mr Weasley’s hand had switched to "traveling." "He’s coming!"
Book6-chapter5_Sc1.description: The Weasley clock shows people in mortal peril and it just told us Dad was traveling, so he's on his way back.
Dumbledore brought me to the Burrow late at night. He still looks out for me and comes when needed.

Book6-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Every single one of its nine hands was now pointing at 'mortal peril.' ... 'It’s been like that for a while now,' said Mrs Weasley, in an unconvincingly casual voice, 'ever since You-Know-Who came back into the open.'"
Book6-chapter5_Sc1.description: Everyone is more at risk now that You-Know-Who is back. The danger isn't just rumor, it feels real and constant.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Let — let the others go, and I’ll give it to you!" said Harry desperately.
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: I will do anything to protect the others. If giving up something matters to keep them alive, I will try to do it.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "The prophecy was hot with the heat from his clutching hand as he held it out."
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: The prophecy is real and it's physically hot in my hand. It's important and dangerous in more ways than one.
When Sirius went through that veil I believed I could pull him back. I lunged for him because I refused to accept he was gone.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "There’s nothing you can do, Harry . . ." "He’s gone."
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: I trusted Lupin to be honest with me. When he held me back and told me Sirius was gone I had to face the terrible truth. I feel helpless and furious.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "He was laughing at her. 'Come on, you can do better than that!' he yelled... The second jet of light hit him squarely on the chest."
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: Sirius was brave and reckless to the end. I used to think he'd always get away with it. That is no longer something I can rely on.

Book5-chapter31_Sc2.description: I can summon a Patronus in front of examiners. I did it on purpose to put Umbridge in her place and it worked, the stag came out and everyone noticed.

Book5-chapter31_Sc2.source: "An owl will be sent to you some time in July," said Professor McGonagall.
Book5-chapter31_Sc2.description: So the O.W.L. results arrive by owl in July. At least I'll have one piece of mail to expect at Privet Drive next summer.

Book5-chapter31_Sc2.source: "Why don’t you just do it yourself?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc2.description: Hermione's panic about the exam answers is getting on my nerves. I told her to stop fussing and just do it herself because I don't want to be nagged while we're trying to revise.

Book5-chapter36_Sc4.source: If death is nothing, Dumbledore, kill the boy
Book5-chapter36_Sc4.description: I'm being possessed right now. Something with red eyes has me locked in its coils and it can make me speak with my own mouth. The pain is insane and I cannot separate myself from it.
Dumbledore can sound afraid. I thought he was unshakable but when he shouted at me he actually sounded frightened.

Book5-chapter36_Sc4.source: Fawkes swooped down in front of Dumbledore, opened his beak wide, and swallowed the jet of green light whole. He burst into flame and fell to the floor, small, wrinkled, and flightless
Book5-chapter36_Sc4.description: Fawkes will throw himself between Dumbledore and a killing curse. He took that blast to save Dumbledore and was reduced to a tiny, burned form.
When the pain becomes too much I want it to end. If death would stop this, I would beg for it without thinking. I don't want to keep being used like this.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: They want that prophecy more than anything. I am holding something they will do anything to get.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.source: “About both of you, Potter, about both of you . . .”
Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: There is a prophecy about me and Voldemort. That could be why my parents died and why I have this scar.
I believed Sirius might be here with them. I led my friends into this because I thought I had him nearby.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.source: “You’ll have to smash this if you want to attack any of us,”
Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: I will protect my friends no matter what. If anyone wants to hurt them they will have to get past me first.
If I make a move at the right moment we can create a chance to get out. I can lead them to run and smash the shelves to cover our escape.

Book5-chapter36_Sc5.source: Death is nothing compared to this. . . . And I’ll see Sirius again. . . .
Book5-chapter36_Sc5.description: I thought about death and then I thought about Sirius and I kept telling myself I will see him again. I wanted that more than anything.

Book5-chapter36_Sc5.source: He was there! ... it was You-Know-Who, he grabbed a woman and Disapparated!
Book5-chapter36_Sc5.description: I saw him with my own eyes. Voldemort was here, he grabbed someone and Disapparated. He is back.

Book5-chapter36_Sc5.source: you will find several escaped Death Eaters contained in the Death Chamber, bound by an Anti-Disapparation Jinx
Book5-chapter36_Sc5.description: There are Death Eaters trapped downstairs in the Death Chamber and they are being held by an Anti-Disapparation Jinx.

Book5-chapter36_Sc5.source: I shall explain everything, when Harry is back at school.
Book5-chapter36_Sc5.description: Dumbledore is taking responsibility for explaining what happened and wants me back at Hogwarts before anyone else gets the full story.

Book5-chapter36_Sc5.source: You will give the order to remove Dolores Umbridge from Hogwarts
Book5-chapter36_Sc5.description: Dumbledore told Fudge to get Umbridge removed from Hogwarts. That means things might change at school.
Dumbledore gave me a Portkey to get me back to Hogwarts fast. I just had to touch it and go.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "I thought it would be burning all the time now Voldemort’s getting so powerful again."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: My scar should hurt when Voldemort gets stronger, but it is not burning now and that worries me.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "It appears that he is now employing Occlumency against you."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: So Voldemort is using Occlumency to block my access to his thoughts. That explains why I am not getting constant flashes.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "We are here to persuade an old colleague of mine to come out of retirement and return to Hogwarts."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: Dumbledore brought me along to try to persuade a retired teacher to come back to Hogwarts. I am supposed to be useful for that.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "You have not asked me, for instance, what is my favorite flavor of jam, to check that I am indeed Professor Dumbledore and not an impostor."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: Dumbledore thinks checking jam preference is a clever way to tell if someone is an impostor. His favorite jam is raspberry.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "They are corpses," said Dumbledore calmly. "Dead bodies that have been bewitched to do a Dark wizard’s bidding."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: Inferi are bewitched corpses used by Dark wizards. That is terrifying.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "There was no need to stick the wand in that hard," he said gruffly, clambering to his feet. "It hurt."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: I expected the house to contain a corpse or someone dead, but Horace was hiding by pretending to be an armchair. I couldn't believe it.

Book6-chapter4_Sc1.source: "This, said Dumbledore, moving forward to make the introduction, is Harry Potter. Harry, this is an old friend and colleague of mine, Horace Slughorn."
Book6-chapter4_Sc1.description: Dumbledore introduced me to Horace Slughorn. Horace is an old colleague of Dumbledore and he noticed my scar right away.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: I felt sorry for Luna. She gets picked on, but she says things like they will sort themselves out and I didn't mind her talking about Sirius.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "That man the Death Eaters killed was your godfather, wasn’t he? Ginny told me."
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Sirius is dead. He was my godfather. It still hits me and everything I wanted before feels like it belongs to another life.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "Oh, come on. You heard them, just behind the veil, didn’t you?"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Luna believes she heard voices behind the veil and because I thought I heard something too, I can't dismiss her as completely mad.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "The food trolley’s just stopped if you want anything"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: I bought a massive pile of Cauldron Cakes and Pumpkin Pasties on the train. Sweet stuff helps pass the time.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "Hey, Harry," said Ron, nodding toward the glass window onto the corridor."
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Cho and Marietta were on the corridor and Cho and I caught each other's eye. It felt like that part of my life is fading away.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "we thought we might have a little chat with your aunt and uncle before letting them take you home."
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Moody, Tonks, Lupin and the Weasleys were waiting at King’s Cross to meet the Dursleys. They plan to have words with my aunt and uncle before I go with them.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "When the ticket inspector signaled to him, Ron, and Hermione that it was safe to walk through the magical barrier between platforms nine and ten, however, he found a surprise awaiting him on the other side"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: I thought leaving the train would be miserable, but seeing everyone there made me feel better. I even toyed with the idea of never getting off, but that was nonsense.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: The Wizarding community is currently under threat from an organization calling itself the Death Eaters.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: The whole wizarding world is under threat from the Death Eaters. That's the situation and we can't ignore it.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: You are advised not to leave the house alone.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: Don't go out alone. I need to be careful and not wander off by myself.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Particular care should be taken during the hours of darkness. Wherever possible, arrange to complete journeys before night has fallen.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: Night is when it's worst. I should try to get anywhere important done before dark.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Review the security arrangements around your house, making sure that all family members are aware of emergency measures such as Shield and Disillusionment Charms, and, in the case of underage family members, Side-Along-Apparition.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: I need to check the protective spells around where I stay. Shield and Disillusionment Charms matter, and underage folks might need Side Along Apparition if things go wrong.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Agree on security questions with close friends and family so as to detect Death Eaters masquerading as others by use of the Polyjuice Potion (see page 2).
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: People could be using Polyjuice to pretend to be someone else. We should set up security questions so we can tell who's who.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Should you feel that a family member, colleague, friend, or neighbor is acting in a strange manner, contact the Magical Law Enforcement Squad at once. They may have been put under the Imperius Curse (see page 4).
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: If someone is acting weird, they might be under the Imperius Curse. I should get the Magical Law Enforcement Squad involved straight away.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Should the Dark Mark appear over any dwelling place or other building, DO NOT ENTER, but contact the Auror office immediately.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: If I see the Dark Mark over a place, I am not going in. Contact the Aurors and stay away.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Unconfirmed sightings suggest that the Death Eaters may now be using Inferi (see page 10).
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: There are reports the Death Eaters might be using Inferi. That is seriously dangerous and changes how we deal with attacks.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: A large trunk stood in the very middle of the room. Its lid was open; it looked expectant; yet it was almost empty but for a residue of old underwear, sweets, empty ink bottles, and broken quills that coated the very bottom.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: The trunk's mostly empty apart from rubbish and old things. There's nothing important packed up there right now.

Book6-chapter3_Sc2.source: Her amber eyes surveyed the room imperiously, her head swiveling occasionally to gaze at her snoring master.
Book6-chapter3_Sc2.description: Owls are on alert for me even when I'm out cold. I can rely on them to keep watch a bit.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'He\'s \u2018the Boy Who Lived\u2019 again now, though, isn\'t he?'
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: They\'re calling me the Boy Who Lived again. Great, more attention I did not ask for.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'The dementors have left Azkaban,' said Malfoy quietly.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: The dementors have abandoned Azkaban. That means a lot of Death Eaters, including my dad\'s lot, could be out soon.
Malfoy hates me more than ever and is out for revenge. He threatened me and I don\'t trust him a bit.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'I knew Sirius longer 'n you did. . . . He died in battle, an' tha's the way he'd've wanted ter go.'
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Hagrid thinks Sirius died fighting. I can hear how badly that hurts him, but I am not ready to accept that without knowing for certain.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'It is with great regret that I must confirm that the wizard styling himself Lord ... is alive and among us again,' said Fudge.
