Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: The Ministry has finally admitted Voldemort is back. That changes everything. We are not safe and people must be on guard.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I am undoubtedly slower than I was. But on the other hand . . ." He shrugged and spread his hands wide, as though to say that age had its compensations, and Harry noticed a ring on his uninjured hand that he had never seen Dumbledore wear before: It was large, rather clumsily made of what looked like gold, and was set with a heavy black stone that had cracked down the middle.
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: Dumbledore's wearing a big clumsy gold ring with a cracked black stone. He's slower now and his fingers are burned, but he still carries himself like he knows what he's doing.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I haven’t given them the chance. I’ve been on the move for a year. Never stay in one place more than a week. Move from Muggle house to Muggle house — the owners of this place are on holiday in the Canary Islands — it’s been very pleasant, I’ll be sorry to leave. It’s quite easy once you know how, one simple Freezing Charm on these absurd burglar alarms they use instead of Sneakoscopes and make sure the neighbors don’t spot you bringing in the piano."
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: Slughorn's been hiding for about a year, living in Muggle houses, using tricks like Freezing Charms on alarm systems so he won't get caught. He's trying to stay off the Death Eaters' radar.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "What would the Death Eaters want with a poor broken-down old buffer like me?" demanded Slughorn. "I imagine that they would want you to turn your considerable talents to coercion, torture, and murder," said Dumbledore.
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: Dumbledore thinks the Death Eaters would try to recruit Slughorn for nasty work, and Slughorn's clearly worried enough to keep moving instead of staying put.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "You look very like your father." ... "Except for your eyes. You’ve got —" "My mother’s eyes, yeah." ... "Yes, well. You shouldn’t have favorites as a teacher, of course, but she was one of mine. Your mother," Slughorn added, in answer to Harry’s questioning look. "Lily Evans. One of the brightest I ever taught. Vivacious, you know. Charming girl. I used to tell her she ought to have been in my House."
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: Slughorn remembers my mother, Lily, and he liked her a lot. He still talks about her as one of his favorites, so I know he has a soft spot for her and for me because of her.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "I was Head of Slytherin," said Slughorn.
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: Slughorn used to be Head of Slytherin. He collects ex-students and tries to keep ties with powerful people.

Book6-chapter4_Sc2.source: "If that’s how you treat teachers these days —" "Professor Umbridge ran afoul of our centaur herd," said Dumbledore. "I think you, Horace, would have known better than to stride into the forest and call a horde of angry centaurs ‘filthy half-breeds.’"
Book6-chapter4_Sc2.description: I still hate Umbridge, but hearing Dumbledore say she walked into trouble with the centaurs makes me feel she deserved the mess she got herself into.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [Of course not, I have been out of touch with everybody for a year.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: He says he's been out of touch for a year so I can't assume everyone knows where he is.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [He will undoubtedly try to collect you, Harry. You would be the jewel of his collection; 'the Boy Who Lived' . . . or, as they call you these days, 'the Chosen One.']
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: Slughorn will try to collect me. I am a prize to him because of what people call me.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [I think it is time that I took a greater hand in your education.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wants to give me private lessons this year.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [I hope you will forgive me for mentioning it, Harry, but I am pleased and a little proud at how well you seem to be coping after everything that happened at the Ministry.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: Dumbledore thinks I'm coping and is proud of me. That matters.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [Professor Snape, Harry — and no, you will not.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: I do not have to do Occlumency with Snape now.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [I wish you to keep your Invisibility Cloak with you at all times from this moment onward. Even within Hogwarts itself. Just in case, you understand me?]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: Dumbledore told me to keep my Invisibility Cloak on me at all times, even at Hogwarts.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [the Burrow has been given the highest security the Ministry of Magic can provide.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: The Ministry has given the Burrow top security while I'm staying there so they are watching my post and protecting the place.

Book6-chapter4_Sc3.source: [If it is, I’ll make sure I take as many Death Eaters with me as I can, and Voldemort too if I can manage it.]
Book6-chapter4_Sc3.description: Losing Sirius made me determined. If I die, I will take as many Death Eaters down with me as I can.

Book6-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Dunno," said Harry, thinking hard. "He wants something mended . . . and he wants to reserve something in there. . . . Could you see what he pointed at when he said 'that one'?"
Book6-chapter6_Sc8.description: He wants something fixed and he wants to put something aside in the shop. I couldn't see what he meant because he was behind that cabinet.

Book5-chapter38_Sc2.source: "This is a two-way mirror. I’ve got the other. If you need to speak to me, just say my name into it; you’ll appear in my mirror and I’ll be able to talk in yours."
Book5-chapter38_Sc2.description: I've got a two way mirror from Sirius. If I say his name into it he should be able to talk to me through it. I have to try now.

Book5-chapter38_Sc2.source: "He was never one ter sit around at home an’ let other people do the fightin’."
Book5-chapter38_Sc2.description: Sirius wouldn't have just stayed at home and let others fight. He would go help if he could.
Nick says Sirius will not come back as a ghost. I don't want to accept that, but I have to face that he might really be gone.

Book5-chapter38_Sc2.source: "I’ve got to go and visit Ron and Hermione in the hospital wing,"
Book5-chapter38_Sc2.description: I need to go see Ron and Hermione in the hospital wing. They're injured and I have to look after them.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "He looks a bit like a walrus, and he used to be Head of Slytherin," said Harry.
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Slughorn might be the new teacher. He looks a bit like a walrus and used to be Head of Slytherin. Can't be worse than Umbridge, surely.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Bill and I are going to be married!"
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Bill and Fleur are engaged. Right now Mrs Weasley and everyone are skirting around the subject so I only just found out.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Same as usual," said Harry, "they didn’t talk to me much, but I like it better that way."
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Being at the Dursleys is unsurprising. I still get treated like a Muggle oddity and honestly I prefer it when they keep their distance.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Eet was no trouble," said Fleur Delacour, setting the tray across Harry’s knees and then swooping to kiss him on each cheek.
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Fleur is being very forward and friendly with the family. She kissed me on both cheeks and seems keen to impress.
I was woken by a racket and Ron bursting in. He always makes an entrance like that and I should expect no less.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: I got made Quidditch Captain. Right now that just means more responsibility and people expect me to pull the team together.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “There have been another couple of dementor attacks,” he announced
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Dementors are attacking again. That's awful and it makes everything feel ten times worse.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “And they’ve found Igor Karkaroff’s body in a shack up north. The Dark Mark had been set over it — well, frankly, I’m surprised he stayed alive for even a year after deserting the Death Eaters; Sirius’s brother, Regulus, only managed a few days as far as I can remember.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Karkaroff is dead and the Dark Mark was over him. People who turn on the Death Eaters get killed fast.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “Did you hear about Florean Fortescue, Remus?” asked Bill... “Dragged off, by the look of his place.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Florean Fortescue has been dragged off from his ice-cream shop. He used to give me free ice creams. That's awful and I want to know who did it.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “Talking of Diagon Alley,” said Mr Weasley, “looks like Ollivander’s gone too.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Ollivander's wand shop is empty. If the wandmaker's gone, that's terrifying for everyone who relies on wands and for Diagon Alley.

Book6-chapter8_Sc1.description: Malfoy did it. He was the one who got me.
She fixed my nose with a quick spell. It went hot then cold and now it's mended.
Tonks helped me get off the train, handed my cloak back and healed me without fuss. I owe her one; she's useful and calm when it matters.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Malfoy’s not doing prefect duty. He’s just sitting in his compartment with the other Slytherins, we saw him when we passed.
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Malfoy wasn't out bullying first years. He's sitting with the other Slytherins instead. That looks like he's got something else on his mind.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Maybe he preferred the Inquisitorial Squad
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Maybe Malfoy thinks being in the Inquisitorial Squad is more important than being a prefect. That would explain why he skipped duty.
I'm going to follow Zabini and slip into the Slytherin compartment under the Invisibility Cloak. I want to find out what Malfoy is up to.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: He saw me hex Zacharias Smith
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Ginny got noticed by Slughorn because she hexed Zacharias. I respect her for standing up to idiots like him.

Book6-chapter6_Sc6.source: "I’m to wait for you, any idea how long you’ll be?"
Book6-chapter6_Sc6.description: If I'm hiding, the Cloak has to do. Dumbledore trusts this thing, so I'm trusting it too. Ministry or not, the Cloak will have to be enough.
When it matters I take charge. Pull the Cloak out and move now, no faffing around.
Malfoy slipped off toward Knockturn Alley. We have to follow him, now, before he vanishes.
I can't hang about. If I want to catch him I have to push everyone, hurry up and keep going.

Book6-chapter6_Sc7.source: There in the midst of the cases full of skulls and old bottles stood Draco Malfoy with his back to them, just visible beyond the very same large black cabinet in which Harry had once hidden to avoid Malfoy and his father.
Book6-chapter6_Sc7.description: He's in Borgin and Burkes. Malfoy is actually in there, right where I used to hide.

Book6-chapter6_Sc7.source: They peered into windows as they passed, but none of the shops seemed to have any customers at all.
Book6-chapter6_Sc7.description: Buying Dark artifacts is something people try to hide now. If you're seen around places like this, it's a giveaway.

Book6-chapter6_Sc2.source: "Wow . . . look at that . . . he’s not here now! So why not have a go? They might be able to find you a double cell in Azkaban with your loser of a husband!"
Book6-chapter6_Sc2.description: I'm not stepping back just because Dumbledore's not here. If they want to try anything, fine. I'm ready to stand up to them.

Book6-chapter6_Sc2.source: Harry did not lower his wand. "Harry, no!" moaned Hermione, grabbing his arm and attempting to push it down by his side.
Book6-chapter6_Sc2.description: I keep my wand up. I won't let them intimidate me into doing nothing, even if people tell me I'll get in trouble.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: They've put me on top-grade security. Fine. I'm being watched and protected now.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.source: Harry choked over his cornflakes, and Ron thumped him on the back.
Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: I choked on my cereal and Ron smacked me on the back. He's a prat but he'll bash me if I choke and he'd do the same for me.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Was that a Patronus?" asked Harry, who had seen Dumbledore send messages like this.
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: That was a Patronus. Someone just sent a Patronus message to the castle.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: "I’m stationed in Hogsmeade now, to give the school extra protection," said Tonks.
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: Tonks is posted in Hogsmeade to help protect Hogwarts.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: "No, Proudfoot, Savage, and Dawlish are here too."
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: She’s not alone. Proudfoot, Savage, and Dawlish are also stationed up there.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Dawlish, that Auror Dumbledore attacked last year?" "That’s right."
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: Dawlish is the Auror Dumbledore attacked last year. He’s one of the ones on duty at Hogsmeade.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: Last year she had been inquisitive (to the point of being a little annoying at times), she had laughed easily, she had made jokes. Now she seemed older and much more serious and purposeful.
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: Tonks used to be flippant and jokey, but she’s different now. She looks older and much more serious since the Ministry business.

Book6-chapter8_Sc2.source: He reflected uncomfortably that Hermione would have suggested he say something consoling about Sirius to her, that it hadn’t been her fault at all, but he couldn’t bring himself to do it.
Book6-chapter8_Sc2.description: I know Hermione would tell me to comfort Tonks about Sirius, and that it wasn't her fault, but I just can't bring myself to talk about Sirius right now.

Book6-chapter8_Sc5.description: I thanked her for everything and said good night as I walked up to the school with Snape.
My face was covered in blood. I grabbed a spoon, scrubbed at it and felt gross until Hermione cleaned it off.
I shut down the questions and decided to keep quiet for now because I wanted to deal with it myself.

Book6-chapter7_Sc2.source: ["I think he’s replaced his father as a Death Eater."]
Book6-chapter7_Sc2.description: I reckon Malfoy might've taken his father's place among the Death Eaters and that means whatever he's after at Borgin could be proper Dark and dangerous. We should look into it.

Book6-chapter7_Sc2.source: ["You see, when Lucius Malfoy was arrested, we raided his house. We took away everything that might have been dangerous."]
Book6-chapter7_Sc2.description: Mr Weasley says they searched Lucius's home and confiscated anything dangerous, so if something was still needed from Borgin then maybe it's something tricky or new.

Book6-chapter7_Sc2.source: [He felt a strange twinge of annoyance as she walked away, her long red hair dancing behind her; he had become so used to her presence over the summer that he had almost forgotten that Ginny did not hang around with him, Ron, and Hermione while at school.]
Book6-chapter7_Sc2.description: Ginny's not going to stick with me at school the whole time and yeah, it annoys me a bit. I got used to her being around over the summer and it stings when she walks off to meet Dean.

Book6-chapter7_Sc2.source: ["They’re staring at you because you were at the Ministry too," said Harry...]
Book6-chapter7_Sc2.description: People are staring because of the Ministry story and the Prophet garbage. Neville and Luna sticking with me means they've been with me through all of it, and I actually think they're good company.

Book6-chapter7_Sc2.source: ["We didn’t face him, though," said Neville, emerging from under the seat...]
Book6-chapter7_Sc2.description: I kept thinking that Voldemort might've targeted Neville instead of me. The prophecy could've meant him, and if he'd been chosen then he'd be bearing the scar and the whole burden. That stuff about mothers dying to save their kids makes me think Lily's sacrifice is why I'm the one now.

Book6-chapter8_Sc3.source: "Alohomora!" he said confidently, pointing his wand at the padlock, but nothing happened.
Book6-chapter8_Sc3.description: I tried "Alohomora" on the gate and it did nothing. Great, so I can't just charm my way in.

Book6-chapter8_Sc3.source: "That won't work on these," said Tonks. "Dumbledore bewitched them himself."
Book6-chapter8_Sc3.description: Tonks told me the gates were bewitched by Dumbledore himself. So they're specially locked down.

Book6-chapter8_Sc3.source: "No, you couldn't," said Tonks flatly. "Anti-intruder jinxes on all of them. Security's been tightened a hundredfold this summer."
Book6-chapter8_Sc3.description: There are anti-intruder jinxes on the walls and security has been cranked up a hundredfold. Climbing's not an option.

Book6-chapter8_Sc3.source: "I could climb a wall," he suggested. "No, you couldn't," said Tonks flatly.
Book6-chapter8_Sc3.description: I thought maybe I could sneak in by climbing, but clearly that's impossible now. So my usual impulse to try something simple won't work.

Book6-chapter8_Sc3.source: He was cold, he was hungry, and he was quite keen to leave this new, gloomy Tonks behind.
Book6-chapter8_Sc3.description: I'm cold, hungry, and fed up with having to deal with a gloomy Tonks. I just want to get inside.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "He’s a Death Eater," said Harry slowly. "He’s replaced his father as a Death Eater!"
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: I reckon Malfoy might already be one of them. I can't shake the feeling he's up to something dangerous and I think we should take it seriously.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "In Madam Malkin’s. She didn’t touch him, but he yelled and jerked his arm away from her when she went to roll up his sleeve. It was his left arm. He’s been branded with the Dark Mark."
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Madam Malkin tried to touch his left arm and he jumped like he'd been burned. I'm sure he's been branded with the Dark Mark.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "He went into Borgin and Burkes," said Harry, "and started bullying the bloke in there, Borgin, to help him fix something. And he said he wanted Borgin to keep something else for him."
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Malfoy went into Borgin and Burkes and was forcing Borgin to fix something and to keep another thing for him. They seem connected.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Malfoy’s father’s in Azkaban. Don’t you think Malfoy’d like revenge?"
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Because his father is in Azkaban, I think Malfoy might want revenge and that could explain why he's acting so dangerous.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "When we were in Diagon Alley," Harry began, but Mr. Weasley forestalled him with a grimace. "Am I about to discover where you, Ron, and Hermione disappeared to while you were supposed to be in the back room of Fred and George’s shop?"
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: I followed Malfoy because I genuinely thought he was up to something, and I wasn't just being nosy.

Book6-chapter8_Sc6.source: [He hoped very much that they would all assume he had been involved in something heroic, preferably involving a couple of Death Eaters and a dementor.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc6.description: I wanted everyone to think I did something brave, like took on Death Eaters and a dementor. That would keep people guessing and make Malfoy look ridiculous.
Has Dumbledore brought up Voldemort yet? He always saves the proper speech for after the feast so it can't be long.
I missed the Sorting. That was obvious to Hermione and I missed it, so I don't know what happened there.

Book6-chapter8_Sc4.source: “I couldn’t change, I didn’t have my —” Harry began, but Snape cut across him.
Book6-chapter8_Sc4.description: I couldn't change into my robes in time. I tried to explain it straight away because I knew he'd jump on it.

Book6-chapter8_Sc4.source: “Well, well, well,” sneered Snape, taking out his wand and tapping the padlock once, so that the chains snaked backward and the gates creaked open. “Nice of you to turn up, Potter, although you have evidently decided that the wearing of school robes would detract from your appearance.”
Book6-chapter8_Sc4.description: Snape is openly hostile and sneering at me as always. He delights in putting me down and I loathe him for it.

Book6-chapter8_Sc4.source: “There is no need to wait, Nymphadora, Potter is quite — ah — safe in my hands.”
Book6-chapter8_Sc4.description: Snape says I'm 'safe in his hands' but that sounds like a putdown, not protection. I still don't trust him.

Book6-chapter3_Sc5.description: We need to get out of here now. I'm tense and ready to go, not hanging about while Vernon fumes.

Book6-chapter3_Sc5.source: "the minute hand on the alarm clock reached the number twelve and, at that precise moment, the streetlamp outside the window went out"
Book6-chapter3_Sc5.description: Something strange happens at midnight. I woke up as if someone switched the world off, and I react fast when odd things happen.

Book6-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Who the blazes is calling at this time of night?"
Book6-chapter3_Sc5.description: I know Vernon panics and gets loud at anything unusual. I can't rely on him to act calmly or help me.

Book6-chapter3_Sc5.source: "He had completely forgotten to warn the Dursleys that Dumbledore might be coming."
Book6-chapter3_Sc5.description: I messed up by not warning them. I get panicky and do stupid, hurried things when I think trouble is about to happen.

Book6-chapter3_Sc5.source: "as long experience had taught him to remain out of arm’s reach of his uncle whenever possible."
Book6-chapter3_Sc5.description: I keep my distance from Vernon. Years of being pushed around have taught me to stay out of his reach and avoid confrontation.

Book6-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Dumbledore uses that name," said Harry stubbornly.
Book6-chapter8_Sc9.description: If Dumbledore says the name, then I'm going to say it too. I won't stop just because others want me to.

Book6-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Got held up on the train," said Harry.
Book6-chapter8_Sc9.description: I was late because I got held up on the train.

Book6-chapter8_Sc9.source: "Oh yeah, he’s really come on," said Hagrid proudly. "Yeh’ll be amazed. I’m thinkin’ o’ trainin’ him up as me assistant."
Book6-chapter8_Sc9.description: Grawp's better than I expected. I don't want to admit it to Ron, but Hagrid thinks Grawp's improved loads.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Hagrid was only a few minutes late," said Hermione. "Look, he’s waving at you, Harry."
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Hagrid's looking out for me and he still gets excited to see me. I smiled and waved back because he cares, plain and simple.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Having always considered her a bit of a fraud, Harry had been shocked to discover at the end of the previous term that it had been she who had made the prediction that caused Lord Voldemort to kill Harry’s parents and attack Harry himself."
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: I used to think Trelawney was a joke, but she actually made that prophecy about my parents and me. I don't like being near her, and I'm not taking Divination this year.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "So what did Professor Slughorn want?" Hermione asked. "To know what really happened at the Ministry," said Harry.
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Professor Slughorn wanted to know what happened at the Ministry. Everyone's been asking about it and trying to pin down the full story.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Draco Malfoy was miming the shattering of a nose to raucous laughter and applause."
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Malfoy getting away with mocking me just digs at me. I want to sort him out one-on-one more than anything right now.

Book6-chapter10_Sc2.source: "No matter, Harry —" Dumbledore pointed his wand at the bottle and the cork flew out.
Book6-chapter10_Sc2.description: Dumbledore hurt his hand. His fingers are blackened and he was having trouble with the stopper, so he is injured and it looks nasty.

Book6-chapter10_Sc2.source: "You understand him, I'm sure, Harry?" "Yes, of course," said Harry.
Book6-chapter10_Sc2.description: I can speak Parseltongue. I heard that man speak and suddenly I could follow him, which was weird and a bit sickening when I thought about snakes.
Merope survived the attack at the cottage. She did not die in that scene.
Merope Gaunt was Voldemort's mother. That hits hard and makes everything about him even darker.

Book6-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Yes, that was Tom Riddle senior, the handsome Muggle who used to go riding past the Gaunt cottage"
Book6-chapter10_Sc2.description: Tom Riddle senior is Voldemort's father and he was a Muggle who rode past the Gaunts. I can picture him on a horse, totally ordinary.

Book6-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Personally, I am inclined to think that she used a love potion."
Book6-chapter10_Sc2.description: It makes sense that Merope probably used a love potion on Tom Riddle. It explains how a Muggle ended up married to her when everything else seems impossible.

Book6-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Morfin, who already had a record of Muggle attacks, was sentenced to three years in Azkaban. Marvolo... received six months."
Book6-chapter10_Sc2.description: Morfin and Marvolo were convicted. Morfin got three years in Azkaban and Marvolo got six months, so the whole Gaunt family was punished and taken away.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [His hand was like that when I saw him over the summer,]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Dumbledore's hand is still injured. It's not healed and Madam Pomfrey hasn't fixed it.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [Professor Snape, meanwhile, will be taking over the position of Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Snape has been given the Defense Against the Dark Arts job. I can't believe they'd give him that after everything.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [Well, there's one good thing, Snape'll be gone by the end of the year.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: I want Snape gone by the end of the year. I hate him and I'm sure he'd be happy if he didn't stick around.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [But you said —] [Professor Snape, meanwhile, will be taking over the position of Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: I thought Slughorn was going to teach Defense Against the Dark Arts, but I must have been mistaken because Snape got it.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Perhaps, besotted as she was, she had convinced herself that he would by now have fallen in love with her in return. Perhaps she thought he would stay for the baby’s sake. If so, she was wrong on both counts. He left her, never saw her again, and never troubled to discover what became of his son."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: Merope stopped using the love potion and Tom Riddle left her while she was still pregnant. He never came back or looked for his son.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Within a few months of their runaway marriage, Tom Riddle reappeared at the manor house in Little Hangleton without his wife."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: Tom Riddle returned to Little Hangleton alone after the marriage. Merope was gone.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Yes, indeed," said Dumbledore. "We must do a certain amount of guessing here, although I do not think it is difficult to deduce what happened."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: A lot of this is deduction, but it all points the same way. Voldemort's early life needs some piecing together.
Merope did give birth to Tom Riddle's child. That child ended up growing up without his parents.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Yes, indeed," said Dumbledore. "We must do a certain amount of guessing here, although I do not think it is difficult to deduce what happened. You see, within a few months of their runaway marriage, Tom Riddle reappeared at the manor house in Little Hangleton without his wife."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: Voldemort was brought up in an orphanage after Merope's death. He did not have a father who knew him.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "It has everything to do with the prophecy."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: Dumbledore says Voldemort's past is directly connected to the prophecy. This is not just gossip, it matters to why I'm involved.

Book6-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Yes, I think Mr. Weasley and Miss Granger have proved themselves trustworthy. But Harry, I am going to ask you to ask them not to repeat any of this to anybody else."
Book6-chapter10_Sc3.description: Dumbledore told me I can tell Ron and Hermione what I now know. They are trustworthy, but I must make them promise to keep it to themselves.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: There’s no need to call me ‘sir,’ Professor.
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: I snapped at Snape. Calling him ‘sir’ felt wrong and I wasn’t going to take his cheek quietly. That got me detention.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: Do you remember me telling you we are practicing nonverbal spells, Potter?
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: I can cast a Shield Charm without thinking, even when I'm caught off guard. I blasted Snape across a desk with Protego when he aimed at me.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: He loves them! All that unfixed, indestructible stuff
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: Snape doesn’t just teach the Dark Arts. He likes them. That makes me uneasy.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: Professor Slughorn, however, is perfectly happy to accept N.E.W.T. students with ‘Exceeds Expectations’ at O.W.L. Do you wish to proceed with Potions?
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: I don’t need an Outstanding to continue Potions because Slughorn will accept Exceeds Expectations. I also haven’t bought any books or ingredients yet so I’ll have to borrow some.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: Oh, by the way — twenty hopefuls have already put down their names for the Gryffindor Quidditch team. I shall pass the list to you in due course and you can fix up trials at your leisure.
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: I’m the Captain now and people expect me to run trials. I told Ron he didn’t need to try out because I’d watched him play for years, but I know I have to be fair and not favour mates.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Praying that this was the counter-jinx, Harry thought Liberacorpus!"
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: I shouted Liberacorpus to get Ron down. I used the counter-jinx from that old potion book and it worked.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "My dad used this spell," said Harry.
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: I told them my dad used the spell. Truth is, I saw my dad do it on Snape and I kept quiet about that. Now I'm thinking maybe the Half-Blood Prince could be connected to my dad. Could be, right?

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "It was a laugh!" said Ron, upending a ketchup bottle over his sausages.
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: I defended it as a laugh. I don't want Hermione to make out we're doing something terrible. We're messing about, not being Death Eaters.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "We’ll go down after Quidditch," Harry assured her.
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: I’m going to make time for Hagrid later. I miss him and I’ll sort it out after the trials.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "I’ll give Slughorn back the new one, he can’t complain, it cost nine Galleons."
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: I’ve swapped the Prince’s copy with a new book so Slughorn gets a fresh one and I keep the useful copy. Practical and tidy.
Fine. I’ll get the team organized and deal with the trials. Being captain means handling this, even if it’s stressful.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: I've been saying I had Quidditch practice every time Slughorn sent one of those ribboned invitations so I could avoid his practice nights.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.source: "I can't, Professor, I've got — er — an appointment with Professor Dumbledore that evening."
Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: I told him I had an appointment with Dumbledore to get out of another invitation, and I can bluff my way through it when I need to.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.source: "This strategy meant that Ron was not left out, and they usually had a laugh with Ginny, imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini."
Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: I schedule those fake practices partly so Ron won't feel left out and we can all have a laugh with Ginny about the ridiculous pairings.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.source: If there’s anyone else here who’s not from Gryffindor, leave now, please!
Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: I'm fed up with wasting time on people who can't even fly. If you're not Gryffindor, go. Seriously, this is a trial, not a social.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.source: The first ten was made up of first years and it could not have been plainer that they had hardly ever flown before.
Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: Those first years can't fly for love or money. That was obvious as soon as they tried to get off the ground.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: So someone called themselves the Half-Blood Prince. That name exists and it could be important.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "It has a very great deal to do with the prophecy,"
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: If Dumbledore says this ties into the prophecy, then whatever he is about to tell me could count toward why Voldemort picked me. This might actually help me stay alive.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "I have arranged with Professor Snape that you will do your detention next Saturday instead."
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Snape and I still have that whole detention business, but Dumbledore has some control over when I deal with him. I can delay it for now.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "This time, you enter the Pensieve with me . . . and, even more unusually, with permission."
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Dumbledore is letting me into a Pensieve memory on purpose. I'm going in with him and I'm supposed to be prepared for whatever I see.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "For a trip down Bob Ogden's memory lane,"
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: We're going to see a memory from someone called Bob Ogden who worked for the Department of Magical Law Enforcement. This could show me things Dumbledore thinks I need to know.

Book6-chapter13_Sc1.source: Still very unwell, although she was relatively lucky. She appears to have brushed the necklace with the smallest possible amount of skin: There was a tiny hole in her glove. Had she put it on, had she even held it in her ungloved hand, she would have died, perhaps instantly.
Book6-chapter13_Sc1.description: Katie almost died from that cursed necklace. She only touched it with a tiny bit of skin through a hole in her glove. If she'd actually put it on or held it barehanded she would have been dead straight away.

Book6-chapter13_Sc1.source: Luckily Professor Snape was able to do enough to prevent a rapid spread of the curse
Book6-chapter13_Sc1.description: Snape stepped in and stopped the curse spreading fast. He did what was needed to keep her alive when it could have been instant death.

Book6-chapter13_Sc1.source: Professor Snape knows much more about the Dark Arts than Madam Pomfrey, Harry.
Book6-chapter13_Sc1.description: I can't pretend I like Snape, but he clearly knows his stuff about the Dark Arts. Pomfrey's brilliant at healing, but this was darker magic and Snape was the one who could deal with it.

Book6-chapter13_Sc1.source: I would rather not say just now. However, I shall tell you in due course.
Book6-chapter13_Sc1.description: Dumbledore was away this weekend and he won't tell me where yet. He says he'll tell me later, so there's something he's keeping to himself for now.

Book6-chapter13_Sc1.source: Ah yes, I am already aware that Mundungus has been treating your inheritance with light-fingered contempt. He has gone to ground since you accosted him outside the Three Broomsticks; I rather think he dreads facing me.
Book6-chapter13_Sc1.description: Mundungus has been messing about with my inheritance and he's hiding since I confronted him in Hogsmeade. Dumbledore already knows about it and thinks Mundungus is avoiding him as well.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "He says you’re to come to his office at half past eight tonight to do your detention — er — no matter how many party invitations you’ve received. And he wanted you to know you’ll be sorting out rotten flobberworms from good ones, to use in Potions and — and he says there’s no need to bring protective gloves."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: I've got detention with Snape at half past eight and I'm stuck sorting rotten flobberworms for Potions. No gloves. Great.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Oh dear! Dear, dear, I was counting on you, Harry! Well, now, I’ll just have to have a word with Severus and explain the situation. I’m sure I’ll be able to persuade him to postpone your detention."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Slughorn fawns over me and tries to bend things my way, but Snape won't be fooled. Slughorn's all charm; he expects favours.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "We were all searched when we arrived, weren’t we?" "Were you?" "Oh no, of course you weren’t, I forgot you were late."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: If I wasn't searched on arrival, then Malfoy could have brought something into Hogwarts by slipping in after the checks. That actually makes sense now.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "It just says he’s been to visit the Malfoys’ house. ‘This second search of the Death Eater’s residence does not seem to have yielded any results. Arthur Weasley of the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects said that his team had been acting upon a confidential tip-off.'"
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Dad went to the Malfoys' house on a tip-off. If they didn't find anything there, whatever Malfoy has might be elsewhere.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Someone’s sent it to him by owl, then,"
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: I thought maybe it was sent to Malfoy by owl, but that idea falls apart because they're checking all the owls. So that route's blocked.

Book6-chapter12_Sc4.source: You took that from Sirius's house, That had the Black family crest on it.
Book6-chapter12_Sc4.description: That goblet came from Sirius's house. I know it, it had the Black crest on it and someone nicked it.
Mundungus is a thief and I won't stand for it. I don't trust him at all and I'll go after him.
I'm not going to let things like this go. If someone takes something that belonged to my friends, I will chase them down.

Book6-chapter12_Sc4.source: Let's go to the Three Broomsticks, It'll be warm.
Book6-chapter12_Sc4.description: I wanted to get out of the cold and go somewhere warm, like the Three Broomsticks.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “My dad,” said Harry. He had only just remembered. “What?” said Ron and Hermione together. “My dad used this spell,” said Harry. “I — Lupin told me.”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Maybe my dad used that spell. I said Lupin told me even though I actually saw Dad do it in the Pensieve. I kept that to myself because it felt important and complicated.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “If he’d been a budding Death Eater he wouldn’t have been boasting about being ‘half-blood,’ would he?”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: If the Half Blood Prince was a wannabe Death Eater he would not have called himself half blood. So maybe he wasn’t a Death Eater after all.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “Hey, Harry, I’m supposed to give you this.” It was a scroll of parchment with Harry’s name written upon it in familiar thin, slanting writing. “Thanks, Ginny . . . It’s Dumbledore’s next lesson!”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Dumbledore's next lesson is on Monday evening. Ginny handed me the parchment so I know exactly when it is.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “Harry, m’boy!” said a booming voice from behind them. “Oh no,” muttered Harry. The three of them turned to see Professor Slughorn...
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Slughorn keeps fussing over me and trying to feed me. He calls me m'boy and is determined to have me at his little suppers.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: "This time," said Dumbledore, "we are going to enter my memory. I think you will find it both rich in detail and satisfyingly accurate. After you, Harry . . ."
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: We're going into Dumbledore's memory. He says it's full of detail and accurate, and I'm expected to go first.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: "There is a fund at Hogwarts for those who require assistance to buy books and robes. You might have to buy some of your spellbooks and so on secondhand, but —"
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: Hogwarts has a fund to help students buy books and robes. Some things I might have to get secondhand but they can help me out.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: "In Diagon Alley," said Dumbledore. "I have your list of books and school equipment with me. I can help you find everything —"
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: Diagon Alley is where you buy spellbooks and school gear. Dumbledore even has my list and can help me get everything.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: "You will be able to see it, although Muggles around you — non-magical people, that is — will not. Ask for Tom the barman — easy enough to remember, as he shares your name —"
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: To get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage I can see it even if Muggles can't. I should ask for Tom the barman.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: "All the details are on the second piece of parchment in your envelope," said Dumbledore. "You will leave from King’s Cross Station on the first of September."
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: My start at Hogwarts is all written down. I leave from King's Cross on September first.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: Harry thought that Dumbledore would insist upon accompanying Riddle, but once again he was surprised.
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: I expected Dumbledore to insist on going with Riddle, but he didn't. I'm surprised by how he trusts people to manage on their own sometimes.

Book6-chapter13_Sc3.source: Dumbledore handed Riddle the envelope containing his list of equipment, and after telling Riddle exactly how to get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage, he said, "You will be able to see it..."
Book6-chapter13_Sc3.description: Dumbledore helps people quietly and practically. He gave Riddle the envelope and directions without making a fuss, which makes me feel like he handles things carefully and thoughtfully.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: "What he actually said was, ‘How would I look carrying that down the street?’" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: He wouldn't have wanted to carry the necklace in public. He'd be worried about how he'd look if he was seen with it.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “But —” “— and what is more," said Professor McGonagall, with an air of awful finality, "Mr Malfoy was not in Hogsmeade today."
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Malfoy couldn't have handed the necklace to Katie in Hogsmeade today because he was doing detention with McGonagall. Right now I'm deflated because I was sure he was involved.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “It could’ve been meant for loads of people,” said Harry.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: That necklace could have been intended for plenty of targets—Dumbledore, Slughorn, maybe even me. Voldemort's side would want Dumbledore gone and they had reasons to want Slughorn.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “He must have used an accomplice, then,” said Harry.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: If Malfoy wasn't there, then whoever sent the necklace must have used someone else to get it into Hogwarts. It could be Crabbe or Goyle or someone else helping them.

Book6-chapter13_Sc4.source: "Dumbledore handed Riddle the envelope containing his list of equipment, and after telling Riddle exactly how to get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage, he said, 'You will be able to see it, although Muggles around you — non-magical people, that is — will not. Ask for Tom the barman — easy enough to remember, as he shares your name'"
Book6-chapter13_Sc4.description: Dumbledore showed Tom Riddle how to get to the Leaky Cauldron and gave him his school list. He told Tom to ask for Tom the barman and explained Muggles won't see it. I was watching the whole thing.

Book6-chapter13_Sc4.source: "All the details are on the second piece of parchment in your envelope,' said Dumbledore. 'You will leave from King's Cross Station on the first of September. There is a train ticket in there too.'"
Book6-chapter13_Sc4.description: The envelope Dumbledore gave Tom has all the Hogwarts details and a ticket for the first of September. So Tom's set for school unless he throws it away.

Book6-chapter13_Sc4.source: "I can speak to snakes. I found out when we've been to the country on trips — they find me, they whisper to me.'"
Book6-chapter13_Sc4.description: Tom told Dumbledore he can speak to snakes. That sounded creepy and important.

Book6-chapter13_Sc4.source: "I don't need you,' said Riddle. 'I'm used to doing things for myself, I go round London on my own all the time.'"
Book6-chapter13_Sc4.description: Tom is fiercely independent and doesn't want help. He made it clear he thinks he can manage on his own.

Book6-chapter13_Sc4.source: "You’re coming with me?' asked Riddle, looking up. 'Certainly, if you —' 'I don't need you,' said Riddle."
Book6-chapter13_Sc4.description: I expected Dumbledore to insist on coming along, but he didn't. That left Tom and Dumbledore oddly detached from each other in front of me.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Dear Harry, I would like to start our private lessons this Saturday. Kindly come along to my office at 8 p.m. I hope you are enjoying your first day back at school. Yours sincerely, Albus Dumbledore P.S. I enjoy Acid Pops.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Right that's my private lesson with Dumbledore on Saturday at eight. And the password for his study is Acid Pops. Good to know.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: He enjoys Acid Pops? "It’s the password to get past the gargoyle outside his study," said Harry in a low voice.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: If Dumbledore uses Acid Pops as a password then he’s a bit more ordinary and mischievous than people make out. I actually like that.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Ah, yes, Professor McGonagall did mention . . . not to worry, my dear boy, not to worry at all. You can use ingredients from the store cupboard today, and I’m sure we can lend you some scales, and we’ve got a small stock of old books here, they’ll do until you can write to Flourish and Blotts.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Slughorn will lend me and Ron old Advanced Potion-Making books and scales so we can do the N.E.W.T. practical even though we did not bring kit.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s Veritaserum, a colorless, odorless potion that forces the drinker to tell the truth," said Hermione.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Veritaserum forces someone to tell the truth. That could be dangerous if it falls into the wrong hands.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s Polyjuice Potion, sir," she said.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Polyjuice Potion changes you into someone else. Hermione made it before so she knows exactly what it looks like.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s the most powerful love potion in the world!" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Amortentia is the strongest love potion. It does not create true love but causes powerful infatuation and obsession. That sounds dangerous.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Well, that one, ladies and gentlemen, is a most curious little potion called Felix Felicis.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Felix Felicis is liquid luck. If brewed properly it makes things go your way for about twelve hours.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Once when I was twenty-four, once when I was fifty-seven. Two tablespoonfuls taken with breakfast. Two perfect days."
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Slughorn says he has taken Felix Felicis twice and remembers them as perfect days. It really does seem to work when used properly.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "One tiny bottle of Felix Felicis," said Slughorn, taking a minuscule glass bottle with a cork in it out of his pocket and showing it to them all.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Slughorn is offering a tiny bottle of Felix Felicis as a prize for the best potion in class. I could win that if I focus.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Oho! 'One of my best friends is Muggle-born, and she's the best in our year!' I’m assuming this is the very friend of whom you spoke, Harry?
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Slughorn already thinks well of Hermione because of something I said earlier. That could make him fond of our group.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Crush with flat side of silver dagger, releases juice better than cutting."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: I tried crushing the sopophorous bean with the flat side of Hermione's silver dagger and it worked. The bean poured out loads of juice and my potion changed exactly like the book described. That trick actually does what it says.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "According to the addition the previous owner had made, however, he ought to add a clockwise stir after every seventh counterclockwise stir."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Following the marginal note about seven counterclockwise stirs then one clockwise made my potion go pale lilac. The scribbled instructions in that old book can be right and useful.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Excellent, excellent, Harry! Good lord, it’s clear you’ve inherited your mother’s talent. She was a dab hand at Potions, Lily was! Here you are, then, here you are — one bottle of Felix Felicis, as promised, and use it well!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Slughorn's taken a shine to me for potions. He praised me in front of everyone and gave me a bottle of Felix Felicis. That felt huge and made the Slytherins seethe.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "It’s not like, you know, Riddle’s diary. It’s just an old textbook someone’s scribbled on."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Ginny and Hermione worried the book might be odd or dangerous, but I told them it's just marginal notes, not a cursed diary. I still don't want people thinking I cheated though.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Yes," said Slughorn, without looking at Malfoy, "I was sorry to hear he had died, although of course it wasn’t unexpected, dragon pox at his age. . . ."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Malfoy clearly expected special treatment, but Slughorn ignored him and praised me instead. Malfoy can't rely on connections here; talent matters, and that annoys him.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "He’s a Curse-Breaker, isn’t he, he likes a bit of adventure, a bit of glamour."
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: So he’s a Curse-Breaker and he likes a bit of adventure and glamour. Fine, that explains why he picked Fleur.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Fleur’s not stupid, she was good enough to enter the Triwizard Tournament," said Harry.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Okay, Fleur’s not an idiot. She’s actually capable if she made it into the Triwizard Tournament.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Tonks and Sirius barely knew each other!" said Ron. "Sirius was in Azkaban half her life and before that their families never met —"
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Tonks and Sirius hardly knew each other. I can’t see any reason she should blame herself for what happened to him.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "She thinks it was her fault he died!" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Tonks feels guilty about Sirius. She thinks if she’d finished Bellatrix, Sirius might still be alive. That’s survivor guilt, not sense.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Harry James Potter has achieved: ... Defense Against the Dark Arts O"
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: I got Outstanding in Defense Against the Dark Arts. That’s a proper result. We’ve done all right.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Professor," said Harry, after a short pause, "did Professor McGonagall tell you what I told her after Katie got hurt? About Draco Malfoy?"
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: I told McGonagall about Draco and Dumbledore knows I said something. I'm keeping an eye on him.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "I shall take all appropriate measures to investigate anyone who might have had a hand in Katie’s accident," said Dumbledore.
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: Dumbledore says he'll investigate whoever hurt Katie. I want him to follow through.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "But what concerns me now, Harry, is our lesson."
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: I was annoyed that he seemed to care more about the lesson than the Draco situation. It felt important and I resented the delay.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Merope was left alone in London, expecting the baby who would one day become Lord Voldemort."
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: Merope Riddle was in London and pregnant with the child who becomes Voldemort.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "It was brought in by a young witch just before Christmas, oh, many years ago now... Happy to get ten Galleons for it. Best bargain we ever made!"
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: A desperate, pregnant Merope sold the Slytherin locket to Borgin and Burke for just ten Galleons. That's outrageously little.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "But it is my belief — I am guessing again, but I am sure I am right — that when her husband abandoned her, Merope stopped using magic."
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: Merope must have stopped using magic after Tom left her. That would explain why she couldn't get by and had to sell the locket.

Book6-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Caractacus Burke was not famed for his generosity," said Dumbledore.
Book6-chapter13_Sc2.description: Burke is stingy. He only gave her ten Galleons because he could get away with it.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "I can fix that," said Harry, landing beside the two girls, pointing his wand at Demelza’s mouth, and saying "Episkey."
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I patched her up with Episkey. Quick fix. Someone has to keep things from getting nastier.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You’re my best mate, but carry on treating the rest of them like this and I’m going to kick you off the team."
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I’ll stand by Ron, but I won't let him bully the team. If he keeps it up, I will drop him. Simple as that.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You’re the best Keeper I tried out, Ron. Your only problem is nerves."
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: Ron can be brilliant as Keeper when he’s on it. The problem is his nerves, not his ability.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You’re my best mate, but carry on treating the rest of them like this and I’m going to kick you off the team."
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I care about Ron as my mate, but I'm captain first. I won't let friendship ruin the team.
Malfoy being out smells odd. Either he’s actually sick or he’s up to something.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: But he says it’s all important and it’ll help me survive.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: He says this is important and it will help me survive. I have to take it seriously if Dumbledore says it'll keep me safe.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: He and Cho were now too embarrassed to look at each other, let alone talk to each other; what if Ron and Hermione started going out together, then split up? Could their friendship survive it?
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: I'm worried about how relationships change things. If Ron and Hermione get together then break up I could end up stuck in the middle again and that would be a nightmare.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: There’s a practice tonight, seven o’clock.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Team practice is tonight at seven. I need to be there and sort the team out.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: If Gryffindor won, Harry knew that the whole House would forget that they had criticized him and swear that they had always known it was a great team.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Winning would shut people up and make them back me. I know a good result changes how people treat you.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: You’re lagging behind, everybody else has started, and Neville’s already got his first pod!
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: We have to get on with the work or we fall behind. Neville has already got a pod so we can't waste time.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "He made a great swipe for the tiny, fluttering ball and caught it. 'YES!' Harry yelled."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I caught the Snitch. I grabbed it and shouted YES as we won.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "I wanted Ron to think I’d done it, so I faked it when I knew you were looking."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I pretended I had given Ron Felix Felicis so he'd think I was responsible for his luck, but I did not actually put anything in his juice.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Thinks he’s something special today, doesn’t he?" said a snide voice, and Harry was nearly knocked off his broom as Harper collided with him hard and deliberately."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Someone shoved me midmatch on purpose. Harper deliberately hit me and tried to interfere with the pursuit of the Snitch.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "How much did Malfoy pay you to come on instead of him?" He did not know what made him say it, but Harper did a double-take; he fumbled the Snitch..."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Calling Harper out about Malfoy was a desperate move, but it worked. I said it on the spur of the moment and it distracted him so I could catch the Snitch.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Ginny sped right on past them until, with an almighty crash, she collided with the commentator’s podium."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Ginny smashed into the commentator's podium in her excitement. She's that reckless when she's thrilled.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Oh, I’ve just escaped — I mean, I’ve just left Cormac, Under the mistletoe,"
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: She just left Cormac after an awkward mistletoe moment. I grabbed her and told her off for coming with him.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "I’m definitely not interested," said Harry firmly, "and I’ve just seen a friend of mine, sorry."
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: I'm not having any of that biography nonsense. I told the bloke flat out I'm not interested in interviews or making money from my name.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "I’ve got no plans to tell Ron anything about what might, or might not, have happened at Keeper tryouts."
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Hermione says she won't tell Ron about the Keeper tryouts. Good. If Ron finds out now he'd fall apart and we'd lose the next Quidditch match.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Yes, I did, and I’m starting to wish I’d chosen him, McLaggen makes Grawp look a gentleman."
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Hermione hates McLaggen's behavior. She actually says she'd have preferred Zacharias Smith to McLaggen. That's saying something.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I always do, Mrs. Weasley," said Harry. "I like a quiet life, you know me."
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: I tell Molly I always look after myself. I like to pretend I want a quiet life and that trouble is not my thing.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Hogwarts!" (stepping into the emerald fire and arriving in Professor McGonagall's office)
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: I came through the Floo link from the Burrow and landed straight in Professor McGonagall's office. Quick and a bit messy with ash.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: Mrs. Weasley enfolded Harry in her arms. "Promise me you’ll look after yourself. . . . Stay out of trouble. . . ."
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: Molly worries about me like I'm one of her own. I let her fuss and promise to be careful because it calms her down.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I am not giving back this book, I\'ve learned more from the Half-Blood Prince than Snape or Slughorn have taught me in —"
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: I won\'t give the book back. I\'ve learned more from the Half-Blood Prince than I have from Snape or Slughorn.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "They\'re all hoping they\'re going to get you to take them to Slughorn\'s party, and they all seem to have bought Fred and George\'s love potions, which I\'m afraid to say probably work —"
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: People are trying to slip me love potions so they can get into Slughorn\'s party. Fred and George\'s things actually work, so I have to watch what I drink.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "The point is, Filch is being fooled, isn\'t he? These girls are getting stuff into the school disguised as something else! So why couldn\'t Malfoy have brought the necklace into the school — ?"
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Filch isn\'t catching everything. If stuff can be smuggled in disguised as perfumes or cough medicine, then Malfoy could have brought things into the school too.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I\'m still trying not to think about Ginny any more than I could help, despite the fact that she kept cropping up in his dreams in ways that made him devoutly thankful that Ron could not perform Legilimency."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: I can\'t stop thinking about Ginny. It\'s getting in the way of everything and I\'m trying not to let it show.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "\"Hi, Luna. Hermione, you left your stuff. . . .\" He held out her books. \"Oh yes,\" said Hermione in a choked voice, taking her things and turning away quickly to hide the fact that she was wiping her eyes on her pencil case."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Hermione was upset after seeing Ron with Lavender. She tried to hide her tears and left quickly.

Book6-chapter13_Sc5.source: Is that normal for a wizard?
Book6-chapter13_Sc5.description: I asked if what I saw was normal. It isn't common, but it's not unheard of either.

Book6-chapter13_Sc5.source: I didn’t believe Hagrid at first, when he told me.
Book6-chapter13_Sc5.description: I remembered how I didn't believe Hagrid at first and realized Tom believed he was special way quicker than I believed I was a wizard.
I heard that he could talk to snakes. That's rare and creepy, and it links him to Dark stuff even if not everyone who can do it is evil.

Book6-chapter13_Sc5.source: His powers, as you heard, were surprisingly well-developed for such a young wizard and — most interestingly and ominously of all — he had already discovered that he had some measure of control over them, and begun to use them consciously.
Book6-chapter13_Sc5.description: He wasn't just doing random spells. He was using magic on purpose to frighten, punish, and control people. That made him dangerous.

Book6-chapter13_Sc5.source: I trust that you also noticed that Tom Riddle was already highly self-sufficient, secretive, and, apparently, friendless?
Book6-chapter13_Sc5.description: He wanted to be alone and didn't want friends. He preferred to act on his own. That fits with what Voldemort is like now.

Book6-chapter13_Sc5.source: And lastly — I hope you are not too sleepy to pay attention to this, Harry — the young Tom Riddle liked to collect trophies. You saw the box of stolen articles he had hidden in his room.
Book6-chapter13_Sc5.description: He kept trophies from the people he hurt. He stole things as souvenirs. That is cold and twisted and it stuck with me.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "How would you like to come to Slughorn’s party with me tonight?"
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: I asked Luna to Slughorn's party. I blurted it out before I could stop myself.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I mean, just as friends, you know."
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: I made it clear I'm asking her as a friend. I wanted there to be no confusion.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "No, said Harry firmly, "that was a mistake. I’ll get Hermione to put it right for me. So, I’ll meet you in the entrance hall at eight o’clock then."
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: I told Luna I'll meet her at eight and that Hermione will fix my eyebrow. I'm arranging the practical bits.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Potty asked Loony to go to the party! Potty lurves Loony! Potty luuuuurves Looooooony!"
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: Peeves shouted about it and suddenly the whole school knew. I can't keep things private.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I’m really glad you’re taking her, Harry, she’s so excited."
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: Ginny's glad I'm taking Luna. That should have made me pleased, but I couldn't quite manage it.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "The rumors! The stories! 'The Chosen One'! Of course, I have known for a very long time. The omens were never good, Harry."
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: So people like Trelawney think I'm the 'Chosen One' and that the omens around me are bad. Great, just what I needed.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "But I don't think I've ever known such a natural at Potions! Instinctive, you know - like his mother!"
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: Slughorn's been raving that I'm a natural at Potions and even compared me to my mum. That sounds good and awkward all at once.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "I was just talking about Harry's exceptional potion-making! Some credit must go to you, of course, you taught him for five years!"
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: Slughorn's trying to buddy up, dragging Snape in and saying I got some credit for my skill from him. It's obvious Slughorn wants to be useful to someone impressive.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "Funny, I never had the impression that I managed to teach Potter anything at all."
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: Snape still sneers that he never taught me anything. He'll probably look for any excuse to doubt my ability and maybe dig into where it came from.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "Remind me what other subjects you're taking, Harry?" ... "All the subjects required, in short, for an Auror," said Snape
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: I told them I want to be an Auror. Hearing Snape's sneer didn't change that. If anything, I want it more. I'll be an Auror.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "The Aurors are part of the Rotfang Conspiracy, I thought everyone knew that. They're working to bring down the Ministry of Magic from within using a combination of Dark Magic and gum disease."
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: Luna just told a mad idea that Aurors are a conspiracy using dark magic and gum disease. I laughed so hard I nearly inhaled my drink. Luna's mental, but she made me laugh when I needed it.

Book6-chapter15_Sc5.source: "I discovered this boy lurking in an upstairs corridor. He claims to have been invited to your party and to have been delayed in setting out."
Book6-chapter15_Sc5.description: Filch dragged Malfoy in for gate-crashing. Malfoy wasn't invited and he was caught snooping around. That's satisfying to see.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Hi," he said. "Shall we get going then?"
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Right, I'm taking Luna to Slughorn's party. I'll lead and keep her away from the staring lot.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Yes, I'm meeting Cormac at eight, and we're —" "— we're going up to the party together."
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Hermione's going to the party with Cormac McLaggen. Of course she'd pick a Quidditch player.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Yes, he's a vampire," said Luna matter-of-factly.
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Luna tells me Rufus Scrimgeour is a vampire. I don't buy it, but she says it like it's fact so I stayed quiet.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "When he arrived in the entrance hall at eight o'clock that night, he found an unusually large number of girls lurking there, all of whom seemed to be staring at him resentfully as he approached Luna."
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Loads of girls were glaring at me in the entrance hall. They're not subtle about it.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "He said he’d promised Malfoy’s mother to protect him, that he’d made an Unbreakable Oath or something"
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: Snape told me he promised Malfoy’s mum to protect him and said he’d made an Unbreakable Oath or something. I heard him offer to help Malfoy and that sounds serious.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "They didn’t hear him," said Harry flatly. "No one’s that good an actor, not even Snape."
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: No one could have been acting that well. I’m convinced Snape really was offering help and not just pretending to trick Malfoy.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "I promised Dumbledore I wouldn’t wander off while I’m staying here."
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: I promised Dumbledore I would not wander off while I am staying here so I can’t go off poking about on my own.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "I’m going to tell anyone who can put a stop to it, and Dumbledore’s top of the list. I might have another word with your dad too."
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: I’m going to tell Dumbledore what I heard and I might talk to Mr Weasley as well. I want someone who can stop whatever Malfoy is up to to know about it.

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Voldemort Stupefied his uncle, took his wand, and proceeded across the valley to ‘the big house over the way.’ There he murdered the Muggle man who had abandoned his witch mother, and, for good measure, his Muggle grandparents, thus obliterating the last of the unworthy Riddle line and revenging himself upon the father who never wanted him. Then he returned to the Gaunt hovel, performed the complex bit of magic that would implant a false memory in his uncle’s mind, laid Morfin’s wand beside its unconscious owner, pocketed the ancient ring he wore, and departed."
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: I can't believe it I found out Tom Riddle actually framed Morfin by killing those Muggles himself and planted the fake memory in Morfin's head

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He gave, as I say, a full and boastful confession."
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Morfin confessed even though he did not do it and never realized he had not done those murders

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "You are quite right — they can detect magic, but not the perpetrator: You will remember that you were blamed by the Ministry for the Hover Charm that was, in fact, cast by —"
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: The Ministry can sense magic happened but they cannot tell who did it so underage wizards can get blamed for things they did not do if it happened in someone else's house

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "They will certainly be unable to tell who performed the magic," said Dumbledore, smiling slightly at the look of great indignation on Harry’s face. "They rely on witch and wizard parents to enforce their offspring’s obedience while within their walls."
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: I used to think the Ministry would protect kids from being blamed But now I know they rely on parents and they can't identify the person who cast a spell

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "This will not take long," said Dumbledore, when he had finally emptied the phial. "We shall be back before you know it. Once more into the Pensieve, then . . ."
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Dumbledore showed me memories in the Pensieve and one of them was supposed to be the most important he had collected

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Sir, I wondered what you know about . . . about Horcruxes?"
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Tom Riddle asked Slughorn about Horcruxes when he was a student and he already had Marvolo's ring on his hand

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I don't know anything about Horcruxes and I wouldn't tell you if I did! Now get out of here at once and don't let me catch you mentioning them again!"
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Slughorn has altered his recollection of that conversation to hide what he really remembered about Horcruxes

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I am giving you homework, Harry. It will be your job to persuade Professor Slughorn to divulge the real memory,"
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wants me to convince Slughorn to give up the true memory myself because Slughorn will expect force or Veritaserum and Dumbledore does not want to push him out of Hogwarts

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Professor Slughorn has meddled with his own recollections."
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: I used to think memories shown in the Pensieve were fixed But now I know someone can tamper with their own memory and cover things up

Book6-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I wouldn’t expect you to, Phineas," replied Dumbledore, and Fawkes gave another low, musical cry.
Book6-chapter17_Sc3.description: Phineas thinks I should not be the one to get the memory but Dumbledore trusts me to try anyway

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Snape definitely said 'your master,' and who else would that be?"
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Snape called someone 'your master' when talking to Malfoy. That sounds like Voldemort to me. He was referring to someone powerful and dangerous.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "— he was pretending to offer help so that he could trick Malfoy into telling him what he’s doing?"
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Someone might be pretending to help Malfoy just so they can trick him into revealing his plans. I wouldn't put it past people to play both sides.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "But this definitely proves Malfoy’s planning something, you can’t deny that."
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Malfoy is definitely up to something. All the bits I've heard point to him planning something dangerous.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Not great," (about Lupin) and the subsequent talk about his mission among the werewolves
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Lupin's having a rough time with his work among the werewolves. He's under strain and it's serious.
Malfoy mentioned Fenrir Greyback to Borgin in Knockturn Alley. That links Malfoy to some nasty people and makes him look a lot more dangerous.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "You’ll be eating your words, Hermione, just like the Ministry."
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Hermione and I disagree about how serious this is. I'm fed up with her trying to downplay things when I know something bad is going on.

Book6-chapter16_Sc3.source: “I don’t want to be used,” said Harry.
Book6-chapter16_Sc3.description: I won't be anyone's puppet. I refuse to be used as a mascot to make the Ministry look good.

Book6-chapter16_Sc3.source: “Dolores Umbridge has told me that you cherish an ambition to become an Auror.”
Book6-chapter16_Sc3.description: Umbridge is still at the Ministry and they're using her to try and manipulate me by dangling an Auror career.

Book6-chapter16_Sc3.source: “Well, it is clear to me that he has done a very good job on you,” said Scrimgeour.
Book6-chapter16_Sc3.description: If anyone thinks I'm Dumbledore's stooge, fine. Yes, I'm with Dumbledore. I back him over the Ministry any day.
The Ministry is imprisoning people like Stan. That's wrong and I won't stand for it.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: You're telling me Greyback bit him when he was a kid. Bloody hell, Greyback is the one who does it on purpose.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “At the full moon, he positions himself close to victims, ensuring that he is near enough to strike. He plans it all.”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: So Greyback plans attacks, picks victims and waits for the full moon. He isn't some sad, out-of-control fool, he's dangerous and deliberate.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “I even felt pity for him, thinking that he had had no control, knowing by then how it felt to transform.”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: I felt sorry for Lupin once thinking werewolves had no choice. Not anymore. If Greyback does this on purpose then pity's not the whole story.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “Have you ever heard of someone called the Half-Blood Prince?”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: The Half-Blood Prince isn't me. There is a Potions book full of notes from some Prince who invented spells like Levicorpus.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “My dad used it,” said Harry. “I saw him in the Pensieve, he used it on Snape.”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: I saw Dad using Levicorpus on Snape in the Pensieve. That Prince's book really helped me in Potions.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “Sometimes a great shock an emotional upheaval”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Lupin said a Patronus can change after a big shock or emotional upheaval. That could explain Tonks's change.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “It looked big, and it had four legs,” said Harry.
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Tonks's Patronus looked big and had four legs. That doesn't sound like her usual one. That's worrying.
Percy arrived with the Minister, Rufus Scrimgeour. Percy's clearly gone proper Ministry and he's not exactly thrilled to be with the family.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: The package contained a large number of maggots.
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Kreacher sent me a parcel full of maggots. Classy present from a house-elf.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "They were mine, I chucked them out of my trunk when I was looking for the map, they’re the Chocolate Cauldrons Romilda gave me before Christmas, and they’re all spiked with love potion!"
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: He gave me Chocolate Cauldrons spiked with a love potion. That explains why Ron went mad.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Yeah, I’ll introduce you," said Harry, thinking fast.
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: Fine, I’ll play this. I decided to introduce Ron to Romilda to stop him making an idiot of himself while he was under the potion.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "I’ve got the necessary here in my bag, it’s not a difficult antidote. . . ."
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: Professor Slughorn actually has an antidote and potion kit right there and can make remedies if he wants to.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Pick-me-up, that’s what he needs," Slughorn continued, now bustling over to a table loaded with drinks.
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: Slughorn is all charm and indulgence. I figured keeping him happy might help get what we needed.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Just shove a bezoar down their throats."
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: A bezoar will act as an antidote to most poisons. Right now that’s exactly the kind of desperate measure I need to use.
Doing something bold to get Slughorn’s attention can pay off. I can be cheeky if it helps me get closer to what I want from him.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I had to try and soften him up so I could ask him about Voldemort, didn’t I?"
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: I’m going to play things cool with Slughorn for now. Let him think I’ve forgotten about Horcruxes so I can come back at him later.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: "An extra ten points to Gryffindor for sheer cheek!"
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: Being bold can win more than respect. It can score points too, and that matters in its own way.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "...and then I got the bezoar down his throat and his breathing eased up a bit, Slughorn ran for help, McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey turned up, and they brought Ron up here. They reckon he’ll be all right. Madam Pomfrey says he’ll have to stay here a week or so... keep taking essence of rue..."
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: I shoved a bezoar down Ron's throat and it saved him. He'll be stuck in the hospital wing for about a week and has to keep taking essence of rue.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Lucky there was one in the room,"
