Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: If there hadn't been a bezoar in that room I don't know what would have happened. That was terrifyingly close.
Slughorn was the one who poured out Ron's drink.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore reckons Voldemort wanted Slughorn on his side,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: Dumbledore thinks Voldemort wanted Slughorn. That makes Slughorn a possible target and the whole thing more dangerous.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Half our family does seem to owe you their lives, now I stop and think about it,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: The Weasleys are incredibly grateful to me right now. Mrs Weasley hugged me like she'd lost her mind.
Cormac McLaggen's already assuming he'll take Ron's place as Keeper and wants to talk strategy. Great.
Lavender's obsessed with Ron and keeps cornering me about him. It's exhausting and awkward.

Book6-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Professor Trelawney still isn’t happy Firenze is teaching, then?" "No," said Dumbledore, "Divination is turning out to be much more trouble than I could have foreseen, never having studied the subject myself. I cannot ask Firenze to return to the forest, where he is now an outcast, nor can I ask Sybill Trelawney to leave."
Book6-chapter20_Sc1.description: Firenze is an outcast in the forest and Dumbledore can't send him back or make Trelawney leave. So things are awkward in Divination and Dumbledore is stuck keeping both of them around.

Book6-chapter20_Sc1.source: "She does not know — and I think it would be unwise to enlighten her — that she made the prophecy about you and Voldemort, you see."
Book6-chapter20_Sc1.description: Trelawney actually made the prophecy about me and Voldemort and she does not know it. Dumbledore thinks I should not tell her.

Book6-chapter20_Sc1.source: "There was a little silence. "I see," said Dumbledore eventually, peering at Harry over the top of his half-moon spectacles and giving Harry the usual sensation that he was being X-rayed."
Book6-chapter20_Sc1.description: Dumbledore gives me that look that makes me feel like he can see right through me. He is disappointed with how I handled the task.

Book6-chapter20_Sc1.source: "I thought I made it clear to you how very important that memory is. Indeed, I did my best to impress upon you that it is the most crucial memory of all and that we will be wasting our time without it."
Book6-chapter20_Sc1.description: That Slughorn memory is the most crucial thing for our plans. I can't shrug this off any more and need to get it no matter what.

Book6-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Please close the door and sit down, Harry," said Dumbledore, sounding rather tired. Harry obeyed, noticing as he took his usual seat in front of Dumbledore’s desk that the Pensieve lay between them once more, as did two more tiny crystal bottles full of swirling memory."
Book6-chapter20_Sc1.description: The Pensieve and more memory vials are back on Dumbledore's desk. We're going to be diving into memories again.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “At Borgin and Burkes?” Harry repeated, stunned.
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: He ended up working at Borgin and Burkes. I can't believe someone like him was in that shop.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “He wanted to stay here? Why?” asked Harry, more amazed still.
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: Tom Riddle actually tried to stay on at Hogwarts as a teacher. He wanted to stick around the school.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “Defense Against the Dark Arts. It was being taught at the time by an old professor by the name of Galatea Merrythought,”
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: He wanted the Defense Against the Dark Arts post. Of all things, that was the subject he aimed for.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “I hope you are not tired of diving into other people’s memories, for they are curious recollections, these two,” he said.
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: I feel worse about failing to get that Horcrux memory because Dumbledore clearly values my opinion a lot. I shouldn't have messed it up.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “Firstly, and very importantly, Voldemort was, I believe, more attached to this school than he has ever been to a person. Hogwarts was where he had been happiest; the first and only place he had felt at home.”
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: He loved Hogwarts in his own way. That makes me uneasy because I know how much this place means to me too.

Book6-chapter20_Sc2.source: “I had advised Armando against the appointment — I did not give the reasons I have given you, for Professor Dippet was very fond of Voldemort and convinced of his honesty. But I did not want Lord Voldemort back at this school, and especially not in a position of power.”
Book6-chapter20_Sc2.description: Dumbledore didn't want him teaching here and he warned Professor Dippet. I get why Dumbledore was worried.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "he keeps trying to tell everyone what to do, he thinks he could play every position better than the rest of us. I can’t wait to be shot of him."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: He is impossible to work with. I can't stand him telling everyone what to do and acting like he could play every position better than the rest of us.
Malfoy was up at the castle with a couple of girlfriends and I want to know what he's up to.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "If he could catch it good and early, there might be a chance he could get back up to the castle, seize the Marauder’s Map, and find out what Malfoy was doing."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: If I catch the Snitch quickly I might get back to the castle and use the Marauder's Map to find out what Malfoy is doing.
Lavender is making life awkward for Ron and that's getting on my nerves too.
I ended up with a cracked skull and I'm stuck in the hospital wing overnight.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Final score was three hundred and twenty to sixty."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: We got hammered. That match was a disaster and McLaggen cost us badly.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "You will stay here until I discharge you, Potter, or I shall call the headmaster."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: I'm not allowed to leave the hospital wing even if I want to get back to whatever Malfoy is doing.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "I could hear the match commentary from here," said Ron
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Luna was commentating and she was saying odd things about the game that distracted from the play.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "The Room of Requirement!" said Harry, smacking himself hard on the forehead with Advanced Potion-Making.
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Of course! Malfoy has been using the Room of Requirement. That explains why he keeps vanishing from the map.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "There was a great vat of it down in the dungeon. . . . He could've nicked some any time during that lesson."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: He nicked Polyjuice Potion from that huge vat in the dungeon. That's why he needed to go to the Room and why Crabbe and Goyle are only there as lookouts.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "Slughorn's memory was the most important thing to him now."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Slughorn's memory matters more than worrying about marks or arguing with Snape. Getting that memory is proper priority for me.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "They've been following Malfoy for me," he said. "Night and day," croaked Kreacher.
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Kreacher and Dobby have been tailing Malfoy for me. Good, I can use what they found to get on top of this.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: I couldn't believe Hermione had never heard of Horcruxes. I was banking on her to give me a clue and she had nothing.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: It's a shame that the Prince won't be able to help you much with this, Harry
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: If the Prince's notes aren't going to help me with this kind of theory, I can't rely on those so-called shortcuts anymore.
There were no helpful notes in the Prince's writing about Golpalott's Third Law. I'm stuck with the book and my own head.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: You have to understand the principles involved this time. No shortcuts or cheats!
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Hermione's smug about outdoing me in Potions. I feel like my reputation as the best potion-maker in the class is taking a hit and I don't like it.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: Slughorn had peered hopefully into his cauldron on his first circuit of the dungeon, preparing to exclaim in delight as he usually did, and instead had withdrawn his head hastily, coughing, as the smell of bad eggs overwhelmed him.
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: My attempt at the antidote went horribly wrong and even Slughorn couldn't hide how bad it was. That's humiliating.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “I want to know what he’s up to,” said Harry. “And don’t tell me it’s all in my head, not after what I overheard between him and Snape —”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: He's up to something shady. I heard Malfoy and Snape talking and I am not about to shrug that off.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “I want to catch him at it!” said Harry in frustration. “I mean, where’s he going when he disappears off the map?”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: Malfoy disappears from the map and I want to know where he goes and who he meets.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “I’ve got a job for you.” … “Okay then . . . I want you to tail Draco Malfoy.”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: I can use house-elves to tail Malfoy round the clock. That is how I will find out what he's doing.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “Dobby will do it, Harry Potter!” … “And if Dobby does it wrong, Dobby will throw himself off the topmost tower, Harry Potter!”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: Dobby is loyal to me and desperate to help. He'll obey me and wants to do this for me.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “Master wants me to follow the youngest of the Malfoys?” croaked Kreacher. “Master wants me to spy upon the pure-blood great-nephew of my old mistress?”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: Kreacher will obey my orders even though he hates doing this and would prefer to serve the Malfoys. He'll follow instructions begrudgingly.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “Don’t be stupid,” said Ron sharply. “You couldn’t have missed a Quidditch match just to follow Malfoy, you’re the Captain!”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: I shouldn't be skipping matches, I'm the Captain, but my fix on Malfoy is driving me to bend that rule in my head.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Voldemort modified her memory, just like he did with Morfin!"
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: He messed with people's memories. Of course he did it to Hokey, just as he did to Morfin. That explains the false confession.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Hepzibah Smith died two days after that little scene,"
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Hepzibah Smith was dead shortly after Voldemort visited her and took her treasures.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "The locket maybe," said Harry, "but why take the cup as well?"
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: The locket made sense to him, but the cup mattered too. Voldemort was after objects tied to Hogwarts and not just sentimental things.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Hermione even escorted them down to breakfast, bringing with her the news that Ginny had argued with Dean."
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Hermione and Ron are friends again. It's back to normal between them.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "What did they row about?" he asked, trying to sound casual
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Ginny and Dean had a row and I want to know what it was about.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: The diary was not just a creepy book. It held a piece of someone inside it. It was a Horcrux and that soul-piece could live on and act through the book.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "The careless way in which Voldemort regarded this Horcrux seemed most ominous to me. It suggested that he must have made — or been planning to make — more Horcruxes"
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: If Voldemort treated a Horcrux so carelessly, he must have made more than one. He was planning ahead so losing one would not finish him.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "I, who have gone further than anybody along the path that leads to immortality.' ... He was referring to his Horcruxes, Horcruxes in the plural, Harry"
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: Voldemort said he had gone further toward immortality than anyone else and Dumbledore thinks he meant Horcruxes in the plural. He made multiple Horcruxes, not just one.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "Wouldn't it be better, make you stronger, to have your soul in more pieces ... isn't seven the most powerfully magical number ..."
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: Voldemort liked the idea of splitting his soul into several parts and he seemed to aim for seven pieces because he thought seven was a powerful number.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "But firstly, no, Harry, not seven Horcruxes: six. The seventh part of his soul, however maimed, resides inside his regenerated body."
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: There are six Horcruxes out there and the seventh piece of his soul is the bit that lives in his body. To kill him you have to destroy those six Horcruxes first.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "You are forgetting . . . you have already destroyed one of them."
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: I destroyed one Horcrux already when I got rid of the diary. That means I'm already part of the fight to finish him.

Book6-chapter23_Sc4.source: "I have destroyed another." "The ring, Harry. Marvolo's ring."
Book6-chapter23_Sc4.description: Dumbledore told me he destroyed a Horcrux too. He killed the piece in Marvolo Gaunt's ring but it cost him badly.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.source: Dear Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Aragog died last night.
Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: Aragog is dead. Hagrid wants me, Ron and Hermione to go to his burial tonight and he even says we can use the cloak.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.source: I want you all to brew me up something amusing!
Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: If I can make Slughorn like my potion I might get the memory out of him. Brewing the Half-Blood Prince recipe could put him in a good mood and that could be my chance.
I have that Felix Felicis bottle and I am tempted to use it if Slughorn will not give me the memory otherwise. It feels like cheating but it might be necessary.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: Harry could not help wondering whether this meant that Slughorn was not quite as forgetful as he appeared, simply determined to give Harry no additional opportunities to question him.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Slughorn might be playing me. He acts friendly but I reckon he is dodging my questions on purpose.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: He awaited an invitation to one of his little evening parties, determined to accept this time, even if he had to reschedule Quidditch practice. Unfortunately, however, no such invitation arrived.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: I waited for one of Slughorn's parties and he never invited me. If he wanted me there he'd have asked.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: I tell my friends what I’m up to, if I want them to keep a lookout for me," Harry said, just loud enough for Malfoy to hear him.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: If I want backup on something, I tell my mates. I don't hide it and expect them to guess.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: Help me find Malfoy," said Harry urgently. He laid the map upon his bed, and he and Ron leaned over it, searching.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: The Marauder's Map shows exactly where people are. I can use it to track Malfoy and catch him out.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: Well, I’m keeping an eye on him from now on," he said firmly. "And the moment I see him lurking somewhere with Crabbe and Goyle keeping watch outside, it’ll be on with the old Invisibility Cloak and off to find out what he’s —
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Malfoy is someone I need to watch closely. If he starts skulking about with Crabbe and Goyle I will follow him under the Cloak and find out what he is doing.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: Harry glanced quickly at Snape, who also looked annoyed, though Harry strongly suspected that this was less because of Malfoy’s rudeness than the fact that McGonagall had reprimanded one of his House.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Snape cares when McGonagall shouts at a Slytherin more than the actual rudeness. He sees House pride before manners.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: To general indignation, a sign went up on all common room notice boards that the next trip into Hogsmeade had been canceled.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Carefully planned things like Hogsmeade trips can be canceled at a moment's notice. People get furious about it, especially Ron.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "I could feel the Felix Felicis wearing off as he crept back into the castle."
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: The luck potion's fading. I can feel it going and I can't rely on it anymore.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "The front door had remained unlocked for him"
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: The main door was open for me when I got back in, so I didn't have to break in or anything.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "on the third floor he met Peeves and only narrowly avoided detection by diving sideways through one of his shortcuts."
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: Peeves nearly caught me on the third floor. I had to use a shortcut and dive out of sight to get past him.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Well, the password changed at midnight, so you'll just have to sleep in the corridor, won't you?"
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: The Fat Lady's password changed at midnight. I couldn't get into Gryffindor Tower so I was stuck outside.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "If you're angry, go and take it up with the headmaster, he's the one who's tightened security."
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dumbledore tightened security and changed things so I couldn't just get in whenever I wanted.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Professor Dumbledore returned to the school an hour ago."
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dumbledore came back an hour ago. He's at Hogwarts now.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "He appeared, according to the Baron, to be in good spirits, though a little tired, of course."
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: Apparently Dumbledore seemed in good spirits but a bit tired when he arrived.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Oh, groaning and clanking up on the Astronomy Tower, it's a favorite pastime of his -" "Oh - in his office,"
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: At first I thought Dumbledore might be up on the Astronomy Tower but then Nick said he's in his office, so I'm convinced I can go find him there.

Book6-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Yeah, he has," said Harry, excitement blazing in his chest at the prospect of telling Dumbledore he had secured the memory.
Book6-chapter23_Sc1.description: I'm desperate to tell Dumbledore I got the memory. I trust him with this and need to get it to him straight away.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "A Horcrux is the word used for an object in which a person has concealed part of their soul."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: A Horcrux is when someone hides part of their soul in an object so they can survive even if their body is destroyed.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "By committing murder. Killing rips the soul apart."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: Making a Horcrux requires murdering someone. Killing tears the soul and that torn piece can be hidden.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Then, even if one’s body is attacked or destroyed, one cannot die, for part of the soul remains earthbound and undamaged."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: If part of your soul is stored away, you can’t fully die because that piece keeps you anchored to life.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "What he particularly wanted from Horace was an opinion on what would happen to the wizard who created more than one Horcrux"
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: Voldemort was trying to learn whether you could split your soul into more than one Horcrux so you could become even harder to kill.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "As far as I know ... no wizard had ever done more than tear his soul in two."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: Nobody, as far as anyone knew, had ever split their soul into lots of pieces before, so Voldemort was experimenting with something unheard of.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "You handed it to me, Harry. The diary, Riddle’s diary, the one giving instructions on how to reopen the Chamber of Secrets."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: The diary I destroyed was actually one of Voldemort's Horcruxes. That explains why the memory inside could act and hurt Ginny.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "A mere memory starting to act and think for itself? A mere memory, sapping the life out of the girl into whose hands it had fallen?"
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: I can’t believe a memory could become that dangerous. The diary wasn’t just a book, it held a piece of him that could act on its own.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "You heard Voldemort: What he particularly wanted from Horace was an opinion ..."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: Voldemort was obsessed and dangerous from a young age. He wasn’t just clever, he was willing to ruin his own soul to avoid death.

Book6-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Merlin’s beard, Tom! Seven! Isn’t it bad enough to think of killing one person? And in any case ... bad enough to divide the soul ... but to rip it into seven pieces ..."
Book6-chapter23_Sc3.description: Slughorn reacted like splitting a soul into seven pieces is monstrous. The idea of multiple Horcruxes is horrifying and unnatural.
Hearing that existence with a split soul is worse than death makes me even more certain Voldemort’s path was monstrous.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "Happy birthday, Ron," said Harry, when they were woken on the first of March by Seamus and Dean leaving noisily for breakfast. "Have a present." He threw the package across onto Ron's bed
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: It's Ron's birthday. I handed him a present and he already has a pile of gifts on his bed.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "I solemnly swear that I am up to no good," so that Neville, who was passing the foot of his bed at the time, would not hear.
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I use the Marauder's Map and hide it after every use. I tapped it and said the charm to open it quietly.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "I don't think he's in his bed. . . ." "He did not seem to be at the Slytherin table in the Great Hall, eating breakfast. . . . He was nowhere near Snape, who was sitting in his study. . . . He wasn't in any of the bathrooms or in the hospital wing."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Malfoy is missing from all the obvious places in the school. He's not at the Slytherin table, not near Snape, and not in any of the bathrooms or the hospital wing.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "There had to be an explanation for Malfoy's periodic disappearances, but he simply could not think what it could be."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Malfoy's disappearances are not random. There must be an explanation, but I don't know what it is yet and tailing him all day is impossible with my schedule.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "Harry tapped the map with his wand, muttered, 'Mischief managed,' though it hadn't been, and got dressed, thinking hard."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I lied to myself with the map and closed it even though I hadn't solved anything.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "'Harry!' said Ron suddenly. 'What?' 'Harry, I can't stand it!' 'You can't stand what?' 'I can’t stop thinking about her!' said Ron hoarsely."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Ron is a complete mess over some girl. I know he's distracted and not himself this morning.
Romilda Vane is the girl Ron can't stop thinking about.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "He turned to leave; he had got two steps toward the door when a crashing blow hit him on the right ear. Staggering, he looked around. Ron's fist was drawn right back; his face was contorted with rage; he was about to strike again."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Ron suddenly gets violent and just hit me. He's furious and about to hit me again.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “No joy,” said Harry, as Ron joined them.
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Right now I didn't get what I wanted from Slughorn. Plain and simple.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: He did not have to creep along, for he met nobody on his way, but this did not surprise him in the slightest: This evening, he was the luckiest person at Hogwarts.
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm on a roll thanks to the Felix Felicis. Everything feels like it's pointing me the right way.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: When he reached the entrance hall he saw that Filch had forgotten to lock the front door.
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Filch left the front door unlocked. That's how I got out.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: It was not strictly on the way, but it seemed clear to Harry that this was a whim on which he should act, so he directed his feet immediately toward the vegetable patch, where he was pleased, but not altogether surprised, to find Professor Slughorn in conversation with Professor Sprout.
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Going to the vegetable patch paid off. Slughorn was there when I showed up.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “It’s not ev’ryone appreciates how beau’iful they are,” said Hagrid to Slughorn’s back.
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Aragog has died. Hagrid is crushed and wants a proper burial.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “But acromantula venom is very valuable . . . If the beast only just died it might not yet have dried out. . . . Of course, I wouldn’t want to do anything insensitive if Hagrid is upset . . . but if there was any way to procure some . . . I mean, it’s almost impossible to get venom from an acromantula while it’s alive. . . .”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Slughorn's interest in Aragog is not sentimental. He sees the spider's venom as something valuable to obtain.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “Well, if you wanted to come, Professor, Hagrid would probably be really pleased. . . . Give Aragog a better send-off, you know . . .” “Yes, of course,” said Slughorn, his eyes now gleaming with enthusiasm. “I tell you what, Harry, I’ll meet you down there with a bottle or two.”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: I got Slughorn to come to Hagrid's and pretend to pay respects. He agreed quick enough when there was something in it for him.

Book6-chapter25_Sc2.source: "It was Snape who had overheard the prophecy. It was Snape who had carried the news of the prophecy to Voldemort."
Book6-chapter25_Sc2.description: He did it. Snape listened at the door and told Voldemort, and because of him my mum and dad were hunted. I am furious and I want answers.

Book6-chapter25_Sc2.source: "I believe it to be hidden in a cave on the coast many miles from here"
Book6-chapter25_Sc2.description: Dumbledore thinks a Horcrux is hidden in a seaside cave that Tom Riddle haunted. We're going after it.

Book6-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Harry, I promised that you could come with me."
Book6-chapter25_Sc2.description: Dumbledore is still trusting me enough to bring me along. I feel needed and I refuse to be left out, no matter how angry I am.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Those two girls I saw him with when he missed Quidditch — ha! Crabbe and Goyle!" "Do you mean to say," said Hermione in a hushed voice, "that that little girl whose scales I repaired — ?" "Yeah, of course!" said Harry loudly, staring at her.
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Of course they were Crabbe and Goyle in disguise. I keep walking past Malfoy and his lot and not twigging he's right under our noses.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Well, they wouldn’t, would they, if he’s shown them his Dark Mark?" said Harry.
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: If Malfoy has shown them the Dark Mark then that explains why they put up with him. That changes how dangerous this lot might be.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "But, Harry, before you get all excited, I still don’t think you’ll be able to get into the Room of Requirement without knowing what’s there first. And I don’t think you should forget" — she heaved her bag onto her shoulder and gave him a very serious look — "that what you’re supposed to be concentrating on is getting that memory from Slughorn. Good night."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: I know I need that memory from Slughorn. As much as I want to chase Malfoy, getting Slughorn's memory is what matters most right now.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Late again, Potter," said Snape coldly, as Harry hurried into the candlelit classroom. "Ten points from Gryffindor."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Snape still hates me and is happy to punish me for any slip up. I can't let him wind me up but it still gets to me.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "I haven’t forgotten about Slughorn, but I haven’t got a clue how to get that memory off him, and until I get a brain wave why shouldn’t I find out what Malfoy’s doing?"
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: I have no idea how to get Slughorn's memory out of him yet. While I try to work that out, it makes sense to find out what Malfoy is up to.

Book6-chapter23_Sc2.source: All right, I lied! I was annoyed you woke me up! The password’s still 'tapeworm'!
Book6-chapter23_Sc2.description: I lied because I was annoyed you woke me up, and the password is still 'tapeworm'.
I said 'toffee éclairs' to the gargoyle so it would let me in.

Book6-chapter23_Sc2.source: Sir, I’ve got it. I’ve got the memory from Slughorn.
Book6-chapter23_Sc2.description: I've got the memory from Slughorn in this tiny bottle. This is what we've been after.

Book6-chapter23_Sc2.source: Sir, I’ve got it. I’ve got the memory from Slughorn.
Book6-chapter23_Sc2.description: Of course I've got it now. I actually have the memory and I can show it to Dumbledore.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: He doesn’t want to talk to me, Hermione!
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: He doesn’t want to talk to me. He can tell I’ve been trying to get him on his own and he won’t let it happen.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I pulled the Marauder’s Map and his Invisibility Cloak from his bag.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I use the Marauder’s Map and the Invisibility Cloak to get around and see what’s going on without being seen.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: There, alone in the seventh-floor corridor, was Gregory Goyle.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: If Goyle’s standing outside that wall, someone is inside and they’re guarding the room.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: Hello . . . you’re very pretty, aren’t you?
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I scared Goyle off by talking to him quietly. Making him panic confirms people like him are easily rattled.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I thought she looked terrible: thinner than usual, her mouse-colored hair lank.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Tonks looked awful and off her normal self. She’s not her usual confident self.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: He’s not there. Apparently he’s gone away again.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Dumbledore’s not in his office. He’s gone away again and people don’t seem to know where he is.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I’m sorry. I mean . . . I miss him, as well.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I miss Sirius. Saying it out loud made it clear I’m still grieving and that other people notice when his name is mentioned.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I wondered whether it hadn’t become . . . you know . . . him.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: When Tonks nearly cried at Sirius’s name and her Patronus changed, I started wondering if her Patronus might have become him. Maybe she’s attached to Sirius in some way.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: No one from the Order writes to me anymore, said Harry, not since Sirius —
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I don’t get letters from the Order anymore since Sirius died. I’m out of the loop.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: Losing his patience completely, Harry ran at the wall and kicked it.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I get furious when I can’t find answers. I’ll keep pushing until I get something.

Book6-chapter27_Sc3.description: He's hurt. Albus is injured and I have to get him help.

Book6-chapter27_Sc3.source: “Madam Rosmerta, can he come into the Three Broomsticks while I go up to the school and get help for him?”
Book6-chapter27_Sc3.description: I need to move him inside the pub so I can run up to Hogwarts and fetch help.

Book6-chapter27_Sc3.source: “The — the Dark Mark, Albus.” And she pointed into the sky, in the direction of Hogwarts.
Book6-chapter27_Sc3.description: The Dark Mark is hovering over Hogwarts. Something terrible is happening there right now.

Book6-chapter27_Sc3.source: “If you help me support him,” said Harry, not listening to her, “I think we can get him inside —”
Book6-chapter27_Sc3.description: If someone helps me carry him we can get Albus into the Three Broomsticks immediately.

Book6-chapter26_Sc2.description: Magic does leave traces. Things like a hidden boat or a chain can be tracked by someone who knows the maker's style.

Book6-chapter26_Sc2.source: Voldemort would never have expected a sixteen-year-old to reach this place: I think it unlikely that your powers will register compared to mine
Book6-chapter26_Sc2.description: Voldemort did not expect someone my age to get this far. I'm not supposed to 'register' the same way as a powerful adult wizard.

Book6-chapter26_Sc2.source: I think we must resign ourselves to the fact that they will, at some point, realize we are not Lord Voldemort
Book6-chapter26_Sc2.description: The creatures in the lake will probably react once they figure out we are not Voldemort. They're dangerous and we can't assume they'll stay calm.
There are dead bodies floating under the water. They look eerie and they can lunge out when disturbed.

Book6-chapter26_Sc2.source: I can only conclude that this potion is supposed to be drunk
Book6-chapter26_Sc2.description: That green potion has been set up so you have to drink it to reach whatever is at the bottom. You can't scoop it out or charm it away.

Book6-chapter26_Sc2.source: Once and for all, Harry, do I have your word that you will do all in your power to make me keep drinking?
Book6-chapter26_Sc2.description: I was brought along so I would force Dumbledore to keep drinking even if it hurts him. I promised to follow his orders even when it scares me.
Dumbledore literally cannot get close to the potion because of his burned hand. He needs me to do the difficult part if things go wrong.

Book6-chapter27_Sc1.source: "We did it, Professor!" "We did it! We got the Horcrux!"
Book6-chapter27_Sc1.description: We did it. We actually got the Horcrux.
That potion was not a health drink. It messed him up and knocked him right down.

Book6-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Sir — it’s okay, sir, you’re going to be all right, don’t worry —"
Book6-chapter27_Sc1.description: I have to get him to the hospital wing. I can't leave him here; I need to help him now.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "positively awed when he told them about Voldemort’s Horcruxes and Dumbledore’s promise to take Harry along, should he find another one."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Dumbledore is going to take me with him if he finds another Horcrux. I'm actually going to go with Dumbledore and try to destroy them.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "having first cast the Muffliato spell upon those nearest them"
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: I silenced the people near us with Muffliato so I could tell Ron and Hermione everything without being overheard.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Ginny and Dean split up too, Harry."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Ginny and Dean have split up. That could affect the Quidditch team if they're not speaking.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Harry’s vinegar turned to ice; Ron’s flask exploded."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: My Charms worked; my vinegar turned to ice during the lesson.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “I’m really well!” she said happily. “They let me out of St. Mungo’s on Monday, I had a couple of days at home with Mum and Dad and then came back here this morning.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Katie’s back and she’s fine. They let her out of St. Mungo’s and she even went home for a few days.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “No,” said Katie, shaking her head ruefully. “Everyone’s been asking me, but I haven’t got a clue. The last thing I remember was walking into the ladies’ in the Three Broomsticks.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Someone gave Katie the necklace in the girls' bathroom at the Three Broomsticks and she has no memory of who did it.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “Or someone who looked like a girl or a woman,” said Harry. “Don’t forget, there was a cauldron full of Polyjuice Potion at Hogwarts. We know some of it got stolen.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: It might not have been actually a woman. With Polyjuice around, any bloke could have been made to look like a girl. That makes the whole thing more dangerous.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “I think I’m going to take another swig of Felix,” said Harry, “and have a go at the Room of Requirement again.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: I want another hit of Felix and I’m going back to the Room of Requirement to try again. I’m not giving up on finding what we need.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: Harry pulled his copy of Advanced Potion-Making out of his bag and looked up Felix Felicis. “Blimey, it’s seriously complicated,” he said, running an eye down the list of ingredients. “And it takes six months.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Felix is really complicated and takes six months to brew. I can’t just make a quick stash of it.

Book6-chapter27_Sc4.source: "There it was, hanging in the sky above the school: the blazing green skull with a serpent tongue, the mark Death Eaters left behind whenever they had entered a building . . . wherever they had murdered."
Book6-chapter27_Sc4.description: The Dark Mark is over Hogwarts. That green skull with the serpent tongue is hanging above the school and it means Death Eaters have been there.

Book6-chapter27_Sc4.source: "Dread flooded Harry at the sound of the words."
Book6-chapter27_Sc4.description: I felt dread the second I saw the Mark. This is serious, that feeling was instant and cold.

Book6-chapter27_Sc4.source: "Go and wake Severus," said Dumbledore faintly but clearly. "Tell him what has happened and bring him to me. Do nothing else, speak to nobody else, and do not remove your Cloak."
Book6-chapter27_Sc4.description: Dumbledore wants Severus woken and brought to him, and he ordered me to say nothing to anyone and not to take off the Invisibility Cloak.

Book6-chapter27_Sc4.source: "Rosmerta, please send a message to the Ministry," said Dumbledore.
Book6-chapter27_Sc4.description: Dumbledore wants Rosmerta to contact the Ministry right away in case nobody at Hogwarts knows yet.

Book6-chapter27_Sc4.source: "I've got a couple behind the bar," she said, looking very frightened. "Shall I run and fetch — ?" "No, Harry can do it." Harry raised his wand at once. "Accio Rosmerta's Brooms!"
Book6-chapter27_Sc4.description: There are brooms behind the bar in the pub and I can summon them with Accio. Two brooms came racing out and stopped by me.

Book6-chapter28_Sc1.source: "As they vanished through the door, Harry realized he could move again. What was now holding him paralyzed against the wall was not magic, but horror and shock."
Book6-chapter28_Sc1.description: I was frozen with horror, not a spell. It wasn't magic stopping me, it was shock. Once they moved I could move.

Book6-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Out of here, quickly," said Snape. He seized Malfoy by the scruff of the neck and forced him through the door ahead of the rest;
Book6-chapter28_Sc1.description: Snape shoved Malfoy out and barked at everyone to get out. He wasn't hanging about, he grabbed Malfoy and forced him through the door.
I blasted the Death Eater with Petrificus Totalus and he went rigid. That let me clamber over him and get down the stairs.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Or someone who looked like a girl or a woman," said Harry.
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: There was Polyjuice involved at Hogwarts and people could look like girls or women if they wanted. That could explain a lot about who was sneaking around.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I think I\'m going to take another swig of Felix," said Harry, "and have a go at the Room of Requirement again."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: I kept thinking more Felix would fix things, especially to get time alone with Ginny or to slip into the Room of Requirement, but Hermione was right that luck only goes so far.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "He had still not found out what it did, mainly because he did not want to test it around Hermione, but he was considering trying it out on McLaggen"
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: I had Sectumsempra marked in Advanced Potion-Making and I really did not know what it did. I was tempted to try it on McLaggen if I ever got the chance.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "The battle still raged inside his head: Ginny or Ron?"
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: I'm stuck between wanting Ginny and not wanting to betray Ron. I keep talking to Ginny and looking for chances to be alone with her, but I'm worried about Ron's reaction.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "he saw Malfoy\'s tiny, labeled dot standing in a boys\' bathroom on the floor below, accompanied, not by Crabbe or Goyle, but by Moaning Myrtle."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Malfoy was in a bathroom with Moaning Myrtle, and when I found him he was actually crying and terrified about something he had to do.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "SECTUMSEMPRA! bellowed Harry from the floor, waving his wand wildly."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: I cast Sectumsempra without knowing what it would do and it seriously injured Malfoy. I feel sick about it and I did not mean for him to get hurt like that.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Apparently I underestimated you, Potter," he said quietly. "Who would have thought you knew such Dark Magic? Who taught you that spell?"
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Snape thinks I know Dark Magic because I used Sectumsempra. He suspects I learned it from somewhere suspicious and he is furious.

Book6-chapter28_Sc2.source: "What was now holding him paralyzed against the wall was not magic, but horror and shock."
Book6-chapter28_Sc2.description: I was frozen by pure horror, not by a spell. I couldn't move because I was terrified, not because someone had me under a jinx.

Book6-chapter28_Sc2.source: "'Petrificus Totalus!' The Death Eater buckled as though hit in the back with something solid and fell to the ground, rigid as a waxwork"
Book6-chapter28_Sc2.description: I cast or someone cast Petrificus Totalus on that Death Eater and he went rigid. That gave me a way past him.

Book6-chapter28_Sc2.source: "He had to get to Dumbledore and he had to catch Snape. Somehow the two things were linked."
Book6-chapter28_Sc2.description: Dumbledore and Snape are connected in whatever just happened. If I can get them both together I can undo this.
Dumbledore is not dead. I refuse to accept that. There has to be some way to fix this.

Book6-chapter28_Sc2.source: "he heard the hated voice shout, 'It's over, time to go!' and saw Snape disappearing around the corner at the far end of the corridor; he and Malfoy seemed to have forced their way through the fight unscathed."
Book6-chapter28_Sc2.description: Snape shouted it's over and ran off with Malfoy. They got through the fight without a scratch. They're the ones who left when everything exploded.

Book6-chapter27_Sc5.description: I protested, but he reminded me I swore to obey him, so I have to do as he says even if I don't want to.

Book6-chapter27_Sc5.source: "You swore to obey me, Harry - go!"
Book6-chapter27_Sc5.description: He's ordering me to leave and expects me to follow that promise right away.
He's staying behind and waiting, so I'm the one who has to move on.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "No Muggle could reach this rock unless they were uncommonly good mountaineers, and boats cannot approach the cliffs, the waters around them are too dangerous."
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: This place is impossible for ordinary people to get to. Voldemort or his kind had to use magic to bring victims here.
The cave is saturated with magic. I could feel it as soon as we got in.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I rather think that we are required to make payment to pass."
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: To get through the entrance the door wants blood as payment. It is crude and ugly but it is the lock.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "But your blood is worth more than mine."
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: Dumbledore was willing to use his own blood but he thought my blood mattered more for the protection on the door. He treats me like I matter in this fight.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I think the Horcrux is in the middle."
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: The Horcrux is not at the bottom or on the shore. It sits in the middle of that black lake.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Something, I think, that is ready to respond should we attempt to seize the Horcrux."
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: The lake is defended by things that will react if we try to grab the Horcrux. Trying an obvious trick told us that.

Book6-chapter26_Sc1.source: "You are very kind, Harry," said Dumbledore, now passing the tip of his wand over the deep cut he had made in his own arm, so that it healed instantly, just as Snape had healed Malfoy’s wounds.
Book6-chapter26_Sc1.description: Dumbledore can heal himself fast. I stopped thinking of him as just frail with one bad hand. He can still do real, serious magic when it counts.
Dumbledore's light showed us the fissure and the path. Small spells like that can change everything in a dangerous place.

Book6-chapter26_Sc3.source: "You\'ve got to keep drinking, remember? You told me you had to keep drinking."
Book6-chapter26_Sc3.description: He needs to keep drinking that potion even if it tortures him. I had to force him to keep going to get to the Horcrux.
When he came back to himself he needed water badly. I tried every spell and even plunged the goblet into the lake to get him any I could.
Dumbledore is fallible and exhausted. He can still work magic, but he can also be wiped out and need me to help him. I can actually support him when he cannot go on alone.

Book6-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore scooped the locket from the bottom of the stone basin and stowed it inside his robes."
Book6-chapter26_Sc3.description: The locket was down there in the basin and he took it. That thing is one of the pieces we are after and he made sure it was safe.
He relied on me and praised me for it. I did not just follow orders, I saved us both from the Inferi and helped him when he was weak.

Book6-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Through the darkness, fire erupted: crimson and gold, a ring of fire that surrounded the rock so that the Inferi... did not dare pass through the flames."
Book6-chapter26_Sc3.description: Fire stops Inferi. Dumbledore made that ring and it kept them safe long enough to leave. Fire is the one thing they will not cross.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "He was a genius, the Prince. Anyway . . . without his bezoar tip . . . I wouldn’t be here to discuss it, would I?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Right now I think the Prince was brilliant at Potions and his tricks saved people. I still want that book back because it helps, even if I know Snape might be after it.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "He wants me to go to his office as quick as I can!"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Dumbledore wants to see me straight away. I need to go, maybe he found something about the book or he has important news.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "He’s hinting now that if I don’t get all the boxes done by the end of term, we’ll carry on next year."
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Snape is piling on detentions to keep me away from everything I want to be doing, and it feels deliberate. He is definitely making my life harder.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "I told her it’s a Hungarian Horntail," said Ginny
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Ginny teases people about the tattoo nonsense and she sits close to me. I like having her around and I don’t want Snape’s detentions to steal my time with her.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "I walked into the room and I heard a voice, which has never happened before in all my years of hiding — of using the room, I mean."
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Trelawney says someone was in the Room of Requirement and there was a whooping voice in there. If someone else is using it then my book might be at risk.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "Bring me your schoolbag," said Snape softly, "and all of your schoolbooks. All of them. Bring them to me here. Now!"
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: Snape is going to take my books and he knows about that Potions book. I have to get it back if I can.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "Do you know what I think, Potter?" said Snape, very quietly. "I think that you are a liar and a cheat and that you deserve detention with me every Saturday until the end of term."
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: Snape thinks I cheated and he has me down for detention every Saturday until the end of term. Great timing with the match.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "The Prince only copied it out! It’s not like he was advising anyone to use it!"
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: I still defend the book because I believe the Prince just copied spells for his own notes, not to encourage anyone to use them.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "This is the copy of Advanced Potion-Making that you purchased from Flourish and Blotts?" "Yes," said Harry firmly. "Then why," asked Snape, "does it have the name ‘Roonil Wazlib’ written inside the front cover?"
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: Someone has my Potions book under a fake name in it. That name in the front cover has landed me in even more trouble.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "I had just told her that she would be playing Seeker on Saturday and that Dean would be rejoining the team as Chaser in her place."
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: I told Ginny she would play Seeker and I hoped it would fix things between her and Dean. I want to protect her and make things right if I can.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "They are the records of other Hogwarts wrongdoers and their punishments. Where the ink has grown faint, or the cards have suffered damage from mice, we would like you to copy out the crimes and punishments afresh and, making sure that they are in alphabetical order, replace them in the boxes. You will not use magic."
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: My Saturday detentions are pointless, boring copy work and I am not allowed to use magic. Snape is enjoying making me do it.

Book6-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Voldemort murdered him and then stepped over his body toward my mum,"
Book6-chapter22_Sc3.description: Voldemort killed my dad first and then went for my mum. She could have run but she chose to protect me.
I accept that I'm the Chosen One and that means I have to stop him. I need information that will help me do it.
Slughorn just gave me the memory I needed. He helped me even though he was ashamed. I owe him for this.

Book6-chapter22_Sc3.source: "I had him from an egg, yeh know," said Hagrid morosely.
Book6-chapter22_Sc3.description: Hagrid raised Aragog from an egg. He was very attached to him.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "He hated my dad like he hated Sirius! Haven’t you noticed, Professor, how the people Snape hates tend to end up dead?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Snape hated my dad and Sirius. People Snape hates often end up dead. That makes me suspicious as hell of him.
Dumbledore trusts Snape, but I do not. I think Snape is up to something with Malfoy and I am not convinced by anyone who tells me otherwise.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "I take you with me on one condition: that you obey any command I might give you at once, and without question."
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: If I go with Dumbledore I must follow orders instantly, even if he tells me to run or hide or leave him. I promised I would.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "Very good. Then I wish you to go and fetch your Invisibility Cloak and meet me in the entrance hall in five minutes’ time."
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wants me to come along tonight and told me to grab the Invisibility Cloak and meet him fast.
I took the Marauder’s Map and Felix Felicis and shoved the map at Hermione and the potion at Ron because I need them to watch Malfoy and Snape while I go with Dumbledore.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore says he’s put extra protection in the school,"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Dumbledore put extra protections in the school for tonight, but if Snape is involved he might know how to get around them. That is why I want my friends watching.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "You need what’s wrapped in them, it’s the Felix Felicis."
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: I trust Ron and Hermione to keep an eye on things while I go with Dumbledore. I left them tools to help: the map and some Felix Felicis.

Book6-chapter28_Sc5.description: Hagrid's hut is burning and Fang is trapped inside. I heard Hagrid yelling about Fang and we had to put the flames out with Aguamenti.

Book6-chapter28_Sc5.source: "You haven’t got the nerve or the ability" and "No Unforgivable Curses from you, Potter!"
Book6-chapter28_Sc5.description: Snape kept blocking my spells and taunting me, saying I can't use Unforgivable Curses and that I lack the nerve and skill.

Book6-chapter28_Sc5.source: "You dare use my own spells against me, Potter? It was I who invented them... I, the Half-Blood Prince!"
Book6-chapter28_Sc5.description: Snape was the one who invented those spells in my old Potions book. He calls himself the Half-Blood Prince and is furious that I used them.

Book6-chapter28_Sc5.source: "Have you forgotten our orders? Potter belongs to the Dark Lord — we are to leave him! Go! Go!"
Book6-chapter28_Sc5.description: The Death Eaters were told to leave me for Voldemort, and Snape ordered the others to go even while he stayed fighting me.
Dumbledore is dead and I saw Snape kill him. I couldn't believe it when I told Hagrid and he didn't want to accept it.
Buckbeak attacked Snape and that gave Snape a chance to escape. The hippogriff circled the gates while Snape Disapparated.
Fang survived the fire and was alive and howling when we put the flames out. He's okay, which felt like the only good thing in that moment.

Book6-chapter28_Sc5.source: "You dare use my own spells against me, Potter?... I, the Half-Blood Prince!" and Harry's internal: "he now hated as much as he hated Voldemort himself"
Book6-chapter28_Sc5.description: I hate Snape more than I thought possible. After everything I saw and after Dumbledore, my anger at Snape is as strong as my hatred for Voldemort.

Book7-chapter3_Sc3.source: You’ve got to go into hiding and the Order wants to help. You’re being offered serious protection, the best there is.
Book7-chapter3_Sc3.description: They want us to go into hiding and the Order is offering real protection, the best they can give.

Book7-chapter3_Sc3.source: You heard what Mr. Weasley and Kingsley said. We think the Ministry has been infiltrated.
Book7-chapter3_Sc3.description: The Ministry can’t be trusted anymore. I believe people inside it have been turned against us.

Book7-chapter3_Sc3.source: I still don’t see why we can’t have that Kingsley bloke.
Book7-chapter3_Sc3.description: My uncle keeps wanting someone official like Kingsley to take charge. He still looks to the establishment for protection even when he hates and mistrusts the magical world.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: I should've shown the book to Dumbledore," said Harry.
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: I should have shown that book to Dumbledore. I kept thinking I had proof Snape was like Voldemort at school, and I blamed myself for not telling Dumbledore.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: I’ll bet Dumbledore knew his mother was called ‘Prince.’
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: Dumbledore probably knew the Prince bit about Snape's family. That makes me think Dumbledore might have known more than he let on.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: "I can't be involved with you anymore. We can't be together."
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: I can't be with Ginny anymore. I have to do things on my own and I won't put her in danger just because we're together.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: So they got in through the Room of Requirement.
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: They used the Room of Requirement and those Vanishing Cabinets to get Death Eaters into the castle. That's how they walked straight in.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: He was, but to help them, not to stop them
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: Snape wasn't trying to stop the Death Eaters. He came back to help them, not to save us. I can't stand it.
Snape shouted 'It's over' after he came through the dust with Malfoy. He meant it. He did what he'd planned.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: I don't think he knew they were coming before Filius told him
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: At first I thought Snape might not have known, but everything fits together now and he still helped them. That makes him just as guilty.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: We found the Death Eaters minutes later, heading in the direction of the Astronomy Tower.
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: After they came through the Room of Requirement, the Death Eaters were heading straight for the Astronomy Tower. That's where it all built up.

Book6-chapter30_Sc5.source: "You are, of course, devastated," he said. "I know that you were very close to Dumbledore. I think you may have been his favorite pupil ever. The bond between the two of you —"
Book6-chapter30_Sc5.description: So Scrimgeour thinks I was Dumbledore's favorite and expects me to be devastated. He is using how close we were as leverage.

Book6-chapter30_Sc5.source: "The word is that you were with him when he left the school the night that he died."
Book6-chapter30_Sc5.description: They are saying I was with Dumbledore the night he left and want people to believe I know more than I will tell.

Book6-chapter30_Sc5.source: "The Ministry can offer you all sorts of protection, you know, Harry. I would be delighted to place a couple of my Aurors at your service —"
Book6-chapter30_Sc5.description: I don't buy their protection. Voldemort wants to kill me himself, and Aurors will not stop him. I will not trade silence or loyalty for a couple of guards.

Book6-chapter30_Sc5.source: "the request I made of you at Christmas —" "What request? Oh yeah . . . the one where I tell the world what a great job you’re doing in exchange for —" "— for raising everyone’s morale!"
Book6-chapter30_Sc5.description: He wanted me to publicly praise the Ministry to boost morale in return for favors. I see how they try to use me as a propaganda tool instead of actually helping.

Book6-chapter30_Sc5.source: "Released Stan Shunpike yet?" "I see you are —" "Dumbledore’s man through and through," said Harry. "That’s right."
Book6-chapter30_Sc5.description: I'm not going to be their mouthpiece. They think I'm Dumbledore's man and they hate that. That loyalty is mine and I will not sell it.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "The ring is no longer a Horcrux."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: The ring that was a Horcrux is gone. It was hidden in the Gaunts' ruin and Dumbledore destroyed it.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "You destroyed the diary and I the ring, but if we are right in our theory of a seven-part soul, four Horcruxes remain."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: There are more Horcruxes out there. We took out two, but there are still at least four left.
Dumbledore thinks the locket and Hufflepuff's cup are definitely Horcruxes.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "The remaining two, assuming again that he created a total of six, are more of a problem... I will hazard a guess that, having secured objects from Hufflepuff and Slytherin, he set out to track down objects owned by Gryffindor or Ravenclaw."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Voldemort probably wanted items from the four founders. He definitely has Slytherin and maybe Hufflepuff. He might have something from Ravenclaw or Gryffindor.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "I think I know what the sixth Horcrux is. I wonder what you will say when I confess that I have been curious for a while about the behavior of the snake, Nagini?"
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Dumbledore guesses Nagini, the snake, might be a Horcrux. Voldemort could have turned her into one after she killed someone.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "So, the diary's gone, the ring's gone. The cup, the locket, and the snake are still intact..."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Summary: diary and ring destroyed. Cup, locket, and Nagini still exist. There may also be a founder's item left.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "And if you do," said Harry quickly, "can I come with you and help get rid of it?" Dumbledore looked at Harry very intently for a moment before saying, "Yes, I think so."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Dumbledore trusts me enough to let me help look for and destroy Horcruxes. I can join him on the mission.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "Does Voldemort know when a Horcrux is destroyed, sir? Can he feel it?" "A very interesting question, Harry. I believe not."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Voldemort probably does not instantly know when a Horcrux is destroyed. He might feel it only at death or later, not immediately.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "Without his Horcruxes, Voldemort will be a mortal man with a maimed and diminished soul."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: If all the Horcruxes are destroyed, Voldemort can be killed. He will still be dangerous, but mortal.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "You have a power that Voldemort has never had. You can —" "I know!" said Harry impatiently. "I can love!"
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: My ability to love is a real power against Voldemort. It's not flashy, but it's what protects me and makes me dangerous to him.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "If Voldemort had never heard of the prophecy, would it have been fulfilled? Would it have meant anything? Of course not!"
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: The prophecy only mattered because Voldemort acted on it. He made me his enemy by choosing to try to kill me.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "Imagine, please, just for a moment, that you had never heard that prophecy! How would you feel about Voldemort now? Think!"
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Even without the prophecy, I would still want to finish Voldemort. I wouldn't rest until I tried to stop him.

Book6-chapter23_Sc5.source: "That one of us is going to end up killing the other," said Harry. "Yes."
Book6-chapter23_Sc5.description: Dumbledore and I agree that it's likely one of us will end up killing the other. It's grim but real.

Book6-chapter28_Sc3.description: Fenrir lunged at me and I hit him with Petrificus Totalus. He collapsed on top of me and I shoved him off so I could get away.
I dropped in on Ginny and Amycus and fired Impedimenta to help her. I will jump into fights if it helps my friends.

Book6-chapter28_Sc3.source: Snape must not escape, he must catch up with Snape
Book6-chapter28_Sc3.description: Snape cannot get away. I have to chase him down even if everything else is chaos around me.

Book6-chapter28_Sc3.source: Harry, where did you come from?
Book6-chapter28_Sc3.description: Ginny saw me appear out of nowhere. I pop up where I'm needed and I move fast, even when I'm muddy and bleeding.
McGonagall attacked and distracted enemies so I could close in. The teachers are fighting too and I have to press on.
Neville is down but conscious. He told me Snape and Malfoy ran past, so they are ahead and I have to catch them.

Book6-chapter28_Sc3.source: Snape had an immense head start.
Book6-chapter28_Sc3.description: Even though I sprinted, Snape is already far ahead. I need to push myself harder if I'm going to catch him.

Book6-chapter28_Sc4.source: Was it possible that he had already entered the cabinet in the Room of Requirement, or had the Order made steps to secure it, to prevent the Death Eaters retreating that way?
Book6-chapter28_Sc4.description: The Room of Requirement might be blocked off so they cannot escape through the cabinet, or one of them's already gone in and I'm too late

Book6-chapter28_Sc4.source: he spotted a bloody footprint that showed at least one of the fleeing Death Eaters was heading toward the front doors
Book6-chapter28_Sc4.description: Someone left a bloody footprint leading to the front doors so at least one of them is heading that way

Book6-chapter28_Sc4.source: He could just make out three figures racing across the lawn, heading for the gates beyond which they could Disapparate
Book6-chapter28_Sc4.description: There are three of them running for the gates to Disapparate: the huge blond Death Eater, and Snape and Malfoy

Book6-chapter28_Sc4.source: “Out of the way!” yelled Harry, knocking two boys aside as he sprinted toward the landing and down the remainder of the marble staircase.
Book6-chapter28_Sc4.description: I pushed past everyone without waiting because I had to catch them now

Book6-chapter28_Sc4.source: The oak front doors had been blasted open, there were smears of blood on the flagstones, and several terrified students stood huddled against the walls
Book6-chapter28_Sc4.description: The front entrance is wrecked and people are terrified; whatever happened inside spilled out onto the grounds

Book7-chapter3_Sc1.description: He's calling me like he always does. Sixteen years of that exact yell means I'm the one he wants again. Great.

Book7-chapter3_Sc1.source: ["in which, for a split second, he had thought he saw Dumbledore’s eye"]
Book7-chapter3_Sc1.description: For a moment I actually thought I saw Dumbledore's eye in the mirror shard. I couldn't believe it!

Book7-chapter2_Sc1.source: “I? I see myself holding a pair of thick, woolen socks.”
Book7-chapter2_Sc1.description: I saw myself holding a pair of thick woolen socks when I looked in the mirror. Not some grand family or glory, just socks. Weird and a bit sharp, but that's what I saw.

Book7-chapter2_Sc1.source: After several minutes’ thought, Harry tore the obituary out of the Prophet, folded it carefully, and tucked it inside the first volume of Practical Defensive Magic and Its Use Against the Dark Arts.
Book7-chapter2_Sc1.description: I tore the obituary out of the Prophet, folded it and shoved it inside my Practical Defensive Magic book. I don't want it lying around or anyone else looking at it. I need to keep it to myself for now.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . . He’s just like Voldemort. Pure-blood mother, Muggle father . . . ashamed of his parentage, trying to make himself feared using the Dark Arts, gave himself an impressive new name — Lord Voldemort — the Half-Blood Prince — how could Dumbledore have missed — ?"
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: He pretended to be something he was not to fit in with the pure-blood lot. That is exactly what I hate about him. He used his background to get power and respect.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "He knew when I used Sectumsempra. He didn’t really need Legilimency. . . . He might even have known before then, with Slughorn talking about how brilliant I was at Potions. . . . Shouldn’t have left his old book in the bottom of that cupboard, should he?"
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: I can't believe I was fooled. I trusted him because he helped me, and now I think he knew what I was doing and still let it go on.
I see Snape very differently now. I used to respect him more. Now I feel betrayed and angry. I don't trust him anymore.

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: "I care," said Harry. "How do you think I’d feel if this was your funeral . . . and it was my fault. . . ."
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: I care about Ginny. If anything happened to her because of me I would never forgive myself

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: "I never really gave up on you," she said. "Not really. I always hoped. . . ."
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: Ginny never stopped hoping for me and she still likes me. I wish I'd asked her out sooner because we could have had time together

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: Moving felt much more bearable than sitting still, just as setting out as soon as possible to track down the Horcruxes and kill Voldemort would feel better than waiting to do it.
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: I need to get moving and start hunting Horcruxes right away. Staying here with everyone would break me and stop me from doing what must be done

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: Harry could not bear to hear these things, nor did he think his resolution would hold if he remained sitting beside her.
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: I can't stand listening to how she feels right now. It hurts too much and I don't think I could stick to my plan if I stayed

Book7-chapter2_Sc3.source: He was sure that the Ministry was leaning on the Prophet to suppress news about Voldemort.
Book7-chapter2_Sc3.description: The Prophet is covering up Voldemort. The Ministry must be squeezing them to keep anything important about him out of the paper.

Book7-chapter2_Sc3.source: Rita Skeeter reveals the disturbed childhood, the lawless youth, the lifelong feuds, and the guilty secrets that Dumbledore carried to his grave.
Book7-chapter2_Sc3.description: Rita's running a smear piece on Dumbledore. She's digging up everything she can, saying he had a troubled childhood, a reckless youth and all these secrets.

Book7-chapter2_Sc3.source: The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore, by Rita Skeeter, exclusively interviewed by Betty Braithwaite, page 13, inside.
Book7-chapter2_Sc3.description: There's a full biography coming out next week called The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore by Rita Skeeter. It's meant to blow the lid off everything.

Book7-chapter2_Sc3.source: WHAT was the real purpose of the secret organization known as the Order of the Phoenix?
Book7-chapter2_Sc3.description: People are going to start asking what the Order was really up to. If this gets out, everyone will question why Dumbledore kept it secret.

Book7-chapter2_Sc3.source: HOW did Dumbledore really meet his end? The answers to these and many more questions are explored in the explosive new biography
Book7-chapter2_Sc3.description: They're even promising to explain how Dumbledore died. They're turning his death into another scandalous story.

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "She\'s not that bad," said Harry. "Ugly, though," he added hastily, as Ginny raised her eyebrows, and she let out a reluctant giggle.
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: Well, I suppose I can live with her if Mum can. I don’t like saying it, but I don’t hate Fleur outright.

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "Of course there isn\'t," said Harry, who became angry every time this subject cropped up.
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: They won\'t find Snape until they find Voldemort. They never have, so they won\'t now. That just makes me furious.

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: He kept reciting their names to himself, as though by listing them he could bring them within reach: the locket . . . the cup . . . the snake . . . something of Gryffindor\'s or Ravenclaw\'s . . .
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: There are Horcruxes out there and I have to find them. The locket, the cup, the snake, something from Gryffindor or Ravenclaw. I have to get them before Voldemort can be killed.
If R.A.B. is involved with the locket, that changes things. Whoever R.A.B. is, they matter to this hunt.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "The real Harry thought that this might just be the most bizarre thing he had ever seen, and he had seen some extremely odd things."
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: That's mental. Seeing six of me stripping and stuffing my things away like it was nothing made my skin crawl.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "He felt like asking them to show a little more respect for his privacy as they all began stripping off with impunity, clearly much more at ease with displaying his body than they would have been with their own."
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: I hate how casual everyone is with my stuff and my image. I want people to treat my privacy like it's worth something.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "An’ you’re with me, Harry. That all righ’?"
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: Right now I'm going with Hagrid on the motorbike in the sidecar. Not thrilled about the attention but that is the plan.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "We think the Death Eaters will expect you to be on a broom,"
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: Moody thinks the Death Eaters will look for the Potters on brooms. So they're setting things up so the broom-riding Potters look most like the real deal.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "They'll be here in about five minutes,"
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: They're coming in about five minutes. I need to be ready.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "We shall be leaving before Harry does. Due to the danger of using magic in your house — Harry being still underage, it could provide the Ministry with an excuse to arrest him — we shall be driving, say, ten miles or so, before Disapparating to the safe location we have picked out for you."
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: The plan is that my relatives will drive away first, go ten miles, then Disapparate to safety so no magic in the house gets traced back to me.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Can't do it," said Hestia tersely. "Mad-Eye will explain."
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: Mad-Eye can't take me by Side-Along-Apparition. Something about it being impossible right now.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "We are attempting to time your departure from the house with your family's Disapparition, Harry; thus, the charm breaks at the moment you all head for safety."
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: They're timing my departure so the protective charm will break exactly when my family gets to safety.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Dad,— I'm going with these Order people." (Dudley) and "For the first time in your life, you're talking sense." (Harry)
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: Dudley actually agreed to go with the Order. If Dudley will go, his parents will too. That means I won't be left behind alone against their stubbornness.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "You saved my life." (Dudley) and "Not really," said Harry. "It was your soul the dementor would have taken."
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: Dudley said I saved his life and thanked me, which is ridiculous but it matters. He admitted I wasn't a waste of space and that shifted things between us, even a bit.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "They think I’m a waste of space, actually, but I’m used to —" and Hestia: "Don’t these people realize what you’ve been through?"
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: My relatives really do think I'm worthless. I'm used to it, but the people coming to help actually care about the danger I'm in and the part I play in this fight.

Book7-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Good day to you, Harry Potter's relatives!" said Dedalus happily, striding into the living room. ... "We shall be leaving before Harry does."
Book7-chapter3_Sc5.description: Dedalus and Hestia are actually polite and painfully cheerful about the whole operation. They're trying to keep things moving and get my family out fast.

Book7-chapter3_Sc4.source: Kingsley is protecting the Mug I mean, your Prime Minister.
Book7-chapter3_Sc4.description: Kingsley is the one protecting the Prime Minister. The Dursleys like him because he looks and sounds proper, but that doesn't change anything about what's happening.
Those crashes and explosions and derailments are not random. They are attacks, not simple accidents.
Voldemort is behind this and he is killing Muggles on purpose. He does it for pleasure, plain and simple.

Book7-chapter3_Sc4.source: Even the fogs they're caused by dementors
Book7-chapter3_Sc4.description: The fogs are caused by dementors. They feed off fear and despair and that's why everything feels worse.

Book7-chapter3_Sc4.source: More? laughed Harry There are hundreds, maybe thousands by this time
Book7-chapter3_Sc4.description: There are far more dementors than the two that attacked us. There could be hundreds or even thousands now because they multiply whenever there's fear.

Book7-chapter3_Sc4.source: But Hestia Jones and Dedalus Diggle are more than up to the job
Book7-chapter3_Sc4.description: I trust people like Hestia Jones and Dedalus Diggle to handle things if needed. They're capable and ready.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Snape killed him," said Harry. "I was there, I saw it. ... and then Snape ... did it. The Avada Kedavra."
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: He's dead. I saw Snape cast Avada Kedavra and kill Dumbledore.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Snape passed Voldemort the information that made Voldemort hunt down my mum and dad. Then Snape told Dumbledore he hadn't realized what he was doing, he was really sorry he'd done it, sorry that they were dead."
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: Snape gave Voldemort the info that led him to my mum and dad. He lied about being sorry to get Dumbledore to trust him.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "He stepped over Bill, but it's all right, he's alive." "Greyback attacked him." "No charm will work on these," said Madam Pomfrey. "I've tried everything I know, but there is no cure for werewolf bites." "No, I don't think that Bill will be a true werewolf," said Lupin, "but that does not mean that there won't be some contamination. Those are cursed wounds. They are unlikely ever to heal fully, and and Bill might have some wolfish characteristics from now on."
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: Bill's alive but he's been horrifically mauled by Greyback. He probably won't become a full werewolf but those wounds are cursed and he could have wolfish traits for ever.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Harry, if we hadn't had your Felix potion, I think we'd all have been killed, but everything seemed to just miss us —"
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: The Felix potion saved us. If we'd not had it, we might all have been killed.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "We’re going to the hospital wing," said Ginny. "I’m not hurt," said Harry. "It’s McGonagall’s orders," said Ginny.
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: People are looking to me and I'm at the center of this. I was with Dumbledore when he died and everyone expects answers from me.

Book7-chapter4_Sc1.source: "He can get along without me for one night," said Kingsley. "You’re more important."
Book7-chapter4_Sc1.description: All right, Kingsley thinks I'm more important than the Muggle Prime Minister for tonight. Fine, I get it, I'm needed here.

Book7-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Harry, guess what?" said Tonks ... and she wiggled her left hand at him; a ring glittered there.
Book7-chapter4_Sc1.description: Okay, Tonks got married. I couldn't be there and it was quiet. That's brilliant for her, even if I missed it.

Book7-chapter4_Sc1.source: "As Dedalus probably told you, we had to abandon Plan A."
Book7-chapter4_Sc1.description: Moody just said Plan A was abandoned. Plans changed. We need to move on and work out the next step.
