Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: Dumbledore is dead. I can't believe he's gone. That's it, the man who kept everything together is gone.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "It wasn't there?" "No," said Harry. "Someone had already taken it and left a fake in its place."
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: Someone stole the Horcrux we went for and left a fake locket. We didn't get it.
The stolen locket had the initials R.A.B. written on it. R.A.B. is connected to whoever took the Horcrux.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "They’re talking about closing the school," said Harry.
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: People are discussing closing Hogwarts because of what's happened tonight. Everything we knew feels like it's falling apart.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "See you in a bit" to Ron, Hermione, and Ginny, and followed Professor McGonagall back down the ward.
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: McGonagall is acting as head now. She wants to talk to me alone, so I'm expected to answer questions and help with what's next.

Book7-chapter6_Sc2.source: Well, Harry, while we’ve still got you here, you won’t mind helping with the preparations for Bill and Fleur’s wedding, will you? There’s still so much to do.
Book7-chapter6_Sc2.description: They want me to help with Bill and Fleur's wedding. There's loads to do and I'm expected to stick around and lend a hand.
Molly treats me like family. She asks me to help and is pleased when I agree, even if it catches me off guard.

Book7-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Well, Dumbledore left me . . . stuff to do," mumbled Harry.
Book7-chapter6_Sc1.description: Dumbledore left me something important to do. He told me about it and I can't just ignore it.

Book7-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Ron and Hermione know about it, and they want to come too."
Book7-chapter6_Sc1.description: Ron and Hermione know what Dumbledore told me and they want to come along. They're choosing to stick by me.

Book7-chapter6_Sc1.source: "I didn't misunderstand," said Harry flatly. "It's got to be me."
Book7-chapter6_Sc1.description: I know it's got to be me who does this. I don't think I misunderstood Dumbledore. This is my responsibility.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: Hedwig's gone. I couldn't believe it when she lay motionless in her cage. I feel sick thinking about it.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "An' the last time yeh was on it, Harry, I could fit yeh in one hand!"
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: Sirius's bike is massive and Hagrid loves it. Sitting in the sidecar makes me feel tiny and exposed.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "It's got a few tricks up its handlebars now. Tha' one was my idea."
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: The bike has crazy built-in tricks and buttons. Hagrid and Arthur have been tinkering with it, and some of those tricks are dangerous.
I can hold my own in a fight from a sidecar. Stunning spells work even when I'm terrified and half falling apart.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "That's him, it's him, it's the real one!"
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: One of the hooded Death Eaters was Stan Shunpike. I hit him with Expelliarmus and that moment made someone shout it's the real one. That makes everything worse and more confusing.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "Voldemort was flying like smoke on the wind"
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: Voldemort can fly without a broom. I saw him up close and my scar burned like mad. He is real and he's hunting me directly.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "As the pain from Harry's scar forced his eyes shut, his wand acted of its own accord."
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: My wand reacts when my scar hurts. When my scar screamed, my wand moved and fired on its own. I can't ignore that anymore.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "I punched it with his wand-free hand and the bike shot more flames into the air"
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: In a panic I can still act. I hit the dragon-fire button to try and save us even when everything was falling apart.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "I don't think anyone in this room would ever sell me to Voldemort."
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: I trust all of you. Even if something went wrong, I don't believe anyone here would betray me to Voldemort.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "I’ve got to go too," said Harry.
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: I need to go with them to recover Mad-Eye's body. I can't just sit here while people are in danger because I'm here.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "It wasn’t me," said Harry flatly. "It was my wand. My wand acted of its own accord."
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: My wand did something on its own and hit Voldemort. I didn't mean to do that magic.
If Voldemort discovers where I am it puts everyone here at risk. That's why me staying is dangerous for them.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "My scar was burning: He felt angry and frustrated; he hated the idea that they were all imagining him to have power to match Voldemort’s."
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: My scar burning tells me something serious is happening and it scares me to think people expect me to have Voldemort-level power.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: Thank God George is alive. I was desperate when I thought he might be dead.
Hermione and Kingsley made it back. At least some of us are accounted for.
Mad-Eye Moody is dead. That hit me like a punch. If Moody is gone then things are worse than I wanted to believe.
George still knows me after everything, even joking about it. That small bit of normality matters to me.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Hedwig's gone. My owl got hit and she's dead. I can't believe she's gone.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Hagrid's fine, son," said the man, "the wife's seeing to him now."
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Hagrid's alive and being looked after. Thank Merlin — he's all right.
Me, Hagrid, George and Hermione are back. The others aren't here with us.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "The Death Eaters were waiting for us," Harry told her. "We were surrounded the moment we took off — they knew it was tonight —"
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: The Death Eaters ambushed us as soon as we left. They knew it was tonight and set a trap.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "he joined the chase halfway through but vanished pretty quickly."
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Voldemort caught up with us during the chase. He showed up, hunted us, then disappeared again.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Harry behaved a little too kindly to Stan Shunpike," said Lupin.
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Because I was kind to Stan Shunpike, Voldemort changed his target to go after me. Great.
George lost an ear. That's awful and I can't bloody believe it.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Snape's work," said Lupin. "Snape?" shouted Harry. "He lost his hood during the chase. Sectumsempra was always a speciality of Snape's."
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Someone used Sectumsempra on George during the chase. Lupin thinks it was Snape's doing.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "I saw him too, he came after Hagrid and me."
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: I saw Lupin fly after us during the chase. He left to follow when Voldemort diverted his attention.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "then Harry saw him. Voldemort was flying like smoke on the wind, without broomstick or thestral to hold him"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: He can fly on his own. Voldemort does not need a broom or a thestral to get around.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "His snakelike face gleaming out of the blackness, his white fingers raising his wand again"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: He is focused on me. When I saw his face and the wand go up I knew he was after me and not just anyone.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Barely gripping the plummeting bike with his knees, Harry heard Voldemort scream, 'Mine!'"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: He wants me. Voldemort actually screamed that I belong to him.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "As the pain from Harry’s scar forced his eyes shut, his wand acted of its own accord"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: My wand moved like it had a mind of its own. When my scar burned the wand dragged my hand like a magnet.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "He felt it drag his hand around like some great magnet, saw a spurt of golden fire through his half-closed eyelids, heard a crack and a scream of fury"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: My wand fired when my scar screamed. I caused that golden blast without meaning to and it hit someone.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Somehow, Harry found his nose an inch from the dragon-fire button. He punched it with his wand-free hand and the bike shot more flames into the air"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: I can trigger the bike's dragon-fire in a panic. I hit the button and sprayed flames even while falling.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "'Hagrid!' Harry called, holding on to the bike for dear life. 'Hagrid - Accio Hagrid!'"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: I can try to summon Hagrid even in chaos. I yelled for him and shouted Accio Hagrid to pull him back.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "to his horror, Harry saw both Hagrid and the Death Eater falling out of sight, their combined weight too much for the broomstick"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: Hagrid fell. He and that Death Eater went down together because the broom couldn't carry both.

Book7-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Behind him came another scream, 'Your wand, Selwyn, give me your wand!'"
Book7-chapter4_Sc6.description: Voldemort orders other wizards to hand over their wands. He told Selwyn to give him his wand.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Maybe they won’t know which of the twelve secure houses I’m heading for at first, but won’t it be sort of obvious once" — he performed a quick headcount — "fourteen of us fly off toward Tonks’s parents’?"
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: This plan has a glaring problem. If fourteen people all head for the same place it will give us away. I can see that straight away and I don’t like it.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "No!" he said loudly, his voice ringing through the kitchen. "No way!"
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: I refuse to let people risk being turned into me unless there is really no other option. I will not agree to this lightly.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "So, Potter — some of your hair, if you please."
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: They need a lock of my hair to make the Polyjuice Potion and create the decoys. If I don't give it, they can't do it.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "You’ll be going to Tonks’s parents. Once you’re within the boundaries of the protective enchantments we’ve put on their house, you’ll be able to use a Portkey to the Burrow. Any questions?"
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: The Order has arranged safe houses and Portkeys. People I care about are being used to protect me and I have to decide how far I'm willing to cooperate.

Book7-chapter6_Sc4.source: The Daily Prophet hasn’t said a word about him dying or about finding the body,” Bill went on. “But that doesn’t mean much. It’s keeping a lot quiet these days.
Book7-chapter6_Sc4.description: They're keeping Moody's death quiet. The papers and the Ministry are hiding things and that feels wrong.

Book7-chapter6_Sc4.source: And they still haven’t called a hearing about all the underage magic I used escaping the Death Eaters?”
Book7-chapter6_Sc4.description: They won't call a hearing about my underage magic. It's because they'd rather cover up that Voldemort attacked me than face the truth.

Book7-chapter6_Sc4.source: Because they know I had no choice or because they don’t want me to tell the world Voldemort attacked me?”
Book7-chapter6_Sc4.description: Either they know I had no choice, or they're keeping me quiet so the public doesn't find out how bad things really are. I won't be brushed off.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source: Once I’m seventeen, the protective charm that keeps me safe will break, and that exposes you as well as me.
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: Once I'm seventeen the charm breaks. That's it. We're all exposed if Voldemort comes back full force.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source: The Order is sure Voldemort will target you, whether to torture you to try and find out where I am, or because he
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: The Order told me Voldemort won't just go after me, he'll go after the people around me to get to me or to punish them.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source: I’ve already got a house, my godfather left me one.
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: I already have a house left by my godfather, so I wouldn't want the Dursleys' place. It's not about their house for me.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source: “According to you,” Vernon Dursley said now, resuming his pacing up and down the living room, “we — Petunia, Dudley, and I — are in danger. From — from —”
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: The Dursleys are scared and panicking about supposed danger to them because of me, especially Vernon who can't stop changing his mind.
Vernon keeps flipping between decisions all the time. He's packed and unpacked the car so many times I can't take him seriously when he warns me.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source: “I was awake half the night thinking it all over, and I believe it’s a plot to get the house.”
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: Vernon genuinely thinks there's a plot to grab their house and that I'm somehow involved, which is absurd.

Book7-chapter3_Sc2.source:
“You claim,” said Uncle Vernon, starting to pace yet again, “that this Lord Thing —”

“— Voldemort,” said Harry impatiently, “and we’ve been through this about a hundred times already.
Book7-chapter3_Sc2.description: I've had to correct Vernon about who Voldemort is more times than I can count. He still refuses to accept what's been explained to him by others.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: But when did you do this? Harry asked, regarding Hermione with a mixture of admiration and incredulity.
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: When did you do it? I mean, I can't believe you took those books right after Dumbledore's funeral. That's risky but clever.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: She said imploringly, "I can’t believe Dumbledore would have been angry, it’s not as though we’re going to use the information to make a Horcrux, is it?"
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: I want to trust Hermione's judgement here. If she thinks we won't use the info to make a Horcrux, then maybe she's right, but we still need to be careful.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "He only approached Slughorn to find out what would happen if you split your soul into seven," said Harry.
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Dumbledore reckoned Riddle already knew how to make a Horcrux. Slughorn was only asked about what happens if you split your soul into seven.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Dumbledore was sure Riddle already knew how to make a Horcrux by the time he asked Slughorn about them. I think you’re right, Hermione, that could easily have been where he got the information."
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Right then I started thinking Dumbledore was probably correct and that Riddle could well have learned the basic Horcrux stuff from the library before he ever went to Slughorn.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: Phoenix tears are the only antidote to basilisk venom. Of course they are.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "What, stabbing it with a basilisk fang?" asked Harry.
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: Stabbing a Horcrux with basilisk venom will destroy it. That's one of the few foolproof ways.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: Pius Thicknesse has gone over, which gives us a big problem. He’s made it an imprisonable offense to connect this house to the Floo Network, place a Portkey here, or Apparate in or out.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: So Thicknesse has just made it illegal to use the Floo, Portkeys, or Apparition from here. Basically they have sealed this place off and made it punishable if anyone tries to help me get out that way.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: You’re underage, which means you’ve still got the Trace on you.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: I've still got the Trace on me because I'm under seventeen. Any magic cast around me will alert the Ministry and the Death Eaters. That makes any obvious escape spell a huge risk.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: We can’t wait for the Trace to break, because the moment you turn seventeen you’ll lose all the protection your mother gave you.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: Waiting until I turn seventeen isn't an option. The moment I do, my mum's protection drops and Voldemort will be able to grab me, so we have to move before then.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: We’re going to use the only means of transport left to us, the only ones the Trace can’t detect, because we don’t need to cast spells to use them: brooms, thestrals, and Hagrid’s motorbike.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: We're forced to use things the Trace can't pick up like brooms, thestrals, or Hagrid's bike. No spells, no Floo, no Portkey, no Apparition. It's risky but it's the only way.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: Now, your mother’s charm will only break under two conditions: when you come of age, or you no longer call this place home.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: I get it now. Mum's protective charm only ends when I turn seventeen or when I stop calling this place home. Leaving tonight means breaking it early but staying isn't safe either.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: The one thing we’ve got on our side is that You-Know-Who doesn’t know we’re moving you tonight. We’ve leaked a fake trail to the Ministry: They think you’re not leaving until the thirtieth.
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: They don't know we're moving tonight. We've fed them a fake trail so the Ministry expects me to leave on the thirtieth. That gives us a cover for tonight if we act fast.

Book7-chapter4_Sc2.source: You and your aunt and uncle are going your separate ways tonight, in the full understanding that you’re never going to live together again, correct?
Book7-chapter4_Sc2.description: I'm leaving the Dursleys tonight for good. There's no going back to living with them, so this is the end of that life.

Book7-chapter6_Sc11.source: "That diary sort of died when I stabbed it,"
Book7-chapter6_Sc11.description: I know the diary actually died when I stabbed it. Ink poured like blood and that bit of Voldemort's soul screamed and vanished.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: "It's fine, I understand," said Harry, speaking more to Lupin than Tonks.
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: It's fine, I understand. I don't blame him for being careful about his being here.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: Lupin gave him a swift smile, but as they turned away, Harry saw Lupin's face fall again into lines of misery.
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: He looked all right for a second, then he went back to being miserable. I can't fix that right now.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: Hagrid was causing a certain amount of disruption. Having misunderstood Fred's directions he had sat himself ... on five seats that now resembled a large pile of golden matchsticks.
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: Hagrid's a walking disaster sometimes. He sat in the wrong place and smashed a load of seats to bits. Of course he did.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: a rather deaf old couple fell to Harry's lot.
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: I ended up with a deaf old couple to look after. Great. Talk about being stuck on duty.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: The measures they had taken to protect their families made him realize, more than anything else could have done, that they really were going to come with him and that they knew exactly how dangerous that would be.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: They are coming with me and they know how dangerous this is. I can't find words for what that means to me but it's real and it's terrifying.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: I know you said you wanted to go to Godric’s Hollow first, Harry, and I understand why, but . . . well . . . shouldn’t we make the Horcruxes our priority?
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: I want to go to Godric's Hollow first. There's something about the place that pulls me there. Maybe it holds answers because that is where I survived Voldemort's curse.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: 'I have stolen the real Horcrux and intend to destroy it as soon as I can,'
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: R.A.B.'s note says the real locket was stolen and he meant to destroy it. If he actually destroyed it that's one less Horcrux we might have to deal with, but we still have to find the real locket to be sure.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "That’s your ghoul, isn’t it?" asked Harry
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: So Ron has a ghoul in his attic and he expects me to meet it. I can see it now and I can barely believe it looks like someone in pajamas.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Once we’ve left, the ghoul’s going to come and live down here in my room," said Ron.
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: They plan to leave the ghoul in Ron's bed so anyone who comes snooping will think Ron is seriously ill and contagious.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Dad is. He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul."
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Ron’s dad and Fred and George helped turn the ghoul into the spattergroit disguise. The Weasleys are involved in this ruse.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "But Bill saw him hit by the Killing Curse," said Harry.
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Bill said he saw Moody hit by the Killing Curse, so I can't just pretend he's alive without good reason. If Bill saw it, that counts for something.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "Fleur said his wand was blasted out of his hand," said Harry.
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Fleur saw Moody's wand blasted out of his hand. If that's true, Moody was disarmed before he fell.
I'm determined they're coming with me. I know they said they'd follow me before, and I'm not backing down on wanting them at my side now.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: For the first time, Harry imagined Mad-Eye’s body, broken as Dumbledore’s had been, yet with that one eye still whizzing in its socket.
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: I pictured Moody dead, like Dumbledore, and it made my stomach flip. I couldn't help it, but I saw him broken and it felt sickening.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "No news about Mad-Eye?" Harry asked Bill. "Nothing," replied Bill.
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: Mad-Eye's body hasn't been found and there's no news about him. They couldn't hold a funeral because they couldn't recover him.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "The Daily Prophet hasn’t said a word about him dying or about finding the body," Bill went on. "But that doesn’t mean much. It’s keeping a lot quiet these days."
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: The papers and the Ministry are keeping things quiet on purpose. They're hiding information instead of telling the truth.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "And they still haven’t called a hearing about all the underage magic I used escaping the Death Eaters?" Harry called across the table to Mr Weasley, who shook his head.
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: The Ministry still hasn't called me in for a hearing about the underage magic I used when the Death Eaters attacked.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Because they know I had no choice or because they don’t want me to tell the world Voldemort attacked me?" "The latter, I think. Scrimgeour doesn’t want to admit that You-Know-Who is as powerful as he is, nor that Azkaban’s seen a mass breakout."
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: It's not about me getting in trouble. It's because Scrimgeour and the Ministry don't want people to know Voldemort is back and how bad things are.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: Harry clenched his knife so tightly that the faint scars on the back of his right hand stood out, white against his skin: I must not tell lies.
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: I'm still angry and tense about all this. I want to tell the truth and I'm frustrated that no one is willing to admit what's happening.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "You look smart. I told Daddy most people would probably wear dress robes, but he believes you ought to wear sun colors to a wedding, for luck, you know."
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Luna thinks I look smart and her dad has odd ideas about wedding luck. I just went along with it.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Your friend is not pleased to see me," said Krum... "Or is he a relative?" he added with a glance at Harry's red curly hair.
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Krum spotted the Weasley connection and noticed Ron's reaction. I tried to move him away from Ron by showing him to his seat.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Because," said Krum, "if he vos not a guest of Fleur's, I vould duel him, here and now, for vearing that filthy sign upon his chest."
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Krum thinks Xenophilius is wearing Grindelwald's sign and said he'd duel him if he wasn't Fleur's guest. That's serious enough to make me keep an eye on things.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Fleur invited me," said Krum, eyebrows raised.
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Krum says he was invited by Fleur. He's friendly enough with the wedding crowd, so I shook his hand and offered to show him his seat.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "The diary sort of died when I stabbed it," said Harry, remembering ink pouring like blood from the punctured pages, and the screams of the piece of Voldemort’s soul as it vanished.
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: The diary Horcrux actually died when I destroyed it. I remember the ink and the screams. Once it's properly destroyed the bit of soul trapped in it can no longer exist.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "Ginny tried to get rid of the diary before you did, flushing it away, but obviously it came back good as new."
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: Ginny tried to get rid of the diary by flushing it, but the Horcrux came back like nothing had happened. It's not enough to just get rid of the object casually.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "I wonder how Dumbledore destroyed the ring?" said Harry. "Why didn’t I ask him? I never really . . ."
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: I should've asked Dumbledore how he destroyed the ring. I keep thinking I should've known more about destroying Horcruxes.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: I'm not leaving. I'm going to be right here with Hermione and Ron, and we won't be split up for this.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "'To Harry James Potter,'" he read, "I leave the Snitch he caught in his first Quidditch match at Hogwarts, as a reminder of the rewards of perseverance and skill.'"
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Dumbledore left me that Snitch as a keepsake about perseverance and skill. It's supposed to remind me what you can get if you stick at something.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "This Snitch will remember your touch, Potter."
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: That Snitch has flesh memory. It can identify the first person to touch it and might be enchanted to open only for me.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Take it," said Scrimgeour quietly. Harry met the Minister's yellow eyes and knew he had no option but to obey."
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: When the Minister told me to take it I had to. I couldn't refuse him in that moment even though I was worried about what might be inside.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Nothing happened. As Harry's fingers closed around the Snitch, its tired wings fluttered and were still."
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: I half expected something dramatic to happen when I touched the Snitch, but it didn't. That was a bit of an anticlimax.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Why didn’t I make sure I had the Invisibility Cloak with me?"
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: I should have kept the Cloak on me. What the hell, I left it behind and that was stupid.
If I fire a Stunning Spell fast and hard I can take a Death Eater out, even when things are chaos.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: "We can’t worry about that now," whispered Hermione. "It’s you they’re after, Harry, and we’ll just put everyone in even more danger by going back."
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: Hermione's right, they're after me. I can't let my guilt make us go back and risk everyone else.
Even unseen, I still have to agree and keep moving. Arguing won't help when people are in danger.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: Grimmauld Place is the best chance we've got. It's where we should go if we need somewhere to hide.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "You — you don’t think you’ve still got your Trace on you, do you, Harry?"
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: I felt rotten thinking the Death Eaters might have tracked us because of a Trace on me. I felt contaminated and worried that maybe they found a way to put it back on a seventeen-year-old.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "If I can’t use magic, and you can’t use magic near me, without us giving away our position —" he began.
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: If I can't use magic and they can't use magic near me without giving us away, we're in real trouble. We can't go around using magic or we'll draw them straight to us.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "No! It wasn’t us! We didn’t kill you —"
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: Seeing that horror-figure made me think some of this stuff is just meant to scare Snape or any intruder. It wasn't the real thing, it was a trick to frighten whoever shows up.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: You were muttering in your sleep. 'Gregorovitch.' You kept saying 'Gregorovitch.'
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Gregorovitch keeps popping into my head in my sleep. I keep saying his name in dreams and my scar prickles when it happens.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: I think Voldemort’s looking for him.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I reckon Voldemort is hunting Gregorovitch. I can feel it, like I saw him somewhere abroad looking for someone.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: I think he's got something to do with Quidditch. There’s some connection, but I can’t — I can’t think what it is.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: There’s some link between Gregorovitch and Quidditch. I kept seeing it, even if I can't quite pull the rest together right now.
I’m seventeen now. Once I'm seventeen the protective charm will break and everything changes. That's it. We're all exposed.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: She was kissing him as she had never kissed him before, and Harry was kissing her back
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Ginny and I kissed. It was amazing and real and I wanted it to be private, but Ron walked in and it all fell flat. That was rubbish timing.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: Do me a favor and don’t tell Hermione
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I don't want Hermione knowing about everything I see in my sleep. I want her not to worry me about it right now.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: I require a private word with you
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Scrimgeour wants to speak to me alone. That makes me nervous. If the Minister is hovering around my seventeenth birthday then nothing good is simple.
I can use magic freely now that the Trace is gone. It feels good to do little things for myself, even if they end up being a bit messy.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore left you a second bequest, Potter."
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Dumbledore left me things in his will. He wanted me to have stuff even after he was gone.
People argue the sword is not mine to keep. The Ministry think it belongs to history, not to me.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Was it because Dumbledore believed that only the sword of Godric Gryffindor could defeat the Heir of Slytherin?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Maybe Dumbledore thought the sword was important against Voldemort. If he wanted me to have it, he must have had a reason tied up with the Horcrux business.
The Snitch I caught has writing that appears and vanishes that says I open at the close. I tried to make sense of it and it meant nothing in the moment, but it clearly matters.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "I wasn’t going to try too hard in front of Scrimgeour, was I?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: I held back in front of Scrimgeour. I won’t always show everything when it’s dangerous or the wrong people are watching.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "You may wear that scar like a crown, Potter, but it is not up to a seventeen-year-old boy to tell me how to do my job!"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: I can’t trust the Minister. He’s controlling and quick to intimidate. The Ministry is not on the side I want right now.

Book7-chapter8_Sc3.source: "There’s a chance that Xenophilius doesn’t actually know what the symbol means. The Lovegoods are quite . . . unusual."
Book7-chapter8_Sc3.description: He might have picked that symbol up somewhere and think it means something harmless, not that Xenophilius is a supporter of the Dark Arts.

Book7-chapter8_Sc3.source: "Probably trying to get rid of a Wrackspurt,"
Book7-chapter8_Sc3.description: Luna is behaving like she has Wrackspurts in her ears or head, that’s why she’s waving her arms around.

Book7-chapter8_Sc3.source: "Gregorovitch!" and the memory of Ollivander examining Krum’s wand
Book7-chapter8_Sc3.description: Gregorovitch is a famous wandmaker and his name popped back into my head when I saw Krum’s wand; wandmakers leave marks in people’s memories.

Book7-chapter8_Sc3.source: "Don’t believe a word of it! Not a word, Harry! Let nothing tarnish your memories of Albus Dumbledore!"
Book7-chapter8_Sc3.description: Elphias Doge defends Dumbledore fiercely and expects me to dismiss Rita Skeeter’s claims, but I can’t just decide not to know the truth because someone asks me to.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: Do Not Enter Without the Express Permission of Regulus Arcturus Black
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: I found Regulus's sign on the door. R.A.B. is real and linked to Regulus Arcturus Black.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: Sirius told me about him, he joined up when he was really young and then got cold feet and tried to leave — so they killed him.
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: Regulus was a Death Eater who turned against them and paid for it. He had access to Voldemort and then tried to get away.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: R.A.B. I think I’ve found him.
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: If R.A.B. is Regulus, then someone in the Blacks tried to fight Voldemort from the inside.
We couldn't Summon the locket. It might be under counter-enchantments like the one in the cave.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: Kreacher nicked loads of things back from us,
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: Kreacher stole a bunch of our old junk and keeps a stash in his cupboard in the kitchen. The locket could be there.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'Muggle-borns are being rounded up as we speak.'
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: This is happening right now. Muggle-borns are being rounded up, and the Ministry is onto them.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'Attendance is now compulsory for every young witch and wizard.'
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: They're forcing every kid to go to Hogwarts so Voldemort can keep an eye on them and weed out anyone without the right blood.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'I’m pretty sure my father would have wanted to know why you aren’t sticking with your own kid, actually.'
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: If someone in the Order is going to abandon their family, I can't respect them. Parents shouldn't leave their kids unless they've got to.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'Don’t you understand what I’ve done to my wife and my unborn child? I should never have married her, I’ve made her an outcast!'
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: Lupin's hiding his shame and thinking of running rather than standing by his wife and child. I feel betrayed and furious at him for it.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Show yourself!" he called back. Lupin moved forward into the lamplight, hands still held high in a gesture of surrender. "I am Remus John Lupin, werewolf, sometimes known as Moony, one of the four creators of the Marauder's Map, married to Nymphadora, usually known as Tonks, and I taught you how to produce a Patronus, Harry, which takes the form of a stag."
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: I had to check him out. I drew my wand and made sure it was Remus before I lowered it. I trust him, but I checked anyway.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Here," he said, pushing it across the table to Harry, "you'll know sooner or later anyway. That's their pretext for going after you." Harry smoothed out the paper. A huge photograph of his own face filled the front page. He read the headline over it: WANTED FOR QUESTIONING ABOUT THE DEATH OF ALBUS DUMBLEDORE"
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: They've put my face all over the Prophet. I'm wanted for questioning about Dumbledore's death. That's how they're turning people against me.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "What you've got to realize, Harry, is that the Death Eaters have got the full might of the Ministry on their side now," said Lupin.
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: The Ministry is basically working with the Death Eaters now. They have the power to act without fear. We are being hunted and no one is safe.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "So Death Eaters have taken over the Daily Prophet too?" asked Hermione furiously. Lupin nodded.
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: The Daily Prophet is compromised. The people who might have protected me are being silenced or turned. I can't count on the paper or the Ministry to help.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Master Regulus told Kreacher to come back,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Regulus ordered Kreacher to come home from the cave.
Kreacher got away from the Inferi by using elf magic to Apparate or Disapparate, not the same as wizard magic.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Master Regulus took from his pocket a locket like the one the Dark Lord had,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Regulus stole a locket Horcrux from Voldemort and brought it back.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "And he ordered — Kreacher to leave — without him. And he told Kreacher — to go home — and never to tell my Mistress — what he had done — but to destroy — the first locket."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Regulus told Kreacher to leave him and to go home, to never tell the family what happened, and to destroy the locket after switching it.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "And he drank — all the potion — and Kreacher swapped the lockets — and watched . . . as Master Regulus . . . was dragged beneath the water . . . and . . ."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Regulus drank the potion meant to protect the Horcrux and was dragged under by the Inferi and died.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Nothing Kreacher did made any mark upon it,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: The locket Horcrux cannot be destroyed by the usual things Kreacher tried, so it's much harder to get rid of than we thought.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Kreacher failed to obey orders, Kreacher could not destroy the locket! And his Mistress was mad with grief,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Kreacher feels guilty and terrified because he couldn't obey Regulus's final order and that made the whole Black household miserable.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Kreacher, I want you, please, to go and find Mundungus Fletcher."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: I asked Kreacher to find Mundungus so we can track down Regulus's locket and finish what Regulus started.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "The S stands for Selwyn. . . . I am related to the Selwyns. . . . Indeed, there are few pure-blood families to whom I am not related."
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: She lied to boost her pedigree. I saw the locket she took from a petty criminal being used so she could pretend she was pure-blood. That made my blood boil.
I wasn't going to sit there and let her pretend. I blasted Umbridge and Yaxley because enough was enough.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "EXPECTO PATRONUM!" The silver stag soared from the tip of Harry's wand and leaped toward the dementors
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: My Patronus is a stag. It overwhelms the dementors and lights up a whole place. It works better than the cat.
The locket is a Horcrux. Getting it is the priority. Everything else comes after that.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "It’s been decided that you should all go home and go into hiding with your families," Harry told the waiting Muggle-borns
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: People need to get out now. I told the Muggle-borns to leave the country if they can and hide with their families so they do not get shipped off.

Book7-chapter14_Sc3.source: [Even now, he could be bringing other Death Eaters in there by Apparition. Gloomy and oppressive though the house was, it had been their one safe refuge]
Book7-chapter14_Sc3.description: This place might not be safe anymore; Death Eaters could Apparate in at any time and we could be walking into a trap.

Book7-chapter14_Sc3.source: [even, now that Kreacher was so much happier and friendlier, a kind of home. With a twinge of regret that had nothing to do with food, Harry imagined the house-elf busying himself over the steak-and-kidney pie that Harry, Ron, and Hermione would never eat. "Harry, I'm sorry, I'm so sorry!" "Don't be stupid, it wasn't your fault! If anything, it was mine."]
Book7-chapter14_Sc3.description: Kreacher's changed; he's happier and friendlier now, and I feel guilty that he was making a home for us that we won't even use.

Book7-chapter14_Sc3.source: [Harry put his hand in his pocket and drew out Mad-Eye’s eye.]
Book7-chapter14_Sc3.description: I've got Mad-Eye's magical eye on me now; it's something real I can use or check, and it matters.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Kreacher knows things and I can order him to speak. I called him and he appeared, so I can get answers from him when I press him.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: "I forbid you to call anyone 'blood traitor' or 'Mudblood'"
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: I will not let him abuse people in my house. I had to step in and stop Kreacher insulting the Weasleys and Hermione.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Two years ago... there was a big gold locket in the drawing room upstairs. We threw it out. Did you steal it back?" / "Yes."
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: The locket we got rid of was taken back by Kreacher, so it's linked to something important in this house.
Mundungus Fletcher nicked the locket and other Black family things. He is the one who ran off with them.
That locket belonged to Regulus Black. It's not just junk. It has a direct tie to the Black family and to Regulus himself.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: "The Dark Lord made Kreacher drink it. Kreacher drank, and as he drank, he saw terrible things"
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Voldemort used Kreacher to test something awful in a cave. The elf was forced to drink a potion and saw terrible things, which matches what I know happened at a Horcrux site.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Master Regulus had proper pride; he knew what was due to the name of Black"
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Regulus was proud enough and involved enough with Voldemort to have done something drastic. He might have been trying to help or to make amends in his own way.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: Harry wrenched open Kreacher's cupboard, grabbed blankets and called Kreacher; he also flattened Kreacher to stop him from hurting himself
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: I am in charge here and I will control Kreacher. He is contemptuous and foul, but I can force him to obey and make him tell the truth when it matters.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: Engraved in foot-high letters at the base of the statue were the words MAGIC IS MIGHT.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Magic is being celebrated as superior here. They mean it. This place thinks wizards are above everyone else.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: what he had thought were decoratively carved thrones were actually mounds of carved humans: hundreds and hundreds of naked bodies, men, women, and children, all with rather stupid, ugly faces, twisted and pressed together to support the weight of the handsomely robed wizards.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: They turned Muggles into decoration and support. I couldn't believe how grotesque that is.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: With a nod and unpleasant smile to Harry, who was evidently expected to appreciate this treatment of Cattermole, Yaxley swept away toward another lift.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: People here expect me to go along with their cruelty. They see me as someone who should approve of punishing others.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: The man’s scowling, slightly brutish face was somehow at odds with his magnificent, sweeping robes, which were embroidered with much gold thread.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Yaxley is dangerous and important. He's intimidating and has power at the Ministry.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "I think we should do it tomorrow," said Harry.
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: We're not getting any safer by waiting around. If we hang about, that locket could get tossed or moved. We have to act now.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "We know they've stopped Apparition in and out of the Ministry."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Apparition to and from the Ministry is blocked. That affects how we get in and out.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "We know only the most senior Ministry members are allowed to connect their homes to the Floo Network now, because Ron heard those two Unspeakables complaining about it."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Only top Ministry people can use the Floo from home now. That narrows our options.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "And we know roughly where Umbridge's office is, because of what you heard that bearded bloke saying to his mate - 'I'll be up on level one, Dolores wants to see me'"
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Dolores is on level one. We know where to start looking.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "He reached up, pulled the chain, and next moment had zoomed down a short chute, emerging out of a fireplace into the Ministry of Magic."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: I used the loo entrance, pulled the chain and flooed straight into the Ministry. It works, so that's our route in.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "If the plan works, we will have," Harry continued calmly.
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Mafalda's tokens will give us access if everything goes to plan. We can steal our way in with them.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Harry, I don’t think we’re going to be able to go back there."
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: We can't go back to Grimmauld Place. I thought we were headed back but that's not possible now.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Since Dumbledore died, we’re Secret-Keepers, so I’ve given him the secret, haven’t I?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: Yaxley might know the secret to Grimmauld Place and could get inside. That's a huge problem.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "It’s all I feel safe doing," said Hermione shakily.
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: Hermione is too frightened to try risky healing magic on whoever's hurt, and she's shaken up.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Let’s stay here for now," Harry said.
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: We should stay put for now. Moving him is asking for trouble.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "You could get out the tent, Harry."
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: Of course the tent's in the bag. I can summon it instead of rummaging around.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: Harry recognized it, partly because of the smell of cats, as the same tent in which they had slept on the night of the Quidditch World Cup.
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: That's the World Cup tent. The smell of cats gives it away.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: I — I think it’s started opening again whenever he loses control, that’s how it used to —
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: My scar is opening again when he loses control. It burns and slams anger into me like a shock, and I can feel when he's raging.
It closed for a while, but it is not shut anymore. I have to deal with this or it will keep dragging me into his head.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: No, I just felt anger — he’s really angry —
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: I can only pick up raw emotion from him sometimes, mostly anger. I don't always get clear images or words, just that burning fury.
I know Dumbledore wanted Occlumency so Voldemort could not use our connection. I do not need Hermione to tell me what that cost before.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: I acted clueless and said "Sorry?" because pretending to be daft was my best shot at keeping people off my back.
I slipped in behind her and whispered "I'm behind you," because I would do whatever it took to protect Hermione from those Dementors and that awful hearing.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.source: As she passed the dementors, Harry saw her shudder.
Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: Seeing Mrs. Cattermole shudder as she passed the Dementors told me exactly how terrified ordinary people are in that place. It made me want to stop it, now.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.source: The moment he had passed the place where the Patronus cat patrolled, he felt the change in temperature: It was warm and comfortable here.
Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: There was a Patronus cat keeping the prosecutors comfortable while the accused froze. That showed me who Umbridge protects and who she wants to break.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Splinched," said Hermione, her fingers already busy at Ron's sleeve, where the blood was wettest and darkest.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Splinching is not a joke. That was brutal, a chunk of Ron's arm gone like someone had taken a knife to him. I had to act fast.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Bag — right —" Harry sped to the place where Hermione had landed, seized the tiny beaded bag, and thrust his hand inside it.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Hermione's bag holds whatever you need. I reached in, found things by feel, and went for what would help.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Accio Dittany!" A small brown bottle zoomed out of the bag; he caught it and hastened back to Hermione and Ron
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: When it matters, I can get a spell out under pressure. Accio Dittany pulled the potion right into my hand.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "He’s fainted," said Hermione, who was also rather pale; she no longer looked like Mafalda, though her hair was still gray in places.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Ron passed out. I had to be quick because he was unconscious and bleeding badly.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Now, if you’ll just follow the Patronuses, you’ll be able to leave from the Atrium."
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Follow the Patronuses and they'll lead us out through the Atrium. That's the route out, plain and simple.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "It’s been decided that you should all go home and go into hiding with your families,"
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: People are being told to go into hiding, get away from the Ministry. Get families out, go abroad if you can.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Harry, they know there are intruders inside the Ministry, something about a hole in Umbridge’s office door, I reckon we’ve got five minutes if that —"
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: They know there are intruders and there's not much time. We have maybe five minutes before they react properly.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Would you like me to have your family tree examined, like I had Dirk Cresswell’s?"
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: I can bluff authority and use threats about family trees to cow them. If I sound convincing they'll do as I say.
Some of the Ministry lot are helping Muggle-borns escape, or at least pretending to. People can be forced into doing awful things.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Reg!" screamed Mrs. Cattermole, and she threw herself into Ron’s arms.
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Reg Cattermole is mixed up in this mess. There are two Regs now and it's confusing as hell for everyone concerned.

Book7-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Isn’t it the same symbol Luna’s dad was wearing round his neck?" "Then it’s Grindelwald’s mark."
Book7-chapter16_Sc2.description: I checked it and I know that symbol from what Krum told me — it's Grindelwald's mark. That's what it is.

Book7-chapter16_Sc2.source: "And you’d think Scrimgeour would have recognized it. He was Minister, he ought to have been expert on Dark stuff."
Book7-chapter16_Sc2.description: Scrimgeour should've spotted this if it was Dark stuff. If he missed it, something's off.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I know I shouldn’t have called him a coward."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: I lashed out at Lupin and I know I was wrong to call him a coward, but I still feel he was acting like one.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "But if it makes him go back to Tonks, it’ll be worth it, won’t it?"
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: If upsetting Lupin gets him back with Tonks, then whatever I said was worth it. I want that more than I want to be right.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "The Dumbledore family, left to right: Albus; Percival, holding newborn Ariana; Kendra; and Aberforth."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: There was a photograph of the Dumbledore family with Percival, Kendra, Ariana and Aberforth. They looked ordinary and happy in the picture.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "EXCLUSIVE EXTRACT FROM THE UPCOMING BIOGRAPHY OF ALBUS DUMBLEDORE by Rita Skeeter" (paragraphs describing Kendra and Percival)
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Rita Skeeter's piece says Kendra moved the family to Godric's Hollow after Percival was sent to Azkaban and that she kept to herself, which adds context to the Dumbledores' past.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Kreacher has returned with the thief Mundungus Fletcher, Master."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Kreacher brought Mundungus to me. Kreacher tracked him down and is loyal to the people from this house.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I panicked, okay? I never wanted to come along, no offense, mate, but I never volunteered to die for you, an’ that was bleedin’ You-Know-Who come flying at me..."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Mundungus admits he panicked and ran when You-Know-Who appeared; he is unreliable and cowardly when things get dangerous.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I was selling in Diagon Alley and she come up to me and asks if I’ve got a license for trading in magical artifacts... She was gonna fine me, but she took a fancy to the locket an’ told me she’d take it and let me off that time..."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Mundungus sold or gave the locket to a little woman in Diagon Alley with a bow on her head who looked like a toad. The locket left his possession that way.

Book7-chapter16_Sc3.source: "I — I want to go to Godric’s Hollow."
Book7-chapter16_Sc3.description: I want to go to Godric's Hollow. We need to go there.
Hermione hears me and agrees with what I said. She's on the same page about going.

Book7-chapter17_Sc4.source: "Good luck, Harry, wherever you are. If you read this, Harry, we’re all behind you! Long live Harry Potter."
Book7-chapter17_Sc4.description: People have been leaving messages for me. They're backing me and wishing me luck. That actually makes me smile.

Book7-chapter17_Sc4.source: "A heavily muffled figure was hobbling up the lane toward them, silhouetted by the bright lights in the distant square."
Book7-chapter17_Sc4.description: There's someone coming up the lane. I think it's a woman and she's hobbling, but I can't be sure yet.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: I can feel something from that locket against my chest, like a tiny metal heart or my blood thudding along with it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Keep it safe till we work out how to destroy it,"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: We have to keep the locket safe until we figure out how to destroy it, so I'm going to wear it under my robes.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "I think we should take it in turns to keep watch outside the tent,"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: We need to take turns keeping watch and sort out food — someone has to stay on guard.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "He found Gregorovitch. He had him tied up, he was torturing him."
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: Voldemort had Gregorovitch tied up and was torturing him.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "He asked him to hand it over, but Gregorovitch said it had been stolen from him"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: Voldemort wanted something from Gregorovitch that Gregorovitch said had been stolen.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "He read Gregorovitch’s mind, and I saw this young bloke perched on a windowsill, and he fired a curse at Gregorovitch and jumped out of sight."
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: Voldemort read Gregorovitch's mind and I saw a young bloke on a windowsill who fired a curse, stole whatever Voldemort wanted, and then vanished.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "He said nothing about the twin cores"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: It feels odd because Voldemort didn't mention my wand or those twin cores, so something about what he wanted doesn't add up to me.

Book7-chapter14_Sc8.description: It was probably something small the thief had. I reckon whatever it was, you couldn't tell much from a distance.

Book7-chapter14_Sc8.source: "I don't know," said Harry slowly. "Maybe. But wouldn't it be dangerous for him to make another one? Didn't Hermione say he had pushed his soul to the limit already?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc8.description: Maybe Voldemort could try to make another Horcrux, but that would be risky for him. Hermione warned he's already pushed his soul too far, so it should be dangerous for him to do it again.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Harry, who did not feel as sanguine as he had pretended when reassuring Hermione, was glad to reach the gate and the slippery pavement."
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: I wasn't as calm as I pretended to be when I told Hermione everything would be all right. I was glad to get out of there and onto safer ground.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "The pub was fuller than before: Many voices inside it were now singing the carol that they had heard as they approached the church."
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: The pub's got people in it and they're singing that carol we heard near the church. It's crowded and loud enough that it might hide us if we needed it.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "He was looking toward the dark mass that stood at the very end of this row of houses."
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: There's something dark and large at the end of the row of houses. That's where I'm looking now and it looks important.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "For a moment Harry considered suggesting they take refuge inside it, but before he could say anything Hermione murmured, 'Let’s go this way,' and pulled him down the dark street leading out of the village in the opposite direction from which they had entered."
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: I thought about ducking into the pub for shelter, but Hermione pulled me the other way. I didn't argue because she was sure about where to go.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: There was next to no chance that this woman was a Muggle
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: She's not a Muggle. That's nearly certain.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: By all the rules of normal magic, meanwhile, she ought not to be able to see Hermione and him at all
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: She can see us even though she shouldn't be able to. That's wrong and worrying.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: he had the strangest feeling that she knew that they were there, and also who they were
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: She knows we're here and she probably knows who we are. That feels personal.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: SEVERUS SNAPE CONFIRMED AS HOGWARTS HEADMASTER
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: Snape's actually been made headmaster. Snape is running Hogwarts now.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: 'If the Ministry and Voldemort are behind Snape it’ll be a choice between staying and teaching, or a nice few years in Azkaban'
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: If the Ministry and Voldemort back Snape, the teachers won't have a real choice. They'll probably stay and teach to try to protect the students rather than end up in Azkaban.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: 'There are still a load of Death Eaters watching the house'
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: There are more Death Eaters than usual around the house. They're waiting like they want us to leave for the Hogwarts Express.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: 'I landed badly on the top step, and the Cloak slipped.'
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: The Invisibility Cloak slipped when I landed, so we almost got seen coming back in.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: The quality of Kreacher’s cooking had improved dramatically ever since he had been given Regulus’s locket
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: Kreacher's cooking has actually got better since he has Regulus's locket. His French onion soup is proper good.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: Ghosts can't move snow, so whatever kicked up that snow in the bush wasn't a ghost.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.source: ["It's a cat," said Harry, after a second or two, "or a bird. If it was a Death Eater we'd be dead by now."]
Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: If it was a Death Eater we'd be dead by now, so it's probably just a cat or a bird and not someone dangerous.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.source: ["Harry thought of A History of Magic; the graveyard was supposed to be haunted: what if — ?"]
Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: The graveyard is supposed to be haunted, but that doesn't fit the snow-moving thing.

Book7-chapter17_Sc6.description: She's right here and I had to ask her point blank. I confronted her straight off because something about her felt wrong.

Book7-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Was it possible that she had been waiting for them all these long months?"
Book7-chapter17_Sc6.description: Could she have been waiting for me this whole time? I can't just write that off anymore. It looks like she might have been expecting me.

Book7-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Even her ability to sense them suggested some Dumbledore-ish power that he had never encountered before."
Book7-chapter17_Sc6.description: She can sense us. That's not ordinary. It feels like some Dumbledore-level kind of thing, which makes her way more dangerous and mysterious than a normal old witch.

Book7-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Was it not likely that it was she who had moved in the shadows in the graveyard and had followed them to this spot?"
Book7-chapter17_Sc6.description: I'm starting to think she followed us. She might have been in the shadows in the graveyard and trailed us here.

Book7-chapter17_Sc8.description: My scar screams when he's near. When that pain hits, Voldemort is coming.

Book7-chapter17_Sc8.source: He thought "worse than the snake was coming" and his head felt like it would split with pain from his scar
Book7-chapter17_Sc8.description: At first I was focussing on the snake, but then I knew something worse was nearer. The snake isn't the worst thing to worry about.

Book7-chapter17_Sc8.source: He stooped down and picked up the smashed photograph. There he was, the unknown thief, the thief he was seeking.
Book7-chapter17_Sc8.description: I saw the face in the broken photograph. That's the thief I'm after.
Hermione thinks I'm okay because I told her I was. I lied about being all right.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Dumbledore said fear of a name matters, but I'm not sure saying his name helps us any. Calling him by his name didn't save Dumbledore.
Kreacher was right about the locket being important. This thing is a Horcrux and we've actually got it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "We're going to have to work out how to open this thing before we can destroy it."
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: We have to figure out how to open the locket first. If we cannot open it we cannot destroy it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "Even after all their efforts to find it, he felt a violent urge to fling the locket from him."
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Holding the locket feels wrong to me. There's something inside it that makes me want to get rid of it straight away.
My attempts to pry the locket open by hand and with the charm failed. It won't open easily.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: The Fidelius Charm died with Mum and Dad. The house is visible now.
The cottage is mostly standing but the right side of the top floor was blown apart. That must be where the curse backfired.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.source: "You’re not going to go inside? It looks unsafe, it might — oh, Harry, look!"
Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: A sign grew up in front of the house and it calls me the only wizard to survive the Killing Curse.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.source: "On this spot, on the night of 31 October 1981, Lily and James Potter lost their lives. Their son, Harry, remains the only wizard ever to have survived the Killing Curse. This house, invisible to Muggles, has been left in its ruined state as a monument to the Potters and as a reminder of the violence that tore apart their family."
Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: The house has been left as a ruined monument to my parents and to the violence that destroyed our family.
Maybe the damage from Dark Magic is like an injury you cannot fix. That could be why nobody has rebuilt the place.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He slipped a hand from beneath the Cloak and grasped the snowy and thickly rusted gate, not wishing to open it, but simply to hold some part of the house."
Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: The gate is old, snowy and thickly rusted. I didn't want to open the gate. I just wanted to touch something that belonged to my family.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "As they had passed it, it had transformed. Instead of an obelisk covered in names, there was a statue of three people: a man with untidy hair and glasses, a woman with long hair and a kind, pretty face, and a baby boy sitting in his mother’s arms."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: I saw a statue of my parents and me as a baby. It was surreal to see myself in stone, happy and without my scar.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "KENDRA DUMBLEDORE and, a short way below her dates of birth and death, AND HER DAUGHTER ARIANA."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Dumbledore's family is buried here. His mother Kendra and his sister Ariana are in the graveyard at Godric's Hollow.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Harry could not help thinking that he and Dumbledore both had deep roots in this graveyard, and that Dumbledore ought to have told him so, yet he had never thought to share the connection."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: I feel a bit thrown. Dumbledore and I share this place and he never told me. I wish he had; it would have mattered to me.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "It was made of white marble, just like Dumbledore’s tomb, and this made it easy to read, as it seemed to shine in the dark. ... JAMES POTTER LILY POTTER BORN 27 MARCH 1960 DIED 31 OCTOBER 1981 BORN 30 JANUARY 1960 DIED 31 OCTOBER 1981"
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: My parents' graves are here in Godric's Hollow. Their names and dates are on the marble stone.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "'The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death' . . . 'Isn’t that a Death Eater idea? Why is that there?'"
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Seeing that inscription freaked me out at first. It sounded like something a Death Eater would like, so I panicked and wondered what it meant on my parents' grave.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "He moved toward her, feeling as if something heavy were pressing on his chest, the same sensation he had had right after Dumbledore had died, a grief that had actually weighed on his heart and lungs."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Being that close to my parents' graves hit me like a weight. I felt grief the same way I did after Dumbledore died.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "I’m going to keep looking for my parents, all right?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: I'm determined to find my parents' graves and see them no matter what. I need to.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: There was a scarlet oval over his heart where the locket had burned him. He could also see the half-healed puncture marks to his forearm.
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: The locket burned me. I've got a scar over my heart and half-healed puncture marks on my arm.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: Where’ve you put the Horcrux? "In my bag. I think we should keep it off for a while."
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: I've got the Horcrux in my bag. We should keep it switched off and away for a while.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: “We shouldn’t have gone to Godric’s Hollow. It’s my fault, it’s all my fault, Hermione, I’m sorry.”
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: We shouldn't have gone to Godric's Hollow. I feel responsible and I'm sorry about what happened there.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: “It’s not your fault. I wanted to go too; I really thought Dumbledore might have left the sword there for you.” “Yeah, well . . . we got that wrong, didn’t we?”
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: I thought Dumbledore might have left the sword there and I was counting on that. We got it wrong and that stings.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: We got away. We're out of whatever that was.
I've been really ill. I mean proper sick, not just a bit off.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "You’ve been shouting and moaning and . . . things,"
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: I was shouting and moaning while I was... out of it. I must have been awful to listen to.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "I couldn’t get the Horcrux off you," Hermione said, and he knew she wanted to change the subject. "It was stuck, stuck to your chest."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: There was a Horcrux stuck to my chest. It wouldn't come off until Hermione did something to separate it.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "You’ve got a mark; I’m sorry, I had to use a Severing Charm to get it away."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: I've got a mark where the Horcrux was. Hermione used a Severing Charm to tear it off me.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "The snake bit you too, but I’ve cleaned the wound and put some dittany on it."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: A snake bit me too. Hermione cleaned it and put dittany on the bite.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "I had to use a Hover Charm to get you into your bunk, I couldn’t lift you."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: I was too weak to move, so Hermione used a Hover Charm to get me into the bunk because she couldn't lift me herself.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: They're goblins. I heard them say their names plain as day, so this isn't ordinary smugglers or Muggles, it's goblins right there on the riverbank.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: The sword at Gringotts is a copy. The real Gryffindor sword isn't in that vault, it's gone. Of course it is, why would it be left where anyone could get at it?

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: Ginny and the others who tried to take the sword were caught and punished, though not seriously injured. That's not good enough, but at least they're alive.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Hard to help a boy who’s vanished off the face of the earth," said Dirk.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: People think I'm vanished and hiding. They expect me to be leading the fight. I shouldn't be surprised they're talking like that, but it stings. If they think I'm run off, I have to be more careful and smarter about where I go.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: I know Harry Potter," said Dean. "And I reckon he’s the real thing — the Chosen One, or whatever you want to call it.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: Some of them still believe in me. That's something I can use. Not everyone has given up on me or thinks I'm a fraud.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: You cast the Muffliato charm over us, right?" he whispered to Hermione.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: I listen hard and I act fast. I made them be quiet, had Hermione set up protections, and used the Extendable Ears so we could hear everything without being seen.

Book7-chapter17_Sc13.description: My wand just split into two while I tried to disarm Hermione. I couldn't believe it!

Book7-chapter17_Sc13.source: "It was an accident," said Harry mechanically.
Book7-chapter17_Sc13.description: Okay, it was an accident. She didn't mean to. I know that even if it feels awful.

Book7-chapter17_Sc13.source: "Well, I'll just borrow yours for now, then. While I keep watch."
Book7-chapter17_Sc13.description: I'll borrow Hermione's wand for now and keep watch. I'll rely on her wand until I can sort this out.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I couldn’t . . . make one," he panted, clutching the stitch in his side. "Wouldn’t . . . come."
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: I couldn't make a Patronus when the dementors came. I tried and it just wouldn't come. I felt useless and ashamed.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Of course!" cried Hermione, clapping a hand to her forehead and startling both of them into silence. "Harry, give me the locket! Come on," she said impatiently, clicking her fingers at him when he did not react, "the Horcrux, Harry, you’re still wearing it!"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: The locket weighs on me. The moment Hermione took it off me I felt lighter and less clammy. That thing affects how I feel and probably how I act.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore said in front of me that he never assumed he knew all of Hogwarts’s secrets. I’m telling you, if there was one place Vol —" "OI!" "YOU-KNOW-WHO, then!" Harry shouted, goaded past endurance. "If there was one place that was really important to You-Know-Who, it was Hogwarts!"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Hogwarts keeps coming back to me as the most likely place for a Horcrux. It was his home, what made him special. Even if others doubt it, I still think it's important.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "A face," muttered Harry, every time. "The same face. The thief who stole from Gregorovitch."
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: When my scar burns I see the same blond kid, the thief who stole from Gregorovitch. I can't tune into other things, only what Voldemort is thinking at that moment.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: As the days stretched into weeks, Harry began to suspect that Ron and Hermione were having conversations without, and about, him.
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: I'm starting to feel left out. Ron and Hermione have been whispering together and going quiet when I come near. I worry they expect me to have a secret plan I don't actually have.

Book7-chapter17_Sc12.description: Where's my wand? My holly and phoenix wand is nearly snapped in two, hanging on by a single feather strand and splintered right through.
I couldn't just stand by I had to try to get it fixed but it's not going to be simple or clean. Reparo might not bring it back properly.
Even after Hermione mended it the light was weak. The wand's not functioning like it should.

Book7-chapter17_Sc12.source: Harry took it into his hands as though it was a living thing that had suffered a terrible injury.
Book7-chapter17_Sc12.description: Hermione cares enough to try even when she's unsure. She gave it everything she had and she was upset about it.

Book7-chapter17_Sc7.description: Nagini almost strangled me. She had the Horcrux pressed into my chest and I could not breathe. I had to fight her off and then she let go.

Book7-chapter17_Sc7.source: the snake coiled itself around his torso, squeezing the air from him, pressing the Horcrux hard into his chest
Book7-chapter17_Sc7.description: The Horcrux is dangerous to touch and it feels like ice against your heart. It nearly stopped me from thinking or breathing.

Book7-chapter17_Sc7.source: He was abruptly awake in the sour smelling darkness
Book7-chapter17_Sc7.description: I know how close I came to losing it in there. I have to stay sharp and get that Horcrux out of play before it kills me.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: Snape seemed to be facing a constant, low level of mutiny from a hard core of students. Ginny had been banned from going into Hogsmeade. Snape had reinstated Umbridge’s old decree forbidding gatherings of three or more students or any unofficial student societies.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Snape's running into trouble. His crackdown is real and harsh. Ginny is banned from Hogsmeade and any student groups are outlawed. They're trying to squash Dumbledore's Army.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: From all of these things, Harry deduced that Ginny, and probably Neville and Luna along with her, had been doing their best to continue Dumbledore’s Army.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Ginny and probably Neville and Luna are keeping the DA going even now. They're resisting. That means the fight at Hogwarts is still on.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: This scant news made Harry want to see Ginny so badly it felt like a stomachache;
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: I miss Ginny like mad. Hearing she's in danger makes me desperate to see her.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: He imagined simply going back to school to join the destabilization of Snape’s regime: Being fed, and having a soft bed, and other people being in charge, seemed the most wonderful prospect in the world at that moment.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: The idea of going back to Hogwarts is ridiculously tempting. Food, a proper bed, other people in charge would be a relief.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: But then he remembered that he was Undesirable Number One, that there was a ten-thousand-Galleon price on his head, and that to walk into Hogwarts these days was just as dangerous as walking into the Ministry of Magic.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: I can't just stroll back to Hogwarts. I'm Undesirable Number One and there's a huge bounty on me. Returning would be suicidal.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: Phineas Nigellus inadvertently emphasized this fact by slipping in leading questions about Harry and Hermione’s whereabouts. Hermione shoved him back inside the beaded bag every time he did this, and Phineas Nigellus invariably refused to reappear for several days after these unceremonious good-byes.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Phineas Nigellus is nosy and asks where we are. Hermione shuts him away when he pushes. He sulks and doesn't show up for days.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: They did not dare remain in any one area too long, so rather than staying in the south of England, where a hard ground frost was the worst of their worries, they continued to meander up and down the country, braving a mountainside, where sleet pounded the tent; a wide, flat marsh, where the tent was flooded with chill water; and a tiny island in the middle of a Scottish loch, where snow half buried the tent in the night.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: We're moving constantly to avoid being found. We've been through mountains, marshes and a snowed under island. It's miserable and cold.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: He had also had the foresight to suggest that they take a few hours’ break from wearing the Horcrux, which was hanging over the end of the bunk beside him.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: I suggested we take a break from wearing the Horcrux. Even a few hours off feels necessary and smart.
I was about to suggest going back to Hogwarts again. I keep thinking that's the only unexplored option, even though it's dangerous.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: He pulled the pieces of the broken wand out of his pocket and, without looking at them, tucked them away in Hagrid’s pouch around his neck.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: My wand is broken. I shoved the pieces away and there is nothing I can do with them now.
