Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: Impenetrable, unhelpful, useless, like everything else Dumbledore had left behind — And his fury at Dumbledore broke over him now like lava, scorching him inside, wiping out every other feeling.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Dumbledore left us to flail about with no plan. I'm furious with him for leaving us in the dark.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: And he had dropped the photograph of the thief, and it would surely be easy now for Voldemort to find out who he was.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: I dropped the photograph. If Voldemort gets that, he has everything he needs to track us down.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: Albus Dumbledore, shortly after his mother’s death, with his friend Gellert Grindelwald.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Dumbledore used to be friends with Grindelwald. That's a name I did not expect to see next to Dumbledore's.
Seeing Dumbledore and Grindelwald together changes how I see Dumbledore. He had ties I never knew about.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: Now approaching his eighteenth birthday, Dumbledore left Hogwarts in a blaze of glory — Head Boy, Prefect, Winner of the Barnabus Finkley Prize for Exceptional Spell-Casting, British Youth Representative to the Wizengamot, Gold Medal-Winner for Ground-Breaking Contribution to the International Alchemical Conference in Cairo.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Dumbledore had a brilliant youth and was celebrated for loads of achievements before all this mess.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: The answer, it seems, is ensuring the continued imprisonment of his sister.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Dumbledore might have been involved in keeping his sister locked away. That makes me question a lot about him.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: “No,” he said quietly. “No, Hermione, I know it was an accident. You were trying to get us out of there alive, and you were incredible. I’d be dead if you hadn’t been there to help me.”
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: I told Hermione I wasn't angry with her. She saved us, and I owe her my life.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "I’m going to ask it to open, using Parseltongue," said Harry.
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: I can open that locket by speaking Parseltongue. It comes straight to me, like I always knew how to do it.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "Perhaps it had taken his recent encounter with Nagini to make him realize it."
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: After being near Nagini I get how deep this is. It clicked for me, like something I already had inside.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "Let’s get rid of the damn thing, it’s been months —"
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: We have to get rid of that locket now. I want it gone, no more putting up with it.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "You can do it," said Harry, "you can! You’ve just got the sword, I know it’s supposed to be you who uses it. Please, just get rid of it, Ron."
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: I believe Ron is the one who should destroy the locket with the sword. He can do this, so come on, do it.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "All was ashes: How much more could he lose? Ron, Dumbledore, the phoenix wand . . ."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: I trusted Dumbledore completely and now that trust is smashed to bits. I feel like I have nothing left to hang on to.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "He shared a damn sight more of what he was really thinking with Gellert Grindelwald than he ever shared with me."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: Dumbledore kept way more of himself for Grindelwald than for me. That cuts harder than anything else.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "'For the Greater Good' became Grindelwald’s slogan, his justification for all the atrocities he committed later."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: That phrase helped Grindelwald justify horrible things. If Dumbledore fed him ideas back then, that explains how it got started.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "I don't know who he loved, Hermione, but it was never me."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: I used to think Dumbledore loved and protected me. Now I don't believe he ever loved me the way I needed.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Look what he asked from me, Hermione! Risk your life, Harry! And again! And again! And don't expect me to explain everything, just trust me blindly, trust that I know what I'm doing, trust me even though I don't trust you! Never the whole truth! Never!"
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: He expected blind trust and kept me in the dark. Asking me to risk my life without full explanations feels like a betrayal.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Thanks for the tea. I’ll finish the watch. You get back in the warm."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: I still look after my mates. Even when I'm furious, I take responsibility and keep going. I'll finish the watch.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.source: She was the snake or the snake was her all along
Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: Bathilda was dead and the snake was inside her. Voldemort put it there in Godric's Hollow to wait for me.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.source: Once we were up in the room the snake sent a message to You Know Who I heard it happen inside my head I felt him get excited he said to keep me there and then she changed changed into the snake and attacked
Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: I could understand Parseltongue; the snake sent a message to Voldemort in my head, he got excited, and Bathilda turned into the snake and attacked me.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.source: It wasn't supposed to kill me just keep me there till You Know Who came
Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: It wasn't meant to kill me, only to hold me until Voldemort showed up. If I'd managed to kill the snake, it would have been worth it.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.source: You're the one who needs sleep No offense but you look terrible I'm fine
Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: I'm tired but I'm okay. I can handle it; she's the one who looks like she needs sleep.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: Well, I saw the doe first, obviously.
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: I saw a silver doe leading us to the sword in the pool. It took me straight to it and I jumped in to get it.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: and Ron stabbed it with the sword.
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: The locket opened and Ron drove the sword into it. He did the killing blow on the Horcrux.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "There before him stood Ron, fully dressed but drenched to the skin, his hair plastered to his face, the sword of Gryffindor in one hand and the Horcrux dangling from its broken chain in the other."
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: He's back. Ron turned up, soaked through, holding the sword and the Horcrux. I couldn't believe it at first.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "That’s why you jumped in, right?" "Yeah," said Harry.
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: He dived in after me and saved me. He risked himself to pull me out.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Oh yeah, I got it out," he said, rather unnecessarily, holding up the sword for Harry’s inspection.
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: He actually pulled the Horcrux out. The locket is gone from around my neck because of him.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "My Patronus is a stag." "Oh yeah. I thought it looked different. No antlers."
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: That doe Patronus wasn't Ron's. I thought it might be him, but no. My Patronus is a stag so the doe was someone else.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "I’ve — you know — I’ve come back. If —" He cleared his throat. "You know. You still want me."
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: He's back and he wants to come with us again. He made that offer, awkward as it was, and he risked his life to help me.

Book7-chapter19_Sc12.source: About the best you could hope for, I think,
Book7-chapter19_Sc12.description: It's the best I could hope for. That's about as good as it gets.

Book7-chapter19_Sc3.source: Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you.
Book7-chapter19_Sc3.description: You're the one who pulled the sword from the pool. It has to be you. I'm certain you must do it.

Book7-chapter19_Sc3.source: I'm going to open it, and you stab it. Straightaway, okay? Because whatever's in there will put up a fight.
Book7-chapter19_Sc3.description: I'll open the locket and you stab it straightaway. Whatever's inside will fight back, so be ready and strike hard.
I've found the spot by the sycamore and cleared the rock. This is where we'll do it.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I believe that the last time I saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: So Dumbledore used the sword to break a ring. That means he took it out before Ginny did.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Goblin-made armor does not require cleaning, simple girl. Goblins' silver repels mundane dirt, imbibing only that which strengthens it."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: The sword is goblin made, so it only soaks up what strengthens it. If it touched basilisk venom it would hold that poison.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "And Dumbledore didn't give it to me because he still needed it, he wanted to use it on the locket -"
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Dumbledore kept the real sword because he needed it to destroy Horcruxes. He must have left a fake at Hogwarts.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Go home then," said Harry. "Yeah, maybe I will!" shouted Ron, and he took several steps toward Harry"
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Something between Ron and me has broken. He stormed off and Disapparated. I feel betrayed and furious.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Professor Snape sent them into the Forbidden Forest, to do some work for the oaf, Hagrid."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Snape punished Ginny, Neville and Luna by sending them into the Forbidden Forest with Hagrid.

Book7-chapter19_Sc9.source: “We were there,” said Harry. “We spent two nights there, and the second night I kept thinking I could hear someone moving around in the dark and calling out!”
Book7-chapter19_Sc9.description: We stayed there two nights and I kept thinking someone was moving and calling out in the dark. I was sure someone was nearby.

Book7-chapter19_Sc9.source: “Yeah, well, that would’ve been me,” said Ron. “Your protective spells work, anyway, because I couldn’t see you and I couldn’t hear you."
Book7-chapter19_Sc9.description: Ron trusts our protective spells. They really hid us from him, even though he suspected we were close.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "We were there," said Harry. "We spent two nights there, and the second night I kept thinking I could hear someone moving around in the dark and calling out!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: We were on that hill for two nights. I kept hearing someone moving and calling in the dark and I thought someone was nearby.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "Yeah," said Harry and Hermione together automatically.
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: Right away I agreed with Hermione about the light looking like a Portkey. It made sense to me straight away.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: I had to override everything I felt and shout orders. You don't argue with a Horcrux. Stab it now, Ron.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "The thing that had lived in the Horcrux had vanished; torturing Ron had been its final act."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: The Horcrux can torture someone to the edge and then die when it's destroyed. Breaking it makes the pain stop.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "He was shaking, but not, Harry realized, from cold. Harry crammed the broken locket into his pocket, knelt down beside Ron, and placed a hand cautiously on his shoulder."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: Ron saved us and paid for it. I put the locket away and stayed with him instead of walking off. He's still my mate whether he thinks he is or not.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "Least loved, always, by the mother who craved a daughter . . . Least loved, now, by the girl who prefers your friend . . . Second best, always, eternally overshadowed . . ."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: The Horcrux attacks by twisting the worst things into your head. It dug at Ron with all that 'second best' rubbish.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "Give me back my wand! Give it back to me!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: She's terrified and furious, totally losing control, and I can't calm her down.
Ron saved me. Plain and simple. He risked himself to get back to us.
That silver thing Ron has is the Deluminator and it does more than switch lights on and off.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: “It’s okay, everything’s fine. More than fine. I’m great. There’s someone here.”
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: I'm trying to keep things calm and focused. I told them everything was fine because I didn't want panic, and I'm the one who brought Ron back into the tent.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: Harry backed into a shadowy corner, slipped off Ron’s rucksack, and attempted to blend in with the canvas.
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: I hang back and try to stay out of the way when things get heated between Ron and Hermione. I'm the mediator here and I'm ready to step in when needed.
I cast Protego to stop Hermione from attacking Ron. I act fast and decisively to prevent things getting worse.
I believe I need to try to calm Hermione down even if she won't listen. I'm determined to stop the argument before it destroys everything.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "The signature," said Hermione. "Look at the signature, Harry!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: I saw Dumbledore's handwriting with that tiny triangular mark used as his A. I can't pretend I don't now think Dumbledore had some link to that mark.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "It keeps cropping up, doesn’t it?" said Hermione. "I know Viktor said it was Grindelwald’s mark, but it was definitely on that old grave in Godric’s Hollow..."
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: That symbol has shown up in places older than Grindelwald. It isn't just Grindelwald's thing, and it keeps turning up where it matters.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "Hermione, we don’t need another Godric’s Hollow. We talked ourselves into going there, and —"
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: I'm worried about Hermione dragging us into more danger. I don't want us repeating a trip to Godric's Hollow that puts us at risk.

Book7-chapter20_Sc9.source: "He’s probably worried about what’ll happen to them if the Death Eaters find out I was here," said Harry.
Book7-chapter20_Sc9.description: He's probably worried about what'll happen to them if the Death Eaters find out I was here.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Dumbledore's dead," he said. "I saw it happen, I saw the body. He's definitely gone."
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: Dumbledore's dead. I saw it happen and I saw the body, he's definitely gone.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Dumbledore's dead," he said. "I saw it happen, I saw the body. He's definitely gone."
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: I want him to be alive, but that's not true. He's gone, and I can't pretend otherwise.

Book7-chapter21_Sc4.description: Death's actually got an Invisibility Cloak. So Death can hide himself. That sounds wrong and worrying.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Someone helped us," he kept saying. "Someone sent that doe. Someone's on our side. One Horcrux down, mate!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Someone is helping us. That doe was sent for a reason. One Horcrux is gone and things can turn in our favour.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: Bolstered by the destruction of the locket, they set to debating the possible locations of the other Horcruxes
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Destroying the locket matters. If we can get one, we can get more. I'm feeling hopeful we can find the rest.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: above all, Ron’s return, made Harry so happy that it was quite difficult to maintain a straight face
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Ron being back changes everything. I'm actually that happy to have him with us again.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: Harry had finally managed to tell Ron the whole story of his and Hermione’s various wanderings, right up to the full story of what had happened at Godric’s Hollow
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: I've told Ron everything about what Hermione and I went through and what happened at Godric's Hollow. There's nothing more to hide from him.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: "The what?" "You and Hermione have stopped saying You-Know-Who’s name!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: I've fallen into saying 'You-Know-Who' but I don't mind saying V. It's a bad habit, but it's mine.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: "She’s like my sister," he went on. "I love her like a sister and I reckon she feels the same way about me. It’s always been like that. I thought you knew."
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: She's like a sister to me. I love her like family and I think she feels the same. It's always been that way.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: "With you gone . . ." He could not finish; it was only now that Ron was here again that Harry fully realized how much his absence had cost them.
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: With Ron gone, things fell apart between us. Now he's back I can see how much it cost us and how important he is.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: "You’ve sort of made up for it tonight," said Harry. "Getting the sword. Finishing off the Horcrux. Saving my life."
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: What Ron did tonight mattered. He got the sword, helped finish the Horcrux, and saved my life. That counts for a lot.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: It was gloriously warm after the pool and the forest, the only illumination the bluebell flames still shimmering in a
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: The tent was warm and lit by those bluebell flames when we came back. I couldn't wait to wake Hermione.

Book7-chapter21_Sc1.source: "I'm sorry," said Harry. "I still don't really understand."
Book7-chapter21_Sc1.description: I still don't get what the Deathly Hallows are. Plain and simple, it makes no sense to me yet.

Book7-chapter21_Sc1.source: To be polite, he took a sip from his cup too, and almost gagged: The stuff was quite disgusting
Book7-chapter21_Sc1.description: I sipped that Gurdyroot infusion to be polite and nearly choked on it. That stuff is disgusting.

Book7-chapter20_Sc7.source: "Hello, Mr Lovegood," said Harry, holding out his hand. "I’m Harry, Harry Potter."
Book7-chapter20_Sc7.description: I introduced myself straight away and offered my hand. I make things simple and direct.

Book7-chapter20_Sc7.source: "Xenophilius did not take Harry’s hand, although the eye that was not pointing inward at his nose slid straight to the scar on Harry’s forehead."
Book7-chapter20_Sc7.description: He stared at my scar the moment I showed myself. People still spot it and it makes them uneasy.

Book7-chapter20_Sc7.source: "It won’t take long," said Harry, slightly disappointed by this less-than-warm welcome.
Book7-chapter20_Sc7.description: That was awkward. I felt a bit let down by his coldness, but I kept patient and pushed to come in anyway.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "You want to go to Godric’s Hollow. I agree, I think we should. I mean, I can’t think of anywhere else it could be either. It’ll be dangerous, but the more I think of it, the more likely it seems it’s there."
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: All right. Godric's Hollow is where we need to go. I can't think of anywhere else it could be. It's dangerous but it really does seem the most likely place.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Bathilda Bagshot still lives in Godric’s Hollow."
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Bathilda Bagshot might still be living in Godric's Hollow. Muriel said that and it stuck with me.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Harry, what if Bathilda’s got the sword? What if Dumbledore entrusted it to her?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: I can't rule it out. If Dumbledore wanted someone to hide the sword, maybe he trusted Bathilda with it. That would explain why I didn't think about the sword at first.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Remember what Muriel said?" ... "Bathilda Bagshot still lives in Godric’s Hollow."
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Part of why I want to go is to see my parents' graves and the house where I almost died. Bathilda being there makes it feel more important.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "We’ll need to practice Disapparating together under the Invisibility Cloak for a start, and perhaps Disillusionment Charms would be sensible too, unless you think we should go the whole hog and use Polyjuice Potion?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: We need a plan. We have to practice Disapparating under the Cloak and learn Disillusionment Charms. If disguises must be thicker we might even use Polyjuice, and then we would have to collect hair.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "All this snow!" Hermione whispered beneath the cloak. "Why didn’t we think of snow? After all our precautions, we’ll leave prints! We’ll just have to get rid of them — you go in front, I’ll do it —"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: The snow is a problem. We'll leave footprints. If we go in I'll lead and Hermione will follow to cover the prints. We have to be careful about obvious tracks.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “We keep trying to convince ourselves Dumbledore left us secret signs and clues —”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: I'm sick of convincing myself Dumbledore left secret signs for us. Enough guessing. We need to focus on finding Horcruxes, not chasing every possible clue.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “Only, once we’ve seen Lovegood, let’s try and look for some more Horcruxes, shall we? Where do the Lovegoods live, anyway? Do either of you know?”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: Fine, we'll go see the Lovegoods, but straight after that I want us hunting Horcruxes again. No distractions.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Speaking of Dumbledore, have you heard what Skeeter wrote about him?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Skeeter's written something about Dumbledore being pals with Grindelwald. That's what people are talking about.
He was our age then. That matters to me. It doesn't make Dumbledore some monster overnight.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: Harry continued to practice with the blackthorn wand.
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: I'm still practicing with the blackthorn wand. I need to keep getting better, plain and simple.

Book7-chapter21_Sc7.source: "Thought you’d lure us here to kill us, did you? And you think you’ll get your girl back like this?"
Book7-chapter21_Sc7.description: So they reckon they lured people here to kill them and snatch her back. That's ruthless and desperate, and it means they're playing dirty to get what they want.
Someone just shouted that I'm upstairs. Brilliant, they've blown my cover and given away where I am.

Book7-chapter21_Sc7.source: "Homenum revelio," said the voice at the foot of the stairs.
Book7-chapter21_Sc7.description: They used a Homenum revelio at the stairs. They're trying to detect people, so hiding won't work for long.

Book7-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Anyway, his Patronus was a phoenix, not a doe."
Book7-chapter20_Sc3.description: Dumbledore's Patronus was a phoenix, not a doe.

Book7-chapter20_Sc3.source: "No," Harry corrected him. "He must've known you'd always want to come back."
Book7-chapter20_Sc3.description: Dumbledore didn't expect Ron to abandon me for good. He left things because he knew Ron would come back to us.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "So the Elder Wand," said Harry quickly, before Hermione could retort, "you think that exists too?"
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: You reckon the Elder Wand might be real? If it is, its history of changing hands by force could explain why people end up dead trying to get it.
Hermione and I are both baffled and annoyed by this. I look to her when something sounds daft because we think alike on this sort of thing.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“So how did the sword get in that pool?” “Whoever cast the Patronus must have put it there.”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: The sword wasn’t sitting there by chance. Whoever sent that Patronus put the sword in the pool.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“The Horcrux was still swinging from Ron’s hand. The locket was twitching slightly. Harry knew that the thing inside it was agitated again. It had sensed the presence of the sword and had tried to kill Harry rather than let him possess it.”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: The locket is a Horcrux and whatever’s inside it reacts violently to the sword. It tried to get at me when it sensed the sword.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“You reckon this is the real one?” asked Ron. “One way to find out, isn’t there?” said Harry. ... Now was not the time for long discussions; now was the moment to destroy the locket once and for all.”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: We can test whether that’s the real sword and we can’t dither. This is the moment to destroy the locket straight away.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "It looked like the bizarre offspring of a workbench and a set of old shelves, but after a moment Harry deduced that it was an old-fashioned printing press, due to the fact that it was churning out Quibblers."
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: I worked out that machine was a printing press because it was spitting out Quibblers. That was obvious once I looked properly.
We need help now. I said it straight because there was no time to faff about.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "His good eye moved again to Harry’s scar. He seemed simultaneously terrified and mesmerized."
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: Xenophilius stared at my scar like it meant something huge to him. I can tell he sees me as more than just another person with problems.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: 'And Death spoke to them. He was angry that he had been cheated out of three new victims, for travelers usually drowned in the river.'
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Wait, so in the story Death actually talks to the brothers. That's bizarre, but yes, Death speaks like a character.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: 'So the oldest brother, who was a combative man, asked for a wand more powerful than any in existence: a wand that must always win duels for its owner.'
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Right, the oldest asked Death for an unbeatable wand. That means someone in the tale wanted power to beat Death itself.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "There’s someone up there all right, Selwyn," said the second man sharply. "It’s Potter, I tell you, it’s Potter!" sobbed Xenophilius.
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: They're sure it's me up there. I need to be careful and get out now.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "You can have your little girl, Lovegood," said Selwyn, "if you get up those stairs and bring me down Harry Potter."
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: They're using Luna to force Xenophilius to hand me over. He's terrified for her, so I have to move fast.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "Come on," Harry whispered, "we’ve got to get out of here."
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: We have to get out now. No hanging about, start digging and get Ron free.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "Please, Ron! Harry, hold on tight to my hand, Ron, grab my shoulder." Harry held out his left hand.
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: I trust Hermione enough to follow her plan and hold on. We're a team and I will do what she says.

Book7-chapter21_Sc9.source: Xenophilius was trying to shift it using a Hover Charm.
Book7-chapter21_Sc9.description: He's trying to hover the printing press to clear the stairs. He's mucking about with a Hover Charm.

Book7-chapter21_Sc9.source: Harry did not know what Hermione was waiting for.
Book7-chapter21_Sc9.description: I couldn't work out what Hermione was hanging on for, but I trusted her to do something about it.

Book7-chapter21_Sc9.source: “Obliviate!” cried Hermione, pointing her wand first into his face, then at the floor beneath them. “Deprimo!”
Book7-chapter21_Sc9.description: Hermione's the one who actually fixed it — she slapped an Obliviate at Xenophilius and then used a lowering charm to shift the press. Smart, fast, and direct.

Book7-chapter21_Sc6.source: Peverell . . . he had heard that name before. . . .
Book7-chapter21_Sc6.description: Something in my memory shifted when I heard Peverell. That name means something important.
They're here and they know I'm involved. They think Lovegood brought me to them and they're torturing him for answers.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "Yeah, you are, Hermione," agreed Harry fervently. "I don’t know what we’d do without you."
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: Hermione is absolutely crucial to us. I don't know what we'd do without her, she's the one keeping us going.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "She will," said Harry. He could not bear to contemplate the alternative. "She’s tough, Luna, much tougher than you’d think. She’s probably teaching all the inmates about Wrackspurts and Nargles."
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: Luna will survive Azkaban. She's tougher than people think and she'll cope, even in that place.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Get everyone out first. I am not risking more lives when Voldemort is closing in.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "The moment anyone entered the room and saw the absence of three prisoners, they were lost."
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: If people notice prisoners gone, everything is finished. We had to stop anyone coming down.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "You will not win, you cannot win! That wand will never, ever be yours"
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Voldemort will react with instant, terrifying violence when summoned. His return will hurt me through the scar and make everything collapse fast.
When there is a chance to get someone out, I have to grab it and run. Get people to safety is top priority.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Dobby has no master! Dobby is a free elf, and Dobby has come to save Harry Potter and his friends!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Dobby risked everything for us. He is fiercely loyal and will do something nobody expected. I owe him.
Even when we escape, terrible things can happen. I could not save Dobby in time and that hit me like a knife.

Book7-chapter25_Sc7.source: "No . . . no . . . I really must get back," said Lupin at last, declining yet another goblet of wine.
Book7-chapter25_Sc7.description: Lupin left early. He got up, wrapped his traveling cloak around himself and went off. He's not staying for long.

Book7-chapter25_Sc7.source: "Godfather, Harry!" said Bill as they walked into the kitchen together, helping clear the table.
Book7-chapter25_Sc7.description: Bill's congratulating tone reminded me that people are still celebrating and that I'm meant to be part of this family moment, even if things are tense.
Bill knows about my plan with Griphook. He spelled it out to me as if it were obvious.

Book7-chapter25_Sc7.source: "I know goblins," said Bill. "I've worked for Gringotts ever since I left Hogwarts."
Book7-chapter25_Sc7.description: Bill knows goblins. He worked at Gringotts and he's warning me because he understands them and what they might do.

Book7-chapter25_Sc7.source: "I wanted a private word, actually, Harry. It hasn't been easy to get an opportunity with the cottage this full of people."
Book7-chapter25_Sc7.description: This is serious. Bill wanted privacy to warn me, so I can't treat his words lightly. He's worried enough to pull me aside.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: Don't let anyone touch my scar. It hurts like mad and if they probe it I can't keep my head clear.
People will treat me like a prize to be paraded. They think catching me and my wand is worth everything, but I have to stay focused, not let them use my fear against me.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I haven't got — they say he's using the Malfoys' place as a base. We’ll take the boy there."
Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: Greyback won't summon Voldemort himself. He's useful but not trusted enough to call in the big boss. That means they plan to take me to the Malfoys.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Help us! We're in the cellar of Malfoy Manor, help us!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: I can't rely on magical messages to save us easily. I begged and got nothing. I have to act with what we've actually got in the room.
Dobby cares enough to risk himself for me. He will help get some of us out and I can ask him to fetch people to safety.

Book7-chapter22_Sc2.source: Three objects, or Hallows, which, if united, will make the possessor master of Death . . .
Book7-chapter22_Sc2.description: Three things together would make someone master of Death. If I had them, I'd be the one in control.

Book7-chapter22_Sc2.source: Hallows versus Horcruxes? Was there a way, after all, to ensure that he was the one who triumphed? If he were the master of the Deathly Hallows, would he be safe?
Book7-chapter22_Sc2.description: Maybe the Hallows are the answer against Horcruxes. If I owned the Hallows, maybe I could beat Voldemort and stay alive.

Book7-chapter22_Sc2.source: He had pulled out his Invisibility Cloak and was running it through his fingers, the cloth supple as water, light as air.
Book7-chapter22_Sc2.description: My Invisibility Cloak is astonishingly light and smooth. I can feel it, almost like it's part of me when I touch it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc10.source: “Right,” said Harry as Bill opened the door, “yeah. Thanks. I’ll bear that in mind.”
Book7-chapter25_Sc10.description: Right. I heard him. Thanks. I'll bear that in mind and actually remember it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc9.source: All goblin-made objects are, in goblin eyes, rightfully theirs.
Book7-chapter25_Sc9.description: So goblins think anything they make belongs to them no matter what. Even if a wizard buys something they'd see it as only rented and expect it back eventually.

Book7-chapter25_Sc9.source: They consider our habit of keeping goblin-made objects, passing them from wizard to wizard without further payment, little more than theft.
Book7-chapter25_Sc9.description: They reckon our way of handing goblin stuff down from wizard to wizard is basically stealing. That's mental.

Book7-chapter25_Sc9.source: All I am saying is to be very careful what you promise goblins, Harry. It would be less dangerous to break into Gringotts than to renege on a promise to a goblin.
Book7-chapter25_Sc9.description: I can't promise goblins anything lightly. If I go back on my word to one of them it could be worse than breaking into Gringotts. I need to be careful.

Book7-chapter25_Sc3.description: I won't be lying, honest. I'm doing what has to be done, even if it feels wrong. I'm defiant about it but ashamed at the same time.

Book7-chapter25_Sc3.source: He remembered the words that had been engraved over the gateway to Nurmengard: FOR THE GREATER GOOD. He pushed the idea away.
Book7-chapter25_Sc3.description: That whole 'for the greater good' stuff makes me uneasy. I shove the idea out of my head because we've no choice, but it still sits wrong with me.

Book7-chapter25_Sc3.source: "I have your word, Harry Potter, that you will give me the sword of Gryffindor if I help you?" "Yes," said Harry.
Book7-chapter25_Sc3.description: I gave Griphook my word that I'll hand over the Sword of Gryffindor if he helps us. I meant it, even if I'm worried about it.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "I do," said Lupin firmly. "There is no doubt at all in my mind that his death would be proclaimed as widely as possible by the Death Eaters if it had happened... 'The Boy Who Lived' remains a symbol of everything for which we are fighting"
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Lupin still believes I'm alive and sees me as a symbol. If he thinks that, maybe he forgives me. That hits me hard, and I feel both grateful and ashamed.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Rubeus Hagrid... has narrowly escaped arrest within the grounds of Hogwarts... Hagrid was not taken into custody, and is, we believe, on the run."
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Hagrid got away. He's on the run after supposedly hosting a Support Harry Potter party at Hogwarts. That means he's still out there and dangerous times don't stop him from being reckless.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "And I'd tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right."
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Lupin telling me to follow my instincts makes me trust my gut more. If he says my instincts are nearly always right, I should listen to them.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Keep twiddling those dials: The next password will be 'Mad-Eye.'"
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Potterwatch will use 'Mad-Eye' as the next password. That gives us a lead to find their next broadcast.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Maybe he’s lying," Harry said, opening his eyes again. "Griphook. Maybe Gryffindor didn’t take the sword. How do we know the goblin version of history’s right?"
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: Maybe the goblin story isn't true. I can't just accept their version of history without question.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "We’ll tell him he can have the sword after he’s helped us get into that vault — but we’ll be careful to avoid telling him exactly when he can have it."
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: I'll tell Griphook he can have the sword after he helps us, but I'm going to be careful about the timing so we can use it first.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "He can have it," Harry went on, "after we’ve used it on all of the Horcruxes. I’ll make sure he gets it then. I’ll keep my word."
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: I want Griphook's help and I intend to keep my word about giving the sword back after we've used it on the Horcruxes.

Book7-chapter25_Sc1.source: I have reached my decision, Harry Potter. I have decided to help you
Book7-chapter25_Sc1.description: He's agreed to help us but he expects payment. That's clear. I can't just assume he'll do it for free.

Book7-chapter25_Sc1.source: I want the sword. The sword of Godric Gryffindor.
Book7-chapter25_Sc1.description: He wants the sword, not gold. That sword is exactly what he's after.

Book7-chapter25_Sc1.source: It was Ragnuk the First's, taken from him by Godric Gryffindor
Book7-chapter25_Sc1.description: So goblins don't see the sword as simply ours. They reckon it belonged to goblin ancestors before Gryffindor took it. That changes how I think about who has a claim to it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc1.source: That's great! Griphook, thank you, we're really
Book7-chapter25_Sc1.description: I felt relieved when he seemed willing to help. But that relief turned to worry once I realised what he wanted in return.

Book7-chapter25_Sc5.source: ["You—you'll be godfather?" "M-me?" "You, yes, of course — Dora quite agrees, no one better —"]
Book7-chapter25_Sc5.description: I'm the godfather. I couldn't believe it at first when Remus asked me, but I'm overwhelmed and honoured. I feel stunned and really happy about it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc5.source: ["I — yeah — blimey —" (Harry felt overwhelmed, astonished, delighted)]
Book7-chapter25_Sc5.description: I'm amazed and delighted. Everything feels lighter, like the blast in Grimmauld Place never happened.

Book7-chapter25_Sc8.source: "If you have struck any kind of bargain with Griphook, and most particularly if that bargain involves treasure, you must be exceptionally careful. Goblin notions of ownership, payment, and repayment are not the same as human ones."
Book7-chapter25_Sc8.description: Bill warned me to be careful if I've made a deal with Griphook. Goblins think about ownership differently to wizards and I need to watch my back.

Book7-chapter25_Sc8.source: "To a goblin, the rightful and true master of any object is the maker, not the purchaser."
Book7-chapter25_Sc8.description: Goblins believe the maker is the true owner of an object, not the person who bought it. That could make any treasure-related bargain dangerous.

Book7-chapter25_Sc8.source: "I can’t tell you that," said Harry. "Sorry, Bill."
Book7-chapter25_Sc8.description: I won't tell Bill what I promised Griphook. I kept my mouth shut and I'm sticking to it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc4.source: "It is one of the most ancient chambers. The oldest Wizarding families store their treasures at the deepest level, where the vaults are largest and best protected."
Book7-chapter25_Sc4.description: The Lestrange vault is ancient. The oldest wizarding families keep their valuables down in the deepest, biggest, most protected level.

Book7-chapter25_Sc4.source: "I have visited the Lestranges' vault only once...on the occasion I was told to place inside it the false sword."
Book7-chapter25_Sc4.description: Griphook put the false sword in the Lestrange vault once. He knows how that vault works and has been inside it.

Book7-chapter25_Sc4.source: "I am a werewolf, married to Nymphadora Tonks, and you, the Secret-Keeper of Shell Cottage, told me the address and bade me come in an emergency!"
Book7-chapter25_Sc4.description: Remus Lupin is a werewolf and he's married to Nymphadora Tonks. Someone at Shell Cottage gave him the address and asked him to come in an emergency.
Lupin shouted that it's a boy, so whatever's happened involves a baby boy.
Lupin turned up suddenly and straightaway made himself known. I couldn't believe he was here and that he'd come to help.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "The Cloak was exactly what Xenophilius had described: A cloak that really and truly renders the wearer completely invisible"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: The Cloak is the real deal. It makes you truly invisible and it lasts forever. It's not just a trick.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "He’s my ancestor! I’m descended from the third brother!"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: I'm descended from Ignotus Peverell. That makes the Cloak part of my family inheritance. That's mine by right.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "IT’S IN HERE! He left me the ring — it’s in the Snitch!"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Dumbledore left me something hidden inside the Snitch. I think it's my mum's ring, which must be the Resurrection Stone.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "That’s what he’s after." "You-Know-Who’s after the Elder Wand."
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Voldemort isn't looking for a new wand. He's hunting the Elder Wand, an old wand with a bloody history, and he doesn't see the whole picture about the Hallows.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "The Deathly Hallows are real, and I’ve got one — maybe two —"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: The Hallows are real. I already have at least one Hallow and maybe two. If I get them all I'm master of death, or at least that's what it looks like to me now.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore usually let me find out stuff for myself. He let me try my strength, take risks. This feels like the kind of thing he’d do."
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: I trust that Dumbledore left this for me to discover. He wanted me to learn and to face things on my own.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "He took a Hallow, and turned it into a Horcrux"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Voldemort used part of what he found as a Horcrux. That shows he didn't know everything about the Hallows or he'd have done something different.
That message on the Snitch matters. The Snitch will open at some specific time or event, not straight away, and I have to wait until the right moment.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "If Voldemort had known about the Deathly Hallows, surely he would have sought them"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: If Voldemort had known the Hallows made someone master of death, he would have chased them instead of relying solely on Horcruxes. So he didn't know the full truth.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "I remember, Harry Potter. Even amongst goblins, you are very famous."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Griphook knows who I am and holds me in a kind of wary respect. That can help or hinder us depending on how I play it.
Griphook remembers I brought him here and that I saved him. That debt affects how he reacts to me.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "What do you seek within the Lestranges' vault?"
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: There is something in the Lestrange vault that terrified Bellatrix. I am sure now it is a Horcrux. We have to get in.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "The sword that lies inside it is a fake. This is the real one."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: The sword Griphook touched is the real Gryffindor sword and the one in Bellatrix's vault is a fake. That changes what we can trust about the vault's contents.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "It is against our code to speak of the secrets of Gringotts. We are the guardians of fabulous treasures."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Goblins take vault secrets very seriously. If we want into Gringotts we need a goblin's cooperation, not just brute force.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "He probably told her it was a treasured possession and asked her to place it in her vault."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Voldemort would have hidden a Horcrux where he thought it would seem like a private treasure. The Lestrange vault fits that exactly.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "The right to carry a wand has long been contested between wizards and goblins."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Goblins resent wand-carriers and feel their craft is stolen from them. Any deal with Griphook will be tangled up with that grievance.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "I think he would have envied anyone who had a key to a Gringotts vault."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Voldemort would have seen a Gringotts vault as a symbol of belonging and power. That explains why he trusted the Lestranges with something important.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "I shall think about it," said Griphook maddeningly.
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Griphook is not agreeing yet. He is keeping us hanging. I have to be careful and persuasive if I want his help.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "Mr. Ollivander, I’m sorry to disturb you," "You rescued us. I thought we would die in that place."
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Ollivander and others were rescued because of me. People who suffered under Voldemort's followers are grateful and weakened. Time is short and I need to act fast.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: Hermione needed help and Ron had taken her inside. I felt responsible and needed to know she was safe.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: I want to do it properly. Not by magic. Have you got a spade?
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: Dobby deserved respect, not a quick wand-fix. I wanted to do things properly for him, even if it meant getting my hands dirty.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: I need to speak to Griphook and Ollivander
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: I have to talk to the goblin and Ollivander right now. Nothing can wait; there's something important I must sort out with them.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: We can't tell you what we're doing
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: This mission is secret. I can't explain our plans even to allies. It's on us to carry it out without spreading details.
Dobby's death hit me hard. I owe him everything he did for us, and losing him makes me more determined and angrier at whoever's responsible.

Book7-chapter28_Sc1.source: "The Summoning Charm had not worked on it."
Book7-chapter28_Sc1.description: The Summoning Charm didn't work on the cloak. I grabbed it and it stayed put.

Book7-chapter28_Sc1.source: "They were ready for us," whispered Harry.
Book7-chapter28_Sc1.description: They set a trap for us. Of course they knew we were coming.
They're searching the streets and ready to split up to find us. We're being hunted.

Book7-chapter27_Sc1.source: "No idea," Harry bellowed back. His hands were numb with cold but he did not dare attempt to shift his grip.
Book7-chapter27_Sc1.description: I don't know what it's after. My hands are numb with cold but I am not letting go no matter what.

Book7-chapter27_Sc1.source: He had been wondering for some time what they would do if they saw the coast sail beneath them, if the dragon headed for open sea; he was cold and numb, not to mention desperately hungry and thirsty.
Book7-chapter27_Sc1.description: If that dragon heads for the sea and we see the coast disappear, we're in real trouble. I'm freezing, starving and parched, and I keep thinking when that thing last had a meal.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "No," whispered Ollivander. "I am sorry, very sorry, but a wand that has suffered this degree of damage cannot be repaired by any means that I know of."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: My wand is gone for good. I can't fix it and I can't pretend otherwise. That's that.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "In general, however, where a wand has been won, its allegiance will change."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: If you take a wand from someone, the wand will usually switch its loyalty to you. Taking it matters.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "The wand chooses the wizard," said Ollivander.
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Wands pick witches and wizards, not the other way round. That's how wandlore works.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I had . . . never heard of such a thing. Your wand performed something unique that night. The connection of the twin cores is incredibly rare,"
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: My wand did something nobody expected because of its twin core link. It's weird and rare and it explains why my wand beat another that night.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "He wanted to know everything I could tell him about the wand variously known as the Deathstick, the Wand of Destiny, or the Elder Wand."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Voldemort was asking about the Elder Wand. He wants it and he thinks it could beat whatever protects me.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "The Dark Lord in possession of the Deathstick is, I must admit . . . formidable."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: If Voldemort gets the Elder Wand he could become terrifyingly powerful. That's plain as day.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Gregorovitch had the Elder Wand a long time ago," he said. "I saw You-Know-Who trying to find him. When he tracked him down, he found that Gregorovitch didn’t have it anymore: It was stolen from him by Grindelwald."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: The Elder Wand has a history. Gregorovitch had it, Grindelwald stole it from him, then Dumbledore beat Grindelwald and took it.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore had the Elder Wand?" "At Hogwarts," said Harry.
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Dumbledore got the Elder Wand and kept it at Hogwarts. Voldemort knows that and he's already gone after it.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore didn’t want me to have it. He didn’t want me to take it. He wanted me to get the Horcruxes."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Dumbledore didn't want me chasing the Elder Wand. He wanted me focused on the Horcruxes. I see now why he set things up that way.

Book7-chapter27_Sc2.source: Every part of Harry ached with the effort of holding on to the dragon’s back.
Book7-chapter27_Sc2.description: My whole body is dead from holding on to this dragon, I can barely keep my grip.

Book7-chapter27_Sc2.source: Harry looked down and saw deep green mountains and lakes, coppery in the sunset.
Book7-chapter27_Sc2.description: We're getting lower, I can see mountains and a lake down there, the view is getting clearer.

Book7-chapter27_Sc2.source: he wondered whether it had divined the presence of fresh water by the flashes of reflected sunlight.
Book7-chapter27_Sc2.description: I reckon the dragon might be homing in on that lake because it saw the sunlight on the water.

Book7-chapter27_Sc2.source: Lower and lower the dragon flew, in great spiraling circles, honing in, it seemed, upon one of the smaller lakes.
Book7-chapter27_Sc2.description: The dragon is spiraling down toward that smaller lake, it's definitely aiming for it.

Book7-chapter26_Sc3.description: I lit my wand to find things fast. Point, bright, get on with it.
Don't touch the treasure. Touching makes copies and burns you. Simple as that.

Book7-chapter26_Sc3.source: "If you want the sword, Griphook, then you’ll have to help us more than — wait! Can I touch stuff with the sword? Hermione, give it here!"
Book7-chapter26_Sc3.description: I thought the goblin would help if we needed the sword. I had to try bargaining and then use the sword to get the cup. I can't rely on goblins to keep their side.
I can yank someone down from being hoisted and use that moment to grab what we need. Quick spells, quick moves.
When things go wrong, blasting forward works. I will stun and force a way through rather than wait around.
If you break the dragon's chains the dragon will get free and you can use it as your escape. Dangerous, but desperate times call for desperate moves.
Griphook betrayed us the moment he could. I gave him my trust and he chose the sword over his promise. I will not be naive about goblins taking what they can.

Book7-chapter27_Sc4.source: "Harry’s ribs ached, he felt lightheaded with hunger, but he lay back on the grass beneath the reddening sky and laughed"
Book7-chapter27_Sc4.description: My ribs hurt and I'm starving, but I couldn't stop laughing — lying back on the grass, I just laughed to keep myself going.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "They ran behind the counter and through a second doorway, which led to a rickety wooden staircase that they climbed as fast as they could."
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: We ducked behind the counter and up a rickety staircase into a grubby sitting room. It's the Hog's Head and it's as dingy as you'd expect.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "Their savior, whom Harry now recognized as the Hog’s Head’s barman, was the only person not wearing a hood."
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: I recognized the barman. He wasn't hooded like the others. He stood out, plain as day.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "So what? You send dementors down my street, I’ll send a Patronus back at ’em! I’m not having ’em near me, I’ve told you that, I’m not having it!"
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: The barman shouted he wouldn't stand for dementors in his street and that he'd send a Patronus back. He sounds stubborn and protective of his place.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "That wasn’t your Patronus!" said a Death Eater. "That was a stag, it was Potter’s!"
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: Someone accused the Patronus of being a stag and called it mine. They think the stag Patronus belongs to me.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "Stag!" roared the barman, and he pulled out a wand. "Stag!"
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: The barman yelled 'Stag' and pulled his wand like he meant to fight. He was ready to act, wand out and loud about it.

Book7-chapter28_Sc4.source: "Still wearing the Invisibility Cloak, they crept toward the grimy window and looked down."
Book7-chapter28_Sc4.description: We're under the Invisibility Cloak, sneaking to see what's happening without being spotted.

Book7-chapter29_Sc1.source: "I don't know how to thank you. You've saved our lives twice."
Book7-chapter29_Sc1.description: You're a lifesaver. I owe you one, plain and simple.
It is true. We did break into Gringotts and we did escape on a dragon.

Book7-chapter29_Sc1.source: "There’s no chance of getting through any of them now, not with curses over the entrances and Death Eaters and dementors waiting at the exits."
Book7-chapter29_Sc1.description: All the old passages are sealed up and guarded. There is no safe way in or out through them now.

Book7-chapter27_Sc3.source: I say we jump when it gets low enough! Straight into the water before it realizes we're here!
Book7-chapter27_Sc3.description: We'll jump when it gets low enough, straight into the water before it realises the dragon spots us

Book7-chapter27_Sc3.source: At least we can't wear it this time, that'd look a bit weird hanging round our necks
Book7-chapter27_Sc3.description: I got the Horcrux, but we don't have the sword. I even had to drip dittany on the burn from my ripped jeans
No sword. That's messed everything up, it's annoying and I need to figure out how to cope without it

Book7-chapter28_Sc3.source: "He could not, would not, suffer the Dementor’s Kiss, whatever happened afterward."
Book7-chapter28_Sc3.description: I will not let them give anyone the Dementor's Kiss. I can't, I won't stand for that.

Book7-chapter28_Sc3.source: "Could they sense fear in the vicinity? ... tasting despair on the air, closing in"
Book7-chapter28_Sc3.description: Dementors home in on fear and despair. When people are terrified they come faster.

Book7-chapter28_Sc3.source: "He whispered, 'Expecto Patronum!' The silver stag burst from his wand"
Book7-chapter28_Sc3.description: I shouted Expecto Patronum and a silver stag came out of my wand. It works for me.

Book7-chapter28_Sc3.source: "It was of Ron and Hermione that he thought as he whispered, 'Expecto Patronum!'"
Book7-chapter28_Sc3.description: Ron and Hermione are everything right now. I thought of them the second I cast the Patronus.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "Act now, act now," whispered Griphook in Harry’s ear, "the Imperius Curse!"
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Right now I have to use Imperio. If I don't act quick I lose control of the whole plan.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "They’re Imperiused," he added, in response to Hermione and Ron’s confused queries about Travers and Bogrod, who were both now standing there looking blank.
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: The Imperius actually makes people look blank and do exactly what I tell them when it takes hold.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "I don't think I did it strongly enough, I don't know. . . ."
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: I can't half-arse an Unforgivable. If I don't mean it properly it might not work.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "The Thief’s Downfall!" said Griphook, clambering to his feet and looking back at the deluge onto the tracks, which, Harry knew now, had been more than water.
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: There's a defense in Gringotts that washes away enchantments and disguises. It ruined our cover and stripped Hermione back to herself.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "We need him," said Griphook, "we cannot enter the vault without a Gringotts goblin. And we need the Clankers!"
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: We can't open a vault without a goblin. We need Bogrod and those Clankers to get past the dragon.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "Good, good! So, if you will follow me, Madam Lestrange," said the old goblin, hopping down off his stool and vanishing from sight, "I shall take you to your vault."
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: The goblins will play along if they think it's their orders. I can use that to manipulate them with Imperio when I must.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "Make him press his hand to the door!" Griphook urged Harry, who turned his wand again upon Bogrod. The old goblin obeyed, pressing his palm to the wood, and the door of the vault melted away to reveal a cavelike opening crammed from floor to ceiling with golden coins and goblets..."
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Once the goblin touches the vault it opens. Getting a goblin to press the door is the key to getting inside.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "It’s your eye I’ve been seeing in the mirror."
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: That mirror showed me Aberforth has been watching us. He buys mirrors like that and keeps an eye out.
Aberforth sent Dobby to help us. He expected the elf to be around with us.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "He’s dead," said Harry. "Bellatrix Lestrange killed him."
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: Dobby is dead. Bellatrix killed him and I buried him. That matters to me and it will matter to how I carry on.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "Bought it from Dung ’bout a year ago," said Aberforth.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: Aberforth bought Sirius’s mirror from Dung. He knew what it was and has been trying to keep watch.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "He thought he was back there with you and Grindelwald, I know he did," said Harry.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: Dumbledore was not free of the past. He was tormented and not the untouchable figure people make him out to be.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "Professor Dumbledore cared about Harry, very much," said Hermione in a low voice.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: I still trust Dumbledore enough to follow his plan. I know there are things he hid, but I'm committed to finishing what he started.

Book7-chapter29_Sc2.source: "You’re right," said Harry, "but tell us about Hogwarts, Neville, we haven’t heard anything."
Book7-chapter29_Sc2.description: Right, so Hogwarts is basically under their control. The Carrows run discipline and it's brutal. They're teaching Dark Arts and forcing kids to use the Cruciatus on others.

Book7-chapter29_Sc2.source: "They’re in charge of all discipline. They like punishment, the Carrows."
Book7-chapter29_Sc2.description: That's worse than I thought. This isn't just harsh rules, it's deliberate torture and humiliation, and the whole place has been twisted into something cruel.

Book7-chapter29_Sc2.source: "The thing is, it helps when people stand up to them, it gives everyone hope. I used to notice that when you did it, Harry."
Book7-chapter29_Sc2.description: People still took courage from what I did. I didn't realize how much my actions mattered to students like Neville.

Book7-chapter29_Sc3.source: "They what?" said Harry, Ron, and Hermione together.
Book7-chapter29_Sc3.description: They kidnapped Neville's gran to try to control him. That's brutal and desperate.
We're in some kind of hideout — it looks like the Room of Requirement they've set up as a D.A. base.

Book7-chapter29_Sc3.source: "Look who it is! Didn’t I tell you?" As Harry emerged into the room beyond the passage, there were several screams and yells: "HARRY!" "It’s Potter, it’s POTTER!" "Ron!" "Hermione!"
Book7-chapter29_Sc3.description: People here clearly trust and cheer me — I'm a symbol for them, and they're glad I'm back.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “And you’ll be using her actual wand,” said Harry, nodding toward the walnut wand, “so I reckon you’ll be pretty convincing.”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: If Hermione uses Bellatrix’s actual wand, people will buy her as Bellatrix. That will help our disguise.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “This is the wand that tortured Neville’s mum and dad, and who knows how many other people? This is the wand that killed Sirius!”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: That wand is dangerous and feels wrong. I suddenly want to get rid of it, smash it with the sword, because it feels like a bit of her.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: The door of the bedroom opened and Griphook entered. Harry reached instinctively for the hilt of the sword and drew it close to him, but regretted his action at once: He could tell that the goblin had noticed.
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: I’m on edge around Griphook. I reach for the sword when he comes in, and I don’t trust him. I want him gone as soon as possible.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: They had been firm on this point, because Hermione would need to transform into Bellatrix before they left, and the less that Bill and Fleur knew or suspected about what they were about to do, the better.
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Hermione must change into Bellatrix before we leave. Bill and Fleur must not know what we’re up to.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: It was just possible to discern Ron under his disguise, but only, Harry thought, because he knew him so well.
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Ron’s disguise works enough that only I can pick him out. I know him that well.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: Gringotts had seemed a place of wonder that day, the enchanted repository of a trove of gold he had never known he possessed, and never for an instant could he have dreamed that he would return to steal.
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: I stood here as a kid and thought Gringotts was magical and safe. Now I’m back planning a break-in. That feels wrong and huge.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “Too polite,” Harry whispered in Hermione’s ear as they passed out of the inn into the tiny backyard. “You need to treat people like they’re scum!”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: We have to play Bellatrix properly. Politeness will blow the act. I want Hermione to be ruthless and nasty while we’re inside.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "He knows, and he’s going to check where the others are, and the last one is at Hogwarts."
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: He knows about our Horcruxes and he is going to check them. One of the Horcruxes is at Hogwarts.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "I saw him find out about the cup, I — I was in his head, he’s... he’s seriously angry, and scared too"
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: I was in his head when he found out about the cup. He is furious and terrified that we know.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "He thinks the Hogwarts one is safest, because Snape’s there, because it’ll be so hard not to be seen getting in, I think he’ll check that one last, but he could still be there within hours"
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: He believes the Hogwarts Horcrux is safest because Snape is at school. He might check the Hogwarts Horcrux last, but he could be there very soon.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "Can you imagine what he’s going to do once he realizes the ring and the locket are gone? What if he moves the Hogwarts Horcrux, decides it isn’t safe enough?"
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: If he notices the other Horcruxes are gone he could move the Hogwarts one or take other drastic steps. We need to act fast.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "We’ll go to Hogsmeade, and try to work something out once we see what the protection around the school’s like. Get under the Cloak, Hermione, I want to stick together this time."
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: We are going to Hogsmeade to check the school's protections and try to figure out how to get in. We will stick together under the Invisibility Cloak.

Book7-chapter29_Sc7.source: "He gave the wall a little push. It melted away at his touch and they slipped outside"
Book7-chapter29_Sc7.description: I pushed the wall and it just melted away under my hand. I can get through parts of the castle that way if I need to.

Book7-chapter29_Sc7.source: "Holding it close to his nose he searched, and located his and Luna’s dots at last. "We’re up on the fifth floor," he whispered"
Book7-chapter29_Sc7.description: The Marauder's Map shows me exactly where Luna and I are. We're on the fifth floor right now.

Book7-chapter29_Sc7.source: "Harry had prowled the castle at night many times before, but never had his heart hammered this fast, never had so much depended on his safe passage through the place."
Book7-chapter29_Sc7.description: I used to think sneaking around Hogwarts was routine, but this time it's different. My heart's racing and I know getting through safely actually matters.

Book7-chapter29_Sc7.source: "He expected to encounter an obstacle at any moment; his worst fear was Peeves"
Book7-chapter29_Sc7.description: If anything's going to ruin this, it's going to be Peeves. I'm on edge listening for him the whole time.
When we reached Ravenclaw Tower I half expected a password. Instead the door asks riddles and you have to answer to get in.

Book7-chapter29_Sc7.source: "Well reasoned," said the voice, and the door swung open."
Book7-chapter29_Sc7.description: The riddle-answering actually works. Give the right answer and the door opens.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: My face is a mess, it's all puffed up and I can barely see. I got stung.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Dudley," said Harry. "And your first name?" "I — Vernon. Vernon Dudley."
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: I lied my way through with a name. I said I was Vernon Dudley to try to get us out of trouble.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "He works at the Ministry," Harry lied. "Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes."
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: I made up that my dad works at the Ministry, Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes, hoping that might scare them off.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "It’s in the dungeons," said Harry clearly. "You enter through the wall. It’s full of skulls and stuff and it’s under the lake, so the light’s all green."
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: When they asked about Slytherin I blurted out something I thought they'd expect, the dungeons under the lake and all that, to sound convincing.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Ve-e-ry nice," said Greyback appreciatively, taking it from his companion. "Oh, very nice indeed. Looks goblin-made, that."
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: They found a sword that looks goblin-made. If they think it's important they might use it as leverage on us.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "’ermione Granger,'" Scabior was saying, "'the Mudblood who is known to be traveling with 'arry Potter.'"
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: They've seen Hermione's face in the Prophet and they think she's traveling with me. That could make things a lot worse for her.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Harry?" It was a new, but familiar, voice, and it came from directly behind Harry, from the person tied to Hermione’s left. "Dean?" "It is you!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: Dean was here too, tied up with us. We're not alone in this, which is something at least.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "As Scabior said it, Harry’s scar, which was stretched tight across his distended forehead, burned savagely."
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: My scar flared and I felt Voldemort's thoughts reach for me. I had to force myself to shut him out so I wouldn't lose control.

Book7-chapter32_Sc2.source: "You stay here and look after Hermione, and I’ll go and get it —” Harry cut across Ron. “You two stay here, I’ll go under the Cloak and I’ll be back as soon as I —”
Book7-chapter32_Sc2.description: I’m going to do it. I’ll go under the Cloak and be back as soon as I can. I’ll take the risk and get it myself.

Book7-chapter29_Sc5.source: Dumbledore left the three of us a job
Book7-chapter29_Sc5.description: Dumbledore left this to the three of us. I'm supposed to do this with Ron and Hermione and no one else.

Book7-chapter29_Sc5.source: We — we can't tell you. We've got to do it — alone.
Book7-chapter29_Sc5.description: We can't tell anyone about what we're doing. It has to be just the three of us. I can't risk more people getting involved.
My scar's burning again. It's a sign something's wrong and it's making it hard to think straight.

Book7-chapter29_Sc5.source: Everyone in here's proven they're loyal to Dumbledore — loyal to you.
Book7-chapter29_Sc5.description: They trust me and they're loyal to Dumbledore. I know they're ready to fight, but I can't put them in danger with what we have to do.
I keep saying they don't understand because I can't explain. I'm frustrated and desperate and I need them to accept that we must go on alone.

Book7-chapter29_Sc5.source: We got your message, Neville! Hello you three, I thought you must be here!
Book7-chapter29_Sc5.description: They came because of the message. People are willing to risk everything for me and for the cause, which makes this even harder.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: He's on his way right now. He's coming for me and fast.
He already knows where I am. That scar tells me when he's close.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "Professor, do you know where the diadem of Ravenclaw is?" "The d-diadem of Ravenclaw? Of course not — hasn't it been lost for centuries?"
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: There might be something hidden in the castle that could be the Ravenclaw diadem. I have to find it.
I'm acting on Dumbledore's orders. I have to trust that's what he would have wanted me to do.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "There’s a way," said Harry quickly, and he explained about the passageway leading into the Hog’s Head.
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: There's a passageway into the Hog's Head that can get students out. If Death Eaters are watching the boundaries, they won't check people disappearing from a pub.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "Have you seen Harry Potter, Minerva? Because if you have, I must insist —"
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: Snape was patrolling and was looking for me. He noticed something, he was ready to insist on finding me.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "He jumped," said Professor McGonagall ... "No, he’s not dead," said McGonagall bitterly. "Unlike Dumbledore, he was still carrying a wand . . . and he seems to have learned a few tricks from his master."
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: Snape escaped. He leapt from the window and isn't dead. He still has a wand and has picked up dangerous tricks.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "With a tingle of horror, Harry saw in the distance a huge, batlike shape flying through the darkness toward the perimeter wall."
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: Something huge and batlike is flying toward the perimeter wall. Voldemort's forces are arriving now.

Book7-chapter30_Sc2.source: "We shall secure the school against He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named while you search for this — this object."
Book7-chapter30_Sc2.description: McGonagall and the other teachers will try to hold him off while I search. I can't just run; I have to keep looking for Horcruxes.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [We’ve got to find it fast. We don’t have to tell them it’s a Horcrux.]
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: We have to find whatever it is quickly, and we do not have to tell everyone it's a Horcrux.
Okay. I am going to let Ron and Hermione in on this. I do not have to carry it all by myself.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [Dumbledore had warned him against telling anyone but Ron and Hermione about the Horcruxes. Secrets and lies, that’s how we grew up, and Albus . . . he was a natural. . . . Was he turning into Dumbledore, keeping his secrets clutched to his chest, afraid to trust? But Dumbledore had trusted Snape, and where had that led? To murder at the top of the highest tower . . .]
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: I used to think keeping things secret was right because Dumbledore did it, but I am worried about blind trust. I do not want to end up repeating his mistakes.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [There’s something we need to find. Something — something that’ll help us overthrow You-Know-Who. It’s here at Hogwarts, but we don’t know where. It might have belonged to Ravenclaw.]
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: There is an object hidden at Hogwarts that can help us beat You-Know-Who. It might be connected to Ravenclaw.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [And none of you have ever seen anything that looks like it?] They all shook their heads.
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: If no one has seen anything like it, a very old lost object like Ravenclaw's diadem seems unlikely to be the Horcrux we're after.

Book7-chapter30_Sc1.description: He spat at Professor McGonagall. I saw it happen and I knew I couldn't stand by while that went unpunished.
I used the Cruciatus Curse. It worked exactly like Bellatrix said it would when you actually mean it — it throws someone into real agony.

Book7-chapter30_Sc1.source: "I see what Bellatrix meant," said Harry, the blood thundering through his brain, "you need to really mean it."
Book7-chapter30_Sc1.description: I used to think some spells were just about words and wandwork. Now I know for certain that intent matters — a lot. You have to mean it, or it won't have the force you want.

Book7-chapter30_Sc1.source: "Why would Harry Potter try to get inside Ravenclaw Tower? Potter belongs in my House!"
Book7-chapter30_Sc1.description: I care about Professor McGonagall. Hearing her defend me like that made me feel proud and protective of her.
I spoke up and acted when someone crossed a line. I will step in and fight when people I respect are attacked.

Book7-chapter31_Sc1.description: She admits she stole the diadem from her mother. That means someone else could have taken it later but it definitely left Ravenclaw hands because she ran off with it.
The diadem was hidden in a hollow tree in a forest in Albania. Of course Voldemort could have come and taken it from there.

Book7-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He hid the diadem in the castle, the night he asked Dumbledore to let him teach!"
Book7-chapter31_Sc1.description: It makes sense he brought the diadem back to Hogwarts the night he applied for the job. So the Horcrux is likely hidden somewhere in the castle now.
I nearly forgot about the Horcrux in the chaos. I can't let that happen. Finding the diadem is urgent and I need to get on with it right now.
Hagrid turned up to join the fight. He shows up when it matters and I can count on him being here to help.

Book7-chapter28_Sc2.source: Let ’em have free rein, they’d find him quick enough!
Book7-chapter28_Sc2.description: They reckon the dementors would find me quick. I can't risk trying a Patronus because it would give me away.

Book7-chapter28_Sc2.source: The Dark Lord wants Potter’s life, not his soul. He’ll be easier to kill if he’s been Kissed first!
Book7-chapter28_Sc2.description: They think the Dark Lord wants my life, not my soul, and that a Kiss from a dementor would make me easier to kill.
We couldn't Disapparate. The Death Eaters' charms were stopping us from moving.

Book7-chapter28_Sc2.source: Light was sucked from the environment right up to the stars, which vanished.
Book7-chapter28_Sc2.description: The darkness and cold rolled in so fast the stars disappeared and the cold bit into me. It felt like everything was being drained away.

Book7-chapter32_Sc10.source: trying to see the single knot in the bark of the old tree that would paralyze it
Book7-chapter32_Sc10.description: If I can find and hit that single knot in the bark the Willow will be paralyzed. That's the target and that's what will stop it.

Book7-chapter32_Sc10.source: Panting and gasping, Harry slowed down, skirting the Willow’s swiping branches, peering through the darkness toward its thick trunk
Book7-chapter32_Sc10.description: I'm knackered and I'm having to be careful. I need to edge round those swiping branches and steady myself to get a clear shot at that knot.

Book7-chapter34_Sc1.source: Colin Creevey, though underage, must have sneaked back just as Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle had done. He was tiny in death.
Book7-chapter34_Sc1.description: Colin's dead. He must've sneaked back even though he's underage, just like Malfoy and his mates. He's so small in death it felt like a punch in the stomach.

Book7-chapter29_Sc4.source: He looked at Ron and Hermione, trying to tell them without words that Voldemort had just discovered the loss of one of the other Horcruxes. Time was running out fast
Book7-chapter29_Sc4.description: Voldemort knows one Horcrux is gone. If he comes to Hogwarts now we will miss our chance. We have to move, and we have to move fast.

Book7-chapter29_Sc4.source: There’s something we — Ron, Hermione, and I — need to do, and then we’ll get out of here
Book7-chapter29_Sc4.description: Dumbledore left me, Ron and Hermione a job. This is something only the three of us can do. We have to do it alone.

Book7-chapter29_Sc4.source: He rubbed his scar, trying to soothe the pain
Book7-chapter29_Sc4.description: My scar is burning and it still hurts. I need to keep control or I will lose it to whatever he is feeling.

Book7-chapter32_Sc8.description: Run! The giants are fighting and I need to get Hermione out of the way, so I grabbed her hand and dragged her down the steps. I'm not hanging about.

Book7-chapter32_Sc8.source: the night was full of hideous yells and blows as the giants wrestled
Book7-chapter32_Sc8.description: That's mental out there with all that noise and smashing. I know this is dangerous and loud and we have to move fast.
