Book7-chapter34_Sc3.source: People were moving around, trying to comfort each other, drinking, kneeling beside the dead
Book7-chapter34_Sc3.description: People are in shock all over the place. They're comforting each other, drinking, kneeling over the dead. It's chaos and grief.

Book7-chapter34_Sc3.source: he could not see any of the people he loved, no hint of Hermione, Ron, Ginny, or any of the other Weasleys, no Luna
Book7-chapter34_Sc3.description: I can't see Hermione, Ron, Ginny, any of the Weasleys, or Luna. They're not where I expect them to be and that terrifies me.

Book7-chapter34_Sc3.source: He felt he would have given all the time remaining to him for just one last look at them; but then, would he ever have the strength to stop looking? It was better like this.
Book7-chapter34_Sc3.description: I wanted one last look at them so badly I'd give everything for it, but if I kept looking I wouldn't be able to stop. It's better this way. I have to go without that goodbye.

Book7-chapter32_Sc5.source: [“LET’S GO!” Harry yelled, and he, Ron, and Hermione gathered the Cloak tightly around themselves and pelted, heads down, through the midst of the fighters...]
Book7-chapter32_Sc5.description: We have to move now, heads down, wrap the Cloak tight and get through the fight before we get caught.

Book7-chapter32_Sc5.source: [There came a great “Wheeeeeeeeeeee!” and, looking up, Harry saw Peeves zooming over them, dropping Snargaluff pods down onto the Death Eaters...]
Book7-chapter32_Sc5.description: Peeves will cause chaos for us, like dropping those Snargaluff pods to distract the Death Eaters.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named is coming," she told the other teachers.
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Voldemort is coming. We're not guessing it. He's on his way here.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "We need to put in place every protection of which we are capable while Potter does what he needs to do."
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wants me doing some job in the castle right now while everyone else bolsters protections. I'm supposed to stay and do it.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "You realize, of course, that nothing we do will be able to keep out You-Know-Who indefinitely?" squeaked Flitwick. "But we can hold him up," said Professor Sprout.
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: No matter what spells we throw up, we can only delay him. We can slow him down, not stop him forever.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "— Protego Horribilis — the diadem of Ravenclaw?" squeaked Flitwick. "Seen it? Nobody has seen it in living memory! Long since lost, boy!"
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: The Ravenclaw diadem? Nobody's seen it for ages. If that's the Horcrux, it's been lost for a very long time.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "Snape's run for it — What are you doing here? How did you know?"
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Snape has fled. He ran. That changes things for how we expect events to play out inside the castle.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "We sent messages to the rest of Dumbledore’s Army," Fred explained. "You couldn’t expect everyone to miss the fun, Harry, and the D.A. let the Order of the Phoenix know, and it all kind of snowballed."
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: The D.A. called the Order. People rallied. I can't believe how many of them showed up to stand and fight alongside us.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "I was a fool!" Percy roared... "I was an idiot, I was a pompous prat, I was a — a —" "Ministry-loving, family-disowning, power-hungry moron," said Fred.
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Percy finally came back to the family. He's ashamed and apologizing. He's not the same distance he used to be with Mum and Dad.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "You can’t do this. Everyone underage will have to leave, it’s only right."
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: The younger kids are being evacuated to the Great Hall. Underage witches and wizards will be sent away from the fighting.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "I can’t go home!" Ginny shouted... Her eyes met Harry’s for the first time. She looked at him beseechingly, but he shook his head and she turned away bitterly.
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Ginny wants to stay and fight. I shook my head. I can't let her stay in the middle of this even though she begged me. That hurt both of us.

Book7-chapter30_Sc3.source: "Where’s Ron?" asked Harry. "Where’s Hermione?" "They must have gone up to the Great Hall already," Mr. Weasley called over his shoulder. "They said something about a bathroom," said Ginny.
Book7-chapter30_Sc3.description: Ron and Hermione are not with me. They said something about a bathroom and might be in the castle somewhere. I need to find them when I can.

Book7-chapter34_Sc4.source: "It’s all part of the plan," said Harry. "There’s something I’ve got to do. Listen — Neville —"
Book7-chapter34_Sc4.description: This is part of the plan. I have something I have to do on my own and I might be out of sight for a while.

Book7-chapter34_Sc4.source: Harry had pulled off the Cloak: The idea had come to him out of nowhere, born out of a desire to make absolutely sure.
Book7-chapter34_Sc4.description: I took the Cloak off to make absolutely sure. I needed to check it for myself.

Book7-chapter34_Sc4.source: "Harry, you’re not thinking of handing yourself over?" "No," Harry lied easily.
Book7-chapter34_Sc4.description: I lied to Neville about handing myself over. I can't let him know everything right now.

Book7-chapter32_Sc9.description: I have to run. I can't stand here thinking about everyone I love; I need to get to the snake and Voldemort because that's the only way to stop this.

Book7-chapter32_Sc9.source: he ran so fast that they were halfway toward the forest before they were brought up short again
Book7-chapter32_Sc9.description: I'm moving faster than I've ever moved in my life because I won't let anything stop me from reaching that tree and whatever's at its roots.

Book7-chapter32_Sc9.source: Thoughts of Fred and Hagrid, and his terror for all the people he loved, scattered in and outside the castle, must all wait
Book7-chapter32_Sc9.description: I care about Fred and Hagrid and everyone back at the castle, but right now I have to put that aside and focus on ending this.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.source: "It was still hot, blackened with soot, but as he looked at it closely he was just able to make out the tiny words etched upon it: WIT BEYOND MEASURE IS MAN’S GREATEST TREASURE."
Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: This rotten thing was a Horcrux, the diadem. I grabbed it, it was scorched and leaking a tarry blood. It fell to bits in my hands.
That fire was Fiendfyre. Dangerous as anything, but it destroys Horcruxes. Crabbe's spell did what we needed even if he didn't mean to.
Crabbe is dead. I didn't want any of this, but Crabbe's recklessness killed him.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.source: "The Dark Lord wants him alive —" "So? I’m not killing him, am I?"
Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: Malfoy wanted me alive, but that did not stop his mates trying to kill us. I can't trust that his position means he'll protect me.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.source: "The diadem seemed to fall in slow motion, turning and glittering as it dropped toward the maw of a yawning serpent, and then he had it, caught it around his wrist"
Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: I can still move under pressure. I caught the diadem even as that cursed fire was trying to eat us.

Book7-chapter34_Sc7.source: "We’re all going to keep fighting, Harry. You know that?"
Book7-chapter34_Sc7.description: They're not giving up. Neville grabbed my wrist and made it clear everyone will keep fighting whether I want them to or not.

Book7-chapter34_Sc7.source: "You’ve been so brave." "You are nearly there," said James. "Very close. We are . . . so proud of you."
Book7-chapter34_Sc7.description: People I love are proud of me. James and Neville think I'm nearly there and brave, and that matters more than I can say.

Book7-chapter34_Sc7.source: "Dying? Not at all," said Sirius. "Quicker and easier than falling asleep."
Book7-chapter34_Sc7.description: Sirius says dying does not hurt and that it is quick and easy. That is what they want me to know so I don't panic.

Book7-chapter34_Sc7.source: "And he will want it to be quick."
Book7-chapter34_Sc7.description: They think I will want it to be quick. I can almost believe that now because they make it sound bearable.
I tried to move on but Neville stopped me. I said thank you and I couldn't finish what I was going to say, which shows how stuck I am in this moment.

Book7-chapter32_Sc6.description: HAGRID, come back, I can't just leave him out there with those spiders.

Book7-chapter32_Sc6.source: he saw it happen: Hagrid vanished amongst the spiders, and with a great scurrying, a foul swarming movement, they retreated under the onslaught of spells, Hagrid buried in their midst.
Book7-chapter32_Sc6.description: Hagrid got swallowed up by the spiders in the grounds, buried in the middle of them even as the spells drove the swarm off.

Book7-chapter32_Sc6.source: He thought he could make out an enormous arm waving from the midst of the spider swarm, but as he made to chase after them, his way was impeded by a monumental foot, which swung down out of the darkness and made the ground on which he stood shudder.
Book7-chapter32_Sc6.description: Something huge stepped out of the darkness and smashed the ground, blocking me from reaching Hagrid.

Book7-chapter32_Sc7.source: glass rained down upon Harry, forcing him back under the shelter of the doorway.
Book7-chapter32_Sc7.description: Glass smashed down and I had to dive back into the doorway. I need to stay under cover.

Book7-chapter32_Sc7.source: the gargantuan monster trying to crush people on the upper floors looked around and let out a roar.
Book7-chapter32_Sc7.description: There is a huge giant smashing at the castle and roaring. This is dangerous and I have to help people get to safety.

Book7-chapter32_Sc7.source: only now did Harry realize that Grawp was, indeed, an undersized giant.
Book7-chapter32_Sc7.description: Grawp is an undersized giant. He is a giant, but smaller than the others.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "I know what the diadem looks like, and I know where it is," said Harry, talking fast.
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: I know what the Ravenclaw diadem looks like and where Voldemort hid it. He put it where I'd hidden my old Potions book. Of course he thought he was the only one who knew.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "He hid it exactly where I hid my old Potions book, where everyone’s been hiding stuff for centuries. He thought he was the only one to find it."
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: He hid the Horcrux in a place people have always used to hide things. That means anyone could get in, not just him.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "Tom Riddle, who confided in no one and operated alone, might have been arrogant enough to assume that he, and only he, had penetrated the deepest mysteries of Hogwarts Castle."
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: Tom Riddle was arrogant. He assumed he was the only one clever enough to find certain secrets. That's a mistake he made.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "It wouldn’t stop Voldemort," said Harry, "and your brother would never have done it."
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: I still trust Dumbledore's choices. I don't think he would have kept Slytherins hostage even if it might have helped.

Book7-chapter32_Sc12.source: Voldemort wanted him to do this, wanted him to come
Book7-chapter32_Sc12.description: He wants me to go where he wants me. I can't let him lead us into something just because he wants me there.

Book7-chapter32_Sc12.source: The only way forward was to kill the snake, and the snake was where Voldemort was, and Voldemort was at the end of this tunnel
Book7-chapter32_Sc12.description: The way on is straight through that snake. It's where Voldemort is, and Voldemort is at the end of the tunnel. Kill the snake, get to him. That's it. No other choice.

Book7-chapter32_Sc12.source: “Harry, we’re coming, just get in there!” said Ron, pushing him forward.
Book7-chapter32_Sc12.description: Ron and Hermione are with me. They're backing me up. I can't duck out on them when they're risking themselves for me.

Book7-chapter34_Sc6.source: "Dumbledore had died knowing that three people still knew about the Horcruxes; now Neville would take Harry’s place: There would still be three in the secret."
Book7-chapter34_Sc6.description: Three people will always know about the Horcruxes. Neville's taking my place so the secret stays safe. That's the plan.

Book7-chapter34_Sc6.source: "Just in case they’re — busy — and you get the chance —" "Kill the snake?" "Kill the snake," Harry repeated.
Book7-chapter34_Sc6.description: If I get the chance and they're tied up, I have to kill the snake. Kill the snake. Plain and simple.

Book7-chapter34_Sc6.source: "This was crucial, he must be like Dumbledore, keep a cool head, make sure there were backups, others to carry on."
Book7-chapter34_Sc6.description: I have to keep a cool head like Dumbledore and make sure there are backups. We can't rely on just one person.

Book7-chapter36_Sc3.source: "I don't want anyone else to try to help," Harry said loudly, and in the total silence his voice carried like a trumpet call. "It's got to be like this. It's got to be me."
Book7-chapter36_Sc3.description: I can't let anyone else risk themselves. It has to be me standing here and finishing this.

Book7-chapter36_Sc3.source: "There are no more Horcruxes. It's just you and me. Neither can live while the other survives, and one of us is about to leave for good."
Book7-chapter36_Sc3.description: There are no Horcruxes left. It's just him and me and one of us has to go for the other to stop existing.

Book7-chapter36_Sc3.source: "Accident, was it, when my mother died to save me?"
Book7-chapter36_Sc3.description: My mother's sacrifice wasn't an accident. Her protection matters and it ties me to the people I'm trying to protect.

Book7-chapter36_Sc3.source: "You won't be killing anyone else tonight," said Harry as they circled, and stared into each other's eyes, green into red. "You won't be able to kill any of them ever again. Don't you get it? I was ready to die to stop you from hurting these people —"
Book7-chapter36_Sc3.description: I was ready to die to stop him and that decision put a real shield around the people here. He can't hurt them now.

Book7-chapter36_Sc6.source: "Severus Snape was never the true master of the Elder Wand. He never defeated Dumbledore."
Book7-chapter36_Sc6.description: Snape was never the wand's master. He did not win it from Dumbledore.

Book7-chapter36_Sc6.source: "Dumbledore’s death was planned between them! Dumbledore intended to die undefeated, the wand’s last true master! If all had gone as planned, the wand’s power would have died with him, because it had never been won from him!"
Book7-chapter36_Sc6.description: Dumbledore planned his own death so the Elder Wand would die with him and stay undefeated.

Book7-chapter36_Sc6.source: "Possessing the wand isn’t enough! Holding it, using it, doesn’t make it really yours. Didn’t you listen to Ollivander? The wand chooses the wizard."
Book7-chapter36_Sc6.description: Having the wand in your hand does not make it truly yours. The wand has to choose you.

Book7-chapter34_Sc8.description: He wants it over. That means whatever is about to happen, it's what he wants and we can't talk him out of it.

Book7-chapter34_Sc8.source: "I didn’t want you to die," Harry said. "Any of you. I’m sorry —"
Book7-chapter34_Sc8.description: I didn't want any of them to die. I feel guilty and I have to say I'm sorry, even if it doesn't change anything.

Book7-chapter34_Sc8.source: "— right after you’d had your son . . . Remus, I’m sorry —"
Book7-chapter34_Sc8.description: Remus, I'm sorry. I can't stop thinking about you losing your son and I feel closer to you and more desperate to make things right.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: I let him kill me and the bit of his soul that was inside me got destroyed. My soul is whole and completely my own now.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.source: "He took your blood and rebuilt his living body with it! Your blood in his veins, Harry, Lily's protection inside both of you! He tethered you to life while he lives!"
Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: Voldemort used my blood to rebuild himself. My blood in his veins kept me tied to life while he lived.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.source: "Something that is beyond either of our help," said Dumbledore, referring to the maimed creature.
Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: That broken thing under the chair is beyond our help. It is left to whatever it is now and I can't fix it.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.source: "It was a Cloak the likes of which I had never seen, immensely old, perfect in every respect . . . and then your father died, and I had two Hallows at last, all to myself!"
Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: Dumbledore had the Cloak the night my parents died. He told me he took the chance to have two Hallows to himself after my father died.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.source: "You know what happened. You know. You cannot despise me more than I despise myself."
Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: Dumbledore admitted he resented his family and chased glory. He feels awful about what he did and thinks I should despise him. I don't despise him, but I do know he made terrible choices.

Book7-chapter35_Sc1.source: "He wanted to come to Godric's Hollow, as I am sure you have guessed, because of the grave of Ignotus Peverell."
Book7-chapter35_Sc1.description: Grindelwald wanted Godric's Hollow because of Ignotus Peverell's grave and the Hallows. That helped explain why they were both obsessed with the same things.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "I won the duel. I won the wand."
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: I beat Grindelwald and took the wand. Plain and simple. That duel happened and the wand is mine.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "You tried to use the Resurrection Stone."
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: Dumbledore actually put the Resurrection Stone on. He wanted to see Ariana and our parents again. He told me he picked it up and put it on.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "You are the true master of death, because the true master does not seek to run away from Death."
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: If what Dumbledore says is right, being the master of death isn't about cheating death. It's about accepting it. That makes me the kind of person who can walk into what's coming without trying to run from it.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "I admit that was my intention," said Dumbledore, "but it did not work as I intended, did it?"
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: Dumbledore planned his death with Snape and meant for Snape to end up with the Elder Wand. He wanted things arranged. That changes how I see what was planned around me.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "We are in King’s Cross, you say? I think that if you decided not to go back, you would be able to . . . let’s say . . . board a train."
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: I was offered a choice to stay away instead of going back. I could take a train and not return to the fight. The choice was actually mine.

Book7-chapter35_Sc3.source: "He believes that the Elder Wand removes his last weakness and makes him truly invincible."
Book7-chapter35_Sc3.description: Voldemort is obsessed with the Elder Wand. He thinks it will make him invincible, so he will go after it and most likely won't care about the other Hallows.

Book7-chapter34_Sc9.description: You said you'll stay with me. I'm not letting you go anywhere. I want you there with me until it's over.

Book7-chapter34_Sc9.source: "We are part of you," said Sirius.
Book7-chapter34_Sc9.description: They're part of me and no one else can see them. That means I won't be alone in front of him.

Book7-chapter34_Sc9.source: "Stay close to me," he said quietly.
Book7-chapter34_Sc9.description: I'm the one who has to choose this. No one will tell me to go. If I'm doing this, it's my decision and I'm staying close to them.

Book7-chapter36_Sc7.source: "The true master of the Elder Wand was Draco Malfoy."
Book7-chapter36_Sc7.description: Draco was the wand's master at some point. What? Draco? That is mental.

Book7-chapter36_Sc7.source: "But you’re too late," said Harry. "You’ve missed your chance. I got there first. I overpowered Draco weeks ago. I took this wand from him."
Book7-chapter36_Sc7.description: I disarmed Draco and grabbed his wand. If the Elder Wand cares who disarmed its last owner, then it's mine. So yeah, I might actually be the true master.

Book7-chapter36_Sc7.source: "You no longer have the phoenix wand: We duel on skill alone . . . and after I have killed you, I can attend to Draco Malfoy."
Book7-chapter36_Sc7.description: Voldemort knows I don't have the phoenix wand anymore and thinks that means it comes down to our skill. Fine. Bring it on.

Book7-chapter36_Sc7.source: "Tears were sliding down from behind the half-moon spectacles into the long silver beard, and the pride and the gratitude emanating from him filled Harry with the same balm as phoenix song."
Book7-chapter36_Sc7.description: Seeing Dumbledore in that portrait, proud and grateful, it hit me right in the chest. His pride steadies me. I felt better, like I could actually do this.

Book7-chapter36_Sc4.source: “I know things you don’t know, Tom Riddle. I know lots of important things that you don’t. Want to hear some, before you make another big mistake?”
Book7-chapter36_Sc4.description: I actually know things he doesn't. I can use knowledge against him and I won't be cowed by his threats.

Book7-chapter36_Sc4.source: “Yes, Dumbledore’s dead,” said Harry calmly, “but you didn’t have him killed. He chose his own manner of dying, chose it months before he died, arranged the whole thing with the man you thought was your servant.”
Book7-chapter36_Sc4.description: Dumbledore chose how and when to die. Voldemort didn't kill him.

Book7-chapter36_Sc4.source: “Snape’s Patronus was a doe,” said Harry, “the same as my mother’s, because he loved her for nearly all of his life, from the time when they were children.”
Book7-chapter36_Sc4.description: Snape's Patronus matched my mother's because he loved Lily. That explains everything about his actions.

Book7-chapter36_Sc4.source: “Snape was Dumbledore’s, said Harry. “Snape was Dumbledore’s from the moment you started hunting down my mother.”
Book7-chapter36_Sc4.description: Snape was working for Dumbledore, not for Voldemort. He was Dumbledore's spy the whole time.

Book7-chapter36_Sc2.source: The enormous hands that lifted him into the air were exceedingly gentle. Harry could feel Hagrid’s arms trembling with the force of his heaving sobs; great tears splashed down upon him as Hagrid cradled Harry in his arms
Book7-chapter36_Sc2.description: Hagrid loves me more than anyone. He was shaking and crying while he held me like I was the most important thing in the world.

Book7-chapter36_Sc2.source: he kept himself floppy and lifeless, and when he fell to the ground for the last time, the clearing echoed with jeers and shrieks of laughter
Book7-chapter36_Sc2.description: I can make myself look dead if I have to. I stayed totally limp and quiet so they actually believed it.

Book7-chapter36_Sc2.source: nobody looked to see whether a pulse beat in the exposed neck of Harry Potter
Book7-chapter36_Sc2.description: They were too busy gloating to check if I was alive. No one bothered to see if I had a pulse.

Book7-chapter36_Sc2.source: “You carry him,” Voldemort said. “He will be nice and visible in your arms, will he not? Pick up your little friend, Hagrid. And the glasses — put on the glasses — he must be recognizable —”
Book7-chapter36_Sc2.description: Voldemort uses Hagrid to humiliate me. I can see how cruel they are by making Hagrid parade me like a prize.

Book7-chapter36_Sc2.source: “Protego!” roared Harry, and the Shield Charm expanded in the middle of the Hall, and Voldemort stared around for the source as Harry pulled off the Invisibility Cloak at last
Book7-chapter36_Sc2.description: I can break cover when I need to. I took off the cloak and threw up a Shield Charm to stop them and catch them off guard.

Book7-chapter34_Sc10.source: I thought he would come. I expected him to come.
Book7-chapter34_Sc10.description: He expected me to come. He thought I'd show up when he wanted me to.

Book7-chapter34_Sc10.source: I was, it seems mistaken. You weren't.
Book7-chapter34_Sc10.description: He's admitting he was wrong and saying I'm not. My heart's hammering, I'm terrified, and I don't want to fight — I even pulled off the Invisibility Cloak and hid my wand so I wouldn't be tempted.

Book7-chapter36_Sc1.source: "He is dead!" Narcissa Malfoy called to the watchers.
Book7-chapter36_Sc1.description: She's willing to say Draco is dead just so they'll let her into Hogwarts to look for him.

Book7-chapter36_Sc1.source: She no longer cared whether Voldemort won.
Book7-chapter36_Sc1.description: She cares more about finding her son than about Voldemort's victory. Family comes first for her, even if it means siding with the victors.
I expected them to humiliate me with Cruciatus and I braced for the pain, but when they lifted me the agony I thought would come never did.

Book7-chapter36_Sc5.source: "I killed Severus Snape three hours ago, and the Elder Wand, the Deathstick, the Wand of Destiny is truly mine!"
Book7-chapter36_Sc5.description: So he killed Snape thinking that made him the true master of the Elder Wand.

Book7-chapter36_Sc5.source: "Yes, I dare," said Harry, "because Dumbledore's last plan hasn't backfired on me at all. It's backfired on you, Riddle."
Book7-chapter36_Sc5.description: Dumbledore's plan didn't fail me. It blew up in Voldemort's face. He's the one who's screwed up, not me.

Book7-chapter36_Sc5.source: "Voldemort's hand was trembling on the Elder Wand, and Harry gripped Draco's very tightly."
Book7-chapter36_Sc5.description: I grabbed Draco's hand and held on. I'm protecting him in that moment and keeping him close while Voldemort is losing his nerve.

Book7-chapter36_Sc5.source: "What is this?" Of all the things that Harry had said to him, beyond any revelation or taunt, nothing had shocked Voldemort like this.
Book7-chapter36_Sc5.description: Calling him to try for remorse actually shook him. Asking him to be a man hit him harder than anything else I said.

Book7-chapter35_Sc2.source: “Grindelwald. You cannot imagine how his ideas caught me, Harry, inflamed me.”
Book7-chapter35_Sc2.description: He told me he fell in with Grindelwald and got swept up in his plans for wizards to rule and Muggles to be subservient. He admitted he helped the schemes and was fascinated by the Hallows.

Book7-chapter35_Sc2.source: “And Ariana . . . after all my mother’s care and caution . . . lay dead upon the floor.”
Book7-chapter35_Sc2.description: He said Ariana ended up dead during that argument, and he was left with guilt and grief over what happened.

Book7-chapter35_Sc2.source: “I had learned that I was not to be trusted with power.”
Book7-chapter35_Sc2.description: He told me he refused the Ministry because he knows power is his weakness and he can't trust himself with it.

Book7-chapter35_Sc2.source: Harry reached out and was glad to find that he could touch him: He gripped his arm tightly and Dumbledore gradually regained control.
Book7-chapter35_Sc2.description: I reached out, gripped his arm, and actually calmed him down. I can comfort him when he's breaking down.

Book7-chapter35_Sc2.source: “But you’d have been better, much better, than Fudge or Scrimgeour!”
Book7-chapter35_Sc2.description: I still think he'd have been a far better Minister than those fools. He might doubt himself but I believe he'd have done a better job.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: "The thing that was hidden in the Snitch, I dropped it in the forest. I don’t know exactly where, but I’m not going to go looking for it again. Do you agree?"
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: I dropped the thing from the Snitch in the forest and I am not going back to hunt it down.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: "I’m going to keep Ignotus’s present, though," said Harry, and Dumbledore beamed.
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: I'm keeping Ignotus's gift. It's mine to keep until I choose to pass it on.
I don't want the Elder Wand. I know it's powerful but I'd rather have my old wand and be done with all that power.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: He laid the broken wand upon the headmaster’s desk, touched it with the very tip of the Elder Wand, and said, "Reparo."
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: I fixed my broken holly and phoenix feather wand by touching it with the Elder Wand and saying Reparo. It actually worked and it felt right in my hand again.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: "I’m putting the Elder Wand back where it came from. It can stay there."
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: I'm going to return the Elder Wand to where it belongs and leave it there. No more fighting over it.

Book7-chapter36_Sc9.source: "If I die a natural death like Ignotus, its power will be broken, won’t it? The previous master will never have been defeated. That’ll be the end of it."
Book7-chapter36_Sc9.description: If I die a natural death like Ignotus, the Elder Wand's power will be broken. The chain of masters ends there and that's the point.

Book7-chapter36_Sc9.source: "It won’t be long, and you’ll be going too,"
Book7-chapter36_Sc9.description: Don't worry, Lily, you'll be at Hogwarts before you know it. I'm telling you that like a fact, you'll love it when you're there.
James is a show off and he winds people up for a laugh. Take what he says with a pinch of salt.

Book1-chapter8_Sc3.source: At this, Hermione stood up, her hand stretching toward the dungeon ceiling.
Book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: Well, of course I knew the answer about monkshood and wolfsbane because I was eager enough to stand up and reach for it.

Book1-chapter8_Sc3.source: Snape was still ignoring Hermione’s quivering hand. "Sit down," he snapped at Hermione.
Book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: Obviously Snape was treating me unfairly by ignoring my hand and ordering me to sit down when I tried to help.

Book1-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Let’s try again. Potter, where would you look if I told you to find me a bezoar?"
Book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: Well, let's try this again. Of course I'm going to test him — where would he look if I told him to find a bezoar?

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Granger, Hermione!" Hermione almost ran to the stool and jammed the hat eagerly on her head. "GRYFFINDOR!" shouted the hat.]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Well, of course I went straight up and shoved the hat on. I wanted to be sorted and the hat put me into Gryffindor right away.
Obviously Ron groaned when I got Gryffindor. Typical. It mattered to him, even if he tried not to show it.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.source: "I do hope they start right away, there’s so much to learn, I’m particularly interested in Transfiguration, you know, turning something into something else, of course, it’s supposed to be very difficult —"
Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: Well, of course I want lessons to start straight away. There’s loads to learn and Transfiguration is proper fascinating. I’m determined to get on with it even if it’s difficult.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.source: "You’ll be starting small, just matches into needles and that sort of thing —"
Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: Obviously teachers will start us small. I’m expecting careful, step by step lessons so I can actually learn things properly.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "This was something you couldn’t learn by heart out of a book — not that she hadn’t tried."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Well, of course I tried to learn flying from a book, but you cannot learn how to fly properly from pages alone.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "At breakfast on Thursday she bored them all stupid with flying tips she’d gotten out of a library book called Quidditch Through the Ages."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Obviously I told everyone every useful tip I could find in Quidditch Through the Ages. I wanted to help, even if they found it dull.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Neville was hanging on to her every word, desperate for anything that might help him hang on to his broomstick later,"
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Of course Neville was desperate for help. I felt responsible to give him every bit of guidance he could use to hold on to a broom.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Hermione Granger’s had simply rolled over on the ground, and Neville’s hadn’t moved at all."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, of course my broom didn't leap into my hand. Mine rolled over on the ground, which is ridiculous if you ask me.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Stick out your right hand over your broom," called Madam Hooch at the front, "and say ‘Up!’"
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Obviously the proper words and technique matter for making a broom behave. You cannot just expect it to work without doing it correctly.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "I couldn’t help overhearing what you and Malfoy were saying — and you mustn’t go wandering around the school at night, think of the points you’ll lose Gryffindor if you’re caught, and you’re bound to be. It’s really very selfish of you."
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: Well, of course I'm not letting you sneak around at night. It's selfish and reckless and you'll lose house points if you get caught.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: Hermione had turned to the portrait of the Fat Lady to get back inside and found herself facing an empty painting. The Fat Lady had gone on a nighttime visit and Hermione was locked out of Gryffindor Tower.
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: Now the Fat Lady's painting's empty and I'm locked out of the common room. What am I supposed to do now?

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "I’m coming with you," "If he finds all three of us I’ll tell him the truth, that I was trying to stop you, and you can back me up."
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I'm not staying out here alone. I'll come with you, and if Filch catches us all I'll say I was trying to stop you and you can back me up.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "Can't a person eat in peace in this place?"
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: Obviously I won't be allowed to eat in peace around here without someone causing trouble.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: I’ve learned all our course books by heart, of course
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Of course I have learned the course books by heart. I always prepare properly.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: I’m Hermione Granger, by the way, who are you?
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I introduce myself straight away and expect people to give their names as well. It's only polite.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Do either of you know what House you’ll be in? I’ve been asking around, and I hope I’m in Gryffindor, it sounds by far the best
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Houses matter. I hope I get into Gryffindor because it seems the best, though Ravenclaw would be all right too.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: I got a few extra books for background reading, and you’re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I read ahead. I find out everything I can about new people and classes. That is practical and useful.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Anyway, we’d better go and look for Neville’s toad. You two had better change, you know, I expect we’ll be there soon.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I boss people a bit because someone needs to get organised. I will help look for Neville's toad and push things along.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: "No!" shouted Hermione Granger. "Madam Hooch told us not to move — you’ll get us all into trouble."
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: Well, of course, Madam Hooch said not to move. If you break the rules we'll all get into trouble, Harry.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: "No!" shouted Hermione Granger. "Madam Hooch told us not to move — you’ll get us all into trouble."
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: Obviously I don't want anyone risking expulsion, but I can't stop worrying when Harry does reckless things.

Book1-chapter9_Sc7.source: "You don’t use your eyes, any of you, do you?" she snapped. "Didn’t you see what it was standing on?" "No, not the floor. It was standing on a trapdoor. It’s obviously guarding something."
Book1-chapter9_Sc7.description: Well, of course it was standing on a trapdoor. Obviously it's guarding something.

Book1-chapter9_Sc7.source: "I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled. Now, if you don’t mind, I’m going to bed."
Book1-chapter9_Sc7.description: Of course I'm furious — we could have been killed or, worse, expelled. I'm done; I'm going to bed.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Now what am I going to do?" she asked shrilly.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: What am I supposed to do now? I'm locked out and I can't just stand around while Gryffindor Tower is inaccessible.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "I’m coming with you," she said. "You are not."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: Of course I want to come. I can't just leave you lot to get into trouble on your own, even if you tell me I can't.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "If he finds all three of us I’ll tell him the truth, that I was trying to stop you, and you can back me up."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: If Filch catches us all, I'll say I was trying to stop you. I expect you to back me up if it comes to that.

Book1-chapter10_Sc5.source: Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint.
Book1-chapter10_Sc5.description: Well, I was terrified and pinned to the wall. Of course I looked like I might faint with that troll coming at me.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Hermione marched away with her nose in the air."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, of course I marched away with my nose in the air. Some things just need a proper reaction when people start making a scene about brooms.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: “You’re saying it wrong,” Harry heard Hermione snap. “It’s Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa, make the ‘gar’ nice and long.”
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, of course you say it properly: Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa. Make the gar nice and long.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: Hermione rolled up the sleeves of her gown, flicked her wand, and said, “Wingardium Leviosa!” Their feather rose off the desk and hovered about four feet above their heads.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Obviously I can do the levitation charm right. I can make the feather float perfectly.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: It was Hermione. Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears. “I think she heard you.”
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, I'm upset and I don't have anyone with me right now. Leave me alone, I need to be by myself.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: Is it dead? Of course I asked that straight away. I need to know if the danger is over.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.source: Hermione had sunk to the floor in fright
Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: I can be terrified, even when I normally try to be sensible. Fear can make anyone collapse, even me.

Book1-chapter11_Sc1.source: "No — he wouldn't," she said. "I know he's not very nice, but he wouldn't try and steal something Dumbledore was keeping safe."
Book1-chapter11_Sc1.description: Of course he can be horrible, but he wouldn't try to steal something Dumbledore was protecting. I don't believe he'd do that.

Book1-chapter11_Sc1.source: "You've got to eat some breakfast." "Just a bit of toast," wheedled Hermione.
Book1-chapter11_Sc1.description: You've got to eat something. Just a bit of toast, come on.

Book1-chapter11_Sc11.source: He was being made a cup of strong tea back in Hagrid’s hut, with Ron and Hermione.
Book1-chapter11_Sc11.description: Well, of course I'm staying with Harry and Ron in Hagrid's after that. We're making him tea and looking after him because he needs it.

Book1-chapter11_Sc9.source: "He’s doing something — jinxing the broom," said Hermione. "What should we do?" "Leave it to me."
Book1-chapter11_Sc9.description: Well, he's jinxing the broom. What should we do? Leave it to me, of course — I'm going to go stop him.

Book1-chapter11_Sc12.source: “So why did he just try and kill Harry?”
Book1-chapter11_Sc12.description: Of course Snape could be responsible. He looked like he was trying to harm Harry, and I don’t think that’s coincidence.

Book1-chapter11_Sc12.source: “I know a jinx when I see one, Hagrid, I’ve read all about them! You’ve got to keep eye contact, and Snape wasn’t blinking at all, I saw him!”
Book1-chapter11_Sc12.description: I know how a jinx works. You have to keep eye contact and Snape wasn’t blinking, so I’m sure something magical was done to Harry’s broom.

Book1-chapter13_Sc2.source: “Go to Professor McGonagall!” Hermione urged Neville. “Report him!”
Book1-chapter13_Sc2.description: Of course we have to tell Professor McGonagall. Report Malfoy now. It’s the sensible thing to do and we can’t let him keep getting away with this.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "We just want to know who Nicolas Flamel is, that’s all," said Hermione. "Unless you’d like to tell us and save us the trouble?"
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: Well, of course I want to know who Nicolas Flamel is. We're asking questions and we expect answers, or we'll find them ourselves.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Nicolas Flamel," she whispered dramatically, "is the only known maker of the Sorcerer’s Stone!"
Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: Of course, Nicolas Flamel is the only known maker of the Sorcerer's Stone. Obviously everyone should know that.

Book1-chapter11_Sc8.description: Of course! I knew something was wrong. Snape's watching Harry and I knew it meant trouble.
Well, leave it to me. I'll sort this out or at least try to figure out what's happening with that broom.

Book1-chapter11_Sc8.source: Before Ron could say another word, Hermione had disappeared.
Book1-chapter11_Sc8.description: Obviously I had to act fast, so I grabbed the binoculars and went to see what's going on. I couldn't just stand there.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: There's still Fluffy guarding something important. We can't ignore that.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Go to Dumbledore. That's what we should have done ages ago. If we try anything ourselves we'll be thrown out for sure."
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, of course we should go to Dumbledore. Trying anything ourselves will get us expelled. That's obvious.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "That's what we should have done ages ago."
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: I trust Dumbledore to sort this properly. He's the person we should be turning to, not sneaking around.

Book1-chapter13_Sc4.description: Harry, where have you been? Everyone's been waiting for you in the common room.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “Hagrid, you live in a wooden house,” she said.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Well, keeping a dragon egg in a wooden hut is obviously dangerous and not sensible at all.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “Got this outta the library — Dragon Breeding for Pleasure and Profit — it’s a bit outta date, o’ course, but it’s all in here.”
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Of course he took a library book on dragons. He means well but reading dusty rules does not make hiding an illegal dragon safe.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: Hermione had now started making study schedules for Harry and Ron, too.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I have to keep them focused. Making study schedules for Harry and Ron shows I am taking charge of our schoolwork even if it drives them mad.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: Well, of course I think you shouldn't play if there's something dodgy going on. It's obvious you should avoid it.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: ["Say you're ill," said Ron. "Pretend to break your leg," Hermione suggested. "Really break your leg," said Ron.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: Obviously I suggested you fake an injury so you wouldn't have to play, because that would stop you being forced into something dangerous.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: [Everyone fell over laughing except Hermione, who leapt up and performed the countercurse. Neville’s legs sprang apart and he got to his feet, trembling.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: I can perform the countercurse that undoes the Leg Locker Curse. I did it straight away to help Neville and get his legs moving again.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: ["Go to Professor McGonagall! Report him!" Hermione urged Neville.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: Of course Neville should report Malfoy to McGonagall. Reporting bad behaviour is the sensible thing to do.

Book1-chapter15_Sc2.source: "They're here to be punished, after all"
Book1-chapter15_Sc2.description: Well, of course we're being punished and Filch is only glad about it; this isn't about fairness, it's about discipline.

Book1-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I bin waitin' fer half an hour already" and "I'll take over from here"
Book1-chapter15_Sc2.description: Hagrid has turned up to take charge, so he'll be the one leading whatever we're meant to do in the forest, not Filch.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: Do you think it had anything to do with the Stone?
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Well, it’s obvious to me that Hagrid was hiding something and it could be connected to the Stone. I want to work it out logically.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: We only wondered who had done the guarding, really.
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Of course I wanted to know which teachers Dumbledore trusted to help guard the Stone. That list matters.
Professor Snape’s name came up when Hagrid was naming the people involved. So Snape has some part to play in the protections.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Snape came out and asked me what I was doing, so I said I was waiting for Flitwick, and Snape went to get him, and I've only just got away, I don't know where Snape went."
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: Snape saw me and went to fetch Flitwick. I had to escape and I don't know where Snape went after that.
I feel guilty for not being able to follow Snape and for failing the plan, but I'm scared of the consequences.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Harry! Harry, are you all right?" Hermione was running toward them down the path, Hagrid puffing along behind her.
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: Well, of course I rushed over the moment I saw Harry wasn't with the others. I was desperate to know he was okay and shoved everything else to the side.

Book1-chapter15_Sc5.description: Well, I was stunned. Seeing a centaur, part man part horse, was completely shocking and upsetting and I was frozen for a moment.

Book1-chapter15_Sc6.source: Are there many of them in here? asked Hermione.
Book1-chapter15_Sc6.description: Well, are there many of them in here? Of course I wanted to know if there were more of them around.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Of course I want to see Dumbledore. This is important and we have to tell him straight away.
I am trying to be careful about what I say out loud because this is serious and needs discretion.
Dumbledore is away and is not coming back until tomorrow. We cannot see him tonight.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "It’ll all be over at midnight on Saturday," said Hermione,
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Well, of course, midnight on Saturday is when it will be done. That’s the plan and it should finish the problem.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "They showed Harry and Hermione the harness they’d rigged up, so they could suspend Norbert between them."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Obviously the harness works. They’ve rigged something that will hold Norbert so he can be carried away safely.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Chuckling about Malfoy, they waited, Norbert thrashing about in his crate."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Of course I was relieved once Norbert was going. Seeing him off made everything feel lighter.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "As they stepped into the corridor, Filch’s face loomed suddenly out of the darkness."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Well, we were discovered as we came back down the stairs. Filch is there and that means trouble.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "You're right, Harry," said Hermione in a small voice.
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: You're right, Harry. Of course I agree with you and I'm with you on this.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "How do you think you’d get to the Stone without us? I’d better go and look through my books, there might be something useful. . . ."
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: How do you think you'd get to the Stone without us? I need to check my books, there might be something useful and I'm going to find it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "But if we get caught, you two will be expelled, too."
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: If we get caught they're in as much trouble as I am. I can't risk them being expelled but I also won't let Harry go alone.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Neville," she said, "I'm really, really sorry about this." She raised her wand. "Petrificus Totalus!"
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: I'm really, really sorry about this, Neville. I have to petrify him to keep him out of danger.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: Harry! "Oh, Harry, we were sure you were going to -- Dumbledore was so worried --"
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: Oh, Harry, I was terrified for you. We were sure you were going to be hurt. Of course I rushed to see you.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: if he did -- I mean to say -- that's terrible -- you could have been killed.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: If Dumbledore really meant for Harry to go after Voldemort, that's awful. You could have died. Well, that's just not acceptable.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: when Harry told them what was under Quirrell's turban, Hermione screamed out loud.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: Seeing the truth about Quirrell and Voldemort under that turban was horrifying. Of course I reacted strongly.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: We must be miles under the school
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, we are miles under the school. It is dark and damp down here so we must be careful.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: I know what this is — it’s Devil’s Snare!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Of course it's Devil's Snare. It likes dark, damp places and wraps around you if you struggle.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Yes — of course — but there’s no wood!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, fire would work on Devil's Snare, but you need something to light with if there is no wood.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Lucky this plant thing’s here, really
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Obviously that plant cushioned our fall. Sometimes dangerous things can still have a useful side.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: These birds . . . they can’t be here just for decoration
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Of course the birds are not just decoration. If something seems odd it probably has a purpose here.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: They’re not birds! ... They’re keys! Winged keys — look carefully. So that must mean . . .
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, look closely. Those 'birds' are actually winged keys. That tells me there must be a key you need to catch to open the door.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: I’m going to be a knight
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Of course I can take my place and play my part when it matters. You do what you must even if it's frightening.

Book1-chapter16_Sc4.description: Of course it’s the full Body-Bind. We had to immobilize Neville quickly, even though I hate the idea of it.
I feel terrible about what we did to Neville, but I know it was necessary.
I’m not going first. No way am I dropping into unknown darkness before everyone else.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Danger lies before you, while safety lies behind, Two of us will help you, whichever you would find, One among us seven will let you move ahead, Another will transport the drinker back instead, Two among our number hold only nettle wine, Three of us are killers, waiting hidden in line.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: This is a logic puzzle. The riddle tells exactly what each bottle does: two help (one forward, one back), two are wine, and three are poison.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: First, however slyly the poison tries to hide You will always find some on nettle wine's left side; Second, different are those who stand at either end, But if you would move onward, neither is your friend; Third, as you see clearly, all are different size, Neither dwarf nor giant holds death in their insides; Fourth, the second left and the second on the right Are twins once you taste them, though different at first sight.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: Using the clues you can deduce which bottles are deadly, which are wine, which sends back, and which moves forward. Logic is enough to solve it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Got it. The smallest bottle will get us through the black fire - toward the Stone.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: I am certain the smallest bottle gets us through the black fire. I am positive about which bottle will send someone back.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Brilliant. This isn't magic - it's logic - a puzzle. A lot of the greatest wizards haven't got an ounce of logic, they'd be stuck in here forever.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: Logic can beat magic sometimes. I trust reasoning and books and that I can figure things out even under pressure.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Harry - you're a great wizard, you know. - Me! - Books! And cleverness! There are more important things - friendship and bravery and - oh Harry - be careful!
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: I care deeply about Harry. I admire him and I want him to be safe. Books and cleverness matter, but friendship and bravery matter more.

Book2-chapter5_Sc5.source: "You’re not telling me you did fly here?" said Hermione, sounding almost as severe as Professor McGonagall.
Book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: Well, you couldn't have flown here, could you? That would be ridiculous and dangerous

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "But you're Muggles!" said Mr Weasley delightedly.
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: Of course my parents are Muggles. I'm introducing them to my friends because they need to meet everyone.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "they were standing nervously at the counter that ran all along the great marble hall, waiting for Hermione to introduce them."
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: My parents are nervous but eager. I feel responsible for making that introduction go smoothly.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.source: "At least no one on the Gryffindor team had to buy their way in," said Hermione sharply. "They got in on pure talent."
Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: Well, of course our team earned their places. Talent matters, not money. Don't you dare suggest otherwise.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Ron! Ron! Are you all right?" squealed Hermione.
Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: Ron, you absolute idiot, are you all right? That curse backfired and he's covered in slugs. This is a disaster.

Book2-chapter7_Sc4.source: An’ they haven’t invented a spell our Hermione can’ do," said Hagrid proudly, making Hermione go a brilliant shade of magenta.
Book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: Well, of course I'm proud that I can do spells, but blimey, I go bright red when people brag about me like that. I hate being the centre of attention.

Book2-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, of course Dumbledore will defend fairness. He's insisting on proper procedure even now and that matters.
We have permission to go. We should leave promptly but calmly, don't do anything foolish.

Book2-chapter7_Sc2.source: Hermione, who nodded bravely, and the pair of them pulled Ron up by the arms
Book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: Of course I nodded, trying to be brave, and I helped pull Ron up by the arms so we could get him to Hagrid's.

Book2-chapter7_Sc3.source: "I think you’re being a bit unfair. Professor Dumbledore obviously thought he was the best man for the job —"
Book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: Well, I still think Dumbledore picked who was right for the job. Obviously he thought that was the best choice.

Book2-chapter7_Sc3.source: "He did," she said. "But I don’t know what it means. I could tell it was really rude, of course —"
Book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: Of course it was rude. I was called something horrible and I don't actually know the exact meaning, only that it was meant to wound.

Book2-chapter9_Sc7.source: Hermione was obviously still trying not to laugh.
Book2-chapter9_Sc7.description: Obviously I was trying not to laugh. I couldn't help it, it was too funny.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: Of course I'm not eating that disgusting stuff. No thanks.

Book2-chapter9_Sc6.source: ["I never knew that," said Hermione, looking at Ron in surprise.]
Book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: Well, I didn't know Ron was afraid of spiders. Of course it's odd since he's used them in Potions.

Book2-chapter9_Sc5.source: “Have you ever seen spiders act like that?” said Hermione wonderingly.
Book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: Well, have you ever seen spiders act like that? Of course I'm amazed that they are all clustering and climbing a silvery thread to get outside.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.source: "It's all right, he's still alive," said Hermione, prodding Errol gently with the tip of her finger.
Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: Well, Errol's alive. Of course I checked him straight away and he's breathing.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.source: "You'd better open it, Ron," said Neville in a timid whisper.
Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: Obviously Ron has to open the envelope or it will only get worse, so I think it's best he deals with it now.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.source: "Myrtle, no one wants to upset you," said Hermione. "Harry only —"
Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: Well, I tried to calm Myrtle down and make it clear we weren't trying to upset her. Of course I wanted to keep things civil so she'd actually answer our questions.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.source: "We wanted to ask you if you’ve seen anything funny lately," said Hermione quickly. "Because a cat was attacked right outside your front door on Halloween."
Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: We went to her because the cat was attacked right outside her door on Halloween. I needed to know if she saw anything suspicious that night.

Book2-chapter8_Sc3.source: "MYRTLE!" "Oh, no, Peeves, don’t tell her what I said, she’ll be really upset," "Hello, Myrtle." "Miss Granger was just talking about you —" "Just saying — saying — how nice you look tonight,"
Book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: Well, obviously I tried to cover for Myrtle and be friendly because she is delicate and gets upset if people tease her. I pretended to flatter her, told Peeves off, and even jabbed Harry and Ron to back me up.

Book2-chapter9_Sc9.source: Honestly, that was almost cheerful for Myrtle.
Book2-chapter9_Sc9.description: Well, honestly, that was almost cheerful for Myrtle. Of course she is dramatic, but that felt oddly bright for her.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "No, it’s not," said Hermione. "All we’d need would be some Polyjuice Potion."
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: Well, Polyjuice changes you into someone else. Obviously if we can brew it we can disguise ourselves and go where we need to go.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "There might be a way," said Hermione slowly, dropping her voice still further with a quick glance across the room at Percy. "Of course, it would be difficult. And dangerous, very dangerous. We’d be breaking about fifty school rules, I expect,"
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: Of course it's risky and rule breaking, but I can see a plan forming. It could work if we're careful and willing to take the chance.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "This is the most complicated potion I’ve ever seen," said Hermione as they scanned the recipe. "Lacewing flies, leeches, fluxweed, and knotgrass," she murmured, running her finger down the list of ingredients.
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, this is the most complicated potion I've ever seen. It needs lacewing flies, leeches, fluxweed and knotgrass and a whole lot more.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Oooh, look, powdered horn of a bicorn — don’t know where we’re going to get that — shredded skin of a boomslang — that’ll be tricky, too — and of course a bit of whoever we want to change into."
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: Of course some ingredients will be hard to get like powdered bicorn horn and shredded boomslang skin, and we have to add a bit of whoever we're changing into at the end.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Well, if you two are going to chicken out, fine," she said.
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, if you two chicken out, that's your choice. I'm willing to go ahead with this if someone will actually help.

Book2-chapter9_Sc4.source: "What’s a boy in his class saying about you?"
Book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I asked Harry what people were saying because I wanted facts. I was trying to work out if there was any truth to the rumors.
I found something odd at the window and called them over. It looked funny and important enough to check properly.
I said it was funny because the detail didn't fit with what we'd expect. It made me more curious and worried.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: “Well, since the fluxweed has got to be picked at the full moon and the lacewings have got to be stewed for twenty-one days . . . I’d say it’d be ready in about a month, if we can get all the ingredients.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: Well, the potion isn't quick. It needs specific timing and long preparation so it will take about a month if we get everything.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: However, while Hermione was checking that the coast was clear for them to leave the bathroom, Ron muttered to Harry, “It’ll be a lot less hassle if you can just knock Malfoy off his broom tomorrow.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: Of course I need to be careful. Checking the coast is sensible. We must not rush and risk being seen.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: But Hermione’s eyes narrowed dangerously again, and he added swiftly, “But it’s the best plan we’ve got, so full steam ahead, I say.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: Of course I'm fed up and serious about this. If anyone threatens our plan or our friends I won't stand for it.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: "I’d say it’d be ready in about a month, if we can get all the ingredients."
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, if we can find every ingredient, it should be ready in about a month. Of course we need everything or it won't work.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: However, while Hermione was checking that the coast was clear for them to leave the bathroom, Ron muttered to Harry, "It’ll be a lot less hassle if you can just knock Malfoy off his broom tomorrow."
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Of course I checked the corridor first. We are not going to leave without making sure it's safe.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: But Hermione’s eyes narrowed dangerously again, and he added swiftly, "But it’s the best plan we’ve got, so full steam ahead, I say."
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Obviously this plan is risky and I won't like it, but if it's the best option we have then we push ahead.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "We still need a bit of the people you’re changing into," said Hermione matter-of-factly
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: Obviously we need physical samples of the people we're turning into. Of course that's a must.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "I’ve filled these with a simple Sleeping Draught. All you have to do is make sure Crabbe and Goyle find them."
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I made chocolate cakes with a Sleeping Draught to knock Crabbe and Goyle out so we can get their hairs. That's the plan, plain and simple.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "I’ve already got mine!" said Hermione brightly, pulling a tiny bottle out of her pocket and showing them the single hair inside it.
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I already have a hair for myself from Millicent Bulstrode, so I won't need anyone else's for my portion.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "It looks like the book says it should . . . once we’ve drunk it, we’ll have exactly an hour before we change back into ourselves."
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: According to Moste Potente Potions it looks right and the effects last one hour. I double checked the book and followed it closely.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "I’m sure I’ve done everything right," said Hermione, nervously rereading the splotched page of Moste Potente Potions.
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I feel nervous but confident I followed the instructions correctly. Of course there are risks, but we have to try.

Book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, I'm the one who wakes people; I'm up early and alert, and I get things done first thing in the morning.
Of course I remembered presents; I give thoughtful ones and I can be a bit brisk about it.

Book2-chapter12_Sc3.source: I’ve been up for nearly an hour, adding more lacewings to the potion.
Book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I've been working ages on the potion; I add lacewings carefully and I don't leave things to the last minute.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: Undaunted, Hermione shoved her hand back into her bag and pulled out what appeared to be a bright red eraser. "It’s a Revealer, I got it in Diagon Alley," she said.
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: Well, of course I bought a Revealer in Diagon Alley. It's useful, obviously.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: No - really - I don't think I'll come.
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Well, I panicked while we were in the middle of the Polyjuice change and I froze up for a moment.
Of course the hair I used turned me partly into an animal because it was cat hair; the potion does animal transformations if you use animal hair.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: M-Millicent Bulstrode m-must have a cat! And the p-potion isn't supposed to be used for animal transformations!
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Well, it's obvious now that Millicent has a cat and that using animal hair was a massive mistake for Polyjuice; I'm furious at myself and upset by what happened.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: We'll meet you back here, all right?
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Of course I still trust Harry and Ron to stick to the plan and meet back after the change, even though I messed up.

Book2-chapter14_Sc5.source: [Harry — I think I’ve just understood something! I’ve got to go to the library!]
Book2-chapter14_Sc5.description: Of course! It all makes sense now! I've got to rush to the library and look it up immediately.

Book2-chapter14_Sc4.source: Do you think we should go and ask Hagrid about it all
Book2-chapter14_Sc4.description: Well, we should ask Hagrid about this. Of course it could affect our whole future, so we need to find out more.

Book2-chapter14_Sc2.source: "But the monster had killed someone, Ron," said Hermione.
Book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: Obviously the monster had killed someone. That changes how dangerous this is and how seriously we need to treat it.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: There’s just no point talking to a Petrified person
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I couldn't answer when I was petrified. I was frozen with the paper in my fist because I had just realised what the monster was and I was trying to warn someone.

Book2-chapter16_Sc4.source: the word Hermione had scribbled at the foot of the page
Book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: Well, of course, I wrote 'Pipes.' It points straight to the plumbing being used as the way in and out.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “Oooh, it might have hidden powers,” said Hermione enthusiastically, taking the diary and looking at it closely.
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: Of course the diary might have hidden powers. If it does, it could explain a lot.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “And this diary is fifty years old,” said Hermione, tapping it excitedly. “So?” “Oh, Ron, wake up,” snapped Hermione. “We know the person who opened the Chamber last time was expelled fifty years ago. We know T. M. Riddle got an award for special services to the school fifty years ago. Well, what if Riddle got his special award for catching the Heir of Slytherin? His diary would probably tell us everything — where the Chamber is, and how to open it, and what sort of creature lives in it — the person who’s behind the attacks this time wouldn’t want that lying around, would they?”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: Obviously, the diary is fifty years old so it could belong to the same Riddle who got that award. Of course his diary might say where the Chamber is and how to open it. That would explain everything about the attacks.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “It might be invisible ink!” she whispered. She tapped the diary three times and said, “Aparecium!” Nothing happened.
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I tried Aparecium on the diary because it might be written in invisible ink, but nothing showed up.

Book3-chapter6_Sc4.source: "He took Hermione's copy and ripped off the Spellotape that bound it. The book tried to bite, but Hagrid ran a giant forefinger down its spine, and the book shivered, and then fell open and lay quiet in his hand."
Book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: Well, of course, you have to stroke the book. It tried to bite and then calmed when Hagrid stroked it, so stroking is what they respond to

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "At these words, both Harry and Ron glanced, grinning, at Hermione, who looked startled at the news that books wouldn’t be much help in this subject."
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: Well, of course I thought books would help. That's worrying and a bit annoying. Books usually explain things properly, so hearing they're not much use here throws me.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: There’s only one vacancy, isn’t there? Defense Against the Dark Arts.
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: Well, of course the new teacher will be for Defense Against the Dark Arts. It fits, obviously.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: Sirius Black escaped to come after you? Oh, Harry, you’ll have to be really, really careful. Don’t go looking for trouble, Harry —
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: Oh Harry, that's dreadful. You must be extra careful and do not, under any circumstances, go looking for trouble.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: In Sites of Historical Sorcery it says the inn was the headquarters for the 1612 goblin rebellion, and the Shrieking Shack’s supposed to be the most severely haunted building in Britain
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: Of course Hogsmeade is historically important. It's full of interesting places and history, not just sweets.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: Right — who wants ter go first?
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: Of course you shouldn't rush into things. You must follow the rules Hagrid gave. Be polite and wait for the hippogriff to make the first move.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: Someone help me — gotta get him outta here —
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: Well, it's obvious we need to be practical and help straight away. I ran to hold the gate open because panicking does no good when someone's hurt.
Right, Harry can handle himself. He did exactly what he should and he was calm when it mattered. I respect that more now.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "You haven’t been fired, Hagrid!" gasped Hermione.
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: Of course I don't think Hagrid's been sacked yet. It can't be over until the governors decide.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "It’s all Malfoy’s fault, Hagrid!" said Hermione earnestly.
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: Obviously Malfoy caused the problem by insulting the hippogriff. Hagrid warned him and he didn't listen.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "We’re witnesses," said Harry. "You said hippogriffs attack if you insult them."
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: We're backing Hagrid. We'll tell Dumbledore what really happened and stick up for him.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Ooh, good, we’re starting some new subjects today,"
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: Of course I'm glad about new subjects. It's all important and I want to get started right away.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "I’ve fixed it all with Professor McGonagall."
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: Don't be ridiculous, I wouldn't actually try to be in three classes at once. Of course I've sorted it out properly with Professor McGonagall.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Ignore him," said Hermione, who was right behind Harry. "Just ignore him, it’s not worth it."
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I will stand up for Harry and tell him to ignore people like Pansy. Obviously it's not worth getting worked up over.

Book3-chapter7_Sc4.source: "I told you not to help him, Miss Granger."
Book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: Well, of course I was helping Neville with the potion. I was giving him quiet instructions because he was struggling and the potion had gone green.
I can't believe Snape would take points off for trying to help. He'll punish us for any kindness he thinks is undermining him.

Book3-chapter7_Sc4.source: "Possibly no one's warned you, Lupin, but this class contains Neville Longbottom. I would advise you not to entrust him with anything difficult. Not unless Miss Granger is hissing instructions in his ear."
Book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: Obviously Snape is openly hostile to Neville and to me. He assumes I interfere and he uses that to humiliate Neville in front of everyone.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: "I think you’ve had enough to drink, Hagrid," said Hermione firmly.
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Well, obviously he’s had too much to drink. I’m not going to stand by and let him carry on like that.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: "Stuck his head in the water barrel," said Hermione, putting the tankard away.
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Of course I stepped in to stop him; I’ll do what I can to keep him steady and safe.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.source: Hermione was muttering instructions to him out of the corner of her mouth, so that Snape wouldn’t see.
Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: Well, of course I was helping Neville quietly while Snape wasn't looking. I couldn't just leave him to ruin his potion.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "We can’t be there yet," said Hermione, checking her watch.
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: Well, obviously the timing is off. I check facts like the time to make sense of odd stops.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Ron," hissed Hermione, pointing at Professor Lupin, "be careful"
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: Of course I warn Ron when he is about to do something stupid. I say it quietly so we do not cause trouble.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I’m going to go and ask the driver what’s going on," came Hermione’s voice.
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I go and find answers. I want to know what is happening so I will take action and ask the driver directly.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: Of course everyone knows about You-Know-Who and what happened to me. It is common knowledge and saying it out loud won't change anything.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "I don't think it looks like a Grim,"
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: Obviously I don't buy that the teacup shows a death omen. I can see other shapes and I want to point out a reasonable explanation.
Well, obviously people are aware of Harry's past. It's not a secret and pretending otherwise is pointless.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “He’s gorgeous, isn’t he?” said Hermione, glowing.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Well, of course I think he's gorgeous. He's been neglected and he needed someone to take him.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “He didn’t mean to, did you, Crookshanks?” said Hermione.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Obviously Crookshanks didn't mean to be rude. He's just a cat, he'll settle with a bit of care.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “That reminds me, you forgot your rat tonic,” said Hermione, slapping the small red bottle into Ron’s hand.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Here, you forgot your rat tonic, take it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “And stop worrying, Crookshanks will be sleeping in my dormitory and Scabbers in yours, what’s the problem?”
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Of course Crookshanks will sleep in my dormitory and Scabbers in yours. There's no reason to worry about it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “Poor Crookshanks, that witch said he’d been in there for ages; no one wanted him.”
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Poor Crookshanks was left alone and unwanted, so of course I had to take him.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “He didn’t mean to, did you, Crookshanks?” said Hermione.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: Well, of course Crookshanks didn't mean to attack Scabbers. He's not vicious for the sake of it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “That reminds me, you forgot your rat tonic,” said Hermione, slapping the small red bottle into Ron’s hand.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: You forgot your rat tonic. Here, take it. I remember that stuff and I packed it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “And stop worrying, Crookshanks will be sleeping in my dormitory and Scabbers in yours, what’s the problem? Poor Crookshanks, that witch said he’d been in there for ages; no one wanted him.”
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: I'm looking out for Crookshanks. He can stay in my dormitory and Scabbers can stay with Ron. Of course I'll take him in.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'And Professor Lupin stepped over you, and walked toward the dementor, and pulled out his wand,' said Hermione, 'and he said, 'None of us is hiding Sirius Black under our cloaks. Go.' But the dementor didn't move, so Lupin muttered something, and a silvery thing shot out of his wand at it, and it turned around and sort of glided away.'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, Lupin confronted the dementor, told it to leave, and when it didn't he used some spell that shot a silvery thing from his wand and made it go away. Obviously Lupin knew how to deal with it.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Ginny, who was huddled in her corner looking nearly as bad as Harry felt, gave a small sob; Hermione went over and put a comforting arm around her."
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: Of course I worry about Ginny. I comforted her because she was shaken by the dementor as much as Harry was.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'Are you sure you're okay, Harry?' said Hermione, watching Harry anxiously. 'I don't get it. What happened?' said Harry, wiping more sweat off his face."
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I am anxious and want explanations. I can't accept that Harry just collapsed without understanding why and how Lupin handled it.

Book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: Well, of course it's a shape-shifter. It changes into whatever it thinks will frighten you most. That's exactly what a boggart is.

Book3-chapter7_Sc5.source: "Couldn’t have put it better myself," said Professor Lupin, and Hermione glowed.
Book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: Obviously I was pleased when Professor Lupin agreed with me. It felt good to be right and to have someone acknowledge it.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Please, sir," said Hermione, "please, I could help Neville put it right —"
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Of course I can help Neville fix his potion. It only needs the right amount of rat spleen and a dash of leech juice, and I can sort it out.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Orange, Longbottom," said Snape, ladling some up and allowing it to splash back into the cauldron, so that everyone could see.
