Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Snape is humiliating Neville in front of the class. He is being cruel and singling Neville out instead of helping.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: Hermione went as pink as Neville.
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: I felt embarrassed when Snape snapped at me for trying to help. I meant well, obviously.

Book3-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Please, sir, we’ve done boggarts, Red Caps, kappas, and grindylows,"
Book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: Well, we've already covered boggarts, Red Caps, kappas, and grindylows in Defense Against the Dark Arts, and we were about to start the next topic.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "the werewolf differs from the true wolf in several small ways. The snout of the werewolf —"
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course the werewolf is different from a true wolf. I can explain the distinctions clearly and precisely.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Five more points from Gryffindor for being an insufferable know-it-all."
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, obviously Snape will punish me for speaking out of turn even when I'm right. He calls me names and takes house points.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "I was under the impression that I am teaching this lesson, not you."
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course I expect to be taught properly. Snape behaves as if he must assert control instead of explaining things.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: Hermione assumed an “all-for-the-best” expression that made Ron even angrier, and Harry had to endure everyone in the class talking loudly and happily about what they were going to do first, once they got into Hogsmeade.
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: Well, of course I tried to look like it would be all right. Somebody has to keep calm and think sensibly about this.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: Ron halfheartedly suggested the Invisibility Cloak, but Hermione stamped on that one, reminding Ron what Dumbledore had told them about the dementors being able to see through them.
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: Obviously I shut down the cloak idea because Dumbledore warned us dementors can see through it. It was ridiculous to suggest it.

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "You and Hermione answered my questions correctly at the start of the class, Harry," Lupin said lightly.
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: Well, of course, I answered Lupin's questions correctly and that got us points
Of course the class clapped when the boggart was defeated and Lupin praised us

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: Hermione checked her watch. “We’d better go down, you know, the feast’ll be starting in five minutes.”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Well, obviously the feast is starting in five minutes so we need to get moving now.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “What did you do?” said Hermione, looking anxious. “Did you get any work done?”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Of course I worry about work. I asked if anyone got any work done while they were out.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: I don’t know, But I really hope Professor Lupin gets better soon.
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: Well, I honestly don't know why Snape's like that, but of course I hope Professor Lupin recovers. Of course I do.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Hermione made a small, squeaky noise. Her eyes were extremely bloodshot."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: Well, I was terrified and crying. My eyes were all red and I couldn't stop making that noise.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "But the match," said Harry. "What happened? Are we doing a replay?" No one said anything. The horrible truth sank into Harry like a stone.
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: Of course I was worried about the match, but then it hit me how serious this was and that the game didn't matter compared to Harry being hurt.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Ron and Hermione were also there, looking as though they’d just climbed out of a swimming pool."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: I am at Harry's side. I care too much about him for words and I am shaken by what happened.

Book3-chapter9_Sc4.source: “Give me your glasses, quick!” "Impervius!" "There!" "They’ll repel water!"
Book3-chapter9_Sc4.description: Well, obviously Impervius repels water. I tapped Harry’s glasses and they kept the rain off so he could see.

Book3-chapter9_Sc4.source: Hermione appeared at his shoulder; she was holding her cloak over her head and was, inexplicably, beaming.
Book3-chapter9_Sc4.description: Of course I wanted to help Harry. I’m glad I could do something useful and that it made a difference for him on the pitch.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Dumbledore was really angry," Hermione said in a quaking voice. "I’ve never seen him like that before. He ran onto the field as you fell, waved his wand, and you sort of slowed down before you hit the ground. Then he whirled his wand at the dementors. Shot silver stuff at them. They left the stadium right away."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: Well, Dumbledore was really angry. I've never seen him like that. He ran out, slowed you before you hit, and blasted the dementors away with some silver stuff.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Well . . . when you fell off, it got blown away," said Hermione hesitantly. "And?" "And it hit — it hit — oh, Harry — it hit the Whomping Willow."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: Well, when you fell your broom was blown away and it hit the Whomping Willow. That's why it's wrecked.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Professor Flitwick brought it back just before you came around," said Hermione in a very small voice.
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: Of course Professor Flitwick brought the broom back just before you came to. He managed to fetch it from the willow.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Harry, listen," said Hermione, exchanging a look with Ron, "you must be really upset about what we heard yesterday. But the thing is, you mustn't go doing anything stupid."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, of course I'm terrified for Harry, but I can't let him do something reckless. He mustn't put himself in danger. It's what Black wants if Harry goes looking for him.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "There's nothing you can do!" said Hermione, looking stricken.
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Obviously I feel helpless because there really isn't anything practical we can do right now. The dementors will catch Black and he'll go back to Azkaban and that's that.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Harry, please," said Hermione, her eyes now shining with tears, "please be sensible. Black did a terrible, terrible thing, but d-don't put yourself in danger, it's what Black wants... Your mum and dad wouldn't want you to get hurt, would they?"
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Of course I love Harry and I want him safe. I keep thinking about what his parents would have wanted for him and I know they wouldn't have wanted him risking his life chasing revenge.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "But Harry isn't going to keep it!' said Hermione, as though the idea were ludicrous. 'He's going to hand it in to Professor McGonagall, aren't you, Harry?'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: Of course I think Harry should hand the map in to Professor McGonagall. Keeping it is reckless and dangerous.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "But what about Sirius Black?' Hermione hissed. 'He could be using one of the passages on that map to get into the castle! The teachers have got to know!'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: Obviously Sirius Black is dangerous and might use secret passages. The teachers must be told about anything that could let him in.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Look, Harry still shouldn't be coming into Hogsmeade. He hasn't got a signed form! If anyone finds out, he'll be in so much trouble! And it's not nightfall yet — what if Sirius Black turns up today? Now?'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: Harry being in Hogsmeade without permission is unacceptable. He could get into terrible trouble and it would be irresponsible with Black possibly nearby.

Book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: Well, of course she thinks she knows what’s going on even if Ron and Harry are being secretive. I say things plainly because it makes sense.

Book3-chapter12_Sc2.source: And what are you tutting at us for?
Book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: Obviously I notice when people are tutting and I call them out on it. I react if I think someone is being unfair or evasive.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: I’m sure I’ve read about a case of hippogriff-baiting
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Well, of course I'll dig up precedents. There might be cases that help Hagrid prove Buckbeak is safe.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: Is it awful in there, Hagrid?
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Obviously Azkaban is horrific. I can't imagine living like that. Hagrid's description shows it's brutal and leaves people shattered.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: I’ll look it up for you, Hagrid, and see exactly what happened.
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Of course I have to try to help. Research and facts matter and could make a real difference for Buckbeak and Hagrid.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Well, isn't it obvious?" said Hermione, with a look of maddening superiority.
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Well, of course I think there's an obvious reason for what Ron was wondering about. I don't see why they won't just say it.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "tuh" from behind them. It was Hermione, who had been sitting at the feet of a suit of armor, repacking her bag, which was so full of books it wouldn't close.
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I was sitting with my books and tutting because I wanted them to answer me. Of course my bag is stuffed with books; I need them.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Harry, I’m sure you’ll be able to go next time," she said. "They’re bound to catch Black soon. He’s been sighted once already."
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I think they’ll catch Sirius Black soon. If that happens, Harry can go next time. It all makes sense.
Of course, Harry is supposed to stay in school. Rules are rules and I’m worried about him breaking them.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Ron, don’t hurt him!" squealed Hermione; the whole common room was watching;
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I care about Crookshanks and I’m defensive when Ron goes for him. I don’t want anyone hurting an animal, even if it’s annoying.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: Well, there might have been something wrong with the Firebolt. At least now I know it's safe.
Of course I can't drop subjects. I have to keep up with everything.
Arithmancy is brilliant and important to me. It's obviously my favorite even if it looks complicated.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "Hermione was barely visible behind a tottering pile of books."
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: Well, of course I'm swamped with work. I keep on top of every class because that's what has to be done. It all makes sense to me, even if it looks mad to everyone else.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "I heard her talking to Professor Vector, that Arithmancy witch, this morning. They were going on about yesterday’s lesson, but Hermione can’t’ve been there, because she was with us in Care of Magical Creatures!"
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: Obviously I'm attending multiple classes and making it work. Missing lessons is not an option for me.

Book3-chapter15_Sc2.source: “This is such a waste of time,” Hermione hissed. “I could be practicing something useful. I could be catching up on Cheering Charms —”
Book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: Well, of course this is a waste of time. I could be practising something useful instead, like catching up on Cheering Charms.
I keep tutting because this is ridiculous and it's not the kind of proper practice I want. I can't stand wasting time on nonsense like crystal gazing.

Book3-chapter14_Sc9.source: "No," said Hermione. She was holding a letter in her hands and her lip was trembling. "I just thought you ought to know . . . Hagrid lost his case. Buckbeak is going to be executed."
Book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: Well, I have a letter and I just thought you ought to know. Hagrid lost his case and Buckbeak is going to be executed.

Book3-chapter15_Sc3.source: “Oh, for goodness’ sake!” said Hermione loudly. “Not that ridiculous Grim again!”
Book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: Well, honestly, not that ridiculous Grim again. Of course I'm fed up with this nonsense and it's just not serious.

Book3-chapter15_Sc3.source: Professor Trelawney stood up, surveying Hermione with unmistakable anger. “I am sorry to say that from the moment you have arrived in this class, my dear, it has been apparent that you do not have what the noble art of Divination requires. Indeed, I don’t remember ever meeting a student whose mind was so hopelessly mundane.”
Book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: Fine, that's it. Of course she thinks Divination is about mystic nonsense and obviously she believes I don't have the right mind for it. Well, I give up on this class.

Book3-chapter15_Sc3.source: “Fine!” said Hermione suddenly, getting up and cramming Unfogging the Future back into her bag. “Fine!” she repeated, swinging the bag over her shoulder and almost knocking Ron off his chair. “I give up! I’m leaving!”
Book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I left the class, bag and book and all. I couldn't stand it any longer, so I walked out.

Book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: Well, of course you're going to be fine. I'm telling you that because I want you to calm down even though I'm terrified too.

Book3-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Well, honestly . . . ‘the fates have informed her’ . . . who sets the exam? She does! What an amazing prediction!"
Book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, honestly, 'the fates have informed her' — who actually sets the exam? She does. That's not prophecy, that's her doing.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: Hermione was sitting at the table right behind them and clearing a space in the wall of books that had been hiding her.
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Well, of course I’m not letting Harry go off alone to Hogsmeade again. After everything with Sirius Black I’m not taking the risk.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: With a soft hiss, Crookshanks leapt onto her lap. Hermione took one frightened look at the expression on Ron’s face, gathered up Crookshanks, and hurried away toward the girls’ dormitories.
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Obviously I’ll look after Crookshanks and get away if things get nasty. I don’t want more trouble than necessary.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Of course I did," said Hermione in a strangely high-pitched voice, not looking up. "And I’m very glad we won, and I think you did really well, but I need to read this by Monday."
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Of course I went to the match. I’m glad we won and I think you did well, but I have to read this huge essay by Monday. I can’t just relax.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I can’t, Harry. I’ve still got four hundred and twenty-two pages to read!" said Hermione, now sounding slightly hysterical.
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I have four hundred and twenty-two pages left. I’m really behind and it’s stressing me out.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "He doesn’t want me to join in." There was no arguing with this, as Ron chose that moment to say loudly, "If Scabbers hadn’t just been eaten, he could have had some of those Fudge Flies." Hermione burst into tears.
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Ron just blamed me about Scabbers and it pushed me over the edge. I’m upset and not prepared to be blamed right now.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Because I thought — and Professor McGonagall agrees with me — that that broom was probably sent to Harry by Sirius Black!"
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Well, I think Sirius Black sent Harry the Firebolt. Of course I told McGonagall because it looks suspicious.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I have been crystal gazing, Headmaster," said Professor Trelawney...
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Obviously Professor Trelawney says Lupin is ill and that his time is short, but I don't take that as proof of anything definite.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I dare not, Headmaster! If I join the table, we shall be thirteen!"
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I saw Trelawney go into hysterics about thirteen at the table. It was ridiculous and made the whole lunch awkward.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: Well, Hagrid took Buckbeak outside and tied him in the pumpkin patch so he could see the trees and smell fresh air.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore’s gonna come down while it — while it happens. Wrote me this mornin'."
Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: Of course Dumbledore is coming to be with Hagrid when Buckbeak is executed.
Well, I started helping Hagrid clean up when he dropped the milk because I couldn't just stand there.
Of course there was another milk jug hiding in the cupboard and I found it.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Ron! I — I don’t believe it — it’s Scabbers!"
Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: Blimey, Scabbers was in the milk jug. He's alive but absolutely filthy and falling apart.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: No, Harry, we must not let you rush in like that. Of course I’m terrified but I try to stop him.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Be quiet!" and "Hermione’s foot swing out of nowhere."
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I will try to protect Harry and Ron even if it frightens me. I act quickly and I will get stuck in to stop harm.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Crookshanks! Hermione moaned. No, go away, Crookshanks! Go away!
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: Well, Crookshanks is attacking Scabbers. Obviously I need to try and stop him, but it's chaos and I'm scared.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Ron — come on — back under the cloak — Hermione panted. Dumbledore — the Minister — they’ll be coming back out in a minute —
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: Of course we have to get back under the Invisibility Cloak now. Ron, hurry, because Dumbledore and the Minister will be coming back any second.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Ron, your dad works for the Ministry, you can’t go saying things like that to his boss!"
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Of course I warned Ron not to insult Fudge. Dad or not he’ll only make things worse if we cause a scene.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "As long as Hagrid keeps his head this time, and argues his case properly, they can’t possibly execute Buckbeak."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Well, I said Buckbeak should be safe if Hagrid behaves and presents his case. I didn’t really believe it deep down but I wanted to stay hopeful.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Hermione and Ron, not being on speaking terms with the Minister of Magic, hovered awkwardly in the background."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Obviously we’re all on edge about Fudge and the situation with the Ministry. It’s making everything strained between us.

Book3-chapter17_Sc8.source: [To his right, Hermione gave a dry sob.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: Well, I was choking back a sob. I was terrified and upset for Harry and what might happen next.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "One hopes, however, that one might have mistaken the Signs. . . . The Inner Eye can be a burden, you know. . . ."
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: Well, of course that's ridiculous to panic over. I'm exhausted and stressed but I'm not leaving Hogwarts because of a vague prediction.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "She was usually last to leave the common room at night, first to arrive at the library the next morning; she had shadows like Lupin’s under her eyes, and seemed constantly close to tears."
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: Well, obviously I'm overdoing it. I'm taking more subjects than anyone and it's getting to me, I'm knackered and close to tears but I have to keep going.

Book3-chapter17_Sc9.source: "WE'RE UP HERE!" Hermione screamed suddenly. "WE'RE UP HERE — SIRIUS BLACK — QUICK!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc9.description: Of course, I shouted to get help. I know we were the ones in danger up here and I had to alert anyone downstairs, fast.
Well, even I get frightened. I was pressed against the door, frozen and trying to be brave but also desperate for someone to arrive.

Book3-chapter17_Sc5.source: Harry's and Hermione's wands shot out of their hands, high in the air, and Black caught them
Book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: Well, my wand got blasted out of my hand and Black caught it. Of course I'm shaking and stuck without it.

Book3-chapter17_Sc4.source: "Where's Ron?" "Where does this tunnel come out?" "I don't know. It goes off the edge of the map, but it looked like it ends up in Hogsmeade."
Book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: Where's Ron? I don't know where this tunnel comes out, the map shows it going off the edge and it looked like it ends up in Hogsmeade, so we might be heading that way.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "How — could — they?" she choked. "How could they?"
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I can’t believe they found out. How could they know? It doesn’t make sense.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Ron, be quiet!" Hermione whispered urgently. "Fudge’ll be out here in a minute —"
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Fudge will be out here soon. We need to keep quiet and move before we get caught.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: They set off back toward the castle, walking slowly to keep themselves hidden under the Cloak.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Of course we’re going back under the Cloak. We have to stay hidden and go slowly so we’re not seen.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "Did you check the lunar chart and realize that I was always ill at the full moon? Or did you realize that the boggart changed into the moon when it saw me?" "Both," Hermione said quietly.
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: Of course I checked the lunar chart and saw the boggart turn into the moon. It all points to Lupin being a werewolf.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "You're the cleverest witch of your age I've ever met, Hermione." "I'm not," Hermione whispered. "If I'd been a bit cleverer, I'd have told everyone what you are!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: Well, I should have said something sooner. I can't believe I didn't tell everyone what he was. I blame myself for not being cleverer about it.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.source: "but of course, they, like you, Hermione, worked out the truth."
Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: Of course I worked it out. I saw how it all fit. They figured out Lupin was a werewolf but stayed loyal.
Obviously, Sirius, Peter and James became Animagi so they could be with Lupin in animal form and keep him company safely.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Peter, as the smallest, could slip beneath the Willow's attacking branches and touch the knot that freezes it."
Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: Peter was the smallest Animagus so he could get past the Willow and stop it, letting them join Lupin in the tunnel.

Book3-chapter18_Sc2.source: "They sneaked out of the castle every month under James's Invisibility Cloak."
Book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: They used James's Invisibility Cloak to sneak out every month and help Lupin during his transformations.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Harry — we’ve got to go for help —" Hermione gasped; she was bleeding too; the Willow had cut her across the shoulder.
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: Harry, we've got to go for help, I shouted between gasps because I'm cut and scared and I know sometimes you have to think of the sensible option.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Oh, help, help," Hermione whispered frantically, dancing uncertainly on the spot, "please . . ."
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: Oh, help, help, please — I panicked because it looked hopeless, but I was desperate for anything that might save Ron.
Crookshanks, thank you — I trusted him to try something, and when he did, I couldn't believe it worked.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: Crookshanks darted forward. He slithered between the battering branches like a snake and placed his front paws upon a knot on the trunk. Abruptly, as though the tree had been turned to marble, it stopped moving.
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: Well, obviously Crookshanks is braver and cleverer than we gave him credit for. He can interfere with the Willow somehow.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: Where is the Cloak? Of course I need to know where it is if we're going to help. Obviously we can't blunder in without a plan.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.source: Hermione returned a quarter of an hour later with the silvery Cloak folded carefully under her robes.
Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I went and fetched the Cloak. Of course I did. Obviously we can't leave him alone and if the Cloak is the only way, I'll get it.

Book3-chapter17_Sc11.description: Well, of course I kept it secret. I didn't tell anyone.
How could you do this? You and him. Of course I'm shocked and I feel betrayed.

Book3-chapter17_Sc11.source: "Harry, don't trust him, he's been helping Black get into the castle, he wants you dead too — he's a werewolf!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc11.description: Obviously I believe Lupin is a werewolf and I think he has been helping Black get into the castle and that he could want Harry dead.
Of course I've been covering up for him. I've been protecting him and hiding things to help him.

Book3-chapter19_Sc6.source: "There was another blinding flash of light and then — It was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing tree. ... a man was standing where Scabbers had been, cringing and wringing his hands."
Book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: Well, of course Scabbers changed back into a man. He was tiny and scared, not a normal rat at all. This explains everything about him behaving strangely.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: “We attacked a teacher. . . . We attacked a teacher . . . ,” Hermione whimpered, staring at the lifeless Snape with frightened eyes. “Oh, we’re going to be in so much trouble —”
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Well, we really did attack a teacher and of course we’re going to be in serious trouble. I’m terrified about the consequences.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Well, explain it properly. Of course I want to know exactly what you mean about Peter and the cat and the passwords.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "He tried to bring Peter to me, but couldn’t . . . so he stole the passwords into Gryffindor Tower for me. . . . As I understand it, he took them from a boy’s bedside table."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Obviously Crookshanks helped by stealing the Gryffindor passwords and tried to get Peter to me. That shows the cat has been interfering on our behalf.

Book3-chapter19_Sc1.source: Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.
Book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: Well, of course I tried to disarm Snape. It was the sensible thing to do to protect Harry and stop Snape from doing anything more dangerous.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["Scabbers can't be Pettigrew . . . it just can't be true, you know it can't . . ."]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, of course Scabbers can't be Pettigrew because there should be an official record. I checked the Animagus register for my homework and Pettigrew's name isn't on it.
Okay, I was right about the register, but apparently there used to be unregistered Animagi at Hogwarts. Obviously the Ministry didn't know everything.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["But Professor Lupin . . . Scabbers can't be Pettigrew . . . it just can't be true, you know it can't . . ."]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm stunned that Lupin and Sirius would support such a claim, but if there were secret Animagi back then, I have to revise my certainty. I want a proper explanation, not just shouting.

Book3-chapter20_Sc5.source: [They were locked, jaw to jaw, claws ripping at each other, Harry stood, transfixed by the sight, too intent upon the battle to notice anything else, It was Hermione’s scream that alerted him, Pettigrew had dived for Lupin’s dropped wand.]
Book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: Of course I screamed, what else was I meant to do? Pettigrew was diving for Lupin's dropped wand and I had to warn Harry.

Book3-chapter22_Sc3.source: Hermione tucking the Time-Turner back under her robes.
Book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: Of course I put the Time-Turner away again, hidden under my robes.

Book3-chapter22_Sc3.source: Panicking, Harry and Hermione ran forward.
Book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: Well, we were panicking but we managed to get back. It all worked out, even if it was terrifying.

Book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, of course I'm terrified, but I'm keeping quiet and trying to be sensible. We need to stay silent and find out if Ron's going to be all right.

Book3-chapter21_Sc1.source: She pressed a finger to her lips, then pointed to the hospital wing door.
Book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: Of course I'm shaken, but I'm protecting Harry and Ron by keeping them calm and making sure we don't draw attention. That matters to me more than panicking.

Book3-chapter22_Sc1.source: They waited a few moments to make sure they’d really gone, then started to run in the opposite direction.
Book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: Well, of course we had to make sure they were gone before moving. Rushing would be stupid.

Book3-chapter22_Sc1.source: They tore into a deserted classroom to their left just in time.
Book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: Get to a safe room and hide. That’s basic sense, obviously, especially with Peeves about.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: We’ve turned the clock back three hours. Of course I used the Time-Turner. I’ve been doing that all year to get to extra lessons.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: It’s called a Time-Turner, and I got it from Professor McGonagall on our first day back.
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: Professor McGonagall trusted me to use a Time-Turner for lessons only. I had to promise and the Ministry had to be told I was responsible.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: If we manage that without being seen, it’ll be a miracle!
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: This is terrifying and brilliant at the same time. It could work but only if we’re perfect about not being seen.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: Don’t you understand? We’re breaking one of the most important Wizarding laws! Nobody’s supposed to change time, nobody!
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: Of course we must be careful. Time travel is forbidden for a reason. If we’re seen meddling it could mess everything up.

Book3-chapter21_Sc2.source: If anyone’s looking out of the window —
Book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: We have to assume someone could spot us from the castle. Of course we need to stay out of sight and plan every move.

Book3-chapter22_Sc2.source: "Oh, he’s horrible," whispered Hermione, her ear to the door. "I bet he’s all excited because the dementors are going to finish off Sirius. . . ."
Book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: Oh, he's horrible. Peeves is gloating because he thinks the dementors will finish off Sirius. Of course he would enjoy that.
We are on a tight countdown. We have minutes, not hours. We need to hurry now.

Book3-chapter22_Sc2.source: "Okay — I can hear Dumbledore," said Hermione tensely. "Come on, Harry!"
Book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: Dumbledore is coming and will lock the door. We must get moving and get inside before he does.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "That's wonderful!" said Hermione, giving Ron a reproving look because he looked as though he was close to laughing.
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: Of course I think what happened last night was serious, but apparently Buckbeak's escaped and some people are celebrating, which I find upsetting and a bit improper.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "That's wonderful!" said Hermione, giving Ron a reproving look because he looked as though he was close to laughing.
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I'm annoyed with Ron for looking like he finds this funny. I expect him to take this seriously, not to be grinning about it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: Of course it's shocking that the Dementors tried to give the Kiss to an innocent boy. That's unacceptable and they must be removed.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Oh yes, they’ll have to go," said Fudge, running his fingers distractedly through his hair. "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy. . . . Completely out of control . . . no, I’ll have them packed off back to Azkaban tonight."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: The Minister claims he'll send the Dementors back to Azkaban tonight. Obviously that's what needs to happen.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: "Perhaps we should think about dragons at the school entrance."
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: Someone suggested dragons at the school entrance. Well, that sounds dangerous, but Hagrid would adore it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc6.source: As he and Fudge left the dormitory, Madam Pomfrey hurried to the door and locked it again.
Book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: Madam Pomfrey locked the door after they left. Of course she would, she's being careful.

Book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: Well, Scabbers has been sleeping in Harry's dormitory for three years. If he's working for You-Know-Who, why didn't he ever try to hurt Harry before now? Of course that makes me question the simple spy story.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Harry and Hermione thought it best to accept their chocolate quietly."
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: Well, of course we stayed quiet and took the chocolate. Making a fuss would only draw attention.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "they heard a distant roar of fury echoing from somewhere above them."
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: Obviously something furious is happening upstairs. We can hear angry voices getting louder and it's worrying.
Someone shouted that he didn't Disapparate. That means there's an argument about whether someone left by Apparition, and it's serious.

Book3-chapter22_Sc4.source: "YOU CAN'T APPARATE OR DISAPPARATE INSIDE THIS CASTLE!"
Book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: Of course Apparition inside the castle is impossible. If people are accusing each other of it, they're panicking and confused.

Book3-chapter21_Sc3.source: What did you do? You said you were only going to keep a lookout!
Book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: Well, I can't believe it, Harry. You weren't just looking out, you did something huge without warning and nearly gave me a heart attack.
Of course I opened the window to get Sirius out. I cast Alohomora so we could get him out quickly.

Book3-chapter21_Sc3.source: We've got about forty-five minutes until Dumbledore locks the door to the hospital wing.
Book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: Right now timing matters. We've got under an hour before the ward is locked, so we have to get Sirius and get back before anyone notices.

Book3-chapter22_Sc8.source: doesn’t sound like there’s anything we can do
Book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: Well, it sounds like there’s nothing we can do about it right now. Of course I wish we could, but we have to be realistic.

Book3-chapter18_Sc3.source: That was still really dangerous! Running around in the dark with a werewolf! What if you’d given the others the slip, and bitten somebody?
Book3-chapter18_Sc3.description: Well, that was still really dangerous. Of course I was horrified at the idea of running about at night with a werewolf and the risk they could have bitten someone.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Why don’t you show Harry where he’s sleeping, Ron?"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Well, I get practical about things, I point out what needs doing and I want everyone to be comfortable, so I tell Ron to show Harry his bed.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "We can all go," said Hermione pointedly.
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Of course I don’t like awkwardness, I nudge people to include themselves so we can all avoid tense moments.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Have you had a good summer, Harry?"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Well, I check in with friends properly, I ask if Harry got the parcels and I actually care if he’s been all right over the summer.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Yeah," said Harry softly, "twice. He sounds okay."
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Obviously I’m close enough to Harry and Ron to be part of their plans about Sirius, we’ve worked closely together to help him escape and we worry about him together.

Book4-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I'll send Bill, Charlie, and Percy along around midday," Mrs Weasley said to Mr Weasley, as he, Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Ginny set off across the dark yard after Fred and George.
Book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: Well, of course Mrs Weasley said she'll send Bill, Charlie, and Percy around midday, and we're all heading out across the yard to follow Fred and George.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "There were footsteps down the passageway and Hermione and Ginny came into the kitchen, both looking pale and drowsy."
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I'm knackered; getting up this early is daft when we've hardly slept.

Book4-chapter5_Sc1.source: "It’s just that it’s very difficult for a large number of wizards to congregate without attracting Muggle attention."
Book4-chapter5_Sc1.description: Of course we have to walk a short way so we don't draw Muggle attention. It all makes sense; safety first.

Book4-chapter5_Sc4.source: “This is Hermione, friend of Ron’s — and Harry, another friend —”
Book4-chapter5_Sc4.description: Well, of course I'm Ron's friend. I'm with him and Harry at the moment, just like everyone says.

Book4-chapter5_Sc4.source: Mr Weasley was shaking hands with a ruddy-faced wizard with a scrubby brown beard, who was holding a moldy-looking old boot in his other hand.
Book4-chapter5_Sc4.description: That Amos Diggory looks like any ordinary wizard, not terrifying at all. He seems friendly enough.

Book4-chapter5_Sc3.source: “Hermione came over the crest of the hill last, clutching a stitch in her side.”
Book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, I’m knackered and I’ve got a stitch, but of course I’m coming — we have to find that Portkey.
Obviously the Portkey will be something small and unremarkable, something Muggles would think is just litter.

Book4-chapter8_Sc2.source: Mr Malfoy’s eyes had returned to Hermione, who went slightly pink, but stared determinedly back at him.
Book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: Well, of course I'm not going to look away. I went a bit pink but I stared him right back. I won't be bullied because of where I'm from.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "You just need to touch the Portkey, that’s all, a finger will do"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: Well, obviously touching the Portkey is enough. A single finger will do the trick, no faffing about needed.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "With difficulty, owing to their bulky backpacks, the nine of them crowded around the old boot held out by Amos Diggory."
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: We squeezed around that manky old boot with our huge backpacks on. It was awkward and I was glad we were all careful and close together.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "he could feel Ron and Hermione on either side of him, their shoulders banging into his; they were all speeding forward in a howl of wind and swirling color;"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: Of course I was beside Harry and Ron when the Portkey went. It was a mad, windy lurch and we all slammed into each other. That sort of thing makes you hold on tight.

Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: Harry, Ron, and Hermione turned quickly.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I don't like the Malfoys being so close. It feels wrong for them to be sitting there after everything Dobby went through.

Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: A pale boy with a pointed face and white-blond hair, Draco greatly resembled his father. His mother was blonde too; tall and slim, she would have been nice-looking if she hadn’t been wearing a look that suggested there was a nasty smell under her nose.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: Of course Draco looks exactly like his father. And his mother looks horrible about something. I can't stand their attitude.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Oooh, thanks, Harry," said Hermione. "And I’ll get us some programs, look —"
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: Of course I'll make sure we have programs. I want us to be organised and actually know what's happening.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Fair enough," said Ron, grinning. "Oooh, thanks, Harry," said Hermione.
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: Well, it's obvious Harry's being generous. I appreciate it and I know it's a bit much, but I'll help make it count.

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: Well, of course I shouted at Harry when he started to do something daft; I pulled him back into his seat because that was reckless
Honestly, I was exasperated with him for even thinking of leaping out of the box; some things you just don't do

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "I wonder what the Bulgarians have got dangling all over their tents?" said Hermione.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Well, I'm curious what the Bulgarians have hanging on their tents. Obviously it's worth checking out.

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "He looks really grumpy," said Hermione, looking around at the many Krums blinking and scowling at them.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: He looks really grumpy. Those moving Krum posters just blink and scowl, and yes I noticed how similar they all are.

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: Hermione was overcome with such a strong fit of the giggles at this point that she had to duck out of the queue and only returned when Archie had collected his water and moved away.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Of course I couldn't stop giggling at Archie and the pinstriped trousers situation. I tried to hide it but I couldn't help myself.

Book4-chapter6_Sc6.description: Well, obviously we are surrounded by children making a mess. Someone trod on a slug and it burst which is horrid and rather unsanitary.
Of course there are witches and wizards from abroad here. Look at their banner. This is more organised than I expected and people are already setting up cooking arrangements.

Book4-chapter6_Sc6.source: "And he was the best Beater the Wimbourne Wasps ever had."
Book4-chapter6_Sc6.description: Obviously some of the camp talk is about Quidditch and local bragging. People are comparing players and telling stories while everyone wakes up.

Book4-chapter6_Sc7.source: They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.
Book4-chapter6_Sc7.description: Well, of course they're decorating their tents with shamrocks. It's obvious everyone wants to show they belong and celebrate in their own way.

Book4-chapter6_Sc7.source: Harry caught snatches of conversation in strange languages from the inside of tents they passed, and though he couldn’t understand a word, the tone of every single voice was excited.
Book4-chapter6_Sc7.description: Of course people would be talking in different languages here. It makes perfect sense that everyone's excited and showing off their national colours.

Book4-chapter8_Sc7.source: “They’re going to crash!” screamed Hermione next to Harry.
Book4-chapter8_Sc7.description: Well, that's mad. I actually thought they were going to crash. It looked like they were falling straight into the ground.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course I'll come with you. I'm going with you straight away. I'm here, I want to help, obviously.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "There’s something I haven’t told you," "On Saturday morning, I woke up with my scar hurting again."
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, my reaction to Harry's scar is immediate and concerned. Obviously something serious might be happening if his scar's hurting again.

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Harry, if you’re not going to watch at normal speed, you’re going to miss things!"
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: Well, of course, if you don't watch at normal speed you're going to miss things, so stop faffing and watch properly

Book4-chapter8_Sc6.source: "Hermione, who was dancing up and down, waving her arms in the air..."
Book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: I was bouncing around because Troy was doing a lap of honor and it was brilliant

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Hermione gasped and started making suggestions at once, mentioning a number of reference books, and everybody from Albus Dumbledore to Madam Pomfrey, the Hogwarts nurse."
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: Well, of course I thought of reference books and everyone who might help, from Dumbledore to Madam Pomfrey.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Oh Harry, you aren't going to pay attention to anything that old fraud says?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: Obviously I think Professor Trelawney is a fraud and I can't believe anyone would take her seriously.

Book4-chapter9_Sc6.source: Hermione left the room, muttering something that sounded very much like "Boys."
Book4-chapter9_Sc6.description: Well, boys. Honestly, I can't be dealing with their nonsense right now.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Why were you asking if Hedwig had come, Harry?" Hermione asked. "Are you expecting a letter?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Well, I'm asking sensible questions. I wondered if Harry was expecting a letter from Sirius because Hedwig might bring one.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "But we don't know where Sirius is . . . he could be in Africa or somewhere, couldn't he?" said Hermione reasonably. "Hedwig's not going to manage that journey in a few days."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Of course Sirius could be anywhere like Africa. Hedwig couldn't possibly make that trip in just a few days.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Ron," said Hermione, in an I-don't-think-you're-being-very-sensitive sort of voice, "Harry doesn't want to play Quidditch right now. . . . He's worried, and he's tired. . . . We all need to go to bed. . . ."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Well, Harry is clearly upset and tired. We shouldn't be pushing him to play Quidditch tonight.

Book4-chapter9_Sc8.source: Hermione was immersed in The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4, copies of which Mrs Weasley had bought for her, Harry, and Ron in Diagon Alley.
Book4-chapter9_Sc8.description: Well, of course I'm buried in The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4. Mrs Weasley bought copies for me, Harry, and Ron in Diagon Alley.

Book4-chapter10_Sc4.source: [After half an hour or so, Hermione, growing tired of the endless Quidditch talk, buried herself once more in The]
Book4-chapter10_Sc4.description: Well, obviously I am tired of endless Quidditch chatter. Of course I buried myself in a book to get away from it.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "There are house-elves here?" she said, staring, horror-struck, at Nearly Headless Nick.
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: Well, of course there are house-elves at Hogwarts. Over a hundred, apparently, living mostly in the kitchens.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "They get paid?" she said. "They get holidays, don’t they? And — and sick leave, and pensions, and everything?"
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: This is slave labor. I can't just sit and eat when people are being treated like that. Of course I refuse to eat.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "They come out at night to do a bit of cleaning . . . see to the fires and so on."
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: Obviously house-elves work mostly unseen. They do the cleaning and fires at times students don't see.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: "Oooh, I wouldn't fancy crossing the lake in this weather," said Hermione fervently, shivering as they inched slowly along the dark platform with the rest of the crowd.
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: Well, of course I wouldn't fancy crossing the lake in this weather. It's freezing and absolutely pouring.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: Hermione bundled up Crookshanks in her cloak
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: I wrapped Crookshanks in my cloak to keep him dry and warm. Obviously I wasn't going to let him get soaked.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Lots of homework?" said Hermione brightly, catching up with them.
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: Well, Professor Trelawney gave us piles of work. Of course I noticed it and I'm thinking about how to get it done properly.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: both he and Hermione had grabbed the back of Ron’s robes to stop him from launching himself at Malfoy
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: Of course I'm going to stop Ron from diving in. I won't let him make a fool of himself or get hurt. Someone has to be sensible.

Book4-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Shh!" Hermione whispered suddenly, pressing her finger to her lips and pointing toward the compartment next to theirs.
Book4-chapter10_Sc2.description: Well, be quiet, of course. We need to listen to what's being said in the next compartment.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Anyone else know one? Another illegal curse?"
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: Well, the Unforgivable Curses are illegal and extremely dangerous. We have to take them seriously.
Of course I can't stand watching needless cruelty. You don't just let people suffer, even if it's to demonstrate a point.
Well, the Cruciatus Curse actually causes real, unbearable pain. It's not just scary, it's horrific.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Oh no, not necessarily, Parvati Patil’s twin’s in Ravenclaw, and they’re identical. You’d think they’d be together, wouldn’t you?
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: Well, siblings don't always get sorted together. Obviously identical twins can end up in different Houses.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Where’s the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher?
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: Where's the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher? Of course it's important we have one. We've never had one last more than three terms so it's worrying.
Of course, maybe they couldn't get anyone to take the job. That explains why there's no new face at the staff table.

Book4-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Thanks for having us to stay, Mrs. Weasley," said Hermione as they climbed on board.
Book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, thank you for having us. Mrs Weasley looked after us properly and I’m grateful for her hospitality.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Yes," said Hermione sniffily, "and it's got a horrible reputation. According to An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe, it puts a lot of emphasis on the Dark Arts."
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: Of course Durmstrang has a bad rep. According to the proper sources, they focus on the Dark Arts a lot more than Hogwarts does.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "There's traditionally been a lot of rivalry between all the magic schools. Durmstrang and Beauxbatons like to conceal their whereabouts so nobody can steal their secrets," said Hermione matter-of-factly.
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, schools keep themselves hidden to protect their secrets. It makes sense they would conceal where they are.
Obviously Hogwarts is bewitched so Muggles just see a ruin. Other schools do similar things, like Muggle-repelling charms or making a place Unplottable.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "But I think Durmstrang must be somewhere in the far north," said Hermione thoughtfully. "Somewhere very cold, because they've got fur capes as part of their uniforms."
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: I reckon Durmstrang is way up north. Those fur capes mean it's built for freezing weather.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "He could have really hurt Malfoy, though," she said. "It was good, really, that Professor McGonagall stopped it —"
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Well, of course it was right that McGonagall stopped Moody. Turning a student into an animal could have done real harm.
Obviously Draco got humiliated by being turned into a ferret. It was disgraceful even if some people think it's funny.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Got to," said Hermione thickly. "Loads to do."
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: I've got a ton of work to do tonight. No choice, even with all this excitement.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Either explain what you’re on about or go away, Malfoy," said Hermione testily, over the top of The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: Well, I told Malfoy to be sensible and either say what he means or go. I won't stand for pointless provocation.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Don’t let Malfoy get to you, Ron —"
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: Of course I think Ron shouldn't let Malfoy wind him up. I'm worried about how much it's upsetting him.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: She pulled out her wand, muttered "Reparo!" and the glass shards flew back into a single pane and back into the door.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: Obviously I fixed the broken glass. I won't let messes like that stay broken when I can sort them.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Of course I was in the library. That's where I go to prepare, so I arrived just in time for Moody's lesson.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: Hermione teaching Neville a Scouring Charm to remove the toad guts from under his fingernails.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: I helped Neville with a Scouring Charm to get horned toad guts out from under his nails. Practical magic like that matters.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Hurry up," she said tensely to Harry and Ron.
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Well, we need to keep moving and not dawdle. Of course I get impatient when things drag.
Neville’s clearly shaken. Of course I check on him. Someone has to be sensible and look after him.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "What does it say?" "He’s flying north?" "He’s coming back?"
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Obviously Dumbledore being alerted is serious. If people think I or Harry are in danger then things could escalate quickly.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: Well, of course I said the name. I wanted everyone to know what the worst curse is. It's terrifying to even whisper it but we have to be able to name it if we're going to fight it.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: "But — but you said it’s illegal, Professor," said Hermione uncertainly as Moody cleared away the desks with a sweep of his wand
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, Professor, you said it was illegal to use the Imperius on someone. Of course I thought we shouldn't be doing this, and I'm not sure I like being told to sit here for it.

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: Hermione went very pink and muttered something about not meaning that she wanted to leave.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: Of course I don't want to leave. I'd rather not look stupid but I also don't want to miss the lesson. Honestly, I'd stay for this even if it's risky.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [What happened to him? What happened to his face?]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, Moody looks terrible. Of course I'm worried about what happened to him.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [There have been several attempts over the centuries to reinstate the tournament, none of which has been very successful.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Of course the Triwizard's dangerous. There were attempts to bring it back before and they failed because it was too deadly.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [This is due to an event that will be starting in October, and continuing throughout the school year, taking up much of the teachers’ time and energy — but I am sure you will all enjoy it immensely.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, if the teachers are tied up with this all year then lessons and routines will change around the tournament.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [People have died, though!]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: People have died in the Triwizard before. Of course that worries me.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [I will personally be ensuring that no underage student hoodwinks our impartial judge into making them Hogwarts champion.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Dumbledore says he'll make sure underage students don't get in. Obviously he cares about our safety.

Book4-chapter16_Sc4.source: "But Harry set Dobby free, and he was over the moon about it!" said Hermione. "And we heard he’s asking for wages now!"
Book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: Well, Harry did free Dobby and Dobby was absolutely over the moon about it. Of course we've heard Dobby is even asking for wages now, so house-elves can want freedom and fair treatment.

Book4-chapter16_Sc4.source: "for he flatly refused to join S.P.E.W. when she showed him her badges. 'It’d be doin’ ’em an unkindness, Hermione,' he said gravely, threading a massive bone needle with thick yellow yarn."
Book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: Obviously Hagrid thinks most house-elves prefer serving humans and that trying to force freedom on them would be cruel. I can't get him to join S.P.E.W. because he genuinely believes taking away their work would make them unhappy.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Is that aftershave?" "Er — eau de cologne," Hagrid muttered.
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: Is that aftershave? Well, it's eau de cologne then. Hagrid's trying to smarten up and it's obvious he thinks it'll help.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "He’s going up to the castle with her!" "I thought he was waiting for us!"
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: He’s actually going up to the castle with Madame Maxime. I thought he was waiting for us, of course I did.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Oh look, they’re all disappointed," Hermione said over the noise, nodding toward the remainder of the Beauxbatons party.
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, look at them. Of course the girls who weren't chosen are upset. It's obvious they're disappointed.
So do I want it to be Angelina. I was actually hoping it's her as much as anyone else.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “Hedwig’ll attract too much attention,” said Hermione at once.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: Of course Hedwig would stand out. A snowy owl turning up at every hiding place is going to draw attention, and that's exactly the last thing we want.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “You can’t Apparate inside the Hogwarts grounds, how often do I have to tell you?” said Hermione impatiently.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: You can't Apparate on Hogwarts grounds. I am telling you this because it's basic rules and it matters if we're guessing how visitors arrive.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “Oh don’t say that,” said Hermione with a shudder.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: Imagine Hagrid's creatures loose on the grounds. That's not funny. That would be a proper disaster and I'm genuinely worried about it.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: Well, I shouted to warn Harry to stop before he did something rash. Of course I try to be sensible even when things get heated.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Look!" He forced Hermione to show Snape her teeth — she was doing her best to hide them with her hands, though this was difficult as they had now grown down past her collar.
Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: Of course I was humiliated. My teeth grew and I tried to cover them. I couldn’t stand being shown off for others to laugh at.
Obviously Snape could not care less about what’s happening to me. He saw my changed teeth and treated it like nothing, and that hurt.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: House-elves are being treated like slaves and that is completely wrong. Of course we're colluding in their oppression.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "It’s all in Hogwarts: A History. Though, of course, that book’s not entirely reliable. A Revised History of Hogwarts would be a more accurate title. Or A Highly Biased and Selective History of Hogwarts, Which Glosses Over the Nastier Aspects of the School."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Hogwarts: A History contains information about past incidents like the Tournament of 1792, but the book is biased and misses the nasty bits. Obviously you have to read widely.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "You do realize that your sheets are changed, your fires lit, your classrooms cleaned, and your food cooked by a group of magical creatures who are unpaid and enslaved?"
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: We rely on house-elves for everything around the school and they are unpaid and enslaved. That is unacceptable and I am going to do something about it.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "She had also taken to rattling around the Gryffindor common room every evening, cornering people and shaking the collecting tin under their noses."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I have been campaigning constantly for S.P.E.W. I go around asking people for donations and trying to convince them to care.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Well, of course I knew you hadn’t entered yourself," she said when he’d finished telling her about the scene in the chamber off the Hall.
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, of course I knew you hadn't put your own name in the Goblet.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "The look on your face when Dumbledore read out your name!"
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Obviously the look on your face when Dumbledore read your name proved you didn't enter yourself.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "But the question is, who did put it in? Because Moody’s right, Harry . . . I don’t think any student could have done it . . . they’d never be able to fool the goblet, or get over Dumbledore’s —"
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, I don't think any student could have fixed the Goblet or tricked Dumbledore. Someone else must have done it.
Oh Harry, isn't it obvious? Ron's jealous. He's always in your shadow and this is probably too much for him.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "I know it’s not your fault," she added quickly, "I know you don’t ask for it . . . but — well — you know, Ron’s got all those brothers to compete against at home, and you’re his best friend, and you’re really famous — he’s always shunted to one side whenever people see you, and he puts up with it, and he never mentions it, but I suppose this is just one time too many."
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: Look, I know it's not your fault and you don't want the attention. Ron has loads of brothers to compete with at home and he feels pushed aside when people fawn over you. That must be getting to him.

Book4-chapter18_Sc1.source: "I’m not telling him anything," Hermione said shortly. "Tell him yourself."
Book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm not going to tell Ron for you. Tell him yourself.

Book4-chapter19_Sc3.source: "Yeah, it can see through Invisibility Cloaks," Moody said quietly.
Book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: Well, obviously Moody's magical eye can see through Invisibility Cloaks. That explains how he spotted Potter.
Hello, I said, smiling. I was being polite and keeping things calm at the table.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "I’m not sure this is going to work, you know," said Hermione warningly. "I’m sure Dumbledore will have thought of this."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Well, of course I think Dumbledore would have anticipated people trying to trick the Goblet. That plan sounded unlikely to me from the start.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Well, I’m glad someone from Gryffindor’s entering," said Hermione. "I really hope you get it, Angelina!"
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Of course I want a Gryffindor in the Tournament. I genuinely hope Angelina gets selected.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "I’ve just realized — I haven’t asked Hagrid to join S.P.E.W. yet!" she said brightly. "Wait for me, will you, while I nip upstairs and get the badges?"
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Obviously I want Hagrid to join S.P.E.W. I need to fetch badges and I expect Ron and Harry to wait while I do it.

Book4-chapter19_Sc5.source: Then Hermione opened the Fat Lady for him from outside as they had planned.
Book4-chapter19_Sc5.description: Well of course I opened the Fat Lady for Harry. Obviously we agreed the sensible thing to do, and I was going to help him.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Write to Sirius. You’ve got to tell him what’s happened. He asked you to keep him posted on everything that’s going on at Hogwarts. . . ."
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: Of course we must write to Sirius. He asked Harry to keep him updated on Hogwarts, so he needs to know about the tournament straight away.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I brought some parchment and a quill out with me —"
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: Well, I came prepared. I have parchment and a quill ready so Harry can write to Sirius right now.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Harry, this isn’t going to be kept quiet," said Hermione, very seriously.
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: This is famous and it's not going to stay secret. People will find out about Harry in the papers, so he should hear it from Harry first.
Sirius will learn about Harry's involvement one way or another, so it's better Harry tells him directly.
Obviously we could borrow an owl from Ron or use a school owl. There's always a way to send a message.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: Well, I hadn't realized Hagrid had asked you. That surprises me.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.source: I wonder what he’s up to? I don’t know whether you should go, Harry. . . .
Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: Well, obviously I'm worried. I don't know what Hagrid's plan is and I don't think you should rush off to a secret meeting without thinking it through.

Book4-chapter19_Sc4.source: It might make you late for Sirius.
Book4-chapter19_Sc4.description: Of course I'm worried you'll miss your chance to see Sirius if you go to Hagrid's midnight meeting. I'm thinking about practical consequences.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: Oh well, I thought maybe we'd meet up with Ron in the Three Broomsticks, but I'm clearly uncomfortable about the idea.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: Oh Harry, this is so stupid —
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: Of course I think this is ridiculous; hiding and not speaking properly to Harry when he's under the Cloak is infuriating.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: I hate talking to you in that Cloak, I never know if I’m looking at you or not.
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I can't stand talking to someone when I can't tell where they are; it drives me mad not knowing if I'm looking at them.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: I look like such an idiot, sitting here on my own, Lucky I brought something to do.
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I feel foolish sitting alone, so I keep busy; I brought my S.P.E.W. notebook and I've been keeping track of members.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: When house-elves have decent wages and working conditions!
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: Of course I'll stop campaigning only when house-elves actually have fair pay and decent working conditions; I'm not giving up.

Book4-chapter19_Sc1.source: You know, I’m starting to think it’s time for more direct action. I wonder how you get into the school kitchens?
Book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I'm thinking we need to do more than paperwork; I want to involve the villagers and maybe even get into the kitchens to speak to house-elves directly.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: Well, obviously if you concentrate properly the Summoning Charm will work. You have to focus every single time.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Harry, I really think you've got it!"
Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: Well, of course he can learn this quickly when he applies himself. I believe he has it now if he keeps practicing.

Book4-chapter20_Sc3.source: "We'd better get some sleep . . . you're going to need it."
Book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: Well, I look out for Harry. I'm not going to let him wear himself out; he needs rest as much as practice and I'll tell him so.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Well, of course I thought he was brilliant, he did exactly what needed doing and got the egg. I was terrified but he handled it perfectly.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: Hermione had "fingernail marks on her face where she had been clutching it in fear."
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Obviously I was terrified watching, biting my nails and clinging to my face, because it was dangerous, but I knew Harry could do it.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: He’s supposed to work out the clue on his own,
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, of course, the tournament rules say Harry must work out the clue on his own. That is how it is supposed to be.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: How do you get in there?
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: Obviously, Fred said there is a concealed door behind a painting in the kitchens. You tickle the pear and it opens. That is how they get in.

Book4-chapter21_Sc1.source: Nothing, said Hermione quickly. Going to try and lead the house-elves out on strike now, are you? said George.
Book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, I was suspicious about how Fred and George got sweets from the kitchens, and I was worried about upsetting the house-elves. I wasn't going to encourage them to go on strike or anything like that.
Of course I stepped on Harry's foot by accident when I moved. Sorry Harry, but it was an accident.

Book4-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Just as long as he didn’t import those skrewts illegally or anything," said Hermione desperately.
Book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: Well, as long as he hasn't imported those skrewts illegally, we're fine. Of course if he did, that would be really bad.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "'Talon-clipping by charms . . . treating scale-rot . . .' This is no good, this is for nutters like Hagrid who want to keep them healthy. . . ."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Well, books about talon-clipping and treating scale-rot are about dragon care, not about getting past them. Obviously not useful for the task.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "'Dragons are extremely difficult to slay, owing to the ancient magic that imbues their thick hides, which none but the most powerful spells can penetrate . . .'"
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Of course dragons have thick hides and ancient magic that makes them hard to injure. That means most spells probably won't work.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Well, there are Switching Spells . . . but what's the point of Switching it? Unless you swapped its fangs for wine-gums or something that would make it less dangerous. . . ."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Well, switching spells could change a dragon's parts, but swapping dangerous things for harmless ones is the only sensible use I can see.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "I'd say Transfigure it, but something that big, you really haven't got a hope, I doubt even Professor McGonagall . . . unless you're supposed to put the spell on yourself? Maybe to give yourself extra powers? But they're not simple spells, I mean, we haven't done any of those in class, I only know about them because I've been doing O.W.L. practice papers. . . ."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Obviously transfiguring a dragon is beyond us, unless the trick is to enchant yourself instead. But those are advanced spells we haven't learned properly.

Book4-chapter20_Sc1.source: "'Oh no, he's back again, why can't he read on his stupid ship?' said Hermione irritably as Viktor Krum slouched in..."
Book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: Of course I'm irritated when people interrupt. Viktor Krum reading in the library is distracting and I don't like it.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.source: Mmm . . . you’re not exactly straining yourself, though, are you?
Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: Well, obviously Harry is taking a break and not working as hard as he should on his schoolwork.
Of course the golden egg matters. If Harry doesn't start working on it he'll look like an idiot when everyone else knows what the task is.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.source: Leave him alone, Hermione, he’s earned a bit of a break
Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: Well, I know Ron will defend Harry. I can't argue with him wanting a rest but I still think Harry ought to be sensible about the egg.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.source: ["What's he avoiding us for?" "He surely doesn't think we'd care about him being half-giant?"]
Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: Well, Hagrid's not answering either, and I can't see why he'd be avoiding us. Of course we care about him being half-giant, so something else must be up.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.source: [But it seemed that Hagrid did care. They didn't see a sign of him all week.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: Obviously he's bothered by this. If he's keeping away all week, there's a reason, and I want to figure out what it is.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "He hasn’t asked me one single thing about Harry, not one —"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Of course he hasn't been asking me about Harry. I would not help anyone use me to spy on Harry.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "I want Harry to win the tournament, Harry knows that, don’t you, Harry?"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I want Harry to win. That's why I'm talking to Krum about accompanying me, nothing more.
Call him what you like but I will not stand being mocked. I will not be called 'Vicky' and I won't tolerate that tone.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Next time there’s a ball, ask me before someone else does, and not as a last resort!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: If someone wants to dance with me properly, they should ask me first. I won't be treated like a backup plan.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "But he’s right, Harry," said Hermione, "you have still got two tasks to do. You really ought to have a look at that egg, you know, and start working out what it means."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Well, of course you have two tasks left and you should examine the egg now. It all makes sense if you start working it out properly.
Of course I greeted Harry. I may be nervous but I still want to be polite and supportive.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "She had done something with her hair; it was no longer bushy but sleek and shiny, and twisted up into an elegant knot at the back of her head."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Obviously I tidied my hair and dressed up for the ball. Yes, I look different when I make an effort and I know exactly how to do it.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "She was also smiling — rather nervously, it was true — but the reduction in the size of her front teeth was more noticeable than ever; Harry couldn’t understand how he hadn’t spotted it before."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Well, I was nervous but I wanted to look presentable. Of course I noticed small things about myself that change how others see me.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: You horrible woman," she said, through gritted teeth, "you don't care, do you, anything for a story, and anyone will do, won't they?
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: Of course she only cares about a story. She'll use anyone and anything to get a scoop and she doesn't care who gets hurt.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: She'll be after you next, Hermione," said Ron in a low and worried voice as they walked quickly back up the street. "Let her try!" said Hermione defiantly; she was shaking with rage.
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: Let her try! I am not going to hide or be silenced. If Rita targets Harry or Hagrid I will fight back.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: And Hagrid isn't hiding anymore! He should never have let that excuse for a human being upset him! Come on!
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: Hagrid isn't going to cower. He's out and I won't let anyone make him retreat. He's a friend and I will protect him.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “We — er — we wanted to see Hagrid,” said Hermione in a rather small voice.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Well, of course I wanted to see Hagrid. We care about him and we wanted to make sure he was all right.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “Come back and teach, Hagrid,” said Hermione quietly, “please come back, we really miss you.”
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Obviously I want Hagrid back at school. He teaches and matters to us and I do miss him when he's gone.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: Hermione went slightly pink, but Dumbledore smiled at her and continued, “Hermione, Harry, and Ron still seem to want to know you, judging by the way they were attempting to break down the door.”
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Well, I know we're not the sort to give up on people. We tried to get in because we were worried for Hagrid.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: It’s a lot colder where he comes from. I suppose it feels quite warm to him.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Well, of course Krum would find this warmer. He comes from a much colder place so this is easier for him.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: They’d normally deal with the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Well, goblins usually work with the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures. It is odd they are here looking for Crouch.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: He’s one of the judges! And anyway, you’ve already worked it out — haven’t you?
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Obviously Bagman trying to help a champion is wrong. He is a judge so offering to give clues would be cheating and I am shocked he even suggested it.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “That’s not very much!” Hermione shouted indignantly from the floor, over Winky’s continued screaming and fist-beating.
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: That pay is nothing. Of course it's not enough for someone who's been treated like that.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Professor Dumbledore offered Dobby ten Galleons a week, and weekends off,” said Dobby, suddenly giving a little shiver
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Dumbledore actually offered Dobby much more, but Dobby turned it down because he prefers work and values his freedom more than money.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “Winky,” said Hermione firmly, “I’m quite sure Mr Crouch is getting along perfectly well without you. We’ve seen him, you know —”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Winky will manage. Once she settles at Hogwarts she'll realize being free is better than clinging to shame for a master who mistreated her.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “I think this is the best thing that could have happened to those elves, you know,” said Hermione, leading the way back up the marble staircase.
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Dobby being free and visible here will show the other house-elves that freedom is an option. Of course they might not change overnight but this is a start.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Well, I told them I\'m going with someone else. Of course I said that to get Neville off my back. I am not coming with Ron or Harry.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Just because it\'s taken you three years to notice, Ron, doesn\'t mean no one else has spotted I\'m a girl!"
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Of course everyone sees I\'m a girl now. Well, obviously. I don\'t need anyone to point it out.
I arrived late to dinner because I had to sort something out. People were already making a fuss about who they\'d asked to the ball.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: Well, of course I comforted Hagrid. I wanted him to know we were there for him and that he shouldn't beat himself up.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Good luck, Harry," Hermione whispered. "You’ll be fine!"
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: Well, good luck, Harry. Of course you'll be fine, I really mean it, try to keep calm.

Book4-chapter20_Sc4.source: She didn’t seem herself either; in fact, she looked nearly as anxious as Hermione.
Book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I'm anxious about Harry. I can't hide it. He needs reassurance and I want to give it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: The ropes of weed tying the hostages to the statue were thick, slimy, and very strong.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: Well, these weeds are ridiculously strong and slippery. Tugging harder isn't going to cut it. We need a proper way to get free.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang.
