Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: Obviously Ron is beside me, and we're all bound together. I can't let him be left there, I have to stay calm and think how to help.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "He asked me if I wasn't doing anything over the summer, would I like to —" "And he did say he'd never felt the same way about anyone else"
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: Well, Viktor Krum actually asked me to visit him in Bulgaria over the summer and said he had never felt this way about anyone else. I went bright red when I told Ron about it.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "If that's the best Rita can do, she's losing her touch," "What a pile of old rubbish."
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: Obviously Rita Skeeter wrote a ridiculous article about me making me look scandalous. It's absolute rubbish and I think she's making things up.

Book4-chapter26_Sc6.source: Cho’s head was on Hermione’s shoulder; the small silver-haired girl was ghostly green and pale.
Book4-chapter26_Sc6.description: Well, of course I'm terrified and weak right now. Cho's leaning on me and she's clearly ill. I need help fast.

Book4-chapter26_Sc8.source: Within seconds, he had done it; he grabbed Hermione around the waist, and without a backward glance, began to rise rapidly with her toward the surface.
Book4-chapter26_Sc8.description: Well, of course Krum cut me free and hauled me up. I'm being taken to the surface now. I need to stay calm and let him get me up.

Book4-chapter29_Sc1.source: "What, at this time?" said Hermione and Fred.
Book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: Well, of course it's odd to be sending letters at this hour. Who sends a letter now unless it's important or suspicious?

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: She seized Harry and pulled him over to Hermione and the others, wrapped him so tightly in a blanket that he felt as though he were in a straitjacket, and forced a measure of very hot potion down his throat.
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Of course I was there at the bank with the others. I helped make sure Harry was wrapped up and safe as soon as he was out of the water.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: She seized Harry and pulled him over to Hermione and the others
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Well, obviously I was worried. He was soaked and exhausted so I stayed right with him and the others to make sure he was all right.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "You said you’d already worked out that egg clue!" said Hermione indignantly.
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Well, I know you worked out the egg clue already. Don't pretend you haven't thought about it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore's not stupid. He was right to trust Hagrid and Professor Lupin, even though loads of people wouldn't have given them jobs, so why shouldn't he be right about Snape, even if Snape is a bit —"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Of course Dumbledore can judge character. He was right about Hagrid and Lupin, so I don't see why he wouldn't be right about Snape even if Snape is unpleasant.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "We thought Snape was trying to kill Harry before, and it turned out he was saving Harry’s life, remember?"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Obviously Snape has acted in ways that looked dangerous but actually saved Harry. We have to keep that in mind.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Of course, the ideal solution would be for you to Transfigure yourself into a submarine or something," Hermione said.
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Of course human Transfiguration would be perfect, but we do not learn it until sixth year and it can go badly wrong if you do not know what you are doing.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I don't think he’d let you choose what you wanted to be turned into, though," said Hermione seriously.
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I don't think Moody would let you pick what you turned into. Relying on someone else to do it is too uncertain.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: "Harry, well done!" Hermione cried. "You did it, you found out how all by yourself!"
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Well, of course I'm proud of you, Harry. You worked it out on your own and that matters.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: "You’re well outside the time limit, though, Harry. Did it take you ages to find us?"
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Obviously we were over the time limit. I think you took longer than you should have to get back.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Hermione brushed away the beetle impatiently
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Ugh, there's a water beetle in my hair. Get it off, quickly.

Book4-chapter26_Sc2.source: Weekend after next," whispered Hermione, who had read the note over Harry’s shoulder.
Book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: Well, of course I read the note over his shoulder and told him the weekend after next, and I handed him my quill so he could send the owl back straight away.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “It’s more likely he did it than Winky,” said Hermione stubbornly.
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Well, honestly, Winky seems less likely to have conjured the Dark Mark than someone else in that box. Of course it could be Bagman or someone like him rather than the elf.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “She sacked her, just because she hadn’t stayed in her tent and let herself get trampled —”
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Of course he sacked Winky just for the way she was found. He punished his household rather than accept any blame.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “We saw him in the forest just before the Dark Mark appeared,” Hermione told Sirius.
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Well, I remember Bagman being in the forest before the Mark. That makes me think he’s someone to be questioned about what happened.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “Look, I don’t care what you say, Dumbledore trusts Snape —”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Well, of course I trust Dumbledore's judgment. If he trusts Snape, there must be a reason.
Obviously it’s late. We should be heading back to school.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I despise Rita Skeeter and I am determined to get back at her for what she has written about people.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Moody says he didn’t see her anywhere near the judges’ table at the second task, or anywhere near the lake!"
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Moody did not see Rita near the judges or the lake during the second task, so her information must have come from somewhere else.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "All those substitutes for magic Muggles use — electricity, computers, and radar, and all those things — they all go haywire around Hogwarts, there’s too much magic in the air."
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Of course! Muggle tech won't explain Rita's spying because it fails at Hogwarts. It has to be magical eavesdropping instead.
I will take this on by myself. I do not need Ron or Harry to help me with tracking down how Rita sneaks information.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “Listen to me, all of you! You’ve got just as much right as wizards to be unhappy! You’ve got the right to wages and holidays and proper clothes, you don’t have to do everything you’re told — look at Dobby!”
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Well, of course house-elves deserve rights. They should have wages, holidays and proper clothes. It’s obvious they don’t have to accept being treated like they have no choices.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “Winky is getting through six bottles a day now,” Dobby whispered to Harry.
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I can see Winky’s drinking herself silly. She’s going through about six bottles of butterbeer a day and she’s in a dreadful state.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: Hermione told him about the hate mail she had received that morning, and the envelope full of bubotuber pus.
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Someone sent me hate mail and bubotuber pus in the post. It’s nasty and it’s been left me with badly bandaged hands.

Book4-chapter29_Sc3.source: "He’s worried about you!" said Hermione sharply. "Just like Moody and Hagrid! So listen to them!"
Book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: Well, he's worried about you. Of course Moody and Hagrid are worried too, so listen to them and take it seriously.

Book4-chapter29_Sc3.source: "Except put your name in the Goblet of Fire," said Hermione. "And they must’ve done that for a reason, Harry. Snuffles is right. Maybe they’ve been biding their time."
Book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: Someone put your name in the Goblet of Fire, and they did it for a reason. Snuffles is right. They might have been waiting for the right moment.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "You don’t think they know something about all this, do you?" Hermione whispered. "About Crouch and everything?"
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: Well, I can't believe Fred and George would know about Crouch. Of course, if it were that serious someone would have told Dumbledore.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Yes, but . . . they wouldn't do anything against the law to get gold." "Wouldn't they?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: Of course this isn't just a school rule. This is the law. Blackmail is serious and they'd get far more than detention for it.
Well, Percy should be told about anything that even hints at blackmail. He would take it seriously and act on it.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: Narration: "Harry, Ron, and Hermione followed her, looking back over their shoulders at Hagrid’s cabin"
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Well, of course I'm worried. Hagrid's curtains are closed and he isn't answering. Something's obviously not right with him.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: Article text: claims about Hagrid breeding Blast-Ended Skrewts and being part-giant
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Obviously that article is saying Hagrid's been making dangerous creatures and that he's part-giant. It's a nasty piece in the Prophet and it could be damaging whether it's all true or not.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "They couldn’t have made it look like an accident if they’d murdered you in the forest!" said Hermione.
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Well, it wouldn't have looked like an accident if they'd killed me in the forest. That's obvious.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "You can't Disapparate on the Hogwarts grounds, haven't I told you enough times?" said Hermione.
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Of course you can't Disapparate on Hogwarts grounds. I've told you that before and it matters here.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "Well, that was his fault," said Hermione testily.
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Well, I think it was his fault. I can't be sympathetic about that one.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Her-my-oh-nee," she said slowly and clearly. "Herm-own-ninny." "Close enough," she said, catching Harry's eye and grinning.
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Well, I get on with helping Krum say my name properly. Obviously I take care to be patient and clear with him and I even grin when Harry notices.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Viktor's just gone to get some drinks."
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Viktor went off to fetch drinks for us. Of course I didn't make a big thing of it, I just mentioned it because I was warm from dancing.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Yes, he did," said Hermione, the pink patches on her cheeks glowing more brightly. "So what?"
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Of course he asked me to come with him to the library. I blushed about it because it was a bit embarrassing, but it's nothing like what Ron's making out.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Don't be so stupid!" she said after a moment. "The enemy! Honestly — who was the one who was all excited when they saw him arrive? Who was the one who wanted his autograph? Who's got a model of him up in their dormitory?"
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Obviously Ron's being ridiculous. I won't let him turn normal friendly interest into some traitorous thing. I'm not fraternizing with the enemy.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "We need to see Professor Moody," said Hermione.
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: We have to go to Moody and find out what he knows. Of course we need answers now.
Quiet. Someone's coming. We shouldn't be heard.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Rita Skeeter," she muttered finally. "How can you be worrying about her now?"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Well, Rita Skeeter causes trouble. Of course she will spin things to make the situation worse.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "I know things about Ludo Bagman that would make your hair curl.' This is what she meant,"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Obviously Rita's been nosing about scandals like Bagman's trial. She will use anything she finds to make trouble.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "I've been trying!" said Hermione. "I think I know . . . because then no one would be able to see . . . even Moody . . ."
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Right, of course. If Rita got into the window ledge and listened, she must have used a clever magical method to hide herself. I think she could have been bugging the place from a ledge no one should have been able to get onto. I need to check library sources to confirm.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "We haven't done any practicing!" she said, looking shocked. "We were going to do the Impediment Curse!"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: We still have to practice the Impediment Curse properly. I absolutely will make sure we do it tomorrow.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.source: "But — it must’ve been an accident, mustn’t it?" said Hermione.
Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: Well, surely it was just an accident that the gold vanished. Of course you should consider that before assuming the worst.

Book4-chapter36_Sc6.source: Hermione, Ron, and Mrs Weasley were all looking at him. None of them spoke for a very long time.
Book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: Well, of course I'm worried about Harry. I can't just stand by when he's staring at the ceiling like that and not saying anything.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: I found out how she was listening in on private conversations when she wasn’t supposed to be coming onto the grounds
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Well, I found out how Rita was eavesdropping on people when she shouldn't have been. Of course I had to do something about it.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: Rita Skeeter isn’t going to be writing anything at all for a while. Not unless she wants me to spill the beans on her.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Of course I'm not going to let her keep getting away with it. I've caught her, and unless she behaves she's not writing again for a good long while.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: — into a beetle. ... I caught her on the windowsill in the hospital wing. Look very closely, and you’ll notice the markings around her antennae are exactly like those foul glasses she wears.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Obviously, Rita can turn into a beetle. I trapped her in a jar, put an Unbreakable Charm on it so she can't transform, and told her she won't be writing for a year. That should stop her for a bit.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: When we saw Malfoy under that tree ... He was talking to her, in his hand
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Well, it all makes sense now. Malfoy talking to a beetle explains how Rita got slimey interviews from the Slytherins. They were feeding her things because they didn't care about the law.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: “He suffered very little then,” she said, when Harry had told her how Cedric had died. “And after all, Amos . . . he died just when he’d won the tournament. He must have been happy.”
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Well, Cedric didn't suffer much and he died right after winning. Of course it's awful but at least he died having won. That thought helps me a bit.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: When they got to their feet, she looked down at Harry and said, "You look after yourself, now."
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Of course I worry about Harry. I told him to look after himself because I meant it. I won't stop looking out for him.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: Harry, Ron, and Hermione looked up at him, shocked.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Well, Hagrid has known about Voldemort for years and expected his return. That shocked me. It means we can't pretend this is over.

Book5-chapter4_Sc2.source: "HARRY! Ron, he’s here, Harry’s here! We didn’t hear you arrive! Oh, how are you? Are you all right? Have you been furious with us? I bet you have, I know our letters were useless — but we couldn’t tell you anything, Dumbledore made us swear we wouldn’t, oh, we’ve got so much to tell you, and you’ve got to tell us — the dementors! When we heard — and that Ministry hearing — it’s just outrageous, I’ve looked it all up, they can’t expel you, they just can’t, there’s provision in the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for the use of magic in life-threatening situations —"
Book5-chapter4_Sc2.description: Well, of course I’m desperate to know you’re okay. I couldn’t tell you before because Dumbledore made us swear. The dementors and that Ministry hearing were awful but listen, I’ve looked it up: they can’t expel you. There’s a provision in the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for magic used in life-threatening situations, so you’re not out of Hogwarts.

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "I thought that too. But he didn’t want you to know anything."
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: Well, I think Dumbledore made a deliberate choice not to tell you anything
Of course he doesn't think you can't take care of yourself, I'm anxious about the situation but I don't believe Dumbledore doubts you

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "Bill, Ron, and Hermione were staring at Fudge."
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: Of course I can't accept Fudge's denial. Everything Dumbledore, Snape, and Harry are saying fits together logically so I believe them

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "None of them spoke for a very long time."
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: We were all shell-shocked and thinking about what to do next after hearing Voldemort is back and after Crouch died

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Harry, we wanted to tell you, we really did —” Hermione began.
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: Well, we really wanted to tell him. Of course we did. I feel awful for not having managed to tell him properly.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “It’s a secret society,” said Hermione quickly. “Dumbledore’s in charge, he founded it. It’s the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time.”
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: Obviously, the Order of the Phoenix is a secret society. Dumbledore set it up and they're the ones who fought You-Know-Who before.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Harry, we’re really sorry!” said Hermione desperately, her eyes now sparkling with tears.
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: Well, I'm sorry to him. I don't want him to hate us. I care about him and I can't stand seeing him like this.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "No, Harry, the meeting’s only for members of the Order. Ron and Hermione are upstairs, you can wait with them until the meeting’s over..."
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: Well, of course I’m upstairs with Ron waiting. The meeting’s for Order members only so we’re supposed to hold back and be quiet in the hall.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "some of them are working on recruiting more people to the Order —"
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: Of course some people in the Order are trying to recruit more members. That’s what you do when you need support.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "We’ve been decontaminating this house, it’s been empty for ages and stuff’s been breeding in here. We’ve managed to clean out the kitchen, most of the bedrooms, and I think we’re doing the drawing room tomo — AARGH!"
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: We have been cleaning the place out thoroughly. I mean obviously it was filthy and needed sorting, and I’m the one keeping things organised so we actually got a lot done.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "We knew you’d be angry, Harry, we really don’t blame you, but you’ve got to understand, we did try and persuade Dumbledore —"
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: I know Harry’s angry and I don’t blame him. I tried to explain that we did try to persuade Dumbledore so he should understand why we acted the way we did.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "He seemed to think it was best," said Hermione rather breathlessly. "Dumbledore, I mean."
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Well, of course Dumbledore thought I was safest with the Muggles. He was trying to protect me and Harry by keeping things quiet.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Hermione was going spare, she kept saying you’d do something stupid if you were stuck all on your own without news,"
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Obviously I was frantic about Harry being alone. I genuinely believed he'd do something dangerous if he had no information or support.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Aren’t you . . . aren’t you worried about the Ministry of Magic hearing?" said Hermione quietly.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Well, I am worried about the Ministry finding out what happened. I think Harry should care about that too, even if he says he does not.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "The warm glow that had flared inside him at the sight of his two best friends was extinguished as something icy flooded the pit of his stomach."
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Of course I wanted to be reunited properly, but it's clear Harry is upset with us for following Dumbledore's instructions. I feel guilty and frustrated because I was only trying to help.

Book5-chapter6_Sc3.source: Kreacher’s really old, he probably couldn’t manage
Book5-chapter6_Sc3.description: Well, of course I think Kreacher might be too old to have done everything people blame him for. Don’t be quick to condemn him.

Book5-chapter6_Sc3.source: Hermione’s face was half concealed by a tea towel but Harry distinctly saw her throw a reproachful look at Mrs. Weasley at these words.
Book5-chapter6_Sc3.description: Obviously I’m not afraid to show my disapproval when someone jumps to conclusions about a house-elf.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: This is Harry, Kreacher, Harry Potter.
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: Of course I told Kreacher who Harry is, because he needed to know that the famous Harry Potter was right there.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: Sirius, he’s not right in the head, I don’t think he realizes we can hear him.
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: I think Kreacher's muddled and talking to himself. He might not understand people can hear him, so we shouldn't assume he's malicious in the normal way.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.source: If you just set him free, maybe
Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: I honestly hoped setting Kreacher free might help him. I wanted to try the humane option even if others said it was impossible.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I asked Ron and Hermione but they said we’re not allowed in the Order, so —"
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: We told Harry he couldn’t be in the Order. I agreed with that at the time. Of course, I wanted him safe and that’s why we kept him out of it.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: Tonks was entertaining Hermione and Ginny by transforming her nose between mouthfuls. "Do that one like a pig snout, Tonks . . ."
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: I was distracted and amused by Tonks showing off her nose tricks. It was a ridiculous way to pass the time but it cheered us up.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "We’ve got a busy day tomorrow. I expect Ginny’s asleep," she added to Hermione, "so try not to wake her up."
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: Well, of course Ginny should be asleep. Try not to wake her, alright?

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: after Hermione bade them good night
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: Well, good night then. I'm saying good night because people are meant to actually go to bed.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "’Course I will," Harry said. Ron and Hermione beamed.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Of course we should all share what we know. I’m glad Harry will tell Ron and me.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Because accepting that Voldemort’s back would mean trouble like the Ministry hasn’t had to cope with for nearly fourteen years," said Sirius bitterly.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: If Voldemort’s back then everyone will have to face a mess the Ministry hasn’t handled in years. We can’t ignore that.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: It's not 'spew', obviously. I think people should take the whole thing seriously.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: It's the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare, and it's not just me, Dumbledore says we should be kind to Kreacher too
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: The group is called the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare. Dumbledore says we should be kind to Kreacher too, so of course I defend him.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: And don't forget to keep your voice down in the hall, Harry
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: We must keep our voices down in the hall. Be quiet and stay sharp.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "They were bound to clear you," said Hermione, who had looked positively faint with anxiety when Harry had entered the kitchen
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Of course they had to clear you. There was no case against you. It was obvious from the evidence.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Don't you go feeling guilty!" said Hermione sternly
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: You belong at Hogwarts and you must not feel guilty. Sirius is being a bit selfish about wanting you to stay here but you should be at school.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "He just didn't want to get his own hopes up even more," said Hermione wisely.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Sirius kept quiet because he did not want to build his hopes higher. He was trying not to get disappointed by getting his hopes up.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "You know, maybe it wouldn't be a bad idea to show people exactly how horrible it is to clean all the time - we could do a sponsored scrub of Gryffindor common room, all proceeds to S.P.E.W., it would raise awareness as well as funds -"
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: We should raise awareness for house-elf rights. Doing a sponsored clean would show people how awful it is and we could raise money for S.P.E.W. Obviously we must act.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Me too, Harry, me too!" She spotted the badge in Harry's hand and let out a shriek.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: I got my Hogwarts letter and I am going back this year. I am excited and I want to help with everything, especially making sure Ron is okay about his new responsibilities.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "You don’t think he’s . . . hurt, or anything, do you?"
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, I worry Hagrid might be hurt if he's not here. I want to know what's happened to him.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "She was at my hearing, she works for Fudge!"
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: Of course, Umbridge was at my hearing and she works for Fudge. That explains why I recognize her.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "What on earth’s she doing here, then?"
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: What on earth is Umbridge doing at Hogwarts? It doesn't make sense that she's sitting at the staff table.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "I wonder if it’s ever given warnings before?"
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, the Sorting Hat sounded like it was warning the school. That made me anxious about what it meant.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Of course not," said Hermione scathingly, before Harry could answer, "The Quibbler's rubbish, everyone knows that."
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Well, the Quibbler is rubbish. Obviously it prints daft stories and you shouldn't treat it as reliable evidence.
Well, I won't stand for Malfoy's sneering. I stepped in to shut him up because he was being obnoxious and trying to rile us.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: Hermione slammed the compartment door behind them and turned to look at Harry, who knew at once that she, like him, had registered what Malfoy had said and been just as unnerved by it.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Obviously Malfoy's comment about dogging struck a nerve. I got unnerved too and I want to treat this seriously rather than laugh it off.
Well, I made them leave because we needed privacy and I was worried about what Malfoy might have overheard or realised.

Book5-chapter11_Sc3.description: Well, of course I'm revolted by that. The idea of a hat deciding things and everyone being cheery about it is gross.

Book5-chapter11_Sc5.source: "First years!" Hermione called commandingly along the table. "This way, please!"
Book5-chapter11_Sc5.description: Of course I called them over and told them where to go. Someone has to be sensible about guiding the new students.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Mum and Dad just sent Hedwig back"
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, my parents sent Hedwig back so I have to bring her cage along. Of course I want her safe.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Mrs Weasley’s patched her up," said Hermione.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Ginny's been patched up by Mum. Obviously she's shaken but she'll be all right.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "But now Mad-Eye’s complaining that we can’t leave unless Sturgis Podmore’s here, otherwise the guard will be one short."
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Mad eye says we must wait for Sturgis Podmore or the guard will be one short. So we are waiting because of security procedures.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "You have to go to King’s Cross with a guard," Hermione corrected him.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Of course we need a guard for the journey. It isn't paranoia, it's what Mad eye insists on and we follow his orders.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "I don't think we'll have to stay there all journey," said Hermione quickly.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, Ron and I are prefects so we have to go to the carriage for some instructions but it should not ruin our whole trip together. I still want to stick with Harry where possible.

Book5-chapter11_Sc4.source: "Nick, he wasn’t really laughing at you!"
Book5-chapter11_Sc4.description: Well, of course I defend people when they're being unfairly mocked. I wasn't going to let Ron make Nick feel worse about his death.
Obviously the speech wasn't just empty words. It explained a lot and made things line up in my head about what's been going on.

Book5-chapter11_Sc4.source: "It means the Ministry’s interfering at Hogwarts."
Book5-chapter11_Sc4.description: It means the Ministry is interfering at Hogwarts. Of course that changes everything about how the school is being run.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: It’s best to know what the enemy are saying
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Of course I keep up with what people are saying. You have to know the facts even if it’s unpleasant.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: You can’t advertise for testers on the Gryffindor notice board
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Obviously rules matter. I won’t let the noticeboard be used for that nonsense and I’ll say so.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: If I refused to lend you my notes this year?
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: My notes are crucial. I could make them fail their O.W.L.s if I wanted but that would be petty so I’ll keep helping, though I won’t be happy about them not trying.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: I think I’d really like to do something worthwhile. I mean, if I could take S.P.E.W. further
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: I want a job that actually makes a difference. Helping causes like S.P.E.W. matters to me and I’m thinking about turning that into real work.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "We'd better change," said Hermione at last.
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Well, of course I knew Hermione wanted everyone to get changed and ready. She pins on her prefect badge properly and expects the same of others.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Malfoy was being absolutely foul to a first year back there, I swear I'm going to report him, he's only had his badge three minutes and he's using it to bully people worse than ever."
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Well, Hermione is furious about Malfoy bullying younger students and she's ready to take action and report him.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Come on, let's get a carriage together before they all fill up"
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Of course Hermione wants us to get organized quickly. She's practical and moves straight away to secure seats.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: Well, there are two fifth-year prefects from each House, Boy and girl from each.
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, of course there are two prefects from each House. It's the rules. It matters who they pick.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: And that complete cow Pansy Parkinson, How she got to be a prefect when she’s thicker than a concussed troll
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: How Pansy became a prefect is ridiculous. Obviously she shouldn't be one if she can't do the job properly.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: Who’s Hufflepuff? Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott are the Hufflepuff prefects. Of course I remembered who belongs where.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: You’re not supposed to abuse your position, Ron!
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Obviously prefects are not meant to bully students. Of course I worry Ron might take it the wrong way.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Don’t pay any attention to them, Ron, they’re only jealous!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, I told Ron not to mind Fred and George. Of course I'm defending him because he deserves the praise and it's important to be supportive.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Thanks," said Hermione. "Erm — Harry — could I borrow Hedwig so I can tell Mum and Dad? They’ll be really pleased — I mean, prefect is something they can understand —"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, I wanted to tell my parents about Ron's prefect badge at once because it's the sort of thing they'll understand and be proud of.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: Hermione and Hedwig had gone. Harry returned slowly to his bed and sank onto it, gazing unseeingly at the foot of the wardrobe.
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course I wanted to share the good news quickly. I think small things like a prefect badge matter to families and we should celebrate them.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, of course we didn't completely get frightened into thinking we'd be attacked every day. We actually learned things that mattered.
Harry, obviously, don't make this worse. Keep your temper under control even if it's unfair.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "Your hand is not up, Miss Granger!"
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Umbridge will shut people down and bully her way through class. We have to be smart about how we respond or she'll punish us.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "How can Dumbledore have let this happen?" Hermione cried suddenly, making Harry and Ron jump;
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: How could Dumbledore let someone like her teach us? That's just not right.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Yes, but to employ someone who’s actually refusing to let us do magic! What’s Dumbledore playing at?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: Obviously it's outrageous that she's stopping us from doing magic, especially in our O.W.L. year.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Of course she’s here to spy on us all, that’s obvious, why else would Fudge have wanted her to come?" snapped Hermione.
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: Of course she's here to spy on us. Why else would Fudge have sent her? It all makes sense now.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "It is NOT excellent!" she said when Fred and George shrugged about the fainting first years.
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: That's completely unacceptable. You can't test dangerous stuff on first years, no matter what you think.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "No," she said, her voice quivering with anger, "but I will write to your mother."
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: I will write to your mother if you keep giving those sweets to first years. I mean it.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "They’re hats for house-elves," she said briskly, now stuffing her books back into her bag. "I did them over the summer."
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: I made hats for house-elves over the summer. I'm going to give them to the elves so they can have something.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Of course they want to be free!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: Of course house-elves want freedom. Don't you dare try to stop me from helping them.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Bowtruckles," said Hermione. "They’re tree-guardians, usually live in wand-trees."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: Bowtruckles are tree guardians and they usually live in wand-quality trees.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Wood lice," said Hermione promptly, "But fairy eggs if they can get them."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: Bowtruckles eat wood lice and, if they can, fairy eggs. If you need wood or leaves from their tree you should distract them with wood lice.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Don’t you dare touch those hats, Ron!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: I'm protective of my plans for the house-elves and I'm not having Ron interfere with the things I think will free them.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "They may not look dangerous, but if angered they will gouge out human eyes with their fingers,"
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: Bowtruckles might look harmless but they can be dangerous and will gouge out human eyes if they get angry.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "What's that got to do with our homework?" said Hermione, her eyebrows raised.
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: Well, obviously the weather shouldn't matter, but of course we need to stay focused on getting everything done. We can't let anything distract us from the work.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: Well, of course I want to see the letter right away. It could be important, especially if it’s from Percy about Ron being a prefect.
Obviously Percy’s letter will matter. I’m curious and a bit worried about what he’s going to say to Ron.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "You’re worried that You-Know-Who's controlling her like he controlled Quirrell?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: Well, you think Umbridge might be controlled the same way Quirrell was, but I don't think possession fits now that You-Know-Who has his own body.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "He could have her under the Imperius Curse, I suppose"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: Of course, if he's behind it he might have put her under the Imperius Curse. That would make more sense than possession.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "But last year your scar hurt when nobody was touching you, and didn't Dumbledore say it had to do with what You-Know-Who was feeling at the time?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: Obviously your scar links to what You-Know-Who feels, so this could be about him rather than Umbridge at all.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "Harry, I think you ought to tell Dumbledore your scar hurt."
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: You should tell Dumbledore about your scar hurting. He would want to know and might help.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "Harry, you can't put something like that in a letter!" and "Don't you remember, Moody told us to be careful what we put in writing!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: Don't write about this to Sirius. Moody warned us that letters could be intercepted, so it's too dangerous to put it in writing.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "I was up until one o'clock making more hats. They're disappearing like mad!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: I'm exhausted because I was up making woolly hats that keep disappearing around the place.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: I did think he might be a bit better this year ... Now he's in the Order and everything.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Well, of course I hoped Snape might behave better now that he's in the Order. It made sense to expect some change.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: That was really unfair ... Your potion wasn’t nearly as bad as Goyle’s
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Honestly, Harry's potion wasn't that bad. It was unfair how Snape treated him compared to what others did.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: I have, of course, been following your fortunes most carefully over the holidays, and am delighted to see that you have all returned to Hogwarts safely
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Trelawney is going to be all misty and dreamy as usual. Divination is useless for me but she thinks she knows everything about our fortunes.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: You will be pleased to know, however, that these problems are now to be rectified. We will be following a carefully structured, theory-centered, Ministry-approved course of defensive magic this year.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Obviously the Ministry has forced a whole new theory syllabus on Defense Against the Dark Arts. That means practical work is being cut out and that's unacceptable.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: There’s nothing written up there about using defensive spells.
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Of course the course aims say nothing about practising spells. That's exactly the problem. Defense is supposed to be practical and there's no mention of that.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: Are you a Ministry-trained educational expert, Miss Granger?
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: When Umbridge asks if I'm a Ministry expert I know she's shutting me down. Well, obviously I'm not a Ministry puppet and I'm not going to accept lessons that don't actually teach defence.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: Well, it's not a dreadful punishment, really. Of course I think she should be punished less harshly, but at least it's only lines.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: "Well, why didn’t you do any last night? Where were you anyway?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: Well, I asked Ron why he had not done his homework and where he had been, because he should have been studying.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "She’s there," said Fred, who was also swigging butterbeer, and pointed to an armchair by the fire.
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: Well, of course I'm sitting by the fire. I'm in the common room over by the armchair.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore would know if something had happened to Hagrid," said Hermione at once.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: Of course Dumbledore would know if Hagrid was in trouble. We shouldn't be showing panic because it just feeds Malfoy and his lot.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "We’ve got to ignore him, Harry. Here, hold the bowtruckle for a moment, just so I can draw its face . . ."
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: Ignore Malfoy. Focus on what matters and keep calm. Also, hold the bowtruckle so I can sketch it for proper notes.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: "I wasn’t going to," said Hermione calmly. "Because she’ll never be as good as Hagrid," said Harry firmly.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: Well, Grubbly-Plank might be competent, but she will never match Hagrid's way with creatures. I believe Hagrid's lessons are far superior.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: Hermione's handkerchief was used to wrap Harry's hand.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: Obviously you help your friends when they get hurt. I gave Harry my handkerchief to wrap his hand because that's what you do.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “How was practice?” asked Hermione rather coolly half an hour later, as Harry and Ron climbed through the portrait hole into the Gryffindor common room.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Well, practice matters and I want to know how it went. Of course I asked straight away.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Well, I suppose he could’ve played better,” Harry muttered, “but it was only the first training session, like you said . . .”
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Well, he might have been a bit off, but I was right that it takes time. Of course I expected that.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Jupiter’s biggest moon is Ganymede, not Callisto,” she said, pointing over Ron’s shoulder at a line in his Astronomy essay, “and it’s Io that’s got the volcanos.”
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Obviously, Ganymede is Jupiter's biggest moon and Io is the volcanic one. I corrected Ron so his essay isn't wrong.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Isn’t that Hermes?” said Hermione, sounding amazed.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Hermes is Percy and Lavender's owl. Of course I recognised him when he landed on the windowsill.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I have already read the textbook. I know what Slinkhard says about counterjinxes because I read it all.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: He says 'counterjinx' is just a name people give their jinxes when they want to make them sound more acceptable.
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Of course I disagree with Slinkhard. Jinxes can be useful defensively and I will say so out loud even if Umbridge tries to shut me up.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: Miss Granger, I am going to take five points from Gryffindor House.
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Umbridge took points from Gryffindor for speaking up. I will keep arguing for what is right even if she punishes me.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: I specifically asked Professor Flitwick whether students were allowed to come in the Hog's Head, and he said yes
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: Of course the Hog's Head is allowed. I checked with Flitwick and the rules let us be here so long as we're careful about publicity.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: I've double- and triple-checked the school rules.
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: I looked up everything about study groups and homework groups. They're allowed. We just mustn't parade what we're doing.
Lord Voldemort is back. We need proper training in Defense Against the Dark Arts, not Umbridge's rubbish.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: I told them to be here about now and I'm sure they all know where it is
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: I organized the meeting and got people to come. I intend to speak first so Harry doesn't have to if he doesn't want to.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: I told you, they just want to hear what you've got to say
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: People want Harry's story, but the group's here because they want real instruction on Defense, not just to hear gossip.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I wish she hadn't taken points from you, but I think she's right to warn you not to lose your temper with Umbridge," said Hermione’s voice
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Of course I don't like the points being taken, but losing my temper with Umbridge is exactly what she wants. I need to keep calm.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: Hermione merely rustled the pages of her Daily Prophet and said nothing.
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Well, sometimes I stay quiet and read. I'm paying attention even when I don't speak up.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: whether you'd thought any more about Defense Against the Dark Arts, Harry.
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Well, of course I think Harry should teach. It is the sensible thing to do. We need proper Defense and he can help us.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: You were the only person last year who could throw off the Imperius Curse completely, you can produce a Patronus, you can do all sorts of stuff that full-grown wizards can't, Viktor always said
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Obviously Harry can do things most people his age can't. He threw off Imperius and can produce a Patronus. Viktor even said Harry knows things he did not.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: I don't think Umbridge would be very happy if she found out what we were up to.
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: We must not hold lessons at Hogwarts because Umbridge would shut them down. We should meet outside school where she won't overhear us.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: until V-Voldemort comes out into the open, Sirius is going to have to stay hidden, isn't he?
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Sirius has to stay hidden until Voldemort shows himself and the Ministry admits Dumbledore was right. Then people will see Sirius isn't a Death Eater.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: I've told the others to meet us in the Hog's Head.
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: I've arranged for interested students to meet us in the Hog's Head in Hogsmeade. It's less busy than the Three Broomsticks and more private.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [Okay, write that down, and then copy out this conclusion that I’ve written for you]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: Of course I want things written properly. Get the notes down and copy the conclusion I gave you. It will save time and it makes sense.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [Harry, yours is okay except for this bit at the end, I think you must have misheard Professor Sinistra, Europa’s covered in ice, not mice]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: I thought Harry had simply misheard Professor Sinistra. I'm practical about mistakes like that and I want him to correct it now.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [But Sirius, this is taking an awful risk —]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: Of course this is dangerous. I can't help being anxious when someone takes risks that could get them caught. I say so out loud because it matters.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “Give them to me, I’ll look through them and correct them,” she said.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Well, obviously I'll go through your essays and correct them. That's what I do.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “What you can say is, ‘We promise we’ll never leave our homework this late again,’” she said, holding out both hands for their essays
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Of course I'm helping because I care about you lot. I'll fix this now, and you can promise never to leave it so late again.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: The only sound was that of Hermione’s quill scratching out sentences here and there on their essays and the ruffle of pages as she checked various facts in the reference books strewn across the table.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: I'm checking facts and editing sentences. I'm making sure everything is correct before dawn.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: Hermione was looking at Ron with an odd expression on her face.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Obviously I'm a bit surprised by Ron right now, but I'm still focused on sorting things out properly.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Well, look on the bright side — at least now you’ll have time to do Snape’s essay!"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Of course there's a bright side. No Quidditch means more time for coursework, even if it's Potions and miserable.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I can’t find a rule that says the other idiots aren’t entitled to buy them, not unless they’re proven to be dangerous in some way, and it doesn’t look as though they are . . ."
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Rules matter. I can't just stop Fred and George if what they're doing isn't technically against the rules.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "That’s always packed with people —" "— which means you’d have been harder to overhear,"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Busy public places can actually be better for hiding conversations. The Hog's Head was a poor choice for secrecy.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Well, Sirius, it’s just that there were only four of you meeting in the Shrieking Shack when you were at school, and all of you could transform into animals and I suppose you could all have squeezed under a single Invisibility Cloak if you’d wanted to."
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: The Shrieking Shack won't work for our whole group. Twenty-eight people are too many and we don't have Animagi or a single cloak.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Fred and George told me it’s blocked," said Harry, shaking his head.
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: The secret passage behind the fourth floor mirror is blocked. We can't use that either.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Obviously," said Hermione, also reading the note.
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Obviously the note meant the fire in the common room. That was the only thing that made sense to me.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "It wouldn't be exactly difficult to reseal the scroll by magic. . . . And if anyone's watching the Floo Network. . . ."
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Well, someone could magically reseal the message and anyone monitoring the Floo could intercept things. We can't be sure it's safe.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "I just hope nobody else has read this . . ."
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Of course I worry that other people might've seen the note. If anyone else read it this could be a disaster.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "You can’t skive off Divination," said Hermione severely.
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: I really think Harry shouldn't miss Divination again. He already missed History of Magic and he can't afford to miss more.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Umbridge has been reading your mail, Harry. There’s no other explanation."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Of course she's been reading your mail. It explains everything. There simply is no other sensible explanation.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "I’ve been suspecting this ever since Filch accused you of ordering Dungbombs, because it seemed such a stupid lie," Hermione whispered.
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, Filch accusing you of ordering dungbombs always struck me as a ridiculous lie. It fits if somebody wanted an excuse to read your post.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Well then, it would be a perfect way for Umbridge to manage it — tip off Filch, let him do the dirty work and confiscate the letter, then either find a way of stealing it from him or else demand to see it — I don’t think Filch would object, when’s he ever stuck up for a student’s rights?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Obviously Umbridge could have used Filch to get hold of your letters. She'd tip him off and he'd do the rest because he's never going to stand up for us.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "It was a very, very close call last night," said Hermione. "I just wonder if Umbridge knows how close it was."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm worried Umbridge might know how near she came to catching Sirius. That would make things far more dangerous for him and for us.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "Well, now he's back it's bound to hurt more often," said Sirius.
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Well, if Voldemort is back then Harry's scar is bound to hurt more often and we need to be careful.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "Imagine wasting your time and energy persecuting merpeople when there are little toerags like Kreacher on the loose —"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Honestly, it's ridiculous to waste energy rounding up merpeople when creatures like Kreacher are dangerous and need sorting out.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "No," said Harry, ignoring Hermione's affronted look at being cut off in her defense of Kreacher. "She's not letting us use magic at all!"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Of course Umbridge is stopping practical lessons; she won't let us use magic in Defense which is completely wrong.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "Sirius!" she said reproachfully. "Honestly, if you made a bit of an effort with Kreacher I’m sure he’d respond, after all, you are the only member of his family he’s got left, and Professor Dumbledore said —"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Honestly, I expect Sirius to try with Kreacher because he's the only family Kreacher has left, and I feel responsible for making him see that.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "Madame Maxime was with him, we’ve been in touch with her and she says they got separated on the journey home — but there’s nothing to suggest he’s hurt or — well, nothing to suggest he’s not perfectly okay."
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Well, Madame Maxime says Hagrid got separated on the journey but there's no clear sign he's hurt, though I'm still worried.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "We need to know what it’s r-really like . . . facing him . . . facing V-Voldemort."
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: Of course we must learn how to handle real danger. Sitting through Umbridge's lessons won't prepare us.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I was thinking that — maybe the time's come when we should just — just do it ourselves."
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: If we do not get proper Defense training from teachers, we must organize and teach ourselves. That is the sensible thing to do.
Harry's experiences make him the best candidate to show us what facing Voldemort is like. This is practical, not sentimental.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Well . . . think about it," said Hermione quietly. "Please?"
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: I believe in Harry and I care enough to ask him to help us learn. I'm pleading because it's important and because I trust him.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "I’ve got permission!" she said. "To re-form the Quidditch team!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: I got permission to re-form the Quidditch team. McGonagall pushed it through and Umbridge had to give in.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Do you honestly trust his judgment?" said Hermione. "You don’t think he has become . . . sort of . . . reckless . . . since he’s been cooped up in Grimmauld Place?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: Well, I can't help worrying that Sirius has become reckless from being stuck at Grimmauld Place. Of course I want him on our side but I suspect he might be living through us a bit.
Talking to Snuffles made me less certain. I care about Sirius, but I'm not sure following his lead without question is right.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: A Compendium of Common Curses and Their Counter-Actions . . . The Dark Arts Outsmarted . . . Self-Defensive Spellwork . . .
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Of course there are proper textbooks here. This has everything we need for practical defensive work.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: Harry, this is wonderful, there’s everything we need here!
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Well of course this proves it's the right thing to do. Everything we need is here and that settles it.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "No, they can\'t have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed," said Hermione grimly.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: Of course I jinxed the parchment. If anyone tried to copy the signatures or tamper with it they would be found out.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source:
"Someone must have blabbed to her!" Ron said angrily.

"They can\'t have done," said Hermione in a low voice.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: I don\'t think people necessarily blabbed. There could be other ways information leaked, but I still believe my protections matter.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Here comes Ernie and Hannah Abbott," said Ron, looking over his shoulder. "And those Ravenclaw blokes and Smith . . . and no one looks very spotty." Hermione looked alarmed. "Never mind spots, the idiots can\'t come over here now, it\'ll look really suspicious \u2014 sit down!" she mouthed to Ernie and Hannah, gesturing frantically to them to rejoin the Hufflepuff table.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: People who look even slightly suspicious must avoid hanging around us now. Having random students near our corner will draw attention and that is dangerous.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "What\'ll happen to them?" said Ron eagerly. "Well, put it this way," said Hermione, "it\'ll make Eloise Midgen\'s acne look like a couple of cute freckles."
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: If someone betrayed us they will regret it badly. I will not tolerate traitors and I will take action to make them pay.

Book5-chapter18_Sc11.source: "Hey, Harry," Hermione called from the other end of the room, "have you checked the time?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc11.description: Well, of course we need to be back on time. It's already ten past nine and we must get to our common rooms now or we'll be punished.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "I think we ought to elect a leader," said Hermione. "Harry's leader," said Cho at once.
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: Well, of course we should elect a leader to make things official, and I think Harry should be it because it gives him authority.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "I also think we ought to have a name," she said brightly. "It would promote a feeling of team spirit and unity, don't you think?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: We need a name to promote team spirit and to be able to refer to the group safely, so we should pick something that doesn't give away our purpose.

Book5-chapter18_Sc9.source: "All in favor of the D.A.?" said Hermione bossily, kneeling up on her cushion to count. "That's a majority — motion passed!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc9.description: A formal vote works; if a majority agrees on a name like the D.A. then it's official and I will organize it properly.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Listen, Neville, can you take it in turns to practice with Ron and Hermione for a couple of minutes so I can walk around and see how the rest are doing?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Well, of course I took turns practising the basics with Neville and Ron when asked. Practicing the fundamental spells first is the sensible thing to do.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Everybody got to their feet at once and divided up."
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Of course I joined in straight away. Standing around won't help anyone learn properly.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "It’s the way you’re moving your wand," said Hermione, watching Ron critically. "You don’t want to wave it, it’s more a sharp jab."
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Well, you have to jab the wand, not wave it. Of course the movement matters if you want the charm to work properly.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Fine, let’s swap," said Hermione, seizing Ron’s raven and replacing it with her own fat bullfrog. "Silencio!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Obviously swapping the creature can help demonstrate the charm. Sometimes you have to change the variables to see what’s actually happening.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I’ve got permission! To re-form the Quidditch team!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Well, Angelina got permission and that means the team is coming back. Of course I want them to have their practice and match plans sorted.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Just thinking . . ." she said, still frowning at the rain-washed window. "About Siri . . . Snuffles?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: I'm worried. I keep thinking about Snuffles, and I can't decide if what we're doing is the right thing. I need to work it out.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Did the giants beat you up, Hagrid?" asked Hermione quietly.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Well, I asked whether the giants had attacked Hagrid because his injuries looked like a beating.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Madame Maxime went with you, then?" Hermione interjected.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Of course Madame Maxime went with Hagrid. I wanted to be sure who he’d been traveling with.
Obviously Muggles sometimes find giants by accident and those deaths get blamed on mountaineering. That explains why the giants are hidden but not unknown.
Well, we had guessed Hagrid had been looking for giants. It seemed obvious from what led up to this.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: "Well . . . it’s just that Dobby’s plans aren’t always that safe. Don’t you remember when he lost you all the bones in your arm?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: Well, Dobby's ideas can be dangerous. Remember when he got you hurt? I don't trust every one of his schemes on instinct.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: "This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball."
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: Of course Dumbledore knows about the Room of Requirement. He actually mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball, so it's not just Dobby being madly inventive.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: "Dumbledore told you about it?" "Oh well, that’s all right then," said Hermione briskly and she raised no more objections.
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: Once Harry said Dumbledore had been mentioned, I dropped my objections. If Dumbledore's involved, I'm willing to go along.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "He wasn’t even there when I arrived, I was knocking for at least half an hour. And then he came stumping out of the forest —"
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, I tried to get Hagrid to follow the proper lesson plan. He ignored me and turned up late after coming out of the Forest. Obviously he's not listening properly.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "He kept saying nobody in their right mind would rather study knarls than chimaeras — oh I don’t think he’s got a chimaera," she added
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: Of course I know Hagrid was talking about chimaeras and eggs. He said he might try to get dangerous things even if it sounds mad.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "I tried to explain about Umbridge, but he just doesn’t get it."
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, I thought explaining Umbridge would make him cautious, but he doesn't seem to understand how serious she is.

Book5-chapter18_Sc7.source: "Harry," said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past.
Book5-chapter18_Sc7.description: Well, obviously we should check that door. Of course it's worth going in when it appears like that.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Well, of course the Ministry is meddling. Educational Decree Number Twenty five gives Umbridge ridiculous powers and that changes everything at Hogwarts.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "I think they deserve rather more than detentions," said Umbridge
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Obviously Umbridge intends to punish more harshly than McGonagall wanted. She's out to make examples of us.
I can see Ron blaming himself. Of course he's feeling terrible, but that doesn't mean he caused this.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "I can think of one thing that might cheer you both up." "Hagrid's back."
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Well, Hagrid coming back could actually cheer us up. It matters who we have on our side right now.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: When I heard about the Gubraithian fire I was impressed. Of course it's called everlasting fire. Flitwick mentioned it in class so I knew what it was.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "But didn’t they try and kill you when they saw you?"
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: I couldn't believe Hagrid and Olympe went straight up to the giant camp knowing how dangerous giants are. Of course they'd be at risk.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Why couldn’t you speak to them that day?"
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: Dumbledore wanted them to be patient, bring gifts over several visits and prove they kept promises. That slow approach was meant to build trust and let the giants test the present.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Blimey, Hagrid," said Ron quietly. (Hermione reacts elsewhere)
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: I was shocked and upset hearing how badly things went. Of course I feel sorry for Hagrid and furious that giants are so dangerous and unstable.

Book5-chapter21_Sc2.source: "The only people who can see thestrals," she said, "are people who have seen death."
Book5-chapter21_Sc2.description: Of course. Only people who have seen death can see thestrals. It all makes sense now.
Well, obviously she is horrible. She is awful, twisted and vicious and I despise her.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: I came on the Knight Bus," said Hermione airily, pulling off her jacket before Harry had time to speak.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Well, I took the Knight Bus straight after term ended. Dumbledore told me what happened early on so I could get here as soon as possible.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: The others have told me what you overheard last night on the Extendable Ears
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Of course I know about what you heard on the Extendable Ears. I don't think you're imagining things and we want to talk, not shout.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: Oh, don't lie, Harry," she said impatiently. "Ron and Ginny say you've been hiding from everyone since you got back from St. Mungo's.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Obviously hiding won't help. You're not the only one who's had a rough time and sitting alone isn't going to make anything clearer.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: Dead, died years ago. They told me.
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: Well, Hagrid's mother is dead. Of course that hurts, but Hagrid seems resigned and not keen to dwell on it.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: Professor Umbridge won't be at all happy if you bring anything to class that's too dangerous
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: Obviously Umbridge will use any excuse to get rid of teachers who are close to Dumbledore. We have to be careful and make Hagrid teach things that look harmless so she can't punish him.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: Not yet. She might not be gone yet
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: I look out for the group and I won't let anyone take risks unnecessarily. I'm the one who thinks ahead and makes sure we don't get caught.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: That foul, lying, twisting old gargoyle! You see what she's up to? It's her thing about half-breeds all over again
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Well, of course I can see what Umbridge is doing. She's trying to twist things to make Hagrid look stupid because of his background and it is not fair.
Well, I noticed Neville was upset and flustered when he was asked about seeing someone die. He isn't being silly about it, he was clearly shaken.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: they are very interesting, aren't they? The way some people can see them and some can't! I wish I could.
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Of course I think thestrals are fascinating and I got carried away saying I wanted to see them, but I didn't actually mean I wanted to see someone die.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: It looked more like a leer to Harry. 'That foul, lying, twisting old gargoyle!' stormed Hermione half an hour later
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: I'm furious about the way Umbridge treats Hagrid and Neville. I'll defend them and I'm not afraid to say so to Harry and Ron.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Is it Cho?" she asked in a businesslike way. "Did she corner you after the meeting?"
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Is it Cho who cornered him after the meeting? Of course I'm going to ask straight away.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Because Cho spends half her time crying these days," said Hermione vaguely. "She does it at mealtimes, in the loos, all over the place."
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Obviously Cho has been crying all the time lately. She's upset and it's everywhere, not just a one-off.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Well, obviously, she's feeling very sad, because of Cedric dying. Then I expect she's feeling confused because she liked Cedric and now she likes Harry, and she can't work out who she likes best. Then she'll be feeling guilty, thinking it's an insult to Cedric's memory to be kissing Harry at all, and she'll be worrying about what everyone else might say about her if she starts going out with Harry. And she probably can't work out what her feelings toward Harry are anyway, because he was the one who was with Cedric when Cedric died, so that's all very mixed up and painful. Oh, and she's afraid she's going to be thrown off the Ravenclaw Quidditch team because she's been flying so badly."
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Of course. Cho's feelings are a complete mess right now. She's grieving Cedric, confused about liking two people, feeling guilty, worrying about gossip, scared about Quidditch, and everything is tangled up.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Viktor." "Krum?" "How many other Viktors do we know?"
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I'm writing to Viktor Krum. Yes, I'm actually writing to him.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Just because you've got the emotional range of a teaspoon doesn't mean we all have," said Hermione nastily.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Don't be daft. People feel things in complicated ways. You can't treat everyone like they're emotionless.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: Hermione looked rather startled that Mrs. Longbottom knew her name, but shook hands all the same.
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Well, obviously Mrs Longbottom knows who I am because Neville's talked about me. I felt a bit surprised but I still shook her hand.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "My son and his wife were tortured into insanity by You-Know-Who's followers."
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Of course it's horrible, but it's clear now that Neville's parents were tortured by Voldemort's followers and that's why they're in this ward.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: Hermione and Ginny both clapped their hands over their mouths.
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Well, I couldn't pretend this wasn't shocking. I can't stop feeling upset about what Neville's family has gone through.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "You shouldn't have told her that you wanted to meet me halfway through your date."
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Well, Harry, you handled that badly. You should have explained things properly so Cho would not get jealous.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "You should write a book translating mad things girls do so boys can understand them."
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Of course I can see why boys are baffled by girls. It makes sense to try and explain their behaviour.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "That's the trouble with Quidditch," "it creates all this bad feeling and tension between the Houses."
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Obviously Quidditch causes tensions and bad feeling between students. It is only a game but it affects everyone.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "at least my happiness doesn't depend on Ron's goalkeeping ability."
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Well, I am not going to let my happiness hinge on Ron's performance. I care about him but I will not base my mood on Quidditch.

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Dumbledore wants to stop you having those dreams about Voldemort," said Hermione at once.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Well, Dumbledore has arranged Occlumency lessons so Harry won't keep having those dreams about Voldemort

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "In the Department of Mysteries, it's got to be," Harry whispered.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Of course, it all makes sense now. The weapon has to be in the Department of Mysteries

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Sturgis Podmore was trying to get through a door at the Ministry of Magic."
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Well, Sturgis trying to get through that door is not a coincidence so something important is definitely being kept in there

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I expect anyone would feel shaky if they'd had their mind attacked over and over again," said Hermione sympathetically.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Obviously anyone would be shaken after repeated mind attacks so Harry being shaky is totally understandable

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "You see the numerals around the edge of the coins?" Hermione said, holding one up for examination at the end of their fourth meeting. "On real Galleons that’s just a serial number referring to the goblin who cast the coin. On these fake coins, though, the numbers will change to reflect the time and date of the next meeting. The coins will grow hot when the date changes, so if you’re carrying them in a pocket you’ll be able to feel them. We take one each, and when Harry sets the date of the next meeting he’ll change the numbers on his coin, and because I’ve put a Protean Charm on them, they’ll all change to mimic his."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Well, of course I explained exactly how the coins work. I put a Protean Charm on them so they all mirror the date Harry sets. That way we can pass messages safely and no one gets suspicious carrying a Galleon.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "You can do a Protean Charm?" said Terry Boot. "Yes," said Hermione. "But that’s . . . that’s N.E.W.T. standard, that is," he said weakly. "Oh," said Hermione, trying to look modest. "Oh . . . well . . . yes, I suppose it is . . ."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Well, obviously casting a Protean Charm is advanced, but I can do it. I tried to stay modest even though it matters for what we are setting up.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Well, the Sorting Hat did seriously consider putting me in Ravenclaw during my Sorting," said Hermione brightly, "but it decided on Gryffindor in the end."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Of course the Sorting Hat thought about Ravenclaw. I still belong in Gryffindor though. I like to point that out when people act surprised about my ability.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "I’ve become accustomed to seeing the Quidditch Cup in my study, boys, and I really don’t want to have to hand it over to Professor Snape, so use the extra time to practice, won’t you?"
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Obviously I told them to practice. The Cup staying in Gryffindor matters and Snape is desperate to hand it over to Slytherin, so we'd better be sharp.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: So . . . like I was saying . . . if you want to learn some defense, then we need to work out how we’re going to do it, how often we’re going to meet, and where we’re going to —
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Well, if we’re going to learn Defense, we need a plan. We have to decide how often we meet and where. Of course we need structure.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: I really don’t think there’s any point in meeting less than once a week
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Obviously once a week is the minimum. This isn’t a casual thing, it’s important and we need regular practice.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: I-I think everybody should write their name down, just so we know who was here. But I also think that we all ought to agree not to shout about what we’re doing. So if you sign, you’re agreeing not to tell Umbridge — or anybody else — what we’re up to.
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Well, everyone should sign so we know who came, but of course we must keep this secret from Umbridge and anyone else. Don’t blab.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: We think the reason Umbridge doesn’t want us trained in Defense Against the Dark Arts is that she’s got some . . . some mad idea that Dumbledore could use the students in the school as a kind of private army. She thinks he’d mobilize us against the Ministry.
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Well, I think Umbridge is terrified of Dumbledore having any power, so she’s stopped proper training because she’s paranoid we’d be used as soldiers. It’s obvious when you think about it.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: “If she could have done one thing to make absolutely sure that every single person in this school will read your interview, it was banning it!”
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: Well, of course banning the interview just made everyone desperate to read it; Umbridge ensured the whole school now knows what you said.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: Hermione telling Harry about girls’ toilets and cubicles
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: Obviously everyone’s talking about the interview everywhere, even in the girls’ toilets and during lessons.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Not really," said Hermione indifferently, who was reading the Daily Prophet. "I've never really liked horses."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: Well, I don't like horses. Obviously that makes Firenze's appearance awkward for me.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "He's not a horse, he's a centaur!" said Lavender. "A gorgeous centaur . . ." sighed Parvati. "Either way, he's still got four legs," said Hermione coolly.
