Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: Of course, I pointed out that having four legs doesn't change anything for me. It's just common sense.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "I've got a feeling Umbridge has only just started being horrible," said Hermione darkly.
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: I have a bad feeling Umbridge is only starting. She's going to get worse, mark my words.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "You mark my words, she's going to want revenge on Dumbledore for appointing a new teacher without consulting her," said Hermione, closing the newspaper. "Especially another part-human. You saw the look on her face when she saw Firenze . . ."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: Obviously she'll want revenge on Dumbledore for this. Of course she'll hate that he appointed a part-human like Firenze without asking her.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: Hermione, Ginny, and Crookshanks, “could you come down to the kitchen? Professor Snape would like a word with you.”
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Well, of course I was there watching the game with them. When I see trouble I try to help, even if it means holding Crookshanks back.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: Looking toward the front of the bus Harry saw Hermione cover her eyes with her hands, Pigwidgeon still swaying happily on her shoulder.
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Honestly, the Knight Bus is unbearable. I cover my eyes because it is just far too chaotic for words, and I want everyone to be all right.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: Hermione was already talking about knitting a few elf hats before bedtime.
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Of course I’m thinking ahead. I always think about practical, comforting things like knitting to keep everyone calm.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “Shhh!” whispered Hermione desperately. “Not so loud — just read it!”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: This is serious. Read the paper quietly so we don't cause a scene or make things worse.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “We saw him,” Hermione whispered. “In St. Mungo’s, remember? He was in the bed opposite Lockhart’s, just lying there, staring at the ceiling. And we saw the Devil’s Snare arrive. She — the Healer — said it was a Christmas present . . .”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: We actually saw Broderick Bode at St. Mungo's and we saw a Devil's Snare get delivered. That looks like a deliberate, disguised attack.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “To send a letter,” said Hermione, swinging her bag onto her shoulder.
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: I'm going to write and send a letter right now. I might be the only one who can do it and it's worth trying.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “He can hardly say, ‘Sorry everyone, Dumbledore warned me this might happen, the Azkaban guards have joined Lord Voldemort’ — stop whimpering, Ron — ‘and now Voldemort’s worst supporters have broken out too.’ I mean, he’s spent a good six months telling everyone you and Dumbledore are liars, hasn’t he?”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Of course Fudge won't admit we were right. He's spent months discrediting us so he can't suddenly accept Dumbledore's warnings now.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, of course I insisted we would be in the library and I dragged Ron off so we'd actually get work done.
I asked Harry about his Christmas because I'm concerned and I want to keep things normal and sensible between us.

Book5-chapter27_Sc3.source: They are sort of nice, aren't they?
Book5-chapter27_Sc3.description: Well, of course, Patronuses are more than spells. I think they're lovely and useful. My otter made me really happy.
I saw Dobby burst in terrified and understood immediately that something awful was happening. Of course I joined in getting everyone to safety.

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Sturgis Podmore," said Hermione, breathlessly. "Arrested for trying to get through a door. Lucius Malfoy got him too."
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Well, of course Sturgis Podmore was arrested for trying to get through a door and I think Lucius Malfoy had a hand in it

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Sturgis had Moody's Invisibility Cloak, right? So what if he was standing guard by the door, invisible..."
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Of course it all makes sense now. If Sturgis had Moody's cloak he could have been guarding the door and been found or controlled by Malfoy

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "And now Rookwood's told Voldemort how to get the weapon?"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Obviously Rookwood used to work there and could have told Voldemort how to get at the weapon

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "But you shouldn't have seen this at all, Harry. You're supposed to be learning how to close your mind to this sort of thing"
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Well, Harry, you were never meant to be seeing this. You need to work harder on Occlumency and try to forget what you saw

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Oh, I expect she really fancied herself sitting up there in the Head's office," said Hermione viciously
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Well, obviously Umbridge is enjoying the power she has been given and she is exactly the sort of person to lord it over everyone.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "You really mustn’t! She'd love a reason to expel you!" whispered Hermione.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Of course I know we must be careful. If anyone gives Umbridge a reason she will use it to expel students, so we cannot be reckless.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "He was bluffing," said Ernie, looking appalled.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Well, obviously I trust that Harry and Ron are not the ones starting trouble. I'm worried though because this new regime will punish even minor things.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "One day," said Hermione, sounding thoroughly exasperated, "you’ll read Hogwarts: A History, and perhaps that will remind you that you can’t Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Well, of course you can’t Apparate inside Hogwarts. Hogwarts: A History says so and it’s obvious.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "It’s Harry!" said George, pointing at the back of the picture. "Says so on the back!" "Good likeness," said Fred, grinning. Harry threw his new homework diary at him; it hit the wall opposite and fell to the floor where it said happily, "If you’ve dotted the i’s and crossed the t’s then you may do whatever you please!"
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Of course I gave Harry a diary-style planner. He needs something to stay organized and that silly book actually nags you into doing work.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Kreacher," said Hermione brightly. "It had better not be clothes!" said Ron warningly. "It isn’t clothes," said Hermione, "although if I had my way I’d certainly give him something to wear other than that filthy old rag. No, it’s a patchwork quilt, I thought it would brighten up his bedroom."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Well, I gave Kreacher a patchwork quilt. It isn’t clothes but it ought to brighten his space and be more comfortable than that filthy rags he sleeps on.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Apparently he sleeps under the boiler in that cupboard off the kitchen."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Of course he sleeps under the boiler in that cupboard off the kitchen. That’s Kreacher’s den, if you can call it that.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I think I’ll just leave his present here," said Hermione, laying the package neatly in the middle of the depression in the rags and blankets and closing the door quietly. "He’ll find it later, that’ll be fine . . ."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: I’m pretty sure leaving Kreacher’s present where he sleeps is best. He’ll find it when he wants to and I won’t force him.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "So you’ve stopped having funny dreams?" "Pretty much," said Harry.
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Well, of course I don't believe Harry should stop Occlumency until he's absolutely sure he can control those dreams. He needs to go back to Snape and ask for more lessons.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "It was the first day of the Easter holidays and Hermione, as was her custom, had spent a large part of the day drawing up study schedules for the three of them."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Well, I always make study schedules for us because it's sensible and obvious that if we follow them we'll stand a much better chance in the exams.
Of course I scheduled Ron an evening off every week for Quidditch practice because practice matters even if he's moaning about our chances.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Harry, don’t do it, please don’t do it!" Hermione said in anguished tones as the bell rang at the end of the class.
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Well, obviously I think Harry is making a terrible mistake. Of course I am begging him not to go. This is dangerous and reckless.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: I can see Ron wants to back off and not argue. Fine. But I still think he needs sense talked into him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "Wha — no!" said Hermione, jumping up, "Hagrid, no, don’t wake him, really, we don’t need —"
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Well, I know waking Grawp was a terrible idea. He’s unpredictable and we did not need him awake right then.
Of course I agreed to be called Hermy if it helps, but that doesn’t mean I’m comfortable with the whole situation.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "I don’t believe him," said Hermione in a very unsteady voice, the moment they were out of earshot of Hagrid. "I don’t believe him. I really don’t believe him . . ."
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Well, I don’t trust Hagrid’s plan to leave Grawp with us. It’s far too risky and I’m genuinely worried about being responsible for him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "A giant! A giant in the forest! And we’re supposed to give him English lessons!"
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Obviously teaching Grawp English sounds impossible given his size and behaviour. The whole idea seems completely impractical and frightening.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "Of course, it all makes sense now" is forbidden so using original quote: "I really don’t believe him"
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Of course I’m convinced now we can’t just trust Hagrid’s assurances. This is a mess and it affects our safety and studies.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "She was transferred to St. Mungo's this morning."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: Of course McGonagall has been taken to St. Mungo's after being stunned. That leaves Hogwarts thin on protection.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "You've dreamed about the place, that's all."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: I think Harry's visions are dreams, not proof. He hasn't actually been to the Department of Mysteries.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "it's five o'clock in the afternoon. The Ministry of Magic must be full of workers."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: It's five in the afternoon so the Ministry should be full of people. It seems impossible for Voldemort and Sirius to be in there unnoticed.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "You do sort of I mean don't you think you've got a bit of a a saving-people-thing?"
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: I'm worried Harry has a habit of throwing himself into danger to save people and I think we need to be sensible about it.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “Hagrid’s nose was gently dripping blood. His eyes were both blackened.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Well, Hagrid is badly hurt. Of course I am worried and upset about how bad his injuries look.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “Umbridge reckons it was me that put tha’ niffler in her office.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Obviously Umbridge is looking for a reason to dismiss Hagrid. It makes no sense but she is determined.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “There’s a good chance I’m goin’ ter be gettin’ the sack any day now.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Well, Hagrid expects to be fired soon and he thinks he needs to confess something important before that happens.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “He’s been hurting you all this time, hasn’t he? That’s why you’ve had all these injuries!”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Of course the injuries make sense now. Grawp has been lashing out because he does not understand his own strength.
What on earth. Grawp is Hagrid’s half brother. That explains Hagrid’s attachment and why he brought him back.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “You want us to teach him” and “Look after him.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Well, I did not expect to be asked to keep an enormous, awkward giant company, but Hagrid asked and I agreed. It feels like a terrible responsibility.

Book5-chapter30_Sc2.source: “If yeh jus’ talk ter him a bit... if he can talk ter people, he’ll understand more that we all like him really.”
Book5-chapter30_Sc2.description: Obviously what Grawp needs most is company and someone to try to teach him how to interact with people.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Maybe it's a bit like an illness," said Hermione, looking concerned.
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: Well, it might be like a fever. Things can get worse before they get better so Harry has to stick with Occlumency and work harder.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Dumbledore doesn't want you to have dreams about that corridor at all, or he wouldn't have asked Snape to teach you Occlumency."
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: Of course Dumbledore has a reason for sending Snape. If Dumbledore wants Harry to stop dreaming about that corridor then Harry must do the Occlumency lessons properly.
Well, if Dumbledore trusts Snape then we should accept that. We can't go around doubting everyone's motives when Dumbledore has chosen him.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "Of course not," said Hermione scathingly. "Hagrid might have set it off accidentally."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: Of course I know Hagrid wouldn't hide anything dangerous where students could find it. I'm not going to let Umbridge blame him for everything.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "In there, of course," said Hermione, pointing into the dark trees. "It had to be somewhere that students weren't going to find it accidentally, didn't it?"
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: Obviously the thing would be hidden where students won't stumble on it. That's why I'm pointing into the deeper part of the forest.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "I want us heard," she answered quietly, as Umbridge jogged noisily after them. "You'll see . . ."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: Well I meant for us to be heard. Making a scene was part of the plan. I wanted them to react and for Umbridge to look foolish.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "Don't call them that!" Hermione said furiously, but Umbridge did not appear to have heard her.
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: I won't stand for Umbridge insulting the centaurs like that. Of course I'm going to defend them and try to stop her when she insults them.

Book5-chapter33_Sc1.source: "Harry grabbed Hermione and pulled her to the ground."
Book5-chapter33_Sc1.description: Harry reacts without hesitation to protect me when things go wrong. We're a team when it turns dangerous and he looks out for me.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: ["Umbridge hates part-humans," said Hermione bitterly, flopping down into an armchair.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Well, of course Umbridge hates part-humans. She's always been that way, and she was bound to try to get Hagrid out.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: ["Well, I think I’ve done all right in Arithmancy," she said, and Harry and Ron both sighed with relief.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Obviously I did okay in Arithmancy. At least that's one exam I can be confident about.

Book5-chapter32_Sc4.source: “We . . . we wanted to tell him it’s r-ready!”
Book5-chapter32_Sc4.description: Of course I would say we needed to tell Dumbledore because something we worked on is ready now and he must know about it
We finished a weapon or some method of resistance that Dumbledore told us to work on and we cannot find him to tell him
I would never let Umbridge use an illegal curse if I can stop it. I tried to stop her and it terrified me but I still fought

Book5-chapter34_Sc3.source: Harry, I don’t think you should touch it
Book5-chapter34_Sc3.description: Well, obviously he should be careful. I don't trust touching things that might be important or dangerous. Of course we should be cautious.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "That’s all very well, but what if Montague's permanently injured?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: What if Montague is permanently injured? We should be sensible and consider whether he needs proper help.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "I wasn't going to say anything about Fred and George!"
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Well, I wasn't going to go on about Fred and George. Of course I was worried in a different way.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "You are trying to block your mind, aren't you? You are keeping going with your Occlumency?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: You're trying to block your mind and keep up with Occlumency. Obviously you need to continue properly.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "I think Ron might do better without Fred and George around. They never exactly gave him a lot of confidence . . ."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I really think Ron would gain confidence if Fred and George weren't always around undermining him.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "I’ve been wondering whether Mundungus has persuaded them to sell stolen goods or something awful . . ."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I suspect Mundungus might have been involved with Fred and George somehow, maybe in dodgy business, so we should be cautious.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "But I'm sure she won't, I mean, if it's really true they've got premises in Diagon Alley now, they must have been planning this for ages . . ."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: If they've actually got a shop in Diagon Alley, they must have planned it for ages. Of course that would explain a lot.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "We need to get back up to the castle," said Hermione faintly.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: We have to get back to the castle now. That's the sensible starting point even if everything's gone wrong.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Well, we can't do anything without wands," said Hermione hopelessly, dragging herself up again.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: Without our wands we are seriously limited. Of course we need them if we're going to try anything.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "I'm not staying behind!" said Hermione furiously.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: I refuse to be left behind. Of course I'm coming. This is too important for me to sit out.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Well, we need three," said Hermione, who was still looking a little shaken, but determined just the same.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: We need enough thestrals for everyone who is going. That is practical and it matters.

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "You can make some more, can’t you?" she said, her voice becoming more sweetly girlish as it always did when she was furious.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Well, Umbridge expects people to just whip up things like Veritaserum, but of course she doesn't understand how long it actually takes

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "You’re on probation!" shrieked Professor Umbridge, and Snape looked back at her, his eyebrows slightly raised.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Obviously Snape will pretend not to know, but that doesn't mean he's uninterested. We have to be careful what we say in front of Umbridge

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him," said Hermione, who looked positively terrified at the thought.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Right, we have to try the Floo. We have to check Grimmauld Place before we rush off to London

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "I’m begging you, please! Please let’s just check that Sirius isn’t at home before we go charging off to London ... if we find out he’s not there then I swear I won’t try and stop you, I’ll come, I’ll d-do whatever it takes to try and save him"
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Of course I will go with you if we need to. I'm terrified but I'm with you every step, I won't let you go alone without checking first

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "Five minutes’ll be enough," said Harry. "C’mon, let’s go —" "Now?" said Hermione, looking shocked. "Of course now!" said Harry angrily.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Obviously we have to move fast. We can't wait around when Sirius could be hurt right now

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “I mean, you can — can check whether Sirius is at home or not while I keep watch, I don’t think you should be in there alone, Lee’s already proved the window’s a weak spot, sending those nifflers through it.”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Well, we can check Grimmauld Place by using the Floo while I keep watch. The window is a weak spot so be careful.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Dumbledore wanted you to learn to shut these things out of your mind, if you’d done Occlumency properly you’d never have seen this —”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Of course Dumbledore wanted Harry to learn Occlumency. If he'd done it properly he might not have had these visions.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him,”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Well, we have to use Umbridge's fire to contact Grimmauld Place and check whether Sirius is there before risking London.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: Even through his anger and impatience Harry recognized Hermione’s offer to accompany him into Umbridge’s office as a sign of solidarity and loyalty.
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Of course I'll go with Harry into Umbridge's office. I'm not letting him do this alone. I'll do whatever it takes to help save Sirius.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Right . . . well . . . One of us has to go and find Umbridge and — and send her off in the wrong direction, keep her away from her office. They could tell her — I don’t know — that Peeves is up to something awful as usual . . .”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: We need a diversion. Someone must lead Umbridge away while lookouts keep people from her office.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Five minutes’ll be enough,” said Harry. “C’mon, let’s go —” “Now?” said Hermione, looking shocked. “Of course now!” said Harry angrily.
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Obviously we have very little time. If Harry insists it's now, we move immediately and act fast.

Book5-chapter33_Sc2.source: "Please," said Hermione breathlessly, "please, don\'t attack us, we don\'t think like her, we aren\'t Ministry of Magic employees! We only came in here because we hoped you\'d drive her off for us —"
Book5-chapter33_Sc2.description: Well, of course I tried to explain we aren\'t like Umbridge. I begged them not to attack because we only wanted help to get rid of her, not to insult or use them.

Book5-chapter33_Sc2.source: "We haven\'t done anything to hurt you, we haven\'t used wands or threats, we just want to go back to school, please let us go back —"
Book5-chapter33_Sc2.description: I kept saying we hadn\'t hurt anyone and that we just wanted to go back to school. I was desperate and terrified because pleading seemed to be our only option.
Obviously I realised Grawp was trying to say Hagrid. I said it quietly because it might mean Grawp knows Hagrid and that changes what he might do.

Book5-chapter33_Sc2.source: "Goodness," said Hermione, gripping Harry\'s arm so tightly it was growing numb and looking as though she was about to faint, "he \u2014 he remembered!"
Book5-chapter33_Sc2.description: Of course I clung to Harry when Grawp recognised Hagrid. I was shaking and relieved that Grawp remembered, and I relied on Harry in that moment.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "It's time," said Hermione in an awestruck voice. "Time . . ."
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: Well, I could feel something significant was happening, like a moment had finally arrived. Obviously it was important and weird.
Of course I won't let anyone harm a child, even if that child is part of something monstrous. There are lines you don't cross.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "Silencio!" cried Hermione, and the man's voice was extinguished.
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: I can stop someone speaking when I need to. Sometimes taking away their voice is the quickest way to stop them from giving orders.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: Of course I mark doors. If something’s dangerous we put a fiery cross on it so we don’t keep going in circles.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: This isn’t right, Harry, come on, let’s go
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: I actually felt scared here. Even though I try to be sensible, this archway felt wrong and I wanted us out.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: There isn’t any ‘in there,’ it’s just an archway, there’s no room for anybody to be there
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: I know it sounds impossible but logically there shouldn’t be anyone inside that archway. It doesn’t make sense for people to be there.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: Harry, we are supposed to be here for Sirius!
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: We’re here for Sirius and I keep that in my head. I push Harry away from things that would distract or endanger us so we can focus on rescuing him.
I can read the layout and the numbers. I know which row we need. It’s row ninety-seven and we need to go right to find him.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "As a matter of fact, the only bit of the match Harry and I saw was Davies’s first goal."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Well, Harry and I only watched Davies’s first goal. Obviously we missed the rest.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Grawp’s about sixteen feet tall, enjoys ripping up twenty-foot pine trees, and knows me, as Hermy."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Grawp is enormous, destructive, and he knows me by name. Of course that complicates things.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Yes, I’m starting to think he has."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Well, I’m beginning to think Hagrid has genuinely lost his mind over this Grawp situation, even though I hate that it’s true.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "But unfortunately, he made Harry and me promise."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Hagrid made Harry and me promise to help. Of course I feel bound by that promise even if it seems daft.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "I confiscated that too. None of these things actually works you know —" "Dragon claw does work!"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: I confiscated a bunch of junk, including Dingle’s powdered dragon claw, because none of it is what people think. It’s nonsense and dangerous.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "This stuff can, I’ve had a look at it, and it’s actually dried doxy droppings."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Of course, that powdered dragon claw was actually dried doxy droppings. That’s disgusting and it proves these so called brain boosters are fake.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “You could be miles away.” “We’re coming with you, Harry,” said Neville. “Let’s get on with it,” said Ron firmly.
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: Of course we are going with Harry. We don't leave him to face something like this alone.
Well obviously those creatures in the tanks are brains. That explains everything about what they are.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: Half a dozen badges slid out of the metal chute where returned coins usually appeared. Hermione scooped them up and handed them mutely to Harry over Ginny’s head;
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: I grabbed the visitor badges quickly. Practical things like that matter when we're sneaking around.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "STUBEFY!" shouted Neville, wheeling around and waving Hermione’s wand at the oncoming Death Eaters.
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: Well, someone grabbed my wand and tried to use it. If I can't get my wand back, others will be left using it for them.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Luna hit a desk, slid over its surface and onto the floor on the other side where she lay sprawled, as still as Hermione."
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: Of course I got knocked out at some point and was lying still. I couldn't help while unconscious, and that left the others vulnerable.

Book5-chapter31_Sc2.source: "Please, Professor, when will we find out our results?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc2.description: Of course I need to know when the results come out. It's sensible to plan ahead and an owl in July means I can stop worrying about it until the holidays.

Book5-chapter31_Sc2.source: "I’ve got Arithmancy and it’s probably the toughest subject there is!"
Book5-chapter31_Sc2.description: Well, Arithmancy really does feel like the hardest thing right now. Obviously I must study it properly or I won't get the grade I want.
Because I'm stressed I snap at people when they underestimate how much there is to do. I can't stand complacency when exams are so important.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: Of course I will seal doors to keep us safe when I can. Locking the door buys us time.
I will trust and follow Harry when he hisses a plan under his breath. I act fast to help make his plan work.
We cannot stay and wait. We must move and think logically even when we are terrified.
If I can get a wand back to someone in the middle of a mess I will. I try to be the practical one and keep everyone fighting.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "It hasn’t really started yet," sighed Hermione gloomily, folding up the newspaper again. "But it won’t be long now"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Well, the situation is getting worse. The Prophet is full of panic about dementors and Death Eaters, and of course trouble is coming.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "I — er — heard she’s going out with someone else now," said Hermione tentatively.
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Well, I heard Cho might be seeing someone else. I told Harry in case he cared, though of course his mind is elsewhere.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "Hermione was reading the Daily Prophet again, Ginny was doing a quiz in The Quibbler"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Of course I was reading the Prophet. I want to know everything that's happening so we can be prepared.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: '\'A lone voice of truth . . . perceived as unbalanced, yet never wavered in his story . . . forced to bear ridicule and slander . . .\' Hmmm,' said Hermione, frowning, 'I notice they don\'t mention the fact that it was them doing all the ridiculing and slandering, though . . .'
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Well, the Prophet is finally saying Harry was right, but of course they won\'t admit they were the ones doing the ridiculing and slandering. That is infuriating.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'Madam Pomfrey says she\'s just in shock,' whispered Hermione.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Obviously Umbridge is not speaking and Pomfrey thinks she\'s in shock. Of course I\'m suspicious she might be sulking instead.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'It is a pity it broke,' said Hermione quietly, shaking her head.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Of course the prophecy broke. That is unfortunate, but it means people did not get the full truth from it.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'So anyway, what\'s going on in school?' 'Well, Flitwick\'s got rid of Fred and George\'s swamp,' said Ginny.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Well, school is trying to move on. Flitwick removed the swamp but left a bit as a monument. It seems some normality is returning, even if it\'s only small things.

Book6-chapter6_Sc8.source: "You two stay here," whispered Hermione. "What are you — ?"
Book6-chapter6_Sc8.description: No, you lot are staying put. This is risky, of course it is, but running off would be daft. I'm not letting you go anywhere.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "So, um, did Slughorn seem like he’ll be a good teacher?"
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Well, I'm desperate for someone better than Umbridge. Of course I want to know if Slughorn will actually teach properly.
Well, I think Mrs Weasley is being treated oddly by Fleur. Of course it annoys me to hear people talk down about her.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "No, of course not! So, um, did Slughorn seem like he’ll be a good teacher?"
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Of course I care how Harry is. I was watching him like he might be ill. I want to protect him and make sure he is all right.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.source: "That gives you equal status with prefects! You can use our special bathroom now and everything!"
Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: Well, of course being captain gives you the same status as prefects. You can use our special bathroom and all the privileges that come with it.

Book6-chapter6_Sc3.source: "now I know the kind of scum that shops here. . . . We’ll do better at Twilfitt and Tatting’s."
Book6-chapter6_Sc3.description: Well, of course they think we're scum. I can't believe they'd say that out loud and walk out like it's nothing.

Book6-chapter6_Sc3.source: "They'll make do with other makers," said Lupin. "But Ollivander was the best, and if the other side have got him it's not so good for us."
Book6-chapter6_Sc3.description: Of course this is serious. If Ollivander is with the other side then our wand supplies and whoever's helping them are in trouble.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Maybe being a prefect seems a bit tame after that
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Well, obviously if you get to be part of the Inquisitorial Squad, being a prefect would seem boring by comparison.

Book6-chapter6_Sc6.description: Well, I did worry about hiding like that. Of course it felt risky, and I hesitated because it didn't seem entirely right.
Of course the Cloak is tricky when more than one person is under it. Feet showing means we could be spotted, so we must be careful.
I can tell when someone's moved off. We're not imagining it, that's Malfoy heading left into Knockturn Alley.

Book6-chapter6_Sc7.source: If only we could hear what they’re saying!
Book6-chapter6_Sc7.description: Well, of course I wanted to know what they were saying. Of course I thought hearing them would help.

Book6-chapter6_Sc7.source: Hermione gave his arm a hard pinch. “Ouch!” “Shh! Look! He’s in there!” she breathed in Harry’s ear.
Book6-chapter6_Sc7.description: I pinched Harry to get his attention and whispered that Malfoy was inside. Obviously I was tense and wanted them to be quiet and careful.

Book6-chapter6_Sc2.source: "Harry, no!" moaned Hermione, grabbing his arm and attempting to push it down by his side. "Think. . . . You mustn’t. . . . You’ll be in such trouble. . . ."
Book6-chapter6_Sc2.description: Well, of course I tried to stop him. Think, Harry. You mustn't do this, you'll get into so much trouble. I was trying to make him see the consequences.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.source: He, Harry, Hermione, and Ginny were all sitting in roomy comfort in the wide backseat.
Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: Well, of course we're travelling in a roomy Ministry car. It's more comfortable than the Burrow and clearly meant to keep us safe.
Well, obviously Harry has been granted top-grade security. That explains the driver and the way the front seat stretches into a sofa.

Book6-chapter8_Sc5.description: Well, I saw his face was covered in blood and I panicked a bit because we had all been terrified.
Of course I moved in and used Tergeo to siphon the dried blood off his face so he was clean again.
I checked his nose and said it looked normal, asking him urgently what had happened.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Yes, I’ve already agreed it was fishy, Harry," said Hermione a little impatiently. "But haven’t we agreed there could be a lot of explanations?"
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Well, it was odd, but of course there could be loads of other explanations. We shouldn't jump to conclusions.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "It seems very unlikely, Harry," said Hermione in a repressive sort of voice. "What makes you think — ?"
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Obviously it seems unlikely that You-Know-Who would let a sixteen year old like Malfoy join up, so I don't think that's right.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "I think he just wanted to get out of there, Harry," said Hermione.
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Well, maybe Malfoy just wanted to leave quickly. That could be why he reacted the way he did.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "We can’t, Harry," said Hermione, looking apologetic. "Ron and I’ve got to go to the prefects’ carriage first and then patrol the corridors for a bit."
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Of course I had duties to get to on the train. I couldn't ignore being a prefect.

Book6-chapter8_Sc6.description: Well, you missed the Sorting anyway. Obviously you weren't listening to the Hat.
Of course I asked what the Hat said. I want to know if it said anything useful or different this year.

Book6-chapter8_Sc6.source: [More of the same, really . . . advising us all to unite in the face of our enemies, you know.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc6.description: The Hat just went on about unity in the face of our enemies. That's the same warning again and it's getting a bit predictable.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Hagrid was only a few minutes late," said Hermione. "Look, he’s waving at you, Harry."
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Well, Hagrid is late but he's here and he waved at Harry. Of course I pointed it out because it's obvious and important.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Him and everyone else here," sniffed Hermione.
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Obviously everyone's curious about what happened at the Ministry. They're all asking Harry questions and it's driving Hermione mad.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "What happened to his hand?" gasped Hermione.
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: What the hell happened to Dumbledore's hand? It's black and dead looking and that's worrying.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Well, Dumbledore's hand looks like it's dead. Some injuries can't be cured and there are poisons without antidotes, obviously.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [But Harry, you said that Slughorn was going to be teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts!]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Of course I thought Slughorn would teach Defense Against the Dark Arts. I was surprised to hear Snape got the job instead.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [I implore you, should you notice anything strange or suspicious within or outside the castle, to report it to a member of staff immediately.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: We have to report anything suspicious to a teacher straight away. It's important for everyone's safety.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: Your adversary has no warning about what kind of magic you’re about to perform
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: Of course nonverbal spells give you the element of surprise. That split second can make all the difference.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: I thought he sounded a bit like you.
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: Well, when Snape described fighting the Dark Arts it reminded me of what Harry says about facing Voldemort. Brave and quick thinking matter as much as the spells themselves.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: There’s no need to call me ‘sir,’ Professor.
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: I gasped when Harry called Snape on that. It felt like he’d crossed a line but part of me admired his spine.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Because it’s probably not Ministry of Magic–approved," said Hermione.
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: Well, of course this book probably isn't approved. Using handwritten spells without knowing what they do is irresponsible.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I’m starting to think this Prince character was a bit dodgy."
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: Of course I think the Prince was dodgy. Who writes spells to dangle people by their ankles? That tells you something about the person.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left," said Hermione stubbornly.
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: Obviously the Death Eaters won't all be pure-blood. Lots of them must be half-bloods pretending otherwise. It's the Muggle-borns they really hate.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "We’ve got to go and explain," said Hermione, looking up at Hagrid’s huge empty chair at the staff table the following Saturday at breakfast.
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, of course we have to explain to Hagrid. I hate leaving things unsaid and I can’t stand that he thinks we abandoned him.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "It’s not Quidditch that’s popular, it’s you! You’ve never been more interesting, and frankly, you’ve never been more fanciable."
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: Obviously people are interested in Harry because of what he’s been through, not just because of Quidditch. He’s suddenly very noticed.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Everyone knows you’ve been telling the truth now, don’t they? The whole Wizarding world has had to admit that you were right about Voldemort being back and that you really have fought him twice in the last two years and escaped both times."
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, Harry’s reputation has changed. People finally believe him about Voldemort and that changes how everyone treats him.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, I do love them, don't I? Of course I do, they're really something.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.source: "I can't believe you've wriggled out of another one," said Hermione, shaking her head.
Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: I can't believe you've wriggled out of another one. They're not that bad, you know.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: Well, I can't just stand there. Of course I'm going to try to help Hagrid when he's upset. I put my arm around him because someone has to be sensible and comforting.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.source: Is there anything we can do?
Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: Obviously Aragog is very ill and Hagrid is terrified. Of course I asked if there was anything we could do, even if it probably isn't safe.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Or herself," said Hermione irritably, ... "It might have been a girl. I think the handwriting looks more like a girl's than a boy's."
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, the handwriting could be a girl's. It might not be a man behind the Half-Blood Prince notes after all.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Two of spades: conflict, Seven of spades: an ill omen. Ten of spades: violence. Knave of spades: a dark young man, possibly troubled, one who dislikes the questioner —"
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Obviously she was reading fortunes and got a whole load of gloomy cards. She thought the knave sounded wrong for the situation and stopped herself.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Ooooh! Good luck! We'll wait up, we want to hear what he teaches you!"
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Of course I want Harry to be all right and I want to know what Dumbledore tells him. I'm staying up for it and I expect him to come back with answers.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "We smashed the entire stock of Ministry Time-Turners when we were there last summer. It was in the Daily Prophet."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Well, the Time-Turners at the Ministry were smashed. Of course they weren't an option for squeezing Hagrid into our timetables.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the entrance hall. Any Dark object would have been found, I know for a fact Crabbe had a shrunken head confiscated."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Of course Filch used Secrecy Sensors on us when we arrived. Any Dark object should have been caught then. Crabbe even had a shrunken head taken.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "All the owls are being checked too," said Hermione. "Filch told us so when he was jabbing those Secrecy Sensors everywhere he could reach."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Well, if all the owls are being checked as well, then sending something by owl is unlikely. That rules out that possibility.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I wish you could come, I don’t want to go on my own!"
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: I really don't want to go to Slughorn's party alone. Of course I'm nervous about who'll be there, like McLaggen.

Book6-chapter12_Sc4.source: Oh, look, they've got deluxe sugar quills, those would last hours!
Book6-chapter12_Sc4.description: Well, those deluxe sugar quills would last ages, they sound brilliant for studying and staying sweet while working.
Harry, of course you mustn't choke someone, that's not the way to deal with this even if it's awful.
I care about Harry and I'll yell at him when he goes too far. I won't let him hurt someone like that.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “Maybe your dad did use it, Harry,” said Hermione, “but he’s not the only one. We’ve seen a whole bunch of people use it, in case you’ve forgotten. Dangling people in the air. Making them float along, asleep, helpless.”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Well, it’s not just Harry’s dad. I know we’ve seen loads of people use that spell, even to abuse people by making them float helplessly.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “I just think it’s very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don’t even know what they’re for, and stop talking about ‘the Prince’ as if it’s his title, I bet it’s just a stupid nickname, and it doesn’t seem as though he was a very nice person to me!”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Of course it’s irresponsible to use spells you don’t understand. And calling someone 'the Prince' like it’s a title is daft. I reckon it’s just a stupid nickname and he doesn’t sound like a nice person.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left,” said Hermione stubbornly. “I expect most of them are half-bloods pretending to be pure. It’s only Muggle-borns they hate, they’d be quite happy to let you and Ron join up.”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Obviously the Death Eaters cannot all be pure blood. I expect a lot of them are half bloods pretending otherwise. Their real target is Muggle-borns, not half bloods like us.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “Because he didn’t want to touch it, obviously!” said Harry angrily. “What he actually said was, ‘How would I look carrying that down the street?’” said Hermione.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Of course he didn't want to touch it. He was worried about appearances. He asked Borgin to keep the item so he wouldn't have to be seen with it.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “I asked Borgin about the necklace, don’t you remember? When I went in to try and find out what Malfoy had asked him to keep, I saw it there. And Borgin just told me the price, he didn’t say it was already sold or anything —”
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Well, I went into Borgin and Burkes and saw the necklace. Borgin only told me the price and didn't say it was sold. I was being obvious and he twigged that straight away.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “Harry, Malfoy wasn’t in Hogsmeade!” said Hermione, actually stamping her foot in frustration.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Obviously Malfoy couldn't have been the one in Hogsmeade today. I'm frustrated because that means someone else must have been involved.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “It was all wrapped up, so he wouldn’t have to touch it, and quite easy to hide inside a cloak, so nobody would see it!”
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Of course the seller could wrap the necklace so the buyer wouldn't touch it. It would be easy to hide in a cloak and slip it into Hogwarts unnoticed if they tried.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s Veritaserum, a colorless, odorless potion that forces the drinker to tell the truth," said Hermione.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, Veritaserum forces someone to tell the truth. Obviously that makes it a very dangerous tool in the wrong hands.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s Polyjuice Potion, sir," she said.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course Polyjuice Potion lets you take someone else's appearance. I made it before so I know how it looks and smells.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s the most powerful love potion in the world!" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Amortentia is the most powerful love potion. It causes obsession rather than true love. Obviously that is why it is so risky.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: And the steam rising in characteristic spirals," said Hermione enthusiastically, "and it’s supposed to smell differently to each of us, according to what attracts us, and I can smell freshly mown grass and new parchment and —
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Of course Amortentia smells different to each person. Right now I can smell freshly mown grass and new parchment and something else that made me blush.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Hermione Granger, sir." "Granger? Granger? Can you possibly be related to Hector Dagworth-Granger, who founded the Most Extraordinary Society of Potioneers?"
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well I had to tell Slughorn my name and explain I'm Muggle-born. He still thinks I might be connected to famous potioneers but I had to say I am Muggle-born.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: It’s liquid luck," said Hermione excitedly. "It makes you lucky!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Liquid luck is real. Felix Felicis seems amazing but I know it is risky and should not be misused.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: Oho! 'One of my best friends is Muggle-born, and she's the best in our year!' I’m assuming this is the very friend of whom you spoke, Harry?
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Slughorn reacted to Harry's mention of me. He clearly approves and I feel pleased and a bit flattered.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Ginny's got a point," said Hermione, perking up at once. "We ought to check that there's nothing odd about it. I mean, all these funny instructions, who knows?"
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Well, of course we should check the book. Those weird marginal notes could mean something is wrong. I don't trust unknown scribbles.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Add a clockwise stir —" "No, no, the book says counterclockwise!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Obviously the textbook's main instructions say counterclockwise, but someone else wrote a different method. That difference matters and we should be careful which to follow.
I tried Specialis Revelio on the book and nothing happened. The book looks ordinary and didn't reveal anything magical when I cast that charm.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "It seems all right," said Hermione, still staring at the book suspiciously. "I mean, it really does seem to be . . . just a textbook."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Even though I'm suspicious, I couldn't find anything overtly dangerous with the book. I'm uneasy but have to admit it might just be an ordinary, messy textbook.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "It’s pathetic," said Hermione furiously, ... "You don’t really want her around forever?"
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, I think Ron being casual about someone staying around forever is pathetic. Of course I care about who stays and why.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "She’s a damn sight nicer than Phlegm," said Ginny. "And she’s more intelligent, she’s an Auror!" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, Tonks is an Auror and she’s clever. Of course being an Auror matters.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "It’s survivor’s guilt," said Hermione. "I know Lupin’s tried to talk her round, but she’s still really down. She’s actually having trouble with her Metamorphosing!"
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Obviously Tonks is suffering. She’s depressed and her Metamorphing is affected. That explains why she’s not herself.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "I can’t go around looking like this forever!" squeaked Hermione.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, I’m desperate to fix this joke. I can’t be stuck like this and I’m frantic to find an antidote.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "I asked Professor McGonagall at the end of last term."
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Of course I already asked Professor McGonagall about our options if we fail O.W.L.s. We have to discuss things with our Head of House if needed.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Yep — nine ‘Outstandings’ and one ‘Exceeds Expectations’ at Defense Against the Dark Arts." said Ron about Hermione.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, I did extremely well. Nine Outstandings and an Exceeds Expectations. I’m annoyed at myself for worrying but I did brilliant.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Ron, I warn you, don’t drink it!" Hermione said again, alarmed,
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: Well, I told Ron not to drink that. Of course it looked dodgy and he shouldn’t have drank it.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You should be expelled for that. I’d never have believed it of you, Harry!"
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: Of course I was shocked at Harry. That was wrong and I said he should be expelled. I can’t just let dangerous behavior slide.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You should be expelled for that. I’d never have believed it of you, Harry!"
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I care about rules and safety. Seeing Harry do something reckless made me furious and disappointed.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: I think it’s fascinating. It makes absolute sense to know as much about Voldemort as possible. How else will you find out his weaknesses?
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Of course it makes sense to learn everything about Voldemort. Obviously knowing him is the only way to find his weaknesses.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: Slughorn’s going to have a Christmas party, Harry, and there’s no way you’ll be able to wriggle out of this one because he actually asked me to check your free evenings, so he could be sure to have it on a night you can come.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Slughorn is arranging a Christmas party and he asked me to check Harry's free evenings. Obviously Harry has to go because Slughorn scheduled it around him.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: We’re allowed to bring guests, and I was going to ask you to come, but if you think it’s that stupid then I won’t bother!
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: I was going to ask Ron to come as my guest. If he thinks the Slug Club is stupid then fine, I won't bother asking him.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: Hand that over, Harry. It says we’re supposed to puncture them with something sharp.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: We are supposed to puncture Snargaluff pods with something sharp to juice them properly. That is the right way to do it.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "You spiked Ron’s juice with lucky potion at breakfast! Felix Felicis!"
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Well, of course I believed Harry had put Felix Felicis in Ron's drink because everything went so well for Ron that day.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "You go!" said Hermione, blinking back tears. "I’m sick of Ron at the moment, I don’t know what I’m supposed to have done."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I'm furious and hurt with Ron. I feel ignored and I do not know what I'm supposed to have done to deserve this.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "She was sitting on the teacher’s desk, alone except for a small ring of twittering yellow birds circling her head, which she had clearly just conjured out of midair."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I was practicing spells by conjuring those little golden birds. I was trying to calm down and focus.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Oppugno!" came a shriek from the doorway. ... The little flock of birds was speeding like a hail of fat golden bullets toward Ron..."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Obviously I lost control of my temper. I sent the birds at Ron because I was so angry and hurt by what he was doing with Lavender.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Oh, I’ve just escaped — I mean, I’ve just left Cormac, Under the mistletoe,"
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Well, I just left Cormac because of an awkward mistletoe moment. Obviously coming with him was a mistake.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "I debated for a while about Zacharias Smith, but I thought, on the whole —" "You considered Smith?" "Yes, I did, and I’m starting to wish I’d chosen him, McLaggen makes Grawp look a gentleman."
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Of course I thought about who to go with. I even considered Zacharias Smith and now I wish I had, because McLaggen is unbearable.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "There’s a difference," said Hermione with dignity. "I’ve got no plans to tell Ron anything about what might, or might not, have happened at Keeper tryouts."
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Well, I won't stoop to telling Ron about the Keeper tryouts. Of course I'm not going to sabotage him like that.

Book6-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Serves you right for coming with him,"
Book6-chapter15_Sc4.description: Obviously I think she deserved being hassled by McLaggen for going with him. I said it to make the point.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "He\'s at perfect liberty to kiss whomever he likes,\" said Hermione
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, he can kiss whoever he likes. I don\'t care about who he kisses.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "And incidentally, you need to be careful."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Of course you need to be careful. People are trying to slip you love potions so watch what you drink.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "They didn\'t have the potions with them in the bathroom," said Hermione scornfully. "They were just discussing tactics."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well, they weren\'t carrying potions then. They were plotting and discussing how to get you to drink them.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Fred and George send them disguised as perfumes and cough potions," said Hermione. "It\'s part of their Owl Order Service."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Obviously Fred and George disguise their products as perfumes and cough medicine so they can send them by owl into school.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "She had just spotted Ron and Lavender, who were entwined in the same armchair."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Of course I was upset when I saw Ron with Lavender. I left straight away because I couldn\'t stand it.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: Hermione was sitting alone, playing with her stew.
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: Well, I'm sitting by myself, playing with my stew. I'm apart from the others for now.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Yes, I'm meeting Cormac at eight, and we're —" "— we're going up to the party together."
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Well, yes, I'm going to meet Cormac McLaggen at eight. Of course we're going to the party together.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I like really good Quidditch players," Hermione corrected her, still smiling.
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: I like really good Quidditch players. Obviously I admire skill, not just the name.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Oh — yes — didn't you know?" said Hermione, with a most un-Hermione-ish giggle.
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Well, it's a surprise even to me that I'm going out with someone like McLaggen. I'm a bit pleased about it.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "And he’s acting on Voldemort’s orders, just like I said!"
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Of course he’s following Voldemort's orders. It all fits together once you think about who would give orders like that.
Malfoy told Borgin that Fenrir Greyback was an old family friend and that he’d be checking up on Borgin. That is a sign Malfoy has dangerous contacts.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Well . . . there is the possibility it was an empty threat."
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Okay, I admit it might have been an empty threat. But even so, you can't ignore how suspicious it all looks.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "It was the Fat Lady who drank a vat of five-hundred-year-old wine, Harry, not me."
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: I visited Hagrid and Buckbeak when I got back. Also, the Fat Lady and her friend got wasted on ancient wine. Honestly.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: "And you thought of a bezoar all by yourself, did you, Harry?"
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: Well, of course I think someone should actually learn the proper antidotes instead of relying on a rare stone. Intuition is fine, but knowledge matters.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: Her half-finished antidote, comprising fifty-two ingredients, including a chunk of her own hair, bubbled sluggishly behind Slughorn
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: I spent ages trying to do the antidote properly, even if it made me sweaty and covered in soot. Doing it the right way is important to me.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "But you said Slughorn had been planning to give that bottle to Dumbledore for Christmas,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: Well, if Slughorn intended that bottle for Dumbledore then the poison could have been meant for Dumbledore, not Slughorn.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Then the poisoner didn’t know Slughorn very well,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: Of course, anyone who knew Slughorn would expect him to keep something tasty for himself, so the poisoner probably did not know him.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Well, for one thing, they both ought to have been fatal and weren’t, although that was pure luck. And for another, neither the poison nor the necklace seems to have reached the person who was supposed to be killed. Of course, that makes the person behind this even more dangerous in a way, because they don’t seem to care how many people they finish off before they actually reach their victim."
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: Well, it all points to a connection between the attacks. It's worrying because the attacker doesn't seem to care who gets hurt before they reach their real target.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "No, she’s already gone down to the pitch with Ginny."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Of course I already went down to the pitch with Ginny.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "Only you can get the memory, Dumbledore says. That must mean you can persuade Slughorn where other people can't."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Well, of course Dumbledore means Harry has to persuade Slughorn himself. It's not about potions or tricks.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "I think it'll be part of the magic of the room," said Hermione. "If you need it to be Unplottable, it will be."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Obviously the Room of Requirement changes according to what you need. If Malfoy wanted it Unplottable, the room will be Unplottable for him.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "Malfoy already knew exactly how we were using the room, didn't he, because that stupid Marietta had blabbed."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Of course Marietta gave the game away. Malfoy knew how we used the room, so he could use it for his own secret purposes.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: He must be determined to hide what really happened if Dumbledore couldn't get it out of him
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, if Dumbledore couldn't get the truth from him, then he must be bent on hiding whatever happened. That worries me.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: Horcruxes . . . I've never even heard of them
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Of course I know a lot of magic, but I haven't heard of Horcruxes either. That means they're probably rare and dangerous.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: They must be really advanced Dark Magic, or why would Voldemort have wanted to know about them? I think it's going to be difficult to get the information, Harry, you'll have to be very careful about how you approach Slughorn, think out a strategy.
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, obviously Horcruxes are advanced Dark Magic. If Voldemort wanted to learn about them, it must be serious. We need a careful plan to get this from Slughorn.
Of course Golpalott's Third Law says the antidote for a blended poison is not just the sum of the separate antidotes. That changes how to approach making antidotes.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: You have to understand the principles involved this time. No shortcuts or cheats!
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, shortcuts won't cut it. I believe mastering the principles is essential if you're to succeed in Potions.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Hermione even escorted them down to breakfast, bringing with her the news that Ginny had argued with Dean."
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: I've patched things up with Ron. We're on speaking terms again and I walked them to breakfast together.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Oh, Dean was laughing about McLaggen hitting that Bludger at you," said Hermione.
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Ginny and Dean argued because Dean was laughing at McLaggen hitting that Bludger at Harry.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "It’s all right!" said Hermione kindly, hurrying forward to help her. "Here . . ." She tapped the broken scales with her wand and said, "Reparo."
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: I help when someone needs it and I fix things with a quick spell. Of course I stepped in when that little girl dropped her scales.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.source: It would mean a lot to me if you'd nip down for the burial later this evening.
Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: Well, Hagrid wants us to go to Aragog's burial at dusk. He expects us to leave the castle at night and that is dangerous because security is much tighter now.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.source: Harry, you can't be thinking of going
Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: Of course I think going out at night for that is a pointless risk that could get us heavy trouble. We must not throw away our Apparition tests and safety for sentiment.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.source: Harry, you’ve got to get that memory
Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: Well, the memory from Slughorn is crucial because it's about stopping Voldemort. Stopping him matters more than other things, so Harry must get it.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: I haven’t found one single explanation of what Horcruxes do!" she told him. "Not a single one! I’ve been right through the restricted section and even in the most horrible books, where they tell you how to brew the most gruesome potions — nothing!
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Of course I checked every book I could, even the awful ones in the Restricted Section, and there is nothing that explains what Horcruxes actually do.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: The Hogwarts library had failed Hermione for the first time in living memory. She was so shocked, she even forgot that she was annoyed at Harry for his trick with the bezoar.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Well, the library letting me down felt impossible. I was furious and shocked, and for a moment I even forgot to be cross with Harry about the bezoar trick.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: "All I could find was this, in the introduction to Magick Moste Evile — listen — 'Of the Horcrux, wickedest of magical inventions, we shall not speak nor give direction. . . .' I mean, why mention it then?" she said impatiently, slamming the old book shut; it let out a ghostly wail.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Obviously it's maddening that books even mention Horcruxes only to refuse to explain them. That makes no sense and it drives me mad.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “I know,” said Hermione soothingly, “it does seem really harsh. . . .”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Well, that really is harsh. Of course it seems unfair.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “Don’t push me, please, Dean,” she said, sounding annoyed. “You’re always doing that, I can get through perfectly well on my own. . . .”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Well, I can manage on my own and I won't have people pushing me around. Obviously I'm annoyed when someone won't back off.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Do you mean to say," said Hermione in a hushed voice, "that that little girl whose scales I repaired — ?"
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Well, of course it was Crabbe or Goyle disguised. It all makes sense now that those girls turned up.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Hmmm . . . the Dark Mark we don’t know exists," said Hermione skeptically, rolling up Ron’s dried essay before it could come to any more harm and handing it to him.
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Obviously we can't assume the Dark Mark is definitely involved until we have proof. We need facts, not panic.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "I’ve already told you, you need to persuade Slughorn," said Hermione. "It’s not a question of tricking him or bewitching him, or Dumbledore could have done it in a second. Instead of messing around outside the Room of Requirement" — she jerked the Prophet out from under Harry’s hand and unfolded it to look at the front page — "you should go and find Slughorn and start appealing to his better nature."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Of course you have to persuade Slughorn. We cannot trick him. You appeal to his vanity and his feelings. That is how we will get the memory.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "You’d do better," said Hermione, when he confided this plan to Ron and her in the entrance hall, "to go straight to Slughorn’s office and try and get that memory from him."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Obviously Harry should be focusing on Slughorn right now. Chasing other leads will only distract from the main task.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Of course she performed perfectly. That’s what I expect when someone’s been practicing.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: She’s supposed to be guarding the school, why’s she suddenly abandoning her post to come and see Dumbledore when he’s not even here?
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Tonks should be on guard duty. It’s worrying and odd that she’s leaving her post to look for Dumbledore when he isn’t even at his office.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: It’s a thought, said Hermione slowly.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: It’s possible Tonks could be attached to Sirius, but I’m not convinced that explains why she rushed into the castle.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I doubt you’d find a woman who sulked for half an hour because Madam Rosmerta didn’t laugh at their joke about the hag, the Healer, and the Mimbulus mimbletonia.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Women aren’t that likely to sulk for ages over a silly prank. Tonks’ behavior doesn’t quite match that kind of petty sulking.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Ron, you’re making it snow," said Hermione patiently, grabbing his wrist and redirecting his wand
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Obviously Ron was waving his wand and making fake snow fall, so I grabbed his wrist and stopped him.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "We split up," he told Harry ... "Last night. When she saw me coming out of the dormitory with Hermione."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Well, Ron and Lavender have split up because she saw Ron coming out with me. It was messy while she was yelling.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Coward," said Hermione, though she looked amused.
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Well, I called Ron a coward but I wasn't really cross; I found the situation a bit amusing.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Of course, this puts you in a bit of a dilemma, doesn’t it?" said Hermione.
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Of course, if Ginny and Dean are not speaking, that creates a dilemma for Harry's place on the Quidditch team.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “So it must have been a girl or a woman who gave Katie the necklace,” said Hermione.
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, whoever handed Katie the necklace was in the ladies’ bathroom. That means it was either a girl or someone who looked like one.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “That would be a complete waste of potion,” said Hermione flatly, putting down the copy of Spellman’s Syllabary she had just taken out of her bag. “Luck can only get you so far, Harry. The situation with Slughorn was different; you always had the ability to persuade him, you just needed to tweak the circumstances a bit. Luck isn’t enough to get you through a powerful enchantment, though. Don’t go wasting the rest of that potion! You’ll need all the luck you can get if Dumbledore takes you along with him.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Of course I won’t let you blow the rest of the Felix. Luck helps sometimes but it will not defeat a strong enchantment. We must be sensible about this or you’ll have nothing left when it really matters.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: Hermione had just taken out of her bag. “Couldn’t we make some more?” Ron asked Harry, ignoring Hermione. “It’d be great to have a stock of it. . . . Have a look in the book . . .” Harry pulled his copy of Advanced Potion-Making out of his bag and looked up Felix Felicis.
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Obviously making more Felix would be helpful, but the book shows it is far from simple. We’ll need time, ingredients, and careful brewing if we even try.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "That would be a complete waste of potion," said Hermione flatly.
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Well, luck only gets you so far. Making more Felix is a terrible idea because it takes months and you can\'t rely on luck to break powerful enchantments.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Luck can only get you so far, Harry. The situation with Slughorn was different; you always had the ability to persuade him, you just needed to tweak the circumstances a bit."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Of course. Slughorn was persuadable because of circumstances, not pure luck. You can\'t use Felix as a substitute for proper skill or planning.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "She dropped her voice to a whisper. "Couldn\'t we make some more?" Ron asked Harry, ignoring Hermione."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Obviously I\'m worried Harry will waste the potion. I\'d rather him not risk making more or using it foolishly, especially with Dumbledore\'s affairs coming up.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "Look at that! Look at the picture!"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Well, I dug out an old Prophet and found Eileen Prince. Obviously Prince could be a family name and she could be the Half Blood Prince just as much as anyone.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "If, say, her father was a wizard whose surname was Prince, and her mother was a Muggle, then that would make her a ‘half-blood Prince’!"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Of course it makes sense to consider surnames and parentage. I am going to look up records and old Potions awards to find more on Eileen Prince.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "The library. There’s a whole collection of old Prophets up there."
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Well, I used the library archives to find that article. I will carry on researching because you cannot just drop something like this until you know the facts.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "I told you there was something wrong with that Prince person," Hermione said, evidently unable to stop herself.
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: Well, I told you there was something dodgy about that Half-Blood Prince book. Of course I was right to be suspicious.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "But you can’t call that Sectumsempra spell good, Ginny, look where it’s landed him!"
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: That Sectumsempra spell is dangerous and it caused a real mess. Obviously spells like that are not something to praise.
Well, I can't believe Harry is defending the book after what it did. Of course I think he should see how risky it is.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Well, of course I am worried. Harry looks a mess and I am scared for him and everyone else. I gasp and panic because this is dangerous.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "You’ve got to watch him and you’ve got to watch Snape too. Use anyone else who you can rustle up from the D.A., Hermione, those contact Galleons will still work, right?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Obviously the Marauder’s Map is for watching Malfoy and Snape. I am to organise the D.A. and use the contact Galleons to call people. I will keep watch.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "We don’t want it, you take it, who knows what you’re going to be facing?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: I do not want Harry risking himself on a potion meant to make him lucky. I insist he keep it because he is going into danger and we cannot let him go alone.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: "'Evil' is a strong word," said Hermione quietly. "You were the one who kept telling me the book was dangerous!"
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: Well, 'evil' is too strong a word for the Prince based on what we know, and of course I kept saying the book was dangerous because it really could have been harmful.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: Hermione's face was glazed with tears
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: Of course I'm upset and worried. I'm emotional about what happened and about Harry, but I still try to think logically about what to do next.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: Outside Snape's office, yes, with Luna. We hung around for ages outside it and nothing happened.
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: We waited outside Snape's office with Luna for ages and nothing happened. We didn't know what was going on upstairs.
I feel awful about it. Snape told us to look after Professor Flitwick so we stayed and then let Snape go. Of course! It all makes sense now, he must have Stupefied Flitwick.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: We went into his office to see if we could help Professor Flitwick and found him unconscious on the floor
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: Professor Flitwick was on the floor unconscious when we went in. We thought we were helping but we actually let Snape leave.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "I was going through the rest of the old Prophets and there was a tiny announcement about Eileen Prince marrying a man called Tobias Snape, and then later an announcement saying that she’d given birth to a —"
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Well, I found the notice that Snape's mother was Eileen Prince and that she married Tobias Snape. Of course that means Snape is a Prince on his mother's side.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "So . . . I was sort of right. Snape must have been proud of being ‘half a Prince,’ you see? Tobias Snape was a Muggle from what it said in the Prophet."
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Obviously, Snape liked the Prince name. It explains why he'd use it and why he might hide his Muggle father.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "I don't think he wanted to associate himself with that book," said Hermione. "I don't think Dumbledore would have liked it very much if he’d known. And even if Snape pretended it hadn’t been his, Slughorn would have recognized his writing at once."
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Of course he didn't want to be linked to that book. Dumbledore would not have approved, and Slughorn would spot Snape's handwriting right away.

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: "Hermione told me to get on with life, maybe go out with some other people, relax a bit around you, because I never used to be able to talk if you were in the room, remember?"
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: Well, of course I told Ginny to try and get on with her life a bit, to go out and be herself so Harry might notice her more

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: Ron ... was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: I'm sobbing into Ron's shoulder and I'm devastated. I'm upset for Ginny and for Harry and it's all just too much

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "No," she said reprovingly, folding up the newspaper. "They\'re still looking for Snape but no sign . . ."
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: No, there\'s been no sign of Snape. They\'re still searching but they haven\'t found him.
