Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "No," she said sadly, "I\'ve been trying, Harry, but I haven\'t found anything. . . ."
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: I went through the library and I couldn\'t find anyone with those initials who fits. I\'ve been looking and I can\'t find a lead.

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "No, actually, it\'s about . . . well, Snape." She looked nervous even saying the name again.
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: Well, I was right about the Half-Blood Prince being connected to that book. It looks like Eileen Prince did once own it, and that points towards Snape in a way I didn\'t want to say out loud.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: Well, of course, Harry can hardly see without his glasses. Obvious really.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "Miss Granger with Kingsley, again by thestral —"
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: I'm going with Kingsley on a thestral. I'm relieved. I don't feel confident on a broom so that suits me.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: Well, of course I'm worried about you, Harry. Are you all right?

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: Dumbledore is dead. Well, of course that's devastating. We have to keep our heads even though everything's awful.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "No," said Harry. "Someone had already taken it and left a fake in its place."
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: The Horcrux we went after was already taken and replaced with a fake. Obviously that changes our whole plan.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: Harry stood up, murmured "See you in a bit" to Ron, Hermione, and Ginny, and followed Professor McGonagall back down the ward.
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: Of course we're going to have to rethink everything now. We can't just carry on as before after losing Dumbledore and failing to retrieve the Horcrux.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively."
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: Well, it sounds impossible, but you're saying you did magic without meaning to, that you reacted on instinct.

Book7-chapter5_Sc3.source: "But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively."
Book7-chapter5_Sc3.description: Of course I find it hard to believe at first, but if your wand moved and cast something without your intent then we have to accept you can produce magic under extreme pressure.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: Well, Kingsley and I got back. Obviously getting everyone home is a mess and we still do not know where some people are.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.source: "They recounted the stories of their own journeys, but all the time the continued absence of Bill, Fleur, Mad-Eye, and Mundungus seemed to lie upon them like a frost, its icy bite harder and harder to ignore."
Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: Of course I am worried. We all shared our journeys, yet the fact that Bill, Fleur, Mad-Eye, and Mundungus are missing feels like a threat hanging over us.
Obviously we have to keep track of everyone. I will make sure to tell the others as soon as anyone returns.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Stan?" repeated Hermione. "But I thought he was in Azkaban?"
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Well, Stan Shunpike isn't where we thought he was. He was supposed to be in Azkaban, but he's out.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "Hermione, there's obviously been a mass breakout which the Ministry has hushed up."
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: Obviously, there's been a mass breakout from prison and the Ministry is covering it up. Of course they'd try to hide it.

Book7-chapter5_Sc1.source: "He lost an ear," said Lupin."Lost an — ?" repeated Hermione in a high voice.
Book7-chapter5_Sc1.description: George has lost an ear. That's horrific and I can't stop thinking about how much he'll be hurt.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "I told them you’d take it like this," said Hermione with a hint of complacency.
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: Of course I expected Harry to be stubborn, but I also knew he would come round when he understood how dangerous it is if we do nothing.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Ooh, you look much tastier than Crabbe and Goyle, Harry," said Hermione, before catching sight of Ron’s raised eyebrows, blushing slightly, and saying, "Oh, you know what I mean - Goyle’s potion looked like bogies."
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: I notice details about how the potion changes people. I compare results and I make awkward jokes to lighten the tension even when it is serious.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "You can’t do it if I don’t cooperate, you need me to give you some hair."
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: I know Harry's cooperation is crucial. He is central to the plan and my confidence in the plan depends on him agreeing to help.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Well, it was easy," said Hermione in a small voice. "I just did a Summoning Charm. You know, Accio. And, they zoomed out of Dumbledore’s study window right into the girls’ dormitory."
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Well, it was easy. I did a Summoning Charm, Accio, and the books flew straight through the open window into the girls' dormitory.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Just after his Dumbledore’s funeral," said Hermione in an even smaller voice. "Right after we agreed we’d leave school and go and look for the Horcruxes. When I went back upstairs to get my things it, it just occurred to me that the more we knew about them, the better it would be... and I was alone in there... so I tried... and it worked. They flew straight in through the open window and I packed them."
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Obviously I took them right after Dumbledore's funeral, after we'd agreed to leave and hunt Horcruxes. I was alone, it occurred to me that the more we knew, the better, so I tried and it worked.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: "I can’t believe Dumbledore would have been angry, it’s not as though we’re going to use the information to make a Horcrux, is it?"
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Of course Dumbledore wouldn't have wanted us taking things, but I don't think he'd be angry if we use the info to stop Voldemort rather than to make a Horcrux.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: "This is the one that gives explicit instructions on how to make a Horcrux. Secrets of the Darkest Art — it’s a horrible book, really awful, full of evil magic."
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: This book, Secrets of the Darkest Art, gives explicit instructions on how to make a Horcrux. It's horrible and full of evil magic.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "And the more I’ve read about them," said Hermione, "the more horrible they seem, and the less I can believe that he actually made six. It warns in this book how unstable you make the rest of your soul by ripping it, and that’s just by making one Horcrux!"
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Well, the more I read the worse it gets. Making one Horcrux already makes the rest of your soul horribly unstable. I can hardly believe he made six.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Yes," said Hermione with a hollow smile, "but it would be excruciatingly painful."
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Of course you can put yourself back together but only through remorse and it would be excruciatingly painful.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Remorse," said Hermione. "You’ve got to really feel what you’ve done."
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Obviously the only way to mend a torn soul is real remorse. You have to truly feel what you've done.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "It doesn't have to be a basilisk fang," said Hermione patiently. "It has to be something so destructive that the Horcrux can't repair itself."
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: Well, a Horcrux can only be destroyed by something so viciously destructive that it cannot possibly mend itself. Of course that makes sense.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "From all that I've read, what Harry did to Riddle's diary was one of the few really foolproof ways of destroying a Horcrux."
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: The book warns Dark wizards how strong Horcrux protections must be, and stabbing a Horcrux with basilisk venom is one of the very few reliable methods to destroy one.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Basilisk venom only has one antidote, and it's incredibly rare —"
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: Obviously basilisk venom is almost irreversibly deadly and the only cure is phoenix tears, which are incredibly rare.

Book7-chapter6_Sc11.source: "Because a Horcrux is the complete opposite of a human being."
Book7-chapter6_Sc11.description: Well, of course, a Horcrux is the complete opposite of a human being. The fragment of soul inside depends entirely on its enchanted container for survival and it cannot exist without that container.

Book7-chapter6_Sc11.source: "Look, if I picked up a sword right now, Ron, and ran you through with it, I wouldn’t damage your soul at all."
Book7-chapter6_Sc11.description: Obviously, whatever happens to your body your soul will survive untouched, but a Horcrux fragment is the other way round and needs its container to keep existing.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: What we really need to decide," said Hermione, tossing Defensive Magical Theory into the bin without a second glance and picking up An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe, "is where we’re going after we leave here.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: Well, we have to decide where we go after we leave. Horcruxes should be our priority even if I can see why Harry wants Godric's Hollow first.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: There weren’t," said Hermione, who had turned pink. "Dumbledore removed them all, but he didn’t destroy them.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: Well, Dumbledore took the Horcrux books off the shelves but he didn't destroy them. They were still library books.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: It — it wasn’t stealing!" said Hermione, looking from Harry to Ron with a kind of desperation. "They were still library books, even if Dumbledore had taken them off the shelves.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: Of course I didn't steal them. I just took the books. They were still library property even if Dumbledore had hidden them. I'm desperate to help and I would never do something wrong on purpose.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "If I don’t — well, I think I’ve cast a good enough charm to keep them safe and happy."
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Well, I’ve put a charm on the Wilkins so they don’t even know they have a daughter. I’m trying to protect them.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "But hopefully it’ll look like I’ve gone away with Mum and Dad; a lot of Muggle-borns are talking about going into hiding at the moment," said Hermione.
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Of course it makes sense for me to seem to have gone off with my Muggle parents. Lots of Muggle-borns are planning to hide, so it looks plausible.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "We can’t hide my whole family, it’ll look too fishy and they can’t all leave their jobs," said Ron."
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Obviously I can’t get my whole family to vanish. It would draw attention and they can’t just abandon their lives.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "We were just talking about Mad-Eye," Ron told Harry. "I reckon he might have survived." "But Bill saw him hit by the Killing Curse," said Harry. "Yeah, but Bill was under attack too," said Ron. "How can he be sure what he saw?" "Even if the Killing Curse missed, Mad-Eye still fell about a thousand feet," said Hermione.
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Well, Moody fell a long way. Even if the Killing Curse missed, he still hit the ground from a great height, so we can't ignore the likelihood he's dead.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "It’s dreadful that he’s dead! But we’re being realistic!"
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Of course it would be awful if Moody is dead, but we have to be realistic and face the facts rather than hope for miracles.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "I’ve been packing for days, so we’re ready to leave at a moment’s notice, which for your information has included doing some pretty difficult magic, not to mention smuggling Mad-Eye’s whole stock of Polyjuice Potion right under Ron’s mum’s nose."
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: I've already packed and done hard magic to prepare. I even smuggled Moody's Polyjuice stock without Mrs Weasley noticing, so we're ready to leave whenever.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "I’ve also modified my parents’ memories so that they’re convinced they’re really called Wendell and Monica Wilkins, and that their life’s ambition is to move to Australia, which they have now done."
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Obviously I altered Mum and Dad's memories so Voldemort can't use them to find me. They're now convinced they've moved to Australia and have new identities until I undo it.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "Assuming I survive our hunt for the Horcruxes, I’ll find Mum and Dad and lift the enchantment."
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: I will go back for my parents if I make it through this. I can't leave it forever; I'm determined to lift the charm and bring them home when it's safe.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "You look vunderful." "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag... "I didn't know you were — goodness — it's lovely to see — how are you?"
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Well, obviously I was stunned to see Viktor. Of course I blushed and made a fuss. It was embarrassing but lovely to see him.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag...
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Well, this shows I'm flustered around Viktor. It matters to me enough to lose my composure in front of everyone.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "It should be, actually! But my point is that whatever happens to your body, your soul will survive, untouched," said Hermione. "But it’s the other way round with a Horcrux. The fragment of soul inside it depends on its container, its enchanted body, for survival. It can’t exist without it."
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: Well, of course your soul survives if your body is damaged, but a Horcrux is the other way round. The bit of soul inside a Horcrux needs its magical container to survive. It can't exist on its own.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "While the magical container is still intact, the bit of soul inside it can flit in and out of someone if they get too close to the object. I don’t mean holding it for too long, it’s nothing to do with touching it," she added before Ron could speak. "I mean close emotionally. Ginny poured her heart out into that diary, she made herself incredibly vulnerable. You’re in trouble if you get too fond of or dependent on the Horcrux."
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: Obviously, if the container's intact the soul bit can flit into someone who gets emotionally close to it. I mean emotionally close. Ginny poured her heart into that diary and made herself vulnerable. Be careful getting fond of or dependent on a Horcrux.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Of course they held onto Dumbledore's things so they could examine them. That is why it took so long to release the will.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "They wanted to examine whatever he’s left us. You had no right to do that!"
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Well, I believed the Ministry had no right to seize Dumbledore's bequests unless they had real proof the items were dangerous.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "'To Miss Hermione Jean Granger, I leave my copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard, in the hope that she will find it entertaining and instructive.'"
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Dumbledore left me The Tales of Beedle the Bard. He must have thought I'd like and learn from it, which of course means it's important to me.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "She held the book in her lap and gazed at it. Harry saw that the title was in runes; he had never learned to read them. As he looked, a tear splashed onto the embossed symbols."
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: I'm really touched. Of course I'm upset and emotional about what Dumbledore left me; it matters to me more than anyone outside Hogwarts might understand.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: Well, we're in Tottenham Court Road now. We need to walk, move, find somewhere safe.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: "It’s okay, I’ve got the Cloak, I’ve got clothes for both of you,"
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: Of course I packed essentials. I used an Undetectable Extension Charm to fit the Cloak and clothes in my bag.
Obviously, the Extension Charm works. I can hide a lot in a tiny bag when I need to.
Put the Cloak on now. Hurry and hide yourself so we can move without drawing more attention.
When things get dangerous I will act straight away. I will freeze an attacker if it helps protect my friends.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: "D-diffindo," she said, pointing her wand at Ron,
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: I will do whatever I can to free people, even if my hand is shaking and I mess it up and hurt them by accident.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "But how did they find us?" Hermione asked, looking from one inert man to the other.
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: How did they find us? Obviously something gave our location away and we need to figure out what it was.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "You — you don’t think you’ve still got your Trace on you, do you, Harry?"
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, it could be the Trace. Of course the Trace should break at seventeen, but what if someone has found a way round that? We have to consider that possibility.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "That m-must have b-been the T-Tongue-Tying Curse Mad-Eye set up for Snape!"
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: That tongue-tying curse was set up for Snape. Of course Mad-Eye would put protections like that on for someone like him.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "We’re not splitting up!" said Hermione firmly.
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: We are not splitting up. We have to stick together no matter what. Splitting up would be stupid and dangerous.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: Harry, will you come in here a moment?
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Well, I asked Harry to come to Ginny's room. Of course I wanted to keep things steady and sensible, even if everyone is a bit wound up.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: He took him by the elbow and tugged him on up the stairs.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Obviously I pulled Ron along and tried to keep things calm. I'm nervous about them, but I try to hold it together.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: There was a strained silence, then Ginny said in a flat little voice, 'Well, happy birthday anyway, Harry.' Hermione looked nervous.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt nervous after Ron barged in on Ginny and Harry. Of course it was awkward and I worried how everyone was feeling.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "It chose him, he was the one who found it, it came to him out of the Sorting Hat"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Of course I think the sword choosing a person matters. If it presented itself to Harry it might mean he’s worthy.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "He couldn’t tell us in the will why he was leaving us these things, but that still doesn’t explain"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Well, Dumbledore left things for a reason and he knew the Ministry would meddle. He must have been trying to hide meaning in plain sight.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Writing! There’s writing on it, quick, look!"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Obviously the Snitch is enchanted to reveal a message. I saw the writing appear and then disappear again.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "If these things are important enough to pass on right under the nose of the Ministry, you’d think he’d have let us know why . . . unless he thought it was obvious?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Of course he expected us to understand something, but I’m not convinced it was as obvious as he thought. We’re missing a piece.
The Tales of Beedle the Bard are important enough for Dumbledore to leave to me, yet I had never heard of them before this.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, of course the clippings are about Voldemort. Regulus seemed obsessed with him for a while before he joined the Death Eaters.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: If he was a Death Eater he had access to Voldemort, and if he became disenchanted, then he would have wanted to bring Voldemort down!
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: Obviously, if Regulus turned against Voldemort he would try to hide something that could undermine him.
There was a locket in the cabinet in the drawing room that nobody could open. That has to be the one.
I can pick basic locks. I opened Regulus's door so we could search his room properly.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: '"The Ministry is determined to root out such usurpers of magical power..."' (reading the Prophet)
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: Well, the Ministry are openly hunting Muggle-borns and demanding proof of Wizarding ancestry to attend school. That is terrifying and unjust.
Of course Tonks should be included in decisions about Remus. I don't like the idea of leaving her isolated or ignored.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'Remus!' whispered Hermione, tears in her eyes. 'Don’t say that — how could any child be ashamed of you?'
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: I'm protective of Remus. I can't stand him putting himself down or treating Tonks and their baby like they don't matter.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "I don't think so," said Hermione, though she looked frightened, "or they'd have sent Snape in after us, wouldn't they?"
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: Of course they'd send Snape if they knew. If he had been able to, he would have led them straight in.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "We wondered," said Hermione tentatively, "whether Harry could still have the Trace on him?" "Impossible," said Lupin.
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: Well, the Trace can't have been on Harry. That's obviously not how they tracked them in Tottenham Court Road. Something else is going on and that's worrying.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "So Death Eaters have taken over the Daily Prophet too?" asked Hermione furiously.
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: This is mental. The Prophet is being used to blame Harry instead of exposing Voldemort. People will be misled and frightened.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Of course, Voldemort would have considered the ways of house-elves far beneath his notice, just like all the purebloods who treat them like animals . . . It would never have occurred to him that they might have magic that he didn’t."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Of course Voldemort would have overlooked house-elf magic; pureblood arrogance blindfolds them to other kinds of magic.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "The house-elf’s highest law is his Master’s bidding,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: House-elves obey their masters above all else, so Kreacher did exactly what he was told.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "He’s a slave; house-elves are used to bad, even brutal treatment; what Voldemort did to Kreacher wasn’t that far out of the common way."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Well, house-elves accept abuse as normal, so Kreacher wasn't thinking politics, he was reacting to how people treated him.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Sirius was horrible to Kreacher, Harry, and it’s no good looking like that, you know it’s true."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Sirius treated Kreacher badly, and that affected how Kreacher behaved around the rest of the family and who he trusted.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "M-Master Regulus took from his pocket a locket like the one the Dark Lord had,"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Regulus brought back a locket Horcrux and tried to have Kreacher destroy it after swapping it.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "That’s — that’s pretty, Dolores," she said, pointing at the pendant gleaming in the ruffled folds of Umbridge’s blouse.
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: Well, I could see right away she was using that locket to pretend she belonged to proper wizarding families. It was insulting and obvious.
Of course I can duplicate an object quickly. I made a copy of the locket so Mrs. Cattermole would not wake and realize it was gone.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Relashio!" The chains clinked and withdrew into the arms of the chair.
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: I can break restraints and get people free. I used Relashio to release Mrs. Cattermole from the chair.

Book7-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Expecto patronum!" A silver otter burst from the end of Hermione’s wand
Book7-chapter13_Sc2.description: I worry about Patronuses, but I got one. At first I struggled and nothing happened, then I managed to produce an otter to push the dementors back.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: Hermione closed her eyes. "Harry, let him up!" whispered Hermione.
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Well, I want Harry to show some mercy. Of course I care about how Kreacher is treated even if he is unpleasant.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: Hermione closed her eyes and reacted to Kreacher's confession about the Dark Lord and the cave
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Of course this is important. Kreacher's story about Regulus and the cave fits with what we know about Horcrux protection and dark magic.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "You got in all right, then?" Hermione whispered to Harry.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, of course I was checking that we all made it in. I worried about you lot the whole time.
Of course I recognised what those carvings meant. They are treating Muggles like they belong beneath wizards.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "If it doesn’t, something's gone wrong with an Atmospheric Charm, which will be more difficult to fix, so as an interim measure try Impervius to protect his belongings," said Hermione.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Well, try Finite Incantatem first to stop the rain if it's a hex. If that fails then it's an Atmospheric Charm problem and it's nastier. Meanwhile cast Impervius to keep things dry.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "If we're going to get into the Ministry and not give ourselves away when they're bound to be on the lookout for intruders, every little detail matters!"
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Well, if we're going in, every tiny detail counts. We can't afford sloppy mistakes.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "'I'll be up on level one, Dolores wants to see me,'" Hermione recited immediately.
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Of course I remember what the bearded man said. Dolores wants someone on level one, so that's where her office is.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Hermione plucked a few hairs from the witch's head and added them to a flask of muddy Polyjuice Potion she had taken from the beaded bag."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Obviously I took hairs for the Polyjuice and finished the potion. We needed a perfect copy of Mafalda to get those tokens.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "'Take one of Mafalda's tokens,' Hermione told Harry, 'and let's go, it's nearly nine.'"
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Right, I handed over the tokens and told Harry to get moving. Timing matters, so we went when we had to.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "She passed Harry several curly black hairs, 'but he's gone home with a dreadful nosebleed! Here, he's pretty tall, you'll need bigger robes...'"
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Of course I found hairs from the maintenance guy and got robes ready. We had to make Harry look the part.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "As we Disapparated, Yaxley caught hold of me and I couldn’t get rid of him, he was too strong, and he was still holding on when we arrived at Grimmauld Place,"
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: Well, when we Apparated I couldn't shake Yaxley off because he had hold of me. He was still hanging on when we reached Grimmauld Place.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "I — I forced him to let go with a Revulsion Jinx, but I’d already taken him inside the Fidelius Charm’s protection."
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: Of course I tried a Revulsion Jinx to make him let go, but I'd already brought him inside the Fidelius protection first.

Book7-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Since Dumbledore died, we’re Secret-Keepers, so I’ve given him the secret, haven’t I?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc2.description: I think I've accidentally given Yaxley the secret to Grimmauld Place by bringing him into the Fidelius, so he's basically got access now.
He's really badly hurt and bleeding a lot. I can't risk doing complicated magic in case I make it worse.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "If we’re staying, we should put some protective enchantments around the place," she replied, and raising her wand, she began to walk in a wide circle around Harry and Ron, murmuring incantations as she went.
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: If we're staying we need protections. I'm going to set up enchantments now.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Salvio Hexia . . . Protego Totalum . . . Repello Muggletum . . . Muffliato . . ."
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: Right, Salvio Hexia, Protego Totalum, Repello Muggletum, Muffliato. Those should do the job.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Apparently he didn’t want it back, his lumbago’s so bad," said Hermione, now performing complicated figure-of-eight movements with her wand, "so Ron’s dad said I could borrow it."
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: Obviously Perkins left the tent because of his lumbago and Ron's dad let me borrow it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Erecto!" she added, pointing her wand at the misshapen canvas, which in one fluid motion rose into the air and settled, fully constructed, onto the ground before Harry... "Cave Inimicum," Hermione finished with a skyward flourish.
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: Erecto to set the tent up and Cave Inimicum to protect the site. That's as much as I can do for now.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: Before we go any farther, I think we’d better check,
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: Well, we should check for other people before moving on. Of course I will try a spell to reveal human presence.
Homenum revelio is the spell I used to look for human presence here. Obviously it would show if anyone else was in the house.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: Your scar, again? But what’s going on? I thought that connection had closed!
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: Of course I thought the connection was closed. I am frightened that Harry's scar is acting up again and that Voldemort might be getting through.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: But then you’ve got to close your mind!
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: Of course Harry must work on Occlumency and close his mind. Otherwise Voldemort can plant images in his head and trick him.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: I don’t want to be on my own. Could we use the sleeping bags I’ve brought and camp in here tonight?
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: I do not want to be alone. Of course I suggested we camp in the drawing room together with my sleeping bags so we are safer.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: Well, I stammered "Y-yes" when Umbridge addressed me because I was terrified and trying to do what I was told, even though this whole setup is unfair.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.source: she jumped so violently she nearly overturned the bottle of ink with which she was supposed to be recording the interview
Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: Of course I jumped when Harry whispered; I nearly knocked over my ink because I was already tense and frightened in that courtroom full of Dementors.

Book7-chapter13_Sc1.source: Here, behind a balustrade, sat Umbridge, with Yaxley on one side of her, and Hermione, quite as white-faced as Mrs. Cattermole, on the other.
Book7-chapter13_Sc1.description: Well, I was white-faced and trying to record everything properly while Umbridge sat there like she owned the place. It was humiliating having to help her.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Splinched," said Hermione, her fingers already busy at Ron's sleeve, where the blood was wettest and darkest.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Well, he has been Splinched. Of course I have to check the wound straight away.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Harry, quickly, in my bag, there’s a small bottle labeled ‘Essence of Dittany’ —"
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Quickly, grab the Dittany from my bag. Of course it's labeled and of course it should be used now.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Unstopper it for me, Harry, my hands are shaking." Hermione took it and poured three drops of the potion onto the bleeding wound.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: My hands are shaking but Dittany works. Pour three drops on the wound and the bleeding will stop.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Well, obviously if we're trapped here it would be catastrophic. We have to move fast and be logical about who has wands and who needs attaching to someone who does.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Hermione’s Patronus vanished with a pop as she turned a horror-struck face to Harry."
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Of course I panic when things go wrong. My Patronus can fail when I'm shocked, so I need to keep calm if we're to get people out.

Book7-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Grindelwald’s mark?" "I’ve never heard that Grindelwald had a mark. There’s no mention of it in anything I’ve ever read about him."
Book7-chapter16_Sc2.description: Well, I've never read anything about Grindelwald having a mark. Of course that makes this really strange.

Book7-chapter16_Sc2.source: "That’s very odd. If it’s a symbol of Dark Magic, what’s it doing in a book of children’s stories?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc2.description: This is odd. If it really signals Dark Magic, why is it in a children's book? That doesn't add up.

Book7-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Perhaps he thought it was an eye, just like I did."
Book7-chapter16_Sc2.description: Well, maybe Scrimgeour just saw it as an eye and didn't realize it meant anything darker.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "No, you shouldn’t," said Ron at once. "But he’s acting like one." "All the same . . ." said Hermione.
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Well, even if Lupin has been behaving badly, we should still be careful about how we treat him. I feel sympathetic but conflicted.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "For your information, none of the rest of us Disapparated."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Obviously, none of us Disapparated from the Ministry situation. Mundungus left on his own; we did not run.
I disarmed Mundungus quickly to stop him from using his wand. That gave us control of the situation.
When Mundungus hesitated, I jumped on the possibility that he still had the locket. I thought he might be hiding it.
I used Aguamenti to douse Mundungus when he caught fire from Harry's dropped wand sparks. Quick thinking and a simple charm saved him from worse harm.

Book7-chapter14_Sc4.source: Umbridge had stuck it to her office door, to spy on people. I couldn’t leave it there, but that’s how they knew there were intruders.
Book7-chapter14_Sc4.description: Of course she stuck it to her office door to spy on people. I couldn't leave it there, but that explains how they knew there were intruders.

Book7-chapter16_Sc3.source: "She did not speak, but continued to pore over the strange mark."
Book7-chapter16_Sc3.description: I'm still thinking about that strange mark on the book. It's important, obviously.

Book7-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Yes," she said. "Yes, I’ve been wondering that too. I really think we’ll have to."
Book7-chapter16_Sc3.description: Of course we have to go to Godric's Hollow. I've been wondering about it and I really think we'll have to.
I heard Harry. I'm listening and I agree with him.

Book7-chapter17_Sc4.source: "They shouldn’t have written on the sign!"
Book7-chapter17_Sc4.description: Well, of course they shouldn't have written on the sign. It's wrong and it's vandalism and it's not acceptable.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "What are we going to do with it?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: Well, of course we must keep the locket safe until we know how to destroy it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Keep it safe till we work out how to destroy it,"
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: We should take turns to keep watch and plan properly so nothing goes wrong while it's in our care.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: Well, of course we're not staying near the church. Let's head away from where we came in and keep moving before anyone notices us.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "How are we going to find Bathilda’s house?"
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: How are we going to find Bathilda's house? I'm starting to worry about where she actually lives and whether we're going to manage this in the dark.

Book7-chapter17_Sc2.source: "who was shivering a little and kept glancing back over her shoulder."
Book7-chapter17_Sc2.description: I'm cold and nervous. I'm glancing back because I can't shake the feeling someone might be following us.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: It was odd behavior to come out on a night this cold, simply to look at an old ruin
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: Well, of course it's strange she'd be out in this weather just staring at an old place. Something else is going on.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: There was next to no chance that this woman was a Muggle
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: Obviously she's not a Muggle. If she can see the house, she must be a witch.

Book7-chapter17_Sc5.source: By all the rules of normal magic, meanwhile, she ought not to be able to see Hermione and him at all
Book7-chapter17_Sc5.description: Of course the fact she can see us means ordinary rules don't apply. I don't trust this.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: What the hell, Snape as headmaster? That's mental and utterly wrong.

Phineas Nigellus's portrait can travel between Grimmauld Place and Dumbledore's office, but if Snape tried to use him now he'd only see the inside of my handbag, because I can hide the portrait there.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: "There’s nothing in here about navy blue robes, nothing!"
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: Everything matters. Even small details like robe colours could be important for figuring things out.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: Harry, stop. I really think someone's there watching us.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.source: ["There’s someone there. Someone watching us. I can tell. There, over by the bushes."]
Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: There's someone over by the bushes; I can tell—I'm sure I saw something move.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.source: ["I saw something move, I could have sworn I did."]
Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: I trusted my eyes; I broke away to free my wand arm because I'm convinced there's someone there and I need to be ready.

Book7-chapter17_Sc1.source: ["Harry, I’m sure there’s someone over there!"]
Book7-chapter17_Sc1.description: Of course I'm sure there's someone there; I'm not imagining it, and we shouldn't act like Muggles.

Book7-chapter17_Sc6.description: How does she know? Well, obviously that's terrifying. I pressed closer because I was scared and wanted to stay hidden.

Book7-chapter17_Sc8.description: I used Confringo under pressure to get us out of that mess. It can blast things and make a way.

Book7-chapter17_Sc8.source: "Harry, it’s okay, wake up, wake up!" and "Do you feel all — all right?"
Book7-chapter17_Sc8.description: I was terrified for Harry. Even when everything was chaos, I kept trying to pull him through and make sure he was conscious and safe.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "At the very least, we should know they're coming, I can't guarantee it will keep out Vol —"
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Well, we need warning if they're coming. I can't promise any protection will keep You Know Who out.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "Here." And she pulled the locket out of the pocket of her robes and handed it to Ron.
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Of course I kept the locket with me. I was the one who had it after the escape and handed it over so Ron could see it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "I think so," said Hermione, taking it back from him and looking at it closely. "There'd be some sign of damage if it had been magically destroyed."
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Well, the locket looks intact. If it had been destroyed magically there would be obvious damage, so it seems to still be a Horcrux.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "She passed it to Harry, who turned it over in his fingers."
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Of course I tried to use the charm that opened Regulus's bedroom door, but it didn't work on the locket.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: Harry, hurry or be careful, we might slip on the ice.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.source: "I wonder why nobody’s ever rebuilt it?"
Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: Why hasn't anyone rebuilt the cottage? It seems odd that it has been left like this.

Book7-chapter17_Sc3.source: "You’re not going to go inside? It looks unsafe, it might — oh, Harry, look!"
Book7-chapter17_Sc3.description: It looks unsafe to go inside. Also the sign appeared and we have to look at it.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, it's obviously Christmas Eve. That's what it feels like here.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "They . . . they’ll be in there, won’t they? Your mum and dad? I can see the graveyard behind it."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Of course they should be in the churchyard. I can see the graves behind the church and I think Harry's parents are there.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "'Look at this, it’s an Abbott, could be some long-lost relation of Hannah’s!' 'Keep your voice down,' Hermione begged him."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, I recognized names from Hogwarts. I was excited but I wanted Harry to be careful and not shout around graves.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Harry, here!" ... "No, but look!" She pointed to the dark stone. Harry stooped down and saw, upon the frozen, lichen-spotted granite, the words KENDRA DUMBLEDORE ... AND HER DAUGHTER ARIANA."
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: I found Dumbledore's mother's and sister's graves here. The Dumbledore family lived in Godric's Hollow and part of them died here.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "'Harry, that’s the mark in the book!'"
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Obviously that triangular symbol matched the mark from the book on Ignotus Peverell. I pointed it out because it could link to the tale of the Peverells.

Book7-chapter16_Sc5.source: "'It doesn’t mean defeating death in the way the Death Eaters mean it, Harry,' said Hermione,"
Book7-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, it doesn't mean what the Death Eaters think. The phrase on the grave isn't a Death Eater slogan. It means something different about death itself.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: “It’s not your fault. I wanted to go too; I really thought Dumbledore might have left the sword there for you.”
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: It's not your fault, Harry. I wanted to go as well and I thought Dumbledore might have left the sword at Godric's Hollow.

Book7-chapter17_Sc10.source: “What happened, Harry? What happened when she took you upstairs? Was the snake hiding somewhere?”
Book7-chapter17_Sc10.description: Tell me what happened when she took you upstairs. I need to know if the snake was hiding somewhere or if something else went wrong.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: We got away. Of course we did, but that doesn't mean we're out of danger yet.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "I had to use a Hover Charm to get you into your bunk, I couldn’t lift you."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: I had to use a Hover Charm to get you into your bunk because I couldn't physically lift you.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "You’ve been shouting and moaning and . . . things,"
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: You've been shouting and moaning and doing things you don't remember. It was horrible to hear.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "I couldn’t get the Horcrux off you," Hermione said... "It was stuck, stuck to your chest."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: The Horcrux was stuck to your chest and I couldn't get it off easily. It was firmly attached.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "You’ve got a mark; I’m sorry, I had to use a Severing Charm to get it away."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: You've got a mark where it was, and I had to use a Severing Charm to remove it. I'm sorry about the mark, I did what I had to.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: "The snake bit you too, but I’ve cleaned the wound and put some dittany on it."
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: The snake bit you as well, but I cleaned the wound and put dittany on it so it should start healing.

Book7-chapter17_Sc9.source: She had been wiping his face.
Book7-chapter17_Sc9.description: I wiped your face because you were covered in sweat and I couldn't just leave you like that.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: You cast the Muffliato charm over us, right?" he whispered to Hermione.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: Of course I put protections on us. I did Muffliato, Muggle-Repelling and Disillusionment Charms so they shouldn't be able to hear or see us, whoever they are.
They're goblins. I worked out from what they said that Griphook and Gornuk are with them, so we have goblins right nearby.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: Griphook said the sword at Gringotts is a wizard-made copy and not the goblin-forged original, so the real sword isn't in that vault. Obviously that's crucial.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: They punished Ginny and the others who tried to steal the sword, but apparently they survived without serious injury. That's a relief and also worrying.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Here . . . we . . . are . . ." she said between gritted teeth, and she pulled at something that was evidently in the depths of the bag.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: I always carry what we might need. I hauled out Phineas Nigellus's portrait because if the sword was swapped in Dumbledore's office, he would have seen it. Of course I'm prepared.

Book7-chapter17_Sc13.source: "I'm so, so sorry. I think it was me. As we were leaving, you know, the snake was coming for us, and so I cast a Blasting Curse, and it rebounded everywhere, and it must have — must have hit —"
Book7-chapter17_Sc13.description: I'm so, so sorry. I think I accidentally hit Harry's wand with a spell when the snake was coming. I didn't mean to wreck it.

Book7-chapter17_Sc13.source: "Harry, I don't think we're going to be able to," said Hermione, the tears trickling down her face. "Remember . . . remember Ron? When he broke his wand, crashing the car? It was never the same again, he had to get a new one."
Book7-chapter17_Sc13.description: Well, I don't think it's going to be fixable. Remember Ron's wand after the car crash? It was never right again.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Harry, what happened? Why do you think you couldn’t make your Patronus? You managed perfectly yesterday!"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Harry, why couldn't you make your Patronus this time? You did it yesterday, so something's changed or wrong.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Harry, give me the locket! Come on," she said impatiently, clicking her fingers at him when he did not react, "the Horcrux, Harry, you’re still wearing it!"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Don't have the Horcrux lying around. Let me wear it for a bit so none of us keeps it on too long. We need to take turns and keep it hidden.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "We can just keep it in the tent." "We are not leaving that Horcrux lying around," Harry stated firmly. "Oh, all right, all right," said Hermione, and she placed it around her own neck and tucked it out of sight down the front of her shirt. "But we’ll take turns wearing it, so nobody keeps it on too long."
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Okay fine. I'm wearing the locket now. We'll rotate it so no one is affected for too long.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "It’s not stealing, is it?" asked Hermione in a troubled voice, as they devoured scrambled eggs on toast. "Not if I left some money under the chicken coop?"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: I'm worried about taking food without asking. If I left money under the chicken coop then it isn't stealing, right? I still worry about the ethics of it.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Food is the first of the five Principal Exceptions to Gamp’s Law of Elemental Transfigur —"
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Well obviously food can't be created from nothing. You can summon or transform or increase it, but you can't make good food appear out of thin air.

Book7-chapter17_Sc12.description: Okay, I tried Reparo even though I wasn't sure it would work. The wand resealed but it only sparks weakly.

Book7-chapter17_Sc12.source: She reached down beside the bed and held it out to him.
Book7-chapter17_Sc12.description: Of course I couldn't leave him without trying. I felt horrible and I wanted to help even if I knew it might not be enough.

Book7-chapter17_Sc12.source: She was biting her lip, and tears swam in her eyes.
Book7-chapter17_Sc12.description: I care about Harry. Seeing him like that upset me enough that I nearly cried, and I did everything I could to fix his wand.

Book7-chapter17_Sc7.source: Hermione dived aside with a shriek, her deflected curse hit the curtained window which shattered
Book7-chapter17_Sc7.description: Well, of course I had to move. I dived aside with a shriek and my curse glanced off the window and smashed it. I had to act fast to avoid the snake.

Book7-chapter17_Sc7.source: They stepped toward the woman and, at once, she turned and hobbled off back the way they had come
Book7-chapter17_Sc7.description: I nodded and followed. I'm with Harry on this, even when it's dangerous. We stick together and we keep going.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: She was curled up in one of the sagging armchairs with The Tales of Beedle the Bard. He could not imagine how much more she could get out of the book, which was not, after all, very long; but evidently she was still deciphering something in it, because Spellman’s Syllabary lay open on the arm of the chair.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Of course I'm still studying The Tales of Beedle the Bard. I'm working through everything carefully and I'm using Spellman’s Syllabary to help decode it.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: “Look at that symbol,” she said, pointing to the top of a page. Above what Harry assumed was the title of the story (being unable to read runes, he could not be sure), there was a picture of what looked like a triangular eye, its pupil crossed with a vertical line. “I never took Ancient Runes, Hermione.” “I know that, but it isn’t a rune and it’s not in the syllabary, either. All along I thought it was a picture of an eye, but I don’t think it is! It’s been inked in, look, somebody’s drawn it there, it isn’t really part of the book.”
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Well, that symbol isn't a rune and it isn't in the syllabary. It's been inked in by someone. Of course it looks like an eye at first, but it's been drawn into the book and that's suspicious.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: They had just eaten an unusually good meal: Hermione had been to a supermarket under the Invisibility Cloak (scrupulously dropping the money into an open till as she left),
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: Obviously I slipped into a supermarket under the Invisibility Cloak and paid properly. We need to be careful but honest where we can be.

Book7-chapter16_Sc1.source: Hermione shoved him back inside the beaded bag every time he did this, and Phineas Nigellus invariably refused to reappear for several days after these unceremonious good-byes.
Book7-chapter16_Sc1.description: I won't let Phineas pry. I shove him back in the beaded bag whenever he asks nosy questions. He sulks and doesn't reappear for days.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: It was in Bathilda’s sitting room, just lying there.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, I found a pristine copy of The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore in Bathilda's sitting room. It was just there.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: This note was sticking out of the top of it.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Of course there was a note stuck in it. It said 'Dear Batty, Thanks for your help. Here’s a copy of the book, hope you like it. You said everything, even if you don’t remember it. Rita.'

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: Hermione read the few lines of spiky, acid-green writing aloud.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: I read the note out loud because Harry needed to know Rita had been involved and the book had been sent to Bathilda.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: “Harry?” Hermione looked frightened that he might curse her with her own wand. Her face streaked with tears, she crouched down beside him, two cups of tea trembling in her hands and something bulky under her arm.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm scared of upsetting Harry. I came close to leaving him alone but I couldn't. I was shaking and crying because I care.

Book7-chapter18_Sc1.source: “You’re still really angry at me, aren’t you?” said Hermione; he looked up to see fresh tears leaking out of her eyes, and knew that his anger must have shown in his face.
Book7-chapter18_Sc1.description: Well, I thought Harry was still furious with me, but he told me it was an accident and that he knows I saved him.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "It — it doesn't make very nice reading —"
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: Well, that book is horrible to read. It's upsetting stuff and we should remember who wrote it.
Of course I read the letter to Grindelwald. I did it and it bothers me.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "He changed, Harry, he changed! It's as simple as that! Maybe he did believe these things when he was seventeen, but the whole of the rest of his life was devoted to fighting the Dark Arts!"
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: Dumbledore wasn't the same person his whole life. He may have been wrong as a teenager but he spent his life fighting for the right things.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "He loved you," Hermione whispered. "I know he loved you."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: I believe Dumbledore loved you, Harry. I know he did, even if he didn't tell you everything.

Book7-chapter18_Sc3.source: "All that 'right to rule' rubbish, it's 'Magic Is Might' all over again."
Book7-chapter18_Sc3.description: Obviously that stuff about ruling Muggles is monstrous. It sounds just like other dangerous ideas we've seen.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: What the hell? That's revolting. Bathilda was the snake and she was dead inside her body.

Book7-chapter17_Sc11.source: Harry no I'm sure you ought to rest
Book7-chapter17_Sc11.description: No, you need to rest. You look terrible and you shouldn't be up like this.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: But it must have been a Patronus!
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: Well, of course it was a Patronus. It was a silver doe and it led you to the sword so it had to be one.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: Couldn’t you see who was casting it? Didn’t you see anyone? And it led you to the sword! I can’t believe this! Then what happened?
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: Well, I didn’t see anyone casting it. The Patronus led you to the sword and I can’t believe you actually got it. Tell me exactly how it happened.

Book7-chapter19_Sc12.source: I still haven’t ruled it out,
Book7-chapter19_Sc12.description: Well, I still haven't ruled it out. I might be wrong but I'm not dismissing it yet.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "'Please' always helps," said a cold, snide voice, and Phineas Nigellus slid into his portrait.
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Please works when you are polite to portraits. Of course asking nicely matters.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Obscuro!" A black blindfold appeared over Phineas Nigellus's clever, dark eyes
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I used Obscuro to blind Phineas so he could not see where we were. Obviously a necessary precaution.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I believe that the last time I saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Phineas remembers Dumbledore taking the sword to break a ring. That proves Dumbledore took it out before Ginny did.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Goblin-made armor does not require cleaning, simple girl. Goblins' silver repels mundane dirt, imbibing only that which strengthens it."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: Goblin-made blades imbibe only what makes them stronger. If the sword absorbed basilisk venom then it can destroy Horcruxes.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I . . ." She looked anguished. "Yes - yes, I'm staying. Ron, we said we'd go with Harry, we said we'd help -"
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I will stay with Harry and help. I am not leaving him even though Ron walked out.

Book7-chapter19_Sc9.source: “No, actually,” said Hermione. “We’ve been Disapparating under the Invisibility Cloak as an extra precaution. And we left really early, because, as Harry says, we’d heard somebody blundering around.”
Book7-chapter19_Sc9.description: Well, of course we Disapparated under the Invisibility Cloak to be extra careful. We left early because we'd heard someone blundering about.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "No, actually," said Hermione. "We've been Disapparating under the Invisibility Cloak as an extra precaution. And we left really early, because, as Harry says, we'd heard somebody blundering around."
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: Well, of course we Disapparated under the Invisibility Cloak to be extra careful, and we left early because we heard someone blundering about.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "Yeah," said Harry and Hermione together automatically.
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: Obviously I agreed that the light Ron described looked like the kind around a Portkey. It just fitted what he said.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "Give it back to me!" "Don’t you tell me what to do, Harry Potter!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: Well, of course I'm furious and desperate about my wand. Don't you dare tell me to calm down.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "I don’t care what he’s done! Weeks and weeks, we could have been dead for all he knew —"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: Well, I don't care about any of Ron's excuses. He left when we needed him and that could have been fatal.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "How exactly did you find us tonight?"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: Of course I need to know how he found us so we can make sure no one unwanted can find us again.
So my voice somehow came out of that Deluminator. That is surprising and embarrassing.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: “What’s wrong? Harry? Are you all right?”
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: Well, of course I check on Harry straight away. If he calls my name I'm going to make sure he's okay.
Of course I want to know who has come into the tent. I don't accept mystery intruders without answers.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: Hermione launched herself forward and started punching every inch of him that she could reach.
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: I am furious with Ron for coming back. I feel betrayed and I want to make him pay for leaving us and for whatever he did while he was away.
You are a complete arse Ronald Weasley. I can't stand how he left and how thoughtless he was.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: “You — crawl — back — here — after — weeks — and — weeks — oh, where’s my wand?”
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: You crawl back here after weeks and weeks and expect everything to be as before. Of course I'm furious and of course I want my wand.
I will not calm down. I am not ready to forgive or listen right now. My emotions are in charge and I mean it.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "I want to go and see Xenophilius Lovegood."
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: I want us to go see Xenophilius Lovegood, Luna's father. He might know about that symbol.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "The signature," said Hermione. "Look at the signature, Harry!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: Of course that mark keeps appearing. Seeing Dumbledore's A changed into that triangle proves it's important.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "It keeps cropping up, doesn’t it?" "He was wearing the symbol at the wedding."
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: The mark showed up on a grave, in Dumbledore's letter, and Mr. Lovegood wore it at the wedding. Obviously we should ask Mr. Lovegood about it.

Book7-chapter20_Sc9.source: "Well, I agree with Ron," said Hermione. "Awful old hypocrite, telling everyone else to help you and trying to worm out of it himself."
Book7-chapter20_Sc9.description: Well, he's an awful old hypocrite, telling everyone else to help and trying to worm out of it himself.

Book7-chapter20_Sc9.source: "And for heaven’s sake keep away from that horn."
Book7-chapter20_Sc9.description: Well, whatever else is going on, keep away from that horn.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "It was only people who were serious about standing up to him, like Dumbledore, who ever dared use it."
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: Well, only people prepared to stand up to him, people like Dumbledore, ever used that name aloud.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Now they’ve put a Taboo on it, anyone who says it is trackable — quick-and-easy way to find Order members! They nearly got Kingsley —"
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: Of course they put a Taboo on the name so anyone who says it can be tracked. That's a quick way to find Order members and they nearly caught Kingsley.

Book7-chapter21_Sc4.description: Of course the youngest brother kept the Cloak and only gave it to his son when he was ready to die. He greeted Death as an old friend and went with him gladly. It all ties up neatly and tragically.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: Hermione’s sulkiness could not mar his buoyant spirits: ... Late in the afternoon he and Ron escaped Hermione’s baleful presence again, and under the pretense of scouring the bare hedges for nonexistent blackberries, they continued their ongoing exchange of news.
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Well, I may be sulky and moody, but that does not change the fact we have to keep focused. Of course I worry, but I will keep at the facts.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: Hermione (nose buried in a book at the tent entrance) to scowl over at them.
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Obviously I am buried in reading because we need answers. I'm not impressed with fooling around when there is work to be done.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: It was gloriously warm after the pool and the forest, the only illumination the bluebell flames still shimmering in a
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: Well, of course I was asleep in the tent when they came back. They'll be relieved we're all together again.

Book7-chapter21_Sc1.source: Hermione said, "I've got a copy, Mr Lovegood, I I've got it right here."
Book7-chapter21_Sc1.description: Of course I have a copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard. I have the original with me.
Well, all right then. I'll read the Tale aloud so we all understand it.

Book7-chapter20_Sc7.source: "looking first at Hermione, then at Ron, and finally at Harry"
Book7-chapter20_Sc7.description: Well, he looked at me first. Obviously he was trying to work out what to do, and I was ready to be sensible about it.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Well, the sword, Harry! Dumbledore must have known you’d want to go back there, and I mean, Godric’s Hollow is Godric Gryffindor’s birthplace —"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Well, of course the sword could be in Godric's Hollow. Dumbledore must have guessed you'd want to go there and Godric's Hollow is where Gryffindor came from.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "There’s a bit about the village in A History of Magic, wait . . ."
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Obviously there is information in A History of Magic about Godric's Hollow. I dug the book out to check the history and the graveyard and stuff.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "The graveyard is full of the names of ancient magical families, and this accounts, no doubt, for the stories of hauntings that have dogged the little church beside it for many centuries.'"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Godric's Hollow has a graveyard full of old magical families. That explains the haunting stories about the little church.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "You and your parents aren’t mentioned," Hermione said, closing the book, "because Professor Bagshot doesn’t cover anything later than the end of the nineteenth century. But you see? Godric’s Hollow, Godric Gryffindor, Gryffindor’s sword; don’t you think Dumbledore would have expected you to make the connection?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Of course. Bagshot doesn't cover recent history so Harry and his parents won't be in the book. But it all adds up. Godric's Hollow and Gryffindor's sword go together and Dumbledore would have expected Harry to work that out.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Harry, what if Bathilda’s got the sword? What if Dumbledore entrusted it to her?"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: Well, it's possible Dumbledore left the sword with Bathilda. We have to consider that even if Bathilda might be very old or not all there.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "Yes, but we’ll have to think it through carefully, Harry." "We’ll need to practice Disapparating together under the Invisibility Cloak for a start, and perhaps Disillusionment Charms would be sensible too, unless you think we should go the whole hog and use Polyjuice Potion? In that case we’ll need to collect hair from somebody. I actually think we’d better do that, Harry, the thicker our disguises the better."
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: We must plan everything. We should practice Disapparating under the Cloak, use Disillusionment Charms, and probably use Polyjuice Potion. The thicker our disguises the better. We will need to collect hair if we do Polyjuice.

Book7-chapter16_Sc4.source: "All this snow!" Hermione whispered beneath the cloak. "Why didn’t we think of snow? After all our precautions, we’ll leave prints! We’ll just have to get rid of them — you go in front, I’ll do it —"
Book7-chapter16_Sc4.description: All this snow will leave prints. Of course we have to sort them out. I'll clear the prints if Harry goes ahead. We cannot be careless.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: Well, I'm sure this is important. Of course we should take any lead that might matter.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “Maybe . . . maybe it’s something you need to find out for yourself,”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: Maybe this is something Harry needs to find out for himself. It might be personal and he has to learn it the hard way.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “A symbol that links Dumbledore, Grindelwald, and Godric’s Hollow? Harry, I’m sure we ought to know about this!”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: Obviously a symbol connecting Dumbledore, Grindelwald and Godric's Hollow is worth investigating. We ought to know what it means.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "For ten minutes or so Ron tapped and muttered, Hermione turned the pages of her book"
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Well, obviously I'm not going to join in with gossip. I kept reading instead of making a scene.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Speaking of Dumbledore, have you heard what Skeeter wrote about him?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Of course I've heard about Skeeter's piece on Dumbledore. It's ridiculous that they make it into a scandal.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "But there's no mention of the words 'Deathly Hallows' in the story," said Hermione.
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: Well, obviously the tale doesn't call them 'Deathly Hallows', but that does not mean the story couldn't be describing three real objects.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "We all know that there are such things as Invisibility Cloaks. They are rare, but they exist. But —"
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: Of course invisibility cloaks exist, but I am not convinced every cloak is the legendary one that renders someone eternally and completely invisible.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "Say the Cloak existed . . . what about the stone, Mr. Lovegood? The thing you call the Resurrection Stone?"
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: Well, if the cloak could be true, the Resurrection Stone still sounds absurd. You cannot expect me to prove every pebble is not a magical relic.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "But that's — I'm sorry, but that's completely ridiculous! How can I possibly prove it doesn't exist? Do you expect me to get hold of — of all the pebbles in the world and test them?"
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: I refuse to accept 'prove a negative' as a reasonable argument. Of course that is not how you establish something exists.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“They both looked at the ornate silver sword, its rubied hilt glinting a little in the light from Hermione’s wand.”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: I’ve got my wand on and I’m lighting the place up so we can see the sword properly.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: Well, of course I had to ask what that enormous horn was. It looked wrong.
Obviously it is not a Crumple-Horned Snorkack horn.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "But Harry, it’s an Erumpent horn! It’s a Class B Tradeable Material and it’s an extraordinarily dangerous thing to have in a house!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: That's an Erumpent horn. It's Class B tradeable and it can explode at the slightest touch, so it is dangerously irresponsible to keep it inside a house.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "Mr Lovegood, I recognize the grooved markings around the base, that’s an Erumpent horn and it’s incredibly dangerous — I don’t know where you got it —"
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: Of course I can tell by the grooved markings that it's an Erumpent horn. I don't care where he got it, he must get rid of it immediately.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: 'There were once three brothers who were traveling along a lonely, winding road at twilight —'
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Well, of course the tale opens with three brothers traveling on a lonely road at twilight; that's the whole set-up of the story.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: 'In time, the brothers reached a river too deep to wade through and too dangerous to swim across. However, these brothers were learned in the magical arts, and so they simply waved their wands and made a bridge appear across the treacherous water.'
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Obviously the brothers were skilled wizards; they just conjured a bridge instead of risking the river.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: 'Then the second brother, who was an arrogant man, decided that he wanted to humiliate Death still further, and asked for the power to recall others from Death.'
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Of course the second asked for the power to bring people back from Death; he wanted to mock Death by undoing it.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: Well, I'm asking Harry if he trusts me because we need to act together. Of course I expect him to follow my lead.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "All right," breathed Hermione, as the broken printing press blocking the top of the stairs began to tremble; Xenophilius was feet away from them.
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: Obviously the danger is right on top of us. We have to be as quick and quiet as possible.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "She managed to free Ron with the use of a Hover Charm."
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: Of course I used a Hover Charm to free Ron. It worked and now he can put the Invisibility Cloak on.

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "Please, Ron! Harry, hold on tight to my hand, Ron, grab my shoulder."
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: Of course I expect cooperation from Ron and Harry. I'm taking charge because it's necessary and I need them to trust me.

Book7-chapter21_Sc9.source: “Hold tight,” she whispered. “Hold tight . . . any second . . .”
Book7-chapter21_Sc9.description: Well, hold tight. Of course, just hang on a moment, it'll happen any second.

Book7-chapter21_Sc9.source: “Obliviate!” cried Hermione, pointing her wand first into his face, then at the floor beneath them. “Deprimo!”
Book7-chapter21_Sc9.description: Obliviate, then Deprimo. Of course I need to erase his memory and then move the press downwards to clear the stairs.

Book7-chapter21_Sc6.source: That was the name on the grave with the mark on it, in Godric’s Hollow, Ignotus Peverell.
Book7-chapter21_Sc6.description: Well, Ignotus Peverell was the name on that grave in Godric's Hollow. Of course that link matters.

Book7-chapter21_Sc6.source: The sign of the Deathly Hallows on Ignotus’s grave is conclusive proof!
Book7-chapter21_Sc6.description: Obviously the sign on Ignotus's grave suggests the Peverells are the three brothers from the tale and were the original owners of the Hallows.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "That’s why I wanted the Death Eaters to get a glimpse of Harry before we left, so they knew Xenophilius hadn’t been lying!"
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: Of course I wanted the Death Eaters to see Harry so they'd know Xenophilius wasn't lying about him.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "Oh, I hope they don’t kill him!" groaned Hermione.
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: I really hope Xenophilius isn't killed. I can't bear the thought of that happening to him.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "They’re in Australia," said Hermione. "They should be all right. They don’t know anything."
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: My parents are in Australia and they should be safe because they don't know anything about what's going on.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Hermione was lying at Bellatrix’s feet. She was barely stirring."
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Well, I got seriously hurt. I was knocked out and looked very vulnerable at Bellatrix's mercy.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "'Drop your wands,' she whispered. 'Drop them, or we’ll see exactly how filthy her blood is!'"
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Of course I know what Bellatrix will do. She is capable of aiming to terrorize and humiliate, and she used me as bait to force them to surrender.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Bellatrix was supporting Hermione, who seemed to be unconscious, and was holding her short silver knife to Hermione’s throat."
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Obviously Bellatrix hates me in a very personal way. That is terrifying and makes her utterly dangerous to my friends and me.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.source: "We found it — we found it — PLEASE!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: We tried to be honest under torture and I kept shouting that we found the sword. I was desperate and terrified and said the same thing over and over.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.source: "We’ve never been inside your vault. . . . It isn’t the real sword! It’s a copy, just a copy!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: I said the sword is a copy to stop them believing we raided Gringotts. I argued it logically while being tortured because logic is what I reach for even when panicking.
I know how strong I am under pressure, but being screamed for and tortured felt unbearable. I keep fighting to stay upright and to think.

Book7-chapter22_Sc2.description: Harry? Well, I called his name because he was lost in thought and fiddling with the cloak, and I was worried.

Book7-chapter25_Sc3.description: Well, I don't like this plan. It's clever and all, but it doesn't sit right with me emotionally even if it makes sense.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Romulus, do you maintain, as you have every time you’ve appeared on our program, that Harry Potter is still alive?" "I do," said Lupin firmly.
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Well, of course Lupin still insists Harry is alive. That should reassure anyone listening who wants evidence rather than panic.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "And I'd tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right."
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Well, obviously Lupin believes in Harry's instincts. Hearing that makes me cry because it's such a hopeful thing to say about someone we care about.

Book7-chapter22_Sc4.source: "Rubeus Hagrid... has narrowly escaped arrest within the grounds of Hogwarts... Hagrid was not taken into custody, and is, we believe, on the run."
Book7-chapter22_Sc4.description: Of course Hagrid escaped arrest and is on the run. That sounds reckless and worrying, but it also shows his commitment to supporting Harry.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Goblins have got good reason to dislike wizards, Ron," said Hermione. "They’ve been treated brutally in the past."
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: Well, goblins have been treated badly by wizards in the past. Of course that explains a lot of their anger.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Ron, he’d know the difference better than we would!" said Hermione. "He’s the only one who realized there had been a swap!"
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: Of course Griphook would spot a fake. He's far better at goblin-made things than we are.

Book7-chapter25_Sc2.source: "That," she said quietly, "is despicable. Ask for his help, then double-cross him? And you wonder why goblins don’t like wizards, Ron?"
Book7-chapter25_Sc2.description: I can't stand the idea of tricking Griphook. We shouldn't double-cross him if we want his help and any chance of trust.

Book7-chapter25_Sc5.source: ["We’ve named him Ted, after Dora’s father!"]
Book7-chapter25_Sc5.description: We named the baby Ted after Dora's father. Of course it's a lovely, proper name.

Book7-chapter25_Sc5.source: ["Wha — ? Tonks — Tonks has had the baby?"]
Book7-chapter25_Sc5.description: Tonks has had the baby. Well, that's wonderful news, absolutely brilliant.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "I’m sorry, but I think you’ve got this wrong, all wrong."
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Well, I don't think the Deathly Hallows theory holds up. I really think Harry is jumping to the wrong conclusion.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "If the Deathly Hallows really existed, and Dumbledore knew about them, knew that the person who possessed all three of them would be master of Death — Harry, why wouldn’t he have told you? Why?"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Of course, if Dumbledore had believed the Hallows meant mastery over death, he would have warned Harry. I can't see why he would hide something so important from him.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Harry, this isn’t a game, this isn’t practice! This is the real thing, and Dumbledore left you very clear instructions: Find and destroy the Horcruxes!"
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: We must focus on destroying Horcruxes. This is not the time for fanciful quests after legendary objects.

Book7-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Thank you, Ron. I’ll take first watch."
Book7-chapter22_Sc3.description: Of course I'm taking responsibility for watch. We have to be practical and keep each other safe rather than chase distractions.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "We protest! And I’m hunted quite as much as any goblin or elf, Griphook! I’m a Mudblood!"
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, of course I can see this is about more than just wizards and goblins. I am directly affected by the new order and I will stand up and say it.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "Did you know that it was Harry who set Dobby free?"
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, Harry has a history of standing up for others. That matters to Griphook and it strengthens his reasons to consider us.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "We’ve wanted elves to be freed for years"
Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Of course I have wanted house-elves freed for a long time and I made that clear. It ties our cause to the wider injustices goblins face.

Book7-chapter24_Sc2.source: "It was me they chose to torture, back at the Malfoys’!"
