Book7-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, I was tortured because of blood status. That gives me standing when arguing against the way wand-carriers treat other magical folk.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: Hermione was wrapped in a borrowed dressing gown, pale and unsteady on her feet
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: I was badly shaken and exhausted, but I held myself together enough to help when it mattered.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: You were amazing - coming up with that story when she was hurting you like that -
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: I know I was pushed to my limits, but I did what I had to. I can be brave and clever under pressure, even if it nearly breaks me.

Book7-chapter24_Sc1.source: Hermione gave a weak smile as Ron gave her a one-armed squeeze
Book7-chapter24_Sc1.description: I need my friends. When I'm fragile, Ron and the others are the ones who steady me.

Book7-chapter28_Sc1.description: Well, we should get out of here right now. Disapparate and go.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "No!" said Hermione, sounding frightened. "He can’t know that, Harry, how could he— ?"
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Of course I'm terrified at the thought that Voldemort might learn your wand is broken. That would be horrible and dangerous.

Book7-chapter24_Sc3.source: "We left your wand and the blackthorn wand at the Malfoys', Hermione. If they examine them properly, make them re-create the spells they’ve cast lately, they’ll see that yours broke mine, they’ll see that you tried and failed to mend it, and they’ll realize that I’ve been using the blackthorn one ever since."
Book7-chapter24_Sc3.description: Obviously if they study those wands closely they can work out what happened. They might figure out my wand broke and that you've been using the blackthorn wand instead.

Book7-chapter26_Sc3.description: Of course I tried summoning the cup first. It would have worked if the vault hadn't been tricked. I always go for the sensible spell.
I can hoist someone up by the ankle to reach things. It hurts them a bit but it buys crucial seconds.
I use protective spells to try to keep us from burning. Quick, practical magic when things heat up.
I panic when Harry acts recklessly, but I will still climb and follow because leaving him isn't an option. Brains and bravery both matter.
I can dig through rock when needed. I try to think ahead and solve problems even while everything is collapsing around us.

Book7-chapter27_Sc4.source: "What’ll happen to it, do you think? Will it be all right?"
Book7-chapter27_Sc4.description: Well, of course I'm worrying about the dragon. What'll happen to it? Will it be all right?

Book7-chapter29_Sc1.description: Well, I was not trying to keep the dragon as a pet. Obviously that was never realistic.

Book7-chapter29_Sc1.source: Neville held out his hand to Hermione and helped her to climb up onto the mantelpiece and into the tunnel;
Book7-chapter29_Sc1.description: Neville helped me get into the tunnel. Of course I appreciated it and trusted him to get us moving.

Book7-chapter27_Sc3.source: What'll happen to it, do you think? Will it be all right?
Book7-chapter27_Sc3.description: Well, of course I'm worried about the dragon, what will happen to it and will it be all right

Book7-chapter28_Sc3.source: "He, Ron, and Hermione retreated down the side street, groping their way along the wall, trying not to make a sound."
Book7-chapter28_Sc3.description: Well, we were crawling along the wall, keeping absolutely quiet and trying not to make a sound, because the dementors were nearby.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Well, that wand is not Bellatrix's. Obviously something about it is wrong and I had to say so.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "The Thief’s Downfall!" said Griphook, clambering to his feet and looking back at the deluge onto the tracks, which, Harry knew now, had been more than water.
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Of course the Thief's Downfall strips away enchantments. It washes foolproof disguises and enchantments right off.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "Harry, I think I can hear people coming!" said Hermione, and she pointed Bellatrix’s wand at the waterfall and cried, "Protego!"
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Well, shielding spells can stop that enchanted water. I used Protego to halt the flow so we could get away.

Book7-chapter26_Sc2.source: "C-Cushioning Charm," Hermione spluttered, as Ron pulled her to her feet, but to Harry’s horror he saw that she was no longer Bellatrix; instead she stood there in overlarge robes, sopping wet and completely herself;
Book7-chapter26_Sc2.description: Of course I knew the Cushioning Charm. But the Thief's Downfall proved that no matter how clever a disguise, some defenses will undo it.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "Professor Dumbledore cared about Harry, very much," said Hermione in a low voice.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: Of course Dumbledore cared about Harry. He cared enough to make plans for him even if he did not say everything.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "‘The Order of the Phoenix is finished,’" Harry repeated.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: Well, we all know the Order has been shattered and things look grim. That does not mean we stop thinking and acting.

Book7-chapter28_Sc5.source: "I’m so . . . I’m so sorry," Hermione whispered.
Book7-chapter28_Sc5.description: I feel horrified and sorry about what happened to Ariana. It makes me more determined that people who suffer because of lies or neglect need justice and care.

Book7-chapter29_Sc2.source: "From his pocket he pulled a golden coin, and Harry recognized it as one of the fake Galleons that Dumbledore’s Army had used to send one another messages. 'These have been great,' said Neville, beaming at Hermione."
Book7-chapter29_Sc2.description: Obviously the fake Galleons worked. Our secret communications kept going and gave people a lifeline even with the Carrows watching.

Book7-chapter29_Sc2.source: "These have been great," said Neville, beaming at Hermione.
Book7-chapter29_Sc2.description: Well, Neville looks to me like someone who really appreciated what we set up. Our efforts meant something to them.

Book7-chapter29_Sc3.source: "They what?" said Harry, Ron, and Hermione together.
Book7-chapter29_Sc3.description: What the hell? They went after Neville's gran to try to get to him. That's vicious and completely unjustifiable.

Book7-chapter29_Sc3.source: "Look who it is! Didn’t I tell you?" As Harry emerged into the room beyond the passage, there were several screams and yells: "HARRY!" "It’s Potter, it’s POTTER!" "Ron!" "Hermione!"
Book7-chapter29_Sc3.description: Of course people here are relieved and excited to see us — this hideout is clearly a safe place for the D.A.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “I hate this thing,” she said in a low voice. “I really hate it. It feels all wrong, it doesn’t work properly for me. . . . It’s like a bit of her.”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Well, I hate Bellatrix’s wand. Of course it feels wrong to me. It’s like carrying a piece of her and it unsettles me.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “This is the wand that tortured Neville’s mum and dad, and who knows how many other people? This is the wand that killed Sirius!”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Of course I know what that wand has done. It’s linked to terrible things and terrible people. That matters.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “I miss my wand,” Hermione said miserably. “I wish Mr. Ollivander could have made me another one too.”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Well, I miss my own wand. I wish Ollivander could have made me a replacement. It’s difficult working without it.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “There,” said Hermione, “how does he look, Harry?”
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: I’ve transformed Ron into Bellatrix’s male lackey. Of course I need to know if the disguise is convincing enough for Harry.

Book7-chapter26_Sc1.source: “Madam Lestrange,” murmured Tom, and as Hermione passed he inclined his head subserviently. “Good morning,” said Hermione, and as Harry crept past, still carrying Griphook piggyback under the Cloak, he saw Tom look surprised.
Book7-chapter26_Sc1.description: Obviously I have to play the part precisely. I must be polite and commanding enough to make people believe I am Madam Lestrange.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: Well, we cannot just rush off. We need a plan before we try anything.

Book7-chapter27_Sc5.source: "We can’t just go, we haven’t got a plan, we need to"
Book7-chapter27_Sc5.description: Of course we do not have a plan yet. We need to think and prepare before attempting to get into Hogwarts.
Well, the three of us do not fit properly under the cloak, at least not comfortably, though it might be dark enough that no one notices our feet.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Penelope Clearwater," said Hermione. She sounded terrified, but convincing. "What’s your blood status?" "Half-blood," said Hermione.
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: I used an alias, Penelope Clearwater, and said I was a half-blood to try to fool them. Well, it was terrifying but necessary.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "It isn’t! It isn’t me!" Hermione’s terrified squeak was as good as a confession.
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: When they showed the picture from the Prophet I freaked out. Of course I shouted that it wasn't me, because they were trying to force a confession.

Book7-chapter23_Sc1.source: "' . . . known to be traveling with Harry Potter,'" repeated Greyback quietly.
Book7-chapter23_Sc1.description: They're convinced I'm with Harry now because of that picture. Obviously that puts me in immediate danger.

Book7-chapter32_Sc2.source: "No," said Hermione, "it makes much more sense if I take the Cloak and —"
Book7-chapter32_Sc2.description: Well, it obviously makes more sense if I take the Cloak and go. I’m being practical about this.

Book7-chapter29_Sc5.source: We don't know where it is.
Book7-chapter29_Sc5.description: Well, obviously we don't know where the Horcrux is. That means we have to plan carefully and think logically about where to start.
Of course I'm between Harry and Ron when they need to talk quietly. I'm trying to keep things calm and make sure we discuss this properly.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.]
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: Well, Ron is right. We do not even know precisely what we are hunting. We need help from others to gather information.

Book7-chapter29_Sc6.source: [You don’t have to do everything alone, Harry.]
Book7-chapter29_Sc6.description: Of course you do not have to do everything on your own, Harry. We can share the burden and help you.

Book7-chapter28_Sc2.source: We're going to have to try to Disapparate, Harry!
Book7-chapter28_Sc2.description: Well, of course, we have to try to Disapparate, Harry. We can't just stand here and wait.

Book7-chapter28_Sc2.source: he felt Hermione take hold of his arm
Book7-chapter28_Sc2.description: Of course I grabbed his arm and turned with him. We had to move together even if the charms might stop us.

Book7-chapter32_Sc3.description: Well, Ron, I'm just as capable, of course I can do this and I will prove it.

Book7-chapter32_Sc3.source: They ran down the next staircase and found themselves in a corridor full of duelers.
Book7-chapter32_Sc3.description: Of course the tapestry ripped and we ended up in a corridor full of duelers. That's ridiculous and dangerous.

Book7-chapter29_Sc4.source: He looked at Ron and Hermione, trying to tell them without words that Voldemort had just discovered the loss of one of the other Horcruxes. Time was running out fast
Book7-chapter29_Sc4.description: Of course I understand what this means. If Voldemort knows a Horcrux is destroyed, we have to act immediately and precisely.
Well, I get it. This is Dumbledore's task for the three of us. It is right that we see it through together and keep it private.

Book7-chapter32_Sc8.source: he seized Hermione’s hand and tore down the steps into the grounds
Book7-chapter32_Sc8.description: Well, of course I'm holding on to Harry's hand and running with him. We're getting away from the fighting straight away.

Book7-chapter32_Sc5.source: [Harry, Ron, and Hermione raised their wands at once, ready to strike, but the duelers were weaving and darting around so much that there was a strong likelihood of hurting one of their own side if they cast curses.]
Book7-chapter32_Sc5.description: Well, we can’t just blast spells in the middle of that. Of course we risk hitting our own people, so we need to be careful and get out.

Book7-chapter32_Sc11.source: [Hermione so out of breath she could not speak.]
Book7-chapter32_Sc11.description: Well, I'm completely knackered and I can hardly breathe. I can't speak properly right now.

Book7-chapter32_Sc11.source: [“Crookshanks?” wheezed Hermione, bent double, clutching her chest. “Are you a wizard, or what?”]
Book7-chapter32_Sc11.description: Of course I think you can be a bit daft sometimes, but honestly, are you actually a wizard or what?

Book7-chapter32_Sc9.source: because that was, as Hermione said, the only way to end it
Book7-chapter32_Sc9.description: Of course! The only way to end this is to get to the snake and to Voldemort. That's obvious and that's what we have to do.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: Well, of course it was Fiendfyre. It is the one cursed fire that will destroy Horcruxes, but it's horrendously dangerous to use.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.source: "What can we do?" Hermione screamed over the deafening roars of the fire.
Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: What we can do is think fast and stick together. Panicking won't help. We have to get out and save anyone we can.

Book7-chapter31_Sc3.source: "Let's stick together. I say we go — Harry, what's that on your arm?"
Book7-chapter31_Sc3.description: We need to stay together and check everything. Also, that diadem on Harry's arm matters. It could be what we've been hunting for.

Book7-chapter32_Sc6.source: but before either Harry or Hermione could answer they were bowled aside: Hagrid had come thundering down the stairs, brandishing his flowery pink umbrella.
Book7-chapter32_Sc6.description: Well, we were shoved aside before I could say anything because Hagrid thundered down the stairs with his umbrella, shouting not to hurt them.

Book7-chapter32_Sc6.source: Hagrid vanished amongst the spiders, and with a great scurrying, a foul swarming movement, they retreated under the onslaught of spells, Hagrid buried in their midst.
Book7-chapter32_Sc6.description: Of course Hagrid ended up in the middle of the spiders, buried among them as spells drove the swarm back.

Book7-chapter32_Sc7.description: Oh my! That's a giant. Of course I'm terrified, but we have to think this through.

Book7-chapter32_Sc7.source: she and Ron caught up with Harry and gazed upward at the giant now trying to seize people through the window above.
Book7-chapter32_Sc7.description: We're looking up at a giant trying to grab people from the upper windows. We must be careful and act logically.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: Well of course Ron can speak Parseltongue. He managed to open the Chamber of Secrets by getting the hissing right.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "Accio Diadem!" cried Hermione in desperation, but nothing flew through the air toward them.
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: Obviously the Room of Requirement is stopping summoning charms when it does not want items to be taken easily.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: There was a clatter as the basilisk fangs cascaded out of Hermione’s arms. Running at Ron, she flung them around his neck and kissed him full on the mouth.
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: Well this is obvious now. Ron and I are together. I couldn't hold back any longer. Of course I kissed him.

Book7-chapter31_Sc2.source: "Hermione stabbed it. Thought she should. She hasn't had the pleasure yet."
Book7-chapter31_Sc2.description: Of course I was the one to destroy the Hufflepuff cup. It had to be done and I did it.

Book7-chapter32_Sc12.description: Well, perfect. It's working the way it should.
Of course I need to stop things if they're about to go wrong. Wait, hold on, make sure we're doing it right.

Book7-chapter34_Sc6.source: "Ron and Hermione know that, but just in case they —"
Book7-chapter34_Sc6.description: Of course I know about the Horcruxes. We're keeping that knowledge safe between the three of us and now Neville will fill in if needed.

Book7-chapter34_Sc6.source: "This was crucial, he must be like Dumbledore, keep a cool head, make sure there were backups, others to carry on."
Book7-chapter34_Sc6.description: Well, obviously we must be methodical about this and have backups. Getting emotional won't help us, we need a plan and contingencies.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: Hermione had said that they could not be repaired, that the damage was too severe.
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: Well, of course I said the wand pieces looked beyond repair. I was convinced the damage was too severe to fix.

Book7-chapter36_Sc8.source: Ron and Hermione looked at it with a reverence that, even in his befuddled and sleep-deprived state, Harry did not like to see.
Book7-chapter36_Sc8.description: Obviously I felt reverent about the Elder Wand at first, but I'm practical too and concerned about what keeping it would mean.

Book7-chapter36_Sc9.source: "I think Harry’s right," said Hermione quietly.
Book7-chapter36_Sc9.description: Well, of course Harry's right. It all makes sense when you think it through.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Nine and three-quarters!" piped a small girl, also red-headed, who was holding her hand.
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: Blimey, it's platform nine and three quarters. Of course it is. That's where we're going.

Book1-chapter6_Sc1.source: "First time at Hogwarts? Ron's new, too." She pointed at the last and youngest of her sons. He was tall, thin, and gangling, with freckles, big hands and feet, and a long nose.
Book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I'm the youngest and a bit gangling and everyone knows it's my first time. Great, everyone's looking at me.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I nearly passed out when I was sorted; I was dead green but then I collapsed into the chair next to Harry when it called Gryffindor.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: “I know who you are!” said Ron suddenly. “My brothers told me about you — you’re Nearly Headless Nick!”
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I recognised Nearly Headless Nick because my brothers told me about him. I wasn't shy about saying it.

Book1-chapter7_Sc2.source: He was pale green by now.
Book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I go proper green with nerves sometimes; being sorted was terrifying before it happened.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["Harry could see Ron’s twin brothers catcalling."]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Blimey, Fred and George were already shouting and catcalling when people started being sorted. They make everything louder, don't they?
When Hermione got Gryffindor I groaned. It was one of those 'oh, not again' sort of groans, but you know I was glad she wasn't anywhere else.

Book1-chapter7_Sc1.source: ["The table on the far left exploded with cheers; Harry could see Ron's twin brothers catcalling."]
Book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: Seeing Harry get sorted and the whole table cheering made me feel chuffed. I wanted him in our house, and when he got Gryffindor we all went a bit mad with happiness.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: Blimey, I want to know other people's stories. I asked Neville about his family because I’m interested in who’s from where and who’s got wizarding relatives.

Book1-chapter7_Sc3.source: Everybody finished the song at different times. At last, only the Weasley twins were left singing along to a very slow funeral march.
Book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: My brothers are proper mad about messing around. They’ll sing the daftest things and carry on, and I’m used to them being loud and ridiculous.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.source: “Ron, you’ve got something on your nose.”
Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: My mum fusses over me loads. She still pokes my nose and calls me Ronnie even though I’m nearly as tall as Fred and George.
Percy’s a proper prefect now and he’s all proud about it. He’s got new robes and a shiny P badge.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.source: “Don’t worry, ickle Ronniekins is safe with us.”
Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: My brothers are a pain but they look out for me in their own daft way.
Chocolate Frog cards are a thing and everyone collects them. I’ve loads but I’m still missing Agrippa or Ptolemy. Typical.

Book1-chapter6_Sc2.source: “You don’t want this, it’s all dry,” said Ron.
Book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: School food is rubbish sometimes. My mum always forgets what I don’t like so I get stuck with the corned beef sandwiches.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “Seeker?” he said. “But first years never — you must be the youngest House player in about —”
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: Blimey, you're the Seeker? You must be the youngest House player in ages.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “Wood told me.” Ron was so amazed, so impressed, he just sat and gaped at Harry.
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: Wood told you? That's brilliant. I can't believe it, I'm gobsmacked.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “I start training next week,” said Harry. “Only don’t tell anyone, Wood wants to keep it a secret.”
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: You start training next week and it has to be secret. Right, my lips are shut.

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: “Of course he has,” said Ron, wheeling around. “I’m his second, who’s yours?”
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I'm your second for any duel, alright? I'll stand by you, who does Malfoy have?

Book1-chapter9_Sc4.source: When Malfoy had gone, Ron and Harry looked at each other.
Book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: That lot won't walk all over us. I'm ready to back you up, no messing about.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "You don’t know that you’ll make a fool of yourself," said Ron reasonably. "Anyway, I know Malfoy’s always going on about how good he is at Quidditch, but I bet that’s all talk."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: You don't know you'll make a fool of yourself. Malfoy? He's all talk about Quidditch. I reckon he's full of it.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Even Ron would tell anyone who’d listen about the time he’d almost hit a hang glider on Charlie’s old broom."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: Blimey, I keep saying how I nearly hit a hang glider on Charlie's old broom. It's a great story and it proves I've had my share of close calls.

Book1-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Ron had already had a big argument with Dean Thomas, who shared their dormitory, about soccer."
Book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I argued with Dean about soccer. I can't see what's good about a game where you can't fly and there's only one ball.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Harry and Ron jumped to their feet. They were half hoping for a reason to fight Malfoy,"
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Blimey, I wanted to take Malfoy on. When he grabbed Neville's Remembrall we were ready to fight.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Harry and Ron were delighted when she told Malfoy he’d been doing it wrong for years."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Ha, I loved it when Hooch told Malfoy he had his grip wrong. Good on her. Serves him right.

Book1-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Come back, boy!" she shouted, but Neville was rising straight up like a cork shot out of a bottle — twelve feet — twenty feet."
Book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, Neville is hopeless on a broom when he's nervous. It's dangerous when someone gets that jumpy.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "But people only die in proper duels, you know, with real wizards. The most you and Malfoy’ll be able to do is send sparks at each other. Neither of you knows enough magic to do any real damage. I bet he expected you to refuse, anyway."
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: People only get killed in proper duels between skilled wizards. Harry and Malfoy will just throw sparks around and that's it. Malfoy probably thought Harry would turn him down.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "Throw it away and punch him on the nose,"
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: If a wand fizzles, you chuck it and sock them. That's what I'd do.
Blimey, I'm making a point here and calling attention when I need to.

Book1-chapter9_Sc5.source: "That’s your problem," "We’ve got to go, we’re going to be late."
Book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: Hermione can worry about being locked out herself. We've got to move or we'll be late and get into trouble.
I don't think Hermione believes she couldn't overhear us. I'm not surprised she jumped in to scold us.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Don’t tell me you’d never heard of Dumbledore!
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Dumbledore's a big name. If you don't know him, where have you been? He's famous, simple as that.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Do they? What, they don’t move at all? Weird!
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Moving pictures are the norm here. If Muggle photos don't move, that's proper weird to me.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: When they say every flavor, they mean every flavor
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Bertie Bott's really does mean every flavour. You can get nasty ones like sprouts or even booger if you're unlucky.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: If I’d brought a toad I’d lose it as quick as I could. Mind you, I brought Scabbers, so I can’t talk.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Toads are a magnet for getting lost. I brought Scabbers instead, which is probably safer even if he's dull.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Stupid spell — George gave it to me, bet he knew it was a dud.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Some of George's spells are rubbish. If a wand or spell came from him, it might not work properly.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: I don’t know what they’ll say if I’m not. I don’t suppose Ravenclaw would be too bad, but imagine if they put me in Slytherin.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I'm proper worried about the Sorting. If I'm not in Gryffindor Mum and Dad will be gutted. Slytherin would be a nightmare.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Charlie’s in Romania studying dragons, and Bill’s in Africa doing something for Gringotts
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Loads of Weasleys went into proper jobs after school. Charlie studies dragons and Bill works for Gringotts abroad.

Book1-chapter6_Sc3.source: Did you hear about Gringotts? It’s been all over the Daily Prophet, but I don’t suppose you get that with the Muggles — someone tried to rob a high security vault.
Book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: Gringotts got targeted in a robbery attempt. Nobody's been caught and that freaked everybody out because it might be You-Know-Who.

Book1-chapter11_Sc5.source: “What are you talking about, Dean?” said Ron. “Red card!” said Dean furiously. “In soccer you get shown the red card and you’re out of the game!” “But this isn’t soccer, Dean,” Ron reminded him.
Book1-chapter11_Sc5.description: What the hell, Dean's shouting about a red card like this is a soccer match. I told him flat out, this isn't soccer, you can't just use those rules here.

Book1-chapter11_Sc5.source: Hagrid, however, was on Dean’s side. “They oughta change the rules. Flint coulda knocked Harry outta the air.”
Book1-chapter11_Sc5.description: Blimey, even Hagrid reckons the rules should be tougher — people actually think Flint should've been sent off for that. That's mental.

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: He pulled his broomstick up a little to take it even higher, and heard screams and gasps of girls back on the ground and an admiring whoop from Ron.
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: Blimey, Harry! That was brilliant. Show him, Harry!

Book1-chapter9_Sc3.source: He pulled his broomstick up a little to take it even higher, and heard ... an admiring whoop from Ron.
Book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: He's my mate and I'm right behind him. When Harry does something mad and brilliant, I'm cheering him on.

Book1-chapter9_Sc7.source: "What do they think they’re doing, keeping a thing like that locked up in a school?" "If any dog needs exercise, that one does."
Book1-chapter9_Sc7.description: Blimey, what do they think they're doing keeping a thing like that locked up? If any dog needs exercise, that one does.
No, we don't mind. (I'm stuck for words, but I'm following Hermione anyway.)

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "That’s your problem," said Ron. "We’ve got to go, we’re going to be late."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: That's your problem, not mine. We've got to hurry or we'll be late, so move it.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "You’ve got some nerve —" said Ron loudly.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: You've really got some nerve, honestly. I'm not impressed with that at all.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "If either of you get us caught, I’ll never rest until I’ve learned that Curse of the Bogies Quirrell told us about, and used it on you."
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: If you two get us caught I'll be furious. I swear I'll learn that Curse of the Bogies and use it on you if you let that happen.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "He’s late, maybe he’s chickened out," Ron whispered.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: Maybe he's not showing up. He might have chickened out, but I don't want to count on that.

Book1-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Mrs Norris?" breathed Ron, squinting through the dark.
Book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I thought I heard Mrs Norris at first, so I'm on edge and watching for Filch's cat or Filch himself.

Book1-chapter10_Sc5.description: Good idea, lock it in. We can use the lock to keep the troll contained. Simple and obvious.

Book1-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Oh, no," said Ron, pale as the Bloody Baron. "It's the girls' bathroom!"
Book1-chapter10_Sc5.description: Oh no, it's the girls' bathroom. Blimey, Hermione's in there. We have to get back, even though that is terrible.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "It’s not any old broomstick," he said, "it’s a Nimbus Two Thousand. What did you say you’ve got at home, Malfoy, a Comet Two Sixty?"
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: Blimey, that broom is a Nimbus Two Thousand. Comets might look flashy, but they're not in the same league as a Nimbus.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Comets look flashy, but they’re not in the same league as the Nimbus."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: Of course Comets are just showy. A Nimbus is proper quality. That's what matters.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "What would you know about it, Weasley, you couldn’t afford half the handle," Malfoy snapped back. "I suppose you and your brothers have to save up twig by twig."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: I took the bait and stuck up for Harry and the broom. I won't let Malfoy take the mickey about money and brooms.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Wow," Ron sighed, as the broomstick rolled onto Harry’s bedspread.
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: Wow. Seeing that broom in person was something else. I'm well impressed and proper excited for Harry.

Book1-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Yes, don’t stop now," said Ron, "it’s doing us so much good."
Book1-chapter10_Sc1.description: I joked that Harry rubbing it in would do us good. I'm cheeky and I like winding people up when we're on a roll.

Book1-chapter10_Sc4.source: Don’t ask me, they’re supposed to be really stupid
Book1-chapter10_Sc4.description: Trolls are supposed to be thick as two short planks, honestly. They'd be useless unless someone let them in.

Book1-chapter10_Sc4.source: Maybe Peeves let it in for a Halloween joke.
Book1-chapter10_Sc4.description: Could be Peeves messing about. Brilliant, a prank that nearly kills someone, that's just typical.
There's this vile pong in the air, like old socks and a filthy loo. Whatever it is, it's huge and disgusting.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: “Wingardium Leviosa!” he shouted, waving his long arms like a windmill.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Blimey, I know the words, but I keep getting it wrong. I'm not the most graceful with my wand.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: “You do it, then, if you’re so clever,” Ron snarled.
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: Oh yeah? Do it yourself then, if you're that clever. I'm not having that smart-arse comment.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: “It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: She rubs people up the wrong way. Honestly, no wonder she gets on people's nerves, she's a nightmare sometimes.

Book1-chapter10_Sc3.source: Parvati Patil telling her friend Lavender that Hermione was crying in the girls’ bathroom and wanted to be left alone. Ron looked still more awkward at this,
Book1-chapter10_Sc3.description: She must've noticed she hasn't got any friends. That's awkward, and I feel a bit guilty about it.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: I can shout something daft and it might distract an opponent. Sometimes a bit of cheek does the trick.
I actually did a spell in a crisis and it worked. Blimey, I managed to levitate the club and knock the troll out.

Book1-chapter10_Sc6.source: Ron was standing there with his wand still raised, staring at what he had done.
Book1-chapter10_Sc6.description: I didn't expect to pull that off. I can be useful when it matters, even if I don't always know what I'm doing.

Book1-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Honestly, Hermione, you think all teachers are saints or something," snapped Ron. "I'm with Harry. I wouldn't put anything past Snape. But what's he after? What's that dog guarding?"
Book1-chapter11_Sc1.description: Honestly, Hermione, you think teachers are saints? I'm with Harry. I wouldn't put anything past Snape. But what is he after? What is that dog guarding?

Book1-chapter11_Sc10.description: Neville, you can look! I was shouting that, buzzing that Harry could get back on his broom and wanting everyone to see.

Book1-chapter11_Sc11.source: He was being made a cup of strong tea back in Hagrid’s hut, with Ron and Hermione.
Book1-chapter11_Sc11.description: Blimey, Harry nearly swallowed the Snitch! That's mental. We're getting him a strong cup of tea and celebrating — we won by a massive amount.

Book1-chapter11_Sc9.description: Come on, Hermione! Hurry up — Harry's broom is jumping all over the place and he can't hold on, for Merlin's sake.

Book1-chapter13_Sc2.source: “You’ve got to stand up to him, Neville!” said Ron. “He’s used to walking all over people, but that’s no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier.”
Book1-chapter13_Sc2.description: Blimey, you can’t let Malfoy push you around. He’s always walking all over people, but you’ve got to stand up to him and stop making it easy for him.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Just have to find out for ourselves, then," said Ron, and they left Hagrid looking disgruntled and hurried off to the library.
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: Fine, we'll find out about Flamel ourselves. Can't rely on Hagrid to tell us everything.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I’d give anything for one of these," he said. "Anything."
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I'd give anything for a cloak like that. It's brilliant, I'd love one.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I hate maroon," Ron moaned halfheartedly as he pulled it over his head.
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I hate maroon. Those sweaters are horrible, honestly.

Book1-chapter12_Sc1.source: "You can come tonight, I’m going back, I want to show you the mirror." "I’d like to see your mum and dad," Ron said eagerly. "And I want to see all your family, all the Weasleys, you’ll be able to show me your other brothers and everyone." "You can see them any old time," said Ron. "Just come round my house this summer. Anyway, maybe it only shows dead people."
Book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: Come to my house and I'll show you the mirror. It might only show dead people, but you can see my family any time when you come round this summer.

Book1-chapter13_Sc3.description: The Sorcerer's Stone? Blimey, I didn't know about that. That's mental.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "I am — I'm wearing the badge like Bill used to — and I'm holding the House Cup and the Quidditch Cup — I'm Quidditch captain, too!"
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, in that mirror I'm proper famous. I'm Head Boy, Quidditch captain and holding loads of cups. That's mental.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Do you think this mirror shows the future?"
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I reckon that mirror might show the future. It looked like what I'd want to happen, not just some trick.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "This isn't safe — she might have gone for Filch, I bet she heard us. Come on."
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: Mrs. Norris can give us away. Even if the Cloak hides us from people, animals like her could still cause trouble. We should leg it.

Book1-chapter12_Sc2.source: "You had it to yourself all last night, give me a bit more time."
Book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I'm gutted Harry had it first, but I'm dead keen for a look. I can be selfish about stuff I'm excited by, but I want to share it with him too.

Book1-chapter11_Sc8.description: Blimey, what are you doing? I was panicking, gray-faced, grabbing the binoculars because I wanted to see what's happening to Harry.
I had the binoculars in my hands and I kept watching Harry. The broom's jumping higher every time someone gets close. That's mental.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Snape's done it, then!" said Ron. "If Quirrell's told him how to break his Anti-Dark Force spell —"
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: Snape's had a hand in this. If Quirrell told him about the anti-dark force spell, I'm bloody convinced Snape's involved.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "Maybe Snape's found out how to get past him without asking Hagrid," said Ron, looking up at the thousands of books surrounding them.
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: There might be a way past Fluffy that Snape could have discovered. I bet there's some book that explains how to get past a giant three-headed dog.

Book1-chapter15_Sc1.source: "If we just do a bit of poking around —"
Book1-chapter15_Sc1.description: Blimey, I still think we should do a bit of poking around. I can't just sit on my hands when there's adventure staring us in the face.

Book1-chapter13_Sc4.description: We won. You won. We actually won. That's mental.

Book1-chapter13_Sc4.source: "And I gave Malfoy a black eye, and Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle single-handed! He’s still out cold but Madam Pomfrey says he’ll be all right — talk about showing Slytherin! Everyone’s waiting for you in the common room, we’re having a party, Fred and George stole some cakes and stuff from the kitchens."
Book1-chapter13_Sc4.description: I gave Malfoy a black eye. Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle and got knocked out but he'll be all right. We're having a party in the common room and Fred and George nicked cakes from the kitchens.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “It bit me!” he said, showing them his hand, which was wrapped in a bloody handkerchief.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Blimey, the dragon actually bit me and it hurt. That creature is the most horrible thing I have ever met.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: “Won it,” said Hagrid. “Las’ night. I was down in the village havin’ a few drinks an’ got into a game o’ cards with a stranger. Think he was quite glad ter get rid of it, ter be honest.”
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Hagrid won the dragon egg in a card game in the village. It must have cost nothing to him but it's a right mess for everyone else.

Book1-chapter14_Sc2.source: Wonder what it’s like to have a peaceful life,” Ron sighed, as evening after evening they struggled through all the extra homework they were getting.
Book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: Life at Hogwarts is chaotic and stressful. I wish things could be peaceful for once instead of being swamped with extra work.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: ["Don't talk to me for a moment," said Ron when Harry sat down next to him, "I need to concen —" He caught sight of Harry’s face. "What's the matter with you? You look terrible."]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: Blimey, Harry looks awful. I told him to keep quiet for a moment because I was trying to focus, but then I had to ask what's wrong when I saw his face.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: ["Say you're ill," said Ron. "Really break your leg," said Ron.]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: I suggested faking illness and even joked about really breaking a leg to stop him playing. I'm all for anything that gets him out of a dodgy game.

Book1-chapter13_Sc1.source: ["You've got to stand up to him, Neville!" said Ron. "He's used to walking all over people, but that's no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier."]
Book1-chapter13_Sc1.description: He's used to walking all over people, so Neville has to stand up to him. Come on, don't let Malfoy push you about, that's just making it easier for him.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Blimey, Hagrid was looking up dragons in the library. He’s up to something dragon-related, I’m sure of it.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: Dragon breeding was outlawed by the Warlocks’ Convention of 1709, everyone knows that.
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: Dragon breeding’s illegal. It’s a mad idea to keep dragons about because Muggles would notice and it’s dangerous. Charlie’s got the scars to prove it.

Book1-chapter14_Sc1.source: Of course there are, Common Welsh Green and Hebridean Blacks. The Ministry of Magic has a job hushing them up, I can tell you.
Book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: There are wild dragons in Britain like Welsh Greens and Hebridean Blacks and the Ministry has to keep wiping Muggles’ memories when they spot them.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "You can pretend to be waiting for Professor Flitwick, you know."
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: Hermione could pretend to wait for Professor Flitwick to keep an eye on Snape.
I think Harry is being reckless and that what he wants to do is insane and dangerous.

Book1-chapter16_Sc2.source: "Oh, shut up," said Hermione, but she agreed to go and watch out for Snape.
Book1-chapter16_Sc2.description: Hermione will still help despite being annoyed. We're all still trying to work together even when tensions are high.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Stop saying the name!" said Ron in a terrified whisper, as if he thought Voldemort could hear them.
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: Blimey, saying his name makes everyone jumpy. I can't stand it, so I hiss that he shouldn't be named, like it might make him listen.

Book1-chapter15_Sc10.source: "Will you stop saying the name!" Ron hissed.
Book1-chapter15_Sc10.description: Honestly, keep that name out of our mouths. It's too dangerous and it makes my skin crawl every time someone says it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Where are we off to now? I am sleepy and trying to get a grip on what is happening.
What on earth are you lot going on about? I am confused and need it explained.

Book1-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Yes, please," said Ron, but Harry cut him off.
Book1-chapter16_Sc1.description: Fine, yes please, but we are in a rush. I just want to help but we do not have time to faff about.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "It’s not just my hand," he whispered, "although that feels like it’s about to fall off. Malfoy told Madam Pomfrey he wanted to borrow one of my books so he could come and have a good laugh at me. He kept threatening to tell her what really bit me — I’ve told her it was a dog, but I don’t think she believes me — I shouldn’t have hit him at the Quidditch match, that’s why he’s doing this."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: It’s not just my hand that’s sore, it feels like it’s going to drop off. Malfoy’s been winding people up, trying to get Pomfrey to laugh at me, and he’s threatening to tell her what actually bit me. I told her it was a dog because I didn’t want the trouble, but she probably thinks I’m daft. I shouldn’t have slugged Malfoy at the Quidditch match. That’s why he’s out to get me.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "They looked at one another. 'We’ve got the Invisibility Cloak,' said Harry. 'It shouldn’t be too difficult — I think the cloak’s big enough to cover two of us and Norbert.'"
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Blimey, with the Invisibility Cloak we can do it. If it will cover two of us and Norbert, that’s the only way to get him out without being seen.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "On the contrary, he sat bolt upright and broke into a sweat."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I’m not calm about this. Saying it’ll be over at midnight doesn’t help; I’m proper nervous and sweating at the thought.

Book1-chapter14_Sc3.source: "About ten minutes later, four broomsticks came swooping down out of the darkness. Charlie’s friends were a cheery lot."
Book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: Charlie’s friends showed up on broomsticks and they were sound. They helped strap Norbert into a harness and got him away.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "But will it cover all three of us?" said Ron. "All — all three of us?"
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: I asked if the cloak would cover all three of us. I need to know we're all safe under it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Oh, come off it, you don't think we'd let you go alone?"
Book1-chapter16_Sc3.description: Oh, come off it. You don't think we'd let Harry go alone? Of course I'm coming with you.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: The whole school’s talking about it.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: Everyone at school is buzzing about what happened. It's all anyone can talk about.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: I always said he was off his rocker.
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: Dumbledore's a mad old git, but I'm impressed by him. He's completely bonkers and brilliant at the same time.

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: D'you think he meant you to do it? "Sending you your father's Cloak and everything?"
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I reckon Dumbledore might have planned for Harry to try. Giving him his father's Cloak and not stopping him looks suspicious, doesn't it?

Book1-chapter17_Sc3.source: So what happened to you two? "Well, I got back all right," said Hermione. "I brought Ron round -- that took a while --"
Book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: That whole mess on the third floor was mental. We got through it, but it was touch and go. Bloody hell, it was stressful.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Oh, I’m so glad we know what it’s called, that’s a great help
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Blimey, knowing the name doesn't help unless you do something about it. Say the name all you like, it won't save you.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: HAVE YOU GONE MAD? ARE YOU A WITCH OR NOT?
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: What the hell, Hermione? Of course use your wand. If you're a witch, act like one when we're strangling to death.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Lucky! ... Lucky!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Lucky we landed on that soft plant. That was pure luck, but I'll take it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: Now what do we do? ... It’s obvious, isn’t it? ... We’ve got to play our way across the room.
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Right, think about it. If it's a giant chessboard, we play chess. Simple as that, use your head.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: I suppose we’ve got to take the place of three of the black pieces.
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Blimey, sometimes you actually have to be a piece on the board. You step up and do a job when there's no other option.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: That’s chess! ... You’ve got to make some sacrifices! I’ll make my move and she’ll take me — that leaves you free to checkmate the king, Harry!
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Sacrifices are part of the game. If someone has to go, then someone has to go. I'll do it. Don't hang about once you've got your chance.

Book1-chapter16_Sc5.source: NO! ... That’s chess! ... Do you want to stop Snape or not?
Book1-chapter16_Sc5.description: Listen, if we're going after Snape and the Stone, we've got to trust each other to do what's necessary. I expect Harry and Hermione to pull through when it counts.

Book1-chapter16_Sc4.description: Don’t be daft about this. We’re coming with you, no leaving anyone behind.
That thing at the dog’s feet looks like a harp. Snape’s left it to keep the dog awake unless someone plays it.
Fine, I’ll go first. I’ll pull the trapdoor and have a go at getting us down. Bit nervous, but I’ll do it.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: With one last desperate look back at Ron, Harry and Hermione charged through the door and up the next passageway.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: I was left behind for the moment while Harry and Hermione went on. They expect me to get help if I can.

Book1-chapter16_Sc6.source: Get back and get Ron. Grab brooms from the flying-key room, they'll get you out of the trapdoor and past Fluffy - go straight to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore, we need him.
Book1-chapter16_Sc6.description: If I'm told to, I need to grab brooms, get out, go to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore. That's my job right now.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Er, no," said Ron, "he had to work tonight."
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: My dad had to work so we nicked the car. We hope to get it back in the garage before Mum notices.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "He works in the most boring department," said Ron. "The Misuse of Muggle Artifacts Office."
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: Dad's job is all about bewitching Muggle things so no one notices when enchanted stuff turns up. He goes mad over Muggle gadgets and takes them apart to study them.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "That’s the main road," said George, peering down through the windshield.
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: Gnomes keep coming back through the hedge. De-gnoming means grabbing them, making them dizzy and chucking them over the hedge. It's horrible but it's what we do.

Book2-chapter3_Sc5.source: "Ginny," said Ron in an undertone to Harry. "My sister. She’s been talking about you all summer."
Book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: Ginny's been talking about Harry loads. She's keen, and Fred teased that she'll want his autograph. Family's buzzing about Harry being here.

Book2-chapter3_Sc4.source: "I reckon old Dobby was sent to stop you coming back to Hogwarts. Someone's idea of a joke. Can you think of anyone at school with a grudge against you?"
Book2-chapter3_Sc4.description: I reckon Dobby was sent to stop you coming back to Hogwarts. Sounds like someone's having a laugh at your expense.

Book2-chapter3_Sc4.source: "Yes," said Harry and Ron together, instantly. "Draco Malfoy,"
Book2-chapter3_Sc4.description: Draco Malfoy is the obvious suspect. Me and Harry both think he might be the one with a grudge.

Book2-chapter5_Sc5.source: “Check that no one’s watching,” said Ron, starting the ignition with another tap of his wand.
Book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: Check no one's watching before we move the car. Seriously, keep your eyes peeled

Book2-chapter5_Sc5.source: “Skip the lecture,” said Ron impatiently, “and tell us the new password.”
Book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: Skip the moaning and just give me the password. I don't want a lecture, I want answers

Book2-chapter5_Sc2.description: We're going to miss the train, that's what it looks like.
It's gone. The train's left and we're not on it, blimey.

Book2-chapter5_Sc2.source: Ron ran to pick up Hedwig, who was causing such a scene that there was a lot of muttering about cruelty to animals from the surrounding crowd.
Book2-chapter5_Sc2.description: I grabbed Hedwig and tried to sort things out, but with people watching and the gateway sealed I knew this was a proper mess.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: It's gone. The train's actually left and we're separated from it. Blimey, that's bad.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.source: "What if Mum and Dad can’t get back through to us? Have you got any Muggle money?"
Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: What if Mum and Dad can't get back to us? Do you have any Muggle money, 'cause we might need it.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Can't hear a thing," he said tensely.
Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I pressed my ear to the barrier and couldn't hear anything. It's completely silent on the other side.

Book2-chapter5_Sc3.source: "What're we going to do? I don't know how long it'll take Mum and Dad to get back to us."
Book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I don't know what's going to happen. I can't stand just waiting not knowing how long it'll be before Mum and Dad get back.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "We’ve never been allowed in," said Ron enviously.
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I've never been allowed in Malfoy Manor. I want to see inside, I'm proper jealous.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Meet you back here," Ron said to Hermione as the Weasleys and Harry were led off to their underground vaults by another Gringotts goblin.
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I'm sticking around the meeting spot. Don't wander off, we'll meet back here.

Book2-chapter4_Sc3.source: "I should ruddy well think not," growled Hagrid.
Book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: Blimey, Hagrid thinks we'd never be allowed in their manor. Good, because I wouldn't want to go without an invite.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: You know we’re not supposed to do spells outside school —
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: We're not supposed to do spells outside school, like everyone knows.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: He works for the Ministry," said Ron.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: My dad works for the Ministry, which is why he knew about that warning.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: Stop gibbering," said Ron. "We’ve come to take you home with us.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: We're coming to take you home. I won't leave you stuck with the Dursleys.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: Oh, this doesn’t count," said Ron. "We’re only borrowing this. It’s Dad’s, we didn’t enchant it.
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: The car is my dad's and we didn't enchant it ourselves. We're only borrowing it.

Book2-chapter3_Sc1.source: You forget who I’ve got with me."
Book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I've got Fred and George with me, so we're not short of ideas or help.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Get in. Hurry up and get into the car, now.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Panting, Ron hoisted them up into the car."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I hauled the bars into the back seat. Took some effort but they're in.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "He snatched up Hedwig’s cage, dashed to the window, and passed it out to Ron."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Harry chucked Hedwig's cage out to me. I've got Hedwig now.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "Put your foot down, Fred!" yelled Ron, and the car shot suddenly toward the moon."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: Put your foot down, Fred! Go, go, go! We need to move or we'll get caught.

Book2-chapter3_Sc2.source: "But the Weasleys gave a gigantic tug and Harry’s leg slid out of Uncle Vernon’s grasp — Harry was in the car — he’d slammed the door shut — 'Put your foot down, Fred!' yelled Ron, and the car shot suddenly toward the moon."
Book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I didn't think we could break Vernon off, but we did. That was mental, we actually got him into the car and flew away.

Book2-chapter3_Sc3.source: So — what’s the story, Harry?" said Ron impatiently. "What’s been happening?"
Book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: Come on then, what's been going on? Spill it, I want to know what's happened and why everyone's acting weird.

Book2-chapter5_Sc1.source: ["Let’s go together, we’ve only got a minute," Ron said to Harry.]
Book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: Come on, let's go together, we've only got a minute. Move it!

Book2-chapter5_Sc1.source: [Both trolleys hit the barrier and bounced backward; Ron’s trunk fell off with a loud thump, Harry was knocked off his feet, and Hedwig’s cage bounced onto the shiny floor, and she rolled away, shrieking indignantly; people all around them stared and a guard nearby yelled, “What in blazes d’you think you’re doing?”]
Book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: Blimey, that was a mess! My trunk fell off with a loud thump and everyone's staring. Great, just great.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "He’s never traveled by Floo powder," said Ron suddenly.
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: He’s never used Floo powder. Blimey, how did he even get his school things last year?
Oops, I forgot to tell him earlier. My fault, really.

Book2-chapter4_Sc1.source: "And keep your elbows tucked in," Ron advised.
Book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: When you go through the Floo, keep your elbows tucked in so you don’t get snagged or fall out the wrong fireplace.
Don’t move about or you might fall out of the wrong fireplace. Stay still and say where you’re going.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: You'll pay for that one, Malfoy! I couldn't stand him insulting Hermione like that.

Book2-chapter7_Sc1.source: A loud bang echoed around the stadium and a jet of green light shot out of the wrong end of Ron's wand, hitting him in the stomach and sending him reeling backward onto the grass.
Book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: Blimey, my wand backfired on me and I got hit myself. I reared back and then started belching slugs. That's mental.

Book2-chapter7_Sc4.source: "It's a disgusting thing to call someone," said Ron, wiping his sweaty brow with a shaking hand. "Dirty blood, see. Common blood. It’s ridiculous. Most wizards these days are half-blood anyway. If we hadn’t married Muggles we’d’ve died out."
Book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: Blimey, calling someone 'dirty blood' is disgusting. Most of us are half-bloods now, and if our families hadn't married Muggles we'd have died out. It's ridiculous to go on about pure-blood nonsense.

Book2-chapter7_Sc4.source: Well, I don’ blame yeh fer tryin’ ter curse him, Ron," said Hagrid loudly over the thuds of more slugs hitting the basin.
Book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: Look, of course I wanted to curse him. What he said was horrible. I don't blame anyone for losing it a bit when someone talks like that.

Book2-chapter9_Sc2.description: Blimey, Dumbledore's not having any of it. He's properly sticking up for the rules and that shuts people up.
We're told to go. Let's scarper quick without making a scene, yeah?

Book2-chapter6_Sc2.source: My gran sent me one once, and I ignored it and, he gulped, it was horrible.
Book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: My gran sent me one once and I ignored it and it was horrible. I know how awful they can be and I'm proper terrified of it.

Book2-chapter6_Sc2.source: which had begun to smoke at the corners
Book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: That thing actually starts smoking at the corners. I was shaking as I reached out, took it from Errol and slit it open.

Book2-chapter7_Sc2.source: Nobody seemed to want to touch him. "We'd better get him to Hagrid's, it's nearest," said Harry ... the pair of them pulled Ron up by the arms.
Book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: Blimey, nobody wanted to touch me, and Harry and Hermione had to haul me up by the arms and take me to Hagrid's.

Book2-chapter9_Sc3.source: "No," said Ron, without hesitation. "Hearing voices no one else can hear isn't a good sign, even in the Wizarding world."
Book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: No. Hearing voices no one else can hear isn’t a good sign, even in the Wizarding world. That’s not something to take lightly.
Course I do believe you. I trust you, but blimey, it’s still weird.

Book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: Blimey, Malfoy called her 'Mudblood.' That is what he said to her.

Book2-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Mudblood’s a really foul name for someone who is Muggle-born — you know, non-magic parents."
Book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: Mudblood is a filthy name for someone with Muggle parents. It means you're calling someone less because their family aren't wizards.

Book2-chapter7_Sc3.source: "I mean, the rest of us know it doesn’t make any difference at all."
Book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I mean honestly, it makes no difference who your parents are. It shouldn't count for anything.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: Look, food! I got excited at first because it looked like something to eat.

Book2-chapter8_Sc2.source: “Can we move? I feel sick,” said Ron.
Book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: Can we move? I feel sick. That stuff's revolting and I want out of here.

Book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: No thanks. I don't want any treacle toffee.
Better not risk it. I reckon trying that toffee could end badly, so I'm staying away.

Book2-chapter9_Sc6.source: ["I - don't - like - spiders," said Ron tensely.]
Book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: Blimey, I hate spiders. I can't stand them.

Book2-chapter9_Sc6.source: ["I don't mind them dead," said Ron, who was carefully looking anywhere but at the window. "I just don't like the way they move."]
Book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: Dead ones don't bother me, it's the way they crawl that freaks me out.

Book2-chapter9_Sc6.source: ["If you must know, when I was three, Fred turned my - my teddy bear into a great big filthy spider because I broke his toy broomstick."]
Book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: Fred's a sod for that prank. He turned my teddy into a spider and I've hated them ever since.

Book2-chapter5_Sc4.source: "If we hurry we’ll be able to follow the Hogwarts Express —"
Book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: We need to hurry if we want to follow the Hogwarts Express. Come on, let's catch up with it.

Book2-chapter5_Sc4.source: Ron unlocked the cavernous trunk with a series of taps from his wand.
Book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I tapped the wand and the trunk popped open. Magic does the job for lugging all our stuff.

Book2-chapter5_Sc4.source: They heaved their luggage back in, put Hedwig on the back seat, and got into the front.
Book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: Hedwig's coming with us; I put her on the back seat so she's travelling with us.

Book2-chapter5_Sc4.source: "Check that no one’s watching," said Ron, starting the ignition with another tap of his wand.
Book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: We can't let Muggles see us. Make sure nobody's watching before we drive off.

Book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: Blimey, they're looking at me like I should know what to do. That's mental, I don't want to stare at the lot of them.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Errol!" said Ron, pulling the bedraggled owl out by the feet.
Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: Blimey, Errol's a wreck. I hauled him in by the feet and he slumped on the table.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.source: "She's sent me a Howler," said Ron faintly.
Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: She's sent me a Howler. Bloody hell, I can't believe she actually sent one.

Book2-chapter6_Sc1.source: "It'll be worse if you don't," said Neville.
Book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I reckon if I don't open it it's only going to be worse, even though I'm dreading it.

Book2-chapter9_Sc8.source: "Where did that come from? Someone’s mopped it up." "It was about here," said Ron, recovering himself to walk a few paces past Filch’s chair and pointing. "Level with this door."
Book2-chapter9_Sc8.description: Blimey, there was something on the floor someone tried to mop up and it looked to have been right level with the door. I pointed it out straight away.
I told Myrtle she was already dead in that blunt, not-nice way I do. It shows I'm fed up with her dramatics and not exactly sugarcoating things.

Book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: Blimey, when Harry froze I was just baffled and listening too. I didn't know what was going on at first, so I shut up and watched him — we all had to hear that voice.

Book2-chapter9_Sc9.source: Harry and Ron stood with their mouths open
Book2-chapter9_Sc9.description: Blimey, did you see that? She just dove into the toilet and vanished. Bloody hell.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Let’s think," said Ron in mock puzzlement. "Who do we know who thinks Muggle-borns are scum?" He looked at Hermione. "If you’re talking about Malfoy —" "Of course I am!" said Ron. "You heard him — 'You’ll be next, Mudbloods!' — come on, you’ve only got to look at his foul rat face to know it’s him —"
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: Malfoy said it straight out and he looks the part. Of course it's him. He's the sort who'd be involved in this dirty business.

Book2-chapter9_Sc10.source: "They could’ve had the key to the Chamber of Secrets for centuries! Handing it down, father to son . . ." said Ron.
Book2-chapter9_Sc10.description: Imagine it kept in the family forever, passed from father to son. That's exactly the sort of thing the Malfoys would do.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Excuse me?" said Ron sharply. "What d’you mean, a bit of whoever we’re changing into? I’m drinking nothing with Crabbe’s toenails in it —"
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: What d'you mean we need a bit of the person we're changing into? I'm not drinking anything that has Crabbe's toenails or anything like that in it.

Book2-chapter10_Sc1.source: "D'you realize how much we’re going to have to steal, Hermione? Shredded skin of a boomslang, that’s definitely not in the students’ cupboard. What're we going to do, break into Snape's private stores? I don't know if this is a good idea."
Book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: Blimey, we're going to have to nick proper dangerous stuff. I don't like the sound of breaking into Snape's stores. That is asking for trouble.

Book2-chapter9_Sc4.source: "You know, it rings a sort of bell,"
Book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: That story about a secret Chamber at Hogwarts rang a bell with me. I thought Bill might have told me something like it once.

Book2-chapter9_Sc4.source: "That’s where Filch has been keeping guard,"
Book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I muttered that Filch had been stationed there. It meant someone thought that spot needed watching, so it felt important.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: “A month?” said Ron. “Malfoy could have attacked half the Muggle-borns in the school by then!”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: A month? Blimey, that's ages. Malfoy could do a lot of damage in that time.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: However, while Hermione was checking that the coast was clear for them to leave the bathroom, Ron muttered to Harry, “It’ll be a lot less hassle if you can just knock Malfoy off his broom tomorrow.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: It'd be a whole lot easier if you just dealt with Malfoy on your broom tomorrow. Less faff, sorted.

Book2-chapter10_Sc2.source: “But it’s the best plan we’ve got, so full steam ahead, I say.”
Book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: Fine, it's rubbish but it's the best we've got, so I'm backing it. Full steam ahead.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Malfoy could have attacked half the Muggle-borns in the school by then!"
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, if we wait a whole month Malfoy could be doing who knows what to Muggle-borns. We can't just sit on our hands.

Book2-chapter10_Sc3.source: "It’ll be a lot less hassle if you can just knock Malfoy off his broom tomorrow."
Book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: Honestly, it'd be much easier if you just knocked Malfoy off his broom tomorrow. Quick and simple, that'd sort him out.

Book2-chapter13_Sc3.source: “Well, it’s not much use to you,” said Ron.
Book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: It's not much use to you, is it?

Book2-chapter13_Sc3.source: He dropped his voice. “Fifty points if you can get it through Myrtle’s nose.”
Book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: Fifty points if you can shove it up Myrtle's nose. Come on, give it a go.

Book2-chapter14_Sc1.source: "How many monsters d’you think this place can hold?" Ron asked dully.
Book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: How many monsters do you reckon this place could hold? Honestly, that's a scary thought.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "Have you ever heard of a plan where so many things could go wrong?"
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: Blimey, this plan is mental. I can't think of one where so much could go wrong.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: "Good. And I sneaked these spare robes out of the laundry," Hermione said, holding up a small sack. "You’ll need bigger sizes once you’re Crabbe and Goyle."
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: Right, I'll need bigger robes to pass as Crabbe or Goyle. Hermione's already sorted the clothes.

Book2-chapter12_Sc4.source: The three of them stared into the cauldron. Close up, the potion looked like thick, dark mud, bubbling sluggishly.
Book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: That potion looks disgusting and I don't like it, but if Hermione says it’s right then we'll try. Still, bloody hell, it makes me uneasy.

Book2-chapter12_Sc3.source: Hermione, you’re not supposed to be in here
Book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: Blimey, I wasn't expecting her here; she's somewhere she shouldn't be and I'm rattled by it.

Book2-chapter12_Sc3.source: shielding his eyes against the light
Book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, the light hit me hard; I was half asleep and irritated when she pulled the curtains back.
She's given me a present; we're clearly mates and she fusses over me in that bossy, helpful way.

Book2-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Hang on," said Ron, who had approached cautiously and was looking over Harry’s shoulder. "I know that name. . . . T. M. Riddle got an award for special services to the school fifty years ago."
Book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: T. M. Riddle won an award for special services to the school about fifty years ago. I know that name.

Book2-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Because Filch made me polish his shield about fifty times in detention," said Ron resentfully. "That was the one I burped slugs all over."
Book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: Filch made me polish that shield loads in detention. Honestly, that was the one I burped slugs all over and it still stuck with me.

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: Blimey, I caught the diary. Lucky, wasn't it?

Book2-chapter13_Sc5.source: But Harry didn’t care, he was one-up on Malfoy, and that was worth five points from Gryffindor any day.
Book2-chapter13_Sc5.description: That's brilliant for Harry. I love seeing Malfoy look stupid, honestly.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Blimey, that potion smelled and looked disgusting when Millicent's stuff went in.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: You don't know how bizarre it is to see Goyle thinking.
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Seeing Goyle look like he's thinking was mental; it makes you realise how odd all this changing is.
We had to split up into separate stalls so we'd fit after changing; good call to move.
When Malfoy said he hoped it would be Hermione who gets hurt, I felt furious; I won't stand for someone wishing that on her.

Book2-chapter12_Sc5.source: Have you two been pigging out in the Great Hall all this time?
Book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: Percy trying to act important annoyed me; Malfoy mocked him and that just made everything more tense between us and Slytherins.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Oh, yes he would," said Ron, even more loudly than Dean.
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: Hagrid wouldn't be taken if he was guilty. I'm sure of it.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I'd light mine, too, but you know — it'd probably blow up or something."
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: My wand's a bit iffy. I'm not risking lighting it in case something goes wrong. Typical, really.

Book2-chapter15_Sc3.source: Ron started to say that he didn't think so, somehow, but stopped in midsentence when Harry kicked him hard under the desk.
Book2-chapter15_Sc3.description: Harry keeps me in check. I want to argue, but he pulls me back because we're trying to be careful.

Book2-chapter14_Sc4.source: We keep all our old subjects or I'd've ditched Defense Against the Dark Arts
Book2-chapter14_Sc4.description: We can't drop our subjects, so I would have dumped Defense Against the Dark Arts if we could. Lockhart's teaching is useless.

Book2-chapter14_Sc4.source: I haven't learned anything from him except not to set pixies loose
Book2-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, Lockhart teaches nothing useful. All I learned from him is how not to let pixies loose.
I didn't hear the voice when Harry did. That freaked me out and made me wide eyed, like something's not right.

Book2-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Riddle does sound like Percy - who asked him to squeal on Hagrid, anyway?" Ron tried a different tack.
Book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: Riddle sounds exactly like Percy, doesn't he? Who told him to squeal on Hagrid anyway? That's suspicious as hell.

Book2-chapter15_Sc2.source: "That's clever of you," said Ron, who didn’t seem to have forgiven Ernie as readily as Harry.
Book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: Yeah, clever. But I'm not over all this yet, am I?

Book2-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Ouch! What’re you —" Harry pointed out the spiders, following their progress with his eyes screwed up against the sun.
Book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: Ouch! Hey, what was that for? Blimey. Right, spiders... I see them now, but we can't go after them at the moment.

Book2-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Oh, yeah," said Ron, trying, and failing, to look pleased. "But we can’t follow them now —"
Book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: Oh yeah. I can see them, but we can't follow them right now. That's just rotten timing.

Book2-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Okay," Ron sighed as though resigned to the worst, "I'm ready. Let's go."
Book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: Blimey, this looks bad, but I'm ready to move and do whatever's needed.

Book2-chapter15_Sc8.source: "That's exactly Hagrid's problem!" said Ron, thumping the wall of the cabin.
Book2-chapter15_Sc8.description: He's always thinking monsters aren't as bad as they're made out

Book2-chapter15_Sc8.source: "He always thinks monsters aren’t as bad as they’re made out, and look where it’s got him! A cell in Azkaban!"
Book2-chapter15_Sc8.description: That got him a cell in Azkaban

Book2-chapter15_Sc8.source: "What was the point of sending us in there? What have we found out, I'd like to know?"
Book2-chapter15_Sc8.description: What was the point of sending us in there? I want to know what we found out

Book2-chapter16_Sc9.description: I'm going with you. I won't let you go alone.

Book2-chapter16_Sc5.source: "What’re we going to do?" said Ron, whose eyes were flashing.
Book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: What are we going to do? This is serious, isn't it?
We should go straight to McGonagall. She needs to know right now.

Book2-chapter16_Sc7.source: "Somewhere there," said Myrtle, pointing vaguely toward the sink in front of her toilet.
Book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: She points at the sink and says the eyes were there. So yeah, the sink's where we need to look.

Book2-chapter16_Sc7.source: Lockhart was standing well back, a look of utter terror on his face.
Book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: Bloody hell, Lockhart looked petrified. He's not the brave expert act he tries to be.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: "Under the lake, probably," said Ron, squinting around at the dark, slimy walls.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: We're probably under the lake. That's where this tunnel leads.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: Ron gave him a push, and he slid out of sight.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: I shoved Lockhart into the pipe. Someone's got to get him moving or we'd all be stuck.

Book2-chapter16_Sc10.source: All three of them turned to stare into the darkness ahead.
Book2-chapter16_Sc10.description: This tunnel is black and slimy. It's proper grim down here.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "What? Are you crazy? It could be dangerous."
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I think menacing books are a real risk. I got worried when Harry tried to pick up that wet little book.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Some of the books the Ministry’s confiscated — Dad’s told me — there was one that burned your eyes out."
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I've heard from Dad that the Ministry confiscates dangerous books. Some can do seriously nasty things like burning your eyes out.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "And everyone who read Sonnets of a Sorcerer spoke in limericks for the rest of their lives."
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: There are cursed books that mess with your mind. People who read certain books can end up acting really weird, like speaking only in limericks.

Book2-chapter13_Sc1.source: "And some old witch in Bath had a book that you could never stop reading! You just had to wander around with your nose in it, trying to do everything one-handed."
Book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: Some books can enchant you so you cannot stop reading them. That sounds dangerous and ridiculous at the same time.

Book2-chapter16_Sc8.source: "Harry," said Ron. "Say something. Something in Parseltongue."
Book2-chapter16_Sc8.description: I told Harry to say something in Parseltongue, urging him to try and open the tap.

Book2-chapter16_Sc8.source: He looked at Ron, who shook his head.
Book2-chapter16_Sc8.description: I shook my head when Harry hesitated, showing I wanted him to stop wasting time and just do it.

Book2-chapter16_Sc13.source: "I'll try and shift some of this rock," said Ron, who seemed to be trying to keep his voice steady. "So you can — can get back through. And, Harry —"
Book2-chapter16_Sc13.description: I'll try and shift some of this rock so you can get back through. I'm going to do whatever I can to help Harry, even if I'm shaking.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: Why don’t you leave us here, sir, we’ve only got one more corridor to go
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: Blimey, Lockhart really bounces off. I told him to leave us because we can manage walking the rest ourselves.
Gone to curl his hair, more like. I don't exactly trust him to be any use in a proper emergency.

Book2-chapter16_Sc1.source: Wonder if she did see the attacker, though?
Book2-chapter16_Sc1.description: Wondering if Hermione saw the attacker before she was petrified. If he sneaked up on them all, no one will ever know unless she managed to warn someone first.

Book2-chapter16_Sc4.source: "But how's the basilisk been getting around the place?"
Book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: How's a giant snake been moving about the school without anyone seeing it? That doesn't add up.

Book2-chapter16_Sc4.source: "The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets!" "What if it’s a bathroom?"
Book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: The entrance might be somewhere ordinary like a bathroom. Blimey, it could be hidden in plain sight.

Book2-chapter16_Sc3.source: I’ve been hearing that voice inside the walls.
Book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I've been hearing that voice inside the walls. It's been going on and it's got me spooked.

Book2-chapter16_Sc3.source: The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets! What if it’s a bathroom? What if it’s in -
Book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: Blimey, the entrance to the Chamber might be in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. What if that's where the whole thing starts?
What're we going to do? Should we go straight to McGonagall? I'm not staying here while this goes on.

Book2-chapter16_Sc12.source: "I'll try and shift some of this rock," said Ron, who seemed to be trying to keep his voice steady. "So you can — can get back through."
Book2-chapter16_Sc12.description: I'll try and shift some of this rock so you can get back through. I'll stay and do what I can, even if I'm shaking.

Book2-chapter16_Sc11.source: I'm here! I'm okay - this git's not, though - he got blasted by the wand -
Book2-chapter16_Sc11.description: I'm alive and kicking, but Lockhart's a mess after getting blasted by his own wand. I even kicked him in the shins.

Book2-chapter16_Sc11.source: What now? We can't get through - it'll take ages.
Book2-chapter16_Sc11.description: We can't get through that rockfall. It's going to take ages to clear unless we find another way.

Book2-chapter16_Sc11.source: There was a dull thud and a loud "ow!" It sounded as though Ron had just kicked Lockhart in the shins.
