Book2-chapter16_Sc11.description: I'm getting fed up with Lockhart. Honestly, the bloke's useless when things go wrong.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “If it has, it’s hiding them very well,” said Ron. “Maybe it’s shy. I don’t know why you don’t chuck it, Harry.”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I reckon if the diary had powers they'd be obvious. Maybe it's shy, but seriously, why not just get rid of the thing?

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “Could’ve been anything,” said Ron. “Maybe he got thirty O.W.L.s or saved a teacher from the giant squid. Maybe he murdered Myrtle; that would’ve done everyone a favor. . . .”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: Riddle could have got his award for any old reason. It might not be anything to do with the Chamber at all.

Book2-chapter13_Sc4.source: “That’s a brilliant theory, Hermione,” said Ron, “with just one tiny little flaw. There’s nothing written in his diary.”
Book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: There is nothing written in the diary as far as I can see. That right there is a problem for Hermione's brilliant idea.

Book3-chapter4_Sc10.source: "I haven't touched it, all right?" Ron roared back.
Book3-chapter4_Sc10.description: I did not touch Percy's Head Boy badge, okay? Don't go accusing me.

Book3-chapter4_Sc10.source: "So's Scabbers's rat tonic," said Ron, throwing things out of his trunk to look.
Book3-chapter4_Sc10.description: Scabbers's rat tonic is missing too. I'm frantically checking my trunk and everything. I might have left it in the bar but I'm packed and ready to go.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Ginny!" Ron thrust an arm through the gap in the rock to pull her through first. "You’re alive! I don’t believe it! What happened? How — what — where did that bird come from?"
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Ginny, you're alive! I can't believe it. What on earth happened and where did that bird even come from?

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "His memory’s gone," said Ron. "The Memory Charm backfired. Hit him instead of us. Hasn’t got a clue who he is, or where he is, or who we are. I told him to come and wait here. He’s a danger to himself."
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Lockhart's had his memory wiped. The Memory Charm backfired and he doesn't know who he is. He's a danger if he wanders about like that.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "But you’re much too heavy for a bird to pull up there —"
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Ordinary birds couldn't lift someone the size of Harry up that pipe. That bird must be something else.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He means you," said Ron sharply to Lockhart. "You hold Ginny’s other hand —"
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Lockhart has to hold Ginny's hand and behave. I don't trust him to do anything sensible but he can at least hang on.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Harry! I think Myrtle’s grown fond of you! You’ve got competition, Ginny!"
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: Myrtle fancies Harry, which is ridiculous, but it means Ginny's upset and needs me to worry about her more than petty stuff.

Book2-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Where now?" said Ron, with an anxious look at Ginny. Harry pointed.
Book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: We escaped to Moaning Myrtle's bathroom and now we have to decide where to go next to help Ginny.

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "Wonder what he’s been getting ready?" said Ron, a note of anxiety in his voice.
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: Blimey, Hagrid's been up since five getting ready for his first lesson. I'm anxious and curious about what he'll have prepared.

Book3-chapter6_Sc2.source: "We’d better go, look, Divination’s at the top of North Tower. It’ll take us ten minutes to get there."
Book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: We need to hurry. Divination's at the top of North Tower and it'll take about ten minutes to get there, so we should move now.
When Trelawney's voice appeared from the shadows I was startled and looking for where she was. That voice came out of nowhere and was creepy.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: What were you going to tell us?
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: Blimey, tell us straight away. Don't keep stuff back when it's about something that serious.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: How thick would Harry have to be, to go looking for a nutter who wants to kill him?
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: How dense would Harry have to be to go looking for someone who wants to kill him? That's mental, he mustn't do that.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: I just want to get inside Honeydukes!
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: Honestly, I want to go to Hogsmeade so I can get into Honeydukes and try all the sweets. That's the main reason, not the history stuff.

Book3-chapter5_Sc1.source: It’s coming from your trunk... Is that a Sneakoscope? ... it’s a very cheap one
Book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: That Sneakoscope went mad in the trunk. It's the cheap kind but it still makes a right racket. We should get it checked in Hogsmeade if we can.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: Blimey, Harry actually did it. You bow, you wait, and if the beast bows back you can touch it. Simple really, once you get the nerve.

Book3-chapter6_Sc5.source: This is very easy... I knew it must have been, if Potter could do it.
Book3-chapter6_Sc5.description: I thought it looked easier than it is, but seeing Malfoy get his arm sliced shows it's not a joke. You don't go showing off with dangerous creatures.
Harry's alright. He handled Buckbeak properly and I feel proud we were there to see him do it.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "How is he?" said Ron as they all sat down.
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: I want to know if Malfoy is badly hurt, but I don't think it's that serious.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Yeah, don’t worry, Hagrid, we’ll back you up," said Ron.
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: Don't worry Hagrid, we'll back you up and tell the truth. We're on your side.

Book3-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Madam Pomfrey fixed him best she could," said Hagrid dully, "but he’s sayin’ it’s still agony . . . covered in bandages . . . moanin’ . . ."
Book3-chapter6_Sc6.description: Malfoy says he's in agony and is wrapped in bandages, but that sounds like he's playing it up to me.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "He wasn’t so cocky last night when the dementors were down at our end of the train. Came running into our compartment, didn’t he, Fred?"
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: That Malfoy was a right coward on the train. He came running like a prat, so you can shut it, Malfoy.

Book3-chapter6_Sc1.source: "But look," said Ron, laughing, "see this morning? Nine o’clock, Divination. And underneath, nine o’clock, Muggle Studies. And look — underneath that, Arithmancy, nine o’clock."
Book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: Blimey, Hermione's timetable looks mental. No one can be in three classes at once, it just can't happen.
I care when Hermione makes herself nuts. I might moan, but I don't want her overdoing it, so I call her out when something's daft.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: He grabbed both Harry and Ron and pulled them into a bone-breaking hug.
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Blimey, that hug nearly cracked me. Hagrid can’t hold it together right now.

Book3-chapter6_Sc7.source: "YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY! AN’ YOU TWO! LETTIN’ HIM!"
Book3-chapter6_Sc7.description: Alright then, I shouldn’t be letting Harry go off after dark to see Hagrid. I’ll stop him next time, I promise.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: Blimey, I called Malfoy out straight away when he stared at Harry. I won't let him sneer without answering.

Book3-chapter7_Sc3.source: "He’s making it up," said Ron savagely. "He’s trying to make you do something stupid."
Book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: He's definitely trying to wind Harry up. I reckon Malfoy is lying to get Harry to do something daft.

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Weasley, cut up Malfoy’s roots for him," said Snape without looking up.
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: Snape will order me around in front of everyone just to humiliate me. What the hell, sir?

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "There’s nothing wrong with your arm," he hissed at Malfoy.
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I won't be made to do Malfoy's work without a fight. I lost my temper and chopped his roots badly on purpose. That showed him.

Book3-chapter7_Sc1.source: "I’m afraid he won’t be a teacher much longer," said Malfoy in a tone of mock sorrow. "Father’s not very happy about my injury -- he’s complained to the school governors. And to the Ministry of Magic. Father’s got a lot of influence, you know."
Book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: Malfoy tries to threaten us by name-dropping his father and the Ministry. Bloody hell, he always uses his family to get his own way.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I’m not going to take any crap from Malfoy this year," he said angrily.
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I mean it. If Malfoy makes one more crack about my family I will not stand for it. Bloody hell, I am done with his rubbish.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I’m starving. I want to get to the feast," said Ron.
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I am absolutely starving and all I can think about is the feast. Food is a priority for me, simple as that.

Book3-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I mean — he hasn’t died, has he?"
Book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: When someone looks out of sorts I panic a bit. I worry that things are worse than they are. Of course he is breathing, but I still freak out.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "You need your Inner Eye tested, if you ask me,"
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: Blimey, tea-leaf reading is nonsense. I called it out because we were both sniggering and it felt daft to sit there taking it seriously.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "There's a blob a bit like a bowler hat,"
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I tried to make something of Harry's cup and came up with daft things like a bowler hat and an acorn. Honestly, it was just guesses and I joked about him working for the Ministry.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "'A windfall, unexpected gold.' Excellent, you can lend me some . . ."
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: If the tea predicts money, I'm not above asking for a loan. That's classic me, hopeful and a bit cheeky when fortune gets mentioned.

Book3-chapter6_Sc3.source: "I thought that was a bowler hat,"
Book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I admitted I got it wrong when the teacher read it properly. Bloody hell, I was embarrassed but it was true, I misread it.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “You bought that monster?” said Ron, his mouth hanging open.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: Blimey, you actually bought that monster?

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “Hermione, that thing nearly scalped me!” said Ron.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: That thing nearly scalped me, honestly, it attacked me.

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “And what about Scabbers?” said Ron, pointing at the lump in his chest pocket. “He needs rest and relaxation! How’s he going to get it with that thing around?”
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: What about Scabbers? He needs rest and relaxation, how's he going to get it with that cat around?

Book3-chapter4_Sc8.source: “I wonder why,” said Ron sarcastically as they set off toward the Leaky Cauldron.
Book3-chapter4_Sc8.description: I wonder why no one wanted that cat, yeah right.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “Hermione, that thing nearly scalped me!” said Ron.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: Blimey, that cat nearly scalped me. That could have been nasty.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “And what about Scabbers?” said Ron, pointing at the lump in his chest pocket. “He needs rest and relaxation! How’s he going to get it with that thing around?”
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: Scabbers needs to rest. With Crookshanks around, Scabbers won't get any peace. That's not fair.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “Would we get a reward if we caught him?” asked Ron. “It’d be good to get some more money —”
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: If anyone caught Sirius Black there might be a reward. Could do with the money, honestly.

Book3-chapter4_Sc9.source: “I wonder why,” said Ron sarcastically as they set off toward the Leaky Cauldron.
Book3-chapter4_Sc9.description: I wonder why no one wanted Crookshanks. Yeah right, like that's surprising.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'I thought you were having a fit or something,' said Ron, who still looked scared. 'You went sort of rigid and fell out of your seat and started twitching'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: Blimey, I really thought Harry was having a fit. He went rigid, fell out of his seat and started twitching and it scared me.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'I felt weird,' said Ron, shifting his shoulders uncomfortably. 'Like I'd never be cheerful again.'"
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: That thing made me feel awful, like I'd never be cheerful again. It sucked the happiness right out of me.

Book3-chapter5_Sc3.source: "'No one screamed,' said Ron, more nervously still."
Book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I kept telling myself no one screamed and trying to stay calm, but I was really rattled and nervous around the dementor.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Malfoy ordered me to slice his caterpillars. Bloody cheeky of him to boss me around like that.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Hey, Harry," said Seamus Finnigan, leaning over to borrow Harry’s brass scales, "have you heard? Daily Prophet this morning — they reckon Sirius Black’s been sighted."
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: Sirius Black's been sighted nearby. Blimey, that could be trouble if he really is around here.

Book3-chapter7_Sc2.source: "It was a Muggle who saw him. ’Course, she didn’t really understand. The Muggles think he’s just an ordinary criminal, don’t they?"
Book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: A Muggle saw him and probably thinks he's just another criminal. That means the sighting might get muddled with Muggle confusion.

Book3-chapter7_Sc9.source: A giant spider, six feet tall and covered in hair, was advancing on Ron, clicking its pincers menacingly.
Book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: Bloody hell, spiders are my nightmare. If one that big comes at me I’m not going to stand there calmly.
I might bluff my way into being brave when I have to, but I'm still terrified inside. I can throw myself at it, but I'm buzzing with fear the whole time.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "You asked us a question and she knows the answer! Why ask if you don't want to be told?"
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: Blimey, I can't stand Snape picking on Hermione, so I shouted back because it was unfair to ask a question and then ignore the answer.
Of course I got detention for sticking up for Hermione. Snape does not forgive being challenged.

Book3-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Hermione went very red, put down her hand, and stared at the floor with her eyes full of tears."
Book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: Seeing Hermione upset makes me angry at Snape. I will defend her, even if it gets me into trouble.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: “There’s always the feast,” said Ron, in an effort to cheer Harry up. “You know, the Halloween feast, in the evening.”
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: There's always the feast. Come on, Harry, at least we'll have the Halloween food. It's something to look forward to.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: Ron halfheartedly suggested the Invisibility Cloak, but Hermione stamped on that one...
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I suggested the cloak because, well, it might help. Bloody hell, it was only an idea.

Book3-chapter8_Sc2.source: Ron called Professor McGonagall a lot of names that greatly annoyed Hermione;
Book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: Blimey, McGonagall's being dead strict about this. I told her a few choice names in my head anyway.

Book3-chapter7_Sc10.source: "Riddikulus!" bellowed Ron, and the spider's legs vanished
Book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: Blimey, I shouted Riddikulus and made that spider lose its legs so it just rolled to Harry's feet
When I get stuck I can still shout the spell and do something useful in a hurry

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “There you go,” said Ron. “We got as much as we could carry.”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: We grabbed as many sweets as we could carry for Harry. Told you we could fit loads in our pockets.

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: “Lupin drank it?” he gasped. “Is he mad?”
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: Blimey, Lupin drank that smoking goblet from Snape. Is he mad or what?

Book3-chapter8_Sc3.source: By the sound of it — everywhere. Dervish and Banges, the wizarding equipment shop, Zonko’s Joke Shop, into the Three Broomsticks for foaming mugs of hot butterbeer, and many places besides.
Book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: We went all over Hogsmeade. Zonko’s, Dervish and Banges, the Three Broomsticks for butterbeer, the lot. Honest to God it was brilliant.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: D’you know what that is making me do? I’ve got to scrub out the bedpans in the hospital wing. Without magic!
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: Blimey, Snape's making me do proper disgusting jobs. Scrubbing bedpans without magic is mental and it makes me furious.

Book3-chapter9_Sc3.source: Why couldn’t Black have hidden in Snape’s office, eh? He could have finished him off for us!
Book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I thought, if Black had hidden in Snape's office, Snape might have sorted him out. That's what I wanted to happen.

Book3-chapter7_Sc7.source: Ron was muttering to himself, “Take its legs off.”
Book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: Spiders are my worst nightmare. My first thought is always 'take its legs off' — anything to stop it moving, honestly.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "Ron and Hermione were also there, looking as though they’d just climbed out of a swimming pool."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: Blimey, I was soaked and covered in mud but I was right there with Harry when he woke up.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: Bloody hell, I really thought he'd died. That was proper terrifying.

Book3-chapter9_Sc6.source: "The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed."
Book3-chapter9_Sc6.description: We're a team and we stick together. Seeing him like that made it clear how much he matters to us.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Then he magicked you onto a stretcher," said Ron. "And walked up to school with you floating on it. Everyone thought you were . . ."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: He magicked you onto a stretcher and walked up to school with you floating. Everyone was staring, absolutely stunned.
Blimey, the Whomping Willow doesn't like being hit. Not a good place for a broom to land.

Book3-chapter9_Sc7.source: "We lost . . . for the first time ever, he had lost a Quidditch match."
Book3-chapter9_Sc7.description: We lost a match for the first time. I still can't quite take it in, it's a proper shock.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Like trying to go after Black," said Ron sharply.
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Blimey, I'm not having Harry go chasing Black. It's not worth him getting himself killed just to get revenge.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "You heard what Fudge said. Black isn't affected by Azkaban like normal people are."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Fudge said Black is different in Azkaban. If that's true, then locking him up won't mean the same thing as it does for anyone else. All the more reason Harry shouldn't go charging about.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Dad told me — the Order of Merlin, First Class, and Pettigrew's finger in a box. That was the biggest bit of him they could find. Black's a madman, Harry, and he's dangerous —"
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: My dad told me how bad Pettigrew was left after Black got him. That makes me sure Black's a right lunatic and really dangerous. I want Harry to take that seriously and stop thinking he can handle it alone.

Book3-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Look," said Ron, obviously casting around for a change of subject, "it's the holidays! It's nearly Christmas! Let's — let's go down and see Hagrid."
Book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: Hey, it's the holidays. We should try to do something normal like visit Hagrid. Get away from all this and not stew on it all day.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Wow!' said Ron, looking very impressed, 'you've learned to Apparate!' 'Course I haven't,' said Harry.
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: Blimey, I thought Harry could Apparate. I'm gobsmacked at first. Then I find out it's the Marauder's Map. Still, that's mental.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: Ron pointed to a notice pasted on the inside of the sweetshop door. "——— BY ORDER OF ——— THE MINISTRY OF MAGIC Customers are reminded that until further notice, dementors will be patrolling the streets of Hogsmeade every night after sundown.
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I reckon dementors patrolling Hogsmeade makes it unlikely Black could sneak into Honeydukes at night. It's safer than Hermione thinks.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Come on, Hermione, it's Christmas. Harry deserves a break.'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: It's Christmas. Harry deserves a break and a bit of fun. Let's not be so grim about the whole thing.

Book3-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Seen the Fizzing Whizbees, Harry?' said Ron, grabbing him and leading him over to their barrel. 'And the Jelly Slugs? And the Acid Pops? Fred gave me one of those when I was seven — it burnt a hole right through my tongue. I remember Mum walloping him with her broomstick.'
Book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I love these sweets. Fred once gave me an Acid Pop that burned a hole through my tongue. Mum gave him a right telling off. I bet Fred would take Cockroach Clusters if I said they were peanuts.

Book3-chapter12_Sc2.source: What d’you reckon’s the matter with him?
Book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, Lupin looks poorly. I can't help staring and wondering what's wrong with him.
She doesn’t know what we’re talking about. I reckon Hermione’s just trying to get us to chat with her again and she’s being all clever about it.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: Er — shall I make a cup of tea?
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Blimey, making a cuppa is what Mum does when someone's upset. It's small, but it's what I can do to try and help Hagrid settle down.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: Blimey, who’d spend that much on you?
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: Someone's bought Harry a Firebolt and it's ridiculously expensive. Whoever did it must be serious about giving him the best broom.

Book3-chapter11_Sc2.source: Malfoy! Wait till he sees you on this!
Book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I can't wait to rub this in to Malfoy. If Harry rides that broom, Malfoy will be speechless. I'm dead keen to see his face.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "He got a Firebolt for Christmas," said Ron.
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Blimey, Harry got a Firebolt for Christmas. A real one. That's mental.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Still looks ill, doesn't he?" said Ron as they walked down the corridor, heading to dinner.
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Moony still looks ill to me. What d'you reckon's the matter with him? I can't work it out.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "She doesn't know," said Ron, staring resentfully after Hermione. "She's just trying to get us to talk to her again."
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: Hermione's being all clever. She doesn't really know what's going on with Lupin; she's only trying to get our attention. Typical.

Book3-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Don't get excited, Oliver," said Harry gloomily. "I haven't got it anymore. It was confiscated." And he explained all about how the Firebolt was now being checked for jinxes.
Book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I can't believe they confiscated the Firebolt to check for jinxes. Bloody hell, that leaves Harry stuck with that rubbish Shooting Star for the match.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "First Hogsmeade weekend," said Ron, pointing at a notice that had appeared on the battered old bulletin board. "End of October. Halloween."
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: Right, Hogsmeade weekend’s the first one. End of October, Halloween. Mark it down, that’s when we can get into town.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "That cat’s got it in for Scabbers!" said Ron, ignoring the people around him, who were starting to giggle. "And Scabbers was here first, and he’s ill!"
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: That cat’s out to get Scabbers. I’m telling you, Crookshanks has it in for him and Scabbers is poorly. Keep that cat away from him, I mean it.

Book3-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Ask McGonagall if you can go this time, Harry. The next one might not be for ages —" "Ron!" said Hermione.
Book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I’m backing Harry to go to Hogsmeade. He shouldn’t be the only third year left behind. I’ll push him to ask McGonagall.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "She gave it to you? Excellent! Listen, can I still have a go on it? Tomorrow?"
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: Blimey, Harry's got his Firebolt back and I need a go on it tomorrow. I can't wait to try it.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "I’ve lost the passwords!" / "I made him tell me what passwords he was going to use this week, because he keeps changing them, and now I don’t know what I’ve done with them!"
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I lost the common room passwords. That's a right mess and caused a row with Neville and Sir Cadogan.

Book3-chapter12_Sc6.source: "SCABBERS! LOOK! SCABBERS!" / "BLOOD! HE’S GONE! AND YOU KNOW WHAT WAS ON THE FLOOR?"
Book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: Bloody hell, Scabbers is gone and there was blood. This is serious and I am terrified something awful happened to him.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Yes!" Ron yelled, yanking Harry's arm into the air. "Yes! Yes!"
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: That was brilliant. I was whooping and dragging Harry into the crowd, buzzing with the win.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: Before he knew it, he had been engulfed by the cheering crowd. "Yes!" Ron yelled, yanking Harry’s arm into the air.
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I threw myself into the celebration and made sure Harry got the cheers. I was right at his side as everyone went mad.

Book3-chapter13_Sc2.source: Ron, who had fought his way through to Harry's side, doubled up with laughter as they watched Malfoy fighting to extricate himself from the robe
Book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: Seeing Malfoy humiliated made me laugh like mad. I'm still fiercely loyal to Harry and this just made us closer in the moment.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: “He probably wants to hear all about Black!” said Ron.
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I reckon Hagrid wants to hear everything about Saturday night and about Sirius Black.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: “All right, Hagrid!” said Ron. “S’pose you want to hear about Saturday night, do you?”
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I'm ready to tell Hagrid what happened on Saturday night if that's why he wanted us.
I'm furious at Hermione's cat for eating Scabbers and it's caused a rift between us and Hermione right now.

Book3-chapter14_Sc2.source: Harry felt a nasty pang of guilt. He had completely forgotten that Buckbeak’s trial was so near, and judging by the uneasy look on Ron’s face, he had too.
Book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I feel uneasy and guilty too because I forgot about Buckbeak's trial and that we promised to help Hagrid prepare a defense.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "How’s she doing it?" Ron muttered to Harry one evening as Harry sat finishing a nasty essay on Undetectable Poisons for Snape.
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: How's she doing it? I can't believe Hermione keeps showing up to everything. That's mental.

Book3-chapter12_Sc4.source: "I heard her talking to Professor Vector, that Arithmancy witch, this morning... Ernie Macmillan told me she’s never missed a Muggle Studies class, but half of them are at the same time as Divination, and she’s never missed one of them either!"
Book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: Blimey, Hermione's schedule is impossible. She's at everything and it's driving me mad wondering how she does it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc3.source: "If she’d just get rid of that cat, I’d speak to her again!"
Book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: I’m furious with Hermione and I won’t speak to her while she defends that cat.

Book3-chapter14_Sc3.source: "But she’s still sticking up for it! It’s a maniac, and she won’t hear a word against it!"
Book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: The cat’s dangerous and Hermione won’t listen when I say so; that’s why I’m not talking to her.

Book3-chapter15_Sc2.source: “Yeah, there’s a burn on this table,” said Ron, pointing. “Someone’s spilled their candle.”
Book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: Blimey, there's clearly a burn on the table from a spilt candle. That's what I see, not visions of anything mystical.

Book3-chapter15_Sc2.source: “I don’t need help,” Ron whispered. “It’s obvious what this means. There’s going to be loads of fog tonight.”
Book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I don't need Trelawney to interpret it. It's obvious—there's gonna be fog tonight. I'm just having a laugh and sniggering because the whole thing's a bit mental.

Book3-chapter14_Sc9.source: "It’s my fault," said Ron abruptly. "I persuaded you to go. Lupin’s right, it was stupid, we shouldn’t’ve done it —"
Book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: It's my fault. I persuaded you to go. Lupin's right, it was stupid and we shouldn't have done it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc9.source: "Come to have a good gloat?" said Ron savagely as she stopped in front of them. "Or have you just been to tell on us?"
Book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: Are you here to gloat or to tell on us?

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: We'd've heard if the shop had been broken into.
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: We would have heard if Honeydukes had been broken into, so that's not how he came in.

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: Ron had become an instant celebrity. For the first time in his life, people were paying more attention to him than to Harry
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I'm a bit of a celebrity now. Weird, but I can't deny I'm enjoying people listening to me for once.

Book3-chapter14_Sc1.source: I was asleep, and I heard this ripping noise, and I thought it was in my dream, you know? But then there was this draft. I woke up and one side of the hangings on my bed had been pulled down. I rolled over and I saw him standing over me like a skeleton, with loads of filthy hair, holding this great long knife, must've been twelve inches
Book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I was woken by a ripping noise, there was a draft, the hangings were pulled down and I looked up and there he was, some horrible figure with filthy hair and a massive knife. I screamed and he ran off.
Why did he run instead of going for Harry? Beats me. I still want to know why he scarpered.
I told Neville to get out fast when that Howler came. Best thing for him was to leg it.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "I — gave — Harry — that — stuff," he choked. "Bought — it . . . in Zonko’s . . . ages — ago . . ."
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: Blimey, I gave Harry that stuff. I bought it in Zonko ages ago.

Book3-chapter14_Sc7.source: "I — gave — Harry — that — stuff," he choked.
Book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I told them straight away it was me who gave Harry the thing, so I'm the one responsible for getting him into this mess.

Book3-chapter14_Sc5.source: Harry! you'd better run for it! If Malfoy tells anyone you'd better get back to the castle, quick,
Book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I panicked when the Cloak slipped. I genuinely thought Malfoy would tattle and that Harry needed to scarper back to the castle or we'd be in proper trouble.
I called for Harry, stunned and hopeless when he disappeared. I felt useless and worried he'd be blamed if word got out.

Book3-chapter14_Sc8.source: He walked away, leaving Harry feeling worse by far than he had at any point in Snape’s office. Slowly, he and Ron mounted the marble staircase.
Book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: Blimey, that was heavy. I went up the marble stairs with Harry, feeling a bit crushed by what Lupin said.

Book3-chapter15_Sc3.source: “Fine!” she repeated, swinging the bag over her shoulder and almost knocking Ron off his chair.
Book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: Blimey, she nearly knocked me off my chair when she stormed out. That's how sudden it was.

Book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: Blimey, you've got a Firebolt. That means you're sorted for the match, honestly, it's brilliant.

Book3-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I can’t believe I missed Cheering Charms! And I bet they come up in our exams; Professor Flitwick hinted they might!"
Book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I missed Cheering Charms and Flitwick hinted it might be on the exams. Brilliant, that's just my luck.

Book3-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I thought we weren’t starting crystal balls until next term," Ron muttered, casting a wary eye around for Professor Trelawney, in case she was lurking nearby.
Book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I honestly thought crystal balls were next term. And keep an eye out for Trelawney, she could be lurking anywhere.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: "Hogsmeade, next weekend!" said Ron, craning over the heads to read the new notice. "What d’you reckon?"
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Hogsmeade next weekend. I’m up for it. Come on, what d’you reckon? It’s about time we went again.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: "Come on, last time we went you didn’t see anything. You haven’t even been inside Zonko’s yet!"
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, Harry missed out before. You’ve gotta come this time. You haven’t even seen Zonko’s yet.

Book3-chapter14_Sc4.source: "Very haunted up here, isn’t it?" said Ron, with the air of one commenting on the weather.
Book3-chapter14_Sc4.description: Very haunted up here, isn’t it? I knew those houses would spook even Malfoy’s lot. Makes those big oafs look proper scared.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "If Scabbers hadn’t just been eaten, he could have had some of those Fudge Flies. He used to really like them —"
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Blimey, Scabbers being gone still gets to me. I keep thinking about the little things he liked. That’s why I snapped at Hermione.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "No," said Ron flatly. "If she just acted like she was sorry — but she’ll never admit she’s wrong, Hermione. She’s still acting like Scabbers has gone on vacation or something."
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I’m convinced Hermione won’t say sorry and she’s not treating Scabbers’ disappearance seriously. I’m annoyed and I won’t let it slide.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Black! Sirius Black! With a knife!" "Here! Just now! Slashed the curtains! Woke me up!"
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: Black was in our dormitory. He was standing over me with a knife and he slashed the curtains. I saw him and I screamed.

Book3-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Ask him!" said Ron, pointing a shaking finger at the back of Sir Cadogan’s picture. "Ask him if he saw —"
Book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I told everyone to ask Sir Cadogan if he let someone in. I’m sure I saw Black and I want someone to back me up.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I know who it could’ve been — Lupin!" "Lupin? Listen, if he had this much gold, he’d be able to buy himself some new robes."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Blimey, at first I thought Lupin might've sent it because he likes Harry, but then I admitted it didn't make much sense that he could afford it.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "It’s the best broom there is, Hermione," he said. "So it must’ve been really expensive..."
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: That Firebolt is the best broom. It's proper expensive. Whoever sent it spent a fortune.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "You’d better take that cat out of here, Hermione," said Ron furiously...
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Crookshanks is dangerous around Scabbers. That cat nearly ripped my pajamas and made Scabbers panic.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "W-what?" said Harry, scrambling to his feet. "Why?" "It will need to be checked for jinxes," said Professor McGonagall.
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned McGonagall is taking the broom to be checked. I wanted a go but she says it must be cleared first.

Book3-chapter11_Sc3.source: "He’s not looking too good, is he?" "It’s stress!" said Ron.
Book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: Scabbers is ill and I'm worried about him. I reckon the stress and that big stupid cat aren't helping one bit.

Book3-chapter15_Sc9.source: ["Huh?" "S’all dark, Harry," Ron muttered thickly. "What’re you on about?"]
Book3-chapter15_Sc9.description: I was half asleep and couldn't see a thing. It's all dark, so I didn't spot anything and thought Harry was making a fuss.

Book3-chapter15_Sc10.source: A loud snore told him Ron had fallen asleep again.
Book3-chapter15_Sc10.description: Blimey, I must've nodded off again. Can't help it, I'm knackered.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: Blimey, that's Scabbers. He's been hiding and he looks terrible, all thin and patchy.

Book3-chapter16_Sc3.source: "No cats! There’s nothing here to hurt you!"
Book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I grabbed him and kept telling him it's okay. I won't let anything hurt him here.
Bloody hell, Hagrid's right. We have to scarper now or we'll be found by Fudge and the others.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "If you want to kill Harry, you’ll have to kill us too!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: If they go for Harry they have to go through me and Hermione. I’m not letting Harry face that alone.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "Lie down," he said quietly to Ron. "You will damage that leg even more."
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: My leg is badly damaged. I can barely stand and I need to hold on but it’s serious.

Book3-chapter17_Sc6.source: "You’ll have to kill all three of us!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I’m fiercely loyal to Harry and Hermione. I’d rather risk everything than see them hurt.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Get away from him — get away — Scabbers, come here —
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: Get away from him, get away. Scabbers, come here. Blimey, I wasn't going to lose him to that cat.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: Gotcha! Get off, you stinking cat —
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: Gotcha. Get off, you stinking cat. I pinned Scabbers down and shoved him back in my pocket.

Book3-chapter17_Sc2.source: He was sprawled on the ground, but Scabbers was back in his pocket; he had both hands held tight over the quivering lump.
Book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I ended up flat on the ground, but Scabbers was safe in my pocket. I was holding him tight like my life depended on it.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Then you might not have to witness an execution at all! The hippogriff might get off!"
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: Blimey, I said Buckbeak might get off and not be executed. I wanted to believe there was a chance.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "You know, I’m starting to think Hermione was right about her"
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I started to think Hermione might be right that Trelawney is a fraud. It felt like she was making a mess of the Divination testing.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Couldn’t see a thing, so I made some stuff up. Don’t think she was convinced, though."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I couldn’t see anything in the crystal and had to fake it. That was rubbish and I reckon Trelawney knew.

Book3-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Hermione and Ron, not being on speaking terms with the Minister of Magic, hovered awkwardly in the background."
Book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: It’s awkward with Fudge around. Hermione and I are on edge and don’t want to be on speaking terms with him right now.

Book3-chapter17_Sc10.source: [Black raised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron.]
Book3-chapter17_Sc10.description: Blimey, he's pointing at me. Am I supposed to do something? This is mental, I'm being singled out right now.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Call this a holiday! The exams are ages away, what’re they playing at?"
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: Blimey, this is mental. Everyone's supposed to be relaxing and they're acting like it's exam panic already.

Book3-chapter15_Sc4.source: "Ron had taken over responsibility for Buckbeak’s appeal. When he wasn’t doing his own work, he was poring over enormously thick volumes with names like The Handbook of Hippogriff Psychology and Fowl or Foul?"
Book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I've got Buckbeak's appeal to worry about and when I'm not on my own stuff I'm buried in these huge books about hippogriffs. Bloody hell, it's a nightmare.

Book3-chapter17_Sc9.source: "Ron’s ragged breathing came from the bed"
Book3-chapter17_Sc9.description: Blimey, I was out of it and breathing like mad on the bed. I was knocked about and not much use right then.

Book3-chapter17_Sc9.source: "His eyes flickered over Ron, lying on the floor"
Book3-chapter17_Sc9.description: What the hell, I was down and useless, and everyone else had to deal with things while I was panting on the floor.

Book3-chapter17_Sc4.source: "Not a dog," "Harry, it's a trap" "He's the dog, he's an Animagus"
Book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: Not a dog, that's the thing — it's an Animagus. Bloody hell, it's a trap, he's been the dog all along.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "We can’t," said Ron, who was paper-white. "He’ll be in worse trouble if they know we’ve been to see him. . . ."
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Blimey, we’re not going back to Hagrid. If they find out we’ve been to see him, he’ll be in proper trouble.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Scabbers, keep still," Ron hissed, clamping his hand over his chest. The rat was wriggling madly.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Keep still, Scabbers. Don’t make a fuss or we’re done for.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: "What’s the matter with you, you stupid rat? Stay still — OUCH! He bit me!"
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: What’s the matter with you, you stupid rat? Ouch, he bit me. Stuff like this always happens to me.

Book3-chapter17_Sc1.source: But Harry had just seen — slinking toward them, his body low to the ground, wide yellow eyes glinting eerily in the darkness — Crookshanks.
Book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, Crookshanks is creeping up on us. He looks right at Scabbers and he’s not messing about.

Book3-chapter17_Sc13.description: No way was anyone with Harry and me. I know we were only two. I can't believe Lupin thinks two of us went into the Willow.

Book3-chapter17_Sc13.source: "Do you think I could have a look at the rat?" "What's Scabbers got to do with it?"
Book3-chapter17_Sc13.description: Someone wants to look at Scabbers. That makes me nervous and defensive because Scabbers is mine and I won't let him go without a fight.

Book3-chapter17_Sc13.source: Scabbers thrashing; Ron seizing his tail
Book3-chapter17_Sc13.description: Scabbers is mine and I cling to him. If anyone says he's not a rat I'll freak out. He's been with me so long I can't imagine him being anything else.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: "Dumbledore hired you when he knew you were a werewolf?" Ron gasped. "Is he mad?"
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: Blimey, Dumbledore actually hired a werewolf. Is he mental? I can't get my head around that.

Book3-chapter17_Sc12.source: Ron edged away from both of them, dragging his leg.
Book3-chapter17_Sc12.description: I was skittish and backing off, trying not to get involved while all this was exploding around us.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "As the dog sprang back toward them he pushed Harry aside; the dog’s jaws fastened instead around Ron’s outstretched arm."
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: Blimey, that dog grabbed my arm and started dragging me. It was like being yanked about like a rag doll.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "Ron’s leg had broken, and a moment later, his foot vanished from sight."
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: My leg cracked — it broke — and then my foot was pulled out of sight. Bloody hell, that was terrifying and awful.

Book3-chapter17_Sc3.source: "All they could see now was one of Ron’s legs, which he had hooked around a root in an effort to stop the dog from pulling him farther underground —"
Book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I tried to hook my leg around a root to stop being dragged in. I fought like mad but I was slipping down.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: Sunset's when it's happening. Blimey, that doesn't give us much time and we'd never be allowed to just go wandering off.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.source: Hermione, I don’t know what’s gotten into you lately!
Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: Hermione's gone and done something daft again. She's off her head brave lately, getting the Cloak and all. It's mental but it might work.

Book3-chapter16_Sc2.source: She hasn’t gone to get it?
Book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I thought Hermione was just leaving the room for a minute. I couldn't believe she actually went to fetch the Cloak. That's typical of her.

Book3-chapter19_Sc5.source: "What are you going to do with him if I give him to you?" Ron asked Lupin tensely.
Book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I didn't want to hand Scabbers over and I asked what they'd do with him but in the end I gave him because I was desperate to stop it all

Book3-chapter19_Sc5.source: There was another blinding flash of light and then -- It was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing tree.
Book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: Blimey Scabbers isn't just a rat any more He's not what I thought at all

Book3-chapter17_Sc11.description: Blimey, I can't believe it. Get away from me, werewolf. I want nothing to do with him.

Book3-chapter17_Sc11.source: Ron made a valiant effort to get up again but fell back with a whimper of pain.
Book3-chapter17_Sc11.description: Bloody hell, I'm in bits and I can't trust this bloke right now. I'm hurt and terrified by what's happening.

Book3-chapter19_Sc6.source: "What are you going to do with him if I give him to you?"
Book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I handed Scabbers over even though I was tense about it. I wanted to know what would happen to him, and I didn't know whether he was safe to give up.

Book3-chapter19_Sc6.source: "Scabbers began to squeak without stopping, twisting and turning, his tiny black eyes bulging in his head."
Book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: Blimey, the rat wasn't a normal pet. He screamed and twisted and then turned into a man right in front of us. That's mental.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Come off it," he said weakly. "Are you trying to say he broke out of Azkaban just to get his hands on Scabbers? I mean . . ."
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Blimey, you’re saying Pettigrew escaped Azkaban just to find Scabbers? That sounds mad to me.

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Okay, say Pettigrew could turn into a rat — there are millions of rats — how’s he supposed to know which one he’s after if he was locked up in Azkaban?"
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Of course, even if Pettigrew can turn into a rat there are millions of rats. How the bloody hell would he know which one is Scabbers if he’d been locked up?

Book3-chapter19_Sc2.source: Ron clutched Scabbers closer to his chest.
Book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: Get away from him. I’m holding on to Scabbers and I’m not letting anyone take him.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "What about it?" said Ron defiantly. "He’s got a toe missing," said Black. "Of course," Lupin breathed."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Look, Scabbers has a missing toe. I still want to defend him but that is something I can't ignore.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "Look, Scabbers probably had a fight with another rat or something! He’s been in my family for ages, right —" "Twelve years, in fact," said Lupin."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: He's been with my family for ages. Blimey, twelve years is a long time and I kept thinking that proves he's just our rat, but now I'm not so sure.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "He’s been scared of that mad cat!" said Ron, nodding toward Crookshanks."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: Scabbers has been terrified of Crookshanks. I thought the cat was just mad, but that fear might mean something else.

Book3-chapter19_Sc3.source: "We — we’ve been taking good care of him!" said Ron."
Book3-chapter19_Sc3.description: I still care about Scabbers and feel defensive. I won't just give up on him without being sure.

Book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: Blimey, he actually changed into a werewolf right in front of us!

Book3-chapter20_Sc4.source: [The enormous, bearlike dog bounded forward. As the werewolf wrenched itself free of the manacle binding it, the dog seized it about the neck and pulled it backward, away from Ron and Pettigrew.]
Book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: That dog just flew at the werewolf and hauled it off us, grabbed it by the neck and pulled it back. Thank Merlin for that!

Book3-chapter19_Sc1.source: Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.
Book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: Blimey, I went for his wand too. I wasn't about to hang back when Harry was being threatened.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["You're nutters, both of you," said Ron shakily, looking round at Harry and Hermione for support.]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Blimey, I thought they were mad. I can't believe they're saying Scabbers might be Peter Pettigrew. That's mental and I don't want to hear it.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["HE'S NOT PETER, HE'S SCABBERS!" Ron yelled, trying to force the rat back into his front pocket.]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: Scabbers is my pet. Of course he's Scabbers. I'm not just going to hand him over because two grown-ups start accusing him.

Book3-chapter18_Sc1.source: ["I've had enough of this. I'm off."]
Book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm fed up and scared. I want out of this whole thing. If everyone thinks my pet's some dangerous rat, I'm not sticking around to find out more without being convinced.

Book3-chapter20_Sc6.source: Ron, unsteady on his bandaged leg, fell.
Book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: Blimey, my leg's knackered and I went down hard.

Book3-chapter20_Sc6.source: Harry saw his bald tail whip through the manacle on Ron’s outstretched arm
Book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: While I was lying there, Pettigrew's rat tail slipped through the manacle on my arm and he scarpered.

Book3-chapter20_Sc6.source: There was a bang, a burst of light — and Ron lay motionless on the ground.
Book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: What the hell, I was out cold one minute and helpless the next.

Book3-chapter20_Sc3.source: Ron was chained to Pettigrew and Lupin. He leapt forward but Sirius caught him around the chest and threw him back.
Book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was stuck chained to Pettigrew and Lupin and I lunged in. Sirius had to grab me and fling me back or I'd be right in the middle of it.

Book3-chapter20_Sc3.source: As the werewolf reared, snapping its long jaws, Sirius disappeared from Harry’s side.
Book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: What the hell, Sirius left us when Lupin went feral. That thing's proper dangerous and I don't want to be anywhere near it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc3.source: It was empty except for Ron, who was still lying motionless in the end bed.
Book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was just lying there, out of it and motionless in the end bed.

Book3-chapter21_Sc1.source: Ron’s red hair was visible beneath Madam Pomfrey’s arm.
Book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: Blimey, I'm here and I'm injured, but I'm alive. I can hear them talking outside even if I can't speak yet.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "Beaky! He escaped! He’s free! Bin celebratin’ all night!"
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: Blimey, Buckbeak's gone and everyone's been celebrating all night. That's mental and I can hardly believe it.

Book3-chapter22_Sc7.source: "That's wonderful!" said Hermione, giving Ron a reproving look because he looked as though he was close to laughing.
Book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I know I shouldn't be laughing after what happened last night, but I can't help it, it's brilliant that Beaky got away.

Book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: Blimey, he's pointing at me like I'm the guilty one. Scabbers is my rat and this is mental, I don't like being accused like that.

Book3-chapter21_Sc3.source: A fourth stretcher, no doubt bearing Ron, was already floating at his side.
Book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was knocked out and being carried on a stretcher back toward the castle. I was out cold while all this was happening.

Book3-chapter22_Sc8.source: Resigned firs’ thing this mornin’. Says he can’t risk it happenin’ again.
Book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: Blimey, so he’s gone already and says he can’t risk it happening again. That’s mental. Feels like we’re stuck, doesn’t it?

Book3-chapter18_Sc3.source: He looked up at Harry, Ron, and Hermione.
Book3-chapter18_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was standing there listening while Lupin talked about his school years and how Snape found out. I took it all in, stunned.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: He and Ron exchanged glances and then quickly looked away from each other; the temptation to burst out laughing was almost overwhelming.
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: Blimey, Dudley is ridiculous and we both nearly cracked up at him. Can't help it, that bloke's a prat.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: George asked eagerly, "How big did his tongue get?" "It was four feet long before his parents would let me shrink it!"
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: The twins make daft, dangerous jokes like Ton-Tongue Toffees and they're proper proud of them. They're going to cause trouble if someone doesn't stop them.

Book4-chapter4_Sc2.source: Ron and George were sitting at the scrubbed wooden table with Bill and Charlie.
Book4-chapter4_Sc2.description: I've still got the family on my side. Bill and Charlie are around and it's good to see older brothers who actually seem sound.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "What are we doing here? Has something gone wrong?"
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: Blimey, I come out of the fire and wonder what on earth is happening. I sound worried and confused at first.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Maybe Harry can hear us, Dad — maybe he'll be able to let us out —"
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I call for Dad and hope Harry can help. I reckon Harry might be able to do something since we're stuck in the fireplace.

Book4-chapter4_Sc1.source: "Yeah, we're having the time of our lives here," said George, whose voice sounded muffled.
Book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: Fred and George are already joking about being stuck. I'm with them and we all muck about together, even when things go wrong.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Shut up, Pig," said Ron, edging his way between two of the four beds"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Blimey, I call Pigwidgeon 'Pig' because he’s daft and annoying, and I’m not shy about saying it.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Ginny named him," he explained to Harry."
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Ginny gave the owl a cute name and I tried to change it but he wouldn’t take to any other name, so I stuck with calling him Pig.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Percy gets to keep his room all to himself because he’s got to work."
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Percy’s all self-important about work, he gets his own room because he’s obsessed with his job and behaves like he’s above the rest of us.

Book4-chapter4_Sc3.source: "So — have you heard from Sirius lately?"
Book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, I’m really worried about Sirius and I want to know if he’s safe, I can’t help asking even when it’s awkward around Ginny.

Book4-chapter5_Sc2.source: "The trouble is, about a hundred thousand wizards turn up at the World Cup, and of course, we just haven't got a magical site big enough to accommodate them all."
Book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: Blimey, a hundred thousand wizards turn up for the World Cup. They're staggering arrivals, only a few use Muggle transport, some Apparate to safe points, and lots use Portkeys.

Book4-chapter8_Sc2.source: “Slimy gits,” Ron muttered as he, Harry, and Hermione turned to face the field again.
Book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: Slimy gits. That's what they are. I can't stand people like Malfoy and his lot.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "he could feel Ron and Hermione on either side of him, their shoulders banging into his;"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: Blimey, I was right beside Harry, shoved up against him with Hermione too. We all got knocked about when it started.

Book4-chapter5_Sc5.source: "His feet slammed into the ground; Ron staggered into him and he fell over;"
Book4-chapter5_Sc5.description: Bloody hell, that Portkey threw me. I staggered straight into Harry and we all went down. That was proper disorienting.

Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: Harry, Ron, and Hermione turned quickly.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: Blimey, the Malfoys are here. That's awkward as anything.

Book4-chapter8_Sc1.source: Mr Weasley and Mr Malfoy looked at each other and Harry vividly recalled the last time they had come face-to-face: It had been in Flourish and Blotts bookshop, and they had had a fight.
Book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: My dad and Malfoy can't stand each other. That little stare-off just proves they haven't smoothed things over.

Book4-chapter6_Sc9.source: 'Spect they go to some foreign school," said Ron. "I know there are others. Never met anyone who went to one, though.
Book4-chapter6_Sc9.description: They're probably from a foreign school. I reckon there are other schools out there, I've just never met anyone from one.

Book4-chapter6_Sc9.source: Bill had a penfriend at a school in Brazil this was years and years ago and he wanted to go on an exchange trip but Mum and Dad couldn’t afford it.
Book4-chapter6_Sc9.description: Bill once had a penfriend in Brazil and wanted to go on exchange, but Mum and Dad couldn't afford it. That's why I've never met anyone from a foreign school either.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "His penfriend got all offended when he said he wasn’t going and sent him a cursed hat. It made his ears shrivel up." "Been saving my pocket money all summer for this," Ron told Harry as they and Hermione strolled through the salesmen, buying souvenirs.
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: Blimey, I saved up all summer for this and then that cursed hat business happened. I really wanted to get stuff and I've been counting my Galleons.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Wish I hadn’t bought this now," said Ron, gesturing at his dancing shamrock hat and gazing longingly at the Omnioculars.
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: What the hell, I want those Omnioculars more than this daft shamrock. I regret spending on the hat when those would be brilliant.

Book4-chapter6_Sc10.source: "No — don’t bother," said Ron, going red. He was always touchy about the fact that Harry, who had inherited a small fortune from his parents, had much more money than he did.
Book4-chapter6_Sc10.description: I'm always touchy about Harry's money. I don't like being reminded that he can buy things I can't, even if I'm glad he gives stuff sometimes.

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.source: Next to him, Ron was frozen in an attitude that looked as though he were about to dive from a springboard
Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was there frozen like I was going to dive right into the stadium; couldn't move, just staring

Book4-chapter8_Sc3.source: Ron, meanwhile, was absentmindedly shredding the shamrocks on his hat. "Huh?" said Ron
Book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: Huh? I was just absentmindedly tearing the shamrocks on my hat to bits while I gaped at the veela

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Like we’d say anything else surrounded by that lot," said Ron.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Like we'd say anything else surrounded by that lot. We're not about to admit we're backing anyone else when they're watching.

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Krum," said Ron quietly. "What?" said Hermione. "Krum!" said Ron. "Viktor Krum, the Bulgarian Seeker!"
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Krum. Viktor Krum is the Bulgarian Seeker. He's famous and everyone knows him.

Book4-chapter6_Sc8.source: "He looks really grumpy," said Hermione. "Who cares what he looks like? He’s unbelievable. He’s really young too. Only just eighteen or something. He’s a genius, you wait until tonight, you’ll see." said Ron.
Book4-chapter6_Sc8.description: Who cares what he looks like? He's unbelievable. He's only about eighteen and he's a proper genius. Wait until tonight, you'll see.

Book4-chapter6_Sc6.description: Blimey, the kids are mental. One of them just stomped a slug and it popped. That was gross and made a right fuss.
Bloody hell, there are people from America here with a big banner. This place is buzzing, and everyone is getting up and doing their own thing.

Book4-chapter6_Sc6.source: "And he was the best Beater the Wimbourne Wasps ever had."
Book4-chapter6_Sc6.description: People are already bragging about old Quidditch players. Everyone seems to be trading stories while they sort out breakfast.

Book4-chapter8_Sc4.source: “There you go,” Ron yelled happily, stuffing a fistful of gold coins into Harry’s hand, “for the Omnioculars! Now you’ve got to buy me a Christmas present, ha!”
Book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: Here, take these coins for the Omnioculars — and you owe me a Christmas present, yeah? Don't forget it.

Book4-chapter8_Sc4.source: “Excellent!” yelled Ron as the shamrock soared over them, and heavy gold coins rained from it, bouncing off their heads and seats.
Book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: Brilliant — gold raining from a giant shamrock! That's mental, absolutely brilliant.

Book4-chapter8_Sc4.source: “That’s him, that’s him!” yelled Ron, following Krum with his Omnioculars.
Book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: That's Krum! That's him — got to watch him, he's the one everyone's been talking about.

Book4-chapter6_Sc7.source: Er, is it my eyes, or has everything gone green?
Book4-chapter6_Sc7.description: Blimey, everything's gone green! The whole place is covered in shamrocks, it's mental.
Seamus is sitting with his mum and Dean and he spotted us straight away. They're still sound with us, and his mum's proud as anything about the decorations.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "All right if I go and dump my stuff in your room, Ron?" "Yeah . . . think I will too," "What's up, Harry?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Yeah, go on then, dump your stuff in my room. I’ll do the same. What's up, Harry? I'm eager and worried in the same breath.

Book4-chapter9_Sc2.source: "There’s something I haven’t told you," "On Saturday morning, I woke up with my scar hurting again."
Book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: Blimey, Harry's scar's been hurting again. That's worrying. I can't just shrug that off.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "But - he wasn't there, was he? You-Know-Who? I mean - last time your scar kept hurting, he was at Hogwarts, wasn't he?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: Blimey, I can't believe it, but it seems your scar hurting has matched up with when You-Know-Who turned up before.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "It was only a dream," said Ron bracingly.
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I want to believe it's just a nightmare and nothing more, to keep this from being real.

Book4-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Don't - say - his - name!" Ron hissed through gritted teeth.
Book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: Don't say his name. Bloody hell, the name itself makes me furious and scared.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: No, Mum. I'm not having my bits fussed with right now.

Book4-chapter9_Sc7.source: "Bill, who was playing chess with Ron."
Book4-chapter9_Sc7.description: I'm sitting here playing chess with Bill while all this fuss goes on.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Good thinking!" said Ron, his expression clearing. "I bet Sirius'll know what to do!"
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I reckon Sirius will know what to do. That's what I'd bet on.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: "Come and have a game of Quidditch in the orchard, Harry," said Ron. "Come on — three on three, Bill and Charlie and Fred and George will play. . . . You can try out the Wronski Feint. . . ."
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: Blimey, come on Harry, let's play Quidditch. It'll cheer you up. Try out the Wronski Feint with us.

Book4-chapter9_Sc4.source: There was a silence in which Ron fidgeted absentmindedly with a hole in his Chudley Cannons bedspread.
Book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I fiddle with my stuff when I'm nervous. It's how I show I'm worried but trying to keep things light.

Book4-chapter9_Sc11.source: [“I’m never wearing them,” Ron was saying stubbornly. “Never.”]
Book4-chapter9_Sc11.description: I'm not wearing those. Never. I mean it, I'm sticking to my guns.

Book4-chapter9_Sc11.source: [“Fine,” snapped Mrs. Weasley. “Go naked. And, Harry, make sure you get a picture of him. Goodness knows I could do with a laugh.”]
Book4-chapter9_Sc11.description: Brilliant. Mum's going to embarrass me and expects Harry to take a picture. Just great.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "It’s got to be a pretty boring life, hasn’t it, being a hat? I suppose it spends all year making up the next one."
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, the hat sings a different song every year. That must be a dull job, thinking up new songs forever.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Oooh c’mon, ’Er-my-knee," said Ron, accidentally spraying Harry with bits of Yorkshire pudding.
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: I joke with Hermione loads and wind her up, but I still look out for her. And I can be a prat, like spraying Harry by accident, sorry mate.

Book4-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Yeah, we thought Peeves seemed hacked off about something," said Ron darkly.
Book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, Peeves causes trouble in the kitchens and gets everyone stirred up. Nothing surprises me about him.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: Ron left his dress robes over Pigwidgeon as they left the train, heads bent and eyes narrowed against the downpour.
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: Blimey, I threw my dress robes over Pigwidgeon so he wouldn't get drenched while we forced our way through the storm.

Book4-chapter10_Sc6.source: Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Neville climbed gratefully into one of them, the door shut with a snap, and a few moments
Book4-chapter10_Sc6.description: We all piled into a carriage and slammed the door shut to stop the rain. Couldn't get in there quick enough.

Book4-chapter9_Sc12.source: Why is everything I own rubbish?
Book4-chapter9_Sc12.description: Blimey, why is everything I own rubbish? I'm furious about always ending up with rubbish stuff.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Nah, it would’ve been in the Daily Prophet," said Ron. "The Ministry would want to show they’d caught someone, wouldn’t they?"
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Nah, if Sirius had been caught it would be all over the Prophet. The Ministry would want the publicity, that's obvious.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Look, here’s the stuff Mum got for you in Diagon Alley. And she’s got some gold out of your vault for you . . . and she’s washed all your socks." He heaved a pile of parcels onto Harry’s camp bed and dropped the money bag and a load of socks next to it."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Mum's bought Harry stuff from Diagon Alley and even took gold from his vault. She's done his lot and washed his socks too. Mum does everything.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "What is that supposed to be?" He was holding up something that looked to Harry like a long, maroon velvet dress."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: What is that supposed to be? I was horrified when I saw what looked like a long maroon velvet dress. I couldn't believe Mum would give me anything like that.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Mum, you’ve given me Ginny’s new dress," said Ron, handing it out to her."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: I thought Mum had given me Ginny's new dress because it looked that bad. I was sure she'd mixed them up.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "I’ll go starkers before I put that on," said Ron stubbornly."
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: I'd sooner go starkers than wear those dress robes. I'm not wearing that, no way.

Book4-chapter9_Sc10.source: "Everyone wears them, Ron!" said Mrs. Weasley crossly. "They’re all like that! Your father’s got some for smart parties!"
Book4-chapter9_Sc10.description: Apparently everyone has dress robes and Dad's even got some for smart parties. Fine, everyone wears them, so I can't exactly refuse without looking odd.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Can I have a look at Uranus too, Lavender?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: Blimey, I asked to look at Uranus in class because I was curious. I don't care if it sounds daft.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: "Miserable old bat," said Ron bitterly as they joined the crowds...
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: That was a rotten bit of teaching. Trelawney going all strict on homework? That's mental. It'll take all weekend and I'm not happy about it.

Book4-chapter13_Sc2.source: Malfoy...brandishing a copy of the Daily Prophet..."Your dad’s in the paper, Weasley!"
Book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: My dad's been made fun of in the Prophet and they printed a picture of Mum. I'm furious and shaking with rage. Don't rub it in.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.source: Ron rolled his eyes at Harry
Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: Blimey, I rolled my eyes at Harry because he wasn't paying attention. I can't help being deadpan about some of this nonsense.
I muttered Harry's name to snap him out of nodding off. Don't be an eejit, I was thinking.

Book4-chapter13_Sc1.source: “Aaaaah, when two Neptunes appear in the sky, it is a sure sign that a midget in glasses is being born, Harry.”
Book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: I mocked Trelawney by doing her whispery voice and taking the piss about two Neptunes. I can't resist winding him up.

Book4-chapter10_Sc2.source: "Bagman wanted to tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts," he said grumpily, sitting down next to Harry. "At the World Cup, remember? But my own mother won’t say. Wonder what —"
Book4-chapter10_Sc2.description: Blimey, Bagman was going to tell everyone what's going on at Hogwarts, but Mum won't say anything. That's annoying and makes me wonder what she's hiding.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Er," said Ron tentatively, "my dad told me about one. . . . Is it called the Imperius Curse, or something?"
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: Blimey, yeah, the Imperius Curse. Dad's warned me about it before.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Total control," said Moody quietly as the spider balled itself up and began to roll over and over.
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, to see someone control another creature like that is terrifying. It's proper total control.

Book4-chapter14_Sc3.source: "The spider swelled. It was now larger than a tarantula."
Book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: That's mental, Moody can make things change size and then make them suffer with the Cruciatus. Stay well away.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Oh hurry up, I could eat a hippogriff.
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: Blimey, I'm starving. I could eat a hippogriff, I really could.

Book4-chapter12_Sc1.source: Ron muttering furiously under his breath as he pushed his sopping hair off his face.
Book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: My hair's soaked and I'm properly cross about being drenched. It's annoying and I'm grumpy about it.

Book4-chapter10_Sc1.source: "What d’you three know that we don’t?"
Book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: What d'you three know that we don't? I want to know what’s going on. Don’t keep me in the dark, that’s mental.
Mum, seriously. She’s hinting at something between us and Dumbledore and it’s doing my head in.
There’s something coming this year that might make it an interesting term. I’m expecting trouble or excitement and I’m ready for it.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: Blimey I thought he might be staying but Moody says he's only here for one year.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.source: "You’ll be Arthur Weasley’s son, eh? Your father got me out of a very tight corner a few days ago."
Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: Turns out my dad helped Moody out recently and Moody knows him. That's why Moody's doing Dumbledore a favor and sticking around for a year.

Book4-chapter14_Sc2.source: "I’m not supposed to show you what illegal Dark curses look like until you’re in the sixth year."
Book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: So they usually don't teach the nasty curses until sixth year but Moody's going to show us sooner.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Where is it? What country?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: Where the hell is Durmstrang? What country is it in?

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Come off it," said Ron, starting to laugh. "Durmstrang's got to be about the same size as Hogwarts — how are you going to hide a great big castle?"
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: Come off it. A massive castle like that can't just be hidden. That's mental.

Book4-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Ah, think of the possibilities," said Ron dreamily. "It would've been so easy to push Malfoy off a glacier and make it look like an accident. . . . Shame his mother likes him. . . ."
Book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: Blimey, imagine pushing Malfoy off a glacier. Would have been brilliant. Shame his mum fusses over him.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Don’t talk to me," Ron said quietly to Harry and Hermione as they sat down at the Gryffindor table a few minutes later, "Because I want to fix that in my memory forever," said Ron, his eyes closed and an uplifted expression on his face. "Draco Malfoy, the amazing bouncing ferret . . ."
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Blimey, I want to remember Malfoy as the bouncing ferret forever. That's up there with the best things ever.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "We haven’t got him till Thursday!" he said in a disappointed voice.
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, Moody is teaching Defense and I don't get him until Thursday. I'm gutted I'll have to wait.

Book4-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Moody!" he said. "How cool is he?" "Beyond cool," said George.
Book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: Moody is absolutely brilliant. I think he's proper cool and someone you actually want teaching Defense.

Book4-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Yeah, I know," said Ron, who was skipping on every alternate step. He had had much more difficulty with the curse than Harry, though Moody assured him the effects would wear off by lunchtime.
Book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I had a nightmare with that curse and it hit me worse than Harry. Moody says it should wear off by lunchtime, so I just need to hang on.

Book4-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Talk about paranoid . . ." Ron glanced nervously over his shoulder to check that Moody was definitely out of earshot and went on. "No wonder they were glad to get shot of him at the Ministry."
Book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: Moody is proper paranoid. No wonder the Ministry were glad to be rid of him. That's mental.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Weasley . . . what is that?" said Malfoy, pointing at Pigwidgeon’s cage. A sleeve of Ron’s dress robes was dangling from it... "Weasley, you weren’t thinking of wearing these, were you? I mean — they were very fashionable in about 1890"
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: Blimey, Malfoy had the nerve to mock my robes in front of everyone. He thinks he can make me look daft.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "‘Father’s always associated with the top people at the Ministry.’ . . . Dad could’ve got a promotion any time . . . he just likes it where he is. . . ."
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: My dad's not useless. He could've had more, but he likes what he does. I won't have Malfoy sneer at him.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Eat dung, Malfoy!" said Ron, the same color as the dress robes as he snatched them back out of Malfoy’s grip.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: I snapped at Malfoy and made it clear I won't take his insults. I'm furious and I'm protective of my family.

Book4-chapter10_Sc5.source: Ron got to his feet and slammed the sliding compartment door so hard behind them that the glass shattered.
Book4-chapter10_Sc5.description: I lost my temper and slammed the door. I was raging at how Malfoy was making us feel small.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: Imagine if Moody turned Snape into a horned toad," said Ron, his eyes misting over, "and bounced him all around his dungeon.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Blimey, the thought of Moody turning Snape into a horned toad and bouncing him around the dungeon made me laugh, I could nearly cry thinking about it.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: You’ll be Arthur Weasley’s son, eh? Your father got me out of a very tight corner a few days ago. . . . Yeah, I’m staying just the one year. Special favor to Dumbledore.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: I was dead relieved when Moody said he's staying for a year. Hearing my dad's name pop up made me feel chuffed and a bit proud.

Book4-chapter14_Sc1.source: Neville melting his sixth cauldron in Potions.
Book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: Neville managed to melt his sixth cauldron in Potions. Poor bloke, Snape gave him detention and it knocked him about.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Blimey, not the library. I’m sick of always going there for answers when it’s all guesswork and stress.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "Yeah, probably," said Ron. "But Dumbledore’s always done things his way, hasn’t he, and Moody’s been getting in trouble for years, I reckon. Attacks first and asks questions later — look at his dustbins. Balderdash."
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: I reckon Dumbledore and Moody do what they think is right even if the Ministry complains. Moody’s rough but he gets things done, even if it’s a bit mad.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "You know," said Ron, "I think it’s back to the old Divination standby." "What — make it up?" "Yeah," said Ron, sweeping the jumble of scrawled notes off the table, dipping his pen into some ink, and starting to write.
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: Bloody hell, making up fortunes is easier than pretending we understand that Divination waffle. If she’s happy with misery, give her misery.

Book4-chapter14_Sc5.source: "You know her — just put in loads of misery, she’ll lap it up."
Book4-chapter14_Sc5.description: I know how Hermione reacts when she’s worried. Wind her up with drama and she’ll take it seriously. I can use that to get a reaction or deflect attention.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.source: Ron had thrown himself backward and almost toppled off his seat as the spider skidded toward him.
Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, that was mental. I nearly fell off my seat when Moody killed that spider. It was like a punch to the stomach seeing it done so cleanly.

Book4-chapter14_Sc4.source: Several people looked uneasily around at her, including Ron.
Book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: Of course I'm uneasy hearing the name Avada Kedavra uttered in class. It's horrible to think anyone would actually use it, and worse to know there's no countercurse. That's proper scary.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: Blimey, they're pulling out a big old casket for the Goblet. I wasn't expecting that either.

Book4-chapter16_Sc1.source: "The champions will be chosen by an impartial selector: the Goblet of Fire."
Book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: So the Goblet picks the champions. Three champions, one from each school, and whoever does best after three tasks wins the Cup. Sound mental, doesn't it?

Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: Harry and Ron grinned at each other. They knew Hermione would rather eat bubotuber pus than miss such an important lesson.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: Blimey, Hermione would never miss this. We both knew she'd stick around no matter what. That's just her, really.
