Book4-chapter15_Sc1.source: Moody began to beckon students forward in turn and put the Imperius Curse upon them. Harry watched as, one by one, his classmates did the most extraordinary things under its influence.
Book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, Moody made everyone do daft things. Nobody could fight it, they all did what they were told until he lifted it.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [Must be]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Must be Mad-Eye Moody. Blimey, he looks proper rough.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [I’m going for it!]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: I'm dead keen on trying for the Triwizard. A thousand Galleons would be brilliant.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [I’m going for it! ... The champions’ll get to do all sorts of stuff you’d never be allowed to do normally. And a thousand Galleons prize money!]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Being a champion sounds ace. You get to do things you normally couldn't and there's loads of prize money.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [Dumbledore knows you’re not of age, though, ... Yeah, but he’s not the one who decides who the champion is, is he?]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: Dumbledore might stop us entering but maybe the judge is the one who actually picks champions. So there might be a way round it.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [I reckon a couple of drops of Aging Potion might do it, George.]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: If we really wanted to fool the judge we could try Aging Potion or some dodge like that. Sounds risky but tempting.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [Yeah, a thousand Galleons . . .]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: A thousand Galleons is stuck in my head. That'd sort out loads of stuff for me and my family.

Book4-chapter12_Sc3.source: [I s’pose they might want someone older. . . . Dunno if we’ve learned enough. . . .]
Book4-chapter12_Sc3.description: We might not have the experience for the tasks and they might want older students. I ain't sure we're ready.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: Hagrid, what's that? Blimey, he’s wearing cologne and acting all awkward about it.
He fancies her, honestly. Hagrid's gone and proper fallen for Madame Maxime.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "Well, if they end up having children, they’ll be setting a world record — bet any baby of theirs would weigh about a ton."
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: Well, if Hagrid and Madame Maxime ever have kids they'll be massive, won't they? Bet any baby of theirs would weigh about a ton.

Book4-chapter16_Sc5.source: "No!" said Ron loudly, but nobody heard him except Harry;
Book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: No! I couldn't believe it when Cedric was called. I wanted him to be shouted about differently, I don't know, it felt like a shock.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “Why d’you have to keep changing owls?” Ron asked in a low voice.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: Why do you keep swapping owls? It seems daft to use different ones all the time, especially if we're trying to be quiet about things.

Book4-chapter15_Sc4.source: “Nearly six,” said Ron, checking his watch and then staring down the drive that led to the front gates.
Book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: It's nearly six. I'm on watch for their arrival and I'm getting impatient, staring down the drive like you do when you're waiting for something good to happen.
Maybe Hagrid's beasts have got out. That would be awesome to see, though maybe a bit worrying. Still, imagine it, wild creatures everywhere.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: Blimey, I reacted straight away when Malfoy attacked Hermione. I’ll stand up for her and shout it out when she’s been hurt.

Book4-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Fifty points from Gryffindor and a detention each for Potter and Weasley."
Book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: We both got punished by Snape even though it was a mutual attack. That’s so unfair and it makes me furious.
What the hell, I thought, when Goyle got nailed. It showed our spells landed and we weren’t just causing trouble for no reason.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: Blimey, Hermione's gone on about house-elves loads and I still don't get why everyone is up in arms about it.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "True, both of them had paid two Sickles for a S.P.E.W. badge, but they had only done it to keep her quiet."
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I paid two Sickles for a S.P.E.W. badge, but only to shut Hermione up. I wasn't serious about joining her campaign.

Book4-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Ron now rolled his eyes at the ceiling, which was flooding them all in autumn sunlight,"
Book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I roll my eyes at Hermione's constant nags. Honestly, sometimes I just tune out and let her get on with it.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Anyone put their name in yet?" Ron asked a third-year girl eagerly.
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Anyone put their name in yet? I'm dying to know who’s trying for the Tournament.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Bet some of them put it in last night after we’d all gone to bed," said Harry. "I would’ve if it had been me . . . wouldn’t have wanted everyone watching. What if the goblet just gobbed you right back out again?"
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I reckon some people might have sneaked their names in during the night. I would have, if I wanted to avoid a crowd watching me.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "’Course she is, can’t see a beard, can you?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: She's old enough. I mean, Angelina's definitely seventeen. Can't see a beard, can you?

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "What is it with her?" said Ron, exasperated, as Hermione ran away up the marble staircase.
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: Blimey, Hermione and her causes. I find her obsession with things like badges a bit much sometimes.

Book4-chapter16_Sc3.source: "Okay," said Ron, "just as long as he doesn’t ask us to donate a few fingers to the skrewts."
Book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: If we go see Hagrid I just hope he does not expect me to lose any fingers to those blasted skrewts.

Book4-chapter18_Sc2.source: Ron was standing against the wall with Dean and Seamus. He wasn’t laughing, but he wasn’t sticking up for Harry either.
Book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: Blimey, I stood there with Dean and Seamus and did nothing. I wasn't joining in the laughing but I didn't speak up for Harry either.

Book4-chapter19_Sc13.source: "I just wondered where you —" Ron broke off, shrugging. "Nothing. I’m going back to bed."
Book4-chapter19_Sc13.description: Blimey, I shouldn't have poked my nose in. I'll just bugger off and go to bed then.

Book4-chapter19_Sc13.source: "Sorry about that," said Ron, his face reddening with anger. "Should’ve realized you didn’t want to be disturbed. I’ll let you get on with practicing for your next interview in peace."
Book4-chapter19_Sc13.description: Right, you're furious and I'm sorry. I get that you want to be left alone, even if I'm not sure what's going on.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: Ron said he would wait, so Harry reentered the tent
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: I'll stick with Harry. I said I’d wait for him and I will. Can’t leave him on his own right now.

Book4-chapter20_Sc8.source: It wasn’t just Ron . . . those weren’t only Gryffindors cheering in the crowd.
Book4-chapter20_Sc8.description: Blimey, it wasn’t just me cheering. Most of the school was on Harry’s side and Cedric’s too.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: Ron was "very white and staring at Harry as though he were a ghost."
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Blimey, I was terrified and stunned when Harry pulled it off, I just stood there white as a sheet staring at him like a ghost.

Book4-chapter20_Sc6.source: Ron entered the tent closely after Hermione.
Book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: Well, seeing him come out of that mess alive and with the egg changed everything for me, it was just mental.

Book4-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Hagrid’s been in loads of trouble before, and Dumbledore’s never sacked him," said Ron consolingly.
Book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: Hagrid's been in trouble loads of times but Dumbledore never sacks him. Blimey, Dumbledore sticks by Hagrid.

Book4-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Worst that can happen is Hagrid’ll have to get rid of the skrewts."
Book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: Worst that can happen is Hagrid'll just have to get rid of the skrewts. That's about it, really.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: Blimey, Krum's date is good-looking. I was laughing but I noticed it.
Bloody hell, the professor springing a test on us at the last minute is evil. It spoils the end of term for everyone.

Book4-chapter22_Sc1.source: Leave him alone, Hermione, he’s earned a bit of a break
Book4-chapter22_Sc1.description: Of course I stick up for Harry. He deserves a breather after everything he's done.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.source: [Ron even went and banged on one of the windows]
Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: Blimey, I even banged on the window and nothing. He's not answering us at all.

Book4-chapter24_Sc3.source: [They hammered on it for ten more minutes; ... but there was no response.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: That's mental. If Hagrid's shut himself away for a whole week, something's happened and it's not good.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Then he’s hoping you’ll help him find out what his egg means! I suppose you’ve been putting your heads together during those cozy little library sessions —"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Blimey, I reckon Krum might be trying to worm information out of Hermione to get to Harry. I don't trust him around her like that.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "No it isn’t!" shouted Ron. "It’s about winning!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Honestly, I think the whole Triwizard thing is about winning. Friends and making pals are secondary to the competition.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Did you know? About Hagrid being half-giant?" "No," Harry said, shrugging.
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: Hagrid being half-giant is a big deal. Giants are vicious, everyone knows that. No wonder Hagrid kept it quiet.

Book4-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Why don’t you go and find Vicky, he’ll be wondering where you are," said Ron. "Don’t call him Vicky!" Hermione jumped to her feet and stormed off"
Book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I was jealous and annoyed Hermione went with Krum. I don't like being last choice and I wanted her attention. That's why I snapped and called him 'Vicky'.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: [Harry finished reading and looked up at Ron, whose mouth was hanging open.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: Blimey, that's shocking. I can't believe they'd print that about Hagrid and his mother.

Book4-chapter24_Sc2.source: [Ron was sniggering, apparently very pleased with himself.]
Book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: Well, that's just daft. If anyone's laughing, it's daft, because Hagrid's not someone you poke fun at like that.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: ["Harry — we’ve just got to grit our teeth and do it," said Ron on Friday morning, in a tone that suggested they were planning the storming of an impregnable fortress.]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: We have to bite the bullet and do it. No faffing about. Just go and ask them.

Book4-chapter22_Sc2.source: ["When we get back to the common room tonight, we’ll both have partners — agreed?"]
Book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm convinced we'll sort partners tonight. I'm not letting us end up without someone.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Fancy a game of chess, Harry. It's a proper way to calm down and I know I can beat you if I play right.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "They’re only socks," said Ron, who had gone slightly pink around the ears, though he looked rather pleased all the same.
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, they're only socks, but yeah I feel chuffed. I get embarrassingly proud when someone notices what I gave.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "I still can’t work out how you two got the best-looking girls in the year," muttered Dean. "Animal magnetism," said Ron gloomily, pulling stray threads out of his cuffs.
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: Animal magnetism. I keep telling myself that's why I and Harry got dates. It sounds daft but I need to believe I've got some charm.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "Ron was watching Hermione pass with narrowed eyes."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: What the hell? Hermione looks different and I don't like it. I walked past her because I was annoyed and didn't fancy making a fuss.

Book4-chapter23_Sc1.source: "There was just no getting around the fact that his robes looked more like a dress than anything else."
Book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: My dress robes are pants. I had to Severing Charm the ruff and cuffs because otherwise I'd look ridiculous. Still looks a bit frayed but better than lace.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: She'll be after you next, Hermione," said Ron in a low and worried voice as they walked quickly back up the street.
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: She's going to come for you next, Hermione. I can see it, and that worries me.

Book4-chapter24_Sc5.source: You don't want to go upsetting Rita Skeeter," said Ron nervously. "I'm serious, Hermione, she'll dig up something on you —
Book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I'm serious, Hermione. Don't go poking Rita. She'll dig something up on you and it'll cause trouble. Blimey, it could get messy.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: “Yeh — yeh’re not half-giant!” said Hagrid croakily.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Blimey, Hagrid's really upset. I feel gutted for him and want him back with us at school.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: Hermione, Harry, and Ron still seem to want to know you, judging by the way they were attempting to break down the door.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Obviously we made a noise trying to get in. I wasn't going to sit there while Hagrid was miserable.

Book4-chapter24_Sc6.source: Dumbledore stood up. “I refuse to accept your resignation, Hagrid, and I expect you back at work on Monday,” he said.
Book4-chapter24_Sc6.description: Good on Dumbledore. I reckon Hagrid's coming back and that's what matters. No faffing about.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: Yeah, but there’s still the giant squid.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: Blimey, that squid is still out there. Krum swimming near the lake and the squid makes this mental.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: Maybe Percy’s poisoning him. Probably thinks if Crouch snuffs it he’ll be made Head of the Department of International Magical Cooperation.
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I reckon Percy might be plotting to get Crouch out of the way so he can get promoted. Sounds daft but it could happen.

Book4-chapter24_Sc4.source: Who cares if Diggory’s getting help?
Book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I don’t much care if Cedric gets help. If anyone deserves a fair go it is him but I am not fussed about Bagman favouring one champion over another.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “I’ll give you the one my mum knits me this Christmas, I always get one from her. You don’t mind maroon, do you?”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I like Dobby. I'll lend him Mum's Christmas jumper. He can have it, maroon and all.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “All these years I’ve been really impressed with Fred and George, nicking food from the kitchens — well, it’s not exactly difficult, is it? They can’t wait to give it away!”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Right, the house-elves are only too happy to hand out food. No need to be impressed with Fred and George for taking it. That's mental really.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “She seems to love him,” said Ron thickly (he had just started on a cream cake).
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Winky clearly loves Mr Crouch, even though she's free. It's weird and a bit sad but you can see how stuck she is in her loyalty.

Book4-chapter21_Sc3.source: “I’d still rather work for him than old Crouch,” said Ron. “At least Bagman’s got a sense of humor.”
Book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: Given a choice I'd pick someone like Bagman over Crouch. Bagman might be a bit of a toss up but at least he can crack a joke. Percy wouldn't understand any of that.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "I don\'t know what made me do it!"
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Blimey, I walked up to Fleur and just asked her to the ball with no idea why I did it. It was mad.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "She looked at me like I was a sea slug or something. Didn\'t even answer."
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: Fleur looked at me like I was nothing. She didn\'t even answer me properly. That was humiliating.

Book4-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Hermione, Neville\'s right \- you are a girl . . ."
Book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: What the hell, I only just noticed Hermione is a girl. Suddenly she looks different to me. That\'s mental.
Hermione insists she\'s already going with someone else. I don\'t believe her, but Ginny thinks she\'s telling the truth.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Barking mad said Ron shaking his head Harry c mon they ll be putting up your scores.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Barking mad. Come on Harry they re putting up your scores so stop standing about.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [You were the best you know no competition Cedric did this weird thing where he Transfigured a rock on the ground turned it into a dog ...]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Honestly you were the best. Cedric tried to distract the dragon by turning a rock into a dog.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Well that kind of worked too it went all sleepy but then it snored and this great jet of flame shot out and her skirt caught fire she put it out with a bit of water out of her wand.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Fleur's charm made the dragon nod off then it snored fire and set her skirt on fire, she put it out with water from her wand. Mad stuff.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Krum he wasn t supposed to do any damage to them they took marks off for that he wasn t supposed to do any damage to them.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Krum hit the dragon and made it go mental so it smashed a load of eggs. They docked him points for doing damage.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [It s marks out of ten from each one Madame Maxime ... Mr. Crouch nine ... Dumbledore nine ... Ludo Bagman ten ... Karkaroff four.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: Marks are out of ten from each judge. Maxime did a silver figure eight thing, Crouch put up a nine, Dumbledore a nine, Bagman gave a ten and Karkaroff gave a four.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Four? You lousy biased scumbag you gave Krum ten!]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: What the hell? Karkaroff's a biased idiot if he gives Krum a ten and me a four. That s just unfair.

Book4-chapter20_Sc7.source: [Harry don t complain Ron yelled excitedly Ron s indignation on his behalf was worth about a hundred points to him.]
Book4-chapter20_Sc7.description: I m dead proud of Harry. I ll shout for him and get angry on his behalf every time.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: Blimey, he's right. Dumbledore is a great bloke.

Book4-chapter24_Sc7.source: "Can I have one of these cakes, Hagrid?"
Book4-chapter24_Sc7.description: I'm casual with Hagrid, I can joke and help myself to his cakes. He's one of ours.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: Four people were bound tightly to the tail of the stone merperson. Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: Blimey, I'm stuck between Hermione and Cho and tied to that massive statue. This is mental. I need to get out of this fast.

Book4-chapter26_Sc5.source: There was also a girl who looked no older than eight, whose clouds of silvery hair made Harry feel sure that she was Fleur Delacour’s sister.
Book4-chapter26_Sc5.description: That's Fleur's sister there, poor kid's asleep like the rest of us. This isn't just about me and the others now, it's everyone. I can't leave any of them.

Book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I stood outside and gave the Fat Lady the password banana fritters. I waited there for Harry so he could sneak through.
I muttered good luck to Harry as he went past me. I wasn’t coming with him, just doing the password duty and wishing him well.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "I told you!" "I told you not to annoy Rita Skeeter!"
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: Blimey, I warned Hermione not to annoy Rita Skeeter. I'm annoyed and I feel protective about Hermione because that article makes her look awful.

Book4-chapter27_Sc1.source: "And what did you say?" "And what did you say?"
Book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I realised Hermione was keeping something about Viktor from me. I was jealous and desperate to know what she told him because I care and I can't help being nosy about it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc6.source: Ron floated, unconscious, a few inches above the lake bottom, drifting a little in the ebb of the water.
Book4-chapter26_Sc6.description: Blimey, I'm out cold and floating near the lake bottom. I can't move or do anything until someone gets these ropes off me.

Book4-chapter26_Sc8.source: the mermen now closed in around Ron and the little girl, shaking their heads at him.
Book4-chapter26_Sc8.description: Blimey, they're all over me and the little girl. This is bad, really bad. If they decide to drag us down I'm done for.

Book4-chapter29_Sc1.source: "What’re you doing here?" Ron and Fred said at the same time.
Book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: Blimey, I just turned up and demanded to know what they were doing here. It looked dodgy to me.
Who are you blackmailing? I wasn't going to let that slide. If you're extorting someone that's my business.

Book4-chapter29_Sc1.source: "It’s my business if you’re blackmailing someone," said Ron. "George’s right, you could end up in serious trouble for that."
Book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I genuinely think this is serious. If they're blackmailing someone they could land themselves in real trouble and I won't stand for it.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: Then he spotted Fleur’s sister. “What did you bring her for?”
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Bloody hell, what did you bring her for? I couldn't believe Harry had grabbed her in the first place.
Wet this, isn't it? I was soaked to the bone and trying to get my breath back.

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: “Harry, you prat,” said Ron, “you didn’t take that song thing seriously, did you? Dumbledore wouldn’t have let any of us drown!”
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: Harry, you prat. I thought that song was just to get you back in time. I didn't think Dumbledore would let us drown, so why risk it?

Book4-chapter26_Sc9.source: “It was only to make sure you got back inside the time limit!” said Ron. “I hope you didn’t waste time down there acting the hero!”
Book4-chapter26_Sc9.description: It was only to make sure you got back inside the time limit. I hope you weren't mucking about down there trying to be a hero.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "What . . . d’you reckon Moody’s here to keep an eye on Snape as well as Karkaroff?" Ron whispered
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Blimey, maybe Moody is watching Snape as well as Karkaroff. That would mean Snape is under suspicion.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Harry . . . maybe Moody thinks Snape put your name in the Goblet of Fire!"
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, what if Moody thinks Snape put Harry's name in the Goblet? That would explain all this searching.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "You just don’t like Crouch because of that elf, Winky," said Ron
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: You do not like Crouch because of Winky. That is why you jump to think Snape is guilty.

Book4-chapter26_Sc1.source: "Yeah, I don’t fancy walking around with a periscope sticking out of my head," said Harry. "I s’pose I could always attack someone in front of Moody; he might do it for me. . . ."
Book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I reckon if someone attacked Harry in front of Moody he might do the turning for him. It is not a perfect plan but it might work.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: Madam Pomfrey had gone to rescue Ron from Percy’s clutches; she led him over to Harry and the others, gave him a blanket and some Pepperup Potion
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: Blimey, I was a wreck and needed Pomfrey. Pepperup and a blanket fixed me up a bit.

Book4-chapter26_Sc10.source: "Yeah," said Ron, looking extremely hopeful, "yeah, a bit"
Book4-chapter26_Sc10.description: I helped out, sort of. I want people to think I did more than I did, but I did my bit.

Book4-chapter26_Sc2.source: What's he want to know about the next Hogsmeade weekend for?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: Blimey, what's he wanting to know that for? I kept asking why Sirius needed the Hogsmeade date, because it seemed odd to me.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “I bet it was Lucius Malfoy!” said Ron suddenly, so loudly that his voice echoed all around the cave,
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, I reckon Lucius Malfoy could easily have done it. He’s the sort who’d do something like that.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “Come off it,” said Ron incredulously. “Are you saying you reckon Ludo Bagman conjured the Dark Mark?”
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Come off it, Bagman being the one to conjure the Dark Mark sounds daft, but he was in the forest and he’s a bit odd so you can’t rule him out.

Book4-chapter27_Sc2.source: “Told you,” said Ron, looking meaningfully at Sirius, “told you she’s obsessed with house —”
Book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: Told you Hermione’s obsessed with house-elves. Still, she might be onto something about how people treat their servants being telling.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: Blimey, I reckon Snape avoiding Karkaroff and Crouch snooping about could mean Snape's up to something.

Book4-chapter27_Sc3.source: “I can try,” said Ron doubtfully. “Better not make it sound like I reckon Crouch is up to anything dodgy, though. Percy loves Crouch.”
Book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: I might ask Percy about Crouch, but I won't say anything that makes Percy think badly of him. Percy idolizes Crouch.
Bloody hell, just because Dumbledore's brilliant doesn't mean someone clever can't be bad. I'm not ready to dismiss that possibility.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "What . . . put fleas on her or something?"
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Blimey, when Harry talked about being bugged I first thought of something daft like fleas. Then I began to get interested in these hidden muggle devices.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Yeah," said Ron, "Gets it for the recipes."
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: My mum gets Witch Weekly for the recipes. That's why she reads it even if it's a bit rubbish.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Haven’t we got enough to worry about?"
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: Do we really need another thing to worry about? A vendetta against Rita sounds like overkill with everything else going on.

Book4-chapter28_Sc2.source: "Your mum doesn’t read Witch Weekly, by any chance, does she, Ron?" "Yeah," said Ron, whose mouth was full of toffee.
Book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: My family spoils each other. Mum sends Easter eggs and Percy writes, and I get stuck with massive toffee ones. It's all a bit Weasley.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “No chance of more of those eclairs, is there?” said Ron, who was looking around at the beaming and bowing house-elves.
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: Blimey, those eclairs are brilliant. I’m always on the lookout for more food when the house-elves are about.
I’m fed up with being poor. I really wish I had more money. It’s rubbish having to watch everyone else with things you can’t afford.

Book4-chapter28_Sc1.source: “The leprechaun gold I gave you for my Omnioculars. In the Top Box. Why didn’t you tell me it disappeared?”
Book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: That leprechaun gold I handed over for the Omnioculars vanished. I thought I was paying Harry back but it turns out it doesn’t stick around.
I’d love a niffler. They find gold everywhere. If I had one I reckon I could sort myself out a bit.

Book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: Who're you blackmailing? If you're messing about like that it could get you into proper trouble.

Book4-chapter29_Sc6.source: "George's right, you could end up in serious trouble for that."
Book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: George's right. I actually think this could land someone in deep trouble, so I can't just stand by.

Book4-chapter29_Sc6.source: "You're starting to sound a bit like our dear older brother, you are, Ron. Carry on like this and you'll be made a prefect." "No, I won't!"
Book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I don't want to be like Percy and I won't be made a prefect by acting like him. Don't even joke about it.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Well . . ." said Ron slowly, "I dunno if they would. They’re . . . they’re obsessed with making money lately, I noticed it when I was hanging around with them — when — you know —"
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: They're totally obsessed with making money lately. They're going on about their future and starting a joke shop and they need gold to get going.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Yeah, but blackmail . . ." "It’s this joke shop idea they’ve got," said Ron.
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I reckon they might do dodgy stuff to get cash. They don't exactly mind breaking rules, so who knows, they could cross the line.

Book4-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Are you mad?" said Ron. "Tell Percy? He’d probably do a Crouch and turn them in."
Book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: Tell Percy? No way. He'd squeal on them straight away. I won't dob Fred and George in to Percy.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Who is this woman and where's Hagrid? I'm gobsmacked that Hagrid's not at his own door.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: "What d’you reckon’s wrong with him? You don’t think a skrewt — ?"
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: Blimey, I half thought Hagrid might've been attacked by one of his creatures, but Malfoy says he's too ashamed to show his face, which makes me even more worried.

Book4-chapter24_Sc1.source: Narration: "Harry finished reading and looked up at Ron, whose mouth was hanging open."
Book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: That article in the Prophet about Hagrid being part-giant and dangerous really shocked me. I can't believe they'd print that about him.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "It must've been Crouch," said Ron at once. "That's why he was gone when Harry and Dumbledore got there. He'd done a runner."
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Blimey, I reckon Crouch did a runner. That's why he wasn't there when Harry and Dumbledore turned up.

Book4-chapter29_Sc4.source: "Okay . . . how's this for a theory," said Ron excitedly. "Krum attacked Crouch — no, wait for it — and then Stunned himself!"
Book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: Right, here's a mad one. What if Krum attacked Crouch and then accidentally Stunned himself? That's mental but could explain things.
Oh yeah, that's not convincing. Still, something weird happened and we need to sort it out.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "He's from Durmstrang!" spat Ron. "He's competing against Harry! Against Hogwarts!"
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Blimey, I'm furious that Hermione's been cozying up to Krum. He's from Durmstrang and he's competing against us. That's the whole point.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: "I s'pose he asked you to come with him while you were both in the library?" "Yes, he did," said Hermione, the pink patches on her cheeks glowing more brightly.
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: Obviously I reckon Hermione's been letting him hang about in the library to get close to her. I don't trust it and I'm not holding back.

Book4-chapter23_Sc2.source: Padma was sitting with her arms and legs crossed, one foot jiggling in time to the music. Every now and then she threw a disgruntled look at Ron, who was completely ignoring her.
Book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I ignored Padma while sulking. I wasn't interested in sitting civilly. I was glaring at Hermione and Krum and not bothering to hide it.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "But he was out of his mind, like you said, so half of it was probably just raving,"
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: Blimey, he was raving half the time. A lot of what he said might not mean anything.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "Maybe he didn't want you to get there!" said Ron quickly.
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: Maybe Snape actively tried to stop me getting there. What the hell, why would he do that?

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "Maybe - hang on - how fast d'you reckon he could've gotten down to the forest? D'you reckon he could've beaten you and Dumbledore there?"
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: How fast could he have gotten to the forest? Could he have beaten me and Dumbledore there? Sounds mad, but we have to consider it.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "Not unless he can turn himself into a bat or something," said Harry. "Wouldn't put it past him," Ron muttered.
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: Wouldn't put it past him, really. I can imagine anything with that lot.

Book4-chapter29_Sc5.source: "Unless Crouch was already outside the grounds," said Ron, "because it only shows up to the boundaries, doesn't -"
Book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: If Crouch was outside the grounds the Map wouldn't show him. That could explain it.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore reckons You-Know-Who's getting stronger again as well?" Ron whispered.
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Blimey, Dumbledore thinks You-Know-Who is getting stronger again. That's terrifying.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He really trusts Snape, even though he knows he was a Death Eater?"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: He trusts Snape despite Snape being a Death Eater. I don't like it, but if Dumbledore does, maybe I should keep my mouth shut about it.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "What’s Malfoy doing?" Ron said. "He looks like he’s using a walkie-talkie,"
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Malfoy was up to something suspicious with Crabbe and Goyle, acting like he had a walkie-talkie. Probably showing off or setting me up to be mocked.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "No way. Not today. That old cow." reaction to newspaper
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Honestly, that Skeeter woman is poisonous. Seeing that article about me makes me boil. She's gone too far.

Book4-chapter31_Sc1.source: "We’ve got our History of Magic exam in ten minutes! Blimey," he said, turning back to Harry, "she must really hate that Skeeter woman to risk missing the start of an exam."
Book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: Hermione hated Skeeter enough to risk missing an exam to chase this. She really is furious about what that reporter's done.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: All right, so what actually happened then? Come on, tell us straight.

Book4-chapter37_Sc3.source: "But that was all your savings!" said Ron.
Book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: Blimey, that was everything they had. That's rotten luck and it makes me angry for them.

Book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I told Mum to shut up and tried to calm things down. I was defending Harry, making sure she didn't make things worse.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: It’s very good already, said Ron in a strangled sort of voice.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: Blimey, Fleur's English is pretty good already. I couldn't help being a bit uselessly jealous, really.
Bloody hell, I actually asked Krum for his autograph. I can't believe I did that, but I wanted it, plain and simple.

Book4-chapter37_Sc2.source: That’s never — you’re kidding — No, I’m not ... I caught her on the windowsill in the hospital wing.
Book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: What the hell? Rita Skeeter's a beetle. I saw her in the jar and I couldn't believe it at first, but Hermione's nailed it. She's been sneaking about like some creepy bug.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Who?" called Hagrid, coming to the door. "Harry!" ... "Who?" said Ron curiously.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Who? I asked because I wanted to know who was here. I can't help being nosy and I say things straight out.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Madame Maxime, o’ course!" said Hagrid. "You two made up, have you?" said Ron.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: Blimey, I asked if Hagrid and Madame Maxime had made up. I was curious and a bit cheeky about them getting on again.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: "Dunno what yeh’re talkin’ about," said Hagrid airily.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: When Hagrid brushed it off, I went along with it but I was still watching. If Hagrid's hiding something, that's mental.

Book4-chapter37_Sc1.source: Harry, Ron, and Hermione looked up at him, shocked.
Book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: When Hagrid said he knew Voldemort would come back, we were all stunned. Bloody hell, that's terrifying and it means it's real.

Book5-chapter4_Sc2.source: "Let him breathe, Hermione," said Ron, grinning, closing the door behind Harry.
Book5-chapter4_Sc2.description: Give him a minute, will ya? I’m here for Harry, backing him up and trying to calm Hermione down.

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "We told Dumbledore we wanted to tell you what was going on," "We did, mate. But he’s really busy now, we’ve only seen him twice since we came here and he didn’t have much time, he just made us swear not to tell you important stuff when we wrote, he said the owls might be intercepted"
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: We asked Dumbledore about telling you and he told us not to. He's been busy and we only saw him a couple of times

Book5-chapter4_Sc4.source: "We’re not!" "Mum won’t let us near the meetings, she says we’re too young"
Book5-chapter4_Sc4.description: We're not in the big meetings either. Mum won't let us go because she thinks we're too young
Don't be thick, Harry. It isn't that Dumbledore thinks you can't be trusted, stop jumping to the worst conclusions

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: Blimey, Mum's terrified but I know Sirius isn't a threat to Harry and I back him and Harry no matter what

Book4-chapter36_Sc5.source: "Bill, Ron, and Hermione were staring at Fudge."
Book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: Fudge is refusing to accept the obvious and that makes me furious because we all saw what happened

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix,” said Ron at once.
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: This place is the Order of the Phoenix's headquarters. I know it straight away. Didn't want him to be left out, really.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “— we’ve met about twenty of them,” said Ron, “but we think there are more . . .”
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: We've met about twenty members of the Order so far, but there must be more. It's bigger than we thought.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “Fred and George have invented Extendable Ears, see,” said Ron. “They’re really useful.”
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: Fred and George have made Extendable Ears. They're dead useful for eavesdropping, though Mum went mad when she found them.

Book5-chapter4_Sc5.source: “FOUR WEEKS I’VE BEEN STUCK IN PRIVET DRIVE, NICKING PAPERS OUT OF BINS TO TRY AND FIND OUT WHAT’S BEEN GOING ON —”
Book5-chapter4_Sc5.description: I've been stuck at Privet Drive for four weeks scrapping around to find out what's been happening. I'm not happy about being left out or kept in the dark.

Book5-chapter4_Sc1.source: "No, Harry, the meeting’s only for members of the Order. Ron and Hermione are upstairs, you can wait with them until the meeting’s over..."
Book5-chapter4_Sc1.description: Blimey, so me and Hermione are stuck upstairs while the meeting's started without us. We’re meant to wait quietly until it finishes.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "— and some of them are standing guard over something," "They’re always talking about guard duty."
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: Blimey, some of them are on guard duty. They keep banging on about guard duty like it’s the only thing that matters.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Oh yeah," said Ron, with a look of dawning comprehension.
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: Oh yeah, I suddenly twigged what Harry meant. It all makes sense now.

Book5-chapter4_Sc6.source: "Both of them were watching him apprehensively, as though they feared that he would start shouting again now that everyone else had gone."
Book5-chapter4_Sc6.description: We were all on edge around Harry because we thought he might blow up. I feel bad seeing him like that and it makes me watch him more carefully.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "She’s been in a right state," said Ron. "Pecked us half to death when she brought your last letters, look at this —" He showed Harry the index finger of his right hand, which sported a half-healed but clearly deep cut.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Blimey, Hedwig's been ferocious bringing letters. She nearly pecked me to bits and I even got a proper cut for my trouble.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "We wanted to give them to you, mate," said Ron.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: We wanted to tell you everything, mate, but Dumbledore made us promise not to. We were only obeying orders.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "I think he thought you were safest with the Muggles," Ron began.
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: I reckon Dumbledore honestly believed keeping you with the Dursleys was safer. I don't agree with how it went, but that's what he thought.

Book5-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Had to look after myself after all, didn’t I?" said Harry. "He was so angry," said Hermione in an almost awestruck voice. "Dumbledore. We saw him."
Book5-chapter4_Sc3.description: Well, I feel guilty that Harry thinks we kept things from him. We were trying to follow Dumbledore and keep him safe, not to shut him out.

Book5-chapter6_Sc3.source: She doesn’t trust us at all, you know
Book5-chapter6_Sc3.description: Blimey, she really does not trust us, does she? It’s rubbish but bloody obvious.

Book5-chapter6_Sc5.description: I got furious when that elf insulted Hermione. Bloody hell, calling her a Mudblood was not on, and I said so straight away.
I was thinking about Mum's reaction to Mundungus bringing dodgy cauldrons here. I knew she’d go mad.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "We’re of age!" Fred and George bellowed together. "If Harry’s allowed, why can’t I?" shouted Ron.
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: I think it’s unfair that Harry might get to ask questions and we don’t. I want to know what’s going on too. If he’s allowed, why not me?

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Mum, I want to!" wailed Ginny. "NO!" shouted Mrs Weasley.
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: Mum’s strict about who stays in the kitchen and who gets told things. I’m right behind Harry and Ginny in wanting in, but Mum won’t hear it.

Book5-chapter5_Sc2.source: "I don’t think we need to hear any more of your business dealings, thank you very much, Mundungus," said Mrs Weasley sharply, as Ron slumped forward onto the table, howling with laughter.
Book5-chapter5_Sc2.description: We all laughed at Mundungus’s story. I thought it was brilliant. It lightened the mood before things got tense again.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “Well, they didn’t tell us much we couldn’t have guessed, did they?”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: They didn’t tell us anything we hadn’t already worked out. Don’t see the point of all that fuss if it was obvious.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “We already knew nearly everything they told us, from using the Extendable Ears.”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: We’d already picked up most of that by eavesdropping with the Extendable Ears. It wasn’t new information to us.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “But there can’t be anything worse than the Avada Kedavra curse, can there?”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: If something worse than killing exists, I can’t even imagine it. What’s worse than death?
If there is a weapon, I’d rather it’s on our side. I’m nervous about who’s got it.
I guessed it might be kept at Hogwarts. If Dumbledore has it, that at least makes me feel slightly safer.

Book5-chapter6_Sc2.source: “You two just Apparated on my knees!”
Book5-chapter6_Sc2.description: Blimey, Fred and George just Apparated on me and it hurt. Don’t do that in the dark.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "We can’t let them out to hunt every night," Ron explained.
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: Blimey, Dumbledore doesn't want lots of owls swooping about. We can't let Hedwig and Pigwidgeon hunt every night or it looks suspicious.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "Kreacher," said Ron as he turned off the light. "First night I was here he came wandering in at three in the morning. Trust me, you don’t want to wake up and find him prowling around your room."
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: I'm bolting the door because of Kreacher. He turned up in the middle of the night before. You do not want him prowling your room, honestly.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "But there can’t be anything worse than the Avada Kedavra curse, can there?" said Ron. "What’s worse than death?"
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: What's worse than death? I can't imagine anything nastier than the Killing Curse, but if this weapon exists it might be worse. That's worrying.

Book5-chapter6_Sc1.source: "If it is, Dumbledore’s probably keeping it," said Fred. "Where?" said Ron quickly. "Hogwarts?" "Bet it is!" said George.
Book5-chapter6_Sc1.description: I half hope our side has it. If it is safe with us, Dumbledore's probably keeping it at Hogwarts. That would make me feel a bit better.

Book5-chapter11_Sc2.source: "Excellent," said Ron, with a kind of groan of longing, and he seized the nearest plate of chops and began
Book5-chapter11_Sc2.description: Brilliant, I'm starving. Give me food now, those chops look perfect. Honestly, I'm not thinking about anything else right this second.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Harry’ll tell me and Hermione everything you say anyway!" said Ron hotly. "Won’t — won’t you?" he added uncertainly, meeting Harry’s eyes.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Harry’ll tell us everything, right? Don’t leave me out, I’m not having it.

Book5-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Well, as everyone thinks I’m a mad mass murderer and the Ministry’s put a ten-thousand-Galleon price on my head, I can hardly stroll up the street and start handing out leaflets, can I?" said Sirius restlessly.
Book5-chapter5_Sc3.description: Looks like the situation is dangerous and complicated. People can’t just go around warning everyone because of politics and bounties and all that.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: That's Kreacher, the house-elf who lives here. He's a weird one, honestly.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: Nutter. Never met one like him.
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: He's a right nutter, I tell you. I've never seen a house-elf like that before.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: His life's ambition is to have his head cut off and stuck up on a plaque just like his mother,
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: Apparently Kreacher's idea of a good life is insane stuff like having his head stuck on a plaque. That's just mental.

Book5-chapter4_Sc7.source: Hermione still hasn't given up on spew —
Book5-chapter4_Sc7.description: Hermione still believes in that Society for Elfish Welfare thing. She won't drop it.
I'm starving, so let's go to dinner. I can't hang about listening to all this.
Wait up. If they're still in the hall we might be able to hear something, so don't move yet.
Snape doesn't eat here. Thank goodness for that.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "'Course, once Dumbledore turned up on your side, there was no way they were going to convict you," said Ron happily
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Once Dumbledore backed you, it was a done deal. I knew you would get off. Of course he swung it for you.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "I bet Dumbledore turns up this evening to celebrate with us, you know," said Ron happily.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: I was hoping Dumbledore would come round to celebrate. It would mean a lot to have him here with us.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Prefect?" said Fred, staring incredulously at the letter. "Prefect?"
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: I am actually a prefect. I still cannot quite believe it but Mum is over the moon and the twins are taking the mickey. It is a massive deal for me and the family.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Get him red and gold to match his badge," said George, smirking.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Everyone is making a fuss about my prefect badge. Mum is thrilled and the twins are joking but I am proud even if it is embarrassing.

Book5-chapter9_Sc1.source: "I feel like a house-elf," grumbled Ron.
Book5-chapter9_Sc1.description: Help around the headquarters is hard work and I moan about it but I know we need to do it. Still, blimey it is a lot of scrubbing.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: He can't have just left. Hagrid wouldn't do that.
Okay, maybe Hagrid's away on that job for Dumbledore. That settles it for now.
Blimey, Umbridge's cardigan is ridiculous. I can't help sneering at her.

Book5-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Branched out a bit this year, hasn’t it?"
Book5-chapter11_Sc1.description: The Sorting Hat went beyond its usual lines and even tried to give the school advice this year. That's unusual.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Anything good in there?" asked Ron as Harry closed the magazine.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Blimey, I was just asking if there was anything worth a look. I don't take the Quibbler too seriously but I was curious.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: "Chuck us another Frog," said Ron, who had clearly noticed nothing.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: Give us another Chocolate Frog, yeah? I was still messing about and hadn't clocked how tense Harry and Hermione were.

Book5-chapter10_Sc4.source: Ron, Hermione, Ginny, and Neville laughed.
Book5-chapter10_Sc4.description: I laughed with the others because that's what you do, but I can see now I missed how worried Harry was. I should pay more attention when he looks like that.

Book5-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Ow kunnit nofe skusin danger ifzat?" (How can it know if the school's in danger if it's a hat?)
Book5-chapter11_Sc3.description: How can a hat know when the school's in danger? That's mad. A hat can't pick up danger like a person can.

Book5-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Only because you’re terrified of him," said Ron.
Book5-chapter11_Sc3.description: He's terrified of the Bloody Baron. Honestly, Nick's all puffed up about bravery but he's scared of that ghastly bloke.

Book5-chapter11_Sc5.source: "See you later," he said to Ron and Hermione and he made his way out of the Great Hall alone,"
Book5-chapter11_Sc5.description: Blimey, he just left us and scarpered off on his own. Fine by me, see you later then.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Oh lighten up," said Ron, "he hasn't seen daylight for months, poor bloke."
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Blimey, Sirius hasn't seen much daylight. He's not causing trouble on purpose, he's just starving for some freedom.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "We’re — well — Ron and I are supposed to go into the prefect carriage," Hermione said awkwardly.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Right, I'm supposed to go to the prefect carriage with Hermione. It's a pain but rules are rules.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "I’m not enjoying it, I’m not Percy," he finished defiantly.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, I'm not taking this prefect thing like Percy's going to. I don't like it and I'm not pretending I do.

Book5-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Yeah, definitely," said Ron, casting a shifty, anxious look at Harry.
Book5-chapter10_Sc1.description: I don't want to leave Harry alone. I feel bad about being pulled away by prefect duties and I hope we see each other later.

Book5-chapter11_Sc4.source: "I’m not allowed to ask a simple question?"
Book5-chapter11_Sc4.description: Blimey, I'm only trying to ask a simple question and suddenly I'm the villain. That's a bit much, isn't it?

Book5-chapter11_Sc4.source: "That was about the dullest speech I’ve ever heard, and I grew up with Percy."
Book5-chapter11_Sc4.description: That speech was dreadfully dull. Honestly, it was one of the dullest things I've sat through, and I've endured Percy.
I got carried away and called the first years names. I didn't mean to be cruel, I was just being loud and stupid.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: That’s the worst Monday I’ve ever seen.
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Blimey, today is horrendous. Loads of nightmare classes all in one go and I’m not looking forward to it.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: Well, it’d be cool to be an Auror
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Being an Auror sounds dead brilliant. It’s elite and you have to be really good, but yeah I’d love that.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: They bought me a new set of dress robes this summer, and I couldn’t understand where they got the Galleons
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: Fred and George have more money than I expected. I’m wondering where they got it from and that’s a bit suspicious.

Book5-chapter12_Sc1.source: You don’t support them, do you?
Book5-chapter12_Sc1.description: I can be clueless and tactless. I upset Cho by being daft about her badge and Hermione is right to tell me off.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: She and Ron pinned their prefect badges carefully to their chests.
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Blimey, I was fussing with my prefect badge, checking how it looked in the window, making sure it was on right.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Where's Pig?" said Ron's voice, right behind Harry.
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Where's Pig? I kept asking, worried because Pigwidgeon had gone with Luna and I hadn't got him back yet.
I was seriously worried about Harry when he started going on about things I couldn't see. I asked him if he was all right because it looked odd.

Book5-chapter10_Sc5.source: "Shall we get in, then?" said Ron uncertainly, looking at Harry as though worried about him.
Book5-chapter10_Sc5.description: Bloody hell, I wasn't seeing the horses and I thought Harry might be losing it, so I hesitated and just wanted him to get on with us.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Blimey, I'm starving and a Chocolate Frog will sort me out. Always room for food, honestly.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: And guess who’s a Slytherin prefect? Malfoy
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Malfoy got made a prefect. Of course he did. That's just wonderful, isn't it?

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: You went to the Yule Ball with Padma Patil
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Yeah, I went with Padma. She didn't enjoy it much because I wouldn't dance with her properly. Not my fault, but awkward all the same.

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: I’ll make Goyle do lines, it’ll kill him, he hates writing
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: I'll make Goyle do lines and he's going to hate it. That's the sort of thing I can get away with as a prefect, so why not have a bit of fun?

Book5-chapter10_Sc3.source: Are you taking the mickey? Baboon’s backside!
Book5-chapter10_Sc3.description: Luna found me hilarious for some reason and laughed her head off. I was baffled, honestly. What the hell was that about?

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "I never thought it would be me!" he said, shaking his head, "I thought it would be you!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Blimey, I couldn't believe I'd been made a prefect. I honestly thought Harry would get it.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "She says she’ll get the Cleansweep if she can."
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: Well, Mum's going to try and get me a new Cleansweep. I know she won't be able to afford a Nimbus but I'll be happy with that.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Listen — Ron — well done, mate." The smile faded off Ron’s face."I never thought it would be me!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I wanted to be pleased for Harry when he congratulated me, and I am. It still means a lot that he said well done.

Book5-chapter9_Sc2.source: "They’ve always said only prats become prefects. . . . Still," he added on a happier note, "they’ve never had new brooms!"
Book5-chapter9_Sc2.description: I know the twins think prefects are prats, but I'm looking forward to getting a new broom, and that makes being a prefect feel worth it.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Blimey, when Harry said Voldemort's back it shocked everyone. We're shaken but we're with Harry on this.

Book5-chapter12_Sc3.source: "Harry, no!" said Hermione in a warning voice, tugging at his sleeve, but Harry jerked his arm out of her reach.
Book5-chapter12_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, things are getting tense. I'm backing Harry even when it's risky. He needs us to stick by him.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "And she’s trying to get people to spy for her," said Ron darkly. "Remember when she said she wanted us to come and tell her if we hear anyone saying You-Know-Who’s back?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: She's trying to get people to spy on us. Remember she asked us to report anyone saying You-Know-Who's back? That's dodgy.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "No — come on, Hermione — we can’t tell them off for giving out sweets . . ."
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: Blimey, we can't exactly tell them off for handing out sweets. It's awkward.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: Ron rose halfway out of his chair, hovered uncertainly for a moment or two, then muttered to Harry, "She’s got it under control," before sinking as low in his chair as his lanky frame permitted.
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: She'll handle it. I'll back off and let Hermione sort them out. Don't want to get in her way.

Book5-chapter13_Sc1.source: "Thank you for your support, Ron," Hermione said acidly. "You handled it fine by yourself," Ron mumbled.
Book5-chapter13_Sc1.description: I didn't help much with Hermione and the twins. I kept my head down. Bit useless, really.

Book5-chapter13_Sc6.source: Ron, who had been fast asleep when Harry got back to the dormitory, muttered something about “doing other stuff,” bent low over his parchment, and scrawled a few words. “That’ll have to do,” he said, slamming the diary shut, “I’ve said I dreamed I was buying a new pair of shoes, she can’t make anything weird out of that, can she?”
Book5-chapter13_Sc6.description: Blimey, I nearly missed that. I fobbed her off with 'I dreamed I was buying a new pair of shoes' so she can't get anything weird from me. Worked well enough.

Book5-chapter13_Sc6.source: “Hey — I forgot — did she let you off for Friday?” “No,” said Harry. Ron groaned sympathetically.
Book5-chapter13_Sc6.description: She didn't let him off for Friday. That's rotten. Poor Harry, that's tough luck.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "That’s not on," said Ron angrily. "You’re trying to trick them into picking up the hats. You’re setting them free when they might not want to be free."
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: That's not on. I reckon Hermione's trying to trick house-elves into being set free and that might not be what the elves want.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "They should at least see what they’re picking up," he said firmly.
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: If someone's going to pick up a hat they should at least see it. I cleared the rubbish off so they know what they're grabbing.

Book5-chapter13_Sc2.source: "There’s no point trying to finish this now, I can’t do it without Hermione, I haven’t got a clue what you’re supposed to do with moonstones, have you?"
Book5-chapter13_Sc2.description: I can't finish the homework on my own. I haven't a clue about moonstones and need Hermione to sort it out.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "What d'you reckon are the odds of Umbridge letting you off on Friday?" said Ron skeptically.
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: Blimey, the odds of Umbridge letting me off are about zero. She's not exactly the forgiving type.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: Ron moaned and for some reason glanced up at the ceiling. "And it looks like it's going to rain."
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: I moaned about everything piling up and then got all awkward about the weather. I'm easily distracted and not great at hiding it.

Book5-chapter13_Sc4.source: "Nothing," said Ron at once, his ears reddening.
Book5-chapter13_Sc4.description: I get embarrassed and say stuff to cover it up. I hate being caught out and I turn red like a beetroot.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: Blimey, that’s Percy's writing all right. He’s sent me a letter.
What’s he written to me? I need to know what he thinks about my becoming a prefect.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.source: When he had finished reading, he looked disgusted.
Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: That letter’s full of Percy’s smug congratulations and advice. Bloody hell, he’s acting like he’s superior and expecting me to follow his rules.

Book5-chapter14_Sc5.source: "I must admit that I have always been afraid that you would take what we might call the 'Fred and George' route"
Book5-chapter14_Sc5.description: Percy still sees me as childish and is trying to peg me as the one who should behave like him. That’s made things awkward between us.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: Ron, who had pelted toward the ground to catch the Quaffle before it landed, pulled out of the dive untidily, so that he slipped sideways on his broom, and returned to playing height, blushing.
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Blimey, I went in too hard for that catch and totally lost my footing. Ended up all sideways and bright red.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Sorry!" Ron groaned, zooming forward to see whether he had done any damage.
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: I felt awful when I hit Katie in the face with the Quaffle. I shot straight over to check she was okay.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "It would have been hard to say whether Ron’s face or the Quaffle was a deeper scarlet when he returned again to playing height."
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: I know I looked a right mess after that. Proper embarrassing, but I kept at it until I actually caught the Quaffle.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "On his third attempt, Ron caught the Quaffle; perhaps out of relief he passed it on so enthusiastically that it soared straight through Katie’s outstretched hands and hit her hard in the face."
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: When I finally caught it I overdid the pass out of relief and hit Katie. I’m useless at calming down once I’m wound up.

Book5-chapter14_Sc2.source: "Fred and George converged on Katie. 'Here, take this,' Fred told her, handing her something small and purple from out of his pocket."
Book5-chapter14_Sc2.description: Fred and George look out for people when something goes wrong. They’ll shove a quick fix into someone’s hand and make it better fast.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "Well, she said she was pleased when I told her," said Ron, looking slightly put out.
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: Well, I told her and she said she was pleased. I felt a bit put out about it all.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "Come here, Ron, and see if Oliver’s old robes fit you"
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: I moved off to try on Oliver's old robes when they called me over.

Book5-chapter13_Sc9.source: "Look, I know he’s your best mate, but he’s not fabulous," said Angelina
Book5-chapter13_Sc9.description: People are being blunt about me. Angelina thinks I'm not fabulous but she expects me to improve with training.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Yeah," said Ron, who had become quieter and quieter all the way down to the pitch.
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: I’m feeling quiet and tense before the match. Don’t ask for a chat, I’m focusing.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "Why would anyone put a Flying Charm on a moldy old log like that?"
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: Blimey, their sneering about my broom gets to me. I’m not having that—I'll show them it flies just fine.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "They fitted him well considering they had been Oliver Wood’s, who was rather broader in the shoulder."
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: These robes fit surprisingly well even if they were Wood’s. Lucky me, I suppose.

Book5-chapter14_Sc1.source: "The Slytherins, led by Malfoy, roared and screamed with laughter."
Book5-chapter14_Sc1.description: When I dropped the Quaffle and they laughed, it stung. That’s embarrassing but I’m not going to let it finish me off.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: Poisonous toadstools don’t change their spots
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Poisonous toadstools don't change. Snape's a nastypiece and I don't trust him any more now than I ever did.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: where’s the evidence he ever really stopped working for You-Know-Who?
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: I keep thinking, show me proof Snape stopped working for You-Know-Who. I don't trust him just because Dumbledore says so.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: D’you realize how much homework we’ve got already? ... that Umbridge woman had better not give us any
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, we've got tons of homework. Binns, Snape, Trelawney, and now Umbridge. O.W.L. year is going to be a nightmare if she piles more on.

Book5-chapter12_Sc2.source: We’re not going to use magic?
Book5-chapter12_Sc2.description: Hang on, we're not going to use magic in Defence? That's daft. How are we supposed to learn to fight if we never practise spells?

Book5-chapter14_Sc7.source: "Your loyalty, Ron, should be not to him, but to the school and the Ministry."
Book5-chapter14_Sc7.description: Blimey, someone's telling me to be loyal to the school and the Ministry instead of Dumbledore like it's the obvious thing to do!

Book5-chapter14_Sc7.source: "a certain Sturgis Podmore, who is a great friend of Dumbledore’s, has recently been sent to Azkaban for trespass at the Ministry."
Book5-chapter14_Sc7.description: Bloody hell, they reckon Sturgis Podmore, a mate of Dumbledore's, got sent to Azkaban for trespass at the Ministry. That's meant to make my family open their eyes apparently.

Book5-chapter14_Sc7.source: "I am afraid I can no longer live under their roof while they remain mixed up with the dangerous crowd around Dumbledore"
Book5-chapter14_Sc7.description: So they're saying someone can't live with their parents any more because the parents are mixed up with Dumbledore's crowd. That's mental and a bit personal, isn't it?

Book5-chapter14_Sc7.source: "a student who shows himself willing to help Professor Umbridge now may be very well placed for Head Boyship in a couple of years!"
Book5-chapter14_Sc7.description: They're basically saying helping Umbridge now could get you Head Boy later. Bloody hell, that's a proper carrot to dangle at students.
Right, they've congratulated me on becoming a prefect. Well, cheers for that I suppose.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: From something the Minister let slip when telling me you are now a prefect
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: Blimey, people know I'm a prefect now because the Minister went and let it slip.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: I gather that you are still seeing a lot of Harry Potter
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: So everyone's clocked that I'm still hanging about with Harry. Great.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: nothing could put you in danger of losing your badge more than continued fraternization with that boy
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: I can't lose my badge over Harry. If people say I'm risking it by sticking with him then I have to be careful, otherwise I might actually get into trouble.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: Dumbledore may not be in charge at Hogwarts much longer
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: Apparently Dumbledore might not be running the place for much longer. That's worrying.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: given that our father escorted him to court, Potter had a disciplinary hearing this summer in front of the whole Wizengamot and he did not come out of it looking too good
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: Harry had that big hearing at the Wizengamot over the summer and people reckon he didn't come out well. Dad even took him to court, so it's out there.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: He got off on a mere technicality if you ask me and many of the people I’ve spoken to remain convinced of his guilt
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: Loads of people think Harry only escaped on a technicality and still suspect him. I can't pretend that won't stick to me by association.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: Seriously, Ron, you do not want to be tarred with the same brush as Potter, it could be very damaging to your future prospects
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: If I keep being seen with Harry it could damage my future. That makes me think twice about how openly I hang out with him.

Book5-chapter14_Sc6.source: I urge you to speak to Dolores Umbridge, a really delightful woman, who I know will be only too happy to advise you
Book5-chapter14_Sc6.description: They reckon I should go chat to Umbridge if I'm worried. Yeah right, like I'd trust her, but that's what they're saying I should do.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: Oh, sorry. I know I mess up by drifting off; I feel rubbish when they're shouting at me and I apologize straight away.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: Ron, who was hovering in front of the left-hand hoop, leaving the other two completely unprotected.
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: I'm hovering on the left hoop and leaving the others wide open. I try to cover things but I can drift and that leaves gaps.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: “You keep shifting around while you’re watching the Chasers!” said Angelina. “Either stay in center position until you have to move to defend a hoop, or else circle the hoops, but don’t drift vaguely off to one side, that’s how you let in the last three goals!”
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: Blimey, I get told off for shifting about. I should either hold center or circle the hoops properly instead of drifting and letting goals in.

Book5-chapter14_Sc3.source: “Sorry . . .” Ron repeated, his red face shining like a beacon against the bright blue sky.
Book5-chapter14_Sc3.description: I go bright red and say sorry when I'm called out. I know I look a right mess and it bothers me.

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: "I can’t believe how much homework we’ve got,"
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: I can't believe how much homework we've got. It's mental, honestly.
I was out for a walk. I felt like getting away for a bit, all right?

Book5-chapter13_Sc7.source: Harry had the distinct impression that he was not alone in concealing things at the moment.
Book5-chapter13_Sc7.description: Blimey, I'm not the only one hiding stuff. Everyone's keeping things to themselves right now.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "I-I thought I’d try out for Gryffindor Keeper now I’ve got a decent broom. There. Go on. Laugh."
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: Blimey, I'm going to try out for Keeper now I've got a decent broom. I know it's a bit much but I'm serious.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "Every evening since Tuesday . . . just on my own, though, I’ve been trying to bewitch Quaffles to fly at me, but it hasn’t been easy and I don’t know how much use it’ll be."
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: I've been practicing every night since Tuesday, trying to get Quaffles to come to me. It's been tricky but I'm giving it a go.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "Fred and George are going to laugh themselves stupid when I turn up for the tryouts. They haven’t stopped taking the mickey out of me since I got made a prefect."
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: They're going to wind me up rotten. Fred and George won't stop laughing and taking the mickey out of me over this.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "I’m — I’m hiding from Fred and George, if you must know," said Ron.
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: I'm hiding from Fred and George right now because I don't want them to see me practicing or laugh at me.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "The old hag!" Ron said in a revolted whisper as they came to a halt in front of the Fat Lady...
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: The old hag's gone too far. That's sick, we should go to McGonagall or Dumbledore about this.

Book5-chapter13_Sc8.source: "Harry, I did it, I’m in, I’m Keeper!"
Book5-chapter13_Sc8.description: I actually made it in. I'm Keeper now. I can't believe it, I'm in the team.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: I laughed at Harry's sarcastic line because it was dead funny, but I'm still with him. If anyone gives him trouble, I'll back him even if I tease him first.

Book5-chapter13_Sc3.source: Ron laughed at the idea of Hagrid being sacked along with Crabbe and Goyle's guffaws.
Book5-chapter13_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, some people find the idea of Hagrid getting the sack funny. Not me, but I laughed with the lot for the moment because that's how things go sometimes.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Completely lousy,” said Ron in a hollow voice, sinking into a chair beside Hermione.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, I thought practice was dreadful. I felt awful about how it went.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Who said it was me who made it lousy?” snapped Ron.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: I don't like being blamed for everything. Don't assume it was me who ruined practice.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “Blimey, it is!” said Ron quietly, throwing down his quill and getting to his feet.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, Hermes actually turned up. Percy sent me a letter. That explains who the owl was for.

Book5-chapter14_Sc4.source: “I’m going to get started on some homework,” said Ron angrily and stomped off to the staircase to the boys’ dormitories and vanished from sight.
Book5-chapter14_Sc4.description: I'm fed up and snappy after practice. I storm off when I'm overwhelmed, but I still try to get on with homework afterwards.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Blimey, I did the dream thing last time so it was Harry's turn. I do not want to keep repeating it.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: It doesn’t matter, pick any of them
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Okay, dream details can be a mess. I was busy doing the sums about age and letters and it was all a faff, but we managed to make something up.

Book5-chapter15_Sc1.source: She snapped her long fingers under Harry’s nose, uncharacteristically brisk.
Book5-chapter15_Sc1.description: Umbridge is the sort who snaps at us and takes control. We all hate her more now, and I'm right there with Harry and Hermione about that.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: We could order anything we liked in here, I bet that bloke would sell us anything
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: The Hog's Head bloke looks like he'd sell anything. I was thinking we could get proper drinks in here like firewhisky.
I'm a prefect. That bloody spoils messing about with drinks for me, doesn't it.
I'm with Harry. I'm nervous too but I'm backing him and sitting right by him. I'll help pull up chairs and support him as needed.

Book5-chapter16_Sc2.source: Could we have ... twenty-five butterbeers, please?
Book5-chapter16_Sc2.description: Fred and George turned up with Zonko's stuff and decided to buy drinks for everyone. The whole thing blew up into a massive crowd.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "I know, mate," said Ron sympathetically, "she’s bang out of order."
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: She's gone too far this time. Umbridge is completely out of order with how she treats Harry.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Excellent," whispered Ron, as they sat down in their usual seats. "Let's see Umbridge get what she deserves."
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Good. I want Umbridge to get put in her place. We'll see her mishaps and enjoy it.

Book5-chapter15_Sc2.source: "Well, it’s a start," said Ron, holding up a long, wriggling mouse tail and dropping it back into the box Lavender was passing around.
Book5-chapter15_Sc2.description: Small victories count. If the class is doing all right and Hagrid wouldn't be let down, that's good enough for now.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: I thought it was a good idea from the start
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Blimey, I did think the idea of Harry teaching was good from the beginning. Once I knew Harry wasn't going to shout I was all for it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: He didn’t only want to be your pen pal
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Er, I got a bit jumpy about Viktor and Hermione. I think Viktor fancied her more than just pen pals and I wasn't happy about it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: Well, you can't blame him for wanting to get out and about
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: Sirius has been on the run for ages and I'd understand why he'd want to get out. But I still reckon he wouldn't be stupid enough to turn up in Hogsmeade and risk it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc1.source: Dumbledore'd go mad if he did and Sirius listens to Dumbledore even if he doesn't like what he hears
Book5-chapter16_Sc1.description: I believe Sirius actually listens to Dumbledore and wouldn't do anything that would make Dumbledore furious. So he's probably staying put.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [Hermione, you are honestly the most wonderful person I’ve ever met, and if I’m ever rude to you again —]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: Hermione is brilliant and kinder than anyone gives her credit for. I feel like an idiot for being rude sometimes and I meant it when I said she's the most wonderful person I've met.
I couldn't believe Harry just slid off his chair and started staring into the fire. I asked him what on earth he was doing because it was weird and worrying.

Book5-chapter14_Sc9.source: [You didn’t say you’d written to Sirius!]
Book5-chapter14_Sc9.description: I didn't know Harry had written to Sirius. That surprised me and made me feel out of the loop; I reckon I should pay more attention next time.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “Give it back,” said Ron, holding out his hand. “He is —” Ron said jerkily, tearing Percy’s letter in half, “the world’s” — he tore it into quarters — “biggest” — he tore it into eighths — “git.” He threw the pieces into the fire.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Percy's a bloody git. I'm not having him tell me to drop Harry or rat him out. Burn that rubbish.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “Come on, we’ve got to get this finished some time before dawn,” he said briskly to Harry, pulling Professor Sinistra’s essay back toward him.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Blimey, we've got to finish before dawn. Let's crack on and get this done.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: “Are you serious? Ah, Hermione, you’re a lifesaver,” said Ron, “what can I — ?”
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: Hermione's a lifesaver, honestly. I can't believe she'd do this for us.

Book5-chapter14_Sc8.source: Thanks a million, Hermione,” said Harry weakly, passing over his essay and sinking back into his armchair, rubbing his eyes.
Book5-chapter14_Sc8.description: I'm knackered and I'll do whatever it takes to get this finished. I'll help, but Hermione's sorting most of it.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "She’s given the Slytherins permission, why not us?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: I think Umbridge is favouring Slytherin or playing favourites. It's not fair and it's obvious she's enjoying the power.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "She says on no account whatsoever are you to take part in an illegal secret Defense Against the Dark Arts group. She says you’ll be expelled for sure and your future will be ruined."
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: Mum told me not to join the secret group or I'll be expelled and my future will be ruined. She really means it.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "He was banned from the Hog’s Head twenty years ago," said Sirius, "and that barman’s got a long memory."
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: We learned Mundungus is dodgy and has a history. I wanted to see him but he was hiding for a reason.

Book5-chapter17_Sc3.source: "How about the Shrieking Shack?" suggested Sirius. "Hey, that’s an idea!" said Ron excitedly,
Book5-chapter17_Sc3.description: I liked Sirius's suggestion about the Shrieking Shack. I'm excited about any decent place to meet and practise.
