Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "What in the name of Merlin," said Ron slowly, as they followed Neville, "was that about?"
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Blimey, Neville just charged Malfoy like that. I can't work out why he exploded like that either.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Hark who’s talking, you walked out of Divination, you hate Trelawney!" said Ron indignantly.
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: Well, Hermione can argue all she likes, but I think it's rich of her to complain about Harry skipping lessons when she walked out on Divination herself.

Book5-chapter17_Sc2.source: "You can’t skive off Divination," said Hermione severely. "Hark who’s talking, you walked out of Divination, you hate Trelawney!" said Ron indignantly.
Book5-chapter17_Sc2.description: I'm on Harry's side about Snape's essay and all that. We bicker with Hermione but we stick together when it matters.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "Harry, Ron, and Hermione’s whispered discussion about how Umbridge had nearly caught Sirius went quite unnoticed."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Blimey, it sounds like Umbridge was practically on top of Sirius. We're lucky she didn't catch him.

Book5-chapter18_Sc1.source: "There was generally so much movement and activity that the danger of being overheard was very slight. Today, with the room full of croaking bullfrogs and cawing ravens..."
Book5-chapter18_Sc1.description: Charms class is perfect for whispering stuff because of all the noise and chaos. Good place to plan without anyone listening.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "All we do is read the stupid textbook," said Ron.
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: Blimey, in Defense all we do is read that stupid textbook and we don't get to practise any spells.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "That's the stupidest thing I've ever heard, including all the stuff that Luna Lovegood comes out with."
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: That's mental, the idea that we're being kept from learning because Fudge thinks we're an army is the daftest thing I've heard.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "I would, I just don't want you chucked back in Azkaban!" said Harry. There was a pause in which Sirius looked out of the fire at Harry, a crease between his sunken eyes.
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: I'd hate for Sirius to get sent back to Azkaban, so I'm with Harry on not wanting him to risk coming here where people like Malfoy might spot him.

Book5-chapter14_Sc10.source: "So you haven't had any news about Hagrid, either?"
Book5-chapter14_Sc10.description: So we haven't heard for sure what happened to Hagrid, he was meant to be back by now and that worries us.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: Blimey, I say things half-joking when I'm angry. Sometimes I go too far but I mean how awful Umbridge is.
Actually, the thought of Harry teaching us Defense makes sense. I didn't expect to be serious about extra work but this matters.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "We weren't saying anything like that, mate," said Ron, looking aghast.
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: I care about Harry and I'm worried when he gets upset. I don't want him to think we're mocking his experiences.

Book5-chapter15_Sc3.source: "'S too late, isn't it? She got the job, she's here to stay, Fudge'll make sure of that."
Book5-chapter15_Sc3.description: The Ministry will back Umbridge and there's bugger all we can do about her official position. We have to find other ways to learn.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "I don’t reckon he’ll risk it again," said Ron. "He’s not stupid, he knows she nearly got him."
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: I reckon Sirius won't risk sending an owl again. He's not daft and he knows how close he came to getting caught.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Ravens are harder than frogs," said Ron testily.
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: Blimey, ravens are tougher to deal with than frogs. That's that.

Book5-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Sirius is right," he said, "you do sound just like my mother."
Book5-chapter18_Sc3.description: Hermione going on about worrying sounds like Mum to me. I don't always agree but I can see her point sometimes.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: These will be good when we’re practicing Stunning,
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Blimey, these cushions and instruments will be brilliant for practicing Stunning.

Book5-chapter18_Sc8.source: prodding one of the cushions with his foot.
Book5-chapter18_Sc8.description: Looks comfy and useful. Perfect for practice rounds, honestly.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I don\'t think we\'re going to be as lucky, though, do you?" he asked Harry as the second years hurried away.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: I don\'t think we\'re going to be as lucky as Harry. Something is off and I reckon we are in trouble.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Zacharias Smith!" said Ron at once, punching a fist into his hand. "Or \u2014 I thought that Michael Corner had a really shifty look too \u2014"
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: Zacharias looks dodgy to me and Michael Corner gave me a shifty look. One of them might have told Umbridge. Blimey, I can think of suspects.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Let\'s go and tell her," said Ron. He bounded forward, pulled open the door, and set off up the spiral staircase.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: I want to protect Hermione and be there for her. I rush to tell her when I think she might be affected.

Book5-chapter17_Sc1.source: "I don\'t think we\'re allowed in the girls\' dormitories," said Harry, pulling Ron to his feet and trying not to laugh.
Book5-chapter17_Sc1.description: We can\'t go into the girls\' dorms. I tried and ended up sliding down the stair like an idiot. That taught me not to break rules like that, well not without thinking first.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Listen, Neville, can you take it in turns to practice with Ron and Hermione for a couple of minutes so I can walk around and see how the rest are doing?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Blimey, I was practising with Neville and Hermione when Harry asked us to take turns. Basic drills are worth doing even if they seem dull.

Book5-chapter18_Sc10.source: "Everybody got to their feet at once and divided up."
Book5-chapter18_Sc10.description: Right, everyone switched into pairs straight away. It was proper chaotic but at least we were all actually trying.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Ravens are harder than frogs," said Ron testily.
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Blimey, ravens are trickier to charm than frogs. Who knew they'd be such a pain?

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Wha — ? Oh — oh, right," said Ron, very flustered. "Er — Silencio!"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: I get flustered when everyone watches me. I botched the first try but I can get it right when I concentrate.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "I’ve got permission! To re-form the Quidditch team!" "Yeah," said Angelina, beaming. "So I want you down at the pitch at seven o’clock tonight…"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: Bloody brilliant, the team's back. I’m buzzing to get on the pitch tonight. We need to make up time before the first match.

Book5-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Hope this clears up . . . What’s up with you, Hermione?"
Book5-chapter18_Sc2.description: I noticed Hermione's off and it worries me. She’s not herself when she’s quiet, and that makes me worry about her.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Come off it," said Ron, "you’re in a right state!"
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Blimey, Hagrid’s in a shocking state and no way is it nothing. I called him out on it straight away.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Would you say it was nothing if one of us turned up with a pound of mince instead of a face?" Ron demanded.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, I pointed out how obvious it was that Hagrid had been attacked. You don’t look like that for no reason.
I wondered why Muggles don’t notice where giants are. It struck me as odd that they’d get away with it.

Book5-chapter20_Sc1.source: "A month?" said Ron, as though he had never heard of a journey lasting such a ridiculously long time.
Book5-chapter20_Sc1.description: A month to get there? That’s mental. I can’t get my head around a journey that long.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: Together with Ron they had spent most of the day seeking out those people who had signed their names to the list in the Hog’s Head and telling them where to meet that evening.
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: I spent the whole day helping round people up who signed the list. Blimey, asking everyone where to meet took ages but we got them together.

Book5-chapter18_Sc6.source: At half-past seven Harry, Ron, and Hermione left the Gryffindor common room, Harry clutching a certain piece of aged parchment in his hand.
Book5-chapter18_Sc6.description: I'm with Harry and Hermione on this. We're heading out together tonight to use that map and see what's what. Bloody nerve-wracking, but I'm in.

Book5-chapter21_Sc1.source: "So?" said Ron, looking up when she entered. "Got all his lessons planned for him?"
Book5-chapter21_Sc1.description: Blimey, I was just asking if Hermione had sorted Hagrid's lessons. I wanted to know if he'd follow the proper plan.
Why isn't Hagrid calling the creatures properly? I was still looking around, expecting him to shout again.

Book5-chapter18_Sc7.source: Ron was staring at it, looking slightly wary.
Book5-chapter18_Sc7.description: Blimey, that door just turned up out of nowhere. Looks a bit dodgy, but I suppose we ought to see what's inside.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: I wandered off after the match and froze out in the snow. I couldn't face everyone when things went wrong.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "For thinking I can play Quidditch," "I'm going to resign first thing tomorrow."
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: I'm gutted. I honestly think I'm hopeless at Quidditch and I want to quit. Blimey, I feel like I let the team down.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "Yes, Mr. Potter, I think a lifelong ban ought to do the trick"
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: Umbridge wants to ban me and the twins from Quidditch for life. That's mental and it's ruining everything for us.

Book5-chapter19_Sc3.source: "This is the worst I’ve ever felt in my life."
Book5-chapter19_Sc3.description: I've never felt so low. It really is the worst. I don't know how to fix it right now.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: all except Ron, who had dismounted from his broom over by the goalposts and was making his way slowly back to the changing rooms alone.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: Blimey, I let a couple of goals in and everyone knows. I walked off alone because I felt proper rubbish about it.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: “Saved Weasley’s neck, haven’t you?” he said to Harry.
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: Harry caught the Snitch and basically saved my neck. I owe him one and I know everyone'll remember the win, not my mistakes.

Book5-chapter19_Sc2.source: They were saved, it did not matter that Ron had let in those goals, nobody would remember as long as Gryffindor had won
Book5-chapter19_Sc2.description: Well, okay, maybe nobody'll harp on about my goals now that we won. Still, I can't shake feeling embarrassed.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm stunned and pale and I can't get my words out. Everything's happening and I don't know what to say.

Book5-chapter22_Sc2.source: "Harry looked at Ron, who made a funny movement somewhere between a nod and shrug, and they sat down too."
Book5-chapter22_Sc2.description: I'm backing Harry right now even if I can't speak. A nod's about as much as I can manage, but I'm with him.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: How did you see this? I'm stunned and asking questions because I need to know if my dad is really hurt.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: Ron looked from Harry to Dumbledore white-faced and shocked
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: I'm white as a sheet and can't speak at first. I'm terrified for Dad and it's all I can do to stand there.

Book5-chapter22_Sc1.source: Is Arthur seriously injured Yes said Harry emphatically
Book5-chapter22_Sc1.description: My dad is seriously injured and that fact has hit me hard. Everything else feels secondary right now.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Just like that?" said Ron, looking awestruck.
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: They actually walked into a giant camp. Blimey, they just went straight up to them after watching from afar.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "How could you tell which one was the Gurg?" asked Ron.
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: You spot the Gurg because he's the biggest, ugliest and laziest. Karkus sat there waiting to be fed, sounded mental.

Book5-chapter20_Sc2.source: "What do you give a giant?" asked Ron eagerly.
Book5-chapter20_Sc2.description: You don't give them ordinary food. Dumbledore gave them magic — the Gubraithian fire branch — because giants like magic but hate it used against them.
They managed to talk to Karkus and he listened because he knew of Dumbledore. Then everything went wrong when the giants started fighting and Karkus ended up dead.
I was stunned and shaken hearing they were nearly killed and had to hide. I thought it would be quick but it turned into a proper dangerous mess.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: Harry," said Ron's voice, from far, far away, "Mum says dinner's ready, but she'll save you something if you want to stay in bed
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: Mum says dinner's ready and she'll save you some if you want to stay in bed. Don't worry, we've got you covered at dinner if you can't face everyone yet.

Book5-chapter23_Sc1.source: Ron looked down at his feet but Ginny seemed quite unabashed.
Book5-chapter23_Sc1.description: I felt awkward about the whole thing and kept my head down. I don't want to make it worse for Harry but I'm not great at saying the right thing.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: So Macnair's persuaded the giants to join You-Know-Who?
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: Blimey, Macnair's involvement means the giants might be siding with Voldemort. That's dangerous and explains why Golgomath's gang are a real threat.

Book5-chapter20_Sc3.source: Well that's not bad — are they going to come over here and start fighting You-Know-Who with us?
Book5-chapter20_Sc3.description: I was hopeful the giants might help us fight. I wanted to believe we'd get backup, but it's obvious now that's not likely.
Umbridge is a proper menace. She snoops around and scares everyone, so we have to be extra careful and cover our tracks.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: Doctors? Those Muggle nutters that cut people up? Nah, they’re Healers.
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: Healers are not like Muggle doctors. They're proper magical healers, not those Muggle types who cut people up.

Book5-chapter22_Sc3.source: "Arthur Weasley?" said the witch, running her finger down a long list in front of her. "Yes, first floor, second door on the right, Dai Llewellyn ward."
Book5-chapter22_Sc3.description: Arthur is on the first floor in the Dai Llewellyn ward. That's where we need to go to see him.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Blimey, Umbridge calls the thestrals dangerous. I heard her say it and I was ready to believe her for a second, but I'm not completely convinced.
Well, it's odd to see three people in one class who can see thestrals. That's not something you expect and it made me wonder how rare it is.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: D'you reckon if you saw someone snuff it you'd be able to see the Quaffle better? He, Crabbe, and Goyle roared with laughter as they pushed past on their way to the castle and then broke into a chorus of 'Weasley Is Our King.' Ron's ears turned scarlet.
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, Malfoy and his mates can be proper cruel. I got mocked and it made me red as anything. I hate being the joke.

Book5-chapter21_Sc3.source: Ignore them, just ignore them, intoned Hermione, pulling out her wand
Book5-chapter21_Sc3.description: Hermione will step in and try to fix things when I'm cornered. She gets annoyed and doesn't put up with rubbish.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: Ron sniggered, breaking off when Hermione caught his eye.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Ha. I sniggered because it's brilliant and a bit ridiculous. Can't help it.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "HA!" Ron made a triumphant gesture with his fist and went into a raucous peal of laughter
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I was buzzing when Harry said he kissed Cho. Couldn't help celebrating a bit loudly.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "One person can't feel all that at once, they'd explode."
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: Come on, that's mental. No one can be feeling everything Hermione listed all at once.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Don't blame you, mate," said Ron, looking alarmed at the very thought.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I reckon I wouldn't blame Harry for being awkward. If it happened to me I'd be the same.

Book5-chapter21_Sc4.source: "What does she see in Krum?" Ron demanded as he and Harry climbed the boys' stairs.
Book5-chapter21_Sc4.description: I still can't see what's so great about Krum. He's older and a bit grim, so what does Cho see in him?

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Let's not stay long," Ron said quietly.
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Blimey, I just wanted to get in and out. This place is horrible, so let's not hang about.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Neville!" and "It's us, Neville!" and "Have you seen? Lockhart's here! Who've you been visiting?"
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Neville, mate! I made a fuss as soon as I recognised him. I wasn't thinking, just called out because I wanted to be friendly.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: Ron was now standing on tiptoe to look over at the inhabitants of the two beds.
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, when I spotted Neville's parents I had to have a look, even though it's awful to see.

Book5-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Well, it's nothing to be ashamed of!" said Mrs. Longbottom angrily. "You should be proud, Neville, proud!"
Book5-chapter23_Sc3.description: I felt rubbish for making Neville jump. He's embarrassed but he shouldn't be. He's got no reason to be ashamed of his parents.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "This one’s from a bloke who thinks you’re off your rocker,"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Blimey, some people reckon Harry's gone barmy for saying Voldemort's back. Not everyone believes him.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "I haven't got the heart to take the mickey out of him, even,"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: I feel rubbish about winding Harry up right now. I can't be cruel when he's that down.
Angelina has faith in me. She thinks I can do the job even if everyone else is ragging on me.

Book5-chapter26_Sc1.source: "What is going on here?" said a falsely sweet, girlish voice. "Why have you got all these letters, Mr. Potter?"
Book5-chapter26_Sc1.description: Umbridge is nosing about trying to make trouble over Harry's mail. She's looking for any reason to punish him and that worries me.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: I was half asleep and grunted goodnight earlier before all this started.

Book5-chapter21_Sc5.source: [Harry, mate, you . . . you were just dreaming . . .]
Book5-chapter21_Sc5.description: I thought Harry had only been dreaming. I didn't get what he was saying at first.
Seeing him sweating and sick made me scared. I thought he was ill and needed help.
Neville ran to get help. That’s why I was standing there shocked and worried.

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Extra lessons with Snape?" said Ron, sounding aghast. "I'd rather have the nightmares!"
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: Blimey, I'd pick the nightmares over extra lessons with Snape any day

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "I know they call the people who work in there 'Unspeakables,'" said Ron, frowning.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: My dad's told me they call the people in the Department of Mysteries 'Unspeakables' because no one knows what they do

Book5-chapter24_Sc3.source: "How come Sturgis was trying to break in when he's on our side?" said Ron.
Book5-chapter24_Sc3.description: How the hell was Sturgis trying to break in if he's supposed to be on our side

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Fat chance," said Ron, who was examining his own fake Galleon with a slightly mournful air. "I haven’t got any real Galleons to confuse it with."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Blimey, I don’t even have any proper Galleons. I thought about how I might accidentally spend one of those fake coins but then remembered I have nothing real to mix them up with.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Weasley cannot save a thing, He cannot block a single ring, That’s why Slytherins all sing: Weasley is our King. Weasley was born in a bin, He always lets the Quaffle in, Weasley will make sure we win, Weasley is our King."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: That singing got to me. Bloody hell, hearing them chant that made my stomach flip and my hands shake. I couldn’t just laugh it off like Harry.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "The only thing really worrying Harry was how much Ron was allowing the tactics of the Slytherin team to upset him before they even got onto the pitch. Harry, of course, had endured their snide comments for more than four years, so whispers of, 'Hey, Potty, I heard Warrington’s sworn to knock you off your broom on Saturday,' far from chilling his blood, made him laugh. 'Warrington’s aim’s so pathetic I’d be more worried if he was aiming for the person next to me,' he retorted, which made Ron and Hermione laugh and wiped the smirk off Pansy Parkinson’s face.'"
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Yeah, I do let it get to me. I try to keep my nerve but once they start in the corridors and on the pitch I go all green and shaky. I have to stop that if I want to be a proper Keeper.

Book5-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Even Fred had said that Ron might yet make him and George proud, and that they were seriously considering admitting that he was related to them, something he assured Ron they had been trying to deny for four years."
Book5-chapter19_Sc1.description: Blimey, hearing Fred say I might make him and George proud actually boosted me a bit. I want to prove them right and stop feeling like the joke.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: Here’s an idea, why don’t you shut your mouth?
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Why don’t you shut your mouth? I’m not having anyone slagging off Harry when he’s trying to help.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: Mum told Ron not to spread it around… She said you got enough attention as it was.
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: Blimey, Mum told me not to go spreading Harry’s business. He gets enough attention already, so I’m not running my mouth about it.

Book5-chapter16_Sc3.source: McGonagall might let us have hers, she did when Harry was practicing for the Triwizard
Book5-chapter16_Sc3.description: McGonagall might let us use her classroom. She did before when Harry was practicing. It could work if we ask.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: “Will you stop acting like a maniac, and I can get you out of here!”
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: Blimey, I’m not having Harry flailing about like that; I pulled him out because he was acting mental and could’ve hurt himself.
I was scared and kept telling him he had to tell people about seeing You-Know-Who because I didn’t know what else to do.

Book5-chapter26_Sc2.source: Ron’s shocked questions after Harry’s vision
Book5-chapter26_Sc2.description: What the hell? At first I thought Harry was a nutter, but seeing him like that made me realize something serious is going on.

Book5-chapter27_Sc1.source: "Impossible," said Ron, who was tucking into a large plate of eggs and bacon. "She can't get any worse than she's been already."
Book5-chapter27_Sc1.description: Impossible. She can't possibly get any worse than she's been, can she?
Blimey, that classroom change was mental when the trees and stars appeared.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "You haven't done anything, have you?" said Ron, looking unnerved as Mrs Weasley withdrew from the room.
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Blimey, when adults talk like that I get nervous. Of course I asked Harry if he'd done something, because that's what you do.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "I never want to ride on here again."
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, the Knight Bus is mental. After that I am never getting on it willingly again.

Book5-chapter24_Sc1.source: "You keepin’ well, then, ’Arry? I seen your name in the paper loads over the summer, but it weren’t never nuffink very nice."
Book5-chapter24_Sc1.description: Famous or not, I care about mates. I told Harry people had been saying things about him, but I still want him safe.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “There you are, Harry,” said Ron, looking awestruck. “That’s why he was happy last night . . .”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Blimey, so that's why Sirius was celebrating. The breakout explains his mood.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “Bode . . .” said Ron. “Bode. It rings a bell . . .”
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Bode's name rings a bell because Dad's mentioned him. He worked in the Department of Mysteries.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “I hate it when she does that,” grumbled Ron as he and Harry got up from the table and made their own, slower way out of the Great Hall.
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: I can't stand Hermione when she bolts off without telling us what she's up to. Tell us for once, will you? It'd take two seconds.

Book5-chapter25_Sc1.source: “You’re on probation?” said Ron very loudly, so that many students passing looked around curiously.
Book5-chapter25_Sc1.description: Hagrid's on probation after that inspection. That's rough and everyone's going to be talking about it.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "Shall I jinx him? I can still get him from here,"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Blimey, I was ready to jinx Zacharias the moment he mouthed off about Harry taking Remedial Potions because that was insulting.

Book5-chapter24_Sc2.source: "Shall I jinx him? I can still get him from here,"
Book5-chapter24_Sc2.description: Honestly, when someone annoys me I say I'll jinx them straight away, it's just how I react.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: Blimey, that star display is mental.

Book5-chapter27_Sc2.source: "He’s not very definite on anything, is he?"
Book5-chapter27_Sc2.description: He's not saying much useful. I want proper details about this war we're supposedly heading into.

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was bewildered when Hermione dropped that Sturgis bombshell. I didn't have a clue what she was on about at first

Book5-chapter26_Sc3.source: "Ron, be quiet" interruption during Hermione's theory
Book5-chapter26_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, I got told to be quiet because Hermione was on a roll with her theory about Sturgis and Malfoy

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Weasley, your shirt's untucked, so I’ll have another five for that," said Malfoy.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Blimey, Malfoy is looking for any excuse to nick points off me and the others. He's being really petty about it.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "We don’t care about staying anymore. We’d walk out right now if we weren’t determined to do our bit for Dumbledore first," said Fred.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: Well, bloody hell, Fred and George don't care about getting expelled anymore. That changes things because they mean business now.

Book5-chapter28_Sc1.source: "Have you ever?" asked Hermione. "'Course we have," said George.
Book5-chapter28_Sc1.description: We've always pushed the line before but not properly crossed it. Now with Dumbledore gone they're ready to up the chaos and I can feel it in the air.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "You didn’t leave your bed, mate," said Ron. "I saw you thrashing around in your sleep about a minute before we could wake you up . . ."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: I saw you thrashing in your sleep, Harry. You didn’t actually get out of bed, mate.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Mum’s crying again," said Fred heavily. "Percy sent back his Christmas jumper." "Without a note," added George. "Hasn’t asked how Dad is or visited him or anything . . ."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Percy sent his jumper back and didn’t even ask after Dad. Mum’s proper upset about it.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "What’s that supposed to be anyway?" asked Fred, squinting at Dobby’s painting. "Looks like a gibbon with two black eyes." "It’s Harry!" said George, pointing at the back of the picture. "Says so on the back!"
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: That painting Dobby did is shocking. Looks like a gibbon, not very flattering at all.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "They found Mr. Weasley propped up in bed with the remains of his turkey dinner on a tray in his lap and a rather sheepish expression on his face."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Typical Dad. He messes about with things and tries odd Muggle remedies and ends up looking a right mess in front of Mum.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "They can leave the house if they really want to," Harry contradicted him. "Dobby did, he left the Malfoys’ to give me warnings three years ago. He had to punish himself afterward, but he still managed it."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: I reckon house-elves can sometimes leave if they choose. Dobby did it once, so it's not impossible.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "‘Tis a most grievous affliction of the skin, young master, that will leave you pockmarked and more gruesome even than you are now —" "Watch who you’re calling gruesome!" said Ron, his ears turning red. "The only remedy is to take the liver of a toad, bind it tight about your throat, stand naked by the full moon in a barrel of eels’ eyes —" "I have not got spattergroit!" "But the unsightly blemishes upon your visage, young master —" "They’re freckles!" said Ron furiously."
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, don’t call me gruesome. Those are freckles, alright? I will not stand for that toad liver nonsense.

Book5-chapter23_Sc2.source: "Blimey!" said Ron, also staring at the man.
Book5-chapter23_Sc2.description: Blimey, seeing Lockhart like that is something else. He hasn’t exactly kept himself together.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "If it hadn’t been for her . . ." Ron went into a rant about Marietta Edgecombe
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Blimey, that Marietta's the reason things went south. I can't stand her; if it hadn't been for her we'd have been fine.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "We’ve got about as much chance of winning the Quidditch Cup this year as Dad’s got of becoming Minister of Magic . . ."
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Honestly, our chances of winning Quidditch this year are rubbish. Dad becoming Minister? Yeah, right. That's mental.

Book5-chapter29_Sc1.source: "You’ve given me an evening off every week!" "That’s for Quidditch practice," said Hermione.
Book5-chapter29_Sc1.description: Great, I get an evening off for Quidditch practice. Still, I can't help feeling gloomy about our actual chances.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Give it a rest, okay? I'm not going to keep arguing. He can decide for himself even if I think it's mad.

Book5-chapter29_Sc2.source: He would not look at Harry, though when Hermione opened her mouth to try dissuading Harry some more, he said in a low voice, "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."
Book5-chapter29_Sc2.description: Blimey, this is awkward. I don't want to be the one stopping him in front of Hermione. I'll keep out of it.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: "WE DID IT! WE WON!" yelled Ron, waving the silver Quidditch Cup in the air
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Blimey, we won the match. I’m buzzing and everyone’s carrying me around, it’s brilliant.

Book5-chapter30_Sc3.source: Weasley is our King song lines repeated in the crowd
Book5-chapter30_Sc3.description: Everyone’s singing 'Weasley is our King' about me. It’s a bit daft but I’m enjoying it while it lasts.
I’m on top of the world right now and I want Harry and Hermione to share in the moment. We’re mates and this feels like ours together.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "Sirius might've cracked and just wanted some fresh air."
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: Maybe Sirius left Grimmauld Place because he wanted out. He could have gone looking for freedom and run into trouble.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "Sirius's brother was a Death Eater, wasn't he? Maybe he told Sirius the secret of how to get the weapon!"
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: It could be that Sirius's family connections mean he knows something about how to get this mysterious thing in the Department of Mysteries.
I'm backing Harry here. I believe he saw Voldemort and Sirius and I want us to act on it.

Book5-chapter32_Sc1.source: "I never said I had a problem!"
Book5-chapter32_Sc1.description: I'm worried and panicked like everyone, but I'm not accusing Harry of acting reckless. I'm with him, even if I'm scared.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "Maybe he's actually trying to open Harry's mind a bit wider . . . make it easier for You-Know-"
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: Blimey, what if Snape isn't helping at all and is doing the opposite? Maybe he's making Harry more open to Voldemort. It's worrying.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "He used to be a Death Eater," said Ron stubbornly.
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: He used to be on Voldemort's side. We still haven't seen proper proof he switched, so I don't fully trust him yet.

Book5-chapter25_Sc2.source: "I dunno why Angelina won't just let me resign . . ."
Book5-chapter25_Sc2.description: I'm fed up with training when I'm rubbish. I want to quit practice but Angelina won't let me. It's driving me mad and I feel useless.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: ["Well, we were always going to fail that one," said Ron gloomily as they ascended the marble staircase.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Well, we were always going to fail Divination. Can't say I'm surprised, really.

Book5-chapter31_Sc3.source: [He had just made Harry feel rather better by telling him how he told the examiner in detail about the ugly man with a wart on his nose in his crystal ball, only to look up and realize he had been describing his examiner’s reflection.]
Book5-chapter31_Sc3.description: Blimey, I told the examiner about an ugly man with a wart in my crystal ball and it turned out I was describing her reflection. That's just embarrassing.

Book5-chapter32_Sc4.description: I was gagged and hauled in here and couldn’t speak properly because they stuffed a gag in my mouth

Book5-chapter32_Sc4.source: “Got ’em all,” said Warrington, shoving Ron roughly forward into the room.
Book5-chapter32_Sc4.description: I was roughed up by the Inquisitorial Squad and they’re trying to make Hogwarts a Weasley-free place, so things are getting personal and nasty

Book5-chapter34_Sc3.source: It’s — it’s got your name on
Book5-chapter34_Sc3.description: Blimey, there's a glass ball with Harry's name on it. That's not normal. It looked like it had not been touched for years but Harry's name is there.

Book5-chapter34_Sc3.source: What’s your name doing down here?
Book5-chapter34_Sc3.description: I'm rattled and worried for Harry. This is weird and I want answers. I don't want him to mess around with things that might be dangerous.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "'Course not, he'll recover," said Ron indifferently. "Anyway, more trouble for Umbridge, isn't it?"
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: He'll be fine. Besides, if he's out it's one more problem for Umbridge and I don't mind that.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "It'll be my fault Fred and George left, you wait," said Ron darkly. "She'll say I should've stopped them leaving..."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: If Mum gets a letter through Umbridge she'll blame me for Fred and George leaving. I can see it now.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "How do you know?" said Ron and Hermione together."Because —" Harry hesitated..."Because they got the gold from me."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: Harry just admitted he gave Fred and George his Triwizard winnings. That's brilliant for me, Mum can't blame me now.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "If Montague doesn't recover before Slytherin play Hufflepuff, we might be in with a chance of winning the Cup."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: If Montague isn't healed in time, Slytherin will be weaker and we might actually win the House Cup.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "It's a bit dodgy, isn't it? They'll need loads of Galleons to afford the rent on a place in Diagon Alley, she’ll want to know what they've been up to..."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: It does seem dodgy that they'd afford Diagon Alley rent. I reckon Umbridge'll sniff around and blame someone for it, maybe me.

Book5-chapter30_Sc1.source: "You?" she said, catching her teacup as it scampered happily away..."Why should I be worried about you?" "When Mum's next letter...I'm going to be in deep trouble."
Book5-chapter30_Sc1.description: I'm pretty sure I'm going to be in trouble with Mum because of all this. I'm worried she'll get a Howler and I'll take the blame.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "Couple of Stunners, a Disarming Charm, Neville brought off a really nice little Impediment Jinx," said Ron airily, now handing back Hermione's wand too.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: We used spells to get away. I helped, Neville did a decent jinx and Ginny did something brilliant with Malfoy.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "I've got a broom!" said Ginny."Yeah, but you're not coming," said Ron angrily.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: Even though Ginny has a broom, I'm not happy about everyone going and I'm protective about who joins this. Blimey, this is dangerous.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "you might be able to fly without a broomstick but the rest of us can't sprout wings whenever we —" said Ron barely containing his anger.
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: I don't trust magical ways of flying that aren't broomsticks. I think relying on weird methods is risky for most of us.

Book5-chapter33_Sc3.source: "So," said Ron, pushing aside a low-hanging branch and holding out Harry's wand, "had any ideas?"
Book5-chapter33_Sc3.description: I'm backing Harry. I want to help and I'm willing to hand over his wand and do what I can, even if I'm grumpy about the rest.

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: I’ll do it," said Ron at once. "I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something, it’s miles away from her office. Come to think of it, I could probably persuade Peeves to do it if I met him on the way ...
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Right, I'll go and distract Umbridge and get Peeves to cause a diversion. That should keep her away from the office

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "I never said I had a problem!" said Ron heatedly. "But Harry, you’ve just said it," said Hermione fiercely.
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: I might complain, but I back Harry. I don't have a problem with him wanting to save people even if I say otherwise

Book5-chapter32_Sc3.source: "Harry, you’ve just said it," said Hermione fiercely. "Dumbledore wanted you to learn to shut these things out of your mind, if you’d done Occlumency properly you’d never have seen this —"
Book5-chapter32_Sc3.description: Look, Occlumency's supposed to stop this, but right now we need action not lectures. I'll help do the dirty work

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “I’ll do it,” said Ron at once. “I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something, it’s miles away from her office. Come to think of it, I could probably persuade Peeves to do it if I met him on the way . . .”
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Blimey, I'll go and distract Umbridge. I'll tell her Peeves is trashing Transfiguration and maybe get Peeves to help.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “I never said I had a problem!” said Ron heatedly. “But Harry, you’ve just said it,” said Hermione fiercely.
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Look, I didn't mean to sound like I disapproved. I don't have a problem with Harry trying to save people when it's important.

Book5-chapter32_Sc2.source: “Got ’em all,” said Warrington, shoving Ron roughly forward into the room.
Book5-chapter32_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, the Inquisitorial Squad grabbed us and shoved us into Umbridge's office. We're trapped and gagged here.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "There you are. . . . Ha ha ha . . . You look funny, Harry. . . . You’re all messed up . . ."
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: Blimey, I was a mess and I knew it. I couldn't help laughing even when I was all muddled and dazed.

Book5-chapter35_Sc2.source: "You know who this girl is, Harry? She’s Loony . . . Loony Lovegood . . . ha ha ha . . ."
Book5-chapter35_Sc2.description: I can't help being daft at the worst times. Even when things are serious, I make stupid jokes because it's how I cope.
I thought grabbing something weird might be fun or helpful, but that backfired. I won't be messing with odd things without thinking again. Bloody hell, that was mental.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: Blimey, there are doors everywhere. I pointed them out because it means the place is huge and we can’t assume one way leads to the lot.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: ‘I’m here, mate,’ said Ron, appearing around the side of the archway.
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: I’m right here with you. Don’t go off on your own, I’ll stick by you.

Book5-chapter34_Sc2.source: ‘Who’s there?’ said Harry, jumping down onto the bench below.
Book5-chapter34_Sc2.description: When things got weird I reacted like anyone would. I expected someone to answer so I made my presence known. That was me trying to keep on top of it.
When Harry said he heard whispering I wasn’t sure at first but then I could hear it too. It’s not just him being daft.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "And then, when Chambers came at me about five minutes later — what?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Blimey, I made some brilliant saves in the match. I’m still buzzing about them.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Why are you grinning?" "I’m not."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: I got suspicious when Harry started grinning, but he swore he wasn’t. Still, I reckon he was remembering something.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "You didn’t watch? You didn’t see me make any of those saves?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: I was gutted that Harry and Hermione missed most of the match and didn’t see my saves. I wanted the praise, plain and simple.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "He brought one back and hid it in the forest?"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: No way. Hagrid brought a giant back and hid him in the forest. I can’t believe Hagrid actually did that.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Teach him English, yeah."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: What the hell? Hagrid expects us to teach a giant English. That’s mental and I think Hagrid’s gone mad.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Well, you’re just going to have to break your promise, that’s all."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: We’ve got exams and are nearly on the edge of getting kicked out, so I reckon we should just break the promise and save ourselves.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "Dragon claw does work!"
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Dragon claw is supposed to give you a brain boost and make you cunning. I wanted a pinch, I really did.

Book5-chapter31_Sc1.source: "This stuff can, I’ve had a look at it, and it’s actually dried doxy droppings."
Book5-chapter31_Sc1.description: Well, after Hermione checked it and said it was dried doxy droppings, I lost interest fast. That’s disgusting and not worth it.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “What?” he said. “How’re we supposed to get on?” said Ron faintly. “When we can’t see the things?”
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: Blimey, I can't believe we're supposed to mount invisible horses. If you can't see them you can't trust them.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “This is mad,” Ron said faintly, moving his free hand gingerly up and down his horse’s neck. “Mad . . . if I could just see it —”
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: This whole thing is mental. Riding those things was the worst. Never again, honestly.

Book5-chapter34_Sc1.source: “This is bizarre!” Harry heard Ron yell from somewhere behind him, and he imagined how it must feel to be speeding along at this height with no visible means of support.
Book5-chapter34_Sc1.description: Flying like that with nothing visible under you is proper bizarre. Makes your stomach flip.
When we saw the tanks I was the first to blurt out and ask what they were. Couldn't believe my eyes.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "There you are. . . . Ha ha ha . . . You look funny, Harry. . . . You’re all messed up . . ."
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was a right mess. I couldn't stop giggling and I was dazed and out of it, but I still recognized Harry enough to tease him.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Harry, we saw Uranus up close!" said Ron, still giggling feebly. "Get it, Harry? We saw Uranus — ha ha ha —"
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: I kept making daft jokes even when I was injured. Makes me sound stupid, but it was how I was coping.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Accio Brain!" ... The moment they made contact with his skin, the tentacles began wrapping themselves around Ron’s arms like ropes.
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: I grabbed the brain. That was a stupid idea. As soon as I touched it the tentacles wrapped round me and I started choking. I couldn't pull free.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Harry, pull me along" moments and Harry hauling Ron over his shoulder like he had Dudley months ago.
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: Harry will put himself between danger and me. I know he will carry me out if I can't walk. We're stuck together and he won't leave me.

Book5-chapter35_Sc3.source: "Harry, look what’s happen — no — no, I don’t like it — no, stop — stop —"
Book5-chapter35_Sc3.description: I learned that some things in this place aren't jokes. I thought I'd be fine making a funny, but magic can get dangerous fast.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.source: Harry felt Ron stir beside him.
Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: I am terrified and on edge, but I stay close to Harry and follow him when he moves.

Book5-chapter35_Sc1.source: They were all yelling, there were cries of pain, thunderous crashes as the shelves collapsed upon themselves
Book5-chapter35_Sc1.description: When things go mad I panic like anyone, but I run with the others and try to get out alive.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "I must say, I’m looking forward to seeing Malfoy’s mother’s face when he gets off the train," said Ernie"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Blimey, watching Malfoy squirm is great. I still hate the git when he thinks he can order people about.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "Goyle’s mum’ll be really pleased, though," said Ron
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Goyle looks better to his mum now, apparently. Can't say I care much, but it's funny to watch.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "You’re well out of it, mate," said Ron forcefully.
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: You don't need Cho, Harry. You're far better off without someone who brings you down. Honest.

Book5-chapter38_Sc3.source: "Well, I always thought he was a bit of an idiot," he said, prodding his queen forward"
Book5-chapter38_Sc3.description: Good on Ginny for ditching Michael. He was an idiot for sulking over a quidditch result.
WHAT? Ginny's picked Dean Thomas? Bloody hell, that threw me right off. I lost my temper and upended the board.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'He\'s \u2018the Boy Who Lived\u2019 again now, though, isn\'t he?' said Ron darkly. 'Not such a show-off maniac anymore, eh?'
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Blimey, the papers are making a fuss about Harry again, but I\'m glad they\'re on his side now. Still, he\'s not exactly enjoying the spotlight.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'They sent me all these, you know,' he told Harry, pointing at the small mountain of Frogs beside him. 'Must be doing all right out of that joke shop, eh?'
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Fred and George are doing really well with the joke shop. Good for them, honestly. I\'m getting fed with Chocolate Frogs because of it.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'Wish we could come . . .' 'Say hello to him for us!' called Hermione, as Harry proceeded down the ward.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: I wanted to come with Harry to see Hagrid but I stayed behind. I wish we could all go, proper mateship and all that.

Book5-chapter38_Sc1.source: 'He\'s got to,' said Harry, 'the other centaurs won\'t take him back, will they?' 'It looks like he and Trelawney are both going to teach,' said Ginny.
Book5-chapter38_Sc1.description: Divination is staying after all with Firenze and Trelawney. I still reckon Divination is a load of rubbish, but whatever gets lessons running again.

Book6-chapter6_Sc8.source: "What was that about?" whispered Ron, reeling in the Extendable Ears.
Book6-chapter6_Sc8.description: What the hell was that? Something's up with Borgin, he went deadly quiet and looked worried. I was just trying to listen in with the Extendable Ears.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "When did you get here? Mum’s only just told us!"
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: Blimey, Harry got back at one in the morning and Mum only just found out. That's mental timing.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Were the Muggles all right? Did they treat you okay?"
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: I worry about how people treat Harry. Of course I want to know if the Dursleys were being horrible to him.
We kept hoping something big had happened while Harry was away. Bloody hell, we were expecting more drama than just persuading an old teacher to come back.

Book6-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Well, that’s not very long! I know why it’s happened, of course. It’s all this uncertainty with You-Know-Who coming back, people think they might be dead tomorrow, so they’re rushing all sorts of decisions they’d normally take time over."
Book6-chapter5_Sc2.description: I reckon folks are rushing into things because of You-Know-Who. Of course it explains Bill and Fleur moving so fast.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Harry, this is so cool, you\u2019re my Captain \u2014 if you let me back on the team, I suppose, ha ha."
Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: Blimey, Harry, you\u2019re my Captain. That makes me proper proud. If you let me back on the team, I will not let you down.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Wow, I remember when Charlie wore one of these,"
Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: Wow, I remember when Charlie wore one of these. It feels like family doing something big.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.source: "Blimey . . . you can\u2019t even make a joke round here anymore. . . ." and "But Ron was careful not to be flippant about Voldemort over the next few days."
Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: Blimey, I can joke, but I won\u2019t be daft about You-Know-Who. I\u2019ll watch what I say from now on.

Book6-chapter6_Sc4.source: "No, I wanna come, I want to see Fred and George's shop!"
Book6-chapter6_Sc4.description: I really want to go to Diagon Alley. I want to see Fred and George\u2019s shop and not be left at home.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “Did you hear about Florean Fortescue, Remus?” asked Bill... “Dragged off, by the look of his place.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: What the hell? Florean's been dragged off from his ice-cream place. That's mental and I want to know why they'd do that to a bloke like him.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “Talking of Diagon Alley,” said Mr Weasley, “looks like Ollivander’s gone too.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Ollivander's gone and the shop's empty. Blimey, if Ollivander's disappeared that's proper bad news.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “There have been another couple of dementor attacks,” he announced
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: There've been more dementor attacks. That's grim and makes everything feel even more dangerous.

Book6-chapter6_Sc1.source: “And they’ve found Igor Karkaroff’s body in a shack up north. The Dark Mark had been set over it — well, frankly, I’m surprised he stayed alive for even a year after deserting the Death Eaters; Sirius’s brother, Regulus, only managed a few days as far as I can remember.”
Book6-chapter6_Sc1.description: Karkaroff's been found dead with the Dark Mark over him. Bloody hell, deserting the Death Eaters doesn't end well.

Book6-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Watch where you’re putting your pins, woman! Mother — I don’t think I want these anymore —"
Book6-chapter6_Sc3.description: Blimey, he shoved straight into me on purpose. What a prat. I don't like him more than I already did.

Book6-chapter6_Sc3.source: "They'll make do with other makers," said Lupin. "But Ollivander was the best, and if the other side have got him it's not so good for us."
Book6-chapter6_Sc3.description: That's bloody worrying. If Ollivander's been taken by the other lot then things just got nastier for us.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Wish the lunch trolley would hurry up, I’m starving
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: I'm starving and the lunch trolley is taking forever. Hurry up, would you?

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Malfoy’s not doing prefect duty. He’s just sitting in his compartment with the other Slytherins, we saw him when we passed.
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Malfoy skipped prefect duty and just sat with the Slytherins. That's not like him, he usually loves bossing people about.

Book6-chapter7_Sc3.source: Not like him, though, is it? Well — that is but why isn’t he out there bullying first years?
Book6-chapter7_Sc3.description: Blimey, Malfoy skipping the usual bullying is odd. Something else must be going on.

Book6-chapter6_Sc6.description: Blimey, no time for dithering. If Harry says move, you move. Simple as that.
Of course Malfoy would sneak off into Knockturn Alley. That lad's made for trouble, isn't he?
We have to hurry or he's gone. I don't want to lose sight of him, so I'm pushing to get moving.

Book6-chapter6_Sc7.source: “We can!” said Ron excitedly. “Hang on — damn —” He dropped a couple more of the boxes he was still clutching as he fumbled with the largest. “Extendable Ears, look!”
Book6-chapter6_Sc7.description: We can listen. Hang on, damn it, got the Extendable Ears. I'll feed them under the door and listen in.
Brilliant, they work. Bloody hell, this is brilliant. Listen to them now.

Book6-chapter6_Sc2.source: Ron laughed loudly. "Don’t you dare talk to my mother like that, Potter!"
Book6-chapter6_Sc2.description: Don't you dare talk to my mum like that, Potter. I'm not having anyone slag her off.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.source: "It’s good Dad can get us these again,"
Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: Blimey, it's great Dad can get us these cars again. Proper comfy and all that.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.source: "Don’t get used to it, it’s only because of Harry," said Mr Weasley over his shoulder.
Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: Don’t get used to it? Of course it's only because of Harry. Still, I'll enjoy it while it lasts.

Book6-chapter6_Sc5.source: Bill and Fleur waving from the kitchen window.
Book6-chapter6_Sc5.description: Bill and Fleur waved us off. Nice to have family waving like that even if we're packed into a fancy Ministry car.

Book6-chapter8_Sc5.source: "Where’ve you — blimey, what’ve you done to your face?"
Book6-chapter8_Sc5.description: Blimey, I gawped at his face and couldn't believe what I'd seen. I asked what he'd done to it.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Maybe he’s broken his Hand of Glory," said Ron vaguely, as he attempted to straighten his broomstick’s bent tail twigs.
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: Blimey, maybe it's just something like a broken Hand of Glory. It could be nothing to do with dark stuff.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Malfoy, revenge? What can he do about it?" "That’s my point, I don’t know!" said Harry, frustrated.
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: What, Malfoy get revenge? I can't see him doing anything major. It sounds a bit much to me.

Book6-chapter7_Sc1.source: "Yeah, I still don’t reckon You-Know-Who would let Malfoy join. . . ."
Book6-chapter7_Sc1.description: I still don't think You-Know-Who would let a git like Malfoy join up. That's mental.
Well, I suppose it could be odd, but I'm not convinced Malfoy is actually a Death Eater. Sounds unlikely to me.

Book6-chapter8_Sc6.source: [Snape said Hagrid was late for the feast —]
Book6-chapter8_Sc6.description: Snape said Hagrid turned up late for the feast. Blimey, that's typical Hagrid really.
I dived straight in for a massive chocolate gateau. Can't pass up puddings like that, can you?

Book6-chapter8_Sc9.source: "How d’you know Voldemort doesn’t need someone at Hogwarts? It wouldn’t be the first —"
Book6-chapter8_Sc9.description: How d'you know Voldemort doesn't need someone at Hogwarts? It wouldn't be the first time someone was planted where they'd hurt us.

Book6-chapter8_Sc9.source: Ron snorted loudly, but managed to pass it off as a violent sneeze.
Book6-chapter8_Sc9.description: Blimey, Hagrid wants to train Grawp as his assistant. I couldn't stop myself laughing, so I pretended I sneezed.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "How come?" said Ron between frenzied mouthfuls of gateau.
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Blimey, I wanted to know why Hagrid was late or what was going on. I asked straight out while stuffing my face.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "Yeah," said Ron. "All wanting to know if you really are ‘the Chosen One’ —"
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Everyone's been asking if Harry's 'the Chosen One' and it's been nonstop. People can't stop prying.

Book6-chapter8_Sc7.source: "That’s not saying much, seeing as you’re already dead," Ron observed.
Book6-chapter8_Sc7.description: Honestly, I can be blunt and cheeky with Nearly Headless Nick. I don't hold back even when he's being dramatic.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Potions is back on people's minds because Slughorn's been hired as Potions master. That surprised everyone.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [That job's jinxed. No one’s lasted more than a year. Quirrell actually died doing it. Personally, I'm going to keep my fingers crossed for another death.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: That Defense Against the Dark Arts job is jinxed. No one lasts and people die doing it. Blimey, I'm almost hoping it happens again so Snape's out.

Book6-chapter8_Sc8.source: [He might just go back to teaching Potions at the end of the year, That Slughorn bloke might not want to stay long-term. Moody didn't.]
Book6-chapter8_Sc8.description: Slughorn might not stay long term. If he leaves, Snape could go back to Potions and that might change things.

Book6-chapter9_Sc1.source: Look, we’ve got a free period now . . . and a free period after break . . . and after lunch . . . excellent!
Book6-chapter9_Sc1.description: Blimey, I was proper pleased about all those free periods. That’s brilliant for getting stuff done or messing about with mates.
I was dead proud of Harry when he knocked Snape back. I couldn’t help grinning. Good on him.
I was purple trying not to mutter the jinx and Snape called me pathetic. I hate being made to look useless in front of everyone.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "That was different," he said robustly. "They were abusing it. Harry and his dad were just having a laugh."
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: Blimey, that was different. Those Death Eaters abused the spell. Us pretending and mucking about is just a laugh, honestly.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Fred and George," said Ron, shrugging, "it’s their kind of thing. And, er —"
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: I reckon Fred and George would be the sort to make daft spells like that. It's their sort of joke, not some big dangerous thing.

Book6-chapter12_Sc1.source: "You don’t like the Prince, Hermione," he added, pointing a sausage at her sternly, "because he’s better than you at Potions —"
Book6-chapter12_Sc1.description: I defended Harry and the Prince. I told Hermione she's just jealous because the Prince's notes might make someone better at Potions than her. Told you, it's all about bragging, not dark stuff.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "I haven’t forgotten the skrewts," said Ron darkly.
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: Blimey, I’m still furious about those skrewts. I haven’t forgiven that class at all.

Book6-chapter11_Sc1.source: "You can still see where those brains got hold of me in the Ministry, look," said Ron, shaking back his sleeves.
Book6-chapter11_Sc1.description: Look, I’ve got the marks from that Ministry mess. It’s still on me and it pisses me off.
Bloody hell, I’ve grown over the summer. Doesn’t change how I feel about things but I notice people look at me differently.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.source: "This strategy meant that Ron was not left out, and they usually had a laugh with Ginny, imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini."
Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: Blimey, Harry keeps pretending he has practice so I don't get left out, and we end up laughing with Ginny about how awful it would be to sit Hermione next to McLaggen or Zabini.

Book6-chapter12_Sc3.source: "And with a regal wave, he waddled out of the shop, taking as little notice of Ron as though he had been a display of Cockroach Clusters."
Book6-chapter12_Sc3.description: I got the feeling Slughorn barely noticed me at all, like I was just part of the furniture.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.source: Yeah, I think we saw a bit of that side of them,
Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: Blimey, those spiders got nasty when Aragog started going off. I noticed how their behaviour changed when he was ill.

Book6-chapter11_Sc2.source: I don’ reckon it’d be safe fer anyone but me ter go near the colony at the mo’,
Book6-chapter11_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, it really is too dangerous for anyone else to go near Aragog's colony right now. Hagrid insists he's the only one who should try.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: I said I hope Harry's lesson with Dumbledore goes okay. I'm worried and I care.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: "Right," said Harry, ... "Er," began Harry awkwardly, but Dumbledore did not look too stern. "I have arranged with Professor Snape that you will do your detention next Saturday instead." "Right," said Harry,
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: Well, I heard about the detention being moved. It doesn't change much for me except I'm glad Harry won't be dealing with Snape right this instant.

Book6-chapter10_Sc1.source: Ron was trying to read it upside down.
Book6-chapter10_Sc1.description: I was there messing about, trying to read Hermione's essay upside down like an idiot. Typical me, trying to be nosy.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "I don’t want to go on my own!" "I doubt you’ll be alone, Ginny’ll probably be invited," snapped Ron, who did not seem to have taken kindly to being ignored by Slughorn.
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: Blimey, Slughorn ignoring me stung. I reckon Ginny might get invited, but being passed over grated on me.
Drop it, Harry. I don't want to keep going on about Malfoy right now.

Book6-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Well, as I’m not invited to any parties," said Ron, getting to his feet again, "I think I’ll go to bed."
Book6-chapter11_Sc3.description: I'm fed up with not being invited. If I'm not wanted at these parties, I'm off to bed. Simple as that.

Book6-chapter12_Sc4.description: Hang on, that thing looks familiar to me. I think I've seen it before.
I pay attention to things, and if something looks like it belongs to someone we know, I'll call it out even if I'm a bit moody about it.

Book6-chapter12_Sc4.source: [Ron stooped down and picked up something silver.]
Book6-chapter12_Sc4.description: I picked up that silver bit because it caught my eye and I thought it meant something.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “That was different,” he said robustly. “They were abusing it. Harry and his dad were just having a laugh.
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: That was different, honestly. Those lot were abusing the spell. Harry and his dad were just having a laugh, not being nasty about it.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “There is no way they’d let me be a Death Eater!” said Ron indignantly, a bit of sausage flying off the fork he was now brandishing at Hermione and hitting Ernie Macmillan on the head. “My whole family are blood traitors! That’s as bad as Muggle-borns to Death Eaters!”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: There is no way they’d accept me. My whole family are blood traitors to them. That’s as bad as being Muggle-born to Death Eaters.

Book6-chapter12_Sc2.source: “And they’d love to have me,” said Harry sarcastically. “We’d be best pals if they didn’t keep trying to do me in.”
Book6-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, if Death Eaters were sensible they'd want someone like me. I’d never join them though. I’m not having any of that.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “Well, he would look a bit of a prat carrying a necklace,” interjected Ron.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: Blimey, Malfoy would look a prat carrying a necklace. He wouldn't want to be seen with something daft like that.

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “The curse didn’t even make it into the castle. Not what you’d call foolproof.”
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: The whole plan wasn't very clever. The curse didn't even get into Hogwarts. That's hardly foolproof, is it?

Book6-chapter12_Sc5.source: “It could’ve been meant for loads of people,” said Harry. “Dumbledore — the Death Eaters would love to get rid of him... Or —" “Or you,” said Hermione, looking troubled.
Book6-chapter12_Sc5.description: It could have been meant for any of a few people. I reckon it could've been meant for Dumbledore or someone important. Could have been aimed at people the Death Eaters hate.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "He enjoys Acid Pops?" said Ron, who had read the message over Harry’s shoulder and was looking perplexed.
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: He enjoys Acid Pops? So that's Dumbledore's password. Blimey, that's a brilliant password.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Ha! Snape’s not going to be pleased. . . . I won’t be able to do his detention!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: If the password is Acid Pops then Snape won't catch me out with that detention trick. That's a relief.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "Well, what’s so impressive about that?" whispered Ron, who for some reason looked annoyed. "You are the best in the year — I’d’ve told him so if he’d asked me!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: I'm a bit annoyed Hermione got the credit from Slughorn before I could boast. I want recognition too even if I grumble about it.

Book6-chapter9_Sc2.source: "It’s liquid luck," said Hermione excitedly. "It makes you lucky!"
Book6-chapter9_Sc2.description: Felix Felicis is liquid luck. Sounds mental but if it really works then it's something everyone would want.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "He only followed different instructions to ours," said Ron. "Could’ve been a catastrophe, couldn’t it? But he took a risk and it paid off."
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: I reckon Harry used different instructions from the ones we had. It could've gone wrong, but fair play to him, he took a risk and it worked out.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: "Slughorn could’ve handed me that book, but no, I get the one no one’s ever written on. Puked on, by the look of page fifty-two, but —"
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: Blimey, I'm gutted Slughorn didn't give me the best book. Mine's a mess and looks like it's been puked on. I felt proper miffed seeing Harry succeed with the scribbled copy.

Book6-chapter9_Sc3.source: He passed over Ernie’s navy concoction. Hermione’s potion he gave an approving nod. Then he saw Harry’s, and a look of incredulous delight spread over his face.
Book6-chapter9_Sc3.description: I saw Slughorn nod at Hermione and then go mad for Harry's potion. I was stunned. That bottle of Felix Felicis for Harry left me feeling gobsmacked and a bit jealous.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Well, you do," said Ron, "but if she jumps out at you unexpectedly, like then . . ."
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Blimey, yeah, you get used to someone if they live in the house, but it’s still horrible if they jump out at you like that.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Listen, no bloke in his right mind’s going to fancy Tonks when Fleur’s around."
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Look, no bloke’s going to go for Tonks when Fleur’s around. Fleur’s got that glamour and presence, she’s got the advantage.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "She hasn’t been much of a laugh lately," said Ron. "Every time I’ve seen her she’s looked more like Moaning Myrtle."
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: She’s been miserable lately, not funny at all. Honestly, she looks like she’s been crying her eyes out.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Tonks and Sirius barely knew each other!" said Ron. "Sirius was in Azkaban half her life and before that their families never met —"
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Tonks and Sirius barely knew one another. It’s not like they were close family friends or anything.

Book6-chapter5_Sc3.source: "Knew you’d be top at Defense Against the Dark Arts," said Ron, punching Harry on the shoulder.
Book6-chapter5_Sc3.description: Nice one, mate. I knew you’d ace Defense. We’ve done all right, haven’t we?

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I’m rubbish at the moment. I felt like giving up and said I resign. I couldn’t hide how useless I felt.
I don’t like being told what to do, especially when I’m already panicking. Don’t boss me about, all right?
I panicked and messed up. I tried to explain but I couldn’t get the words out properly.

Book6-chapter14_Sc2.source: "I know you haven’t got any time to find another Keeper, so I’ll play tomorrow, but if we lose, and we will, I’m taking myself off the team."
Book6-chapter14_Sc2.description: I agreed to play because I knew Harry needed someone, but I told him if we lose I’m off. I meant it.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: Wow, scary thought, the boy You-Know-Who.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Blimey, thinking about You-Know-Who is proper scary.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: But I still don’t get why Dumbledore’s showing you all this. I mean, it’s really interesting and everything, but what’s the point?
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: I don't see why Dumbledore is putting Harry through all this. It might be interesting but I want to know the point.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: And this is another party just for Slughorn’s favorites, is it?
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: So the Slug Club is just another of Slughorn's favorites. Sounds a bit daft to me.

Book6-chapter14_Sc1.source: You were going to ask me? ... No, I wouldn’t.
Book6-chapter14_Sc1.description: Hermione was going to ask me to the party and I would have said no if she'd thought I'd prefer someone else. I'm not desperate to be her 'plus one' if that's what she meant.
I want to deal with this pod. Hand me a bowl so I can try and smash it like a proper squash.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "He was actually smiling now, and when the crowd greeted a particularly good save with a rousing chorus of the old favorite 'Weasley Is Our King,' he pretended to conduct them from on high."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was loving it. I couldn't help showing off a bit when the crowd cheered 'Weasley Is Our King.'

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "You saved everything because you felt lucky. You did it all yourself."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I thought I might have only been playing well because of luck potion, but actually I saved those goals myself. I can do it without help.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "Ron came in, laughing, pulling Lavender by the hand."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: I'm with Lavender and trying to have a laugh, but I know Hermione's upset. I feel awkward about it and a bit guilty, even if I'm trying to be upbeat.

Book6-chapter14_Sc3.source: "'Gerremoffme!' he yelled, but with one last look of vindictive fury, Hermione wrenched open the door and disappeared through it."
Book6-chapter14_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, Hermione attacked me with conjured birds and I got pecked. I hadn't expected that reaction and it was pretty horrible.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: "Yeah, don’t worry about us," said Ron, permitting his mother to plant a very wet kiss on his cheek, "or about Percy. He’s such a prat, it’s not really a loss, is it?"
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: I shrug off Percy's leaving. I think Percy is a prat and honestly I don't see his going as a big loss.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: Mrs. Weasley planted a very wet kiss on his cheek.
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: Mum still fusses over me like crazy. I let her because, well, she means well even if it is embarrassing.

Book6-chapter17_Sc1.source: Ron came spinning into view after Harry arrived in McGonagall's office.
Book6-chapter17_Sc1.description: I arrive at Hogwarts the same way as Harry through the Floo. We're together when we head off to Gryffindor Tower.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "She had just spotted Ron and Lavender, who were entwined in the same armchair."
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Blimey, I was sitting with Lavender in the armchair. It looked cosy enough.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "\"She\'s a bit upset,\" said Luna. \"I thought at first it was Moaning Myrtle in there, but it turned out to be Hermione. She said something about that Ron Weasley. . . .\""
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Yeah, Hermione and I had a row. I can be a bit daft and say silly things that upset people.

Book6-chapter15_Sc1.source: "\"He says very funny things sometimes, doesn\'t he?\" said Luna. \"But he can be a bit unkind. I noticed that last year.\""
Book6-chapter15_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, people think I say funny things, but I can come across as unkind sometimes.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "You could’ve taken anyone! Anyone! And you chose Loony Lovegood?"
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: Blimey, I can't believe Harry picked Luna. Anyone else would have made more sense to me.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: "What, and get attacked by another flock of canaries?"
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: I muttered that apologizing to Hermione would probably get me attacked by more canaries. I was dodging the hassle.
I defended myself by saying she laughed at my mustache. I was annoyed and trying to justify what I did.

Book6-chapter15_Sc2.source: Squeezing herself in between Harry and Ron, Lavender flung her arms around Ron’s neck.
Book6-chapter15_Sc2.description: Lavender shoved herself between Harry and me and hugged me. That was awkward and a bit embarrassing.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "There was a noise like a plunger being withdrawn from a blocked sink and Ron surfaced."
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: I just surfaced there, felt a bit blank when Hermione announced her thing. Didn't know what to say.

Book6-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Ron looked strangely blank and said nothing."
Book6-chapter15_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was stunned. I couldn't bring myself to jump in when Hermione said she was going with McLaggen.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "An Unbreakable Vow?" said Ron, looking stunned.
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: An Unbreakable Vow is something you cannot break. That’s how it was put to me and it sounds deadly serious.
If someone breaks an Unbreakable Vow they die. That is the plain truth as far as I’m concerned.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Fred and George tried to get me to make one when I was about five. I nearly did too, I was holding hands with Fred and everything when Dad found us. He went mental," said Ron, with a reminiscent gleam in his eyes.
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: Fred and George once tried to get me to make a vow with them when I was little. Dad went mental when he found us. Fred still jokes about it but it was proper scary at the time.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "’Course, you know what they’ll all say? Dad and Dumbledore and all of them? They’ll say Snape isn’t really trying to help Malfoy, he was just trying to find out what Malfoy’s up to."
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: I reckon everyone will say Snape was only pretending to help so he could find out what Malfoy is doing. That’s what Dad and Dumbledore and the others will probably think.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "Yeah, I do!" said Ron hastily. "Seriously, I do!"
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: I do believe you, Harry. Honestly, I do. I’m on your side with this.

Book6-chapter16_Sc1.source: "I’ll be seventeen in two and a bit months’ time," said Ron grumpily, "and then I’ll be able to do it by magic!"
Book6-chapter16_Sc1.description: I’m fed up with having to do dumb chores by hand. Once I’m seventeen I’ll be able to do them by magic and I can’t wait.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Baubles," said Ron confidently, when they reached the Fat Lady
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: Baubles. That’s the password I tried to give, obviously.

Book6-chapter17_Sc2.source: "Yeah," said Ron at once, "pretty eventful, Rufus Scrim —"
Book6-chapter17_Sc2.description: My Christmas was pretty eventful, I was trying to start telling them about it, I was going to say something about Rufus Scrimgeour before I got cut off.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “It’s from Lavender,” said Ron, sounding revolted. “She can’t honestly think I’d wear . . .”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Lavender gave me that ridiculous 'My Sweetheart' necklace. Honest to Merlin, she thinks I'll wear that?

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “Is Hermione really going out with McLaggen?”
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: I asked if Hermione's actually seeing McLaggen. I don't know for sure. I don't like the idea of that at all.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “Fred and George gave them to me! Aren’t they beautiful?” and The package contained a large number of maggots.
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Fred and George sent Harry loads of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes stuff and Kreacher sent maggots to Harry. I thought the maggots were brilliant.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “Harry, you’ve got a maggot in your hair,” said Ginny cheerfully
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Ginny pulled a maggot out of Harry's hair and everyone laughed. That was priceless.

Book6-chapter16_Sc2.source: “You are as bad as zat Tonks,” said Fleur to Ron
Book6-chapter16_Sc2.description: Fleur nicknamed me clumsy and compared me to Tonks for knocking things about. Bloody hell, I am a walking disaster sometimes.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "They were a birthday present!" shouted Ron, revolving slowly in midair as he struggled to get free.
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: I believed those chocolates were a birthday present. I honestly thought someone had given them to me.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Romilda?" he repeated. "Did you say Romilda? Harry — do you know her? Can you introduce me?"
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: Romilda Vane? Yes please. The minute I heard her name I was desperate to meet her. I was sure I wanted her to fall for me.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Now drink that up, it’s a tonic for the nerves, keep you calm when she arrives, you know."
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: I drank Slughorn’s tonic thinking it would steady me for Romilda. Felt great for a moment until everything went wrong after the mead.

Book6-chapter18_Sc5.source: "Ron had dropped his glass; he half-rose from his chair and then crumpled, his extremities jerking uncontrollably."
Book6-chapter18_Sc5.description: After the mead I went from all smiles to collapsing and convulsing. Whatever happened to that drink was horrific.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: Ron had given up completely, and was merely trying to avoid breathing in the putrid fumes issuing from his cauldron.
