Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: Blimey, that potion was a disaster so I just stopped and tried not to puke. Sometimes you have to cut your losses.

Book6-chapter18_Sc2.source: "Look, I had to try and soften him up so I could ask him about Voldemort, didn’t I? Oh, will you get a grip!"
Book6-chapter18_Sc2.description: I winced when Harry said Voldemort's name because it still hits me. I’m worried and annoyed, and I don’t like being dragged into dangerous stuff.

Book6-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Bin in the forest all day! Aragog’s worse, I bin readin’ to him — didn’ get up ter dinner till jus’ now an’ then Professor Sprout told me abou’ Ron! How is he?"
Book6-chapter19_Sc1.description: I was out in the forest all day with Aragog. I missed dinner and only found out I was in the hospital when Professor Sprout told me. How am I? I want to know what's happened to me.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "You don’t want to get hold of him, he’s the size of a troll,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Blimey, McLaggen is huge. I wouldn't fancy getting stuck in with him.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Final score was three hundred and twenty to sixty."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: We lost spectacularly. The final score was three hundred and twenty to sixty.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Personally, I think there’s a lot to be said for hexing him with that toenail thing of the Prince’s."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Honestly, hexing him with that halfblood prince trick sounds very tempting. That's mental but satisfying to think about.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "Ginny came in to visit while you were unconscious,"
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Ginny came to see you while you were out and she cares enough to check on you. That's good to know.

Book6-chapter19_Sc2.source: "I could hear the match commentary from here," said Ron, his voice now shaking with laughter. "I hope Luna always commentates from now on. . . . Loser’s Lurgy . . ."
Book6-chapter19_Sc2.description: Luna's commentary was hilarious from the hospital wing. 'Loser's Lurgy' had me laughing my head off.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "At least you can Apparate, though!" said Ron tensely. "You'll have no trouble come July!"
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Blimey, Harry can Apparate now. He won't have any trouble when July comes round.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "Wish that would happen with me and Lavender," said Ron gloomily.
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: I wish Lavender would stop clinging to me. If I hint I want to finish something she holds on tighter. It's like going out with the giant squid.

Book6-chapter21_Sc1.source: "It can't be B — U — M —" and "It’s one of Fred and George's Spell-Check ones . . . but I think the charm must be wearing off."
Book6-chapter21_Sc1.description: Bloody hell, my quill's gone mad. Fred and George's Spell-Check quill is wearing off and I've almost wrecked my essay.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: Ron reckons I should just hang back after Potions this afternoon
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: Blimey, I think hanging back after class might work. That's my plan, simple as that.
What the hell did you do, Hermione? You went straight to Slughorn like a shot and left us behind.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: You sure the Prince hasn't got any tips?
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: I'm staring at the same book as you and there's nothing useful. Bloody typical that we're left guessing when a trick might have helped.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: After all, when has Won-Won's judgment ever been faulty?
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: People tease me by calling me Won-Won but I still reckon my straightforward ideas count for something. I get a bit flared up when Hermione mocks my judgment.

Book6-chapter18_Sc1.source: Ron kept forgetting that he could no longer rely on Hermione to help him out of trouble when he failed to grasp what was going on.
Book6-chapter18_Sc1.description: I keep trusting Hermione to bail me out in class and I forgot I can't always rely on her. That's worrying when things get tricky.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “Don’t be stupid,” said Ron sharply. “You couldn’t have missed a Quidditch match just to follow Malfoy, you’re the Captain!”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: Don't be daft, Harry. You're the Captain. You can't just miss matches to tail Malfoy.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “I dunno . . . Hogsmeade?” suggested Ron, yawning. “I’ve never seen him going along any of the secret passageways on the map. I thought they were being watched now anyway?”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: Maybe Malfoy is slipping into Hogsmeade. I haven't seen him use the secret passages and I reckon they're watched now.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “You’re getting a bit obsessed with Malfoy, Harry. I mean, thinking about missing a match just to follow him . . .”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: You're getting obsessed, Harry. Seriously, that's worrying.

Book6-chapter19_Sc3.source: “Nice one,” said Ron appreciatively, lifting Dobby into the air so that his flailing limbs no longer made contact with Kreacher. “That was another Prince hex, wasn’t it?”
Book6-chapter19_Sc3.description: That Langlock was brilliant. Pretty sure that was a hex from the Half-Blood Prince's book.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "I swear they’re getting smaller," he said.
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Blimey, those younger kids really seem to be shrinking every year. They look tiny to me now.

Book6-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Hermione even escorted them down to breakfast, bringing with her the news that Ginny had argued with Dean."
Book6-chapter20_Sc3.description: Hermione and I are mates again. Things are sorted out between us, which is great.

Book6-chapter22_Sc1.description: That is mental. Hagrid knew Aragog tried to eat Harry and me, and yet he still wants us to go and cry over the beast's body. I can't believe it.
Blimey, the obvious thing is to use the Felix. If Harry can't get Slughorn on his own, he should take the lucky potion and try again.
Well, I failed my Apparition test. It was rotten luck, just a tiny thing about leaving half an eyebrow behind, and I feel proper miserable about it.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: "Are you going to tell me what we’re doing, then?" asked Ron, panting slightly.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Blimey, I don't like being left out. Tell me what the plan is or I get jumpy.
Harry, hurry up and show me. I can't just stand here waiting.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: "It was on my birthday!" he said. "I was looking forward to that!"
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: It was meant to be my birthday treat. I'm dead annoyed they canceled Hogsmeade. That's rotten luck.

Book6-chapter18_Sc3.source: To general indignation, a sign went up on all common room notice boards that the next trip into Hogsmeade had been canceled. Ron was furious.
Book6-chapter18_Sc3.description: Of course I'm furious about Hogsmeade being canceled. It's exactly the sort of thing that ruins a good birthday.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "But now all I've got to look forward to is stupid Apparition!' said Ron grumpily. 'Big birthday treat . . .'"
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Blimey, I'm stuck with stupid Apparition for my birthday. Not exactly thrilled about it.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "Cheers,' said Ron drowsily and, as he ripped off the paper, Harry got out of bed... 'Nice one, Harry!' said Ron enthusiastically, waving the new pair of Quidditch Keeper's gloves Harry had given him."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I got Quidditch Keeper gloves from Harry and I'm well chuffed about them.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "'See what Mum and Dad got me? Blimey, I think I'll come of age next year too. . . .' 'Cool,' muttered Harry, sparing the watch a glance before peering more closely at the map."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Mum and Dad gave me a mad gold watch. I'm talking about coming of age like it's some massive thing.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "'Want one?' said Ron thickly, holding out a box of Chocolate Cauldrons. 'No thanks,' said Harry... 'Can't have done,' said Ron, stuffing a second Cauldron into his mouth as he slid out of bed to get dressed."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I'm scoffing Chocolate Cauldrons like nothing. I'm not exactly thinking straight when sweets are involved.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "'I'm not hungry.' Harry stared at him. 'I thought you just said — ?' 'Well, all right, I'll come down with you,' sighed Ron, 'but I don't want to eat.'"
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: Even though I just ate loads, I suddenly can't bring myself to eat breakfast because my head's all over the place.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "'I can't stop thinking about her!' said Ron hoarsely... 'Romilda Vane,' said Ron softly, and his whole face seemed to illuminate as he said it, as though hit by a ray of purest sunlight."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I'm head over heels for Romilda Vane. I think I'm in love with her, and I can't stop thinking about her hair and her eyes.

Book6-chapter18_Sc4.source: "He turned to leave; he had got two steps toward the door when a crashing blow hit him on the right ear. Staggering, he looked around. Ron's fist was drawn right back; his face was contorted with rage; he was about to strike again."
Book6-chapter18_Sc4.description: I lost it and socked Harry. I was so cross I nearly hit him again.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “Bad luck, mate, but you’ll pass next time — we can take it together.” “Yeah, I s’pose,” said Ron grumpily. “But half an eyebrow! Like that matters!”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Yeah, harsh luck for Harry now, but I reckon he'll pass next time and we'll sit it together. Half an eyebrow? Bloody ridiculous that matters.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “It’s a great feeling when you take it,” said Ron reminiscently. “Like you can’t do anything wrong.”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Taking Felix Felicis felt ace. Like nothing could go wrong when I thought I'd had it.

Book6-chapter22_Sc2.source: “Yeah, but I thought I had, didn’t I?” said Ron, as though explaining the obvious. “Same difference really . . .”
Book6-chapter22_Sc2.description: Even if I hadn't actually taken the potion, convincing myself I had made me feel like I did. Same difference, more or less.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "He’s got Crabbe and Goyle transforming into girls?" guffawed Ron. "Blimey . . . No wonder they don’t look too happy these days. . . . I’m surprised they don’t tell him to stuff it. . . ."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Blimey, Crabbe and Goyle as girls. No wonder they look miserable. If Malfoy’s bossing them around that badly, that explains loads.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Wish I could Disapparate like a house-elf," said Ron, staring at the spot where Dobby had vanished. "I’d have that Apparition Test in the bag."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: I wish I could just pop about like a house elf. Apparition is a nightmare for me and I could use any shortcut I could get.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Well, what Harry said is the most useful if we’re trying to tell them apart!" said Ron. "When we come face-to-face with one down a dark alley, we’re going to be having a shufti to see if it’s solid, aren’t we, we’re not going to be asking, ‘Excuse me, are you the imprint of a departed soul?’"
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: Yeah, when you meet something creepy you check if it is solid. Practical stuff matters more than spouting definitions.

Book6-chapter21_Sc2.source: "You’re right," he said, swinging his schoolbag back over his shoulder, "I’ll do the practice sessions in Hogsmeade before I decide about taking the test."
Book6-chapter21_Sc2.description: I’ll try the extra practice sessions in Hogsmeade and see if that helps. If not then I can postpone the test. Simple as that.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: I did it — well, kind of!
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I managed to Apparate, sort of. I overshot and ended up near Scrivenshaft’s but at least I moved.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: Perfect deliberation, divination, and desperation or whatever the hell it is — we all went for a quick drink in the Three Broomsticks after and you should’ve heard Twycross going on about her — I’ll be surprised if he doesn’t pop the question soon —
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: Hermione’s voicework for the test was spot on and everyone noticed. Twycross was raving about her and I reckon someone might propose soon.

Book6-chapter21_Sc3.source: She’s gone a bit funny. Lost her nerve. Women, they’re easily upset.
Book6-chapter21_Sc3.description: I reckon Tonks has gone a bit funny after the Ministry mess. Women get upset easily and she looks like she’s lost her nerve.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Wow. You’re actually going to go with Dumbledore . . . and try and destroy . . . wow."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Blimey, you're really going with Dumbledore to try and destroy Horcruxes. That's mental.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "Oh yeah," said Ron, looking down at his shoulders in vague surprise. "Sorry . . . looks like we’ve all got horrible dandruff now."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Oops, I made it snow and now we've all got fake dandruff on our shoulders. Sorry about that.

Book6-chapter24_Sc1.source: "We split up," he told Harry out of the corner of his mouth. "Last night. When she saw me coming out of the dormitory with Hermione."
Book6-chapter24_Sc1.description: Lavender and I split up last night because she saw me coming out with Hermione. I feel really guilty about it.
My Charms attempt went wrong and my flask exploded during the lesson. Bloody hell, that was a mess.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: Neither of them seemed to have noticed that a fierce battle was raging inside Harry’s brain
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Blimey, I’m in decent form again and everyone’s acting like the world’s fine. I’m just glad I’m fit for the match.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: “Couldn’t we make some more?” Ron asked Harry, ignoring Hermione. “It’d be great to have a stock of it. . . . Have a look in the book . . .”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: We should brew more Felix. It’d be brilliant to have a stash. Have a look in the potions book and see what we can do.

Book6-chapter24_Sc2.source: Harry pulled his copy of Advanced Potion-Making out of his bag and looked up Felix Felicis. “Blimey, it’s seriously complicated,” he said, running an eye down the list of ingredients. “And it takes six months.”
Book6-chapter24_Sc2.description: Blimey, Felix takes ages and is really complicated to make. That’s not something we can knock up quick.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: Blimey, it\'s exactly like when you find out something takes ages and you just want the shortcut. That Felix stuff being six months long was a proper pain.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Couldn\'t we make some more?" Ron asked Harry, ignoring Hermione.
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: It would be brilliant to have a stash of Felix. I kept saying we should make more because more luck sounds like the answer to everything.

Book6-chapter24_Sc3.source: "Ron seemed to be there at Harry\'s shoulder every time he saw Ginny."
Book6-chapter24_Sc3.description: I was all over Harry when Ginny was around because I still cared about her and I didn\'t want anyone messing things up, least of all Harry.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "’Course not," said Ron robustly. "He was a genius, the Prince."
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Blimey, I still think the Prince was a right genius at Potions. If it weren’t for his stuff I might not be here talking about it.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "You still got detention with Snape this Saturday?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: I know Harry’s stuck with loads of detentions with Snape and it’s eating into his time. It’s a pain for him and for us too.

Book6-chapter25_Sc1.source: "Just because I’ve given my permission doesn’t mean I can’t withdraw it —"
Book6-chapter25_Sc1.description: Listen, I’ll stick up for Ginny messing about, and I gave my permission about who she dates, but I can be jealous. I say things like watch it, even if I sound hypocritical sometimes.
Blimey, when Dumbledore calls Harry I get that sinking feeling that something big is up. I worry about what it could mean for Harry and the book.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "Where’ve you — ? Why are you soaking — ? Is that blood?" Ron was standing at the top of the stairs, looking bewildered at the sight of Harry.
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: Blimey, Harry came out soaking wet and looking like he'd been in a fight. It looked like there was blood on him and I was shocked.
Leave it, Hermione. I'm backing Harry here and I don't want more of that lecturing when he's already had enough.

Book6-chapter24_Sc4.source: "He had just finished telling Ron, Hermione, and Ginny what had happened,"
Book6-chapter24_Sc4.description: I heard what happened in the bathroom from Harry. I'm worried for him and worried about the match, but I'm with him.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "Thanks," said Ron. "Er — why do I need socks?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: Blimey I was given socks and asked why. I unwrapped them and found the Felix Felicis and I was gobsmacked by it all.

Book6-chapter25_Sc3.source: "We don’t want it, you take it, who knows what you’re going to be facing?"
Book6-chapter25_Sc3.description: I know the potion is powerful. I am awestruck and want it but Hermione tells Harry to take it. Still, I understand it could help whoever goes into danger.

Book6-chapter30_Sc3.source: Ron’s face was screwed up as though the sunlight were blinding him.
Book6-chapter30_Sc3.description: Blimey, I'm stunned and can't even look properly. I never expected Snape could be that kind of person.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: We did exactly what you said, checked the map, and still messed up. I feel rotten about it.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: — Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder, said Ron bitterly. Fred and George's. I'm going to be having a word with them about who they let buy their products.
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: Malfoy used Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder, the stuff from Fred and George. Bloody hell, I'm going to have words with them about who buys that rubbish.

Book6-chapter29_Sc2.source: None of us could break through, and that massive Death Eater was still firing off jinxes all over the place, they were bouncing off the walls and barely missing us.
Book6-chapter29_Sc2.description: We couldn't break through the curse blocking the stairs and that huge Death Eater kept firing jinxes that were nearly hitting us. It was chaos.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "I thought she wasn’t much of a looker," said Ron.
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Blimey, I thought Snape's mum wasn't much to look at. That does not help his image.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "But why didn’t he turn you in?"
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Why on earth didn't Snape turn me in when he knew about the book? It's proper puzzling.

Book6-chapter30_Sc2.source: "Yeah, that fits," said Harry. "He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . ." "Yeah, that fits," said Harry. "He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . . He’s just like Voldemort."
Book6-chapter30_Sc2.description: Right, that makes sense to me now. Snape putting on airs to impress the pure-bloods sounds exactly like something he'd do.

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: Ron ... was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder, tears dripping from the end of his own long nose.
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: Blimey, I'm holding Hermione and stroking her hair to try and comfort her. I'm upset too and I'm not ashamed to say it

Book6-chapter30_Sc4.source: tears dripping from the end of his own long nose.
Book6-chapter30_Sc4.description: I'm crying along with her. This is horrible and it's getting to me

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "Anyone else we know died?" Ron asked Hermione, who was perusing the Evening Prophet.
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: Anyone else we know been killed? I want to know if more of our lot are gone.

Book6-chapter30_Sc1.source: "I\'m going to go to bed," yawned Ginny. "I haven\'t been sleeping that well since . . . well . . . I could do with some sleep." She kissed Harry (Ron looked away pointedly) ...
Book6-chapter30_Sc1.description: Blimey, that was awkward. I looked away when Ginny kissed Harry. I don\'t want to make it weird but notice taken.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "I knew Ginny was lying about that tattoo,"
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: Blimey, I was sure Ginny was having me on, and now I can see she really was. That's mental.

Book7-chapter4_Sc4.source: "An’ you’re with me, Harry. That all righ’?"
Book7-chapter4_Sc4.description: We're taking Harry on the bike. I'll be with him. Not sure how I feel about all the attention but that's the plan.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "But he wasn't bitten at the full moon," said Ron, who was gazing down into his brother's face as though he could somehow force him to mend just by staring. "Greyback hadn't transformed, so surely Bill won't be a — a real — ?"
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: He wasn't bitten at the full moon so Bill probably won't be a full werewolf, but there could still be contamination or lasting damage.

Book6-chapter29_Sc1.source: "Dumbledore might know something that'd work, though," Ron said. "Where is he? Bill fought those maniacs on Dumbledore's orders, Dumbledore owes him, he can't leave him in this state —"
Book6-chapter29_Sc1.description: Dumbledore sent Bill into that fight and Bill got hurt. Dumbledore owes him and he can't just leave Bill like this.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "They’re talking about closing the school," said Harry. "Lupin said they would," said Ron.
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: They're talking about closing Hogwarts. Blimey, that would be a right mess.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: "So?" said Ron in a very low voice. "Did you find one? Did you get it? A — a Horcrux?"
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: I wanted to know straightaway if Harry had got the Horcrux. It mattered more than anything at that moment.

Book6-chapter29_Sc3.source: Wordlessly, Harry pulled the fake locket from his pocket, opened it, and passed it to Ron.
Book6-chapter29_Sc3.description: Harry didn't get the real one. He has a fake locket, which means someone beat us to it.
The initials R.A.B. were inside the locket. Who on earth is R.A.B. and why did they take it?

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "Ron smirked at the sight of him sitting there like a child in a bumper car."
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: Blimey, I couldn't help smirking. Harry in that sidecar looked like a kid in a bumper car and I couldn't help it.

Book7-chapter4_Sc5.source: "Hold tight now, Ron," said Tonks, and Harry saw Ron throw a furtive, guilty look at Lupin before placing his hands on either side of her waist."
Book7-chapter4_Sc5.description: I felt awkward and guilty about grabbing Tonks in front of Lupin. I tried to play it cool but I wasn't.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.source: "What’s wrong with him?" croaked Fred, looking terrified. "Is his mind affected?" "Saintlike," repeated George, opening his eyes and looking up at his brother.
Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: Blimey, George's ear is gone but he is crackin' jokes. That's George for you, still daft after everything.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.source: "How’s George?" asked Lupin. "What’s wrong with him?" piped up Ron.
Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: I was worried and I said so. Seeing George hurt made me sharp, I wanted to know if he was all right straight away.

Book7-chapter5_Sc2.source: "Bill! Thank God, thank God —" Mrs. Weasley ran forward, but the hug Bill bestowed upon her was perfunctory. Looking directly at his father, he said, "Mad-Eye’s dead."
Book7-chapter5_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, Mad-Eye is dead. That makes this whole thing real and terrible. It feels like nothing will be the same.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "- because it’s the first time for all of us," said Ron. "This is different, pretending to be me -"
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: Blimey, this is completely mental. Pretending to be Harry is a whole different kettle of fish because it's the first time for everyone and it's dangerous.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: "Yeah, thirteen of us against one bloke who’s not allowed to use magic; we’ve got no chance," said Fred.
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: Look, I know we are outnumbered and if things go wrong we're in serious trouble. That's why we have to be careful, not stupid.

Book7-chapter4_Sc3.source: Harry glanced at Ron, who grimaced at him in a just-do-it sort of way.
Book7-chapter4_Sc3.description: I will push Harry to do what needs doing. I grimace and give him that look because I want him to cooperate for everyone's sake.

Book7-chapter6_Sc4.source: Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?” asked Ron angrily.
Book7-chapter6_Sc4.description: What the hell? Why is nobody at the Ministry willing to stand up? People are just terrified and that's not good enough.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Get to the point! I'm not having this dragged out, just tell us what happened.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: "Can you hear us complaining?" said Ron.
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Can you hear us complaining? We're not thrilled but we're not going to kick off about it either.

Book7-chapter6_Sc8.source: Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger, Harry Potter are all present in the scene where Hermione reveals she summoned books from Dumbledore's study.
Book7-chapter6_Sc8.description: Blimey, so she actually nicked Dumbledore's books. That's mental but if Hermione says it's for the Horcrux hunt, I'm in.

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Why did he have to ask Slughorn how to make a Horcrux, then, if he’d already read that?" asked Ron.
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Why would he bother asking Slughorn if he could have already read how to make one in the library?

Book7-chapter6_Sc9.source: "Isn’t there any way of putting yourself back together?" Ron asked.
Book7-chapter6_Sc9.description: Is there any way to put yourself back together after splitting your soul?

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "No," said Ron, before Harry could answer.
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: No, I can't see Voldemort trying that. He wouldn't attempt it, simple as that.

Book7-chapter6_Sc10.source: "Oh well, lucky we've got such a large supply of basilisk fangs, then," said Ron. "I was wondering what we were going to do with them."
Book7-chapter6_Sc10.description: Bloody hell, we've actually got a lot of basilisk fangs and they'd do the job for destroying Horcruxes. Lucky us.

Book7-chapter6_Sc11.source: "Which would be a real comfort to me, I’m sure,"
Book7-chapter6_Sc11.description: Hang on, that would be a real comfort, wouldn't it? I thought the bit of soul in a Horcrux might just move on if its container was smashed.

Book7-chapter6_Sc11.source: "The bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn’t it?"
Book7-chapter6_Sc11.description: Hang on, the bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn't it? That explains why flushing it didn't get rid of it.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: Ron took charge of Mr. Weasley's old Ministry colleague Perkins
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: I took Perkins on, like you do. Someone had to deal with the boring Ministry types.
Yeah, I know Luna. Isn't she with you? Kind of weird question, but yeah I know her.

Book7-chapter8_Sc1.source: "Ours do know a lot of excellent swear words," said Ron, "but I think Fred and George taught them those."
Book7-chapter8_Sc1.description: Our gnomes have a cracking vocabulary. Fred and George taught them half of it. Bloody brilliant.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: Ginny’s probably left a speck of dust on a poxy napkin ring," said Ron. "I dunno why the Delacours have got to come two days before the wedding.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: Blimey, Mum's going mental about tiny things like a speck of dust and I don't see why the Delacours have to arrive so early. It's not helping her stress.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: This R.A.B. person," he said. "You know, the one who stole the real locket?
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: This R.A.B. person might have nicked the real locket. If they destroyed it that's one less Horcrux for us to worry about and that's brilliant.

Book7-chapter6_Sc7.source: "Well, guests aren’t going to help Mum’s stress levels," said Ron.
Book7-chapter6_Sc7.description: Guests turning up early are only making Mum more stressed. We need to sort things that actually help, not invite more bother.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Descendo," muttered Ron, pointing his wand at the low ceiling.
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Look, I can open a hatch and bring the ghoul down whenever I want. I’ve set it up so it lives in my attic and can be shown off.
I’m telling everyone the ghoul is me with spattergroit. It’s meant to pass for me, covered in pustules and everything, so people will think I’m too ill to be anywhere else.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Look, when we three don’t turn up at Hogwarts again, everyone’s going to think Hermione and I must be with you, right?"
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: The plan is simple. If Hermione and I don’t show, people will assume we’re with Harry. That should send Death Eaters to our families instead of to Harry.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Spattergroit’s really contagious, so they’re not going to want to go near him."
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: Spattergroit is supposedly deadly contagious, so showing a ghoul that looks infected will keep inquisitive people away from Mum and Dad.

Book7-chapter6_Sc6.source: "Dad is. He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul."
Book7-chapter6_Sc6.description: My dad is in on this. He, Fred and George helped transform the ghoul into the perfect sick-looking decoy.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: I reckon Moody might have survived. I don't want to accept he's gone without question.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "The Death Eaters probably tidied up after themselves, that’s why no one’s found him," said Ron wisely.
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: The Death Eaters would cover their tracks. They'd tidy things up so nobody finds Moody's body, so not finding him doesn't prove anything.

Book7-chapter6_Sc5.source: "He’d tell us to learn from what happened to him. And what I’ve learned is not to trust that cowardly little squit, Mundungus."
Book7-chapter6_Sc5.description: Moody would say 'constant vigilance' and I'd know what he meant. Also, I definitely won't trust that cowardly little squit Mundungus again.
I'm fed up of arguing about this. I'm blunt about it and want us to get on with the plan rather than keep debating.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?" asked Ron angrily.
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: What the hell? I can't believe no one at the Ministry is standing up to You-Know-Who. People are just terrified and doing nothing.

Book7-chapter6_Sc3.source: "There are nasty rumors going around; I for one don’t believe the Muggle Studies professor at Hogwarts resigned. She hasn’t been seen for weeks now."
Book7-chapter6_Sc3.description: There are rumors about people disappearing. The Muggle Studies professor hasn't been seen for weeks and people are saying she resigned, but that smells wrong.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Ron can laugh," said Luna serenely as Harry led her and Xenophilius toward their seats... Ron, passing them in the opposite direction, let out a loud snort.
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Blimey, Luna just calmly took the mick while I snorted. I went bright red again and couldn't help it.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "After a few moments he muttered to Harry, 'Did you see he's grown a stupid little beard?'"
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: I noticed Krum's beard and thought it looked stupid. I muttered it to Harry because I was embarrassed and jealous.

Book7-chapter8_Sc2.source: "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag... As she scrambled, blushing, to pick it up, she said, 'I didn't know you were — goodness — it's lovely to see — how are you?' Ron's ears had turned bright red again.
Book7-chapter8_Sc2.description: Hermione's reaction to Viktor made my ears go scarlet. Bloody hell, it was obvious I was mortified.

Book7-chapter6_Sc12.source: "Hang on," said Ron, frowning. "The bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn’t it? How does that work, then?"
Book7-chapter6_Sc12.description: Hang on. So the bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn't it? That's mental. How does that even work then?

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "A-all of us?" said Ron. "Me and Hermione too?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Hold on, I was surprised Dumbledore left things to all three of us. I didn't expect to be remembered in his will.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "Me? Not — not really . . . It was always Harry who . . ."
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: I don't think I was that close to Dumbledore. I kept meaning to say more, but I always felt like Harry was the one he knew best.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "'To Ronald Bilius Weasley, I leave my Deluminator, in the hope that he will remember me when he uses it.'"
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: Dumbledore left me the Deluminator. I couldn't believe it at first when Scrimgeour handed it over and I just sat there stunned.

Book7-chapter7_Sc2.source: "'Why would he have left you an item so rare?' ... 'To what use did he think you would put his Deluminator, Mr. Weasley?'" and Ron's reply "Put out lights, I s'pose," mumbled Ron.
Book7-chapter7_Sc2.description: I figured the Deluminator is for putting out lights. That's the obvious use, isn't it? I was baffled by why he'd give me something so special.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: Where are we? I need to know where we've landed so we can get our bearings.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: "Most of the Order was there, they’ll look after everyone."
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: Blimey, the Order were at the wedding. They're still there to help, so we can't waste time going back.
How the ruddy hell did Hermione fit all that in her bag? That's mental, she planned this properly.

Book7-chapter9_Sc1.source: The two workmen made identical movements, and Harry mirrored them without conscious thought: All three of them drew their wands.
Book7-chapter9_Sc1.description: When something's dodgy I reach for my wand and act. I jump in to protect mates, even if I don't always see the whole picture at first.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "He can’t have," said Ron. "The Trace breaks at seventeen, that’s Wizarding law, you can’t put it on an adult."
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: He can't have the Trace. Once you're seventeen the Trace breaks, that's the rule. You can't stick it on an adult.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "But Harry hasn’t been near a Death Eater in the last twenty-four hours. Who’s supposed to have put a Trace back on him?" Hermione did not reply.
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: If Harry hasn't been near any Death Eaters recently then who could've put a Trace back on him? That doesn't add up.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "We need a safe place to hide," said Ron.
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: We need somewhere safe to hide and think. We can't stay here forever, we have to find a place where we're less likely to be found.

Book7-chapter9_Sc2.source: "It’s all r-right. . . . It’s g-gone. . . ." Ron, who was shaking from head to foot, patting her clumsily on the shoulder and saying, "It’s all r-right."
Book7-chapter9_Sc2.description: I try to keep Hermione calm when she's scared even if I come across clumsy. I'm there for my mates when things go wrong.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: 'Who’s Gregorovitch?' 'I dunno, do I? You were the one saying it.'
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: Blimey, I heard Harry muttering Gregorovitch and I haven't a clue who he means. I suggested Gorgovitch by mistake because I thought he meant a Quidditch player.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: 'I try not to either,' said Ron.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I still can't stand thinking about that Gorgovitch bloke. Seriously, I'd rather forget him.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: 'Here’s your present. Unwrap it up here, it’s not for my mother’s eyes.' 'A book?' 'This isn’t your average book... Twelve Fail-Safe Ways to Charm Witches.'
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I gave Harry a joke present from Fred and George about charming witches. I thought he'd get a laugh from it and I reckon it was a good one.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: The door banged open behind them and they jumped apart. 'Oh,' said Ron pointedly.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I walked in on Harry and Ginny. I felt awkward and pointed it out. My ears went scarlet and I couldn't help being a bit blunt about it.

Book7-chapter7_Sc1.source: He gave Harry the thumbs-up and mouthed, Good one.
Book7-chapter7_Sc1.description: I thought my mum's cake trick and the rest of the party stuff was spot on. I showed Harry the thumbs-up because I was chuffed with how it looked.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "That was the one you nearly swallowed!"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Blimey, that Snitch Harry caught when he was little is the same one. I remember him almost swallowing it.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "I always said he was mental. Brilliant and everything, but cracked. Leaving Harry an old Snitch — what the hell was that about?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Dumbledore was clever but dodgy. I think he was a bit cracked for doing things like leaving Harry a Snitch instead of explaining himself.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "And the sword," said Ron finally, "Why did he want Harry to have the sword?"
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: I know the sword matters and I’m worried why Dumbledore wanted Harry to have it. It feels serious and confusing.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "Hold ing it up in front of him, he clicked it. The solitary lamp they had lit went out at once."
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: The Deluminator actually works. I clicked it and the lamp went out and then the light came back to us when we wanted it.

Book7-chapter7_Sc3.source: "A brutal triple murder by the bridegroom’s mother might put a bit of a damper on the wedding. I’ll get the lights."
Book7-chapter7_Sc3.description: Right, I’ll handle the lights. Funny way to put it but I don’t want anything ruining the wedding, and I’m prepared to sort things out.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: What? That was Sirius’s brother, wasn’t it? Regulus Arcturus . . . Regulus . . . R.A.B.! The locket — you don’t reckon — ?
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: Blimey, Regulus is R.A.B. and that could mean the locket is connected to him.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: Is that it, then? It’s not here?
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: It looks like the locket isn't in Regulus's room. That was a proper letdown.

Book7-chapter10_Sc1.source: If it’s massive spiders again I want breakfast before I —
Book7-chapter10_Sc1.description: I still need my stomach sorted before anything dangerous. I get jumpy and hungry before a scrap.
Kreacher nicked things back from us. We have to check his kitchen cupboard next.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'People won’t let this happen,' said Ron. 'It is happening, Ron,' said Lupin.
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: Blimey, this is real. They're actually rounding up Muggle-borns and it's getting worse by the minute.

Book7-chapter11_Sc2.source: 'What if purebloods and half-bloods swear a Muggle-born’s part of their family? I’ll tell everyone Hermione’s my cousin —' 'You won’t have a choice,' said Ron fiercely
Book7-chapter11_Sc2.description: I'll do whatever it takes to protect Hermione. I'll lie through my teeth, teach her my family tree, say she's family. No one will touch her if I can help it.
I'm happy for Tonks and Remus. I want to celebrate good news even in all this mess. And I'll back Hermione against anyone who blames her.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Death Eaters, for sure," said Ron, as he, Harry, and Hermione watched from the drawing room windows. "Reckon they know we're in here?"
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: Blimey, there are Death Eaters outside. I kept thinking they might know we're in here and we'd be in serious trouble.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "D'you reckon he's been in here and had his tongue tied by Moody's curse?" asked Ron.
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: Maybe Snape's been here and Moody's done that rotter's tongue up. I said it out loud because it's the sort of thing I'd think.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "— and he left me the Deluminator, maybe I'm supposed to use it!"
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: I keep fiddling with the Deluminator because I suppose I'm meant to have it. I don't know why I keep doing it, but it's mine and I'm using it.

Book7-chapter11_Sc1.source: "Apart from anything else, they'd know for sure Harry was here if he still had the Trace on him, wouldn't they? But I can't see how they could have tracked you to Tottenham Court Road, that's worrying, really worrying."
Book7-chapter11_Sc1.description: If Harry still had the Trace they'd have known he was here, but he doesn't. Still, how they found him in Tottenham Court Road is proper worrying. Something's off.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Well, it’s obvious, isn’t it, Harry? He Disapparated!"
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Blimey, Kreacher must've disapparated away from the Inferi using elf magic.

Book7-chapter10_Sc3.source: "Elf magic isn’t like wizard’s magic, is it? I mean, they can Apparate and Disapparate in and out of Hogwarts when we can’t."
Book7-chapter10_Sc3.description: Elf magic works differently to ours; they can do things like Apparate into places we can't, even Hogwarts.
When I offered the fake locket to Kreacher, it was too much for him and he reacted very badly.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: Ron groaned as he threw himself into a kitchen chair; he looked gleeful when Harry asked about the locket
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Blimey, I was over the moon when Harry thought Kreacher had the locket. I want something concrete to go on and that made me feel hopeful.
Mundungus nicked the locket and a load of Black family stuff. That tells me who to blame and maybe who to chase.

Book7-chapter10_Sc2.source: Kreacher's account of being forced to a cave and made to drink potion by the Dark Lord
Book7-chapter10_Sc2.description: Bloody hell, if Voldemort did that to an elf it shows just how nasty his Horcrux protections are. This is serious and dangerous.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "No, he's still stuck in the bog," said Ron.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Blimey, I was panicking about them back home, thinking someone was stuck. My head's all over the place.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "You think it's funny, Cattermole, do you?" Yaxley said and Ron whispered, "Yes."
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: I was terrified of Yaxley. I kept trying to play it cool but I was scared stiff.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "If I don’t turn up, my wife — I mean, Cattermole’s wife —" Ron asked the other two at once; he looked stricken.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: If I don't get there, people I care about will be in trouble. That's on me. That's mental, I can't just ignore it.

Book7-chapter12_Sc3.source: "Say it again, slowly —" said Ron, searching his pockets desperately for a quill.
Book7-chapter12_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, I needed instructions spelled out. I wasn't thinking straight and needed Hermione to slow down so I could remember the spells.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "Blimey, Hermione, I forget one little thing -"
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, I do forget stuff sometimes, don't I?

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "She's Mafalda Hopkirk," he said, reading a small card that identified their victim as an assistant in the Improper Use of Magic Office.
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Right, she's Mafalda Hopkirk from the Improper Use of Magic Office. That's who we're copying.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "'You'd better take this, Hermione, and here are the tokens.' He passed her several small golden coins, all embossed with the letters M.O.M., which he had taken from the witch's purse."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Here, I nicked the tokens and handed them over. They're stamped M.O.M. and they'll get us in.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "'Blimey, that's scary,' said Ron, looking up at Harry, who now towered over him."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: Blimey, seeing Harry all big and bearded like that is proper scary.

Book7-chapter12_Sc2.source: "'We have to flush ourselves in?' he whispered."
Book7-chapter12_Sc2.description: So we have to flush ourselves down the toilet to reach the Ministry. That's mental but it works.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: Where the hell are you heading? If we're staying here then tell me now.

Book7-chapter14_Sc5.source: "I thought this belonged to that bloke Perkins at the Ministry?" he asked, starting to disentangle the tent pegs.
Book7-chapter14_Sc5.description: I thought that tent was Perkins's at the Ministry. Fancy that it ended up with us.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: Well, you’ve just had a big shock,
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: Blimey, that was a shock for Harry. He just went through something nasty and we need to be careful with him.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: What was that supposed to do?
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: What was that spell supposed to do then? I don't get all these spells, but I know when something should show up and it didn't.
There's no one here except us and old Dusty, the patch of carpet where that corpse thing rose. That's mental.
I checked outside. Can't see anyone. If there was a Trace on Harry they'd have followed, but they can't get in here.

Book7-chapter9_Sc3.source: They’re all right, they’re all right!
Book7-chapter9_Sc3.description: When I heard the Patronus from my family I was relieved. My family are safe and that matters more than anything right now.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: He had always thought of Splinching as something comical, but this . . . His insides crawled unpleasantly as Hermione laid bare Ron’s upper arm, where a great chunk of flesh was missing, scooped cleanly away as though by a knife.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: Blimey, my arm's been messed up. There's a chunk gone from my upper arm and I'm out cold.

Book7-chapter14_Sc1.source: "He’s fainted," said Hermione, who was also rather pale; she no longer looked like Mafalda, though her hair was still gray in places.
Book7-chapter14_Sc1.description: I'm fainted. I can't even stay awake after all that blood.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Why are you so wet?" "Water," muttered Ron, disengaging himself.
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Bloody hell, I'm soaked from that bit of business. It was water, that's it, nothing fancy.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Harry, they know there are intruders inside the Ministry, something about a hole in Umbridge’s office door, I reckon we’ve got five minutes if that —"
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: They've twigged there's intruders. I reckon we've got about five minutes or less before everything goes to pot.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "The balding wizard’s colleagues set up an uproar, under cover of which Ron grabbed Mrs. Cattermole, pulled her into the still-open fireplace, and disappeared."
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Right, when there's a chance I grab it. I pulled Mary through the fireplace when I could. Quick reactions save people, simple as that.

Book7-chapter13_Sc3.source: "Reg, I don’t understand —" "Let go, I’m not your husband, you’ve got to go home!"
Book7-chapter13_Sc3.description: Reg Cattermole's a mess and people are mixed up. I had to step in and get Mary moving, even if it caused chaos with the real Reg turning up.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "No, you shouldn’t," said Ron at once. "But he’s acting like one."
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Blimey, I know calling Lupin a coward was wrong, but I'm convinced he's been acting like a coward.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Right, we’ve got a few questions for you," Harry told Mundungus, who shouted at once, "I panicked, okay?..." "Well, you’re a bunch of bleedin’ ’eroes then, aren’t you..." "We’re not interested in why you ran out on Mad-Eye," said Harry.
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: Mundungus panicked and ran from danger. He'll say anything to save himself, so we need to treat him as untrustworthy and press him hard.

Book7-chapter11_Sc3.source: "Call ’im off, call ’im off, ’e should be locked up!" screamed Mundungus... "We need him conscious, Kreacher, but if he needs persuading you can do the honors," said Harry. "Thank you very much, Master," said Kreacher with a bow, and he retreated a short distance...
Book7-chapter11_Sc3.description: I tackled Mundungus to stop him fleeing and watched Kreacher rough him up. That was necessary to keep Mundungus talking. If someone's dodgy, a bit of a rugby tackle helps get answers.
I figured Mundungus was thinking about money and whether he could have asked more for the locket. He might have sold it to make a quick profit, not kept it.

Book7-chapter14_Sc4.description: Blimey, I feel lousy. I just groaned and opened my eyes, all gray and sweating, that's how rough I am.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: Blimey, I can feel something from that locket when I hold it tight in my fist.
I wasn't sure at first what Harry meant about feeling it, but I passed it to him to see.

Book7-chapter14_Sc7.source: Ron turning a nasty shade of green and attempting to sit up
Book7-chapter14_Sc7.description: I felt really sick after holding the locket and nearly couldn't sit up; that thing makes me feel awful.

Book7-chapter14_Sc8.source: "Couldn’t you see what the thief was holding?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc8.description: Could you actually tell what the thief had? I couldn't see it, so it must have been hard to spot.

Book7-chapter14_Sc8.source: "Harry, you don’t reckon You-Know-Who’s after something else to turn into a Horcrux?" "Yeah, but maybe he doesn’t know that."
Book7-chapter14_Sc8.description: Do you think Voldemort might be after something else to make another Horcrux? He might not even realise his soul is already hanging by a thread.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I’ve been thinking about that all day. It left nearly six hours ago."
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: The Hogwarts Express left without us ages ago. It's weird not being on it.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: "I do that every time. Oh, here she is,"
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: I mess up with the Invisibility Cloak too. Also I'm watching for Hermione coming back in like always.

Book7-chapter12_Sc1.source: "Dad always told us most Ministry people use the Floo Network to get to work"
Book7-chapter12_Sc1.description: Dad says most Ministry people use the Floo Network to get to work. That's why Umbridge would never walk and why we don't see her out and about.
Okay, a lot of details matter. I might sound casual but I know the small stuff could be useful.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Don't you dare say his name. Just call him You Know Who and show him some respect, yeah?

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "I'm sorry," Ron said, moaning a little as he raised himself to look at them, "but it feels like a — a jinx or something. Can't we call him You-Know-Who — please?"
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: Blimey, when I'm like this I can't hear his name without feeling twisted. Call him You Know Who, alright?

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "You got it?" shouted Ron, raising himself a little higher on his pillows. "No one tells me anything! Blimey, you could have mentioned it!"
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: No one tells me anything. I'm the one stuck here and I want to know what's going on. If you had the locket you could have told me.

Book7-chapter14_Sc6.source: "There isn't any chance someone's destroyed it since Kreacher had it?" asked Ron hopefully.
Book7-chapter14_Sc6.description: I'm hoping someone hasn't destroyed it. If Kreacher had it and it was gone I'd be gutted, so I'm quietly relieved it's still here.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: No, it’s because you’re supposed to be the best at magic!" shot back Ron.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: Blimey, I was defending Hermione there, saying she gets stuck with the cooking because she's supposed to be brilliant at magic. I don't think it's fair she has to do everything.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Shut up!" said Harry, leaping to his feet and holding up both hands. "Shut up now!
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: I was impatient and snappy earlier but when Harry warned us I shut it. I know when to keep my gob shut if he says so.
So they're goblins, right? Hearing those names made me realize we're eavesdropping on goblins, not just random wizards.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: The sword in Gringotts is a fake. That's mental. If the real sword's somewhere else, that's a lead we have to chase.

Book7-chapter15_Sc2.source: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently.
Book7-chapter15_Sc2.description: They punished Ginny and the others who tried to take the sword. Lucky they're not badly hurt, but it sounds nasty.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "But you can make a brilliant Patronus!" protested Ron, when Harry arrived back at the tent empty-handed, out of breath, and mouthing the single word, dementors.
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: You're supposed to be able to make a Patronus, Harry. I reckon you can do it, so I was shocked when you couldn't.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "I would, but my arm’s in a sling, in case you hadn’t noticed!" "That’s convenient."
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: My arm's in a sling, and I use that as an excuse when I'm hungry or can't be bothered to help. Hunger makes me grumpy, and I complain about it.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "My mother," said Ron one night, as they sat in the tent on a riverbank in Wales, "can make good food appear out of thin air."
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: Blimey, my mum can somehow rustle up brilliant food from nothing. It feels like magic compared to what we're eating out here.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: "So where next?" was his constant refrain. He did not seem to have any ideas himself, but expected Harry and Hermione to come up with plans while he sat and brooded over the low food supplies.
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: I keep asking where we go next because I'm hungry and bored. I don't have the answers, I want others to come up with plans while I brood a bit.

Book7-chapter15_Sc1.source: He was tugging at the chain of the Horcrux around his neck: Harry was visited by a desire to seize it and throttle him.
Book7-chapter15_Sc1.description: I fiddle with the Horcrux chain when I'm tense. I know it annoys Harry, but being hungry and carrying that thing makes me snappy.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "No!" said Ron. "No, don’t open it! I’m serious!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: No way, do not open that thing. I mean it, I can't let it be opened.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "Because that thing’s bad for me!" said Ron, backing away from the locket on the rock. "I can’t handle it! I’m not making excuses, Harry, for what I was like, but it affects me worse than it affected you and Hermione, it made me think stuff — stuff I was thinking anyway, but it made everything worse, I can’t explain it, and then I’d take it off and I’d get my head on straight again, and then I’d have to put the effing thing back on — I can’t do it, Harry!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: That locket messes with me worse than it did with you lot. It twists what I'm already thinking into something ugly. I keep getting straight then I have to wear it again and it's impossible.

Book7-chapter19_Sc4.source: "You can do it," said Harry, "you can! You’ve just got the sword, I know it’s supposed to be you who uses it. Please, just get rid of it, Ron." The sound of his name seemed to act like a stimulant. Ron swallowed, then, still breathing hard through his long nose, moved back toward the rock. "Tell me when," he croaked.
Book7-chapter19_Sc4.description: Hearing him call my name snaps me a bit. I can get close and do it if I have to, I just need to brace myself. Tell me when and I'll try.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: He explained how he had watched Harry jump into the pool and had waited for him to resurface; how he had realized that something was wrong, dived in, and saved Harry, then returned for the sword.
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: Blimey, I watched Harry go under, thought something was wrong, dived in and pulled him out, then went back for the sword.

Book7-chapter19_Sc10.source: and Ron stabbed it with the sword.
Book7-chapter19_Sc10.description: I got the sword in and, well, I stabbed the locket. That’s what finished it off.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: What the hell. I came straight in and there he was. I can't believe he did that without thinking it through.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "Oh yeah, I got it out," he said, rather unnecessarily, holding up the sword for Harry’s inspection.
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: I got the locket out. I plunged the sword in and pulled it off him. Job done.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "I’ve — you know — I’ve come back. If —" He cleared his throat. "You know. You still want me."
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: I came back because I wanted to be with them again. I wanted Harry to want me with them.

Book7-chapter19_Sc1.source: "I've been looking for you for hours, it’s a big forest, isn’t it?"
Book7-chapter19_Sc1.description: I tracked them for hours through that forest until I found them. It took ages and it was horrible, but I kept at it.
My Patronus is a stag. Don't get it mixed up with a doe.

Book7-chapter19_Sc12.source: Yeah. Could’ve been worse. Remember those birds she set on me?
Book7-chapter19_Sc12.description: Could've been worse, honestly. Remember those birds she set on me? Bloody nightmare.

Book7-chapter19_Sc3.description: Me? Why? Blimey, you're really asking me to do it. I'm shocked and not sure I'm ready.

Book7-chapter19_Sc3.source: Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you.
Book7-chapter19_Sc3.description: I did pull the sword out of the pool, so it feels like it's supposed to be my job. That puts everything on me and it's proper scary.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "I just hoped, you know, after we'd been running round a few weeks, we'd have achieved something."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I'm fed up. I expected us to be getting somewhere by now and we are not. That's what I meant when I said I was disappointed.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "They weren’t thieving," said Harry. "That sword isn’t Snape’s." "It belongs to Professor Snape’s school," said Phineas Nigellus."
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I heard that the sword was not Snape's personal property but something goblin made linked to his school. I'm angry about the whole business.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Yeah, maybe I will!" shouted Ron, and he took several steps toward Harry, who did not back away.
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I left. I told Harry to go home and then I Disapparated. I needed to get away because I was furious and hurt.

Book7-chapter15_Sc3.source: "Didn’t you hear what they said about my sister? But you don’t give a rat’s fart, do you,"
Book7-chapter15_Sc3.description: I am worried about Ginny and the rest of my family. I felt Harry did not seem to care enough and that made me explode.

Book7-chapter19_Sc9.source: “Well, I stayed on that hill all day,” said Ron. “I kept hoping you’d appear. But when it started to get dark I knew I must have missed you, so I clicked the Deluminator again, the blue light came out and went inside me, and I Disapparated and arrived here in these woods."
Book7-chapter19_Sc9.description: I stayed on that hill all day hoping you'd show up. When I couldn't find you, I clicked the Deluminator, the blue light went into me, and I Disapparated to these woods.

Book7-chapter19_Sc9.source: “I still couldn’t see you, so I just had to hope one of you would show yourselves in the end — and Harry did.”
Book7-chapter19_Sc9.description: Blimey, I believed you'd appear at the end. I couldn't see you because the spells worked, but I guessed one of you would eventually show yourselves.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "So I took it out," Ron went on, looking at the Deluminator, "and it didn't seem different or anything, but I was sure I'd heard you. So I clicked it. And the light went out in my room, but another light appeared right outside the window."
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: I took the Deluminator out and clicked it. The light in my room went out and another blue pulsing light showed up outside my window.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "It was a ball of light, kind of pulsing, and bluish, like that light you get around a Portkey, you know?"
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: Blimey, it was a little bluish ball of light, pulsing, exactly like the glow around a Portkey.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "It sort of floated toward me," said Ron, illustrating the movement with his free index finger, "right to my chest, and then — it just went straight through. It was here," he touched a point close to his heart, "I could feel it, it was hot. And once it was inside me I knew what I was supposed to do, I knew it would take me where I needed to go."
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: It floated right to my chest and went straight through me. I could feel it, hot, like it was inside me, and then I knew what to do and where it would send me.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "So I Disapparated and came out on the side of a hill. There was snow everywhere."
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: I Disapparated and ended up on the side of a snowy hill.

Book7-chapter19_Sc11.source: "I still couldn't see you, so I just had to hope one of you would show yourselves in the end — and Harry did."
Book7-chapter19_Sc11.description: I couldn't see you lot, but I trusted one of you would turn up in the end and Harry did. That's what I was counting on.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "Why return? We were better without you, happier without you, glad of your absence."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: Blimey. For a moment I actually believed they were right and we'd have been better off without me.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "The monstrous versions of himself and Hermione were gone: There was only Ron, standing there with the sword held slackly in his hand, looking down at the shattered remains of the locket on the flat rock."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: I stabbed it. I smashed the locket and whatever was inside finally disappeared. I did it, even if it nearly broke me.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "Ron had pierced the glass in both windows: Riddle’s eyes were gone... He had sunk to his knees, his head in his arms. He was shaking..."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: I feel rotten about what I did and what I saw, but I saved Harry and Hermione from that thing. Doesn't make me feel any less rubbish though.

Book7-chapter19_Sc5.source: "Your mother confessed," sneered Riddle-Harry, while Riddle-Hermione jeered, "that she would have preferred me as a son, would be glad to exchange . . ."
Book7-chapter19_Sc5.description: The Horcrux will use anything to wound you. It even pretended Mum preferred someone else to try to break me.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "I came running after you! I called you! I begged you to come back!"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: I tried to get back to them the whole time, I called and I begged, I couldn't just leave them without trying.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "I walked straight into a gang of Snatchers"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: Blimey, I ran into Snatchers, proper gangs rounding up Muggle-borns and blood traitors. That's why I couldn't just go home.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "Told them I was Stan Shunpike. First person I could think of."
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: I lied and said I was Stan Shunpike to get out of being dragged off, and, well, they were not the sharpest.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "I didn’t do it so well, Splinched myself again"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: I messed up a Disapparation and Splinched myself, lost bits of me, like fingernails, which is rotten, but I got away.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "This." "The Deluminator?" "I heard you coming out of my pocket. Your voice, came out of this."
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: That Deluminator actually spoke Hermione's voice to me from my pocket. I heard 'Ron' and something about a wand and it pulled me back.

Book7-chapter19_Sc8.source: "It was a ball of light, kind of pulsing, and bluish"
Book7-chapter19_Sc8.description: There was this little bluish, pulsing ball of light, like a Portkey, that showed up outside my window and I followed it.
The light actually went right into me, into my chest, and once it was there I just knew where to go. So I Disapparated and it dropped me near them.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: She saw Ron, who stood there holding the sword and dripping onto the threadbare carpet.
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: I came back with the sword and I'm a mess. I'm exhausted and I didn't exactly turn up looking fine.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: “Ouch — ow — gerroff! What the — ? Hermione — OW!”
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: Blimey, Hermione's actually attacking me. Ouch ow gerroff what the hell Hermione ow I was hoping for a reaction like relief not a punch up.

Book7-chapter19_Sc7.source: Ron gave a weak, hopeful smile and half raised his arms.
Book7-chapter19_Sc7.description: I was hopeful she'd forgive me or at least not hit me straight away. I still care about her and I wanted it to go back to normal.

Book7-chapter20_Sc5.source: "If it’s annoying you, I’ll stop!" he told Hermione nervously.
Book7-chapter20_Sc5.description: Blimey, I backed off straight away because Hermione was fed up. I don't want to wind her up when she's on a mission.
Er, why do we need to see Mr. Lovegood? I'm not convinced yet, I need convincing.

Book7-chapter20_Sc9.source: "Cowardly old wart," said Ron. "Luna’s got ten times his guts."
Book7-chapter20_Sc9.description: He's a cowardly old wart. Luna's got ten times his guts.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "You don't reckon Kingsley could have sent that doe?" "His Patronus is a lynx, we saw it at the wedding, remember?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: You don't reckon Kingsley sent the doe? I mean, I know his Patronus is a lynx from the wedding, so that doesn't add up.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Harry . . . you don't reckon it could've been Dumbledore?" "Dumbledore what?" "Dumbledore . . . the doe? I mean," Ron was watching Harry out of the corners of his eyes, "he had the real sword last, didn't he?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: Blimey, do you reckon Dumbledore could've been behind the doe? He had the sword last, didn't he? It's a daft hope, but it would be brilliant if it were true.

Book7-chapter20_Sc2.source: "Yeah, a bunch of Death Eaters cornered him, Bill said, but he fought his way out. He’s on the run now, just like us."
Book7-chapter20_Sc2.description: Yeah, Bill said a bunch of Death Eaters cornered Kingsley but he fought his way out. He's on the run now, like we are.

Book7-chapter21_Sc4.source: "So he can sneak up on people,"
Book7-chapter21_Sc4.description: So Death can sneak up on people with the Cloak. Blimey, that is creepy.

Book7-chapter21_Sc4.source: "Sometimes he gets bored of running at them, flapping his arms and shrieking . . . sorry, Hermione."
Book7-chapter21_Sc4.description: Death isn't just dramatic and scary all the time. He might get fed up and do something subtle instead. That's mental. Sorry about the outburst.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: Blimey, getting that locket destroyed feels like a proper win. I'm right back in with Harry and Hermione now.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: "NO!" roared Ron... "but the name’s been jinxed, Harry, that’s how they track people! Using his name breaks protective enchantments, it causes some kind of magical disturbance — it’s how they found us in Tottenham Court Road!"
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: No, you can't go saying his name willy nilly. It's jinxed and it lets them track you. That's why people who dare stand up to him had to be careful.

Book7-chapter20_Sc1.source: "Because we used his name?" "Exactly! You’ve got to give them credit, it makes sense. It was only people who were serious about standing up to him, like Dumbledore, who ever dared use it."
Book7-chapter20_Sc1.description: You've got to give them credit, that whole Taboo idea actually makes sense. Only the really brave or reckless used his name.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: "I’m sorry," he said in a thick voice. "I’m sorry I left. I know I was a — a —"
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: I'm sorry I left. I know I was a right prat for going off like that.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: "That makes me sound a lot cooler than I was," Ron mumbled. "Stuff like that always sounds cooler than it really was," said Harry.
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: Blimey, what I did sounds better when you say it. It wasn't as heroic as it sounds.

Book7-chapter19_Sc6.source: Ron did not respond, but turned his face away from Harry and wiped his nose noisily on his sleeve.
Book7-chapter19_Sc6.description: I was a mess, eyes all bloodshot and sniffling, trying to act like I wasn't ruined by it all.

Book7-chapter21_Sc1.description: Yeah, I know 'The Tale of the Three Brothers.'

Book7-chapter20_Sc7.source: "looking first at Hermione, then at Ron, and finally at Harry"
Book7-chapter20_Sc7.description: Blimey, he looked at me straight after Hermione, like he was checking everyone out. I was just waiting to see what he'd do.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “The Deluminator turned out to be pretty useful,”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: Blimey, the Deluminator actually came in handy. It wasn't just a trinket.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “Lovegood’s on your side, Harry, The Quibbler’s been for you all along, it keeps telling everyone they’ve got to help you!”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: The Lovegoods and The Quibbler are on Harry's side. They're backing him and urging people to help.

Book7-chapter20_Sc6.source: “Yeah, they’re not far from my place,” said Ron. “I dunno exactly where, but Mum and Dad always point toward the hills whenever they mention them. Shouldn’t be hard to find.”
Book7-chapter20_Sc6.description: The Lovegoods live not far from my parents' place. Mum and Dad always point toward the hills when they talk about them, so finding them shouldn't be hard.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Oh yeah," said Ron at once, "people are talking about it quite a lot."
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: People are talking loads about Skeeter's story. It's everywhere right now.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "'Course, if things were different, it'd be huge news, Dumbledore being pals with Grindelwald, but now it's just something to laugh about for people who didn't like Dumbledore, and a bit of a slap in the face for everyone who thought he was such a good bloke."
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Blimey, if the times were different that would be massive. As it is, it's mostly used by Dumbledore's critics to sneer, and it stings his proper supporters.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "There's this one program," he told Harry in a low voice, "that tells the news like it really is. All the others are on You-Know-Who's side and are following the Ministry line, but this one . . . you wait till you hear it, it's great. Only they can't do it every night, they have to keep changing locations in case they're raided, and you need a password to tune in."
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Right, there's this cracking program that tells the truth. The rest are on You-Know-Who's side. You need a password to get it and they keep moving about so they don't get nicked.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "Trouble is, I missed the last one." He drummed lightly on the top of the radio with his wand, muttering random words under his breath.
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: Typical me, I missed the last broadcast. I'm hoping I can catch the next one, so I keep faffing about with the radio trying to get it.

Book7-chapter20_Sc4.source: "He threw Hermione many covert glances, plainly fearing an angry outburst"
Book7-chapter20_Sc4.description: I'm proper worried Hermione will explode if I say the wrong thing. I keep sneaking looks at her and trying not to set her off.

Book7-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Patronuses can change, though, can't they? Tonks's changed, didn't it?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc3.description: Patronuses can change. Tonks's did change, so they are not always fixed.

Book7-chapter20_Sc3.source: "Sometimes I've thought, when I've been a bit hacked off, he was having a laugh or he just wanted to make it more difficult. But I don't think so, not anymore. He knew what he was doing when he gave me the Deluminator,"
Book7-chapter20_Sc3.description: I used to think Dumbledore was having a laugh or being awkward on purpose, but now I reckon he knew exactly what he was doing when he left me the Deluminator.

Book7-chapter20_Sc3.source: "he must've known I'd run out on you."
Book7-chapter20_Sc3.description: I know I ran out on you, and I reckon Dumbledore must've expected that from me. I felt guilty but also like he understood me.

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "When you say 'master of Death' —" said Ron.
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: When you say 'master of Death', you mean someone who has conquered or vanquished death, right?

Book7-chapter21_Sc5.source: "Perhaps you ought to try on the hat, Hermione," said Ron, nodding toward the ludicrous headdress. His voice shook with the strain of not laughing.
Book7-chapter21_Sc5.description: I tease Hermione to lighten the mood. I can't help laughing at that ridiculous hat even when things are serious.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“And I was just thinking I’d have to kip under a tree and wait for morning when I saw that deer coming and you following.” “You didn’t see anyone else?” “No,” said Ron. “I —” But he hesitated, glancing at two trees growing close together some yards away. “I did think I saw something move over there, but I was running to the pool at the time, because you’d gone in and you hadn’t come up, so I wasn’t going to make a detour to — hey!”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: I saw the deer and I saw Harry following it. I might have seen something move by those trees but I was heading straight for the pool because Harry went in and didn’t come up.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“You reckon this is the real one?” asked Ron.]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: I’m not sure if that sword is the real one, but I want to find out.

Book7-chapter19_Sc2.source: [“The Horcrux was still swinging from Ron’s hand. The locket was twitching slightly.”]
Book7-chapter19_Sc2.description: I’m holding the locket and it’s twitching in my hand like it’s alive.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "There’s a description in Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them! Mr Lovegood, you need to get rid of it straightaway, don’t you know it can explode at the slightest touch?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: Blimey, it's in Fantastic Beasts. If it's an Erumpent horn it can blow up on you, so get rid of it now.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "Aren’t you the one who keeps telling everyone it’s their first duty to help Harry?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: You're always going on about everyone helping Harry in your magazine. I called him out on that because it sounded ridiculous for him to say one thing and then act differently.

Book7-chapter20_Sc8.source: "How d'you know it’s an Erumpent horn?"
Book7-chapter20_Sc8.description: I asked how she knew, because it seemed important and a bit alarming, and I wanted an answer right away.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Blimey, I reckon it's definitely spookier at midnight; our mum always said midnight makes a tale scarier.

Book7-chapter21_Sc2.source: "Sorry, I just think it’s a bit spookier if it’s midnight!"
Book7-chapter21_Sc2.description: Look, I just think the whole thing's creepier at midnight — that's how stories work, innit?

Book7-chapter21_Sc8.source: "Ron was buried deepest: Harry and Hermione climbed, as quietly as they could, over all the wreckage to where he lay, trying to prise a heavy chest of drawers off his legs."
Book7-chapter21_Sc8.description: Blimey, I was buried under that lot. I couldn't move until Hermione sorted me out.
Bloody hell, I went straight under the Invisibility Cloak. It's like I disappeared.
Er, I wasn't keen at first and I panicked, but then I had to trust them. Okay fine, I'll do it.

Book7-chapter21_Sc6.source: So where do you think the Elder Wand is now?
Book7-chapter21_Sc6.description: Blimey, where's the Elder Wand supposed to be now then? That's what matters.
Who are these Peverells? That was the name on the grave in Godric's Hollow, wasn't it? That's proper suspicious.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "That treacherous old bleeder!" Ron panted, emerging from beneath the Invisibility Cloak and throwing it to Harry.
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: He's a treacherous old bleeder, I can't believe he tried to sell us out like that.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "Serves him right," said Ron, examining his torn jeans and the cuts to his legs. "What d’you reckon they’ll do to him?"
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: Serves him right that his house got blown apart. I wonder what they'll do to him now.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "Then she’ll be in Azkaban, I expect," said Ron. "Whether she survives the place, though . . . Loads don’t."
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: If Luna's been taken, she'll probably be in Azkaban and I worry she might not survive that place, because a lot of people don't.

Book7-chapter22_Sc1.source: "Why hide me, though?" asked Ron. "You’re supposed to be in bed with spattergroit, Ron! They’ve kidnapped Luna because her father supported Harry! What would happen to your family if they knew you’re with him?"
Book7-chapter22_Sc1.description: They kidnapped Luna because her father supported Harry. I shouldn't be out with him because my family would be in danger if anyone knew I was with Harry.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "'All fine!' Ron called back, in a passable imitation of Wormtail’s wheezy voice."
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: Blimey, I can fake a wheeze when I have to. I tried to bluff our way out when Wormtail came down.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "'Relashio!' said Ron, pointing the wand at the silver hand, but nothing happened;"
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: I tried spells in the heat of it and sometimes they just don’t work under pressure. That was useless and terrifying.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "'NOOOOOOOOOOOO!' Ron had burst into the drawing room;"
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: When Hermione was threatened I lost it. I am not staying back if she's in danger. Bloody hell, I will charge in.

Book7-chapter23_Sc3.source: "Expelliarmus!" he roared, pointing Wormtail’s wand at Bellatrix, and hers flew into the air and was caught by Harry,
Book7-chapter23_Sc3.description: I can pull an Expelliarmus when it counts. I will try anything to disarm them if it saves Hermione.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: Blimey, I can't help it, I scream her name until I'm hoarse. When Hermione's in danger I lose my head.

Book7-chapter23_Sc2.source: "My pocket! In my pocket, there’s a Deluminator, and it’s full of light!"
Book7-chapter23_Sc2.description: I remembered the Deluminator and used it instinctively. Sometimes I spot the simplest trick when we need light and I blurt it out.
